review: This is a new lounge for Aer Lingus as on previous occasions they would use the lounge of a partner airline. The lounge is not overly large but more than enough space for passengers embarking on the four flights they were operating when we were there. There is a small area with food. Sandwiches, salads and wraps during all opening hours and hot food choices late afternoon and evening. The evening hot choices on our visit were Chicken in a mushroom sauce, Boiled potatoes with parsley, steamed green beans and tomatoes and macaroni cheese. I sampled all these and they were very good. Two cakes were on offer as dessert. All the time bags of crisps (chips) and pretzels and fresh apples and oranges were there too. A small selection of wines and beers, including a sparkling wine, and sodas were self-serve. Pleasant and quiet with staff who, while not exactly chatty and communicative, were professional. They cleared tables and refreshed food regularly. Toilets were clean and more than adequate. I didn't see any shower facilities, however that does not mean they were not there.

A small, clean lounge with plenty of seating, a well-stocked, self-serve bar and some food options. Some windows overlooked the runways and boarding gates but, understandably, the other windows overlooking a shabby storage area had blinds fully closed. A few nibbles, a couple of sandwich and wrap options and a beef stew were available. My partner had the stew and left it after a couple of bites as the meat was mainly fat and gristle and the sauce bland and unappetising, a real disappointment. Two flavours of potato crisps (chips in the US) were consumed and these, jalapeno and BBQ, were very good. Staff were helpful and kept the tables and other areas clean and tidy. It was good that the lounge was only a short walk from the gate too.

While the decor etc is nice, the food is absolutely awful. Soup, cheese and crackers is the height of it. It is truly appalling. The staff themselves seem embarrassed by the mostly empty display cabinets.

I would probably rate the lounge as awesome, but since I couldn’t get in I give it a zero. Paid, had the printout, but I was at another terminal so I wasn’t allowed in. Aer Lingus says “Sorry no refunds on unused passes” So I sat at the airport for 4 hours without lounge access Fail Aer Lingus

The Gold Circle Lounge in Dublin T2 is a two storey area with large windows giving good views of the apron. There is a water feature which extends over two floors. Upstairs is a quiet area, where showers are located. There are power points for charging mobile devices, and a couple of computers with printing facilities. Short Haul flights are not called from the lounge, but there are several flight information screens. The food on offer consisted of: Fresh fruit, Cereals, Breads,  pastries etc. Aer Lingus display allergen information beside all food products. A full range of soft and alcoholic drinks is available along with fruit juices, tea and coffee. Being close to the boarding gates is also a big plus. A very pleasant lounge to await a flight.

I book the Aer Lingus flight under BA and am silver member but flying from Dublin to Leeds you still can't access Aer Lingus lounge free so I paid the £23 fee. Small lounge, freezing cold when I arrived but good range of comfortable seating. Drinks very limited and food was very limited (plastic wrapped cheese and crackers or soup) - I have never visited a lounge this poor before. In future I'll go to the nice wine bar in the terminal and do much better for less. By the way I notice these same reviews go back years so clearly Aer Lingus  know all this already and couldn't give a stuff!

The lounge is small, with limited seating. Offers a nice view of the ramp, with views of runway in distance. Very limited selection of snacks, (bread, cheese, biscuits). Tea and coffee from machine. No showers. Alcohol available (limited choice). Possibly the worst stocked Business Class lounge I have ever visited. Staff generally disinterested and bored. Tables left uncleaned. Preferable to sitting outside on hard chairs, but that's about the best that can be said for it. If Aer Lingus reckons this is good enough, they should check out lounges around the rest of the world.

Located after US Preclearance in Terminal 2 and beside the US departure gates, it is close to an active runway. Complimentary access for Aer Lingus passengers is restricted to Business Class ticket holders and Prestige / Elite Gold Circle Club members. The entry fee of 39euro is substantially higher than the DAA lounges. 51st & Green is located beside gate 406, and clearly signposted. Entry is through sliding doors, down a gradual slope where a very pleasant lady welcomed us as Aer Lingus Business Class Passengers, and explained that food and drink were self service and complimentary. No mention was made of the additional menu which is chargeable. First impressions are of a bright, white almost clinical area, Soft drinks and a selection of salads, soups, bread rolls, smoked salmon, duck terrine are nicely displayed on the counters, along with some baked goods and biscuits laid out in wooden serving trays.  A small range of beers, wines and spirits is available from an attended counter which doubles as a coffee bar. DAA state that the coffee is specially ground for the 51st & Green lounge by a micro-roastery. It is good to see local businesses being supported in such a way, and the espresso I sampled was excellent. I asked at the bar/coffee server if it was possible to have some champagne and was amazed to be told that the lounge did not stock champagne. Surely a premium lounge should carry champagne? I would have been quite happy to pay for it, but was unable to do so. The newspaper rack contained two (used) copies of the Irish Independent newspaper. Nothing else whatever being available, There is a wide range of seat types, some facing runways, some in quiet clusters. Numerous power points are in place to charge mobile devices. However there is no business area, no computers for guests to use (to take advantage of the advertised “printing facilities”). In fairness, the receptionist was quick to offer to print any documents which I could email to her. A nice gesture, but surely a premium lounge should have at least one or two PCs for guests to use and print whatever they need? Pea and ham soup was hot and flavoursome, but served in a narrow mug is less than ideal. The cakes were quite pleasant, but there seemed to be a distinct shortage of bread rolls. For over half an hour, the basket was virtually empty. Also disappointing was the lethargic approach taken to clearing tables. One grave omission during the two hours we spent in the 51st & Green was the failure to offer the menu of cooked to order hot meals mentioned in DAAs’ publicity. However, the negatives are many: Lack of newspapers. No business centre. Toilets out of order. Slow replenishment of basic food items. Slow table clearance. Failure to offer any of the meals described on DAA publicity.

The staff was rude. The temperature was 80 degrees in the lounge and they were very unconcerned. There were six other guests complaining, but wouldn't say anything to the staff. They said the air conditioning had been turned off for the season. Then I spent 15 minutes on hold trying to find someone to speak to about getting a refund. Won't be using the lounge again.

This Aer Lingus Lounge at Boston Logan Airport is adequate, but it does not open until 90 mins after check in opens. Perhaps they expect it to take you so long to get through. Very small and was almost full to capacity. Toilets some distance from lounge and not particularly clean. Limited selection of snacks and sandwiches.

Visited the Aer Lingus Gold Circle Lounge in Heathrow Terminal 2 when flying to Dublin. The receptionist was extremely unfriendly. Initial impressions of the lounge were positive, a nice, open and airy lounge with nice colours and comfortable seating. There are great views of the tarmac. The food offering is abysmal. There are some packaged biscuits and crackers and that is about it. Drinks offering is quite good with coffee, wine, spirits and beer. I used the shower room which was excellent and contained L’occitane amenities. The shower was excellent and was just what I needed after a long flight. Overall the lounge is a nice escape from the Heathrow noise, but the food offering does diminish the appeal somewhat.

Greeted by lovely helpful ladies on reception at Dublin Gold Circle lounge, helped clear up a booking issue straight away, very professional, great service. Nice peaceful place to wait for your flight.

Unimpressed. When you enter there is a woman sitting at desk looking miserable. The lounge itself is small and snacks available are the poorest selection I have seen. Not sure this policy about dining before you fly is in play. If it is, all you get for dinner are sandwiches. Toilets are down the corridor. Come on Aer Lingus, inflight service is superb now follow it up in all your lounges.

Aer Lingus Gold Circle at Heathrow airport is a nice spacious area. Wifi is fine. Quiet. Self-serve food and bar area but limited offering for food. For breakfast - cereals and Danish. Staffing need some schooling on customer service a smile goes a long way but no-one was cracking even a small grin. No direction on the layout.

Paid £50 for Are Lingus Lounge use for myself and my daughter on way to New York from Belfast via Dublin Airport. Couldn't believe such poor food offer at breakfast time. 3 cereals in plastic dispensers and a shared bowl of fruit salad to cater for everyone. Some small croissants only and not nice taste at that. Nothing else. Also poor reception from staff. What a rip off.

Aer Lingus Gold Circle lounge at T2 Heathrow is a much nicer lounge than the old terminal 1. There was lots of light from the floor to ceiling windows and good views of the runaway. However the choice of food (we were there 9-10.30am) was very limited: cereals croissants cheese and crackers. No bread or porridge. However the coffee was decent and if you really fancied it there was a good choice of alcohol.
On return to UK visited Aer Lingus lounge. Clean and pleasant enough. Limited facilities and far from gates buried somewhere in terminal 2. At 25 euros per person it is very poor value.

Regularly used this Aer Lingus Gold Circle lounge in the past year always found it good. Used it Saturday 5th October and what a change for the worse no longer provide sandwiches (told they can't find a supplier by one of the staff) so lukewarm soup and brown bread all that was available. No small bottles of sparking water only big bottles that had been opened all day gone flat. A woman told me in bad English that they have stopped the bottles of sparkling water as the airline loses revenue on onboard sales. Felt the whole experience was a let down. Aer Lingus you've done better in the past this is terrible.

Surly and unfriendly receptionists. On my Aer Lingus prestige my wife and I were permitted entry but told my two young children would not be allowed in. Never experienced that in a Gold Circle. So we sat outside and went in to get refreshments. They then watched us and it felt like we were being "watched" the entire time. Not even a great lounge. Very budget.

The Oasis lounge seems to be shared amongst all the users of T4 at JFK. I didn't see any other lounges. Because of that lack of competition it seems that the staff are just not bothered. The "welcome" is perfunctory at best and at worst is really an entitlement check after whether the staff lose interest in the passenger. Signage is poor no times/distances to various gates no advertising other facilities to passengers. Trying to plug in an iPhone charger was tricky as the first 2 sockets I found were both broken exposing the innards of the socket wiring. Seating in the quiet area was not very comfortable. All in all I wouldn't be rushing back.
Showers toilets decent range of snacks and drinks together with newspapers and mags. It is bright and airy and has a quite zone.

Bright and spacious lounge. Drink and food selection reasonable but not brilliant. It is on two levels I would choose the upper level as the views are better but food choice slightly better downstairs.

I used this lounge for a 9.55am departure. It was not very busy but was claustrophobic. The staff were welcoming and seemed happy to play with a passenger's toddler. The seating could do with a good clean. Food limited - cereal cheap cheese and biscuits and even cheaper croissants. As a Gold Circle member I had free entry - but if you have to pay don't bother.

The new Aer Lingus Gold Circle Business Class lounge at Dublin Airport spans two floors with views of the apron A water feaTUre dominates one wall. There are work stations and complimentary wifi. The range of food on offer during the early morning is sufficient and a bar service is available. This lounge has own showers and washrooms something the former lounge lacked. The lounge is also open to non FFP members for a 25euro fee.

Sitting here now kicking myself that I bought a day pass. Absolutely the most dismal depressing miserable lounge. In a windowless bunker. Shoddy uncomfortable furniture inedible old sandwiches indifferent attendant. I guess the troubles in Ireland filter down to their Airport lounges.

Ample seating including armchairs and full-length recliners. Complimentary WiFi and a number of booths to work on your laptop along with three or four PCs (with very old software!). Staff helpful and courteous. Bar has a selection of hot and cold drinks including soft drinks and alcohol. A limited selection of hot food. Large selection of newspapers.

Not to the same standard as other lounges (eg. Amsterdam) but actually pretty good. Staff (when they're there) are nice and the lounge has a nice little selection of food and drink and free internet (although fair play to cork it's free throughout the airport). My only issue with cork is that it doesn't open until i think something like 6:00 although the flight to amsterdam leaves at 6:10. As with their other lounges no toilets although this doesn't really bother me that much.

I'm sitting in the lounge a bit incredulous that I paid for access to this. I paid for it because I had a lot of time to kill and it seemed a good way to pass the day. What a gloomy awful lounge. I found this page because I was looking to see if maybe I'd missed something because it seems there is no free WiFi. Completely insane. I thought this was for business travellers? The girl at the desk looked me up and down when I walked in too so apparently despite having a lounge that looks like a 3rd grade classroom without the fun stuff on the walls (or windows) they have a problem with how people dress? I'm neatly attired but I'm flying today so I am absolutely not wearing a suit. Anyway the long and short of it is that the lounge is unfriendly no amenities no toilets no natural light can't really see myself bothering with it again.

My first visit to the Gold Circle lounge in many months. I was aware from other reviews of the decrease in size but I didn't expect to see the work stations gone too. The only saving grace is that there is a choice of breads and pastries in the morning.

The range of food and beverages is reasonable. The main attraction of this lounge is that it is beside boarding gates. This evening I noticed the red wine bottle was empty. I asked the attendant to replace it but she wasn't able to open the new bottle. I can understand a bottle of wine being used but to have a staff member unable to open another is beyond belief. What used to be a very good lounge has become almost a joke.

The Gold Circle Lounge at EI home airport of Dublin has just been cut in size by around two thirds. Only a corner of the old lounge remains and the rest has been transformed into a staff room. Rather typical of EI really - an airline that typically seems to put staff ahead of customers. What remains of the lounge is mostly hard airport style seating. Not very must when we visited. Limited selection of drinks. Nice cookies. Glasses were very old and a little too dirty to use. Not convenient to most of EI's departure gates (10 min walk and then backtrack + 10 more minutes).

I have posted previous comments on Aer Lingus lounges but nothing prepared me for the filthy tip that is Chicago Gold Circle lounge. Its tiny dirty furniture all stained ceiling was all stained. Drinks okay no food not even a cracker. I don't normally fly biz class with EI and judging by the reviews and the state of the lounges I never will.

I got to use the Aer Lingus lounge as I was flying on Icelandair. This has got to be the pokiest grubbiest lounge I have ever seen or used. The food was soggy and not fresh and the decor is not very good. Gives a feeling of boredom and gloom. Aer Lingus needs to brighten this lounge up a lot. The lady there was nice and friendly - she was the best part about this lounge.

This lounge has so much potential - it's bright clean and offers sweeping views of the airfield. However the desk staff can range from super-friendly (letting me bring my kids in sometimes) to totally indifferent (too busy gossiping with colleagues to say hello). There is a good range of drinks on offer but food is poor and is restricted to bags of twiglets (does anyone actually like them??!) and crackers with Durch cheese (so much for strong Irish brand identity which Aer Lingus supposedly prides itself on). Plus there is a charge for internet usage which is a shame.

Very basic but better than filthy overcrowded terminal. Food choice limited to biscuits and packaged cheddar cheese. Good selection of drinks - alcoholic and non. Staff friendly to indifferent depending on when you visit. Washrooms outside lounge - shared with other lounges and filthy.

Excellent lounge with good selection of food drink and newspapers. Wifi access etc. I suspect that the high standards are not down to Aer Lingus as the lounge is shared with a number of major international airlines. I say this because the Aer Lingus exclusive lounges at Dublin (home base) and London Heathrow are extremely poor by comparison. Their lounges at Chicago O'Hare and Boston are amongst the worse I have ever encountered.

Everyone agrees that this lounge beats sitting in the awful "tube" outside but that's about it. Aer Lingus you need to incorporate free WiFi some food e.g sandwiches or whatever and get some toilets in there. This is as another user points out barely worth the trouble of keeping up Gold Circle Membership for.

The Lounge is located at Terminal C. Its new and was just opened this year. There are three levels. The Ground level, where you can eat some basics, like bread and sandwiches and drink something (softdrinks, tea and coffe). On the second floor is a cafe, which I didn't use and on the 3rd floor is a smoking lounge and a balcony to spot planes. All in all it is a good lounge with fast wifi, but you shouldn't expect to much.

This was the worst lounge I have been into (handling lounge "Jet Lounge"). It doesn't have anything to do with the services, it is about the comfort and how you feel inside it. To start with the fact that it is very difficult to find. I had no idea it is before security, so I had to go through security and then to find out that I have to go out to get to the lounge and go through security one more time. Once I got there, it was so crowded that it was impossible to find a seat on your own and you had to share a couch with other people. getting something to drink or eat was an adventure as well, regarding the number of people waiting in line in order to get something from the small buffet. The staff was however friendly and they were trying to save the situation somehow, but it is obvious that you cannot handle all the frequent flyers from all the airlines in one lounge. It looked clean and well maintained.

This was a pleasant surprise. Who would have thought that before moving to the new Berlin Airport, Air Berlin will open a new lounge at the actual Tegel? And  they have done it (not that it wasn't necessary) and in Terminal C, where most of their flights are. It saves a lot of time if flying from C and not to have to use the one in Terminal A and then walk some good minutes , go through security in Terminal C. And it is quite spacious, with 1st and 2nd floor (this only a smoking lounge). The variety of food and drinks is not outrageous but it is enough to make you fell comfortable and I don't think you would miss anything. There isn't any cooked food, except for some soup. But the good thing about this food is that it is of good quality. We are going away from the sausages and get some nice fresh salads, yoghurt and prezels. Everything is and looks new and it is a very nice surprise for its customers from Air Berlin to think of such a thing. Thank you!

As the alternative to the official Air Berlin Lounge at Tegel airport (the Air France Lounge), British Airways is the one for all other oneworld members flying from there and I use it sometimes when flying with Air Berlin. The plus of this Lounge is that it is more spacious, has better views and looks more professional. The downside is the lack of snacks: it only offers sandwiches with 3 or 4 fillings all the time. The potato chips are not available anymore and only some pretzels. The beverages are in good condition as in most business class lounges. Not a true lounge but this has to do with the infrastructure of the airport, as well.

As a matter of fact it is sad that Air Berlin doesn't have its own lounge at its hub in Berlin Tegel and has to use the one of Air France. I know they are waiting for the new airport to open when they will have their own lounge, but this is another story already. The lounge is very small (one of the smallest I have seen in my life as a frequent flyer) and not in the best condition anymore (the chairs are old and should be replaced) It can get crowded, especially in the evening and it is not a pleasure in using it anymore. Another downside is that the toilets are located some floors beneath and you have to take an elevator to get there. It does offer some snacks: a combined French-German friendship, chesses & pate and sausages & potato salads but it is way behind other lounges. The beverages are OK and one can find almost every good drink there.

As an Air Berlin topbonus Platinum member when travelling to Bucharest I get to use the Tarom Lounge and to be honest I am really disappointed about how this airline maintains its lounge. There is a lack of snacks/food. The things they are presenting as snacks are just bowls with potato chips (always the same flavour) and some biscuits. There is a yogurt bar. The beverages are OK. The room is quite small for a airline's main hub. Too bad there are no alternatives, the other small lounges offering the same treatment.

This Hamburg Airport Lounge is on the top Level of the Center Terminal (between 1 and 2) with a very large window front overlooking the airfield and runways. Perfect spot for planespotters. Many seats even and a good variety of newspapers. Food and Beverages are very average and could be better. Very friendly Lounge staff.

A very poor interior, not at all clean or comfortable. The selection of food was a few dry sort of round bread and some old nuts. Drinks had been offered mostly with strong alcohol, no wine and juice from the machine which didn`t taste at all. The coffee was in big pots, not fresh, minimum 2 to 3 hours old and tasted as bad as old coffee can taste. It was a very bad experience to wait there, even that we had to because of a delay for departure.
Air Berlin lounge facility at Catania Airport (they use VIP Lounge SAC) is very small. It offers a poor selection of drinks and just some potatoe chips. Does not give you a real advantage.

The lounge in Vienna that is open for Flyniki and Air Berlin flights is quite good. Nice range of breakfast stuff. (cheese, ham, marmelade), nice coffee range, some cereals, fresh fruit. The staff in the lounge is friendly and attentive.

Surprised at complete lack of lounge when flying Air Berlin out of Berlin. Because of the need to get transfer passport control and security check at gate you really have no option and then you're in a space too small for the number of people bad wifi inadequate lighting dirty and 1 food vendor as the only amenity. This business class lounge experience was quite surprising. Once I was on-board the experience was great but the departure experience will keep me from connecting through Berlin again.
This is the most underated lounge i have been to. The food, drink and desert options are good and its quite comfortable too. Would definitely recommend

The lounge is spacious, good light and the food options are good. While there is not an a la carte offer or substantial buffet, the sandwiches, pies, salads and sweets were more than enough and all very tasty. Cleanliness could be a tiny bit better.

The lounge is often crowded, leaving little free space. I get the impression many passengers has a gold card or travel in business class. I have visited this lounge several times and the choice on the buffet is the same. The staff are very polite and helpful.

Modern lounge, good size, at busy times it can be a bit crowded, as in other lounges too. There is a large buffet for food with a lot of choice, constantly refilled. The selection of drinks is also very good, from soft drinks to beer, wine, spirits, Nespresso machine, etc. You can relax in the lounge and relax or work at the workplaces. The staff is friendly and courteous.   DE: Moderne Lounge, gute Größe, zu Stoßzeiten kann es mal etwas voller werden, wie in anderen Lounges auch. Es gibt ein großes Buffet für Speisen mit viel Auswahl, ständig wird aufgefüllt. Di Auswahl an Getränken ist ebenfalls sehr gut, von Softdrinks, über Bier, Wein, Spirituosen, Nespresso-Maschine, etc. Man kann sich in der Lounge erholen und entspannen oder aber an den Arbeitsplätzen arbeiten. Das Personal ist freundlich und zuvorkommend.

Quality of food very poor, almost nothing to eat. Toilets clean but with broken sink and some toilets out of order. They only have one newspaper attached to a steel bar so you cannot take with you. All guests must pass it to others to be read again and again. Wifi could not be connected.  I am wondering what Swissport is doing ? Needs to be refurbished or shut down. There is not any link on Swissport page to upload any complains. Maybe they do not care for a feedback

This lounge is very outdated and needs renovation. The toilets are in a very but condition, requires replacements including painting and it will be nice if showers are available like other Business Lounges.

The lounge is very convenient, near most departure gates. If possible pls avoid it during the rush hours because in the morning from 07.00 to 08.00 is very crowded and it is not so big. The day i visit it, there were some far east passenges sleeping on the couches, that means each one occupied on couch as bed. Maybe some long chairs, suitable for a small nap would be added to. Toilets also they were clean , but since there is one for the males and one for the famales it would be a good idea on next refurbisment to make two for each gender. Wifi was good and the 3 table computers were operating smoothly. Concerning the food, it was ok without something special. In fact they hadbefore some small sadwiches made from products all over Greece and these were not any more available. Wines of the month are good and it was a very small selection of liquors.

Sala Monteverdi lounge that Aegean Airlines use is near the gates, actually above them so you can reach your gate in few minutes. The bad is that there are not any windows overlooking the runways and the lounge is dark. Wifi is good but you have to follow some steps to be connected. Toilets are clean, two for each gender. Most magazines and newspapers are in Italian, however there are 2-3 newspapers in English and one in French and in German. Standard seats and couches arrangement, however near the buffet there are around 10-12 tables where you can seat to eat and charge your phone too. There are small sadwiches made with smoked salmon or prociuto ham together with various other sadwiches. If you do not like the ones served on the buffet just wait few minutes and when they will finish, staff will stock the buffet with new in different taste. There are some fruits and olives together with small parmegiano cheses, however a salad is missing.

Aegean Airlines use the Swissport Lounge at  Athens Airport. The place of the lounge is good, with some windows overlooking the aircrafts. Quality of food is poor. I visited several times in the morning and on the noon.  Toilets are bad. Broken and taped with some sealant. I am wondering how do they belong to Swissport. I advise to go out of the lounge and visit the public toilets of the airport. Wifi ok but not on computers in the lounge.

The Aegean Business lounge in Thessaloniki was very clean, modern, and stocked with a variety of food, beverages, and snacks. I arrived at the lounge at 6.30am from a long bus ride down from Sofia, Bulgaria and was extremely tired. They were very accommodating and did not wake me up once while I rested until my scheduled flight later on. In addition to this, we boarded the plane via a door from the lounge using private buses. I was very impressed with the level of professionalism of the staff. I would definitely recommend Aegean to other passengers.
It is a small, dark, windowless lounge located on the 3rd floor, accessible via elevator. The bar is well equipped with soft drinks, coffee, wines and biers.

Both of the lounges have the same food (sandwiches yogurt cheese cheese pie fruits) and beverages (all sorts of coffee tea bottled drinks alcoholic drinks Greek wine). The decoration in Thessaloniki is very stylish and the bathroom too. Athens is nice but probably needs to be updated.

The lounge was clean and the decor is up to date with colourful chairs. Only one PC and mainly empty bar. Food is some sandwiches cheese and nuts. A lot needs to be improved. I went to Lufthansa lounge where hot food was provided.

Big and spacious lounge. Comfy sofas and a nice variety of food/drinks. The lounge was recently refurbished and looks very stylish. stuff very friendly and they let you know when your flight starts boarding.

Surprisingly pleasant lounge. If traveling through Greece Thessaloniki makes a much better transfer point than Athens and this lounge was quite comfy and pleasant. The shuttle from the lounge to our flight is nice. Aegean Airlines was a pleasant host on our trip to Greece.

Large well lit lounge with a separate smoking area. It can be crowded at times but it is still relatively quiet unless somebody starts screaming into hes/her cell phone. Sandwiches ice cream cheese peanuts and croissants are always there and the bar is so so (no champagne!) with good espresso. Three computers are available and lately free Wi-fi is also provided. Relatively comfortable "wire" seats are available at round tables but if one sits at one of the sofas the risk of falling asleep is high. Careful lots of walking to some gates (especially B1 and 2) and sometimes lengthy security screen is after the lounge. Overall though a good lounge.

Service was very poor. Waiter on his mobile. He seems unable to remove used items from table. 30 minutes so far on this call. You need to buy everything here. A slice of lemon for your tea, 500kzt. A beer (in a city bar 500kzt) here 2800. Remember before entering to visit the bank for a loan. Or do not bother, like the only waiter here.

The lounge is run by the airport and the only benefit is that it has a more private WiFi than the public areas of the airport. If you want any food or drinks you must pay for them. There is a toilet. There seems to be enough space for those using it and it is quieter than the public areas of the airport.

As a Business Lounge this is one of the worst I have been in. Only the toilet and WiFi are free. It is relatively small and is really only a place to sit while you wait for the flight. It is a bit quieter than in the general waiting area and that is the only positive. I spend only the minimum time here. I understand that the problem is with the airport and not the company (they have quite a good lounge in Astana) and that it will not be fixed until the airport is redeveloped.

Business class lounge of Air Astana at Astana airport, Domestic departures. The lounge is small and quite, perfectly designed, provides small snacks and beverages, newspapers and magazines, excellent WiFi. Despite lack of shower and proper food service it looks sufficient for domestic flights

This lounge was shared by multiple airlines. I was flying Air Astana from Almaty Kazakhstan to Bishkek Kyrgyzstan in business class. The lounge was small but so was the airport. Seating was not entirely comfortable yet it was more comfortable than the main airport’s single crowded room. There was a small bar and small cold snack food layout. When I first entered and dropped my bag on a chair, I went to check out the food selection. I was asked by the bartender what airline I was flying. When I told him Astana he informed me the buffet was not for me, but I could purchase it. Being that the food looked meager in selection and low in quality, I did not inquire about the cost. So then I went to the bar and looked into the cooler at the drink selection. I was then informed the drinks were not for me either, but I could buy it. I asked, “even a water I have to pay for?” “yes, even water you buy” was his reply. I was so disgusted to be informed this that I didn’t inquire the cost of that either. Because I had about 6 hours at this airport, I had purchased the upgrade to business for this 30 min flight solely for the lounge access. It turned out to be money completely wasted. It also turned out that internet (WiFi) was not even included in this lounge. I would not pay for an upgrade on Air Astana again in the future.

This is the worst Business Class Lounge I have ever visited! For a four star airline and in their home airport the Lounge is a joke! It is merely somewhere a little quieter to wait for a flight. No complimentary food or drink, no secure WiFi and their free WiFi doesn't work in many areas of the lounge. I am waiting for a late night flight and was planning on a light snack so that I could sleep on the plane. It is just as well as I do not judge the airline by its home lounge or I would be recommending against Air Astana which is the best Airline I have flown in the countries of the former Soviet Union.

This is by far the worst business class Lounge that I've been in during my 29 years of business travel. The sign at the front desk says it all. The airline does not provide food or beverages in the lounge, you have to pay for everything. I've never seen this in 29 years of business travel. The staff are completely apathetic, they simply ignore customers when approached with a problem. They just shrug their shoulders and walked away. They do not have dedicated internet service for the lounge and the airport internet service is abysmal at best. It took me over 2 hours just to connect my phone to the Wi-Fi. I have been unable to connect my laptop. I have had better service in far less developed countries. You mention this to the staff they shrug their shoulders and walk away. The only so-called business class Lounge that came close to being this bad was in Shenyang China in the mid-1990s. I'm sure that has improved.

I wouldn't really call it a business class lounge. Its basically just seats in a bar that are reserved for Business Class passengers. There are no free refreshments and although there are a wide range of drinks and snacks available they are all quite expensive.

Somewhat small this is the single airport lounge at Almaty Airport what I believe services all airlines. Seating areas ok small bar and food counter to one side. I could not get my laptop to access any wifi. There was a computer station with internet access at one end of the room but the airport staff seemed to be using this when I visited! A small bathroom area 2 Tv's but not much else.
A new lounge for domestic flights. Great design, great selection of food. Rest areas and sleeping rooms. There are massage chairs. USB charging near each seat.

Kandinskiy Lounge is one of the best Lounges in Sheremetyevo Airport, and in Moscow. It is situated in Sheremetyevo Terminal B-the brand-new Terminal only for Domestic flights of Aeroflot, terminal B has 2 lounges, one of them is Rublyov Lounge (only for Aeroflots Business class passengers and SkyTeam Elite Members), and another one is Kandinskiy Lounge (for Aeroflots Business class passengers and SkyTeam Elite Members and PriorityPass members) I've visited Kandinskiy by PriorityPass card, the Lounge is big, for 450-500 passengers, it has sleeping rooms, buffet, relax-zone and conference rooms. It is beautiful and comfortable, with friendly staff and souveniers. Food is good, beautiful views to the airfield and comfortable seating.

The lounge is located on the right part of the terminal F, it is quite old, it has 3 business lounges and one VIP, business are The Classic Lounge, MasterCard Lounge (only for MasterCard holders, and All Star Lounge, Classic and All Star, are the only lounges for business class passengers of Aeroflot. The main problem is, that in the evening, all direct flights to China departs, all aircrafts are big (B777-300ER, A330-300) So the lounge at this time very crowded, you can wait for 30 minutes until they have a place for you, also they say that at Classic Lounge they have the same problem. But anyway, the lounge food-court has some snacks, little bit hot dishes and beverages. To sum up, to have a great place to seat, you mast come little bit earlier then 2 hours.

One of the Aeroflot's business lounge at Sheremetyevo airport (SVO) was overcrowded. Passengers were laying on the sofas with shoes on. Selection of food and beverages is very limited and it does not look tasty at all. I could allow myself only to drink water there.

Aeroflot lounge Moscow Sheremetyevo Terminal D. To start the toilets are clean, seating is okay not that many for the amount of people that I saw, but you will find one. Power for computers, not that much but again you will find one. Honest selection of drinks and food, many of the food is processed food but the soup was nice and good. The wines are also good. A huge selection of sweets. WiFi works but is a headache. You need to give the phone number then if you have a Mobile and a computer will not work, etc. They can do better with the WiFi, but it is what it is. The lounge is also clean.

This Aeroflot lounge in terminal D, SVO, Moscow, is much better than lounges in New York's JFK I visited before. Less crowded, with a good choice of salads, snacks, hot meals, including soups, and desserts. The lounge is big with different areas to choose from. Overall it's very good.

Another lounge was full and we were asked to go to Gallery Lounge. It is a spacious 2 floor lounge, located airside - 2nd Floor, opposite Gate 32. As a Priority Pass passenger we were invited at the 2 floor. There is a large bufet with cheese, meat, yogurt, hot foods, snaks, soft and alcoholic drinks, including non alcoholic beer, coffee and a wide selection of teas. Food was tasty and fresh. Close to bathroom there are very comfortable seats. Bathroom was clean and well maintained. There is not a dedicated wifi for lounge, only the general airport wifi - fast, free and unlimited. However LinkedIn is not available in Russia. Staff was helpful, announcing via microphone every gate open for lounge guests'. We stayed in the lounge about 2,5 hours. The atmosphere was mixed. From "business style" lounge with decent and educated guests to "railways station" style people yelling and speaking extremely loud. Overall good impression.

I was allowed to use this lounge as Elite Plus member of Aeroflot Bonus program (Sky Team alliance airline). It's on the second floor and not very close to the gates but same for other lounges in Terminal 1. The lounge is quite spacious and overall makes a good impression. There's no special zones for sleeping. The food was quite testy and pasta was warm and really delicious. Not a very big choice of alcohol drinks but there are all kinds of spirits, Italian Prosecco, average wines. But in Dubai airport it's not easy to find good choice of alcohol in bars even if you pay.

Moscows Shermetjevo SVO has several lounges. My flight to Beijing went from the old terminal, hence my lounge was there. It looks impressive, from the second last century. But the selection of beverages and food is disappointing. The ground staff wasn't really helpful and their language skills could have been better. WLan is available, nowadays for free. Foreign newspapers where available as bad copies.

I Flew with Aeroflot London to Bangkok via Moscow in Business and thus had access to two lounge options in Sheremetyevo international Area, I chose Jazz as it looked more modern. The lounge had a large selection of food as I was there in the evening there was a la carte selection or dinner to order as well as snacks that were out out. The layover was not that long so I did not have time to check but the receptionist stated that they have showers. Wifi was fast, seats were comfortable and there were even a couple of snooze areas. The place was pretty clean but the staff could be a little more friendly. Overall somewhat like the old BA lounge in T5.

Visited as connecting passenger from Greece to Korea. The lounge was extremely busy and internet accessibility the worst I have encountered in an airline lounge. Food was acceptable although frequently mislabelled. Hot drinks were plentiful and quite okay, and there was a fair selection of alcohol. No showers, washrooms average.

Air France lounge spacious without being nice, just practical. Breakfast consisted of croissants and some other food. On the Asian side different filled pastries and instant noodles. Plenty of fresh fruit also available. Alcohol and wine bar fully stocked already, even if it was 8 am and serve yourself as much as you want. Fine relaxing lounge with all you can wish for.

The Galaxy Lounge at the E-Terminal looks a bit dated. It is a large and very open space. Enough different seating arrangements. A separate space for computers. And a food and drinks counter. Due to the open space one can hear almost every conversation. To make things worse they play loud music. Food is ok. Enough choice but not much of a display. Drinks are also ok. Enough choice. Alcohol you have to ask (except beer). WiFi speed is great and free. Shower room is a strange affair. You get a 'space towel' and some slippers. If you don't bring your own shampoo and/or soap, you are left with only water to wash yourself. The towel is a big paper cloth you can dispose of after the shower. Slippers have the same design. You don't enter this space for a spa treatment, but it does refresh. If you have to sit here for a long time this will not be a relaxing experience.

Small lounge with not enough comfortable chairs. No english or international reading material. Wifi works well. Food of very poor quality and boring. Was surely not impressed by this lounge but have visited worse in my life.

Aeroflot Galaxy Galaktica Sirius Classic Jazz and Blues Lounges in SVO. Access while travelling on business require invitation card from transfer desk but happened smoothly. In SVO you are semi-free to choose which of 4-5 Aeroflot lounges you want access to. I prefer the newest Galaktica (Galaxy) in terminal E Classic in terminal F and Blues in terminal D. Other lounges like Sirius in E and Jazz in D (a parallel or copy of Blues) must wait for another time (Sirius is a special lounge at terminal E - only for disabled – it is virtually a requirement for entering!). Drinks plenty – up to medium quality. Lounge hopping not always possible - even by use of SKY-gold card. Lounges prefer you stay at the lounges at departing gate but it depends on staff. Galaktika is the best of all of those I know big and smart design and colourful orange furniture with good business and smoking sections – further it has views to and outside airport. Other lounges do not have views. Views are much better from the commercial areas outside the lounges. Food is bread oriented but heating of croissants sandwiches bread rolls are possible. Some lounges (at least Classic) sells quality hot food at an additional price like a restaurant within the lobby. Showers fine but scarce.

The reception turned me back to a transit desk for lounge invitation. Then I was turned again to a transit lounge nearby where I finally got the invitation printed out. Due to transit I was entitled to a lounge in terminal F (Sheremyetevo Classic) but remembering its poor dungeon-like conditions I sneaked into the Galactica - offering more space and windows. Food - only cold snacks (potato chips crackers peanuts bread with cheese bread with some sausage etc). Drinks - range of soft drinks and alcohol. Free WiFi. Lounge quite clean toilets inside shower room and smoking room under construction. On the way to the gate entered Sheremyetevo Classic lounge to find it has been refurbished - larger (but still much smaller than Galactica) completely renovated. Food the same in both lounges but I've noticed champagne available in the Classic. A smoking room inside available.

Aeroflot used CX's The Wing lounge before so I was worried a bit about the new one. The Traveller's is not as airy and spacy as The Wing however well equipped and nice too. Many warm options for breakfast and free access to the alcohol bar. Just 2 showers (so you have to wait for your turn) maintained well and clean. Overall okay experience with good food and drinks.

A throwback to the old Soviet era - except that they have 3 PCs with Internet access. The food is pretty bad: couple of bread rolls - but where is the margarine? Newspapers and magazines are all Russian - yet this lounge is for all Skyteam airlines. Bathrooms aren't clean. Sofas are pretty comfortable but there's no window view. A couple of television sets that are running the same damn Russian TV channel.

Oh dear nothing changes here! Not allowed into the lounge until 2 hours before flight despite having a 5 hour layover. Once in the lounge you wonder what the wait was for. No natural light lounge arrange in 3 areas all rather dark and at peak times impossible to find a seat. The food is poor to say the least and staff at beverage counter seem reluctant to offer drinks! There are some PCs at one end but very variable connection and not very useful. Small toilet area no showers - all in all a disgrace for a SkyTeam member airline.

The Air China lounge at Beijing Capital International Airport is really terrible. I think it is the worst lounge of Air China. The food is terrible and the dishes are hard to swallow. Fortunately, there are more choices of drinks and snacks. The lounge is very crowded at noon and in the evening, and there are many people, which is not a good experience.

Air China Business Class Lounge at Beijing Airport, Terminal 3. I had a 4 hour layover here, and have to agree with other reviews - it was not a very pleasant experience. Busy, noisy and untidy. The seating was comfortable, and towards the evening, it got quieter, so was able to move to a less busy area. For an airline so big, the lounge capacity was so small. The dining was disappointing. Apart from a very small section of Chinese Dim Sum, the other food choices, it looked unappetising. There was plenty of beer, a few wine bottles, but no spirits to be seen. The toilets were a disgrace. I could not believe the toilet doors were so bad, there was about a centimetre gap between rickety old doors, and you could see the person inside the cubicle! The urinals were not clean. No shower facilities either. On my return flight, I had a 8 hour layover. I chose the Air China Transit Lounge (which you can book online). Even at 6.30 in the morning it was fairly crowded, with weary looking passengers huddled up trying to get some rest. I had requested a 'sleeping room', and got one almost immediately. But entering it I did not feel comfortable. There was a crushed pillow and duvet on the bed, and felt that someone had just moved out and the bed linen had not been changed. It was an old worn out room, with TV (local channels), table, stool and wash basin, with no towels or toiletries, but with a hair drier. I was tired but just could not lie on this bed and moved to the lounge area and rested there. Taking a shower, was not an enjoyable experience either. The floor was wet, bin had not been emptied, and the wash basin had not been cleaned either. The towel floor mat was dirty, but forced myself to shower just to freshen up. Soon after, I left that lounge and went back to the regular Business Class Lounge. There was hardly any room, as it was nearly lunch time. Crowds had arrived with a near stampede for food! Tables had to be shared. Leftovers were not cleared. Seating was either occupied or used for dumping hand luggage. Fed up, after a quick coffee, I left the lounge and found a quiet seating area far away, nearer my gate, and waited for my flight back. Both these lounges are badly maintained.

Shabby lounge, overcrowded, few sockets, many of them worn out so that plugs fall off, very limited food choice, wine hidden away at the far end of the lounge, miserable internet, reception people who never were told that smiling is not a crime.

Visited the Le Saigonnais lounge on 3rd January 2019 in the middle of night prior embarking Air China to Peking departing 05:40. Newly opened 3rd Party Lounge (run by SASCO) in SGN Saigon International Terminal, T2. Opened only for a month and a bit hard to find as the signboards are not updated. Nice decor, inspirational, clean and good stocking of hot foods – found about 7 different kinds. Drinks offered are mainly local. No champagne or sparkling but 4 red-wines present of which only one is drinkable (ex. Chile). 3 brands local beers and loads of soft drinks. This is a better and bigger than the Rose lounge hitherto offered. A nice surprise with OK facilities, showers, and superfast WiFi, and nice tarmac views overlooking the aircraft.

United Airlines uses the Air China lounge at T3, Beijing Capital Airport. First of all the views are on the tarmac which are pretty nice and it’s quiet. However the breakfast buffet closes after 1000 AM so as we arrived afterwards there was just some dumplings and packaged crackers and other snacks and there was no coffee, only tea. There was a bar but no bartender and the WiFi did not connect. We found a little area like a gazebo so that was good but overall this lounge wasn’t impressive.
The worst lounge I have ever visited. There was no coffee and breakfast selection was simply awful. It is clearly not up to standards one would expect as a member of Star Alliance

Very disappointing very tiny lounge at Tianjin Airport. Poor Wi-Fi connection. Poor food and beverage offer and   no bathrooms. Responsible person did not care and just occupied by her smart phone. It is better to sit outside at the large waiting halls.

I admit that i was a little bit disappointed. I was expecting more food choice with higher quality, like I am used to from other Asian airlines. The lounge was spacious (two levels) with very comfortable furniture. The overall design is fair and not exceptional.

This lounge at Chengdu Airport is a comfortable venue with good service and a pleasant atmosphere. It has a limited selection of both hard and soft drinks, but serves hot Chinese food throughout the day. It also offers some reading material in English. A nice touch that has recently been added is a corner of the lounge reserved for traditional Chinese tea service - complete with classic Chinese table and chairs and a server wearing a qi pao all of which adds a touch of class to the ambiance of the lounge.

Dirty, under-cared facility at one of world's busiest airport. While transfer took surprisingly short, I got plenty of time to wait for my connecting flight to Frankfurt from Tokyo. I thought spending 3hrs at Air China's business lounge would be a good option; but I was unfortunately wrong. Carpets, sofas and reclining sofas were all dirty. Food did not taste like one. Broken display monitor, reclining sofas outside the lounge area (e.g. in front of Gate E2) are a lot cleaner and comfy that those for priority passengers.

Air China business class lounge at PEK terminal 3 for business class and Star gold passengers. Sofas are comfy enough, and plenty of them. Food can be improved, especially during midnight hours. They only have soft drinks, crackers, sieuw may and meat buns. No beer, no western wine and alcohol. Staff's English can be improved as well. A couple of non-Chinese speaking passengers took ages before they clearly understood instructions how to connect their phones to WiFi, explanations that the bar is self-service etc.

After a 5 hour flight and a 7 hour stop over transfer, and another 9 hour flight ahead we were looking foward to our Hotel Room and Lounge Access to relax and have a clean up. So far Air China have provided us with the worst services I have even seen. The lounge - old, hot, dirty, food of a "bag of nuts". The Hotel Room - we had booked and paid for. We were told no, they are full? (we didn't see anyone). No refund, no apologies just sent to the "Lounge". Air China have a lot of work to do with the total package, with a lack of service and blunt rude people. As others have done, get out find a cafe have a drink. We stink, will be awake for 28 hours with a 3 hour drive home on top.

The furniture was quite old in this Air China lounge and it was impossible to have cold water or even ice. There food was not fresh and there were only few low calories or vegeterian options for food. In terms of privacy as well, there was no proper space to work or to rest in silence. It took me severaly minutes to log in and the instructions were not very clear (passport had to be scanned, which was not mentioned by the receptionist). The staff was very cold, almost robotic.

This Air China lounge at Beijing Airport Terminal 3 was one of the most terrible lounges at a major airport I've been to. Dirty appearance, food inedible, staff with virtually no English skills, and either broken interior or unavailable services (WiFi didn't work, showers broken, beds for a nap better not to lie on if you don't want to get some illness). Speaking about design, it is non-existent. Everything has got the charm of a cheap Chinese restaurant. This lounge is a disgrace for the Star alliance and an insult to every passenger actually paying for Business Class service. Air China: don't worry about losing your face - you do every day with services like this lounge.

Visited this Air China lounge at Beijing Capital Airport hoping to freshen up with a shower and grab a meal. When I arrived they were not serving food since dinner only goes from 6pm to 8pm! I have never struck a lounge that didn't have food service going at all times. They said to wait till 10pm when they would serve a supper snack menu. I then tried to have a shower but found that both were out of order. Tried to connect to the lounge wifi, but found the lounge does not have wifi, the staff suggest using the airport free wifi. Airport free wifi is very difficult to connect to, very slow and being a public wifi in China many sites are blocked. Wine was undrinkable Chinese wine. The entire lounge was in a state of disrepair and in need of a refresh. eg. the drinks fridges were all broken so all drinks were room temperature. Power plugs hanging out of the walls in the bathrooms, etc. They did have good chairs, bottled water, power plugs, and a couple of sleeping pods.

Visited this lounge on 28 January for 6 hours. Some minor shortcomings which are lack of proper repairs of faults in toilets, hangers, showers. The tea-room is a nice touch of Chinese culture with a tea-lady serving during afternoons. Food options are mainly Chinese dishes. Alcoholic drink options very limited (Chinese wines and beer). Seating nice and lounge is spacious though not huge. Good view over airport lanes. The lounge is open with the rest of the terminal only separated by a 1.3 meter tall glass-fender giving a nice air. The ceiling is an architectonic beauty, which can be studied from the beds in the 5 sleeping rooms which also are open. WiFi requires passport scanning.

The international lounge in T3 was absolutely packed, with very few chairs available. The choice and quality of food and beverages was shockingly bad: all packaged cheap products and nothing fresh. No international newspaper or magazine whatsoever. Long queue for the toilets (3 in total in the men's toilet, to serve about 100/150 people in the lounge). Limited and incorrect information provided by the staff. A very bad lounge even by third-world standards.

Air China International Business Lounge at Beijing Capital Airport Terminal 3 has for a few weeks been dry! The bar is closed, and not even beer any more in the coolers! Which is weird as you still can buy a can of Tsingtau beer at all the automatic machines around the terminal for 6 RMB. So if you are on transit and need to keep you level, better prepare some small change of RMB. And all the earlier bad reviews of the lounge here match my opinions.

This Air China lounge at Beijing Airport Terminal 3 is always uncomfortably hot and stuffy. The washrooms are limited and smelly. The food is terrible and not to be gambled with. Cold drinks simply don't exist as the small fridges do not work. Leather seats are comfortable but the rest of the lounge has a grimy look. I peeked into one of the sleeper pods and would not dare even enter it. Announcements are tough to understand. I use this lounge 4 or 5 times a year and have before left it to find a cooler spot and get cold drinks at one of the cafes in the main terminal. This Air China lounge is quite possibly the worst business class lounge throughout Star Alliance.

This Air China lounge at Shanghai Pudong Airport (used on a Thai Airways flight) is one of the worst airline lounges for a business class traveller. The food served lounge was so unappealing and the area messy. The whole upstair lounge looks like a canteen. Staff never greet you and never replenished food when empty. Coffee is lousy and bad quality. Men's toilet is dirty with wet floor and never cleaned. It seemed some people never know how to use urinals and the staff also do not bother to clean it.

This lounge has not been updated or improved since it opened in 2008. As other reviews have said, it is dirty! The carpets have a greasy and dirty look, chairs are worn out and beware the fact that down the side of cushions is filth, crumbs etc. Staff have zero charisma, and very limited English language skills, their duty to check entry pass and nothing else. Inside the lounge, it is stifling and uncomfortable. Asked to take a shower and one look inside the filthy broom cupboard type facility and I abandoned that. Food available at lunchtime is best described as "slop". Not a westerner in sight who was risking a taste or consequence of it. Drink chillers (old small fridges) do not work, and any supposed cold drink is warm - water, coke, you name it. Guy cleaning the lavatories hangs around waiting for customers to tip him, not sure why since the toilets are dirty and unpleasant odours. To echo all others here, how Air China remains in Star Alliance is a complete mystery, and one can only assume that nobody from Star Alliance has visited this lounge in years. It is simply awful.

This Domestic first/business class lounge is one of the worst ones that I have ever visited. It is not clean and has been managed extremely poorly. There is no any fridge in the lounge being able to provide code drink all year long. Those tiny little type of fridges are obviously not adequate for airport lounge, but have been there for years. It seems like that Air China does not care or know how to operate a lounge for Star Alliance customer with the lowest acceptable standard as a Start Alliane member. As far as a lot frquent fliers concern, Air China is not deserving to be called Star alliance member.

Domestic lounge in Terminal 3 just gets worse. It hasn't changed in 2-3 years and can only guess that Air China has financial problems. I arrived at 7.30pm, all food counters were stripped bare, and the only offering (apart from the endless 10cent cup noodle) was some strange breads and pastries that had been there for more than 12 hours. Staff at reception counter could not speak or understand a word of English and it was a case of sign language to even check boarding time. Lounge is fundamentally dirty - they have cleaners around (this is China!) but all they do is push the dirt from one side to another. In the gents washroom I watched the cleaner wipe the rim of a toilet pan and then use the same cloth to wipe down the basin area! Whatever you hear or see about China, their health and hygiene is simply disgusting. The lounge was hot and humid, and after 10 minutes I decided the main terminal area was better. Shame on Star Alliance for permitting Air China to remain part of the alliance. By the way, I'm a Platinum member with Air China, and the level of priority is zero!
Lounge in Beijing which we used twice (London to Sydney return) was fine but did not have enough toilets and showers.

We used this on our inbound flight from New York and clearly we arrived at peak time. Not a seat to be found and the lounge was generally dirty and poorly managed. Staff on front-desk were more like guards than customer service staff. They scowled did not look up to greet us and were a very poor impression of Chinese service - in fact they were just rude. Food (as commented here already) was like a poor quality works canteen and mushy food that was not even hot. I looked at shower after a 50 minute wait and decided against using it. How does Star Alliance allow Air China to stay in with such low standard facilities? Never again on Air China.

At peak times the lounge gets very crowded and on hot sunny days you should avoid this lounge - it is stifling and the aircon never works properly. Staff on reception can be very friendly or very rude and inattentive - there does not seem to be an area in the middle. You can no longer get a fresh coffee and they removed the coffee machine that was installed for a few months and this is first class! The food is canteen type and rather greasy chinese food and probably best to wait for your flight to get a bite to eat. The toilets are kept clean by attendant that waits for you to tip him when you go in! The shower is tiny smells of drains and is best avoided. Furniture is tired and quite grubby and generally feel this lounge has continued to get worse and worse in the last 2 years. Avoid and go downstairs to Pizza Hut or Costa/Starbucks coffee for a nicer experience.

The lounge is spacious with leather seats in groups of two. There are some dining tables in the area of the food. The food was mixed Chinese with a choice of dumplings noodles and stir fries. Sandwiches and other packaged snacks. Beer and wine is available but wine selection is limited. There are several sleeping pods available together with small shower facility.

My wife and I visited the Air China First Class Lounge at PEK on October 8. We were flying United Global First to Washington DC IAD. We had 3 hours to departure at 6:20PM. When we entered the Lounge we found it to be very warm actually hot. It is a very large lounge and there were very few people there at the time. There were about 6 people working the front desk but I never saw any Air China Agents working in the lounge. The seating was leather chairs fairly comfortable with a small table between seating for 2. There was hot food available but it didn't appeal to Western tast mostly rice and soup We passed on the food. Some snacks the kind you scoop out of a jar with a spoon. The guy who was there before us had his hand in all the jars without the spoon so we passed on them also. Next we tried the bar. Self service with very little selection. I only saw Chinese beer in the cooler about 10 bottles of the usual liquor and mixers in the cooler. There was ice but it is not a good idea to use ice unless you know it was purified. No way to know that no one to ask. There were two bottles of Chinese "Great Wall" brand. One was dry red and the other was a cab. We tried the cab then switched to club soda. Star Alliance airlines should inspect this lounge and demand that Air China make necessary changes to bring it up to international standards. If you are going to use the Air China Beijing Lounge don't expect too much.

Quite spacious and busy lounge with nearly all facilities a passenger can demand. Luggage storage computer stations comfortable resting area hot food beverages separate sleeping/shower/TV rooms and digital flight information board. Since it is located on 4F you can also have a good view of the T3 terminal. There is another new Air China domestic lounge located in 2F no hot food is on offer but the lounge is much quieter.

Was there on a stop-over from Singapore to Beijing. Very nicely decorated lounge. Comfortable seats. TV screen with Chinese channel. Separate smoking room. Not a quiet lounge all announcements with flight information given on the speakers (since this a busy airport there are continuous and very loud announcements). Very poor food choice (one soup 2 oriental dishes and some breads and instant noodles) for food. No wine only drinks in cans (including some beers) coffee tea. Staff with no smiles at all tables only cleaned after persons leave (I was there for 4 hours). No real complaints apart from the noise.

Very nice and quiet when we were there. Big issue is that warm food is only served from 06.30 till 09.00 and 11.00 till 19.30. Too bad if your flight is at 23.30. Some snacks available and limited beverages (3 choices of tea) coffee coke fanta beer juices one choice of red wine/white wine. If you want something hot there are instant noodles. Free wireless okay and fast. No TV screens no announcements of flights. Good staff service though.

Its okay but does not come close to First class lounges of other Asian airlines (eg Cathay Thai ANA etc). The staff here were miserable - no smiles no chat ... no nothing really except to check the boarding pass / invitation as if it was a top secret document. Hot food was available at one end of the lounge but this is geared totally to Chinese style and little else on offer. The washrooms have TV on the wall and annoying cleaning staff that stand around expecting you to give them a tip !? Certainly not a memorable lounge and had expected better from Air China since this is really quite new in 2007?

Nice Lounge but when you ask for Champagne nobody knows what is champagne! The white and red wine was around 2-3 weeks open and not drinkable. No food - only peanuts and other nuts. People are very polite but do not understand English. Internet WLAN works . Only small smoking room - no smoking lounge.

Very basic lounge with little by way of food selection - mostly packaged food stuffs - and very limited beverages. Even the Chinese Tea is of poor quality. Reading materials even in Chinese language are very limited and no internet access. However it does have a toilet with a heated seat! Because the airport has an open departure gate system probably few advantages spending time in this lounge.

In general this is a very dreary lounge. Very crowded on all of my visits making it difficult to find a seat. Rather dark with no natural light. Snack and beverage is all right but don’t expect anything filling. Access to an internet connection is nearly impossible with people waiting turns. Smoking section is enclosed but very small and the smoke comes back into the large room. Not pleasant for either the smokers (no room) or the non-smokers. In general I have found sitting at the gate to be happier experience.

Lounge had comfortable lounge chairs. Food was also adequate with hot and cold dishes. sandwiches and rolls in the fridge along with Beer and soft drink. Spirits also available. Not a large room however a good place to get away from the masses unless you needed a smoke.

Air China's international business class lounge is rudimentary at best. There are separate lounges for first & business class passengers. There is complimentary internet access but this tended to be very slow. Open bar & light snacks are available. The room does not seem to be staffed adequately to handle the large number of passengers using the facilities as garbage & dirty dishes lingered for considerable amounts of time. Seating is very primitive arranged in rows of seats like a regular waiting room.

Overcrowded to the extent it was most difficult to find a seat. The choice of drinks was decent and the staff so so. Sad to see that in Africa, so little attention is given to lounges, so important considering the number of late flights!

The computer says no. There is a famous scene in the British series "Little Britain" called "the computer says no". Captures perfectly the AENA lounge experience when they don't let you enter at 10.45am for a 3pm flight cos of their 4hr rule when it's only 1/3 full. The only thing they are good at is saying no reflecting an absence of knowledge of what the word reasonable means AENA that operates this VIP lounge and many others gets away with the most outrageously bad service.

Squalor. I find it difficult to understand how AENA that operates this lounge gets away with such an abysmal service standard. Food was disgusting - the small amount that was available. Glassware was filthy as was the general state of the place.

This is the worst lounge I've encountered in my life. Absence of dining during afternoon and evening. Only vile processed cheese and cold meat. Staff excel in being unfriendly and useless. In fairness to Air Europa they do not manage this lounge, AENA does which owns most Spanish airports.

The front facing staff show little evidence of ability in customer service. They are unfriendly and become belligerent in an immature manner when feedback is given about the poor facilities at this lounge. An example is a request to use the one shower. They tell you it is occupied and expect you go find the cleaners every 20 minutes to go see if it is free. A suggestion that they might have a waiting list and let passengers know when it is free was met with dismissive and I couldn't careless reactions. This airport has a long way to go to understand how to do customer service. If you want sarcasm and infantile behaviour, you can talk to your kids I guess. But not what you want here.

This marks the first time I have left a lounge to seek peace, quiet, and electrical outlets in the main concourse. This lounge is entirely enclosed without a single window. At 09:30 it was overcrowded. My first choice was sparkling wine - no luck. Second choice was a rum and coke - no rum. The food options were meager, nothing warm and little that was appetizing. The escalator up to the lounge was out of service, and there was no elevator. How does the EU permit a public facility that is handicap inaccessible? The only saving grace to an otherwise dismal experience was the pleasant, good humor of the entrance staff. This lounge is a shameful offering, particularly in comparison to the Sala Montvale in the international gates of MXP.

Lisbon Blue Lounge. It is not a bad lounge, since we can’t find too much people here sometimes is the better choice in all airport for different reasons. The Ana Lounge is sometimes full of people and the food is almost the same in the Blue Lounge. Bathroom of the Blue lounge is 3 times bigger than the TAP lounge and the TAP lounge have at least 10 times more passengers. Wi-Fi works fine. Chairs and sofas available, power for computers is also available. The food is the usual fast food, etc, but the lounge is quiet and in my opinion for resting and Wi-Fi the best at this point in time in Lisbon. In 5 days I was twice on this lounge one by the Aeroflot and the other one by air Europe. Both of the times I was received with a smile and a warm welcome.

Amazing quality on food! Organic choices, wines, drinks, the food choice is just wow, they even have posters saying only to eat here, not allowed to take to the Plain (or home). Nice chairs, plenty of space to walk, to work, many Power connections to computers. Wi-Fi works but they can improve a little, space for improvement on the Wi-Fi .Toilets are clean and functional. Reception people can be better, they need some training, all the times I come here is a line (3 or 4 minutes) maybe I come in the wrong hour.

The lounge location is not easily known immediately because it is on the corner and on a different floor with the departure area. The lounge attendant asked me whether I was a business class passenger or not, because the lounge was only for business class passengers; then I replied that I am an economy class passenger but a priority member; then the officer asked for my membership card. It should be without questioning that, the officers already know from the boarding pas I give there is a sign of membership priority. For hot drinks like coffee and tea, have to ask for hot water from a bartender-type officer, it feels more comfortable if you can directly access your own hot water.
Terminal 2 Air Europa lounge. Good food, WIFI also good. Good drinks and service, a lot of choice. Is a good lounge. Reception also kind Fresh food, and a lot of fruit, wine choices beers etc.

I have in the past been scathing of Air New Zealand. However, as time has passed the bar has been raised so significantly I cannot fault the lounge at Auckland airport. The standard of food and what is on offer given my experiences in other airports over the last 10 weeks is excellent. I can recommend the Air NZ lounge

The lounge is very spacious and the colours give a sense of calm. The staff are most friendly, chatty and  professional. The food choice for breakfast at this stage isn't diverse, but the effort they make into fresh-cooked foods e.g. omelettes is excellent. The barista made excellent coffee, almost as good as the coffees from cafes. The seat highlight is the outside garden with swinging seats with views.

I was excited to finally visit this Lounge but how disappointing it was. It looks like a space temporary being rented out before a full renovation. It lacks so much detail of what a proper lounge should be, please take some advice from Cathay or Qantas. The lounge team were great, pleasant to be around and kept the space very clean. Plenty of beverage options including alcohol and coffee but when it came to the food, it was absolutely terrible. Let me just say, serving stale bread should never be allowed. Until they update this lounge and have more fresh catering, I probably won't make a second visit.

I found this lounge very nice. There was a very nice all-you-can-eat buffet style buffet. As it was morning, the breakfast selection was available.  I went for some scrambled eggs and a strawberry smoothie, there was also a kids play place, if your traveling with a child and tables in there if you want to eat while watching your kid. There is also a nice work section, and a relax place closed off for business class passengers only. This lounge is also a Star Alliance Gold lounge, but is free with business class.

My wife and I wanted to use the Business Class Lounge at the Auckland Airport while on transit from Los Angeles to Melbourne. Initially, I was questioned on the validity of my Maple Leaf Worldwide Lounge card as the person in the entrance was not used to see this card before. She checked with the manager inside and he allowed us to enter "this time". In fact, this card should have been allowed our access to the lounge in any of the Star Alliance Business Class Lounges. I would like to suggest that the Maple Leaf Lounge Service should contact all Star Alliance partners. When we went inside, it was a very nice lounge with good seats and good food and beverages. The service people were very friendly and attentive. Except for the fuss at the entrance, I would visit the lounge again.

I was astonished at how poor the seating was in what passes as a Koru lounge in regional departures the seating outside the lounge was far superior Air New Zealand only seem interested in taking money and giving little in return. I have added a photo of the only seating available.

A very upscale offering from Air New Zealand. I find the Lounge a great space to relax with great natural lighting from the tarmac. The Lounge had a dedicated bar which also offered barista coffee. The food selection was decent but slightly limited in terms on options, Eg. vegetarian. The staff were attentive, consistently keeping the space clean and the washrooms were well maintained. Overall, the Sydney location was of standard though I think the Lounge in Auckland is much better.
Large and busy, but well-tended with ample offerings and good quality of food and drink. I was a bit surprised that it was a 15-minute walk to the gate.

What a great experience. We were greeted and had the lounge shown to us. We had almost 10 hrs before our departing flight so we settled in for the wait. The seats were very comfortable and the food was great. Later that evening, a customer relations specialist told us to come out to the main lounge area. She had a special show for us and the rest of the people in the lounge. The Whangara Mai Tawhiti performers were in the lounge waiting to fly to Taiwan to perform there. She convinced them to perform 2 songs for us. It was the greatest entertainment anyone could have asked. They performed traditional New Zealand Maori songs. Everyone in the lounge applauded them afterwords and were honored that they performed for us.

Pathetic lounge: Lukewarm, tasteless food - just like in their Melbourne Lounge I hope I won’t get gastro from the cooled chicken dish. No bottled non-alcoholic drinks, only alcoholic stuff. Non-alcoholic drinks only come from a mixer from the basin. Business class product on the plane is very inferior compared to QF, SQ, JAL, Emirates, Vietnam, Cathay and really any other airline with a flat business seat.

Worst customer service ever, two rude attendants at Queenstown Air New Zealand Lounge would not allow entry as my son was 13 and that therefore was an "adult" and I could only take 1 adult in under my membership. I explained as a Virgin platinum member this wasn't an issue in a Virgin lounge, but was told "well too bad, this is Air New Zealand and we are different" - arms crossed and grumpy faced added for extra emphasis. When I asked if there was any chance of paying for entry for my "adult" 13 year old son, was told "No!, we dont do that here!" additional grumpier face and crossed arms even tighter in case we misunderstood. Thanks for the hospitality, glad this alliance with Virgin is ending soon based on that example of Air New Zealand customer service.
