First time visit to an Air New Zealand Lounge, and it was their flagship location. A great space filled with amazing decor and plenty of seating including a covered outdoor area. Breakfast was being served during my visit with a chef cooking fresh food and barista made coffee was on offer. A bar was also available, but I don't think it opens until lunch time. Lounge staff were very present, consistently keeping the space clean. Overall, definitely a Lounge worth visiting.

On a recent Business Class flight to LAX I had the "displeasure" of using the Air New Zealand Lounge at Auckland International Airport. These lounges have become horribly overcrowded, probably because the lounges are full of Koru Members, plus their families, plus frequent flyers from other Star Alliance airlines, so depending on when you arrive, sometimes it is impossible to find a seat. In addition the food options are appalling. Serving a curry before a long flight is not appropriate. Most of the time, I resort to stocking up on cheese and crackers. I'm beginning to avoid this lounge, its turned into a food trough inhabited by people with appalling manners.

Auckland Domestic was originally a nice lounge but now horribly overcrowded with people who rather than grab a quick coffee and a bite to eat have turned it into an extension of their offices. There should be a time limit instigated. Travelers' arriving from a long haul flight and then connecting with a regional flight are getting turned away as the lounge is horribly overcrowded for the reasons I have just stated.

The Christchurch Koru Lounge is a beautiful regional lounge, well appointed with seating and personal spaces. The toilets are clean and well appointed with Antipodes hand wash. The sounds of birds chirping in the toilets is a nice touch. The food and beverage options are plenty. Hot meal choices are a treat and I believe sets the Koru Lounge apart. The occupancy was low and has been in recent visits. Recommend this lounge absolutely.

The Air New Zealand lounges are not what they once were, and this is down to catering. Food choices are becoming very cheap and the quality is low. Although there appears to be a lot of staff, there is not a lot of food options, and the food that is provided is not great. In addition the food choices on the flights are obviously of low quality, with scrambled eggs on offer on a flight ex auckland to Buenos Aires bordering on the 'non-food" category, obviously made from a powdered substance that was was inedible. Air NZ has prioritised profits over customer experience.

Flying back to Singapore at 1210, and went to Air New Zealand lounge for a quick breakfast. Experience was unpleasant. A temporary staff was trying to clear the empty plates from our table. Her accent was so strong that we couldn't quite get what she said when she asked if she could clear our plates. As she was walking away, we asked her if she could clear the empty plates from our table. We got reprimanded by her! I was appalled by her rude response. Disappointed to see that the service level provided by a leading airline business class lounge is so poor. One temporary staff with poor attitude could tarnish the reputation of a good airline.

Visited both the Auckland and Wellington Air New Zealand lounges on my trip to Wellington via Auckland. As a Virgin Australia lounge member was entitled to use the lounge at both these airports. Found a great range of drink on offer. What was a surprise was a great range of food on offer for its domestic services better than virgin's lounge has to offer. Plenty of space though some of the seats need to be upgraded.

Very impressed. From the App coffee ordering to the range of food and drinks. First class and I will recommend to everyone that they join or fly Business to avail of this Air New Zealand lounge. Looking forward to next month so I can enjoy the experience again. Well done Air New Zealand

I was a little underwhelmed at how little there is to offer at this Air New Zealand lounge in Wellington Airport. I have fairly basic needs in a lounge: comfortable and quiet working space and some healthy food. I felt that neither needs were met in this lounge. The lounge is small but not inadequate on the morning I was flying - I was able to find a seat that was quite comfortable with power source nearby. Admittedly the decor was very uninspiring. The layout was poor, and there was little option for privacy. The food selection left me much wanting - the quality was mediocre and the choice was limited. For the national carrier lounge in the capital city's airport, I expected more.

Quite a big lounge to be in such a small airport. Very clean and airy. Good offer of snacks and drinks. Offer of newspapers is very local, but understandable for an airport that serves almost only domestic destinations. Overall a very pleasant experience.

Visited the newly opened Air New Zealand international terminal lounge at Auckland. Judging from the poor reviews of the old lounge the refresh was overdue. The place had a clean modern look and was very appealing to walk into. Good drinks options and OK food selection. The food selection could be improved though, not up to the expected standards really. A good variety of seating selections, although I didn't see any sleeping area.

My partner and I flew All Nippon Airways in December in Premium Economy, entitling us to access this Air New Zealand lounge. It was clean, well patronised and had a very good selection of both food and beverages. The area was spacious, affording good views of the tarmac, with comfortable seating and USB sockets everywhere. The food selection in particular had various varieties of cheese and hors d'oeuvres, some hot meals and desserts and also some lighter snacks. I did not see a great selection at all of reading materials, magazines or newspapers, but it was Boxing Day evening. The boarding announcements were clear, with TV monitors also placed around the lounge. The reception desk at the entrance was staffed with friendly and warm personnel. My only gripe was that there was no dress code in place, and one young man was dressed extremely casually in a singlet and shorts.

Air New Zealand spent how many million on the new flagship AirNZ Lounge at Auckland Airport and didn't bother to organise for food option changes between lunch and dinnertime (same options for both meals - a real drag if you're stuck there for the day) or provide tea leaf and tea pots for a decent - non tea bag brew (coffee and alcohol options galore I might add)! Sure, there are plenty of different kinds of seating options and configurations of space, acoustically the space works pretty well with only really loud phone talkers audible across the tops of chairs and loungers and the staff were great, but come on - what gives with the menu?

Lovely, calm, comfortable Star Alliance lounge, an oasis of peace in LAX. There is a terrace with tables and chairs and a large lounge with soft settees/chairs and small tables, plus upholstered bench seating at raised tables. There are plenty of restrooms. There was a good range of quality food with hot and cold selections, including Chinese/Asian dishes and soup on a separate counter. There was a wide selection of beverages in the food area and a separate bar also serving tea/coffee. The lounge was clean and tidy with staff clearing away used dishes, polishing etc. Airline representatives manned the desk at the entrance to the lounge to help with onward travel administration. The staff were helpful and unobtrusive. All in all, a very pleasant experience.

I spent all day in this lounge on my trip from Canada to Perth and back and got to experience it from early morning to early evening. The showers were clean and well stocked and the food was amazing. There was lots of it and a wide variety of delicious restaurant quality items. Offerings changed at breakfast morning tea lunch afternoon tea and dinner and all were tasty and carefully presented. An onsite barista and an assortment of beverages made a long long layover a little more bearable. The only thing lacking was somewhere to recline and get some sleep.

I found the lounge to be excellent. The showers were clean and tidy seating comfortable. The snack food including gluten-free was excellent and main course was OK. Drinks excellent. The lounge was busy but not too crowded. Probably the only minus is the very loud and frequent airline announcements which make it difficult to speak on the phone.

Overall quite disappointing. The place is crowded dirty (trash on the floor seats are dirty dirty glasses and plates on many tables). The food selection is good if they have any (some offerings have been empty of 30 min now). No clean gasses for soda etc. Looks like they are trying to cut cost wherever possible. Wifi is incredibly slow.

The furniture is very worn but there are spaces to go to get away from the noise down one end. The toilets have a questionable aroma though and need an update with their chipped toilet seats. Food and drink selection is fairly basic but there is usually something to fill a snack gap before the flight. My favourite is the hotdog stand. Cleaning staff are diligent and clear dishes. It's better than sitting on a plastic chair at the gate.

I fly all the time and have been a Koru Club member for years. Things have deteriorated to the point where I feel compelled to write this review. I can only assume that there has been some serious cost cutting going on air Air NZ as the food served seems to mostly consist of whatever is cheap. It is rarely tasty or nutritious. Then theres the actual state of the lounges - they're increasingly threadbare. In fact it has got to the point where the actual airports public areas are often a better alternative. Air New Zealand has really gone downhill quite suddenly. It is a really sad thing to watch.

Thai Airways uses Air NZ's Koru lounge at Melbourne's Tullamarine airport. TG462 departs at 0030 and it is sad to relate that this excellent lounge has very little to offer the business class traveler at the end of the day. Eats such as they were consisted of a very tired salad bowl a few biscuits and a bowl of fruit salad. In the drinks department there was no chardonnay only Marlborough Sav/blanc in the white range and one brand of red (cab/sav). I have used this lounge on several occasions earlier in the day when it is sparkling clean with plenty of food and drinks choices. I got the impression that the staff just wanted the Thai travelers out of the lounge ASAP in order to close the facility for the day. In fact the whole of Tullamarine Airport at that late hour is a shambles. It was a highly disappointing experience.

Crowded and loud noise. School holidays and full of children. Given the very permissive nature of Koru club membership and size of all the Air NZ lounges in NZ this is not a good time to be a business traveller.

The lounge has had a bit of an update which looks heaps better. I had the misfortune to meet the late night staff (duty manager I think) while trying to catch the Aus vs Fra rugby test before my flight to Singapore. A rather unpleasant experience all round. Not to mention the fact that she then got the departure gate staff to grill me when I boarded (as a result of the exchange in the lounge with the business lounge manager). Quite a miserable front to present to traveling public. I try to not fly Air New Zealand when I can help it amongst others for these reasons. unfortunately the Air New Zealand lounge hosts other airline business passengers so I will have to live with the luck of the draw as to who is on duty when I and others pass through AKL.

Initially looked pleasant. Air con did not work properly. When I asked why I was told that they have no control over the temperature that they had complained countless times to the airport facilities management but no improvement. Food was from the buffet reminded me of a British Rail buffet carriage from the 1980's. Upholstery was in a state of complete disrepair dirty and dilapidated. If the airport outside the lounge were not such a nightmare glorified shopping mall I would not have stayed there.

This lounge is small considering the number of airlines and flights it is supposed to accommodate. On my visit there were no seat available and I was forced to find a seat in what must have once been the business centre which is now a run down little room with a bench desk (no computers). Food options are limited but being breakfast there were scrambled eggs and beans available which weren't bad. Not a toaster in sight however. After the Auckland flight was called and those passengers had left the cleaning staff came out with portable vacuums and vacuumed for a good 20min which ensured there was no relaxation at all. This is a frequent occurrence in this lounge. Showers are available.

Air New Zealand use the Faa'a airport lounge in Papeete. Next time I'm not sure I would bother. The food offerings were poor. Actually mostly pre packaged snacks. If you want a beer or soft drink you'll be ok but don't expect any ice for spirits or mixers and don't dare ask a staff member for any ice. Staff are rude and abrupt. At least it's air conditioned unlike the rest of the airport.

Situated in the bowels of the terminal the ambience is gloomy and it looks very tatty and tired. Very uninspiring food (hot or cold) which isn't replenished as frequently as it should be. Dirty/used crockery stayed on tables way too long as staff were scarce. I visit this lounge fairly frequently and it's the same depressing experience. I don't know if it's bad feng shui poor design neglect or cost cutting but compared to other lounges even other Air NZ lounges this isn't one I look forward to visiting.

Very disappointing. No food lounge overcrowded. No plates or cups to get the limited food there was or make a coffee. Barista on duty but woefully out of their depth making 6 coffees. Air NZ staff happier gossiping around the front them providing assistance. No premium feel as overcrowded. Seating configuration forces people together and eliminates private space. Seen better lounges in Asia.

A very nice lounge. Good food and drink selection not especially crowded and good facilities. A few signs indicating where it is would be helpful having said that as it's a star alliance lounge I think?

I used the lounge prior to a flight to Hong Kong very full with several flights leaving. Just 1 staff was trying to keep the place clean. Food selection was dire. The hot option ran out and not replaced for over an hour. Even the cheese and crackers ran out. Leaving only some very unappetising looking muffins and scones with some soup. There was plenty to drink that is always well stocked. The lounge and bathrooms were reasonably clean. I would like to see Air New Zealand up their game with this lounge. For what is charged per annum for a Koru membership a lot more should be provided.

Fantastic lounge. Plenty of seat choices and a large food/beverage area. Staff keep the place impeccably clean –our empty cup/plate was removed what felt like seconds after you finished. We arrived just at the end of the breakfast service but you could still pick up some items off that menu – cheese & bacon muffins were delicious! The soft drinks were dispensed via a soda machine and my only quibble was that the glasses could have been done with being bigger. The ones there were more for adding a mixer to alcohol than someone just having a soft drink. Good free unlimited wifi too once you get the password from the receptionist on the way in.

Very pleasant experience. Good selection of hot and cold dishes. Above average selection of wines and beers. Clean and good shower facilities. Very handy after long haul intercontinental flight from Europe with international onward flight.

Currently at the Sydney Koru Lounge awaiting my flight. The facilities meet all the necessary requirements (incl showers internet ample space) and on par with that of the AirNZ lounge in Auckland. While the 90's styled furniture could use a facelift the quality of the food and service is brilliant.

Dinner menu - reconstituted chicken meat crumbed (called them chicken burgers) and wedges that were rock hard the only hot food on offer. One plate of cold cuts were the cold offering for the first five clients in the lounge - never re filled. My husband suggested Mcdonalds would offer more variety and fresher food. Very disappointing is the only thing we can say.

Visited with our toddler before a long haul flight and were very pleased. Along with a solid food and drink selection and announcements for all Star Alliance flights there is a kids room with plenty of toys crayons paper etc. we were there for an hour and had staff clean away dishes three times. It is basically the exact opposite of United lounges.

It is tired tatty and ill-conceived (where I was sitting I could hear at least two tv's simultaneously and the clatter of pool balls.) I picked up the seat cushion to try to make myself more comfortable - let's just say I don't think anyone has done that in a long time there were a fair few renegade peanuts bits of paper and dust under there. The carpets and fabrics are well past their best (I don't think cushions with holes in them is a good look). It is self service at the bar and buffet. There was very little choice of food and what there was unappetising and the presentation needed tidying up the platters were virtually empty the pancake machine was surrounded by cast-off pancake pieces. It really seemed like just the scraps were left. It appears that if you want to clean your teeth you ask the person on reception!

Air New Zealand use the Eva Air lounge and it is not very good. The lounge itself is big enough but all available space is crammed with tiny chairs. There is very little space to put your things and relax. Food and beverage is limited and toilets are dirty. Don't even think of a shower there isn't one. Good view of the Tarmac though. Found out later that Air New Zealand Business Class passengers can use the United lounge this would have been helpful to know before heading to the Eva lounge. Wished I had avoided this lounge.
Comfortable lounge with plenty of seating and partial views of the tarmac and runways. Good snacks and food on offer and great selection of drinks. Better than their flagship lounge in Auckland.

This lounge is a nightmare. It is leased by Air NZ and they apparently have no options but one is better off not to even go in. The food selection - none. The wine selection ditto. No showers. It is tiny and cramped and unappealing. When we were called for our flight and saw what was on offer in the terminal we wished we had just stayed there.

Originally attractive but now tired and shabby - carpets furniture fabric look like pub furniture in need of replacement. Food better than previous experience. Flight indicator board useless - our flight was 90 minutes late but this never showed. Staff were also unaware of the delay even though the airline had phoned me. Time for a major upgrade.

We really liked this lounge. Arrived about 5pm on a Monday night and initially there was plenty of room. It got busier later but it still had a nice ambience. Plenty of refreshments and snacks. One of the airlines better lounges and streets ahead of Auckland International lounge.

Spent 2 hours there on a Tuesday afternoon and was a pleasant overall experience. It's a good size and divided into several areas with a good variety of seating cell phone-free zone and kids play area. Food selection with a couple of hot choices and the usual cold fare. Trays of fresh baked cookies was a pleasant distraction. The beers and wines were above average. Customer service at the flight desk was friendly and prompt. My only gripe was the slow pace of table cleaning.

A Friday night at LAX it was an awful, lounge over crowded 2 Air NZ flights and A Virgin all departing within an hour no seats and screaming babies. If you pay to fly Business entry to the lounge should be automatic not on a first come basis.

Used this lounge for a Virgin flight and whilst not a bad lounge it's not a great one either and is certainly no Virgin Clubhouse experience. Decent selection of wines and self serve snacks but other than that the options pretty much amount to sitting and looking out of the window. There's just nothing inspiring about it - that said it's certainly more pleasant than the rest of LAX terminal areas.

Quite a comfortable lounge while not very exciting. Good selection of NZ wines cold meats cheese biscuits and bread with salad all self service. Several work stations with a rather slow internet connection. Staff polite and helpful. One grudge is the seating arrangements all of the side window tables are set for four people they always seem to be occupied by just one person who takes over the whole space confining the rest of the passengers to squeeze into the area in the centre. Not the best but certainly much better than having to use the dreadful facilities (or lack of them ) in LA airport

Lost a bit of sparkle over the last visit. Seems like every airline on the planet has use of this lounge. Drab and uninviting. Good drink selection. Food very average. Koru membership comes up for renewal soon-I won't be renewing.
Lots of changes since last visit. Most changes not good. Overcrowded and uninviting. No views of airport at all. All windows frosted!. Never again. Will not be renewing Koru membership.

Etihad are one of a long list of airlines which use this lounge. Inside it was clear that this lounge was in need of an overhaul. The furniture was tired and a bit grubby. Food on offer was pretty poor by Air New Zealand standards and replenishment was sluggish at best. A good selection of beverages and alcoholic and non alcoholic drinks. The lounge has good views across the airport and good internet and wi-fi facilities. Showers nice and the attendants in the toilets and showers were better than in the catering side of the lounge.

I had not used this lounge for a number of years. The lounge is quite large with good seating - it was late at night so there were few passengers. The drink selection was good but the food was pretty bad only some tired cheese and ham on display.

It's looking tired colors that are drab but it has nice view of the runways okay food offering - very simple but better than many other airlines. It has good drink selection and lots of seats. I have used this lounge many times over the past 4 years and it's starting to look more and more tired. I also noticed that when flying United to LAX we had to use this lounge. When I switched the alliance about 2 years ago I started flying Delta and they also use this lounge so do some other airlines. As a consequence it can get rather busy at times and packed. The beauty about Sydney airport is that you might want to venture outside of the lounge and find equally good seating in many restaurants browse shops etc.

The first impression of this lounge is that all the colour has been sucked out of the room. The "colour" palette is of dull mud brown gum-leaf grey and khaki. To add to the disappointment is that the windows are frosted over - no view. A better view is available in the public areas. The food is very basic simple presentation. Think of simple home cooking rather than restaurant quality. Even though New Zealand produces some excellent wines (and a decent selection available) they did nothing to present these in any way to encourage you to drink them or provide information about them. The bottles where just sitting in the fridge along with beers and soft drinks. The bathroom did not appear to have been updated in the past decade and it was not serviced frequently as there were no hand towels available - empty dispensers. Nothing was presented as a premium lounge of an international airline.

Air NZ can be a fickle airline - great today awful tomorrow. Its all about staff. The lounges are old and tired and the food selection has really gone downhill. No (or hardly any) reading material. Staff can make a difference. Empty food spots at the food counter due to slack staff - and they are very slow to keep the lounge clean and tidy.
A spacious comfortable environment friendly staff excellent food and drink plenty of space and seating was plentiful.

The new lounge is superb with excellent staff service. Décor is fresh and modern. Food and beverages fine but the best bit is the shower facilities now available at Raro (good if you've just come in from an inter-island flight or are in transit to LAX ).

Although inconveniently located in the basement of the Melbourne International Terminal and not easy to find on your first visit this lounge is surprisingly comfortable and peaceful. The food is acceptable and there is a good choice of drinks. Staff friendly toilet facilities are excellent. All in all not too a bad place to wait.

lounge_name: AIR NEW ZEALAND BUSINESS CLASS LOUNGE REVIEW
review: We visited the Lounge flying from Brisbane to London and only wanted a cup of tea and a biscuit as we had been served a light meal on the flight from Brisbane. As there were no biscuits on display I asked a senior member of catering staff if I could have a biscuit only to be told that they were serving dinner and I would have to wait until 21.30 when the biscuits would be put out. When I questioned this I was told "If I give you one everyone will want one". Not the sort of service we would expect (or have previously received) from Air New Zealand.
Dated disinterested staff dirty crockery on several tables. Very poor selection of tired looking and unappetising food.

Space is quite tight in this lounge but if you are early enough you can get a seat. There should be a few more tables for those who prefer not to eat from their knees/laps. Welcome varies according to who is on reception. The range of drinks is great showers wonderful computer/internet access. Food is not great. Cold cuts and rolls. Hot offerings appear very late (within 30 minutes of boarding) and are dreadful. Soup is fine. Good range of snacks (chips nuts cookies). There is a big problem however with children - they run around unsupervised often using the pseudo-marble floors as a skating track (and this has happened the three times this year I've been in the lounge). There is no child-free area. They are also given unfettered access to the computers resulting in loud and raucous behaviour. Primarily it is their parents' responsibility but Air NZ should provide areas free from this noise and behaviour for those looking for a different experience.

lounge_name: AIR NEW ZEALAND BUSINESS CLASS LOUNGE REVIEW
review: Our flight left at 10pm the lounge was a zoo with no seating available. Staff were surly and unhelpful - we didn't try the food it looked unappetising. It was more comfortable outside in the general waiting area.

lounge_name: AIR NEW ZEALAND BUSINESS CLASS LOUNGE REVIEW
review: Excellent lounge from comfort to selection of food and beverages complimented by attentive staff. Different relaxation areas for different customers and area where kids are forbidden ensuring every traveller gets that opportunity to relax before the flight! Nice touch! It would be compliment the flight if the same wines in the lounge were served onboard international flights.

lounge_name: AIR NEW ZEALAND BUSINESS CLASS LOUNGE REVIEW
review: Clean tidy and well stocked for the small airport that it is. Plenty of space to relax and is not just one big open plan room giving the feeling of more privacy. Would happily pay to use this lounge although Napier is so efficient you never need to be there for long. Great for the business traveller. Only wish Auckland ANZ lounge could be half as nice.

lounge_name: AIR NEW ZEALAND BUSINESS CLASS (INT'L) LOUNGE REVIEW
review: This is the worst business class lounge I have ever encountered - difficult to find a seat tables piled high with dirty crockery and glasses - took more than an hour to be cleared. The food on a tiny counter was limited to stir fry or pasta in cardboard cups both of which were unpleasant - no Sandwiches savouries or salad options. If it weren't such along walk from the min terminal we would have returned there and paid for our food and drink. Business Class passengers deserve better than this.

I found this lounge very dirty with cups plates and spoons lying around the tables not collected by service staff. It was a Business Lounge being used by Thai Airways First Class passengers. In the internet room there was a major disagreement between two passengers. One of whom was talking loudly on his mobile phone making it impossible for the other internet users to concentrate. This matter was report to the lounges' front desk but they seemed to ignore the complaint.

We spent a couple of hours in the lounge yesterday and couldn't really fault it. OuR flight was departing around 2130 to LAX. There was plenty of food and drink plenty of seating wifi worked fine the back massage was excellent. Yes some of the furniture looked tired.

Extremely dated and tired furniture messy and crowded. It's supposedly the Business Class Lounge but Premium EY passengers can use it too. Great for them but diminishes the exclusivity that Business Class should get considering the premium price tag. Arrived at the lounge at 10.15pm for our 11.45pm flight hoping to have a light meal so we could go straight to sleep once on the plane. Found staff clearing the "trucker cafe"-buffet-style food table because "dinner was finished." Great. The only food available was picked-through cheese and crackers muffins (?!) and biscuits. Asked service staff for even a cup of hot soup but nope sorry not available. The coffee bar was closed as well and the only coffee/tea available was self-serve brewed. This despite the fact that there were so many people lounging around waiting for their flights - so much so that it was difficult to find any place to sit with any silence or privacy. Any free space on the sofas and tables were littered with crumbs used plates cups and glasses. Some staff were around clearing things away but hardly enough to cope with the number of passengers there. Very disappointing. Finally found a quiet spot to settle it near the back and decided to partake of the "free massage" for long-haul Business passengers. Approached the table presented boarding pass and was told sorry massage room was closing for the night. Quite a number of long-haul ANZ flights leave at night - including flights going to LON and LAX which have the highest fares. Why doesn't the lounge operating hours reflect this and have extended food/service hours to cater to these premium passengers? Considering this is Air New Zealand's main hub we thought the lounge here would be impressive which is why we came for our flight early.

lounge_name: AIR NEW ZEALAND BUSINESS CLASS LOUNGE REVIEW
review: Tired looking lounge with dated decor. Staff pleasant and professional. Limited selection of food & beverages. Washrooms provide very basic facilities and need updating. Screen for flights info only at entrance; no other screen is available elsewhere in lounge though boarding calls were made. Wifi available. Free massage available to Business passengers. One would think NZ has its best lounge at its hub - if you think that you will sure be disappointed.

Air Malta was using Lufthansa's Business Class Lounge at Terminal 2. Visiting it again, nothing noticeably had changed. Everything seemed to be back to normal. It is a pleasant enough place to relax, but only for a short time. The food and drinks were almost the same as before. The cold food, fruit and cereal section were excellent.  I was happy to drop in again.

Spacious and airy ambiance, the best thing about it, is the view towards the runway and apron. There is also an outdoor terrace with seating. A variety of seating and furniture, from bar-style stools and chairs to comfortable sofas. There was a small area with computers and the WiFi was swift. There was no area for privacy or partly secluded parts for relaxing. The food and drinks section was self-service. Many of the breakfast items were pre-wrapped (due to covid), and there were a few pastries. But there was no hot food on offer. There was a fair selection of alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks.
Great food, lovely ambience. A mix of regional dishes and western with ample salad options , coffee and beverages. Cozy ambiance and good orientation of seating arrangement gave a sence of privacy

Second time I’ve used this lounge in Terminal 1 at Delhi Airport. Both times it was very busy, indeed this time a staff member went round until he eventually got me a seat, albeit on a bar stool which meant my knees were higher than the table! Foods pretty good, small range of hot dishes plus chefs cooking street food, and a couple of deserts. Tea, coffee and fruit drinks in cartons. Not many screens giving you the up to date flight information and no separate wifi, so if you don’t have an Indian phone then you’ll need a voucher (available at the lounge check in) to logon.

The international lounge of Air India at Delhi Airport is a disappointment. Old, not too clean with awful food and limited selections.  Unappetizing food, tired interior, substandard toilets. The difference is amazing and very disappointing. Definitely in need of an upgrade. Hardly any changes over the years. The service is not bad. but everything else needs work!

Worst customer experience ever. Flying Air India business class and looking for the lounge at Delhi airport. Lounge has been closed for 3 years and I need to pay to go to other lounge. Air India has lost a business class frequent flyer forever!

Vienna Airport lounge used by Air India. Luckily, I found only one seat unoccupied when I entered. I do not understand why some people keep their backpacks, handbags in a way that obstructs other passengers to sit. Anyway, the lounge was small, and it had a quiet room. I was in that room however some people were loud and talking over phone. The food and beverage options were good. They had some delicious Thai curry. Almost everyone was eating it. They had all kind of drinks as well. Overall a good lounge. I wish they manage it a little better and remove the dirty dishes.

Air India Mumbai lounge operated by GVK is a beautiful lounge and it is a silent lounge, as they are no announcements, but being very large, noise in general is subdued. Seating is comfortable. Very good food, huge choice also in drinks, extremely friendly and helpful staff. Only drawback was the WiFi was very slow, just good to get emails but surfing was impossible. Clean toilets as well.

This is by far the worst airport lounge I have ever experienced. The seating reminds me of a hospital waiting room. The food and beverage choices are pathetic at best. The 'fresh' food looks days old. There is a bar, but with no attendant. That means no drinks. Receptionist barely acknowledged me when entering and pointed and grunted the direction to lounge seating. The WiFi is non-existent. I would have given zero stars, but that was not an option. Shame on Air India for treating customers with such disdain and disregard.

Very Bland. The  Air India combined First Class and Business class lounge at Newark airport could do with some nice wall colour. Everything so bland. It was worse than an office kitchenette. Wifi worked, but was slow. Lounge staff were nice. In comparison to other lounges, I would stroll through the airport rather than go to the Air India Lounge - this needs lots of improvement and a face lift. Food and beverages were below par. Work area is in the open. I would not call this a lounge at all.
Very good lounge as there was a variety of canapés and drinks. Lounge staff were happy to help with any of your needs.
My daughter and I took the AI116 from LHR to Delhi. I have never seen a worse spread of snacks in any lounge before. We had to go downstairs to a cafe to get a bite. Food was stale and cold.

This is the only lounge I have seen which is before the security so if you are at highest member level or are flying business class you need to reach little early if you wish to use the lounge. The purpose of relaxing at lounge and boarding when boarding starts will not stand true in this case. Odd and strange it is but this is Air India you can expect anything. The reason I can think of is if you visit their lounge you would notice that it is generally occupied by Airline staff itself and after a minute or two someone will be visiting from Airline to have a snack so it is a free restaurant for them. Last month I sent them a mail that their lounge plugs are not working from months.

I arrived in the early morning from Toronto to Heathrow on Air Canada and was transferring to Air India flight to Delhi. The lounge does not open until 3 hours prior to the flight which meant I could not use the lounge for several hours. Most airlines use partner lounges when their lounge is not open. The lounge itself isn't too bad but is small and has little services.
No Soft drinks! No towels to shower with! Toilets are dirty. By far the worst Star Alliance lounge we have been to.

What a depressing place! This lounge is definitely not to be recommended for a long transit. Having recently been condemned to staying in the lounge for 12 hours I cannot recommend this lounge. The food was practically non existent. Just one badly bruised banana and a single rotting orange and a few snacks. There was butter and jam but no bread until morning. When I asked for the use of the shower I was made to feel it was putting the staff out. Staff were few and far between and totally disinterested in customer service. The decor is outdated and dirty. Wifi is available but so complicated to connect it is worthless. There is little to redeem this lounge.
The lounge is clean. Seating adequate. There is a meagre but reasonable selection of snacks and drinks. WiFi available. Staffing limited and they seem disinterested.

If you want to feel depressed about your choice of airline Air India's Business Lounge in Delhi International will do it for you. Curry or Curry with rice for a meal. Samosas in an oven that had been there for at least a week. 2 beers in the fridge dirty plates stacked everywhere toilets that need a pressure cleaner desperately. Truly third world and nowhere near international standards. Flickering or dead light fixtures tired interior no staff no food if you are sick of curry just no point. Got so sick of the depressing place I went next door and paid to use another lounge.

Poor service. Imagine the frustration of getting off an overnight flight and finding the lounge closed at 8.30am (their website specifies an 8.00am opening time). With no indication of 'when' they would be open casual discussion with others in the area indicated a 10am opening!

Was shocked at the condition of the place. Staff were incredibly wonderful. No complains abt them. The sofas were all stained. No way anyone could rest there. So small and people were talking so loudly children screaming. No wifi at all. Staff kept apologising to us - it was not their fault. We could not even entertain ourselves with our mobile or tabs (as wifi was totally out). Food was horrible. Coffee machine made alot of noise. No proper reading material. A lady was bringing the roof down saying she was economy but wanted to sit inside and rest. Finally we left this dirty lounge and went to the main seating area near the gates. Tried to buy some food to eat hardly could eat because pigeons were over our heads and that was so unhealthy. We left out food and drinks (which we bought) and went to wait at the gate. We just cannot believe that an International airport is in such a state. The finale is the toilet next to the Lounge - it was like a public toilet. I have to indicate a star at least below otherwise I cannot proceed to submit this. I dont wish to give a star at all for anything below except 5 stars for the poor staff to deal with all this.

I have been using Delhi international airport biz/first class lounge for last two years on way to US and Asia. Pathetic food and same menu. Internet is always down when asked why it is down for 2 years no answer. Selection of alcohol is very sad papers/magazines variety is limited. Too many people working but not working think there are three managers for every person working. Overall disappointing.

Executive Lounge for Air India in Changi Airport Terminal 2 was very comfortable. Wonderful variety of food coffee tea etc. Fruits Sandwiches. 4 exercise lounge chairs. Good wifi connection. Polite staff and helpers inside the lounge. Though we had to wait for 2 over hours we enjoy the comfort in this lounge. I even had a good 1 over hour of sleep to make up for getting up early to come to the airport. Lovely clean toilets.

Air India Terminal 3 international Lounge is very spacious clean and well kept facility. The staff were courteous and helpful. The sofa and slumber lazboys were comfortable for napping and taking a break. Food was fresh tasty but selection was a little limited. The drinks and beverage selection was good and the staff brought it to my sitting area (maybe local regulations about an open bar). The internet connectivity with Tatadocomo was challenging - one of the lounge staff members had to help me connect. The toilet and showers were clean. I can see the lounge getting very busy and crowded in the future. But for me it was a good experience and a pleasant surprise.

I was traveling first class to US from Delhi and had 3 h to spend in the Air India lounge. I was shocked to see that this is the flagship lounge of Air India in India's capital. What a shame. First the first and Executive lounges are not separate. They are separated by a barricade nthat was easily crossed. There is no wait staff even for first class passengers. When one flies Emirates or Lufthansa in first class the respective lounges provide an opportunity for a high quality sit down meal from an a la carte menu. In the AI lounge food left a lot to be desired. The bathroom was in shambles and there was no lotion. Magazine choice was non existent. Wifi was spotty and complicated. why can't they provide free wifi without the need for passwords cell phones etc ? Very absurd. And the bar service was pitiful and most of the time non existent. Again no waiters even in first class section. In summary the premium lounge in the airport shared by many airlines is similar but at least predictable in service (albeit poor). The AI lounge is awful and takes away from first class experience. The managers don't care and are never around to receive feedback leave alone make changes. Best avoided for same reason AI is best avoided. First class pax are not escorted to the plane either.

Had a 4 hour layover in Delhi while returning from Frankfurt and going to Hyderabad. The lounge was easy to find and the ambience was quite decent with enough seating. However every aspect of service is poor. I asked for a toothbrush in the morning; after bring ignored by the lounge manager and then again by the uniformed lady I got it through the attendant but the kit seems to have been "borrowed" from Hotel Centaur (whose name was written on the pack). The breakfast was pathetic - very little options and the one I had Poha was cold dry and just a step above eating sand. The ketchup that was served looked like it was diluted 10 times over. The coffee and tea served were tasteless cold and unappetizing. I had to go out and eat breakfast in a restaurant outside. There is no WiFi in the lounge and they give you some sort of cards that have a validity of 45 minutes. On the day I visited even that was not available. Since I was coming from an international leg I thought of taking a shower before taking the domestic leg. When I asked the lounge manager for a towel I was flatly told that they had "run out of towels" - when I asked how long it will be before they can get fresh ones I was told that it will come the next day only! Since the lounge was quite empty I asked the manager how many towels he keeps a day and he said that they have a limit of 6 towels a day. I asked how they expected other guests to shower and he gave me a look that conveyed that I had exhausted my limit on the questions I can ask him. The lounge manager was very quick to refuse every request for service. He also has a bright future in the Indian Administrative system because he never forgets to treat you with disdain and demonstrate to you that he is under no obligation to provide you any service whatsoever. I am have flown Air India internationally for almost 18 years and they have managed to completely escape the service revolution that has happened everywhere in the world. The quality of service is as poor as it was 18 years back and though the faces of service staff is younger they have managed to encapsulate the same sense of apathy and disdain for passengers that existed earlier.

A large but outdated lounge. Furniture adequate but showing signs of wear and tear. The lighting poor with many light bulbs flashing on and off. Food is basic with little choice. Toilet areas kept clean but no facilities for a wash after a long flight. There are showers but these were closed and out of use. I asked for a shaving kit. Told they are available but none left 'sorry'. Only computer access is via three outdated computers. Staff kept the lounge clean and tidy. This is not however up to modern standards. This is not a place to enjoy a long transit.
Lounge quiet and peaceful. Not a wide range of food but adequate and plentiful. Wifi available.

Air India use the Louis Tavern lounge in Bangkok airport which is open to the general public on payment. There are very limited facilities in the lounge (no TV no toilets) but a better drinks and food selection than either the Air India lounges used on this trip or the Thai lounges used in Bangkok before. Wifi good and accessed via passkeys provided at reception to lounge. Aircraft boarding information needs improvement though. Not busy despite the amount of people in the airport that morning.

Visited whilst in international transit. Good points - this new lounge is huge has a varied selection of seats including recliners shower facilities are good OKAY selection of reading material and half a dozen internet terminals for free internet access. The bad points are that whilst Air India's website shows alcohol is available to international travellers none is available or on show. In fact there's one small fridge with water pepsi 7 up fanta or fruit juice - that's it. The food selection is similarly limited and the hot selection was particularly unsatisfactory (2 veg 1 meat - however there appeared to be no chicken in this!). Wifi is the airports and not the lounges - limited and very slow - had to use the dedicated terminals instead. Was again a good place to rest and read but not on a par with other carriers i have flown.

Myself and fellow passengers entered this lounge 3 hours before the flight to be told the hot food would not be available for another 30 minutes. Good points - plenty of seating good wi-fi newspaper selection tv drinks selection notified when it was time to board. Bad points - except for the shami kebabs the food selection was poor and in the case of the sheesh kebabs revolting. Had the crackers and crisps instead once the shami had run out. The staff were overstretched (there appeared to be only 2 of them) and as a result items were not cleared or refreshed. Recommend the lounge as an escape from the crowds but eat beforehand.

This is not so much of a lounge as somewhere to sit while you wait for a flight. The bar or the lack of one was very disappointing as it was closed. How long it has been that way or if it would open again is anyone's guess. The cold drinks were dreadful food was hot but not a great selection. Okay if you only want Indian food but would be nice to have had a selection after all it was the international lounge with international passengers. The lounge at Heathrow T4 was better bright clean but a very limited selection of Indian food some biscuits and a few alcoholic drinks on show. Air India lounges are best forgotten.

This must be the worst lounge in existence a dreadful room to spend any time in. We had to ask for the air conditioning to be switched on as it was so hot and stuffy. The lounge had a old microwave oven in one corner that they (when we finally were able to find a staff member) could offer an instant coffee or a cup or tea. It looked nasty so we plumped for a small (very small) bottle of water we were also offered a biscuit. After a nine hour Air India flight with not a great deal to eat we were hungry but I am afraid that the cupboard was bare. Just to add that if you (like us) had to transit from the international to domestic 1a leave plenty of time as you will pass through a least 2 xray checks and a least 6 more security checks plus a 5 kilometer bus ride (packed like sardines) up three floors to the so-called lounge and then down one or two floors to your departure gate. We have to repeat it in December as we have already booked the flights. What you get for a cheap fare.

This is the most miserable lounge I've ever been in. Furniture is falling to pieces no toilet paper in the ladies' toilet food terrible and staff as slow as a wet week. Awful coffee delivered after a long wait.

The new Maharaja lounge just past security is still not open. I went to the Maharaja lounge by gate 3 passed security on 14th April 2012. I would not recommend this lounge to anyone. I arrived in this Room full of mosquitoes old worn out furniture with people trying to sleep on the worn out shabby settees I do not know how they could sleep with all that noise and constant phone going off and people just entering the lounge asking questions about other air lines. They will only serve you water or juice as apparently they will not serve alcohol to business or first class passengers on International flights since 1st April so a dry room. When I arrived in this excuse of a lounge there were about 20 children screaming and running around without any supervision apparently they were being looked after by a member of staff so they were not booked as business or first class passengers she then moved them to a more suitable area after about 10 minutes. You have to ask for water or juice. I asked for tea and they do serve this. Snacks are from a microwave and again you have to ask but I would not recommend these over microwave snacks. I walked out and still cannot believe this so called first and business class lounge is still in use it should have been closed years ago.

After the chaos confusion and long wait through immigration and security this was a shocking surprise. At first we wondered if we were in the right place. Dingy and old fashioned with no sign of any refreshments at all. No wifi and a Desk top that had to be repaired before it was usable. The toilet facilities were the worst we have seen in a so called Business Class lounge. While we were there some Indian people were offered a drink and light refreshments (so presume there was catering of some sort somewhere) but not us or other Europeans. A miserable alternative to the much better options just outside the door.

I was shocked when entering the lounge because I wasn't sure if this was the correct place to be? Plenty of seats that look it's straight from the 60s-70s but very little people except a few sleeping. The staff is polite though have trouble understanding English. I wasn't sure if there was food/drink available but noticed the staff asking an India passenger so I inquired. No Wi-Fi but there is one older PC with internet. I needed to use a phone to call a local number for confirmation and that was difficult to do because they couldn't figure out if I could or if I had to use someone's cell though the staff was helpful enough to let me borrow one of their mobile phones. I left after a short time as there were a couple of older TVs that were fairly loud. Overall I'd avoid this lounge and stick to the airport which is much nicer.

Waiting for my flight from Mumbai to Singapore I was entitled to use the Maharaja Lounge since I was a business class passenger. There are two lounges that can be used one before security and one after. I chose to use the one after security because the lines were extremely long. The waiting area after security is very sparse but had an adequate number of seats. The lounge appeared decent from the outside. Once inside I felt I had entered into the 1970s. There were sofas and chairs that were upholstered with a flower pattern. The tables and everything else was wood (mahogany?). The two young men manning the information desk took my lounge pass. I found a seat among the many people who had already taken entire sofas to sleep on. Being a midnight flight there were many sleeping people. There were no drinks or food offered in the open. One of the young men offered water to other passengers and I had to ask for water. Later on the young man was taking the order of another passenger and finally asked me if I wanted coffee or tea. The only redeeming factor of this lounge was that the Masala Chai was decent. Other than that I felt like I had been transported back to the 1970s due to the furniture of the lounge. Also if other Indian passengers had not ordered coffee/tea I feel like I never would have been asked being the only non-Indian passenger in the lounge.
A nice lounge with plenty of seating and a strong Internet connection. Bar/beverage options were great but the food choices could include a bit more variety, not that it is lacking though.

Excellent! The lounge is large and airy with lots of space. It is spread over two floors. It is comfortable and the layout allows for eating and relaxing areas. Food and beverages available was also excellent with an extensive range of beverages (alcoholic and non-alcoholic). The lounge provides free WiFi access and the speed was good. It is possible to pay to enter the lounge if you’re not a business class passenger or a member of the frequent flyer club. Premier Pass is also accepted. A visit to the lounge is highly recommended.

Used this wonderful lounge on our way back from Mauritius last Saturday what a wonderful experience. The staff are lovely and what you supply is excellent. We have a dragon pass and enjoyed visiting the lounge.

Large airy space to sit but that's your lot! Old fashioned choices for food,  really just small nibbles and a few drinks. TV screens and airport announcements which can barely be heard. Toilets were ok this time some all good. I do not understand why anyone would want to pay to use this lounge but they do. I use it as you can always get a seat but it can be busy as so many airlines use it. The WiFi was good.

Air Mauritius have the use of the Air France lounge in Johannesburg. The lounge was small and very quiet. The seating was of modern design to the point of being weird looking (imagine 30+ IKEA designs) and too close together. Other than reception staff (2 ladies who were clearly uninterested in customer service) I did not see a single attendant/waiter. The food was boring limited cold and stale. The coffee (from an automated machine) was quiet OK though. Of the 5 available PC's for client use only 3 were working. Those 3 had such a slow response time for internet surfing that I didn't achieve anything anyway. The screen savers timed out the sessions as well.

The Air Mauritius lounge at Port Louis is as expected for the national airline's home lounge large well-equipped and has a warm welcoming feel. The food is excellent quality and plentiful with staff more than happy to assist.

Not a lot has changed since the review on here from 2007 by the look of it. Used by Air France Emirates and Air Mauritius. Still 2 levels limited choice of food drink not bad. Handy for the departure gates only 20 metres away from Gate 1 for example. Plenty of flat screen large TVs dotted around the lounge but all switched off. Was quite crowded when we passed through with 3 flights departing at the end of the day. (It looks as if they are building another terminal next door to the current one so things will probably be improved all round when its finished.

Small but cosy - no windows. Limited quantity and variety of food drinks ok as far as tea and coffee are concerned. Some place to store luggage. The business lounge is sort of a mezzanine above the first class lounge shared by Air Mauritius and Air France. Very easy to find right after immigration and security check and pretty close to boarding gate. Clean restrooms and clean and comfortable shower rooms - unfortunately just 2 internet PCs that are always busy.

Used Priority Pass to enter this lounge although being an economy class passenger. A nice experience considering that most facilities at Seychelles airport (SEZ) is rather small and outdated. Food options are quite limited so do not expect to be well-fed at the lounge, but the drink options are all there ranging from beer to liquors so clearly this lounge will satisfy alcohol lovers. Moreover, a nice Internet connection is offered for its customers so staying in the lounge should be the better option for most passengers staying in the waiting area.

Business lounge serving all airlines at Mahe. Customers can also pay a fee to use Lounge. Small buffet with comfortable chairs and good views of the runway. Food runs out quickly but is soon replenished. Staff are polite and professional and will assist you in connecting to their free wifi, as well as announcing flights. 2 tv screens and a few magazines but very little else. Toilets are clean but the hand dryers are inefficient.

This was such a disappointment although the seating was nice. The auto taps in the ladies toilet were mostly not functioning event though they were auto. The plastic soap dispenser was cheap and nasty. The food on offer at the commencement of my 'stay' was the same as it was on leaving and there were some hot dishes. Plenty of alcohol available. The welcome on entering was very miserable. I apologised for being deaf due to the air pressure issue having just flown in from Fort Lauderdale. A smile, a nod of understanding would have been welcome. She just wanted my ticket - no interest in my well being.  When I went to look around the duty free shops I came across a sign for the Signature lounge which was supposed to be available but that was closed. So really a poor experience.

This was by far the best airline lounge I have ever visited. You get seated to a table, you order for an incredible menu, they bring you Piper champagne, amazing cocktails, the best chocolate cake I have ever eaten, and incredible steak cooked perfectly, truly this was an amazing lounge for full fare paying business class passengers travelling with Air Canada on international routes.

Both my husband and I have platinum status on Star Alliance and we tried to use the Air Canada lounge. The woman at the lounge refused to let us in because according to her company policy, she cannot let in anyone no earlier than 3 hours before the flight. At that time, our boarding time was only in 3 hours and 10 min. Even after waiting 10 min, she said her “system” still wasn’t allowing her to let us in because the 3-hour rule is based on the flight departure time. When we complained that we had never heard of such rule, she said she only works for her company and that’s not her problem. After this experience, I will never fly Air Canada. They need to do a better job in training their employees (or hire better) as this was the worst form of CRM I have ever experienced in 40 years of business travel.

Never buy a day pass to the Air Canada  Maple Leaf Lounge. I did this and arrived at the lounge in Toronto, and we were denied access because they were full. This would be fine, however, the airline refuses to refund my money. They say that I was “scanned in,” which absolutely never happened, and I have told them that I would pay double the cost if they could produce a video or still image of anyone from my party spending one second in the Lounge. They have produced no evidence and have never refunded my money. Do not take the chance. I would also encourage you to avoid doing business with this dishonest company.

Absolutely unacceptable that there is a new 3 hour limit starting July 13th 2023. Last time I traveled it was unlimited, there was also no mention of the limit when upgrading to business class. Major reason I upgraded was to have access to the lounge. I don't think I will be flying with Air Canada again after this.

I used a 25K pass for this lounge which was well worth the pass. The Maple Leaf Lounge in Ottawa overlooks the ramp with large picture windows. I found all of the lounge to spotless, well stocked with beverages and food (hot and cold). Seats are very comfortable and the WIFI was very fast. Staff that were in the lounge were very friendly and helpful. A great spot to decompress before your flight!

Decent food. Rude server, scoffed at me when I asked for a alcoholic beverage and said no, I had to ask her why because she didn’t offer a explanation. She said only after 11am. Granted it was early but This is a international airport with people coming in from all time zones, don’t appreciate the judgement or lack of accommodation.

Very tragic lounge. Watched a customer being turned away at the front desk due to overcapacity. Lounge is extremely crowded and dated, probably due to cardholder access nowadays. To combat this an expansion triple the size wouldn't hurt. Food selection (particularly for breakfast) is dismal and low in quality. My hashbrowns were closer to mashed potatoes. Service is casual and only helps with picking up rubbish and used plates. I don't see anything being cleaned between settings. Overall feels very unexclusive and really disappointed with the quality of Air Canada's domestic lounges.

The Air Canada Lounge is an alternative for Star Alliance passengers at Frankfurt airport. The catering is the same as in the Lufthansa lounges. The food was fine, but not spectacular. But the lounge was stylish, with lots of light, and reat views of the apron. Furthermore, it was quiet and not to crowded at the time when I visited. I can really recommend the lounge

We stopped in the AC Signature Suite at YYZ for a few hours prior to a flight back to Europe. Our hand baggage, which was extensive, was checked into a luggage room, and we were ushered to the dining room. We had cocktails, champagne, and a three course meal. The food was of high quality - probably akin to what you'd find in a Michelin Plate restaurant. The wine list was small but well curated, and the waiting staff were friendly, professional, and skilled. After eating we found a quiet area with couches to sit back and relax on. The bar area was well-stocked with the bartenders very friendly. A buffet was available adjacent to the bar serving a different selection of food from the dining room, but all of very high quality. Bathrooms were perfectly clean despite the lounge being fairly full. Unfortunately there are no shower facilities. The lounge was physically in excellent condition with no signs of wear. Although I'm not a fan of AC's tendency to use dark woods and brooding lighting I felt it somehow worked very well here. There is no view of the ramps. Overall this is an excellent lounge experience - everything that AC's marketing promises for its Signature Class product is delivered here. The only real downside to the experience was it made the flight that followed seem very mediocre by comparison.

The lounge itself has a nice and relaxing atmosphere. There are plenty of seats and also some private areas. The stuff was very nice also. The choices of food were very limited and super small portioned, but tasty. What absolutely horrified me was that the food was "served" in cardboard boxes.

The Maple Leaf Lounge in Vancouver caters to Business Class passengers for Air Canada and Elite 50k or above members in the airline's loyalty structure. They seem to have recently renovated the lounge, replacing the rather dimly lit 90's or 2000s style lounge with a more hip and prestigious looking aesthetic sporting white marble, driftwood tables and black leather seating. I did however come to the lounge a few days after the COVID-19 measures were implemented, but they were still able to make it a nice experience. The buffet table for obvious reasons was replaced with prepackaged snacks. The self serve beer kegs were also suspended, but it was still possible to ask the bartender for a drink. Sodas and water were still self serve, and among the snacks were sandwiches, wraps, salads, fruit cups and pastries. The bathrooms were clean and there was plenty of seating available. It's rather unfortunate that some of the flight display screens didn't seem to be working. Perhaps I should try their Signature Class Suite product when COVID-19 blows over.
I expected more from this Air Canada Maple Leaf Lounge compared to the complete airport experience. The food and beverage choice is under average. Not really a lounge where you enjoy being at.

This Maple Leaf lounge is a mess, they ran out of food and quality is poor. There should be a revamp of the lounge, maybe get guest chefs to create menus. They should also invest in charging outlets by the seats.

The Air Canada Maple Leaf Domestic Lounge at Terminal 1 is a spacious and big lounge that is designed for frequent and business travellers on domestic trips. Quite all amenities are available. Big buffet with decent food and big varieties of choice. I love the open space with the glass front allow you for plane spotting.

I loved this Signature Lounge at Toronto Pearson Airport. Not only the design, the space and the atmosphere are great but the food and amenities offer. I enjoyed my time in the a la carte restaurant: lamb chops at the best with a great red wine (excellent selection). This made my day. The only thing that was missing are showers.

This Maple Leaf lounge is fine in terms of decor. However, their dinner hours are from 4:30-6:30pm! We arrived at the lounge at 6:40pm, not having eaten dinner. And they had soup and a couple of salads. It’s entirely ridiculous to stop dinner at 6:30pm.

This is the worst lounge I have visited. The lounge is very small and many passengers were turned away. My wife and I needed to stand for some time . Even then we could not sit together but needed to share a small table with other business class passengers. The table for two was so small we could not place even a small laptop computer on the table each. There was very little to choose from as far as food goes. Totally unacceptable as far as business class goes compared to other airlines.

I flew Business class Ethiopian airline, so I was told to use Air Canada maple leaf lounge, as Star Alliance Lounge. Time spent looking for this lounge is 30 minutes. There is no clear signage to the lounge. There is no light on the signage, and hallway is dark and somewhat hidden. The only signage to lounge point us to Air Canada signature lounge, and we were turn away. They told us we have to go to the other lounge. Anyway after we got here, we made suggest to the reception about additional signage and light, so passenger don't have to walk around. We were greet with a very uninterested Air Canada representative, she said the "signage is fine, please go on in." Lounge is nice and big. Pleasant atmosphere. But my food was dried and hard scrambled eggs, over cooked sausage.

This was the first time I used the lounge on the side of US departures at Pearson.  It can only be accessed by an elevator and there is a sign inside of the elevator that at peak times, several extra minutes should be factored in when leaving the lounge. I find it remarkable how poorly designed the infrastructure is. The food showed the same level of carelessness: the labels were inconsistent and the vegan selection was limited to edamame beans and a chickpea salad. The lounge was nearly at full capacity, which made it noisy and it was definitely understaffed. The ambience was identical to sitting outside at the gate. It is certainly not the right environment to prepare you for a productive flight across the continent.

When arriving at the lounge, the only way of entry was by scanning our boarding pass at a machine which would unlock the door. When we got in, the lounge was very small. It had the standard amenities, however. It features a TV, newspapers, an open bar, a coffee machine that makes specialty beverages, and soft drinks/juice. They have a toaster with bread, English muffins, and some bagels. They also have chips and salsa out. If you ever need anyone, it is very hard to find assistance. It felt really crammed in there especially when more people started to come in.
Maple Leaf lounge at Toronto. Upstairs before going to gates. Above average lounge for Star Alliance gold. Food and salads were good. Fine selection of wine and beers. Plenty of space

The Maple Leaf Lounge Transborder lounge was nothing special. I had access through my Star Alliance Gold status. It had a decent amount of seating space available for guests, despite the morning period being a peak time for US flights. The food selection was very limited- cereal, boiled eggs, fruits and pastries. The same was with dinner choices when I visited the International section few months ago. These are breakfast choices people could have at home in their daily life and this does not bring premium quality to Air Canada's Business and Elite frequent flyers. The expectations of lounge food are probably different in North America then. The lounge was pretty quiet despite a lot of people. Staff were polite and promptly cleaned utensils and cutlery on site.

The Signature Suite sets a new standard for airline lounges, the only negative is that the food is of such high quality that one tends to overeat and not be hungry onboard. Entry is limited to paid business class (Signature Class for Air Canada) passengers so is not crowded. Upon entry, they determine how much time you have until your flight and time permitting, offer a choice of dining room service with menu or buffet, I chose the dining room, but checked out the buffet and it was well above above. This high standard also applied to the cocktails, wine and beer service. Wait staff walked about the lounge in case you want a refill or new drink. All in all, best in class.

What a gemstone! Hidden treasure here in FRA, The lounge is of a good size, tarmac view, German sausages, hot dishes, weissbier, champagne, tranquility, good internet, and very kind and advising staff, despite I fly Air China, arrived 7 hours too early, had no boarding pass, but still they embraced me. Cadeaux to Air Canada (and Air China)

A sad lounge. Something out of the 1970s. Small and looking out onto half barrier walls. Seats are uncomfortable. Little round tables from Office Depot or something. Not much to choose from — broccoli was ok, hummus ok, cut pita was stale, cookies were ‘crisp’ and pretty disgusting, espresso maker was broken.

The lounge in Calgary has been recently renovated and upgraded. Comfortable seats, great views, hot food (soup, pasta, vegetables) and full bar service, no longer self serve and minimally stocked, the bartender now serves you upon request from a fully stocked bar. Staff were friendly and the lounge was spotless. This is my major annoyance with airport lounges globally, most (not all) are crowded as they should be in a busy airport but most are untidy with used plates, cutlery and glasses left everywhere waiting to be collected while passengers look for any vacant seat to occupy. Not at this lounge, it was busy but extremely clean. The fireplace is a nice touch.

I visited this lounge using my Star Alliance Gold Status even though I was flying with Lufthansa. The Air Canada Maple Leaf Club is very good and worth the walk. It offers a good bar service (even fresh milkshakes), good food offerings, a shower area and a quiet zone. When I was there, the lounge was quite empty. The staff was very friendly and helpful. I really love that place.

Most Air Canada lounges that I've visited are spacious, have a good wifi signal, and are kept clean and tidy. My biggest complaint with them, however, is that the food is absolutely awful. This morning I got off a 9 hour flight from Tokyo to Vancouver and have a few hours before continuing on to Toronto. I thought I would come to the Maple Leaf Domestic Lounge and have some breakfast. On offer today is sugary yogurt cups, bananas, Cheerios and stale bread. Some eggs would be nice.

As a privilege of being an Aeroplan Visa card holder I am to have access to the lounge once a year. My husband and I each have our own cards. I was denied access to the lounge because the flight was booked with my husbands points,  although he was with me and the card holder info says you can bring a guest on the one time visit. I was told I would have to pay! Are you kidding me?! We both have our own cards and secondary cards on each other's accounts. That equals a lot of fees and I can't even access the card holder Privileges. According the the lady at the counter we would each have to book our flights separately with our own visa and own Aeroplan points to meet her requirements. Yeah that's convenient - all married couple prefer to travel that way.

As a passenger on EVA Air business class I was invited to use Air Canada's lounge in London Heathrow's terminal 2. The staff at the reception was very friendly and welcoming. I used the lounge at around 7-8 pm and it was fairly empty. Plenty of seats by floor to ceiling window. The food and beverage selection was poor, and that was the biggest disappointment and the ambiance was lacking. I prefer the Plaza Premium lounge which is provided to most of the Priority Pass members. Nevertheless it was a soothing place to be before a long flight.

The lounge itself is great looking, modern and spacious, but does not have a separate business centre (just two computers and a few high chairs to work on in a corner of the lounge). Staff are very friendly and helpful. The food is varied (with good vegetarian options), and good variety of (alcoholic) drinks. However, due to a flight delay, many passengers had to wait at the airport for up to 6 hours or more. Despite so many passengers in the international departures lounge being stranded, they closed at the advertised time of 11.15pm. There were no exceptions made due to the exceptional circumstances, and many were obviously upset to be asked to leave when they still had hours to wait till their long-delayed Air Canada flights.

The Domestic Maple Leaf lounge is spacious and well laid out. You can generally find a seat, a nice glass of wine and a strong wifi signal. However, they really sound be embarrassed at the quality and selection of food provided. Anytime I'm in the TO lounge is normally because of a flight delay so I typically have a few hours to wait, and the last three times I was there the food was so bad I left to buy something and then returned. Soup from a package and the same salad served for months on end is nothing short of sad. To add insult to injury they offer 'supper' from 530 to 7pm which typically means sticky macaroni and cheese that is actually only served until it runs out rather than serving until 7. Today for example supper ran out at 630. People arriving at 635pm were told, 'Supper's finished. If you don't like it you can complain.' You can do better. Your staff and your food need to be greatly improved.

The Maple Leaf Lounge in Terminal 1 near gate F57 is very spacious and quiet. The seating arrangement is spread out and does not feel tight or claustrophobic. The reception desk is staffed with very courteous and pleasant staff. The views, or lack of, was a major drawback. For aviation enthusiasts like me, the disappointment came when all you could see was the top of some structure in front of the lounge. In other words, no view of the runways, planes, concourses, etc. Another drawback was the food. I was there at 8 am and so it was early. Not too many passengers in the lounge and breakfast was being served. For a business class lounge, I expected a little more than bread/bagels, a small selection of pastries, and coffee/juice. The employees are very nice and do a great job of maintaining the lounge. However, the food selection was just very poor.

A relatively new lounge, but overcrowded and not big enough for the number of Air Canada flights that depart nearly all at the same time. No such thing as personal space at this venue. Be prepared to sit in cramped conditions. Food and drink selection mediocre and not much is self service anymore.

Star Alliance Gold passengers flying out of Terminal 2 at LHR have a choice of four lounges they can visit. Although my Brussels Airline flight was departing from concourse A, I took the twenty minute hike to concourse B, because the Maple Leaf Lounge has received so many positive reviews. It was worth the effort. The personnel are friendly, the views are excellent, they had the makings of a hot, full English breakfast, and they offer a full range of alcoholic beverages, including real champagne. There are a variety of comfortable seating options, and the whole atmosphere is welcoming. I am a lifetime member of the United Club, and their lounge here is also top notch, but I will award first prize to Air Canada.

This Air Canada lounge has an elegant appearance, has the right size and offers nice views of the tarmac. They have a very nice breakfast buffet - warm and cold items - the serve French Champagne and even barista made coffee. The lounge is divided in several zones: working, eating, relaxing. A great place to spend the time before take-off.

The lounge is located in Terminal 2, 2nd floor above the noisy 1st level. Upon entering (every time I have been there) you will be greeted by a big smile from the agent. This lounge is available to Star Alliance members so when flying out during rush hours be prepared for it to be busy. The lounge has great French and Colombian blends of coffee with a wide variety of teas. There are limited options for food as it is just mostly little snacks vs. full on meals (Continental style). They have computers you can do work on with printing available. Again if it is super busy you might be waiting for a shower or stall. They do a good job of cleaning and refreshing for the next traveler. The staff are some of the nicest I have ever met and take great pride in their jobs. Wifi is good. No alcohol in the mornings except Guinness. I recommend this lounge to anyone who is a frequent flyer! Air Canada offers memberships that gain you access regardless of ticket type (Economy, Latitude etc). I love stopping in here to escape the noise, most travelers are Canadian and we enjoy chatting about hockey and how we love escaping the cold weather!

We arrived at the Lounge a couple of hours before our flight. The staff were friendly and accomodating, not that there was much to do except let us in. The Lounge was very comfortable the food selection was very pleasant and continuously topped up. Beverage selection was excellent, alcoholic and non-alcoholic.
