Cleaning staff were on top of things always tidying up customers left behind plates glasses etc. It was well worth the added price per passenger as we were in Premium Economy. The experience there was probably better than the flightitself.

Air Canada has clearly applied cost cutting measures to the food service at this International Maple Leaf Lounge at Toronto Pearson. It might sound petty, but the artisan tortilla chips and hummus have been replaced by sub par tortillas chips that taste like cardboard - and hummus is eliminated. I would have ranked this lounge as one of the best on any of my travels at one time, but to have the food quality diminished means that that AC Maple Leaf is now reduced to just okay, and by proper Canadian Etiquette, okay does not win my business.

I have been flying with Air Canada for over 3 years and have been a frequent flyer for 2 years. I do a lot of early morning travel and very much enjoy the hot breakfast offered in the lounge at Montreal. It's always been great to have at least one proper meal in case I miss out on others during the course of a travel day. But those hot breakfasts seem to have been replaced by muffins and stone cold boiled eggs. I don't know why the switch was made but it wasn't a good one and all I hear are complaints in the lounges from the patrons. Not only that, but there are no signs telling you what muffin is what or what's in them. I overheard someone asking a lounge employee what was in them as he had allergies but they were not able to tell him. All in all I'm very disappointed as this is a huge step down and only hurts the people that fly with the airline the most. If this is a sign of things to come for the lounge then I will be looking for an alternative airline.

The food was excellent however since they have chaged vendor we no longer have bagles, cream cheese, englush muffins, peanut butter, croissant, danish, fruits other than apples, muffins. Only 1 toaster for 10 persons in line. Why did Air Canada change a great lounge. I will keep writting to them even if they do not respond. I am a Super Elite Million mile client and very loyal to Air Canada but this needs to be addressed. The staff is excellent!

I guess Air Canada isn't making enough money. Gone are hot breakfasts, eggs, sausage etc. So I assume they have cut kitchen staff who prepare these meals. What is left is cold muffins, bananas and oatmeal. Every visitor to the breakfast bar made the same comment that they were disappointed to see what were accepted, appreciated and earned perks of being a frequent flyer being taken away. I haven't seen a reduction in my ticket price, nor have I seen a reduction in the criteria to become an elite member again. It's hugely disappointing that a brand that constantly proclaims service levels and their status within the industry reduces services to its key and most loyal customers. Shouldn't it be the other way around?

A sad state of affairs to call this a business class lounge. Food offerings were slim to say the least. For breakfast there was hard boiled eggs, yogurt, oatmeal, and toast with jam in a bowl and a spoon. Lunch offerings were two types of soup, a salad and some nacho chips. The magazine and drink offerings were plentiful however. Service in this lounge was particularly exceptional in comparison to other Air Canada Maple Leaf lounges. Wish that the Virgin Clubhouse lounge was still part of terminal 2. Prefer Delta Airlines, AMX Centurion, United and Alaska Airline lounges.

The Air Canada Maple Leaf business class lounge in Halifax, Canada, was spacious and comfortable, with a nice view of the runway and planes, and was conveniently close to the connecting gates, but that's where the positives end. The food choice was minimal, two soups, a small bean salad, nachos and hummus, and cookies were all that was on offer, drinks were of slightly better fare, with a small selection of reds and whites to choose from as well beers and spirits. However my main disappointment arose when having been informed that the connecting flight to London had been delayed by over two hours, they then asked us to leave the lounge as it closed at 11pm. Consequently we had to wait at the gate for 2+ hours (all bars and restaurants had also closed by this time). Surely if a flight's delayed (which in my experience with Air Canada has happened regularly), the business class lounge should remain open until embarkation, this after all is part of the price and reason why we buy a premium ticket.

I'm very disappointed that Air Canada has reduced the quality and quantity of food offered at their Maple Leaf lounge at Toronto lounges. There is a very poor selection. What is offered is cheaper quality. Gone are breakfast pastries, no bananas most of the time, only 2 cereals and a cheaper yogourt brand. Other than children who really eats Rice Krispies and white bread? Lunch is no better. They offer a canned bean salad and green salad. What happened to the other healthier salads and sandwiches? Supper hour is no better and cookies are rarely offered. This is a poor way to reward your dedicated frequent flyers! I can't even get a decaf black teabag anymore. It's been cut. Why is decaf coffee offered but not decaf black tea? (herbal teas don't count). Bring back the former menus.
What an appalling standard of this lounge - no shower, washroom was dirty and unserviced. Air Canada is very disadvantaged by this lounge as they offer good service, good food on their airline.

This was my first experience with Air Canada’s Maple Lounge in general, and Vancouver Airport in particular. I used the lounge located near Gate E-85 and was pleasantly surprised. This business lounge is spacious, has comfortable chairs, suitable for dozing-off, TV and WC. I showed up at 7:30am and found many breakfast items ready, such as boiled eggs, cereals, fruit, pastries, Yogurt, and tea-coffee-hot chocolate machine. AC staff kept the lounge clean with constant pick-ups of discarded items.

Located right after security on the international departures floor. Air Canada has numerous flights to Asia, Australia etc, but no shower in this lounge? These are not short flights. Passengers need to take showers to refresh before these sectors. C'mon Air Canada, try to move yourself up to 4.5 or 5 stars, like the airlines in Asia.

I travel all through Western Canada regularly and visit this Maple Leaf lounge at Calgary Airport at minimum twice a month. The lounge having been recently upgraded and with a new menu offering, it makes a trip through Calgary worthwhile. One of the secrets here are the amazing friendly staff at the lounge and bar, excellent selection of magazines and newspapers, and the previously mentioned new menu (which is thoughtful and competently executed). I must confess my last trip through here really left me reconsidering using it as my hub home. I arrived early for my flight to take advantage of some free wifi and a glass of red while I crushed out some expenses and admin (in itself a nice break from kids and other life demands) as my afternoon appointments ended early for a change. I parked myself at the end of the bar and worked for two and a half hours, and enjoyed some banter and a few glasses of red. I then enjoyed a really nice dinner in lounge, and decided on having one scotch for the road and the flight home. In my mind, I was relaxed but in no ways impaired so imagine my surprise when the drink was delivered by the one male staff member, I was told aloud for all to hear, "no more." While I really appreciate that safety is paramount, my issue with how it was delivered was he didn't even ask me how I felt or how I was doing. It felt pretty heavy handed how he handled it, even if he felt he was doing right. I'm a seasoned traveller and frankly this really turned me off. Had I been belligerent or obnoxious I would be the first to chastise myself for the boorish and inappropriate behaviour, however I'm pretty sure I would have blown under but the point is while the airline needs to ensure we all fly safe, it would be incumbent on them to discuss strategies on how to broach this with their customers - at the end of the day, somewhere between depraved indifference and police state we have to exist, but at minimum I would suggest this employee needs to have pointed out to him that we are the paying customer, and a little bit of discretion would have been appropriate. I otherwise think this is one of Air Canada's best lounges, one bad experience notwithstanding.

The Maple Leaf Lounge at Toronto Pearson airport is not huge but fairly decent sized with lots of different seating. Interior decor is simple and modern. Arrived at the lounge around 10am, only a few salads were available for meal at that time. Around 11am however they brought in several different pasta dishes and Thai red curry rice porridge. All the dishes were pretty tasty but I especially enjoyed Thai red curry rice soup. It was truly delicious. All in all found the lounge pretty quiet and comfortable.

The Maple Leaf Lounge at Toronto Pearson is a great lounge but overcrowded at certain times of the day. Food options were good despite the pasta being overcooked. Beverages and snacks were great. Seating was limited due to the amount of people in the lounge, some of which were terribly loud and disrespectful. Lounge staff was attentive and friendly. Bathrooms were clean and wifi signal was good.

This lounge is located on the domestic departures wing in front of gate 2. The lounge is large, and it was not crowded at the time I was there. I do not know if it gets packed during rush hours. The man at the reception was not very friendly, outdid his job correctly. Food options and were really varied and good quality. There was no wifi available. Not much staff around to help. Seating space was comfortable and decor was good. Overall, a nice impression. A good lounge for a domestic product.

We were excited to have access to the Air Canada lounge prior to our Air Canada rouge flight. We were hoping that the lounge would have been open after we checked in for our flight, however, the lounge doesn't open until 5:30 am. (if I am correct). Once inside the lounge, we were pleased to see the clean, roomy space. The food was hot or cold, depending on what you fancied. There were newspapers, a tv and an area with computers for your use. What a very pleasant start to our vacation.

The Air Canada lounge was a nice touch as this was my first time there. The turn off was the parents that allowed a young child to touch the eggs and muffins with his hands and then leave them in the dish. Not once did the parents say a thing. It's a business lounge and there were 10 year olds running around pretending to be cats. I guess I was raised old fashion that this lounge should have some class to it. Especially if it is being called a business lounge and people are trying to work between flights. Yes minor details but the handling off food was a real turn off and the parents need to be taught manners. The lady clearing table was very nice and friendly.

Air Canada Maple Leaf lounge at Toronto Pearson and the check-in process was confusing, since I had purchased my lounge time online. The women's rest room was closed for cleaning for the duration of my 7 hour layover. Considering that I had an 8 hour flight, and no restrooms between deplaning and customs, having to ask for a back-up restroom was unpleasant. The tv was not working, finally an attendant turned it on but did not leave the remote. The food was snacks - broken chips, cookies and random grab and go. Since I don't drink, the wine / beer had no appeal. The only water is from large Dasani bottles that everyone shares - if you can find a glass. There aren't enough outlets to charge everyone's equipment. The wifi didn't work so it was a long layover. The only 'plus' was the lady clearing the tables - she was kind. Today is my second time through here and, amazingly, the same situation with the restroom! The same broken chips. The same slow wifi - my phone cannot even connect to it. The same shared bottled water. The same lack of outlets. This time, they are out of spoons, soup bowls, desserts, salsa, plates - there is one woman whose only job is to stock the food bar and she isn't maintaining it well (and people are complaining). In both cases, as a business traveller, I would like to avoid children so I can concentrate - that is not possible in this so-called VIP Lounge.

The Air Canada Maple leaf lounge in Terminal 1 at Toronto Pearson was pleasantly surprising. The staff were very good about clearing tables and keeping the food stocked. Very good selection of salads but not many main courses for vegetarians. Bread was stale. The big surprise was the 4 beers on tap, including Guinness which was very nice. The main issue was the internet was very very slow. It was impossible to read emails. When I went back to the front desk to ask for a solution one was not given. The women working there seemed to be more interested in texting then helping and only said "our internet is provided by an outsource company, you can move into the terminal and use their internet." Wow poor response. How about "lets try and see what the problem is and work it out." Many of us using the lounge are business orientated and require good internet. Toilets were clean. I did not see showers which would have been a good idea for travelers coming from say Vancouver connecting to Europe.

I was in Franfurt recently and had a wonderful time.  We had seen the Air Canada logo and we decided to go check it out. Walking into the lounge we were hit by a nice breeze from the fantastic air conditioners. The lounge was huge, with lots of nice leather chairs and tables. The greatest thing in the lounge would have to be the buffet. Plenty of fantastic foods to eat.  All in all it made the airport experience so much better.

The Air Canada domestic Maple Leaf Lounge at Toronto Pearson Airport is spacious, clean and relatively quiet. A lot of seating options with a few desk with PC's. Free WiFi was good but reception was inconsistent. Staff were efficient and friendly. Food choices were not that great. Salsa and chips, soup, salad. Beverage selection was good.

The Air Canada Maple Leaf Lounge domestic lounge at Vancouver Airport was a decent size with many seating options. WiFi was good but signal was inconsistent. Standard food offerings with a good beverage selection. Staff were friendly and helpful.

The Air Canada Maple Leaf lounge at Frankfurt Airport is one of the best business class lounges I have visited. Better than some first class lounges, but not as good as Lufthansa First Class in Frankfurt or First class lounges in the Middle East. The attentive and friendly service of all the staff was excellent, and above the Maple Leaf lounges in Canada

Travellers are warned that the Air Canada Maple Leaf Lounge at Calgary Intl Airport is undergoing construction. Based on our visit, this is an understatement. We visited the lounge in mid-July 2015 to be greeted by an experience of very poor seating, meagre food offerings and overcrowding. Even restrooms were only limitedly available, due to cleaning which went on for quite some time. In some cases, an airport may offer venues so peaceful and reasonable that it pays to visit them instead of using the airline lounge. The Maple Leaf Lounge at Calgary international exemplifies a second situation where the lounge is so inadequate and overcrowded that even poor airport venues make for a better place to wait for flights. Lounge personnel here were more interested in surfing the Internet than assisting airline customers with questions about connections or required services.

A nice lounge, with nice view of the tarmac. 2 soups on choice, Dips, as well as salads and sandwiches. Self serve soft drinks and alcohol. Have a kid zone, business center. I can see it can be crowded. Only accessible via elevators. No stairs. So take extra time before leaving the lounge to get to your gate. Better than any Delta, American, United lounges. Still weaker than average premium lounge in Europe.

The terminal is under renovation and as a result it was difficult to find the entrance to the Air Canada business class lounge. The seating in the lounge was okay (we spent a couple of hours there) but the food and the Air Canada staff were poor at best.

Having flow out of T2 twice on Eva Air recently this review covers both visits. Eva use the Air Canada lounge along with a couple of other Star Alliance carriers. It is close (2-3 minutes) to the boarding gates but suffers like some others on T2 in that it's a fair hike from immigration to the gates/lounge. One inside it is very modern and comfortable with a nice bar and service good range of food and good personal space. Travelling on a Wednesday evening there were not many people in the lounge and it felt quite and comfortable. A vast improvement on the old T3 lounge shared with SAS.
Worst lounge we have ever seen. Food buffet was almost empty and dirty and not filled up within hours. Washrooms very dirty. Noisy. Disappointing experience.

Air Canada has made significant improvements in most of its lounges and they are obvious with the upgrade in service and food selection being noticeable. Gone are the days of dirty dishes and rude staff. It has been a welcome improvement. Unfortunately the YYZ MLL International lounge at the E gates seems to have been left behind. On the day I used it it was very busy with limited food offered and an unpleasant ambience. There are just too many people using the lounge many of whom have access because of their frequent flyer status. The end result is that pax who are flying on the expensive long haul flights in business class receive a mediocre experience. It's time for AC to divide the lounge into two sections one for the true international business class and "Super Elite" status pax and the other for the basic "Elite" pax and those flying on shorter route Rouge Premium. Provide a quiet area with better food for the first group and keep the current set up for the second group. My biggest wish is for AC to provide decent wifi access in its Canadian lounges. I have had better wifi access in "developing" world airports.

Now seated in lounge after a two week trip with time spent in other business class lounges Think Toronto maple leaf lounge is one of the worst we have visited. Have visited this lounge often but prompted to finally share my thoughts with other travellers as the offering of a few salad items chilli Con carne and stale bread receives a failing grade Air Canada's food is consistently weaker than other competitors.

Very comfortable and nicely decorated lounge with small but high quality food and drinks selection. Plenty of seating space and some proper tables and chairs to dine at rather than just sofas everywhere. Nice place.

This is the worst lounge. Bathrooms dirty and over flowing trash minimal lounge areas and NO BAR. They don't have a liquor license. All this at a time when the terminal at LAX is under renovation and offers minimal services. I can't believe a first class lounge could be so bad.

I visit this Lounge six times a year in the past few years. In my every visit the feelings are more or less the same in average except the food choices are very disappointing only cup cakes vegetables and cold boiled eggs. I have never encounter of any hot food nor hot soup in this lounge. Asian instant noodle is never seen here. My wife even prefer to sit outside in those paid cafe to have proper eating.

Worst lounge we have ever experienced poor service no food except crackers and cheese. Our flight was late and did not leave till 2:30 am the lounge closed at 11:30 pm. The seating was very uncomfortable bar only had very cheap wines that were free. Overall it was awful.

I am always pretty pleased with the Air Canada Lounges (Vancouver is very good and so is Edmonton). Calgary has always been a large and crowded one. They have just done some renovations and while it looks much better (and the staff are invariably courteous and helpful) there is one down-side. There is no longer a self-serve bar. Been through there at least six times in the last month. When the Lounge is not too busy the bar is just fine (they will mix your drink or pour your wine) BUT when the Lounge is busy you end up standing along the bar with people several travellers deep... trying to get the bartender's attention. Once you have it it is very good - not sure if they are trying to control alcohol cost by not letting you "help yourself" but it certainly (only when the Lounge is busy as it often is) slows you down. I only had a 35 minute change of planes and could not get anything for the first 15minutes - waited at the bar got my wine drank half and had to leave. Again - it looks great but it is tougher if you are in a hurry. Staff still very courteous.

After a very long walk from check in through security and then into T2B (this is the terminal adjacent to the new Terminal 2 at Heathrow where Air Canada has its arrival/departure operations) we finally arrived at the Lounge; access is by elevator (lift) from the departure terminal gates to an upper floor. We found way finding signage lacking in this brand new terminal and directions to Air Canada's ML Lounge were no exception. We were absolutely exhausted by this time and looking forward to settling in for lunch before our 3 p.m. flight to YUL. The Lounge was very large and of course brand new. Seating was plentiful and the menu selection was excellent with a complete self-serve bar. There was a chef preparing various cooked meals however we just helped ourselves to more lighter fare as we knew we would be having lunch/supper on the flight in a few hours. Washrooms were excellent with private toilets and showers. There was also a business centre which we did not use n or did we use WiFi as it was not secure. We would definitely access this lounge again now that we know where it is.

My spouse and I were flying to LHR via YUL on Premium Economy fares so we were able to purchase Maple Leaf (ML) access for the day of our travel. This is a relatively new Lounge in Winnipeg's James Richardson International Airport which opened a new terminal in 2011. The Lounge is easy to find near Gate 9. Staff were not particularly friendly and just verified our boarding passes without comment. We got seating window-side and helped ourselves to beverages and breakfast prior to our flight to YUL. All amenities and services were very good and seating is plentiful and comfortable.

After a long and frustrating process getting through customs and security after our flight from LHR we were looking forward to accessing the domestic terminal ML Lounge before our next two flights home. As usual it was a challenge finding the Lounge and the few Air Canada employees we talked to just grunted and pointed to another annex of the domestic terminal to its location - still not clear. We walked a considerable distance from our departure gate to somewhere near Gate 2 to access the Lounge. We were greeted by the same indifference from Lounge staff we experienced in our previous three ML Lounge visits in our trip to the UK; our boarding passes were scrutinized and handed back to us without comment. We walked into a somewhat small lounge with dated furniture passengers lounging about everywhere (this was about 6:30 p.m.) and almost every seat occupied. We finally found a couple of hard chairs in the walkway between the window seats and airline-style gate seats in th e back of the Lounge. We went to the self-serve food area only to find it barely stocked mostly with appetizers. Very disappointing. We were looking forward to proper meal as we knew we would not get any food service on our two upcoming flights through to YWG. The washrooms were dirty dated and in poor condition (broken panels towels all over the place). The overall condition of this Lounge appeared to be one of neglect or indifference. This would not make a very good impression on AC's frequent travellers or international business travellers. We finished up as soon as we could and left for our gate. We looked for a comment card but could not find one and Lounge staff were busy with other passengers. By this time there was almost just standing room.

After a very long walk from Gate 5 to Gate 52 we finally found the Maple Leaf Lounge in the International area of the YUL terminal. We found way finding signage in YUL to be barely adequate and that is being generous. This also held true for finding this Lounge. Staff were polite but not overly friendly; they just checked our boarding passes and handed them back without even making eye contact. We entered a large brightly lit lounge but could not find a window table; we had to settle for a table in the computer area. As we had a three-hour wait before departing for YUL we had a good lunch of soup sandwiches salads and beverages. Menu selection was varied. Seating was comfortable and washrooms were clean. WiFi is available but not secure. There was a good selection of newspapers and magazines. We would definitely access this lounge again.

I arrived at this lounge and it was hard to find a seat. The food was horrible. Empty hot meal trays just nacho chips salad and dips. Molsen beer tap was broken wine selection of one white and one red.

EVA use the Air Canada Lounge in the new Terminal 2. A very nice airy new lounge at the new Terminal. It was very quiet when I was there 19:00-21:00 there was ample hot/cold food. The lounge is nice and bright/airy. There is a bar tender which in itself is not a problem but sometimes there was a wait while they were out clearing tables or taking orders. All in all a vast improvement than the old lounge that was used in Terminal 3.

We visited the Air Canada transborder Lounge on the 14th of Sept. We were very pleased with the service and facilities offered. We had a long lay over and enjoyed both the breakfast and lunch offered. A variety of beverages were available. The lounge was very clean and roomy.

BRU-YUL-SFO. We went out of our way to fly Air Canada back home from Europe. Had a 6-hour layover in Montreal which was nice. Easy access to the lounge staff speaks English and French (and possibly some other languages) quite fluently. Food in the lounge was not up to par (about 900 ml of cold pasta salad and some other similarly sized items were available for everybody). I went downstairs to the Burger King. Other than that however the internet is fast and functional there is a television and a wide selection of alcoholic beverages in an open-bar format. Not the best lounge but certainly not the worst.

The lounge of transhipment for flights to the United States. provides appropriate care. The Buffett is very good tasty including wide range of drinks. Wi Fi works and is fast. There are several workstation. The furniture is beautiful. In the room you stay comfortable all the time. A proper and respectful service with passengers. If you option Air Canada deserves to be prestigious.

The Maple Leaf Lounge in the International Section of Terminal 1 at Toronto's Pearson Airport is a pleasant lounge with lots of seating. The lounge has a good selection of drinks but the food selection is much less than what one gets in Europe or Asia. I was in the lounge in the evening (after 8:00pm) and they had noodles and a cold salad. They may have had soup as well. Cookies were available. The beverage supply is large and self serve. There are three Air Canada (Maple Leaf) Lounges at Toronto's Pearson Airport Terminal 1 one domestic one International and one for flights to the U.S. This review is for the international lounge which is used for Air Canada and Star Alliance members. In terms of layout and aesthetics this is a very pleasant lounge. It has a business area lots of seating showers and eating areas with big screen tvs. The newspaper and magazibne supply is huge The airport has free wifi; I'm not sure if the lounge has separate wifi. Most of the staff seem to be there to clean up rather than to help customers but the lounge is kept clean and front desk staff are fine. The view of the planes from this lounge is limited but it is a nice place to relax.

Have visited this lounge in the "rock wall" in the domestic area several times over the past few years this visit in March 2014 I noticed that the food selection had improved. I was there at 8am on a Friday morning for 1.5 hrs and aside from the usual cold cereal hot oatmeal make your own toast small muffins/pastries and fruit there was a covered hot container with small omelets hash browns and large home fries. The coffee machines are wonderful offering mochas  lattes cappuccinos etc. Also hot chocolate. The serving dishes were kept filled and there was someone going around picking up used plates/cups etc frequently. The lounge seemed very clean as well as the women's washroom. The lounge is large and was about 1/4-1/3 full all the time I was there. Good selection of newspapers and lots of different magazines. Wifi seemed to work fine the little I used it. Great view of the continuous action out on the tarmac!

I have a Priority Pass and on my way from CPT to BOS via LHR I had about 5 hours to kill. I thought I would use the lounge airside but after a 12 hour flight I wanted a shower and a light breakfast. This Air Canada Arrivals was heaven sent. It is just outside the arrivals hall to the left. Please watch out for signs because it is quite tricky to find. Once you are there the small but cosy lounge welcomes you with open arms. Good hot and cold food plus good coffee or tea a shower (very refreshing) and comfortable seats. Small if the place is crowded but at 8am it was very quiet.

My first experience of YYZ's T1 Domestic lounge got off to a bad start as the agent at the desk was engaged in a scintillating conversation with another agent regarding the closest gas stations to their homes. She never made eye contact offered any sort of welcome and simply handed back my boarding pass without so much as a thank you. Thanks Air Canada for making me feel like a valued customer! The lounge itself is attractive well groomed has ample seating and moderately appealing food choices. A far cry from the catering one would find in Star Alliance lounges in Europe or Asia but not bad by North American (United for example) standards.

Wow a bad terminal in a horrible airport with a terrible lounge. Small poor food poor seating tiny and overall as far as international lounges a real disappointment. The Starbucks on main level is much better.

The quality of internet access that the lounge offers is a joke. They expect Star Alliance Gold customers to pay $3.99 to use the internet because the free service they offer cannot even open basic websites. What's more embarrassing is that the free service offered by Vancouver airport is much faster and doesn't cripple your access to web services. Other Star Alliance members should return the favour for Air Canada visitors to their lounges. In a world where bandwidth has become as cheap as water it is ridiculous that Air Canada can get away with fleecing other Star Alliance customers.

Arriving in Toronto at about 1.00pm we had a very long layover since the departure to CPH was at 21.05. The lounge was ok but the food choices and quality were very disappointing. Sort of dry boring sandwiches and three different warm dishes - all tasteless. If we should have waiting time at Toronto airport another day we rather pay for food in one of the eating places in the terminal than eating in the lounge. For a business class lounge of a 4 star airline the food is not adequate and compared to Scandinavian Airlines lounge in Copenhagen and Chicago it's poor. Even the TAP lounge at Lisbon airport has better food quality.

Nice lounge quiet and good internet but needs to have dirty dishes picked up more often. Also their food offerings are poor. empty wine bottles and no staff to ask for assistance. Chips and hummus you need to scrape the bowl for. They need more staff and replace items more often. I still recommend it but if you need food go get it somewhere else first.

The lounge was physically fine but the snacks/food offerings were pathetic. A few applies and bananas sliced white bread for toast and pitchers of juice. I ended up with cereal and milk and thinking that there was great food for people flying coach right outside the doors. Also even with a sparsely populated lounge there was a line for the mens room because the mens room must apparently only cater to one person at a time.

I was surprised by the selection of quality food and alcoholic beverages. Being US-based I was able to compare the many differences between the US airline lounges with the quality of Air Canada. Maple Leaf Lounges are definitely the benchmark for other North American Airlines.

I used the lounge on 22nd December 2012 at around 8AM. The staff at the welcome desk worked very hard to solve a very tricky problem. Their knowledge and level of care was absolutely great. They solved a problem which could have ruined our long planned holiday. I was very impressed and thankful. If there would be a possibility to rate the level of "Standard of Staff Service" better then Excellent - I would do so. The Transborder Maple Leaf Lounge at Terminal 1 Toronto Airport was exceptional due to the superior staff.
This is a great place to be 2 hours before your flight very quiet not around a lot of people. Many drink choices band a lot of food choices very comfortable and relaxing.
The lounge near the rock wall was the one I enjoyed the most. Wonderful selection of drinks food selection decent but only light foods. WiFi was excellent.

Quiet peaceful and comfortable place to sit. Have never experienced it to be too busy. The decor is new and it is always kept clean. Food area has lots of space and selection is the best I have experienced of any North American airport. Despite all of the shortcomings of this airport the Maple Leaf Lounges here are by far the best experience.
Dirty no food selection crowded with no place to sit. Unappealing decor. Stayed 15 minutes and then left to sit in the public area.

Nice looking large lounge with comfortable seating. Nice greeting on entering. Very good selection of drinks but food options limited and poor. Carrot and celery sticks and mountains of crackers. Only hot option was an unappealing soup and this was at dinner time.

We went to this lounge first thing in the morning because we had an early flight. The are supposed to open at 5:00 am and the door was still locked and the lights off when we arrived. We were let in about 10 minutes after and the girl was just putting things out. There really wasn't a big selection of food. There was tea coffee juice and she put out bread for toast terribly sweet muffins (in packages) and flavoured bagels none plain. There was also cereal. That was about it. I would not want to go there again. The lounge seemed old and in need of an update.

Way too crowded! The place was packed at 4:30 and stayed that way when we left at 6:00. Two planes including ours had slight delays. The food selection was nice especially the Thai soup. Because it was so busy the cleaning staff had a lot of work and empty dishes sat for 20-30 minutes. There didn't seem to be a place for us to drop off our used plates. Good selection of magazines and newspapers.

A very disappointing lounge which I have used several times for the past four years. Nothing much has changed in the period. Granted is a domestic terminal lounge but given the number of people who use it it is far too small. There are many international passengers who connect at YVR but there is not even a shower for people to freshen up after a 10+hr flight! There is no separate area for people who want to take a rest and because of the large number of people present it is very crowded and noisy-- not much different from the terminal building itself. Food is pretty average and always the same salad and soup options (but nothing vegetarian!).

Very spacious lounge with lots of comfortable seating and pleasant ambiance. Good selection of drinks snacks vegetables and dips. I've only used it in the evening when they also offer good pasta dishes and some salads. Staff is friendly. Only critique is that internet connection is often rather slow.

This lounge is big and well designed. Business centre with printing. Great selection of food snacks and drinks. Comfortable leather chair with foot rest in a mood room makes you a little too relaxed! I wish they had dedicated wifi for the lounge rather than using the general airport wifi which is fine but slow. Boarding announcements in a non intrusive way. For me this is the best AC lounge.

Excellent Lounge for North American standards. Drink selection very good food is usually rather light (salads and soups) but good. The weak point is the breakfast which is just cereals muffins and toast without any cheese ham or similar. They have an espresso / cappuccino machine producing excellent coffee. Free internet connection fast for Air Canada Elites usually works well unless the lounge is packed which can happen during peak hours.

Very old school menu hasn't been updated in God knows how long. The dishwasher broke so plastic utensils styrofoam cups and plates were used instead. Despite there being 2 other lounges in the airport to bring equipment from. Air Canada service continues to crumble.

When YVR was a single terminal airport the Maple Leaf Lounges were larger, now there are three (domestic US/transborder international) and I was in the transborder lounge on this trip. Access up one floor in an elevator. Amenities are self serve but more generous and much tidier than Continental or United Airlines lounges. Comfortable seats and workstations. Limited snack buffet is well-attended to. Staff keeping things in order. Wifi the new system where some lounge users get (ostensibly) faster wifi access is silly. It was better when you could just boot up your machine tick the box and get on with things. Overall YYZ lounge is bigger. YYC is grottier. YHZ is tiny. YOW' is probably the nicest (but busiest). On balance I'll take ANY of the YVR lounges thanks.

I have used this lounge many times and love it. Spacious and modern with nice touches like original glass sculpture in the bathrooms and light but good food choices and self serve bar. A world apart from any US airline lounge I have been to where food means pre-packaged tasteless cookies and a pay bar.

This lounge is a complete joke - cramped poor food selection beyond carrot sticks tomatoes soup and stale looking bread. Some breakfast snack items are ok. Can mix your own drink - oh joy. Coffee and cappuccino is fair. Looks dated and worn. Staff moderately helpful. Embarrassing (my home airport) when compared to other airports around the world.

A disgrace there is no plausible reason to use this facility. The coffee is terrible food non-existent no showers apparently domestic has this for some reason and average business facilities. Staff at reception are friendly enough but that appears to be the limit of the hospitality. Wifi is now pointless as you can easily source it from many different services within the airport.

The lounge is within the acceptable range variety of food were served but some of them were poor in taste. The shower facility was very limited only 2 showers were provided and passenger need to ask the lounge staff to unlock the shower door. WI-FI and high-speed internet connection were provided computers and business facility were also available. Chairs were comfortable and few of them were recliners. Overall speaking the lounge is still fair but not the best one I've been to.

All Maple Leaf Lounges at Trudeau are appalling. Domestic is old and cold and needs a refit and the other lounges are a mess newspapers and used plates and wineglasses just left. I broke my rule and connected through Montreal yesterday. Considering the new Terminal One at Pearson is such a nice experience Montreal Trudeau is a disgrace.

The Maple Leaf lounge has been a very good "office away from the office" facility including free wifi a bowl of hot soup and the like. In a recent fit of penny-pinching Air Canada has started demanding that users purchase internet access using a credit card. It is not a huge sum - $10.00 - just enough annoy you especially when you know that you will have a fight with the accountants to claim it back. I sure hope that the pennies they accumulate from this change offset the costs associated with customer dissatisfaction.

This place hasn't changed for years. Shower rooms are large and clean but had a really bad smell - like the sewer had backed up. The staff are welcoming but if I hadn't arrived so early and knew that my hotel room would not be ready I think I would just go straight to the hotel. Food offerings really limited in a small crowded room.
One of the nicest lounges I've seen with great breakfast offerings and superb staff. And then there's the views!

I'm surprised at people complaining about food in Maple Leaf lounge. Air Canada provides comfort food (soup cookies bagels) free drinks internet access a great selection of newspapers and magazines. The lounge in Vancouver has a stunning view of the North Shore mountains - lounge in Edmonton has a fireplace - lounge in Ottawa is glass on 3 sides. Admittedly the domestic lounge in Toronto is often crowded with slow check-in. The international lounge there is soaring.

Rather disappointed with the lack of breakfast choices when I used this lounge for an early morning flight. Bread butter muffin and a small bowl of fruit which emptied very quickly and took the attendants ages to top up. Coffee and tea only beverage choices with just 1 jug of orange on display. The Maple Leaf lounge had a rather' stingy' feel overall would not use it again.

Very pleasant lounge close to our departure gate. Food somewhat limited but my daughter enthused about the soup (only hot dish on offer). Seating comfortable and ranged from lounge chairs to dining with a good few recliners as well. Business services were excellent with swift internet access. Sadly only two showers for the whole of this busy lounge and you have to ask the reception staff to unlock them and then wait while they find a cleaner to re-stock and clear up after the last occupant!

This is one of the poorest lounges I have visited. The seats are worn food on offer consisted of a bowl of soup (in fairness very nice) and some cheese and very tired looking salad. There are no showers in this lounge which really surprised me. Not much of an advert for Air Canada at all. Staff were enthusiastic and pleasant.

Buried in the basement of CDG this lounge gets extremely crowded at times. Two flights a day to Canada and if one is delayed then it is sitting room on the floor only. Food not bad croissants cheeses yogurts etc. for breakfast and some sandwiches later on in the day plus the usual array of drinks. The lone staff person was excellent although it is ridiculous that those of us with connections that we are going to miss because of delays cannot be rebooked onto another flight. We have to wait till we get to Canada to be rebooked making everyone very cranky.
Limited view of the apron. Newspaper/food/drink selections minimal. Good business facilities. Toilet facility inadequate and was not kept clean.

This small lounge is also used by Air France at times and quickly becomes overcrowded. The rest of Terminal 2 at LAX is even more congested. Public washrooms are located outside the lounge but are well-maintained. Good selection of self-serve beverages but food is limited to cheese and crackers. Large west-facing windows provide nice views but only two have pull-down shades. As a result the lounge becomes too hot. Tattered furniture needs replacing.

Very nice small lounge at Heathrow. Good continental breakfast available excellent showers and 2 computers. What makes this lounge special is the excellent staff friendly and helpful. Every time I use this lounge is it very empty could be because it is located outside the terminal a short walk from the arrivals area.

The Toronto Pearson lounge was not very good food wise. I guess they assume everyone would prefer to drink then eat. If you like alcohol then this is the place for you if you don't then take snacks with you.

This lounge was recently opened and is quite nice and very bright inside. It has almost 360 Degree windows which allow light in. As with most Maple Leaf lounges the food is almost non existent. I was there between 8-10AM and there was only some bread for toasting and some yogurt and granola. The business center was good with several computers connected to the internet and several places to dock personal computers. Overall I would say this lounge is much better than the old one.

This lounge is tucked away in a relatively quiet corner at the airport. The lounge was very small though at the time of my arrival it was quiet. I was politely welcomed by the young lady at the desk. However the choice of food was limited as they had little snacks left out on small individual plates that were very slow to be replenished. As I was not on a diet I was not very impressed. However if you are on a diet than this lounge is very helpful. The toilets were also located outside the lounge area which made it quite awkward as you have to ring at the door again to get back into the lounge. The place got very busy shortly before I left to board my flight and I can only imagine that if it had been busier people would have to scramble to get seats.

Lounge is boring and hardly anybody use it despite ample space. No alcoholic beverages offered, a huge fault. Good view. Good food with 4 hot dishes at the buffet. Coffee completely burnt and undrinkable. Not worth paying for (they charge 50 USD) - outside coffee shops much more cozy to engage with. No WiFi.

For the cost of annual membership (AUD $1,000) this Air Niugini lounge is a joke. While they've recently improved their lounge at the International terminal, the one at the Domestic terminal and throughout the rest of Papua New Guinea leaves a lot to be desired. A lot. The catering is basic, no international newspapers or magazines, no free WiFi (or any WiFi at all) and hard seats that make waiting for the ever delayed Air Niugini flights painful.

Nice little lounge. Showers available. You can pay to enter. Food available but not a great selection. Drinks available, alcoholic ones need to be paid for. Great on our trip over to Phuket as it was early morning & there weren't many people there but on our way home, it was very busy & a bit crowded with only uncomfortable seats left. The toilets are actually in the showers so if the two showers are being used, you can't get to the loo. Water wasn't cleaned up in showers after use so you had to navigate that.

Premium passengers on AirAsia X now have access to the Red Lounge at KLIA. They don't tell you this on check in but I did see it on their website. It's a no frills lounge, in keeping with the AirAsia theme. It's got quite a contemporary feel to it but it is small and badly signposted. There are soft drinks (only coke and Sprite) and hot beverages. They mentioned alcohol can be purchased but the staff at the front desk were too busy chatting to themselves so I didn't bother to ask. There are showers and toilets complete with the Malaysian wet floors! The food on offer is very basic and not appealing at all. As lounges go, it's quiet but that's all. You can get in if you pay RM79 but it's not worth it.

The Terminal 2 Power North lounge was a bit far from the security gate and on the extension side of Terminal 2. It was really large, new, shiny with nice view over the tarmac. Flight information was well displayed on a big screen. Seat was comfortable. Free WiFi was fast. Only drink was offered, snacks were available at a fee.

The (finally opened!!) Mera Business Lounge is now one of two options in T-4 International when accessing with a Diners Club card. We arrived, quickly checked-in and found it to be rather devoid of clients. (this did change as time wore on) Still having it's "new lounge smell", it was clean, well appointed and stylish with seating for groups and solo pax. We grabbed seats in the far corner adjacent to one of the two restrooms. (one has a men's shoe buffer!) Once settled, we began grazing the various food offerings and was not disappointed. Followed up with a trip to bar at the opposite end and settled in to relax and duh... update all our envious Facebook friends. Eventually moved over to the bar end to check it out as well. We did decline the "waiter service" as I felt that ordering at the bar allowed one to be precise and confident that the order was going to be correct. A good place to leave those last few Pesos found in your back pocket that you forgot about. Overall, we had a pleasant time and look forward to being able to visit again someday. As a side note, the "other" lounge next door was available, but could only visit one. This one is "dedicated" as well to Air Transat pax who have booked a Luxury holiday package which includes a chit(s) for lounge access.(ours was only, "Distinction") (and unfortunately, I can only post 5 of the dozen photos I took)

Walked out of the lift at T3 Toronto Pearson International pier to quite the surprise. The entire Plaza Premium lounge had "relocated" to the previous BA lounge area next door. A complete revamp to what we previously enjoyed. Still has the window seats we prefer, but still lots of tables for proper dining. A much larger bar area that serves the free stuff as well as paid specialty drinks. (there's a menu card on the bar) Early morning buffet was acceptable, the toaster area is now off to the opposite side. A whole back section was closed off, but will open as the need for more space is required. Wi-Fi was good, the password is on a card up on the bar. The "unisex" restrooms take a bit of getting used to but each toilet stall has it's own washbasin as well as a common area one. Only issue was that one bar server (a trainee perhaps?) was a bit lacking in her English language skills, a women who I took to be a supervisor was much better to deal with. Overall, as much as I will miss our oft used "usual seats" from before, we are quite content with using the Plaza Premium for all our early morning T-3 departures. However, evening flights will be in the KLM Crown Lounge next door as it's also with Diners Club.

A very private lounge which makes it a pleasant place. Good products and very good alcohol. What a pleasure to travel with a French company in Oceania. Only downside sanitary very average. There is a shower but they do not want to provide you with a towel if you are not in transit. Really! What a pity!  FR: Un lounge assez confidentiel ce qui en fait un endroit agréable De bon produits et de très bon alcool Quel plaisir de voyager avec une compagnie française en Océanie Seul bémol les sanitaires dont très moyens Il y a une douche mais il ne souhaite pas vous fournir une serviette si vous n êtes pas en transit Vraiment ! Quel dommage !

Very basic lounge. Very poor service. No food. No one cared. Took over an hour for dirty wrappers, empty cans to be cleared. You are better off to stay in the pay as you go part of the airport. Patrons kept asking when any food was coming. Staff could only say it was on its way. Maybe it was coming from Noumea city over 40km away!

It is difficult to imagine this is a business lounge. Poor food and drink choice and press/magazine nearly absent. Definitely I won't recommend this lounge. I am a frequent flyer (Flying Blue Platinum for life). It is one of the worst lounges (maybe the worst) I have experienced.

Qantas outsource the lounge in Noumea to Air Caledonie. Lounge a bit on the small side for two aircraft at once but very comfortable good runway views excellent food and drink selection and the one staff member very welcoming. All in all a good offering and a nice change from the standard Qantas Club. The only downside is toilet/bathroom is outside the actual lounge.

It should be noted that this lounge is operated by the airport as far as I can tell, and used by several airlines.  Lounge has a soft furnished area and a terrace overlooking the concourse and shops. Food choices very limited. Peanuts, crisps, muesli bar type stuff, some cake stuff and old looking sandwiches, etc. if I recall correctly. None of it looked appetising. There were tea and coffee making facilities and other beverages available. It was just all so unkempt and not particularly clean. The restrooms come in for a lot of criticism here. We were in the lounge for a significant amount of time. The waste bins in the restrooms were full when we arrived and full when we left. The cleaning staff tending to just hang about rather than make any real effort at tidying/cleaning. A totally unloved lounge.

This is a small, comfortable lounge (quite big for the size of the airport and low daily number of international flights). We were travelling on the last flight out of Tahiti that night and the food provided was of good quality and adequate in proportion to the number of passengers. There were plenty of hot and cold beverages. Wi-Fi is available in the lounge. The lounge and the restrooms were tidy and clean and the staff were very pleasant. A good way to end our visit to French Polynesia.

This lounge is used by multiple airlines, provided by LAX until the changes are made to Lounge Services. A large surface area overlooking the runway at LAX comfortable seating with tables. Various forms of seating from single chair to couch. Food choices minimal just peanuts, pretzels however full open bar, coffee and tea making facilities. Had four internet computer stations for use. Entrance to the lounge is on the second floor up the escalator via the Chinese Fast Food Restaurant. I would not call this a "First Class Lounge".

The Adria Airways Business Lounge is located just a few minutes from the departure gates at Ljubljana Airport. I was greeted with a smile and took a seat in one of the comfortable fauteuils which offered some privacy and plug sockets. The snack bar did not offer a great choice of food, however, the selection of drinks was good.

There are 2 separate areas with arm chairs and TV for relaxing and working the other with other arm chairs PC computer TV bar and sitting area. There are newspapers and magazines also some airline magazines. Decoration is fresh and modern. It is clean and well maintained. Bottled drinks coffee machine cheese and salad sandwiches and sweets. This is a very small airport serving about 20 flights a day and the lounge is fine and over the quality of other airlines I visited in the past. If they provide a better coffee machine and a wider choice of snacks it would be quite an interesting lounge to relax.

The ANA Terminal 2 Lounge is the worst lounge I have ever been to. They defeat the exclusivity of the lounge by opening it to Premium Economy Customers yet alone all the credit card and Star Gold customers and their guests makes this place an utter zoo. It is nice for the Premium Economy and credit card customers but it comes at the expense of the Business Class customers who the lounges are primarily supposed to cater to on an industry level. I had a 9 hr layover at Haneda and you would think by having long connection times from North America to Southeast Asia, ANA would create a nice and comfortable for their Business Class customers. The staff are very not personal and reserve. Shower wait times were 3 hours and once you did get a shower they kept making announcements. There were dirty dishes all over the place I will never havea layover at Haneda again.  From a business aspect it makes a Business Class Customer question why they should be paying more just to have the same lounge as Premium Economy. Their flight connections from Haneda are horrible too. ANA inflight service was a B+ but their Lounge is an F.

Please keep in mind that the lounges for international passengers are totally different from the others for domestic passengers. For example, when you visit in the morning, the former serves some food suitable for breakfast while the latter does nothing, except for a packet of arare, or Japanese rice crackers. I guess what ANA intends domestic passengers to do is as follows: ANA prepares such drinks as water, coffee, tea and beer, but on the other, they should buy some food and bring in. Many shops selling various kinds of food stand in the domestic terminal.

This ANA lounge is one of the best lounges in terms of overall quality. The highlight was how spacious, clean, quasi-luxurious the showers were. Not much wait time was amazing. The water functions had extra message nozzles etc which were unique. The food/drinks variety wasn't high, but the fresh & excellently live-cooked ramen/Udon made up for it. The ambience was another amazing thing: there's something so calming and pleasant about Japanese interior design... The staff were so polite and kind as well. No wonder ANA is 5 stars!

I discovered the morning period (10am ish) is the busiest with lots of ANA flights departing at the same time. I think this lounge is practical but a far cry from the best ANA has to offer. Comfort wise it is a simple lounge with different choices for seating. Except for dining chairs. You somehow are expected to keep your own area clean, and the food offering is very lacking, like the dining chairs and tables. The only hot options are curry chicken with rice or Yakisoba and "Vegetarian Meatballs." I don't like ANA's Chicken Curry. The saving grace of the lounge has to be the beer machine and the largest selection of spirits I have ever seen.  I felt staff are a bit cold and robotic and  confusing, saying "We don't make announcements, please keep track of time when your flight boards" but then 15 minutes later the same lady says "We would like to welcome all passengers travelling to Beijing to board now." It does appeal to everything the Japanese business traveller needs, phone booth, smoking room and large selection of alcohol.  So if you're hungry and you have star alliance gold in Kansai Airport, you're going to have to wait until your flight takes off because there really isn't any real dining options past security and the lounges have rubbish food.

A hot buffet is provided in the lounge, along with a wide selection of sake and plum wine. There is also a counter for ramen and udon. The lounge is fairly quiet but can get crowded during the morning hours.

Travelling with ANA I used this Lufthansa lounge which has a sterile atmosphere, good selection of magazines, friendly staff but choice of food very limited and choice of drinks poor (beer and wine only). Good wifi and availability of European power sockets, reserved corner for first class passengers pathetic.

The food selection at this handling agent lounge, "Club International Lounge" is more barebones than restaurant offerings around Gate S. It has 2 soup offerings (miso and creamy tomato), pita bread, sweet breads, cookies and candies, coffee machine, bar, instant cup noodles, and juice in plastic bottles. I miss the sandwiches and warm meal stations done before passengers. The space is tight - near over capacity - with limited access to electric outlets. It is far different from ANA's own Narita lounge and an uncomfortable way to start a long haul flight.

Nice lounge, but at night (9 pm to midnight) the international ANA lounge is overcrowded, difficult to find seating for 2 persons travelling together. Good choice of drinks and sake, food quite weak and limited choice, no desserts, staff extremely helpful. Seating is comfortable, WiFi working very well, ultra clean toilets and facilities in general, atmosphere quite sterile, no design efforts.

I used the ANA Lounge in the late afternoon. This lounge is also used by Star Alliance airlines. There are several ANA lounges to choose from in Narita and I used the one closer to the gate of my connecting flight. First impressions were that the lounge was large, spacious and airy with many seats available. The lighting was dim and soothing though slightly warm. There is a good selection of food to choose from. What's really impressive for me was the cook-to-order ramen (4 options to choose from) and chicken curry. Guests would have to place their orders with the staff who then hands out a buzzer which vibrates when the food item is ready for collection. I waited not more than 5 mins for my ramen to be ready at this very popular counter. Guests are definitely spoilt for choice at this lounge. It would be hard to not overeat.

I visited the ANA Lounge last time early morning before taking off to JFK. Surprisingly even on this hour the lounge was pretty packed and even if we found a seat for two, the overall impression was pretty crowded and noisy. The lounge is situated on the second floor of the departure terminal and has limited view on the tarmac and docking gates. The decoration is is the typical grey and blue colors of ANA in a very decent manner. The lounge offers a wide variety of wine, alcoholic and non-alcolohic drinks but is very poor when it comes to food. I wouldn't bet on having lunch or dinner before taking the flight, because it would be a very light one. The overall noisy ambiance and the high traffic of arriving and departing customers is also not really creating a relaxing environment before the flight. Big advantage is that the lounge is very close to the departure gate so you can wait til the last moment before boarding the plane.

ANA use the Thai Airways lounge in Bangkok, and the counter staff were professional and attentive. There was a staff member standing before the counter (and another behind the counter) who immediately came to assist and checked my ticket which was appreciated. It is nice to have instant attention while the staff behind the counter is attending to other guests. It is a long lounge and was about 40-50% occupied when I was there. The size is 2,410 sq.m. and is able to accommodate 314 passengers. There were western and asian food options available. Chicken congee was served at the hot food station. There was also a machine that makes mini pancakes at the press of a button. Ample staff presence on hand to clear used plates and glasses. Free wifi (password required) available.

The ANA domestic lounge at Tokyo Haneda is conveniently located directly behind the security check. You cant't miss it when you use the dedicated Priority Check in for Star Alliance Gold customers. The lounge is very clean and stylish. Almost a bit sterile. However, the staff is polite, friendly and very efficient. Unfortunately, snack only consisting of a few crackers, but the drink selection was more than enough (including a wide selection of alcoholic bevarages).

Whenever I fly into Tokyo Narita my choice of lounges is either the United Club or the ANA lounge. I inevitably head for the ANA lounge. Although both lounges offer similar amenities, I think the wifi at ANA is better and the food offerings are much more diverse and interesting at ANA. There are two ANA lounges, one at gate 52 and the other further afield in the terminal. The gate 52 lounge is much larger and always more crowded, but it is also more conveniently located. On my latest visit, a sushi chef was making sushi to order! Amazing, truly. All sorts of Japanese inspired dishes are available as are a slew of traditional sakes. It is a treat. There are nice showers (United also offers very nice showers), but you usually have to wait on line to get in. That, and the fact that the lounge is generally packed, are the only drawbacks. Still, it is a comfortable, well-designed, service-oriented lounge. I would say it is another feather in the ANA cap for good service and a good product.

At Tokyo Narita Airport, Singapore Airlines utilizes ANA lounges which I visited. ANA offers different lounges for the class ticket or member status that you hold and for this trip I was on Business Class. The business class lounge for the gates I was at was located on the 2F, unfortunately signage directing to the 2F was not well marked. Basically you will want to take the escalator down from the level that the gates are on since that is 3F, the lounge on the 4F is the First Class/Gold Member only. One of the key things about ANA lounges over other Business Class lounges offered by other airlines is that it is kept meticulously clean. There is also plenty of seating especially with padded arm chairs. There is a good selection of foods available along with drinks, which are typically available from automatic dispensers (including beer). There was also a sake bar available in this lounge. This location also offered shower facilities down the hall from the rest rooms. Overall this lounge was one of the better locations that I have spent time in. One last item of note, but if you need a place to talk on the phone I suggest that you ask for where the seating area is where you can use your mobile phones otherwise you will be quickly asked by staff and the overhead PA to not use your phone in the majority of the lounge as a courtesy to other guests.

A little bit old but overall nice lounge. They have not only nice showers, but also free massage chairs, business center (including free printing) facilities. Good collection of Japanese sake as well as choices of curry and noodles over the counter. ANA's lounge at Narita may not look as appealing as that inside Tokyo Haneda international terminal (newer one) but overall touch of service is just amazing.

This is the Star Alliance lounge for the international terminal, operated by ANA All Nippon Airways. The lounge is a bit dated in terms of furniture, but it is clean, easy to find, and efficient. It grants a great views of some of the gates. Restrooms are clean and comfortable, though insufficient for a lounge that can become rather crowded at times. It offers a protected smoking area. Staff is very friendly and helpful. Drinks and food selection is limited. They have a great tap beer dispenser, like in all ANA lounges. Food selection is very limited.

Large, well-appointed lounge with good selection of food and beverages. Reception staff was very pleasant and helpful. On the day of my visit it was quite crowded in the late afternoon as there were multiple international flights leaving in early evening; after the crowd was gone they closed the section at the farther end which was a pity as I found that section to be more secluded and nicer.

The lounge had a very bright, stylish, and spacious layout. The food was very good, having a variety of local food, fruits, and sweets -the green tea cakes especially! The best feature of the lounge however were the massage chairs. These were probably the most advanced chairs I've ever seen and had interesting features for the feet, sides, and hands - a very relaxing experience.

ANA's International business class lounge at Haneda Airport is always well stocked with their extremely tasty Original Chicken curry, though the selection of alcoholic drinks is poor and there was no sparkling wine or champagne! Also, there was no fresh milk when I visited.  The lounge staff however are very helpful and attentive.

I used the facilities of the lounge on my transit from Chicago to Jakarta. I had to pay in JPY of USD50 equivalent since I was flying economy class. They only receive cash payment. It is quite expensive to my finding, but worth the money spent. The lounge is quite big and very clean. It comprised of two main halls. The first hall near the entrance is quite packed. The first hall offers both sofa and bar seating for lone traveler. However I found the bar seats are quite tight. There are power outlets at every seat. Food served at buffet station are quite limited, yet we can order a decent options of freshly prepared Japanese food at the noodle station. There are a wide variety of drinks available (spirits, including varieties of Japanese sake, coffee, and soda dispenser). I favor the coffee a lot. If you like reading, there are a wide variety of Japanese and international newspapers and magazines available. I found that the toilet and shower rooms are very convenient and clean. Luxurious amenities are provided to ensure you are pampered and refreshed for your next flight. If you decide to take a shower, be cautious about the timing as the queue is quite long. The attendant gave me a remote caller to notify me my turn. This lounge is very recommendable for long haul travelers to freshen up.

I recently visited the ANA suite lounge at T1 Narita airport, as FF star alliance gold member flying economy. The reception service was excellent. Multiple people welcoming you with the most polite and efficient Japanese service. The lounge is huge and offers spaces for working or relaxing and also private spaces for sleeping. The food variety is not that much but just enough to be satisfied. You can also place an order for your choice of noodles, cooked on the spot for you. They offer also shower facility and concierge services.

I visited this lounge on 28 May on my way to Tokyo Haneda. Very nice lounge with nice view and plenty of light. Comfy chairs and plenty of power sockets. Packs left from previous customers were not clean up meaning that some desks had considerable amount of dirty glasses snack packs etc. Very good internet connection reasonably fast and reliable. Small selection of drinks. No food whatsoever only small snacks. Similar to American lounges not European or Asian ones.

Neat and superb. They even have free printing service high-tech and hygienic shower booths. Food can be improved but compared to other Star Alliance lounge like old Silver Kris at LHR terminal 3 and United Club this ANA lounge is much better.

Far superior to any lounge of US carriers at either Narita or Haneda. A wide variety of food offerings allowing one to have a complete meal before boarding. A bit crowded at times but the staff are helpful and courteous.
It was great with all the new stylish shower room and the catering. I loved the food as well as the shower room. The only thing to improve on would be WIFI where I had to work.
Excellent wifi helpful staff large spacious decent F&B selection. One of the better star alliance international lounges and it certainly is superior to lounges outside Asia.

What an excellent lounge at their home base spacious good service and delicious food everywhere! I was impressed by the noodle bar where you can order your choice of hot meals. Great Wi Fi quite a comfortable experience. It's recommended to spend some time to experience this lounge if you ever fly with them or on Star alliance flights.

Very crowded and when I asked staff she mentioned she would help me look for a seat. She forgot about me. Food was okay. Shower is a nice touch but could be better. No service after that and worried about my luggage. Crowded and kids - I expect a lounge to be a quiet place to work or chill out before boarding a flight. If you want to work here forget about it. They have the famous ANA curry.
One of the best lounges I have ever been to. Great food and drinks courteous and efficient staff and excellent shower facilities.

Very slick and comfortable lounge spacious and quiet with a separate cordoned off area to rest on an armchair to soothing music and relaxing fragrance. Wide range of food choices including freshly cooked noodles on demand. Clean bathroom facilities (I did not use the shower) though there are no barriers separating the urinals. There is a separate business section with cubicles and comfortable chair and desk for you to work. Staff very courteous and friendly. The downside is there are no windows so no view of the outside and of airplanes. And the internet connectivity is poor/non-existent in certain areas of the lounge most frustratingly in the business work area!

Decor is minimalist in the extreme but pleasant enough. Plenty of space and privacy with separate work areas. Hot towel and drink of your choice served. The Satellite 4 and Satellite 5 lounges are virtually identical so there is no reason to choose one over the other though the Satellite 4 lounge may be a little quieter. The food choices were uninspiring and not particularly extensive.

ANA moved operations to terminal 3. Ad hoc airline lounge located in the small cafe/bar next to gate area. Cafe provided free wifi access and served mediocre hot/cold snacks and alcoholic beverages. The cafe opens to the departure area and is not a lounge where one can relax work or read.
The Wine and Sake choice are excellent good quality. Choice of food is not extensive but okay. The lounge is very large and seating are plentiful. Showers excellent with individual amenities.
Decent lounge. It had a good variety of food. The comfort level wasn't that great but staff were nice and welcoming. Wi-fi connection was good but there was no TV.

Very large nice design good selection of drinks of all kinds (though the sake bar was not stocked properly as many bottles empty!) and a comfortable experience. The massage service is inconvenient. You cannot book ahead of time and massage attendants are busy when you try to book at the lounge when you check-in so it makes it impossible. They should get a dedicated staff in order to make it a real amenity not just a fake one. In its own right a decent lounge experience but does not compare to the JAL Sakura Lounge at Narita which is superior on all accounts.

Very good lounge for the US! Large decent food with some variety decent drinks on offer too. Free wifi access shower rooms available seemed new or newly refurbished. Only complaint would be that there were not enough toilets available. A good experience and something to look forward to when going in and out of LAX - a rather bad airport.

Really enjoyed this lounge. Lots of room free internet use. The food selection was great. There was sandwiches sushi hot noodles lots of snacks. Very comfortable. Not very many magazines to read though.

Understated and quiet, I really like this lounge. Accessible to certain Amex Card holders, it is a sanctuary from the depressing surroundings of Melbourne Airport. Not exactly First Class, however, the free snacks are edible, drinks are nice enough and service is pleasant. The front desk person was kind enough to mind my luggage whilst I went back to the Duty-Free shop for some iPhone accessories. Wifi is good, it's not crowded and full of screaming kids, and a far more pleasant experience than the rest of the airport or the 3rd world feel of a Qantas flight across the Pacific. They have showers and private facilities available, all clean and well maintained. The only reservation I have about this lounge is that too many people may latch on to it.

Beautiful brand new Centurion lounge opened a week ago. It is a real upgrade for the Phoenix lounge scene that was mostly inexistant before. It is spacious, offers various zones, some very cozy and quiet. The food offering may be lighter than other Centurion lounges though time of visit (mid-afternoon) may be the reason. Looking forward to enjoying that lounge when I fly AA out of PHX.

Normally I would start my journey with a Qantas/Partner Lounge but thought I try something different. Due to my credit card I had a couple of free entries into the Amex Lounge at Sydney Airport. I did do some research and thought it could be a decent space to relax before the flight, and it definitely was not ideal. The space is way too small with the amount of people that is given access. It was not tidy and team members were not consistently cleaning. Plus it was very warm with the windows shining the sun through. I didn't try the food but it was very selected, but the coffee was decent. It's starting to show age, management really needs to start expanding the lounge.

I use this lounge pretty often, and although it is most of the times crowded they have always good food, good beverages and good mood to attend everybody. You can have full breakfast at morning with specialty coffees, and at lunch you can get a good salad, soup and a sandwich. It is not very spacious however since it has a big window facing the runways you don’t really noticed the size of the room. I am very happy with most of the American Express Centurion lounges.

Very pokey for the large number of people in there. Not many seats, all crowded together, some of them were facing the entrance hall where people check in. No real air conditioning to speak of. Only 1 toilet in the men's, 2 in the ladies. No shower facilities. One choice of hot food, a few sandwiches, a few cakes and one choice of salad. Not worth the $50+ to enter. In comparison Heathrow Airport's Plaza lounge is fantastic. Lovely food, lots of choice, plenty of seats, newspapers to read. Bar and shower facilities.

The American Express lounge in Sydney international airport was an interesting experience and venue. The view is great, looks onto tarmac and you can watch the planes come and go. The lounge is small and seating is limited so you may need to be flexible and share with others. Food choices was limited but fresh as the made small batches of the main meals and just kept refreshing it. All drinks are part entry fee. Staff are friendly and very attentive too.

This was my first visit to the American Express Centurion Lounge at SFO. It has a beautiful entry and check-in was fast. The food was plentiful and good. Bartenders were very friendly, though champagne is only available to Centurion card holders. Platinum card holders are limited to sparkling wine. There's also a "wine tour of California" that is self-serve. Location was a bit small, and fairly crowded both times I was there. Bathrooms were also on the small side. It's the best lounge I've been in. My only complaint is the size.

This location is among the D gates, which I'd never visited. It's a much nicer terminal than the C gates. This is also a larger location than SFO. While it was crowded for my first visit, food and drinks were well stocked and bar service was fast. Food was great. There's no self-serve wine like in SFO. Staff attentive and friendly. Nice collection of spaces for socializing, sleeping, or working. First impression: the front doors look a bit beaten up and worn. A little paint would make a notable difference. The Centurion Lounges alone almost make the American Express Platinum card worth its annual fee.

American Express has made a smart decision by opening their own lounges and making sure that the customers come first. Today I had a massage and then an amazing dinner. Thank you to American Express for caring about their members.

Went there first and waited about 10 min for a place to sit. We finally gave up and went to the United Club which was crowded but we could find a seat. Not a big deal since access is granted with my card. I would have been furious had I paid for access.

Nothing had changed in the 3 1/2 months since my previous visit. It's a very small lounge subject to overcrowding and unless there's a construction project I doubt things will change. On the plus side it makes virtually any airline club I've been to look good. It's one small step up from sitting in the departure area. I was happy I finally found a place to visit when someone left.
