Small and not as comfortable as most airline lounges but it's one of the few options outside of security. As we were connecting from an international to a domestic flight we went here. It was overflowing with people waiting some sleeping (sometimes oblivious to the amount of space they were taking up). Due to an absence of sufficient seating some people sat on the chairs by the 3 PC stations making those unavailable to others. One unisex bathroom. It was rather warm inside. The process to access WiFi was unduly complicated: had to go through a long online sign-up procedure to register with the third party commercial service used by the club.

The lounge was very crowded and the staff was inattentive. They came to the table and cleared about 1/3 of the dirty glasses kicked luggage aside and were generally unpleasant and disorganized. The lack of space is the biggest issue but they could make this much better by clearing and cleaning promptly. The food is okay but not great. Overall this is just marginally better than sitting in the regular waiting area and less pleasant than sitting in a restaurant.

This lounge is before security above the gates for United/ British Airways (depending on time of day). It is handy if you've arrived at the airport early and check in is not available otherwise if you have access to other lounges air side you'll probably find those better. There is no WiFi in the lounge however there are 3 computers provided they were in constant use through my visit. There are no showers and just a single toilet for each sex dental floss and mouth wash are provided. Small selection of food and drinks available.

Small but comfortable and quiet lounge next to the domestic departure area (I believe there is also one in the increasingly-seldom-used international departures area). You just need to show your AE gold (or higher) card and show your boarding pass. Staff alerted us when our flight was boarding (you can also see it fairly easily since the lines for some gates are right outside the door). A limited selection or snacks and drinks and one or two PCs for Internet use. All in all basic but probably the most comfortable place in the airport.

Club is fairly small but the only option we found we could use before a domestic departure (used a consolidated "VIP" club when departing on an international flight). A few chairs and sofas which could become crowded during peak times. Very limited selection of snacks but some nice sweets at least. Teas and coffees but no alcohol. No WiFi that I could find but there were three PCs avilable for free use (one had technical problems) and another area with one unmarked cable connection for use with one's PC (connectivity was better with that than with the PCs). One TV with local news station and a large screen showing flight departures and arrivals (this did not seem to be updated at times). Lounge is at the far end of Terminal 1; a rather long walk from Terminal 2. Few airport staff seemed to know where the lounge was.

I concur with the former comment. Either they didn't refurbish the Amex lounge or no result was visible. Clean but empty. Just a place to seat a rest room and nothing to eat. No internet connexion. I went out.

Easy checkin. Its not as packed even if the airport is busy. They have 3 entrees, veggies, pork and pasta. Some pastries and sandwiches. I was expecting more of authentic Korean Meal. The plug are a little bit worn out. Seats are pretty comfortable. Easy to navigate in the airport

Very spacious lounge, quiet atmosphere, comfortable seating and good views on the tarmac and runways. Choice of food is very limited, no comparison with Thai Airlines in Bangkok, and selection of alcoholic drinks limited, with no attendants to prepare cocktails.

Used this lounge as Emirates uses this lounge service at ICN. An appalling state of food options and customers in the lounge are having instant ramen noodle . Bar and beverage options are a bit better though.

As Gold Member Star Alliance I was granted entrance, so I won’t complain too much. It is a very nice looking lounge, but quite underwhelming related to food selection. Alcoholic drinks selection is quite modest too, but as it was morning I enjoyed some coffee (which was ok). What is offered is a bit disappointing considering Seoul Incheon Airport is Asiana’s home base. One thing was really excellent: their shower facilities! Clean, relatively spacious and comfortable with all amenities one needs.

Seats are comfortable. The reclined seats are limited though. Food is okay, they don't serve hot soup but sandwiches are good. The drinks are accessible especially the alcoholic ones. The toilets are clean.

The lounge area is huge but poorly designed and regulated. We all love enough space to stretch out and feel comfortable. However, this space is just not good. In cubby style areas 1 person takes up space that 5-6 could easily enjoy. Then the chairs are taken up and the only place left is the floor or hardwood benches -  it would go a long way to have these areas monitored and kept the interest of the many in consideration.

Asiana Airlines use the Thai Airways lounge at Phuket airport. It's the smallest lounge I've ever been to. It could not hold more than 50 people at a guess, which is why I suppose the information says that should it be busy, you may have to queue up and wait your turn. It felt more like a domestic airport lounge. It's obviously not meant for long layovers. However, small though it is, it was one lovely little place. The design, colours, decor and mood lighting were just beautiful. The magenta orchids spread around also blended nicely with That Airways colour scheme. There were USB ports at every seat and connecting to the Internet was swift. There was no extensive dining, just fresh finger food. They did have hot Shrimp Congee which was delicious, and I had to resist a third helping as dinner would be served on my flight. Similarly, no wines or spirits, only soft drinks and beer. The staff were extremely friendly, chatty and happy to serve drinks at your seat. Perfect for an hour visit.

Incheon International Airport Terminal 1 - I found two lounges located at different areas of the terminal, both which I visited on my outbound and return flights. My expectations were high, although a little disappointed. On the positive side, the lounges were large, with good comfortable furnishings. I only had to wait 10 minutes for a shower going out and no waiting at all during transit. Very clean and the staff were constantly tidying up the areas. One lounge had rest areas, but were all occupied. The other had cosy semi private cubicles you can stretch out on, and with views towards the runway, which was excellent. As I had a very long layover, I spent most of my time moving from one area to another. But dining was not enjoyable. The food was absolutely bland and an inadequate selection. There were tiny portions of finger food and very meagre hot (rather warm) items, and a chef that prepared Pasta for you! I was hoping for some delicious Korean dishes, but not so. And Asiana, please don't offer cheap peanuts as a snack with drinks. It should be Cashews and Almonds for a high end airline. However, I did enjoy my stay, it's just that I felt this airline could have provided more in terms of cuisine.

Pretty big lounge with two compartments. Both of them are quite spacious and big offering additional working desks, massage stool corners and showers. Nevertheless the lounge is over-crowded at peak times, since the lounge is open for quite all business travellers regardless their airlines. The lounge is not exclusive for star alliance. Food offering is more then average but not top excellent.

Well recommended, The shower room is clean, the toilet is ok, the seating is great and very comfortable. My kids sleep for 4 hours in sofa, The food is excellent, morning breakfast served around 7 am, lots of choices of hard liquor. I will recommend this lounge.

I had a very long transit in Seoul and spent the day in the lounge. The lounge was spacious and comfortable, the range and quality of the food was good. WiFi worked well and I managed to achieve what I wanted to do. There were quiet areas and while a little busy at times managed the number of people who visited well. Late in the afternoon I had a shower to freshen up for the flight to Almaty. The shower and the toilets were very clean.

We arrived at Seoul Incheon in the early morning hours with a six year old who had slept just a couple hours facing an 11 hour layover. We headed to Asiana Airlines business class lounge to rest. Unfortunately, there is nothing in the lounge except sitting chairs and fairly uncomfortable ones at that. I asked the attendant if there was somewhere to sleep and was told no. So, my son and I slept on the filthy floor for a couple hours, and my husband did not sleep at all. I then left the lounge and discovered there are these awesome rest and relax free sleeping areas in the terminal that look incredibly comfortable. I was really disappointed that we did not just use those - which are accessible and free to all travelers. It seems really weird that Asiana's business class lounge would offer its travelers a worse experience than that available to all other travelers. They should replace half the chairs with the same sleeper seats that are available elsewhere in the airport. The food was not good either - a salad bar, toast, cereal, nuts, a couple juices. The shower rooms were nice a but those too are available to all travelers in this airport, so the lounge is not even worth visiting except maybe to grab a drink.

There are two Asiana Airlines business lounges at Seoul Incheon. I looked in briefly at the lounge in the main concourse and then moved on to the satellite terminal from which my TG flight was departing. Although the location suggests that this would be a great plane-spotting area ( and it is for the departure gates and public areas ), the lounge itself is an interior space with no views at all. The food choices at breakfast time were limited to fruits, pastries, and salads. The lounge in the main concourse had a chef preparing egg dishes, but alas, there was no chef in the satellite lounge. Beverage choices were even more meager. There was one bottle of red wine and several options for liquor - no champagne and no rum. Because security and emigration formalities take so long at ICN, I had limited time in this lounge. I decided to abandon the lounge idea, board my flight at first call, and enjoy TG business class pre-departure service

Asiana Airlines business class lounge at Incheon International Airport with good ambience. Good choices of beverages - tea, coffee and beers. The food is quite disappointing. Kimchee with tofu, fried egg and fried rice. That's it. Asiana is a 5-star airline and their aircraft and onboard services are all great. They should've put much more effort in adding variations to their flagship lounge at Incheon

I've used the Asiana lounges a couple of times, this time in the main terminal, and they are very good. Showers are available, seats are plentiful and comfortable and there are large luggage lockers. Oh and very good wifi is available. The only minor criticism is that the food and non-alcoholic drink selection is a little limited.

It was great experience at Asiana First Class Lounge at Seoul Incheon Airport. Many comfortable seats and chairs with quiet and space. Video room, business room with high speed wifi, printer and many computers. You do not need to wait to take shower, just go in and enjoy shower with towels, shampoo, dryers and more. Food and drinks are amazing. Many variety healthy food with great wine and champagne. You can even order some hot noodle soup if you are hungry. Staffs are so kind and nice. One of the best experience.

Asiana charges 30$ for non business class and Star Alliance status members if the want to access their lounge. An offer gladly accepted, as we had a 4h stopover after a red-eye flight from Jakarta and were still expecting the longer leg to Frankfurt. The lounge has two section, which have a similar layout. The lounge is huge and wide. There is plenty of space both for working and relaxing. I especially liked the relaxing cubicles with comfortable armchairs where it is possible to take a short nap. There are also some seats available that have a massage function. You can ask for the key to the spotlessly clean shower room at the reception. Towels and amenities are all provided. Next to the buffet, which offers sandwiches, instant noodles fried rice, crackers and salad is a bar where you can enjoy your meal while observing the apron. Alls common drinks are provided as well. Since they offer all soft drinks in cans / bottles you can restock your supllies for the upcoming flight. Very nice indeed. The lounge offers free wifi at a reasonable speed. Staff is always doing its best to keep the lounge incredibly clean. An excellent lounge and definitely worth the money.

This lounge is always busy. It is a nice clean lounge in mostly good shape but starting to show some wear and tear. WiFi is great and there are lots of outlets to plug in. Seating is comfortable and it is usually quiet and peaceful. It is a good place to chill and read or do work. Don't expect to get anything decent to eat though. On my last visit (almost identical to my previous 3 visits this year) - which was more than 4 hours - the offerings consisted of one small EMPTY platter with sign that said 'Sushi' one small EMPTY hot plate with sign that said 'Chicken WIngs'. Food that was actually there consisted of a handful of pretzels with orange 'cheese' paste that tasted like wax a meagre salad bar with undercooked unseasoned flavourless potato salad and four large baskets of dry bread offered with jam and butter. About 10 tiny vegetable sandwiches made an appearance for 30 seconds - but they were immediately hoovered up by patrons desperate for anything decent to munch on. Three cups of vegetable rice also appeared briefly - but it looked and tasted like it was leftover from 3 weeks ago. Oh - and lest I forget two small cereal bowls with thimble sized cookies were offered for dessert. There are also cheap paper instant noodle cups always on offer. No proper bar (some beer on tap no wine to be seen no cocktails). Eat and drink before you come here.

The lounge was great. Lots of room seats cubicles with computer (large screens) to check emails etc. Staff were friendly and helpful. To be able to relax eat (not so great) but lots of choices and shower I'd say this is great

Arrived around 9.30pm for midnight Emirates flight so was looking forward to eating a light dinner. Food and drink selection was extremely mediocre. There was a selection of overcooked tomato pasta a huge bread mountain with toaster which nobody touched. The salad bar and grilled vegetables were depleted and obviously the most popular. No dessert except some cut pineapple and sliced oranges. Pot noodles was obvious choice for Asian travellers. Compared to the business lounges in HK London and Dubai the Asiana lounge really needs to step up. At that time in evening the last thing we want is a carb overload. Suggest you cut out all the pasta and serve cold cuts salads and a decent cheese board some chocolates or dessert of some sort and not the plastic Kraft cheese on display. If we are playing business class fares then I expect half way decent food in the lounge. If I knew it was going to be this bad I would elected to eat in one of the restaurants in the airport but unfortunately everything closes at 10pm in Incheon Airport. On the positive side lounge was spacious wifi works and nice to have massage chairs. However can we have instructions in English as well please?

Roundtrip from HNL to ICN, experienced this lounge before returning to Hawaii. Due to security people watching the escalators was not able to lounge hop to other Star Alliance lounges located at other gates. Lounge is very large with several desktop computers available. You need a password given out at reception to access the internet. Be sure to explore both sides because they have different food available. On the right there was a chef dishing out a cold noodle dish and sandwiches. The left side featured pasta and sushi which kept running out and had to be replaced with different foods. As others have stated. the food choices are very limited and the cup noodles are very cheap looking.

I had a chance to visit this lounge as I was flying business class with American Airlines that day. Came about 2:30 very quiet and lots of seats. They have laptops and the internet and wifi is good. There are rooms with massage chairs. Food was fine. They had a "hot" meal buffet at 3:15. Noodles Fried Rice and Tofu and vegetables. Also had some fruit cold salads sandwiches and kimbap. Coffee was fine. Overall I'd go there again if I had a chance.
Excellent lounge. Food is pretty good and cleanliness is perfect. Since they have expanded the lounge now it's not so crowded even on peak time.

Overall the lounge is comfortable quiet and has showers which is very nice. If you are lucky enough you can get one of about six cubicles which have some privacy and have foot rests so you can stretch out. I was disappointed with the food however. For this trip we used biz class lounges in O'Hare Narita Bangkok and New Delhi and they all had better food especially Narita and Bangkok. I will say the comfort level in Seoul was the best of what we saw.

I had a six-hour stopover in Seoul Incheon and used this lounge. The seats were comfortable the lounge was never too crowded and there was an excellent choice of food. My only gripe was the washroom. It was rather small but I was able to use the one in the neighboring First class lounge. To add some perspective I was on a trip from St Petersburg to Hiroshima via Moscow and Seoul and the lounge was a welcome contrast to the Aeroflot lounge in Sheremetyevo Terrminal D.

Very good lounge for depart from Seoul to LA. Internet service very good food ok. I do note the comments on noodles - yes a tad tacky but actually like noodles so not that bad really. Lots of the chairs are more stadium - rows all facing the same direction so number of seats that are more for 2 people to sit together is a lot less. Still overall not a bad lounge in a stellar airport. And yes Japan and Korea have the best toilets ever.

Great lounge. Very comfortable and nicely decorated. The food was lovely and continually serviced. Coffee great. Toilets were of a high standard with an attendant. High quality toiletries and very clean. We enjoyed this lounge.
Comfortable but a bit dated. Seats comfortable. Didn't like the food set out and ended up eating toast and peanut butter. Good coffee.

Extremely disappointed we were here a month ago and this place has got worse! Now they have plastic cups for wine! I suppose that is an improvement as last time we were here they had no wine! There are four types of lettuce to eat and cups of noodles tea coffee and soft drinks no beer a white wine a red and four types of spirits. I have read the previous reviews and the lounge appears to have got progressively worse. In all fairness to Asiana there is a sign up apologizing for things while they improve the lounge however I would say they have left it far too long before doing anything! As already mentioned the seating is uncomfortable and there are not many power outlets. We have flown business class with a lot of airlines and I can't fault the in air experience with Asiana however their lounge experience leaves much to be desired.

Business class lounge is quite spacious with lots of seats very welcoming staffs. Speedy Wi Fi. Food wise there really isn't a lot of choices it was strange to see so many cup noodles being stacked out kind of cheap to be offered cup noodles rather than proper hot meals (there was only a very few). Choices of drinks not bad quite a busy lounge at 5pm. All in all an average experience slightly underwhelming.

This lounge at 8am was very crowded. The chairs and couches were poorly designed and showing some wear and tear but lounge well maintained and clean. Limited choice of food and salad bar fresh eggs were available. Shower was very good. Great wi-fi and plenty of computers if you do not have one. Overall not too bad but it really needs some attention on seating and food selection.

The lounge was very overcrowded and struggling. Glasses and plates were left uncleared bench top tables were left uncleaned. Food and drink choices were limited and of poor quality. Frankly the lounge was unacceptable for a supposedly 5-star airline. Better quality seating food drink and WiFi was to be found outside of the lounge.

Nothing changed since I started using the lounge in 2010. They only serve little food for their guest. Asiana need to change their lounge service. I think they need to change this better to show their inflight menu.

Clean and spacious with friendly staff was my experience in the Asiana Business Lounge at Incheon. Good mix of food options in a buffet style and drinks were plentiful (alcoholic beverages were perhaps a little limited but onboard wines made up for it). Nice shower rooms available to use good variety of chairs and the lighting created a relaxing atmosphere. Pleasant venue to relax in before long flights.

Excellent state of the art facility to relax in before long haul flight. Lounge design was very attractive and made to look like a European library and the grand piano added a nice touch. Lighting pleasant and plenty of comfortable loungers massage chairs and relaxation rooms were offered. Food and beverages were excellent and much like those served onboard with both hot and cold options. Toilets and shower facilities were very clean and expensive bathing products were offered. Convenient locations to do some work and free wifi was also available. Staff service very pleasant.

An okay interior but some of the chairs are in substandard condition. Remember that ICN is Asiana's hub and I was expecting more. Food that was offered is not good. Two choices plus noodles. Only four choices of hard liqueur.

Asiana's Incheon First class lounge was certainly above average although I expected more considering it is their main hub. The lounge is spacious and luxurious with modern facilities. The shower rooms and toilets were pleasant and maintained well. The staff were immaculately presented and their service was exceptional. The main let down was the substandard food. Although there were still quality food and wine on offer it was nothing spectacular and the options seemed quite limited. Nonetheless the lounge is comfortable and allows for plenty of relaxation which is the main thing.
First time to use this lounge around 5 pm yesterday and it was fairly crowded. It provided us more than adequate facilities. Overall above average.
Very disappointed with Incheon Asiana business lounge. Limited food variety not enough showers tired furniture. Attentive staff but its what they have to work with.

Located on the 2nd level of the departure area the lounge is a windowless spacious room with a self serve bar offering beer hot/cold beverages and mediocre snacks. Private lavatory without any shower facility.

Clean and tidy lounge with comfortable seating this lounge is operated by Swiss Intl Air Lines. No real choice of food except a few cakes and a pretty poor excuse of a shower. Asiana could do with using a much better lounge to compliment their great airline. The lounge is also before security!

Mock European Manor is a little too mock but this is Korea. Friendly and attentive staff. Food for a first class lounge was mediocre. A lukewarm beef dish and a lukewarm prawn dish (these were the better dishes). Only wine was Californian Chardonnay although Moet was on offer too. Seating is comfortable massage chairs excellent and internet connection was very fast - shame seats do not have laptop power outlets. Lacking day beds. Overall compared to Swiss or Lufthansa first class lounges in FRA or ZRH this lounge is lacking behind.

This needs a real sort out. Claustrophobic in the low ceilinged area the high ceilinged area is like being in a 3rd rate hospital waiting area. Seats uncomfortable food average drinks range very average.
Perfect lounge except for the very limited food offering. Shower rooms equipped with brand names amenities. Definitely one of the best airline lounges in Asia.

We transferred through Incheon. On the inward journey we spent a few hours at the lounge in terminal 1 - on the return the lounge in terminal 2. While they are both decorated and laid out similarly terminal 2 is newer. The shower rooms are a little nicer the layout a littler more varied and the business centre much bigger. While Seoul has a phenomenally spacious efficient and relatively pleasant airport there is more shopping in terminal 1 than 2. I compared duty free prices though and while there are savings on alcohol and tobacco many cosmetics and clothing were exactly the same as mall prices in Canada. Some of the areas Asiana could improve would be the inordinate announcement of flights; there is no escape from the PA. The quiet relaxing area is near the showers and bathrooms and cleaners area so there is always a din. The food offerings varied sometimes generous — roast pork hot soup vegetable salads — to scant such as sandwiches lettuce and dried noodles. Drink options not great not bad; no decent wine. Very pleasant staff.

Stunning facility. It's modeled to look like a comfortable manor library with shelves of books attractive lighting and a baby grand piano! Several relaxation rooms with loungers. several more with state of the art massage chairs. A TV/DVD room with large flat panels. Catering includes Korean tea service with traditional snacks cold bar with smoked salmon and duck hot bar with lamb and lobster thermadore. I wish the inflight catering was this good!. Excellent drink selection with proper barware. Business center with three fast computers. Showers and toilets with state of the art Toto technology (a translation card here would have been helpful!).

This lounge is about as old as the airport itself but is clean well furnished and has a perfectly good range of facilities. Food and drinks choices are fine and the staff are helpful and efficient. A quiet oasis of comfort in an otherwise terrible airport.

Actually a very pleasant and spacious, bright lounge. Good selection of hot and cold food, even at breakfast. Varied selection of drinks, including Prosecco. Loads of charging points with International plugs. A pleasant place to work or chill waiting for your flight.
Over booked allocation, poorly managed, tables cleared but not wiped. Lacked atmosphere and looking very tired. Not value for money. Disappointed.

The Aspire lounge is no longer a ‘Business Lounge’ and has become a place for holiday families where many are ensuring that they get their money’s worth. Impossible to work - (quiet area might help) and certainly not now an attractive option for frequent flyers. From KLM my expectations are higher. The staff work hard to keep things in order but on this (and previous) occasion it was not a pleasant experience.

I used this lounge as a third party lounge by invitation from Qatar Airways. Oddly enough there still needs to be a handwritten lounge invitation. This lounge is quite something. It has the most diverse choice of seating and atmosphere. It is as if it is two lounges in one! One part of the lounge is made out of wood, and is very interesting to look at. There are also various decorative items throughout the lounge. There are booths for families, tables, couches, anything you could ask for. I really did enjoy my time in the lounge. The food here was a pleasant surprise. A large selection of international dishes, local dishes etc. I was surprised to find an Indian curry, an Asian noodle stir fry among other things! There was also a manned bar and lots of choices for drinks. One thing I appreciate is when a lounge has fresh squeezed orange juice rather than boxed orange juice. The barman was very openly showing the fresh oranges that have been squeezed behind him! The only thing this lounge is lacking is windows. Although I think they are unnecessary as the lounge itself is designed to be a warm place even with the lack of natural daylight. The wifi was easy to connect but the cleaners seem to be out of sight and just there when you needed them. I was unlucky that we were called to the gate a long time before it was necessary to begin boarding. The receptionist said that "You could've arrived earlier to enjoy the lounge! It's a big shame that you arrived a bit late." I have to agree with her. It is an amazing place to wait for your flight. Although arriving early would've been quite impossible considering we were connecting from Cape Town. I would recommend this lounge even as a priority pass option, and there are many third party lounges in Johannesburg airport.

Booked the airport lounge for Newcastle airport because we have used Manchester’s lounge on many occasions with absolutely no complaints, however I have never been so dissatisfied as I was with Newcastle, Very little food left, no Pepsi, crisps or bread. Luke warm soup, limp salad and dried our rice and pasta was all that was available. Staff upset because they were in the firing line for the complaints from customers. Emailed customer service twice and still no reply from them. Learn by my mistake and save your money, it just wasn’t worth it unless you wanted to get absolute mortal drunk because there was nothing else to do except drink, Would have happily gone to Greggs in the foyer if I’d known how bad the food was going to be.

Flew out from Bristol on the 6th May. First time use of Aspire Lounge. Very unhappy with the whole thing - the choice of food and the take it or leave from the staff left a lot to be desired. I can only say how unhappy I was and will never use this lounge again.

Very underwhelmed at this Aspire lounge at Manchester. Firstly no one to greet me - so I just walked in. Very poor selection of food in terms of light snacks. A bit of cake?!? Will not be using again.

This Aspire Lounge at Terminal 5 is a very busy lounge as its not just a member's only lounge but also pay to use. This lounge is very clean and spacious and somewhat crowded. It has huge open windows with ample of light for one to see planes take off and land. The Wi-Fi is Excellent. Very fast. There is a salad bar, hot soup and hot entree dishes (pasta, quiche, rice and curry) in addition to the usual beverages (tea, coffee, juices and alcohol available). The food quality was good and tasty. Loved the scones with the tea. Would definitely return to this lounge again. The only drawback to this lounge is that the restrooms are outside in the terminal building.

This Aspire Lounge is a third party lounge and also open to paying customers, some credit card holders and lounge access card holders. As such it is always very busy when I go there. I'm absolutely bewildered as to why anyone would pay to enter. Its not a bad lounge, there is an adequate selection of beverages and the food is decent but I find the number of people in the space a little uncomfortable, my prime reason to go into airport lounges is to relax, its not a very relaxing space. I must stress, the facilites provided are up to standard, it is simply the volume of people in it that is a definite downside. Obviously Air France/KLM cannot really justify the expense of their own lounge at Newcastle although I guess BA does have their own which is lovely and has less flights that Air France and KLM combined.

The Aspire by Swissport Lounge is past security and we were positively surprised. It is spacious and has an open air terrace to enjoy a glass of wine in the sun, a cigar or a cigarette. The selection of food is good and included salads, hot dishes, cold snacks and desert. We had a glass of the French Blancs de Blancs wine which was quite good. To eat we had spring rolls, pizza slices and chicken nuggets). We recommend this lounge. It is one of the best contract Lounges I have been to. Why not a ten point rating? Simply because it does not have shower possibilities (restrooms were good and clean) or an area to relax and sleep. And it should have fresh local food.

I used this lounge when travelling with Etihad Airways. After three visits to the Aspire lounge at Amsterdam I have to conclude substandard is the rule rather than exception. The lounge is full, so are the bins in the restrooms. The buffet however, is pretty empty. Based on the leftovers very simple, more like snacks. Beverages are ok, not very exciting but caters for most basic needs. Atmosphere and overall impression: Unorganised, untidy, overcrowded, lacks any form of class, style or elegance. It's just a mediocre cafeteria. Airlines should be embarrassed offering Aspire by Swissport to their premium and frequent customers.

This Aspire lounge is excellent. The food on offer is fresh and tasty, they offer gluten free options and the staff are very friendly. The lounge is spacious, has excellent wifi and plenty of plugs for charging your equipment. I would recommend this lounge to anyone.

I visited 70 lounges on Priority Pass last year. This was the worst by far. It's advertised as "luxury". The latest luxury aspect is that sandwiches are no longer supplied. Dog eared bread rolls are available with big bowls of luxury fillings, such as egg and grated cheese. These are kept in a fridge above open hugs of juice which thus have bits of food floating on the top. The other "luxury" food supplied is some constantly reheated pasta in cheap tomato sauce. Seats in the lounge are looking tatty and there are many times when potential guests are told the lounge is full when many tables have reserved signs in them for 2 hours in the future I would not pay in buttons to use this lounge!

After a dreadful experience clearing security at Manchester T1, we were looking forward to visiting the Aspire Lounge to relax and have a bite to eat before the Aer Lingus flight. When we arrived at approximately 7.30pm I decided to take a newspaper to read. However, only a few national dailies were available and those were worse for wear. We chose seats overlooking the runway, and this view is one of the best features of this lounge, and something we have enjoyed many times. The food was very poor. The receptionist had mentioned how busy the lounge had been all day, but there can be no excuse for the abysmal amount of available food: Lukewarm tomato &red pepper soup, handful of scones, handful of biscuits (many broken) in a jar, few packets of cream crackers and miniature cheese portions, small amount of peanuts, Yoghurts. And that was it: no bread rolls, no crisps, the hot food racks were bare. It beggars belief that a large organization can be so ill prepared for a busy day. Surely sourcing additional supplies is not that difficult a concept to deal with? The lounge website promises great things, but clearly failed to deliver on this occasion.

Manchester Airports Aspire by Swissport lounge used by Singapore Airlines. We were shown into what i can only describe as a small glass box. This was both cold and cramped, the only beverages on offer were drinks from a machine biscuits and buns and some ready made bacon sandwiches. There are no elements of luxury or comfort whatsoever.  They need to have a serious rethink regarding their lounge experience they offer to their customers.

As a Air Berlin topbonus platinum I got to use the only available lounge at Zurich Airport, the Aspire. I got there around 15 o'clock and there was almost nobody inside. Although very small, it didn't seem it can get full. It has a very nice view to the main departures hall. It is very clean and well organised. There were some snacks offered and the offer on beverages was also good. There were also some cooked food options but only for lunch and evening meal, with a good defined schedule. The time I was there, this food was not available so I cannot make any comments about it. The toilets are somewhere outside, somehow separate but very clean. The internet was somehow limited if I understood right and after some time you have to buy credit. A good place to spend the time before departure.

This Aspire lounge at T5 Heathrow is one of the worst lounges I've ever been. Food okay, the service was terrible, they didn't even checked my ID or Lounge membership so apparently anyone can walk in without any check. First I got a glass of orange juice, and then i realised the glass was pretty dirty, but then i got a glass of champagne, the glass was so dirty, it had red lipstick on it and I took pictures. I told the lady serving the bar and she got kind of upset. Terrible service.

This Aspire lounge at Heathrow Terminal 3 was amazing and I had access to it through my Priority Pass membership. Flying from Amsterdam to JFK via Heathrow, I had time to stop in and get some food and drink. The hot food is ordered off a menu and seems made to order. I had lamb stew and then macaroni and cheese. For a pay-per-use lounge it is highly recommended.

I used this lounge when travelling with British Airways, and this Aspire lounge needs more room. It was quite full when I visited and the layout and location of food is horrible. I'm guessing it's the only area that worked, but it is in the middle of a busy, high-foot-traffic area and if enough people are trying to get food on their plates, then there's no room to walk by. On the plus side, the food was good and refreshments were plentiful. Staff came by regularly to pick-up used dishes.

Visited this Aspire lounge on the evening of 1/1/2017 when flying with Qatar Airways. It is substandard on most, particularly the food is incredibly poor without any hot offers apart from a tired asparagus soup. 2-3 hours before closure the food is not replenished anymore and becomes messy. Staff are incredibly tired, inert, boring, without any interest in the job and without will to listen, improve (the lounge and themselves), and refrain from any decision on anything. Language skill very limited. A disaster for the airport, for the airlines that have to use it and for Denmark. No showers, no business centre. No view of the tarmac. Best thing is that very few people use it and thus release some space for those entering. No celebrations or even slightest demarcation of e.g. New Year, X-mas or whatever. Always the same dull atmosphere.

Used this lounge as a customer of KLM leaving Helsinki. The selection of food is rather limited compared to other frequent flyers lounge. Beverage selection is quite nice and enough for the European flights. The comfort is great though and seat and design is pleasant. Service was nice also inside the lounge.

The lounge does not open 24 hours a day, which is inconvenient for passengers with very late or early flights. It looks modern but the food variety is very limited. At breakfast time, there was only scambled eggs, bacon, sausages, a little bread with a small piece of smoked salmon in it, croissant, yogurts, cereals, packed chocolate cake, chips and few others. Hot food choices are not enough and do not taste brilliant. the wifi is quite good though and the seats are quite comfy.

I gained access to the Aspire Lounge on the morning of 5 March 2016 between 6.30am to 7.30am using my Priority Pass membership before getting on my 8.10am Etihad flight. The lounge had no more than 8 guests at that time which made for a quiet visit. First impressions were that the space was clean, bright and airy which is nice for a winter morning (the day after snow had fallen). I enjoy the views which get you up close to the planes if you enjoy planes watching like I do. The breakfast spread was not extensive and the ham bun felt dry.

Used this lounge as a passenger with Cathay Pacific Airways. The new Aspire Lounge at Zurich Airport just opened. Received a very warm welcome at the entrance and escorted to the sofa area at the lounge. I was the only passenger and had the full care of the staff. Everything was clean and tidy, service excellent and staff very helpful. The food was delicious. The offers on beverages is very good, Deutz Champagne is served which is a big plus! Overall experience was amazing! The washrooms are outside the lounge and are facilities of the Airport, which are nothing special at all.

This Aspire lounge at Malaga Airport is the worst premium lounge I have visited. Food is poor - tiny triangular sandwiches, salad, biscuits, olives, soft drinks and hot drinks. Alcohol if required. Staff non existent. Seating comfortable.

As an EVA Air Business Class passenger I spent some time at the Aspire Lounge 41 before my flight to Bangkok. The staff were friendly and professional and kept the place very clean. The lounge is very light with large windows overlooking the tarmac. There's a variety of seats including lounge chairs. The food and beverages are ok, but nothing special. I'd like to see some more options in snacks and non-alcoholic beverages like for example a variety of juices. There is a pay for shower available but I didn't use it. WiFi connection was easy and good. Overall it was a comfortable experience, a little improvement on the catering would give it that extra touch.

I like to visit the Aspire lounge at Edinburgh Airport before a flight (this with Qatar Airways), and the £17 charge for 3 hours was a no brainer. The lounge is small but cosy, has no view of the runway as we are the front of the airport. All alcohol is served by the staff, the other drinks you can help yourself. There is a small buffet with salads pasta etc. I liked the lounge, and a great price too.

This lounge is a disaster for Aspire Lounge, CPH airport, used by Qatar Airways. The idea having a separate section is fine, but in 4 (four!) months the airconditioning has not been working and the stuffy atmosphere persists making it unbearable to sit anywhere. The staff are again bluffing that it will "be repaired on Monday.."(said the same thing twice two and four months earlier). The rest of the lounge is more airy. The section used by Qatar Airways is in no way better than the ordinary section of the lounge and as the climate is extremely stuffy, nobody touch the food and hardly anybody use this section despite business class later on the flight proved to be full of passengers. The lounge provides no hot meals, no champagne, a cheap wine, and lousy bread with cold ham and tasteless cheese served. A shame for the airline which obviously is fooled by Aspire to use this "private section". Discussed the issue with the few other pax who were there. They had the same view. If CPH is aiming being a hub, this is the worst they could do promoting it, as eg. the Qatar Airways lounge in London is  far better.

Two visits and same result. If this is the best American can do then they have a long climb ahead of them. While the drinks, including champagne were very acceptable, the food and seating were pretty poor. Lots of food items on offer, sadly, most of what was on display was a repetition of the same few choices. The hot food was tepid at best and very little choice. There is a risotto station which was closed on our most recent visit. One of the worst lounges we have ever used.

This is a huge and spacious lounge with a broad selection of tapas sized hot buffet items (chef inspired entrees e.g. grilled chicken, swordfish, squash curry, samosa chat), as well as cold buffet items (sushi - different kinds, sandwiches). The lounge also offer a wide selection of premium drinks and amenities (e.g. shower suites). Since OneWorld Alliance member airlines' business class passengers have access to the lounger, the lounge was very busy and crowded for early evening departure. The reception staff as well as the culinary staff and servers were warm and friendly. WiFi was fast and easy to log into. Seating was comfortable with a view of the runways.

Nothing Flagship about it at all. As international first class lounges go, this was one of the worst I’ve experienced and not at all what I expected. The reception staff were warm and friendly, so my visit began with a great start. But on entry I soon discovered it was a small space and overcrowded. There was no a la carte dining service like New York, instead there was a buffet service and what was on offer looked old and tired. So, I decided to give the food a miss thinking it was better to wait and have dinner on board. This would later prove to have been a mistake. I did, however, take advantage of the shower facilities and there was no waiting time and the shower room was nicely designed and the shower had great water pressure.

Located in Terminal 8 at JFK International Airport is the Chelsea Flagship Lounge. It’s the most exclusive of American Airlines 3 premium lounges at JFK. Here you can sip bespoke cocktails or guzzle vintage French champagne at the stunning circular bar. Or if you’re feeling a bit peck you can enjoy meal prepared by a chef from the a la carte menu. It was quiet and relaxed when I visited the staff outnumbered guests. The food was superb and the staff super friendly and eager to please. The only drawback was the so-called ‘relaxation area’. There are no where to grab some shut-eye just a strange series of modern curved single form lounges lined up in a row and separated by a strip of fabric suspended from the roof – very exposed and very strange. But if you have access to this lounge, then I recommend to use it.

American Airlines offers 3 lounges at JFK - Greenwich, Soho and Chelsea with Chelsea being the most exclusive and dedicated to Flagship First Passengers. The lounge features and amazing circular bar and full service restaurant where you can choose from a wide range of chef prepared pre-flight meals. They serve Krug champagne and offer an excellent selection of high quality wines. The atmosphere is calm and quiet. However there is no private space to rest or take a nap. the only option being preform shaped sleeping furniture separated by a fine gold curtain - very strange.

Warm welcome at reception. Thought the chicken sliders were a great hot food idea. Very popular. Seating areas were good with great views. Nice warm lighting.  Don’t expect the champagne to flow. Drinks options are limited cheap brand options. It’s not self service - you have to ask bartender, even for soft drink ! Liquor is a thimble sized amount drowned in soda - I’d just arrived. Smartly dressed. I asked for more whiskey as I couldn’t taste it and was told no at full volume which was very embarrassing. Observed this humiliation happening to several other passengers. Romany has an unfortunate manner and requires people skills training. We walked out.

Nice new club with fresh welcoming interiors and small, but decent food options. Check in staff was efficient and courteous. Unfortunately, the bar staff was rude and unprofessional, and the options subpar. If you're going for the updated interior and limited but tasty food, then it's worth a short stay. If you're grabbing a drink and expecting quality service and drink options, then find somewhere else.

On August 17th 2023 flight number AA5594 arrived in Charlotte on time flight crew perfect 10 we went to the Admirals Club and were told it was at capacity and denied access. The staff on duty today were very rude and not customer friendly, this is unacceptable based on paying for this service. I feel there is a need for some additional customer service training. I asked if there was a call list, the answer I received was why should we have to look for you just keep coming back to check. The persons facial expressions and tone of voice was that of a person trying prove his superiority of over the customers, by far very bad for customer relations. We will be asking for a refund and never will use American Airlines again .
Pathetic. I felt sorry for the attentive wonderful staff. The food offerings were below sub par. This is consistent after several visits this year. Please American, you really look bad

I had an unexpected 4 1/2 hour delay in DC on my way home to Cincinnati. (Flights were a mess due to fog.) Rather than trying to find a seat in the overcrowded gate house (due to delays), I paid for a day pass for the American E Lounge. It was the best decision that I made for the day that I had no control of! The lounge was wonderful with plenty of room, business friendly, wonderful food options, and the most attentive staff. I have to give extra thanks to bartenders Tiana and William who were so cordial to all of the frustrated travelers that came to the E lounge bar. Their service was above and beyond…everyone was served promptly and with a genuine smile! It was so very appreciated by everyone that they served. Tiana and William are the best!

Lounge feels a little cramped and has limited choices but staff is nice and crowd reasonable. And if I compare to the crowding challenges faced with Delta Skyclubs, it is a refreshing experience. Espresso machine was out of service but regular coffee was available. What remains a mastery is the difficulty to access the lounge Internet access at Admiral Clubs … faced the problem At multiple Admiral Clubs where it takes forever to get the authentication page.

American Airlines Flagship Lounge opposite Gate D30 in Miami International. Having been in various US airport lounges before was not expecting that much, but we were actually very impressed: comfortable, spacious (good views over one of the runways) and quiet with lots of available seating. Good choice of beers, wines and spirits along with soft drink and hot drink options. Good choice of food options: at least 3 hot food choices and a counter where a chef would also serve whatever they had prepared, and a nice selection of cold meats and chesses with salads and fresh breads. Business section where you could catch up on work etc. Nice area to while away the time before your flight, and would recommend. Should have got here earlier to take full advantage.

I am writing this review to acknowledge the level of kindness and dedication I received from American Airlines employees. I was flying from Doha to Nashville through JFK. My first 14.5- hour flight landed late at 9:30 am. I missed my connection in JFK. The next flight to Nashville is at 7 pm. There was nothing I could do, I wanted to take a shower and lay down for a couple of hours. Even though AA has no responsibility about the missed connection they went out of their way to help me. Sandra who sits at the VIP counter club with incredible grace worked so hard to find me an earlier flight but there was nothing available. Nevertheless, she was incredibly sympathetic and helpful. Thank you Sandra. AA should be proud to have you.

The only saving grace was the lovely attentive staff. The food and drink offerings were pathetic and truly terrible. The food tasted like it had already been re heated twice and was inedible. The drink choices were poor and the only cream for coffee was fake cream. Inexcusable. The staff seemed embarrassed, I felt bad for them. The Covid excuse doesn’t fly anymore. AA let your great staff be proud of what they offer and make your customers feel valued

I was very excited to check out the new DFW Admirals Club in Terminal E. However, very disappointed. The food bar with the hummus, dressing and dips appeared to be sitting out so long they had crust on the top of them and around the edges. Nothing looked like it was attended to in quite a while. Afraid to eat anything I didn't want to get food poisoning. I actually put on gloves and lifted silver bowls that hummus was in. Room temperature not good! Plan B “Soup” it was crusted and separated. It was so disgusting I grabbed a piece of fruit and went to my gate. Attendant did stir things a little but didn't rotate things out or offer to get me something fresh. Very disappointed!

I tried to recall why I never fly American but was reminded when I entered the Admirals Club. I presented my first class ticket and the agent said “ why do you think you have access to this club”. I stated that I thought my ticket allowed for it. I was informed that only on international travel. I asked if they had a daily rate and proceeded to pay with my platinum american express. The agent couldn't have been more rude or irritated. The lounge looked like a school cafeteria. I have no problem with their policies and I am happy to pay for extra services. American Airlines… you dont beat your competition with rude associates and doing things on the cheap. Now I recall why I dont travel with American.

First Class ticket in hand and over one Million Miles flown, I proceeded to the Admirals Lounge and was denied entry and told only if you pay the $450 fee and get their credit card would you gain access. My First Class Ticket meant nothing to the Staff or American Airlines My million miles flown Status means nothing to the staff or American Airlines. So I went to the B gate Admirals club just to double check if what I actually heard is true. I approached the lady at the desk and said I just want to confirm two things please. I am not looking to argue I just want to make sure I am correct in two things as I will write a review later. Can you please a confirm to me that my First Class ticket and my million mile status mean nothing to American Airlines in regards to gaining access to this lounge. She eventually confirmed what I said after trying to argue with me and tell me all the merits of buying the credit card etc. When I kept explaining to her “ I know it’s not your fault but I just want to confirm two things for my review”. And she kept on arguing and I finally had to tell her - you can write your review but I just need to confirm this. So I was harassed and badgered even just trying to get the facts straight after being told to go for a long walk and your million miles flown and First Class ticket neither matter at All to American Airlines To Add insults to Injury during the flight instead of 20 minutes into the flight or 20 minutes before landing— nope right in the middle about an hour 20 min from landing when half the plane was asleep they broke in for an almost two minute sales job of the Credit Card and bonus miles etc etc etc. American Airlines has become horrific and I will use up my miles but not be giving them anymore of my hard earned money.

They really cannot get it right: lounge had no soft drinks and very little to eat. Electricity at my seat not available so had to go looking for a functioning place to sit. Theirs is an unlawful trust and it should be broken by our government.
Great employees. That’s it. Horrible complimentary offerings. Everything else buy to consume. No cream for coffee only dry non dairy creamer. Never again

The AA Flagship lounge at Dallas Ft Worth, Terminal D, caters for Qantas frequent flyers. Its a lounge that I have visited often. This was no different to earlier visits. Its a great place to while away time as it overlooks the apron and runways so a great view of all outside activities. Now one thing that is simply a fact of the physical layout. It is long, long and thin! If sat near the farthest end then its a mighty fine trek to the restaurant area. But this is a first world problem. The showers are good, F & B was fine. Looking forward to freshly made tacos but this time were serving chicken curry. The lounge was not too busy and plenty of space for all. DFW is a busy airport so quick turnover of passengers. Of all the AA Flagship lounges I have visited (DFW, JFK, LAX and Miami) this is the best one particularly with the lighting (natural) and views. A very nice place to visit.
Admirals Club at Miami Airport. Why bother!?!? Just a waste of time. Week coffee, no food except some fruit and bagels unless you pay for it. And with what AA serves as breakfast it's understandable.

So, it's my understanding that the terminal A at Philadelphia Flagship lounge still isn't available as it's under construction OR being remodeled I suppose. This one, the B/C terminal's connector (they call it) is about the next best choice at the Philadelphia airport for American Airlines. It's an Admiral's Club lounge (like the level below the Flagship one). I can tell you they've changed in the level of services and what you actually get. The food's less appealing and the alcohol drinks less than generous. That being said, this lounge had these sweets if you like that sort of thing. The brownie bits were delicious. Chocolate chip cookies next to these. They also had some raw veggies and like a house salad you could make on your own (it costs them almost nothing). There was this hot chicken tortilla soup as well. There was a fancy looking coffee, espresso, cappuccino machine nearby. It had looked like it would make a decent cup. The bottled fresh spring water is gone! They have a at the bar, a tap water tank dispenser you could fill up your water glass. It had used to be that you could get the premium brands for no additional charges! Now you get 2 coupons which equated to my AA boarding pass. It's how the bartender supposedly keeps a tally on your limit of two drinks. He enters it in his computer register. Anything else, and you can have the free poor house wine or maybe a well drink. All in all, it was a spacious, decent and comfortable lounge. At peak flight times, it can get busy so claim your seat stake near the bigger windows. Especially if you wanted to plug in and recharge your devices. They need many more electrical outlets as those ones are by the table lamps. Staff is fairly attentive. They roam around bugging you, asking to see if you had wanted your obvious empty plate or glass taken away!

This is an updated lounge from when I can remember in the 1990's, 2000's traveling extensively throughout Europe. The food is good. The staff's friendly enough and nice. They have freshly made hot food like scrambled eggs, and there is cold fresh meats, fruits, a nice espresso coffee machine, tap fountain water (still or bubbly), alcoholic drinks, juices, and soda's in a see through refrigerator. Plenty of electrical outlets for ANY plug type you might imagine necessary for a connection. Newspapers like the NYT, Le Monde, etc. All in all this is a good, comfortable business class lounge in terminal 2A after you pass through the MAIN CDG duty free shopping.

There is just something wrong with the staff here at this lounge. Last May I stopped in -- as an Alaska Airlines lounge member I get reciprocal visit rights with the Admirals Clubs as long as I fly on AA or AS the same day. I met those conditions yet was refused entry because their boarding pass scanner didn't recognise my boarding pass and all American Airlines employes do only what the computer tells them to do (I thought computers were out tools -- at AA it seems humans are only employed because they have hands that can manipulate the computer). As a consolation, I was told "maybe they'll let you in in London (they did)." To-day at least they let me in. I asked a swarthy boy at the desk to verify my AS number was properly recorded in the pnr but instead he just looked at the boarding pass and told me my AA number was recorded. I explained to him again slowly why I was asking the question and he accused me several times of being rude. Perhaps I was -- isn't it irritating when a clerk doesn't consider what you say important enough to listen to you? I felt like telling him I'm sorry since I am a member of the Admirals Clubs just to be of service to him. He wouldn't have understood -- abrasive people can take it but are very fragile when you bark back at them.

This lounge had been closed for over a year so pleased to see it open. Its in the same spot overlooking the airfield but has been extended. A great buffet plus also a taco bar. Downsides? The food was occasionally a bit dry sitting on a warming plate but small thing. Plus also, when will the US get some decent coffee instead of the brown liquid that they call coffee. A barista please. Washrooms were immaculate and overall a great place to be.
Very clean facility but to charge three dollars for a Diet Coke is quite low and sends a very cheap message. Shame. The rest of the personnel were most cordial and accomodating.

I have written to AA three times already about this issue but they just ignore me. I have an Alaska AIr Lounge membership which entitles me to use the AA Flagship lounges when traveling on AS or AA. The boarding pass reader would not read my BOAC-issued boarding pass at Roissy and so I was refused entry. It wasn't until I demanded to speak to the station manager that they relented and did their job. Very stressful and embarassing -- and I thought always that the purchase of a lounge membership was to ease airport stresses. AA is really a poor company -- their staff are very discourteous and often hostile with "chips on their shoulders" who think they are princes- & princesses-in-exile who are too good to serve the public. If AA doesn't start treating the traveling public with courtesy and respect, they will find there will no longer be a traveling public for them. I have traveled on AA 135 twice this month and both times it was less that 50% full. I miss Pan Am and other real airlines.

Avoid this Admirals Club lounge in Terminal 4 at Los Angeles Intl if you can. The overcrowding is unbearable. The complimentary food offering is sufficient for a quick snack. Due to the layout of the lounge and the overcrowding if you are at all claustrophobic you should avoid this lounge.

I ordered off the menu a Vegetarian Waldorf salad, when it was served it was smothered with chicken and the server said that’s how it comes and left the dish on the table. She didn’t offer to return the dish and serve me one without the chicken. I didn’t want to make a scene so I said I would pick off the shredded chicken and eat it anyway. She offered no apology and left me to pick it off. The menu clearly shows ‘V’ for vegetarian and no meat is listed in the ingredients. After finishing my meal after picking off the chicken I thought I shouldn’t have had to work so hard to eat a salad in a paid membership club. Customer satisfaction should be the prime aim. I subsequently complained to the manager. He refunded the salad charge and the tip after I requested him to remove the tip. I paid for my premium wine, but a good customer service gesture I feel should have been to refund the entire charge. Lesson learned refuse to eat something I’m less than satisfied with instead of trying to take the high road.

Prior to my flight on Cathay Pacific to Hongkong I was invited to use the Flagship dining section attached to American Airlines Flagship lounge at JFK airport. This is a five-star Manhattan-style dining facility with bar and spectacular views on the tarmac. I spent almost six hours in the Flagship dining section and besides me there were never more than a handful of other diners present. The waiters were very attentive and helpful with explaining the food and wine offers. I had the strip steak and the Flagship signature burger - both dishes were simply superb. The desserts - I went for the signature sundae and the creme brulee - were heavenly good. In contrary to the Flagship lounge - which looked at peak-times like a zoo - the Flagship dining section seemed to be a perfect escape. I was in there during the time the sun was setting down which was another highlight of my visit.

I had a long wait at LAX due to AA problems in getting me to SFO so spent time in the One World lounge at TBIT where I have been many times. Its a known quantity so used it to shower and freshen up. One problem with that lounge is the appalling lighting. Very dim. From there with a couple of hours to kill went to the Flagship Lounge at T4. Great reception area and a very nice lady at the front desk who was happy to chat. If only the AA FA's would have some of her charm. Upstairs and to the Admirals Club which is standard AA fare and level ie comfortable but nothing fancy. Now if invited, I was, one can use the Flagship Lounge. Great lounge, separate areas, plenty of seating and attendant washroom facilities. The catering was superb. It is worth trawling the net for other reviews and images as the food is very varied and good. AA can put on a great show if it wants to and this lounge is proof of it. If it can transfer some of this to its aircraft that would raise AA to the One World standards of its sister airlines. Certainly in future I am more than likely to use this lounge in preference to the One World lounge at TBIT. Top marks to AA.

We were told it was a ‘must’ to use the VIP Lounge at Cancun so we paid $37US per person to use it. What a waste of money. The Lounge was far too small for the number of people in there and we were sat in some really uncomfortable seats. There were crying babies, toddlers, really loud customers and generally no sense of quiet that you would expect from a VIP Lounge. The food was rubbish and we hardly ate anything. The coffee took about a minute to bre per person so there was often a queue to get it. The water ran out and we had to wait for it to be replaced. There was only one female toilet so always a queue. The alcoholic section was actually quite good, if you wanted it, but our flight was early so hardly anyone was drinking.overall, I wish we had saved the money and paid for a nice meal.

There are 2 adjacent lounges, common reception entrance. One is Flagship, the other is called Flagship Bridge. The latter is much quieter with a selection of wines - red, white and sparkling - served by bartenders at the bar or at your seat. There is also a small menu of food available by ordering. This is a much relaxed place though it could benefit from having more comfortable couches. The adjacent Flagship lounge is much larger, very crowded, with buffet service of both hot and cold foods. A large selection of alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks are there for self serving. Good views of the taxiways. A few computer stations. Clean bathrooms and there are showers too. However, the staff is very slow in keeping the place tidy. Counters and tables have plates, glasses, napkins and food leftovers for quite a long time. Both lounges have good complimentary wi-fi and lots of plug points to charge your phones and computers. The lounges are used by One World airlines. The front desk personnel were very helpful with arranging boarding passes for me. The lounges were superb places to catch up on work, relax, watch TV and enjoy premium drinks on the house until your flight was called.

What was once an peaceful, elegant and premiere lounge has become an overcrowded, filthy, and horrible experience. American Airlines charges a lot for their "Flagship" experience but fail horribly on their delivery. The experience is not worth the cost. They now allow so many people in that they had no food to eat or cold drinks. Their soda machine was empty of syrup. Their food counters were filthy and unsanitary. Their wifi was so slow it did not work. It was anything but relaxing. It was actually more peaceful and calm in the general waiting area of the airport. They are incapable of accommodating the number of people they let in their doors.

This American Airlines lounge at Mexico City Airport is ok but often crowded. This time it was at full capacity and I had to leave. Food and drinks are better at the priority pass one. Not worth the walk there from gate 31/36 at the other end of the airport, from where most europe flights leave.

Admiral's Club lounge serving Terminals B/C at Philadelphia. I accessed it with my BA Executive Club Gold/OneWorld Emerald card, and it was my first visit to Philadelphia in transit from an international flight. Reception staff was friendly, and gave me two coupons for bottled water or premium alcoholic beverages upon check-in. There are some alcoholic beverages that do not require a coupon. The snack selection has improved a lot at Admiral's Club lounges recently, and the selection here was very good, including two soup choices at lunchtime. The lounge appeared to have been refurbished recently, and was clean. It offers a nice view of the tarmac, and has both free Wi-Fi and PC terminals available. Plenty of comfortable seating, and it was not too crowded in the several hours that I was there. I don't know if they offer shower facilities, but the restrooms were adequately maintained. I also used the Admirals's Club lounge in Terminal C of DCA (Washington Reagan National Airport) on this trip, and it was as good. However, the lounge in PHL at Terminals B/C had a better layout and felt more spacious with more natural light. Both lounges were good places to spend a few hours.

As a oneworld-Emerald I was allowed to use the American Airlines First Class Lounge in LAX, by passing through the Business Class one. Because it is being redecorated (a whole new concept) the lounge I visited was somehow separated from the main Business one, until the brand new one will be opened (as advertised with tables and seats where you are being served personally by a waiter, possibly with a spa area). The food served (buffet style) was very delicious and although there were not many choices you could feel welcome and taken care of. I did use the business facilities (computers and printers) which worked and the ground stuff helped me at any time. A very nice experience and I can't wait to try the new one.

Inside the national terminal at SFO there is the Admirals Club lounge which is the first one I've been to where you should pay for some snacks, but for the US I can understand this concept as many people fly frequently and probably a lot of them acquire a privilege status. Nevertheless there were enough snacks for free (bagels, butter, fruit, yogurt, cereals and so on) and drinks as well. It was quite spacious and it looked packed although it was 7 am. I didn't miss anything while staying there and it was a very beautiful experience to wait for my flight. A big thumbs up for the restrooms which were very clean and modern and for the ground staff that were so nice in helping me finding another flight as mine was cancelled. They did all the best to help.

I will preface this review with a caveat that the lounge is under reconstruction. With that in mind I still believe this is the dirtiest, most poorly organized lounge I have ever seen. While excusing the construction, there is no excuse for the filthy, scummy bathrooms. They were very busy so constant cleaning is necessary. With construction there are limited bathroom stalls but failing to keep them clean is inexcusable. The club design is so confusing that it is difficult to find anything, including bathrooms and food service. Service was friendly but slow.

As first class passengers traveling on British Airways from DFW to London Heathrow, we were invited to use the Admirals Club in terminal D. This included several drink tickets for premium wine and spirits. We were also given an invitation for the Flagship Dining room which is located inside of this particular Admirals Club and we then had lunch there. The lunch buffet was very good but not excellent. However, the service provided by the staff was excellent and the red wine was better than the premium red wine on offer at the Admirals Club bar. The Admirals Club itself was large, spacious and clean with plenty of available seating and a great view of the ramp and runways. Of special note was complimentary, fresh guacamole quickly made to order while one waited. It was excellent and I thought this was a very nice touch. We later visited the British Airways first and business class lounge at DFW before boarding our BA flight and it wasn't nearly as nice as the Admirals Club in terminal D as it was quite a bit smaller with a vastly inferior red wine selection.

The lounge is very crowded with the maximum number of seats in the smallest space. The food options are basically dips, chips and nuts. This has to be one of the worst lounges available and falls well below the standard expected. Good for somewhere to sit prior to your flight but that's about it.

American Airlines lounge is being renovated so the entry is not as pretty as it will be once finished. The lounge was clean, comfortable and good wifi. The beverages were good but the food a little haphazard menu wise. There was a choice but the combinations a little unusual. Nothing bad and plenty to enjoy. Nice big windows to enjoy watching the planes come and go. Friendly staff and very attentive. Reminder they do not call the flights so you need to pay attention to the time.

I accessed this Flagship Lounge at Chicago O'Hare while in transit, with my One World Emerald card. The AA Flagship Lounge is a cut above the standard Admiral's Club lounges in Terminal 3. It is not large but comfortable, with grouped seating areas including a dining area and a quiet zone room. The lounge will most likely be refurbished soon, and is beginning to show its age. It does not have shower facilities. Staff was very friendly and helpful. Very good quality food, unlike the limited selection in standard Admiral's Club lounges. The beverage selection was also adequate for this type of facility. My flight was cancelled due to bad weather, and the reception staff was most helpful in checking the status of my AA re-booked flights, as I was connecting through Chicago O'Hare Airport from a Cathay Pacific international flight to AA domestic service. A nice place to spend some hours away from the terminal crowds.

Not allowed in to American Airlines lounge, despite having a business class/first class ticket. I was appalled. They only allow members in. I can't think of another airline in the entire world that won't allow first class ticket holders into the lounge. In any event they only offer poor snacks.

The renovation is proceeding along nicely. The club is smartly redesigned with a selection of decent breakfast foods tastefully presented. Wi-fi worked as expected. Bathrooms are temporarily closed due to the renovation. I'm giving the lounge an 8 because of the bathrooms being closed and there still being overflow space since the club isn't large enough to accommodate all guests at periodic times.

Spent a couple of hours in the lounge transiting between Zurich and JFK. Well laid out. There were secluded sections and a large partitioned room to watch TV. Good w-fi connection and several computers to use. Ample power outlets with all possible standards to accommodate every charger! A good selection of drinks. Comfortable couches. Limited selection of hot food or snacks. Staff was regularly moving about keeping the place tidy. All in all, it was a welcome oasis. Unfortunately, no announcements are made and I suddenly realized I had to get to my gate, which was not adjacent.

I connected twice through JFK from London to Brazil in the past week. The Admirals Club in the A Concourse is under renovation until 2017 (there is a temporary facility in this concourse, and full club facilities in the distant B concourse). The Flagship Lounge is still fully open in Concourse A, and compared to other international airline lounges, it is showing it's age. That said however, it is very comfortable, and has decent facilities and the two times I was there, it wasn't that crowded. There is a good selection of beverages at a self-serve area. The food selection is varied with hot and cold foods, and are well presented, and good quality. No table service is offered, but it is still a cut above the normal Admirals Club offering. You won't go hungry in this lounge. The decor is a little dated in muted earth colours, and lacks any style. It is pleasant, but not outstanding. There is a TV area, seated table area for eating, armchairs, and business area with printer. There are well equipped shower facilities to use if you need to freshen up. The massive window area provides a lot of light, and great view of the busy tarmac and Manhattan in the distance. With all the minor shortcomings, what makes this lounge stand out though is the staff. Perhaps the friendliest and helpful attendants in the AA system. Their can-do attitude slightly made up for the extremely unpleasant onboard service from Rio to NYC. I gather that with AA's much-touted 'extreme makeover' of their clubs will eventually see this lounge get the full modernizing treatment, but in the meantime, this is a pleasant place to bide your time before your departure.

Not really as friendly as the TWA Ambassador Club lounge that it replaces, but not bad. It is staffed with many of the same people who worked in the TWA lounge. The décor is the hospital waiting room that one as come to expect from American, but the staff's friendliness makes the difference. A nice place to relax.
I used the American Airlines Admirals Club as a Qantas Club member, and the lounge at LAX Terminal 4 was nice, comfortable with good coffee, bagels, cereal and toast - better than Qantas Club!

Very spacious lounge with big concierge. Lounge assistance very efficient with managing shower slot, checking gate information and flight update. Seating area fairly comfortable. Food and drinks choice of Soft drinks, hot beverages - if you fancy premium drinks you pay for it. Food works the same (carrots, celery sticks, olives, tomatoes, humus, soup free, but premium food is at an extra charge.

Admirals Club at Tampa Airport, the staff in lounge helpful and friendly. Lounge drinks are fairly basic unless you pay extra for premium drinks (wine, mixers, ect.) Food choices are fairly the same as drink choices, carrot, crackers, celery sticks with humous or choice of soup. Other premium food is at an extra charge. Not much staff to clean left over from previous customers. Fairly basic lounge.

One of the brighter spots at Austin Airport is the American Airlines Admirals Club. Great customer agents who work hard to help with schedules and changes. While the club is small, and needs updating, food is good and service is great! It's about the only thing that helps you keep your sanity if you are traveling through Austin. Nice bar!

This lounge in terminal 3 is pathetic compared to other lounges when you see the minimal food choices. The facility is very large with comfortable seating, but the food is limited to cheese cubes, pretzel mix, brownies, cookies and one drink. A drink can be alcoholic or non-alcoholic. I'm not just comparing to Admiral clubs at major airports like Heathrow; even Austin has much better.

We had a very nice breakfast before an 8:40 am flight. It was lovely, with hot options of creamy scrambled eggs, Canadian bacon, potato patties and roasted herbed tomatoes. Cold options included cereals and milk, yogurt, granola, fabulous baked goods including buttery flaky croissants and other puffed pastries, muffins, rolls and very tasty oat & dried fruit treats. They had two kinds of smoothies, juices, choice of coffees and teas. Alcoholic drinks were also available. The room was well staffed and the tables (with plenty of charging possibilities) were frequently cleared.

Had very low expectations, but the Austin lounge was fine. Had a nice salad and croissant sandwich. Other sandwiches were available, and they had a couple of stations with various snacks and even brownie bites. Bartender was very attentive, and staff were always busy busing the tables.
