It doesn’t look like a cafeteria as before but like a real premium lounge. I was flying with the Air France Platinium Ultimate card so I was in a private area  with only 2 other people. The food was great but not a lot of choice. The lounge was quite crowded but very quiet which is very nice. To conclude, I think it’s a very good lounge and possibly the best I tried in CDG.

A small lounge in terminal 1 Munich Airport for the business class guests and frequent Flyers of Air France and KLM. Sky Priority Guests have also access to this lounge. This is a small lounge with minimum of necessary things, like Coffee and small food (finger food, snacks) buffet. That's it.

Stunning! What strikes you at first is the staff: everybody smiles! This lounge has recently been completely redone and it's a true hit. Nice and truly comfortable.Two levels, each one different the lower one having no windows but quite an extraordinary fake sky, the ground one with big windows overlooking the runway. A truly good buffet with lots of choices plus a bar with a large selection of good wines and champagne. But the very best feature of this lounge is that you can have dinner there, not buffet dinner, true dinner with a full menu, sitting down at a nice table with great service. To date it is one of the only 3 Air France lounges offering this great service enabling you to sleep as soon as you board the plane. Congratulations to the fantastic station manager I had the privilege to meet briefly!

Air France lounge at Paris CDG T2E looks like a hive. Many people in all directions, space too open, big. An incessant hubbub. Few seats really comfortable. There is a relaxation area but it is very small. There is a Clarins care service but by appointment, preferable to have a lot of transit time. While the food served is very good and much better than in many other business fairs around the world, the whole is rather except the staff who are professional and helpful.

Expected so much more. Food was really poor and another guest actually advised me to put prawns in my pot noodle to make it better! Was nice that champagne was available to help yourself. Also not good the airline advertise Clarins treatments but when you arrive they are 9-5 - at an airport!

Air France used to have a rather poor lounge at Terminal 2G. However, they recently opened a new lounge, which is quite impressive. The interior is appealing. It is spacious and – at least when we visited it – there were plenty of seating opportunities. The food was the same as in all Air France lounges at CDG, which means that the quality and quantity were very good.

DNATA Lounge in Changi Terminal 1 used by Air France. WiFi speed in lounges is generally not known for its speed but in this case it was very poor although good signal Quality: between 0.25 and 0.39Mbps at tested on three attempts. That is pretty useless. There was a place to take a shower but it was poorly serviced. No towels available and out of toilet paper. Few amenities available: only soap, no comb or toothbrush.

This is the place to be. JAL First class Haneda Lounge decor is perhaps better (and the John Lobb station a very nice addition), but Air France La Premiere Lounge has incredible service and food (Alain Ducasse).

Air France 2F Paris Near gate F 29. The new chairs they have put on the lounge are not convenient to work with a laptop - they are just not comfortable. I don’t complain about the  size of the bathroom since is extremely small for the amount of people here in the morning,  but please decent chairs to rest! Magazines choice are  great, and the food is still fresh, not many options but fresh fruit salad and some decent yogurts. WIFI is still good and staff is still nice and kind.

Greeted as I arrived from Dublin for my connecting flight to Singapore and driven by limousine to this exclusive lounge. The ambiance was perfect. Calm and tranquility throughout. You can order from an à la carte menu of top restaurant standard. Shower facilities and sleeping area readily available. Driven again by limousine to board the plane. No waiting, no queue. Perfectly organised. On my return I was impressed that the hostess who remembered me had booked a massage session for me as I was unable to avail of this during my outbound flight since the service had ended at 1700. This is truly the best lounge I have ever had the privilege to be in. Thank you Air France for providing a truly first class service!

It was good to have access to this lounge away from the crowd but what was on offer was not up to standard. On arrival I was asked if I had been in the lounge before by a woman who was on the computer and made no eye contact. I replied yes and she did not hear me and raised her voice with "pardon?". A little bit of politeness would have been very welcome! That was a very bad impression to start with. There was hardly anything substantial to eat even though it was lunchtime. The staff appeared to be busy cleaning and did not really enquire if you needed anything. Overall it was good to be able to relax in this lounge but it needs a lot of improvement.

The Air France Paris CDG 2E lounge is a mediocre player - nice enough space, comfortable armchairs, solid wifi, and I had a great and necessary shower. Not much of a choice of food, and the red and white wines were limited to just one each. Where's the wine?! I'm being really picky, I suppose, but having just been to the Madrid Adolfo Suarez-Bajaras Sala VIP Cibeles lounge (an open, airy, bright and beautiful space), I think this lounge just doesn't cut it.

I/we did not visit this lounge as due to a petty little issue with our AF Premium Economy tix apparently showing "Prem Econo" on both segments of our journey, (YYZ-CDG-AGP) but in fact our flight connex on Air Europa was dumping us back in Economy, so we were denied access. This, despite seeing on the in-flight AF entertainment system that PE pax were allowed access in both CDG and AMS. After making this all clear to the agent at the AF lounge desk and later at the help desk, calls were made and was confirmed that it's all based on your cabin class on the next flight. Not even being Flying Blue members helped, you'd think they would have cut us some slack on a 5 hour connex to keep us as happy campers.

I used this Air France/KLM lounge as a Xiamen Airlines passenger. Very pleasant, light, comfortable lounge. The food there was great, and since it was operated by Air France, most of the alcohol was the best picks. The food was top notch, and up to expectations, and was very diverse, as in some Thai food and French/Western food. The staff were friendly, and the wifi worked.

Emirates uses the Air France Business class lounge in Dulles as it does not have its own lounge unlike Etihad which has its own lounge in IAD. The lounge was conveniently opposite to our boarding gate and was a bright lounge. There was a separate smaller area for First class passengers. One shower room was present for usage although it lacked anything like shaving or dental items. Food offering were average and included only 1 cereal, breads, 1 type of egg sandwich and yogurt and fruits. There were plenty of seats facing the tarmac. Overall not bad.

Nice lounge with good breakfast. Probably the best of the Air France  lounges at CDG. Most of the others are getting very old and look worn. When you get to the lounge make sure you take the time to go right inside where you will find lots of space. Walking time from the lounge to the M gates is short.

We are currently at CDG. Took the new business class pod seats on Air France from LAX (flight 69). While the new product was quite nice and the service and food were above average, that was where the fun ended. We have a 5 hour layover in CDG and it has been anything but a good time. We arrived in terminal 2E and planned to go to the Air France Lounges in that terminal, as they are supposed to be the best ones. Also, Terminal 2E is supposed to have all the cool things to do/see, like the Sony and Panosonic areas, but nobody tells you that you can only go to the AF Terminal and Lounge in the terminal you are flying out of. Since our connecting flight to Barcelona was in Terminal 2F we were only allowed to go to that Terminal. Especially important because there are only two abysmal lounges there (think small, dated, minimal food, no spa, etc) and very little to do, see, eat (w/maybe exception of Le Duree Restaurant).  We tried to get through security to 2E, but it was a no go since our flight was out of 2F.  The issue is that CDG is a cluster of security and checkpoints, so to get to the lounge area after de-boarding you need to go thru the security hurdle. Part of the fun for us in traveling is getting a good business or first class product and also enjoying the lounges. Not a fun start to an otherwise fabulous vacation. Air France should be ashamed of such dismal facilities at their flagship airport!!

The lounge is comfortable and there is ample food, soft drinks etc. Main problem is that travellers on Air France Premium Economy are denied access. I was given access on my first visit and on my second visit I was given special access as I had been mugged in the airport. Premium Economy ticket gets you access to Business Lounge in CdG Paris but not in Yaoundé. This is ridiculous as the lounge is not full. Air France should take note.

A nice looking little lounge - nicely and subtly decorated. A totally different aesthetic than the rest of the airport. Food was pleasant and plentiful. Not the variety you see at CDG or other Business Class lounges but good enough for a 2 am departure. Good selection of drink as well. Only tiny complaint was it was warmish in there.

I am pretty satisfied with the standard of this lounge. Fast Wifi and conveniently positioned power sockets around the lounge made it easy to catch up with emails and even download a movie to watch later on the plane. Very comfortable armchairs and good selection of drinks. Food (it was lunch time) was pretty decent too, offering a wide selection of different salads and cold/hot dishes.

Flying Icelandair we were offered passes to the Air France lounge, as it is shared with Icelandair, whom we flew with. For a Business Class Lounge, the amenities and services offered were on par. The decor was modern, with a slight hint of days past. Everything adorn with tans and reds helped break up the monotony of white that adorns the airport. You have a spectacular view of the tarmac and gates, which in the evening, offers great plane spotting as the sun goes down. The bar is fully stocked, with traditional offerings of wine and champagne. Since this trip was part of our anniversary, we started celebrating early with some champagne. The refreshments and meal offerings consisted of cheeses from France, coldcuts and crackers as well as mini sandwiches. Cold sodas, coffe and tea are a typical staple and are in abundant supply. The staff frequents the serving area, ensuring that everything stays stocked. Seating is abundant as well, although getting there at or around the time of certain flight's departure could cause you to stand a little. The seating is comfortable and enjoyable if you are in a layover situation. Bathrooms and a shower are available if needed, as well as a niche in the far end of the lounge for extra quiet time. Wifi connectivity was fast, simple and strong, which helped pass the time during our wait for the flight to arrive. If given the chance to visit again, I would, as the comfort factor is rather high and impressive for Air France.

We used the Air France lounge when flying with China Eastern Airlines. The lounge is located to the left, just after security. It's a long and narrow facility divided into three sections. Seating was plentiful as were drinks and snacks. The food was unremarkable, more Bakersfield than San Francisco or Paris. There were two (maybe three) monitors giving departure times and gates. No boarding announcements were made. All in all, it beat waiting near our gate.

Air France lounge is in need of urgent refurbishment and / or a  good clean. Lounge seats dirty. No hot food available until one hour before departure. Only 2 minute noodles available. Had to leave lounge to get some food. Drinks selection was good. One TV not working, the other fuzzy.

This was a Priority pass lounge - not Air France! Comfortable enough but the food offerings here are as basic as you can get. A couple of ordinary sandwiches, some fruit and one type of a small maderia cake. The staff weren't in any rush to replenish either. Lazy lounge. Food and service.
Spacious and quiet lounge with a wide range of quality food and alcohol including champagne. Enjoyable experience. Friendly staff.
Nobody at CDG airport seems to know where the AF arrival lounge is - they made my walk around for nearly one hour with plenty of luggage and I was unable to find. No signs anywhere.

One of the best lounges I have experienced. There are enough showers rooms. This is valuable as I usually come in this lounge before (or after) a 12-hour flight. I would have rated it 5* but the buffet especially drinks is a little bit skimpy.

It's worth noting that it very much depends on the terminal; typically if you are in 2E and 2F it's good level of lounge with showers fresh food coffee/ tea internet and power - all a business traveller wants. If you go to a lesser terminal 2D for example there really is nothing more than a seat coffee and power. It's worth noting that if you do have a long haul flight and you arrive before 2pm you can use the lounge in the arrivals area of 2C.. this has around 6 showers and the usual... not the most comfortable but the staff are polite and it's a hell of allot better waiting for your TGV (Train) in here after a shower.

This is a sorry excuse for a lounge. Drinks are plentiful but there was 1 sandwich when I walked in and an hour later still 1 sandwich. There were no plugs to recharge electronics and when I asked they directed me to unplug a lamp and use the socket! This is Air France's home country and this lounge is the best they've got? Quite sad as it is no better than a waiting room.

We flew Aeromexico Business class from JFK to Mexico City On March 2014. Since the Aeromexico and Air France have a SkyTeam alliance agreement we went to Air France’s Business Lounge in Terminal 1 at JFK. The lounge is small and clean and does offer relaxation time before boarding. One can sit in a deep cushion chair place food on the table or use the complimentary computers. Food offerings on March 19 2014 started with stale roast beef/cheese sandwiches that came from the deep freeze cheap corn chips and packaged cookies one can find in a Supermarket etc. Champagne and other alcoholic and soft drinks were available in ample quantity. The coffee was good and so strong.

Noticed a small improvement in the food served here in this lounge I visit regularly. If you use this lounge after 7pm you might enjoy a light meal . Choices 10 days ago were a nice beef roulade salad and or grilled vegetables. Soup is also available usual cheese and cake for desert. Much better food then before in this lounge and more fun eating here then food served in airplanes at 1 am. Alcohol wines etc are excellent …If only Air France would see to it there would be some decent food all day long instead of having chocolate chip cookies from 1pm to 7pm this would be a further much appreciated improvement.
Absolutely appalling. Dreadful food and tables covered with dirty plates and glasses that the non-existent staff have failed to remove. Quite the worst lounge I have ever been in.

Had a five hour stopover between flights. No problems using this lounge for that length of time. Very spacious lounge with plenty of seating and tables for dining. Food provided was of the snack/light meal variety but was good quality. Champagne and wine available on a help your self basis. Toilet and shower facilities were excellent with really good shower lots of hot water at high pressure and good amenity pack provided. All in all an excellent oasis of calm in a very busy airport.

2 very small elevators as stairs to get to this lounge which is not that easy to find but i know my way around cog terminal 2e gate L OR K. Lounge is small surely for the crowd that makes usage of this lounge. Lounge is dark and not clean . it was early morning so food choice was poor choice as usual in cog airport  croissant  pain au chocolate cereals and something a new a chocolate that has no chocolate taste. Coffee and espresso machine seems to be in need of repair as what i received from this coffee maker had no coffee taste . For those wanting boost early in the morning everything available as soft drinks . As usual af lounge leaves me wondering why do I bother.
Dreadful. Avoid this lounge if you can. Looks like a temporary facility. Food was dreadful staff were invisible as were the facilities.

La Premiere Lounge at CDG is probably the best airport lounge I have experienced. Limo transfer direct from disembarkation gate on arrival from long haul flight. Air France staff accompanies to the dedicated security lane inbound to lounge. In the lounge enjoy the Alain Ducasse restaurant some exceptional wine. Beautifully restful chaise longue area with subdued lighting for resting. Toilets and showers are a work of art. Nice bathrobes and slippers with top of the range cosmetics/shower products. Agent drives you to the steps of your departing plane for the next sector.

Crowded and hard to find a place to sit. Washrooms dirty and small for size of lounge. Food service non existent but decent choice of soft drinks available. Overall not impressive and rather poor offering from a reputable air carrier.
Very poor facilities old lounge what are they doing? Very poor services friendliness cleanliness etc.

I took the opportunity to test the new AF lounge at the newest boarding satellite called S4. A completely new experience from the other lounges I have visited at CDG. Very large seperated in several areas with a real bar with the usual selection and great wines and a first for any AF lounge a self service Hot food corner including some risotto pasta cold meat and some pastries for dessert. A huge step from the S3 lounge. No problem at all to find a table or a sofa to rest. Plenty of working space and reading material too. Modern design with a nice view on the tarmac. Hope they would upgrade the other lounges the same way!

Kind of a fail. This lounge is dated worn and desperately needs air conditioning. The leather chairs are worn and dirty. The wi-fi is slower than the general free Frankfurt Airport wi-fi and just outside the lounge is a long hallway with recliners for regular passengers to lounge in comfort. The only places to sit in the lounge for lounge customers are upright chairs. Additionally there are no bathrooms within the lounge and if you need those facilities you are directed to leave the lounge and go down the hall to use public bathrooms. Given all of this I'm not really sure why you would choose to come in to this lounge unless you would like to eat some of the simple packaged cookies or the cheese that is sitting out in warm temperatures. Very little in the way of hard liquor. No red wine on display and a single white wine in the refrigerator. There was a sparkling wine in an ice bucket that was untouched. I found this whole wine selection to be odd. Air France needs to spend a little effort at improving this lounge in my opinion.

Lounge is easy to find and close to gate but lounge is still the same lounge as I have visited to many times when flying from this airport. Not so comfortable chairs that are already showing there usage. Cheap South African wine and some sandwiches chips crackers and some cheese. Not really a place to enjoy relax after working all day and still having to fly 10 hours. Wifi improved and is working very well now.

A few seats uncomfortable. No decent food coffee and tea from coin machines. Some newspapers. Such a minimal lounge that I now avoid it and use the open bars and cafes of the airport far better and friendlier.

Old and crowded lounge always full. They have 3 flights (2 AF and one KLM) departing early evening so the space is not enough for all passengers. The food is mediocre and there is only one old shower in urgent need of renovation.

We used the business class lounge of Charles de Gaulle as transit passengers. The experience was horrible. Dirty seats empty bags and paper glasses no choice in food just some packaged stuff. Plus the lounge was crowded. On the way back the lounge was almost empty but the manager decided to prevent us from getting in with 10 and 12 yrs old children (who were on economy class tickets). All in all my experience with Air France is way below average.

The lounge is okay and I get to do my work without interruptions or noise. However in the morning and there is no food - just snacks I thought by now with all the complaints something would be different. People care about food they want to eat Air France please listen to your customers!!

A charming stewardess picks you up at the incoming flight taking you to this dedicated Lounge. A butler welcoming you a Michelin starred restaurant with perfect service and outstanding wines. The quality of showers massage is like a hotel. All passport formalities completed in the lounge.

One of the worst I have been in. It is very small and has the most uncomfortable chairs. Before international flights in the evening it is packed. People walking around trying to find a seat. The bathrooms are small and dirty. Food selection is minimal. Plenty of cold drinks. Do not pay extra to get into this lounge.

Absolutely diabolical. The food selection is virtually non-existent unless you like potato As a regular JNB passenger I visit this lunge often. The worst part are the most uncomfortable seats - the seat are designed to make a "statement" but are the most uncomfortable ever experienced among many business lounges around the world. Air France should look at their KLM partner lounges in AMS and its seat / electric outlet convenience (still no international plugs - they require adapters). Food and beverage selection is decent and so is the internet functionality. Men's bathroom typically dirty sometime lacking supplies.

Absolutely diabolical. The food selection is virtually non-existent unless you like potato crisps/chips. What food there is (cold slabs of processed pork a bowl of mini-gherkins and some awful sandwiches) is desperately low quality. There is no service within the lounge itself which is sterile and uncomfortable. In AF's home country at their home airport this is a disgrace.
Pretty awful. Food is very poor and coffee is truly dreadful. Decor is ugly fittings are falling off the walls staff are invisible (debris stays at tables for hours).

It seems that most lounges from Air France I visit suffer from the same acute problem. Food quality and choice is ridiculous compared with lounges from other airlines. AF lounge in Paris terminal 2E food choice is very poor and cheap quality. Most food there is cheap sandwiches crackers and chips. Choice of drinks is ok even if wine quality could be better to even much better.

The design is very trendy and it offers nice views on the apron. It is divided in several zones depending on what you are looking for. Usually AF lounges are not very good for the catering but this one offers a wide choice of food and drinks. I took advantage of the Clarins Spa that is free. It's now time for Air France to offer a consistent product and offer the same comfort and quality and choice of food in all their lounges.

The lounge in 2F at CDG is a shame as the terminal 2F itself. In the entrance the welcome speech from the staff is almost an apology about the lounge situation. One floor was closed so the remaining space was totally crowded. The only seats we could find were at a table in the end facing bathrooms. Very limited food choice only cold croissants and nuts crisps. There were only one shower 40 minutes wait time.

I don't understand the Air France business class product at all particularly compared to similarly priced business class products like British Airways or Virgin Atlantic (which actually are less expensive). At a BA or Virgin lounge you get a fully stocked and staffed bar. At Air France the self- service selections at Air France are limited. At a BAR or Virgin Lounge I can order a full sit down meal. At Air France I got to chose from slices of cold pork some cheese some crackers and potato chips. I do my best to avoid Air France but sometimes I have no other option.

Flew with Icelandair who use this new Air France lounge. Staff in lounge very friendly food was sandwiches and nuts. Food well presented bar staffed at all times this I thought was not good as I like to get my own drinks. Showers great and very refreshing water hot and shower room was well cleaned. If I had one complaint I would say the seating looks like old school chairs. Great views from the big windows of the aircraft coming and going. I also imagine that with a A380 the lounge would be cramped and very busy - Lucky only 2 B777's on my departure day.
Clean and roomy lounge not much selection for food around and usual drinks selections. Nothing special for the time I was there.
Dirty tables uncleared for hours - looks like 3rd class train waiting room. Go to a restaurant instead.
The lounge was airy with good food. Plenty of quality wines. The wi-fi connection was efficient. Toilets were clean. The lounge is close to the boarding gate. This made for a pleasurable experience.

This lounge is small but quiet most of the time. The front desk assistant was friendly and made sure to make announcements about flights which were boarding. The snacks are fresh and delicious. The bar selection was not extensive but there is a reason for this - If you want a drink such as champagne or a caipirinha just ask! The restrooms were small but clean. There was constant removal of empty plates glasses etc. The internet was very slow during the peak hours but at other times the internet speed was fair.

Lounge is used by many airlines too many for the size of the lounge even if I got lucky this time and found a good seat. The lounge is used by so many airlines that announcements for flight boarding are going on forever - maybe they should learn from other lounges and make this one a silent one. Food quality is poor and choice is at the same disappointing level. Drinks consist of cans and bottles that are presented in a very small refrigerator - meaning the cans have no time to become col. Wine served is local brew. Lets hope for a Skyteam lounge in new terminal. Wifi is very badly organised and only 3 computers available.

Same old overcrowded lounge with same food and drinks (choice not very big or interesting) espresso machines are dirty and food is tasteless. Lounge is also used by people having a certain credit card. While waiting to get in and present your invitation one has to wait for the man in front of you deciding if he is going to charge his credit card with money or points.

Too small both the AF and KLM flights leave within a few minutes it is far too crowded. No power outlets seating not very comfortable lounge looks a bit worn. Drink selection just ok food not what you would expect of the French!
This is without doubt the worst lounge as far as food is concerned. A 11pm flight and nothing to eat but crisps and dry cheese. Air France should be ashamed.
A perfectly adequate lounge a bit small. Not as nice as the bigger 2E lounge but nice. Staff very friendly. Food fine - sandwiches yoghurt soup crisps and drinks. I enjoy the Air France lounges.

A good lounge with direct access to gate M7 usually the one used by the AF departure. Great supply of French newspapers adequate Wifi snacks/sandwiches usually OK Champagne very good (but has a tendency to run out quickly and staff less than enthusiastic about bringing new bottle).

Terrible Lounge - no water in the toilets neither for washing hands. I used the only 50CL bottle at around 19.00 hrs. Was sitting close to the toilet entrance and observed that none of the lounge staff put a new bottle of water - during 3 hours (time of boarding). In the meantime people were walking in/out and of course did their thing without washing hands!

Malaysia Airlines use this lounge -small and shabby with uncomfortable seating. The choice of food and drinks was very poor. The staff were rather indifferent and off hand when we asked for more croissants. They were having a delivery of stock which was being wheeled through the lounge during the whole of the one and half hours we were there not a very relaxing atmosphere! There is no left luggage facility so if you want to shop you have to take you hand luggage with you. For a European Airport the standard of this lounge is shocking.

Lounge is really average and comparable to other AF lounges in CDG. The letdown is the poor quality of the food offered. It was lunch time we were provided with a meagre choice of soup sandwiches a slice of turkey and cheese. Needless to say every one rushed for food there was nothing left besides the usual chips and crackers. The lounge is big let down as 2E is the modern part of CDG.

Arriving at 1830 the upper level was very full and everywhere you looked there were trays with empty cans wrappers napkins etc. Catering not that bad. An assortment of grilled sandwiches soup crisps bread cheese nuts etc. Staff manning the desks were a bit sullen. I hope that their other lounges at CDG are of better quality.

The lounge in 2F at CDG is small and very crowded. The only seats we could find were at a table in the cafe area at the back. The whole place feels more like a railway station waiting room than a business class lounge. Limited food choice some sandwiches nuts crisps etc. Are all AF lounges at CDG as abysmal as this?

Air France business lounges in Terminal 2C and 2F are very similar. Upper Deck Closes at 1630 adding to overcrowding of the small main lounge which at peak times is horrible overcrowded loud and noisy. Selection of drinks is limited sometimes there are some snacks (cheese baguettes fruits etc) which disappear within a few minutes because of the big amount of guests. Rest rooms are too small and Staff do not seem to be very motivated or even attempt to pretend they care! The feedback unit did not work which says it all.

Le Patiolounge is located on the 1st floor of Orly-Ouest Hall 2 just after the security check. Staff is very polite and friendly. Lounge is clean and seats are comfortable with a nice view on the apron. There are three free internet computers - all were working properly. Quite a large selection of newspapers but most of them in French and only two in English. The huge disappointment is the poor food and drinks. For hot drinks there are only vending machines - the same type as in gas stations. The choice for cold beverages is a bit larger but only small cans are offered. Forget about food - at any time of the day the lounge offers only chips or biscuits!

The staff are reasonably polite but that's where the positives end. We were both starving when we got to the lounge at 6pm but there was no hot food. I then decided to have some cold food but there was hardly any of that either! What is the use of crackers without cheese or butter? Only Air France knows the answer to that. All they had was crisps. On complaining to the staff I was told since "a few months ago" they only serve food at certain times. When they did eventually serve the much awaited fare it was tepid soup and that was about it.

Basic lounge upstairs of the main alley in the terminal. No view except over the shopping corridor below. Limited range of food except crisps biscuits. Even during lunch hours disappointing. Drink range adequate so is the reading material. Couple of pc with free internet access good but faulty connection. Toilets are outside the lounge.

Very modern looking retro lounge. It has several work stations and free wifi. Several staff had occupied one corner and were trying to hide while being noisy and consuming lounge food and beverages. Food included crisps fruit pies quiches sandwiches. There was a self service bar with wines beers soft drinks coffees sparkling wine and spirits. Good choice. Not too much reading material.

Not a good experience Despite Pudong having a lot of lounges passengers from several flights seem to be packed into just 1 so that the staff end up trying to find seats for guests. The welcome was poor along the lines of "voucher sit down". Food poor no white wine only red and a request for white was met with a simply "no". In the end we moved out To the main concourse as it is quieter more pleasant and far less crowded. What is the point of paying extra for this?

I wonder if we are talking about the same lounge here. There are two international terminals one for Saudi Arabian airlines and one for all other airlines. At the "foreign" international terminal the lounge was crowded and obviously too small but let's say it did the job: a seat free drinks free Wi-fi. Women can access the lounge and sit anywhere (it is not separate). There are large TV screens and staff announce flights on time.

The lounge is pretty basic. Small not particularly well kept. Chairs are worn and electric outlets were not adapted to American plugs. The highlight of the lounge is the older man who works there who showed me how to pour my sweet Vermouth properly (over ice). Lounge has a decent supply of newspapers.

Good selection of food and drinks both alcoholic and non-alcoholic however the seats are the most uncomfortable I have even seen. This is definitely not a lounge you would want to spend a lot of time waiting for a flight! Their old lounge was far more comfortable. Air France need to look into making this more comfortable for passengers especially in this age when increasing security issues make longer stays at the airport more and more common.
Uncomfortable crowded shared with KLM. Not many magazines. Packaged crackers and cookies. Really a drag. No WiFi and no computers provided.
Amazing food. There is a barista and Chef. The mini bar was full of soda beverages but no alcohol, not even beer. The smoking room was fancy with leather couches and dim lighting. Amazing experience.

This Biman Bangladesh Airlines lounge is located on the third level of the airport.  I was greeted by smiling face and given a wifi password. The wifi speed was acceptable. However the password is valid for only 1 hour and one would have get a new one after that. The lounge has a smoking section. Being a non-smoker, I chose the section right in front of the smoking zone. There was a small snack spread and hot drinks station. This lounge was a little different as it did not have a buffet. Instead I had to point out my food selection to the counter staff.  The red wine of the day was Merlot. Tasted quiet good to me. A nice selection of newspapers (local and international) along with magazines was located close to the reception desk. The restroom was spotless with ample amenities. When boarding started, the lounge staff informed me. Overall, this was a nice and cozy little lounge and I wouldn't mind visiting again. I visited there during an off peak hour and do not know how it holds during rush hour.

Alitalia lounge at New York JFK was dull, outdated and the food selection was embarrassing. The staff at the check in were chatting on their mobile instead of paying attention to customers. The worst business class lounge I have experienced.

What an improvement. I must write that any Alitalia lounge i had visited in the past, was such poor quality. Casa Italia really earned its name well. Very friendly and professional welcome when entering the lounge. Large lounge with plenty of seating, plenty of staff attending to lounge. Typical Italian fresh pizza and pasta, Plenty of cured meat and vegetables. Very good and quality food, Large bar serving you any drink. I have visited this lounge several times already the past months and will be visiting it again in two weeks.

By far one of the best lounges I've visited this year: brand new, quiet, and classy. Excellent food offer: regional Italia specialties (Taleggio, ricotta affumicata, fresh baked pizza's), superior cutlery and fine dinnerware. Attentive staff: a staff member re-arranged the fruit cuts on the plate after every other person was taking some bits, so that it would look nice. We asked for a shower: after less than 10min. a staff member came to us and escorted us to the showers when ready to use. We had the feeling of having dinner in a good restaurant, with excellent espresso at the end

Bad experience ever. Just came out now from the domestic lounge. After more than 20 hours of flying myself with one year old baby on Etihad Airways, we went to the lounge as I am Etihad gold member and I’ve been kicked away in a “nice way” just because my little one was a little bit noisy. On top of that the service was really bad at the reception and food was really poor!! I will avoid it next time.

Limited food and beverage selection but was nice food for snack and refreshment and also not so much seating space, but location is quite okay, at the centre almost all of the boarding gate. I was okay for short time waiting, but if there's delay, then will be bored as it is only at a quite small Lounge.

The Alitalia Business Class lounge near terminal E at Rome Fiumicino is a real disappointment. Quite small, it has a bar counter where one has to request any type of drink from a couple of tired barmen (who complain about their workload all the time). This includes asking for coffee, alcoholic drinks or even a glass of water. A couple of small tables present a few uninviting snacks. Given the limited space, I had to sit on the only available chair - which was unoccupied only because it was broken. Used dishes and cutlery wait on the side tables for the infrequent service. Next time I shall pay at one of the cafeterias or fly with another airline.

The Dolci Vita Lounge is located in T1 before the check in area. If you are a business traveler you can check in your bags inside the lounge. They offer some pastries, coffee and many drinks. I went in to try their flight simulator but I was then told but the crew that it no longer exist! It's a medium size lounge. But I personally prefer the the Casa Alitalia inside the terminal

This is probably one of the best Alitalia lounges. It's a busy lounge but large inside and stylish. It offers bed-like seats and I actually good a good 2-3 hours of sleep. Food is very good but not excellent. Wine is good too. The staff are very welcoming and very nice and professional. I do recommend to use this lounge. It is possible to have a shower inside the lounge. Toilets were clean.

This lounge gets busy but is great. Shame that it is open to Priority Pass and Paid entry as this does mean it can get mobbed but is a fabulous lounge because of the food and drink available. Really tasty food including freshly made Pizza, Pasta and Bruschetta. Wide selection of drinks. Great cappuccinos at the bar. Showers are well maintained and nice products available. Wifi fast.

Recently renovated lounge, plenty of choice for food and typical Italian wines, I think it's the only airport lounge with a pizza maker who make the pizza in real time for the guest. Good selection of magazines and newspapers, the lounge at certain times it is a bit crowded, the bathrooms are generally quite clean as well as the showers. Of course, great coffee and cappuccino.

What a change from 2012. We were flying Emirates out of Rome Fiumicino Airport and had a bit of a laugh that we would have to use the Alitalia lounge. But what an unbelievable turn around in this lounge. Staff were amazing, offering suggestions for drinks and food. The food was fantastic.

Quite disappointing. Apart from being overcrowded, this lounge offers limited, uncomfortable seating. There is a bar for coffee and drinks, attended by unfriendly staff (if you ask for a glass of water, you are told to fetch a plastic bottle on the other side of the lounge). Some good salads offered, but the Italian food (pasta, ravioli) is singularly insipid. The worst part are the waiters who pile up dirty dishes on the table where you are dining, and scrape the leftovers in front of you, then leave the pile there waiting for more plates to collect: I have never seen such behavior in any food establishment. Washroom (men) OK but too small.

Recently renovated lounge, good selection of food and beverage, nice looking Italian furniture. Huge windows that overlook the runway. The staff was extremely helpful with my requests. Bathrooms clean.

This newly refurbished lounge is located in Terminal 1 landside before security checks. It is a large, comfortable lounge area equipped with desks for check-in, flight simulator, relaxation room and a well-stocked bar with tasting of hot and cold dishes from Italian ingredients

Do not pay for it and if lounge access was for free, find another one. Decor is basic, food choice is poor, no warm meals, just some canapés. Soft and alcoholic drinks must be asked at the bar but bottles and cans are hidden so you cannot see the range.  The upper floor has no bar or anything just seating and the toilets. Aircon was off up there so was much warmer than the lower floor.  The toilet decor is basic and one of the two cabinets was broken. Staff do not hurry to collect glasses and plates, or refill the food counter even during off-peak when they have plenty of time. Alitalia has other lounges, try them, this is ready for bulldoze.

The lounge is well located, behind the check-in area and before the security controls (which have a fast-track for frequent fliers and business-class passengers). It is possible to do the check-in directly in the lounge. Comfortable seats, great offer of food and drinks, both in quantity and quality. Good selection of newspaper and magazines. The lounge features a cockpit simulator with a flight instructor to try the experience of landing and take-off. Overall a great experience.

The lounge was good. Its not very friendly when you are traveling with a small child as the staff looks at you like you have three heads. As usual in this airport, service, at best, is mediocre. For a city that prides itself on the many small restaurants and overall good food, the lounge food was sub par. I had better service on Bearskin airlines. I have traveled extensively all over the world but I have never experienced less customer service than with Alitalia. We booked business class from Belgrade to Toronto. In Belgrade we were told by Alitalia staff that because we are traveling with a small child business class would be unavailable to us. As if they didn't know any of this when we booked it. In Milan we had to fight with Aliatlia to make sure that we can have 1st class that was paid for at least from Milan to Toronto. We succeeded! When we got to Toronto, they had lost our luggage so we waited 4hrs with a small child to see if they can find our luggage. Of course, no luck! The next day luggage arrived destroyed. I immediately submitted for a refund. Well needless to say its been 8 months now and I am still waiting for Alitalia to issue my refund to me.

Of the SkyTeam lounges at New York JFK (Delta, Air France, Alitalia), this Alitalia lounge is the worst. Furniture is old, dirty, worn and falling apart. WiFi is slow. And food is a random assortment of snacks (saltines and goldfish?) and soggy pre-made sandwiches. Nothing comfortable or relaxing about it. No showers. Staff did not offer Wifi code, had to hunt for a sign.

Very disappointed spent £60.00 for two tickets to this airport lounge. Food and wine poor. Toilet area and shower room dirty. Not worthy of the money paid. Such a let down to start of our long journey.

I'm writing from the lounge. What an absolute rip-off. I paid 30 Euros for the use of the lounge. It is loud and crowded the food is cold and with very poor selection. The wine was poured in a plastic glass and was the tiniest quantity. There's lots of staff but they don't seem to care about much. The wifi does not work.

The Alitalia lounges at FCO are the worst I've experienced for any major airline. They're appalling. The selection of food is so dismal that I don't know why Alitalia even bothers putting anything at all out there. Unfortunately if you travel through FCO these wretched Alitalia lounges are what you get stuck with.

The worst lounge I visited compared to Hong Kong Toronto Singapore Beijing San Francisco Bangkok that I have been. No windows no food available (time 11AM) only a drinks bar no windows male washroom had only two toilets (no urinals so you have to wait for a simple pee). Most disappointing was after an 8 hour flight I love to have a shower to refresh myself but they ran out of shower kits (no towels no soap no shampoo). Never go this lounge. I cannot imagine that Alitalia's lounge in Rome is such poor quality.

Never visited such a poor lounge before. Firstly no daylight as no windows in this lounge. Beside freshly made Italian coffee served by a friendly barman who has a little plate with some change to have every visitor understand what he wishes to receive this lounge has the smallest choice of food. Food choice goes from sweet Italian croissant to greasy couscous. Some other small pieces of bread are available but not worth to be mentioned. There is one toilet in male lavatory and this one toilet is dirty as are 3 showers of which two where mot working. Seating not bad and wifi works well but do not come to this lounge hungry.

Lounge was just fine: clean and conveniently located but overcrowded. Food and beverage was not you would expect from a business lounge in Italy: a few cold sandwiches basic soft drinks and house wine. Overall an average/below average lounge.

Alitalia lounge very much outdated as are the unfriendly staff. Quality of the refreshments and selection of such is poor. The lounge is on the inside of the terminal and has no windows it is like a maze and appears to have no predetermined structure.

Using this lounge in early mornings is really not pleasant: all you are offered for breakfast in terms of food are cheap and tasteless croissants and some other low quality focaccia type bread nothing else. Very sub-standard!

This lounge (accessible to other Skyteam travellers) is probably one of the worst I've seen in Europe. Colors are awful comfort is quite limited and facilities are just ridiculous - drinks server in a plastic cup with a very limited choice (Diet sodas not available!) nearly nothing in terms of food and you wonder what the barmaid just does there so she looks bored.

What is going on Alitalia? What is going on with business class at one of their hubs? This lounge is awful dark unfriendly. No food choices. No internet except it might have been there but did not work. Seats dirty.

A new refurbished business lounge inaugurated just 1 week ago. The lounge has free wi-fi choice of food and drink is fair with snacks and soft drink (and some italian wine). A very nice view of the runway and apron of the airport.

Had the opportunity to use the Alitalia Business Lounge at the JFK airport was pleasantly surprised by the lounge with contemporary decor and layout with enough comfortable seating space. Catering options were adequate. There were not enough power points to plug in a computer.

FCO to LHR in Business class. I was introduced to a small shabby crowded lounge which had no windows. The lounge was very uncomfortable so uncomfortable that I left after a while and went into the Departure area. The Catering in the lounge is not bad but there is a lot of room for improvement and there are no cleaning staff in sight.

The lounge which provides complimentary hot and cold drinks and biscuits is available to all Blue Islands passengers. This seemed to surprise a couple of them who arrived looked around and backed out again as if they thought they'd made a mistake then reappeared looking rather impressed! I would imagine the lounge would be greatly appreciated if there was a delay although I haven't yet experienced a delay with Blue Islands.

The lounge can be accessed by all passengers flying with the (single class) airline. The lounge is comfortable and offers peace and quiet except during periods where two or more full flights are departing at similar times. Self service for complimentary drinks and snacks.

The lounge in Koh Samui was small but pretty good. It had great air conditioning and the beverages were good (I didn’t try the food, but the choices were good). The staff members were polite and friendly. There are no flight announcements, but the supervisor comes out and calls out people for the particular flight that has started boarding. My complaints were that the toilets were dirty and smelly and the WiFi was very poor. Overall good lounge, definitely recommend!

Boutique lounge in keeping with the airline marketing philosophy. Good choice of food and beverages; massage recliners and a lovely hot shower. Well worth the extra B1500 to fly in Business Class to access this lounge

Island style – if I were only allowed to use two words to describe the airport. The airy wide open spaces, lack of walls, and abundance of palm trees just get you into the island lifestyle mood straight away. Tasteful, bright and light nautical/beach themes permeate the airport, and the executive lounge is no different. I actually wish I had missed my flight.

I am impressed by Bangkok Airways' added-value benefit extended to their passengers flying economy by allowing to use their lounge in Bangkok. The place is kept clean, food and drinks regularly topped up (mostly finger food choices and standard refreshments. The lounge also provide comfortable seating and wi-fi connectivity which allows us to check our emails, and keep abreast with the latest news. I hope they can also allow the use of their lounge if the connecting flight is with their partner airlines. It would certainly make waiting a more pleasant experience before we reach our final destination.

Bangkok Airways was a pleasant surprise. It was the first time for me and my family. The lounge, at Phnom Pehn's Airport is small but comfortable. There were some soft and alcoholic drinks. There was also a small but lean menu. Service was just ok. Only one bathroom per gender, which wasn't stupendously clean, it was just fine.  Good overall experience.

My recent visit was horrendous. Food choice has gone downhill, seats were taken up, some groups of people took up six seats for three people.  The quality of staff service has gone downhill, and there are two agents. I think they should keep space available for their frequent fliers. Unfortunately, due to the fact that Bangkok Air have a monopoly on a route I fly so often, I am forced to fly them or else the other option is a lengthy five hour drive.

The lounge was open for every passenger of Bangkok airways, working myself in the aviation industry I find it amazing that this service is offered to every passenger traveling on their flights, I find it comfortable, nice personnel and good catering service. It is more than what you expect for what you pay.

A good airport lounge-decent F&B and great facilities We have used this lounge three times, once using Priority Pass, once Emirates and this time with Bangkok Airways. All the major airlines use the lounge, The food offering is very good with hot and cold options and there is a full bar. Good free WiFi and immaculate toilets and showers. Work zone and private rooms for meetings. Great views of the tarmac and runway. Really charming and friendly smiling staff, so typical of Myanmar.

It was a domestic flight and all passengers of Bangkok Airways can use this free Bangkok Airways Lounge in BKK airport. It's a part of boutique airline policy. It's not far from the gates, Staff is very polite and helpful. Big choice of magazines and leaflets about Samui. There are other places in this terminal for food and drinks (of course you should pay). But there's no free Wi-Fi in general places, so this Lounge is a good place for using free Wi-Fi (Lounge staff provides you with username and password).

I'm sitting in this free economy class lounge right now, it's very noisy due to being overcrowded. When you have at least 3x A320s departing every hour, they should build a bigger lounge.  The staff are polite, answer questions, but I didn't want to waste too much of their time. The food is great, there is a must try, It's a recipe called Khao-tom-mad. Or known as sticky rice with stuffed banana wrapped in banana leaves. It's the lounge's signature dish. The lounge decor is also very nice, Light and pleasant.  Wifi is also pretty fast, even though the download speed is sluggish I was able to send messages rapidly.

Bangkok Airways Business Class lounge in Koh Samui is the only lounge in that unique airport - and the only room for passengers with air-conditioning as the pubic waiting area for all flights is outside (but under a roof). Fine interior and very friendly staff. Welcoming and asking for drink and small food items. They bring it to your table, althought everything is also available at a buffet. Limited choice of newspapers, mostly Thai. But nice atmosphere and a fine place to relax before your flight.

Good lounge with lots of space, the lounge staff come to ensure you are comfortable regularly. There is a spotless shower room, a few hot food menu which are actually passable frozen food, other snacks are better and plentiful. There are a few wines at self service drink bar, Wifi is very quick. I found this lounge to be great, only downside is a constant announcement for flight information. There are only a few passenger in the lounge and I believe more personalized communication is possible.

I found this free lounge for economy passengers a bit crowded, but with acceptable choice of food and drinks (non-alcoholic). As it's accesible for all the passengers you can count on little space at all time. Free wifi access is given at the entrance. A couple os PCs are available. No TVs with flight information.

I upgraded to Bangkok Airways Blue Ribbon lounge by using AIS Serenade gold card; very well appointed lounge with waitress service to every seat. Hot breakfast on offer before my 07.00 flight. Nice choice of snacks and drinks available in a quiet calm well decorated lounge. Much better than the economy lounge next door.

Bangkok Airways provides lounge service for all its passengers regardless of travel class. The lounge at Vientiane International Airport looks a little old and small but considering the small size of the Wattay Airport itself, this lounge is passable. There were a wide variety of juices and light snacks available.

I have to admit that it was quite surprising to find out that travelers for economy class can use a very cozy, free-of-charge Bangkok Airways lounge. The staff are very warm and helpful and a delicious options of snacks (limited though) and a coffee and tea machine. There's also free internet wifi connection. it is also remarkable to say that the service from the dropp off counter was amazing. Thumbs up for Bangkok Airways so far!

Small but well appointed Bangkok Airways lounge in Phuket Airport with excellent wifi and a range of tasty snacks and soft drinks and tea coffee. A range of newspapers and magazines available in a spotlessly clean, comfortable haven away from the bustle outside. Pity no smoking area anywhere inside but appreciated the flight calls - personally by the lounge personnel, a lovely old fashioned touch.

Was transiting in Bangkok on my way to Laos. All economy class passengers were invited to use the lounge. As my flight from Tokyo landed at 5.00 am, there were not many people in the lounge. It was quiet and the seats were very comfortable. The food and drinks served were above my expectation.

The lounge has just been renovated and it looks nice. It seemed to have much more space than it actually is. Food offered included Thai snack, Bakery and pastries items, as well as soft drink, juice, tea, coffee (Alcoholic beverage is not on the list, or made known to visitors). Seating is plenty and comfortable, free wifi offer and the connection is very quick.

Too busy to be an outstanding experience. Choice of snacks and cakes plus tea, coffee, hot chocolate and orange squash. Excellent wifi until the lounge fills up, then streaming from YouTube becomes unacceptable. Very noisy and squashed since these lounges are free to use for all passengers in Economy class.

If you fly economy class and you can wait in a lounge for your next flight you are lucky because not so many airlines allow economy passengers in the lounge without extra charge. This was an extraordinary experience with free WIFI and snacks like mini sandwiches cookies popcorn coffee tea and powder juice. In fact there is a choice of more than 10 snacks to choose from. To be fair the Bangkok airways lounge in Chang Mai is slightly better with some extra ice tea and ice coffee plus a larger selection of snacks.

The Blue Ribbon Lounge at Suvarnabhumi is a disaster. First thing you notice is the heat. This is the second time I have to tell the ladies working there to turn on the air condition. First thing you see is a big stain on their carpet. The service is non smile and non attentive.

Fantastic. I wish Canada and the USA would adopt your service level. We enjoyed the relaxation and the refreshments in the lounges. We travelled to Phuket Koh Chang. Siem Reap and Koh Samui and downtown Bangkok. What a treat to be in comfort at airports where the staff need to be commended for their service.

Business Lounge at Suvarnnabhumi Airport by Bangkok Airways is great good services and variety of food to served and I have connecting flight from Munich at this Lounge has shower room for me to get fresh from long fight and relax at this quality Lounge.

The Blue Ribbon Lounge is located near departure gate 3. We were practically the only two persons in the lounge that day. We were greeted by a staff member who immediately brought us a small menu and took our drinks order. They have a selection of cold and hot snacks which you can help yourself to or order something warm from the menu. There is a massage chair tucked away in a room and another room with a small library and armchairs.

Located near Gate 3. This is a lovely lounge painted bright blue and white. It overlooks the beautiful manicured gardens of the airport. We were greeted warmly and given a cold drink. The staff brought us a menu from which we ordered a hot meal. There is a selection of cold and warm snacks which is self service. There is free internet and the lounge has approx 6 computers. There are no toilets within the lounge itself but outside the lounge near Gate 3. They are clean and tidy and have aquariums with tropical fish incorporated into the walls. The staff kept us up to date the whole time about our flight delay and came to personally collect us when the flight was ready for boarding. A very nice experience and can recommend.

Qualified customers will be entitled to use Blue Ribbon check in counter and Blue Ribbon Lounge once a month. The lounge is in the same area as economy class lounge but properly zoned. Selection of hot food and snack. Service is less smiling more formal and professional than economy class lounge. Nice looking decoration with touch of Thai. Facility include private relaxing room massage chairs WiFi Internet terminal and shower.

I had an economy ticket from Belgrade to Ljubjana, Slovenia, but I paid my way to Air Serbia Business lounge. Price was Euro 35. That was a total mistake. The lounge is a joke. It is dark, unfriendly with terrible food. Avoid it, please. In comparison it's much better to join one of the cafes elsewhere at the airport. An airport which by the way is more or less a dump.

Great lounge experience. Clean, delicate, quiet, just about the right amount and variety of food. Restrooms in impeccable condition. Staff very welcoming and attentive, also comes with a barista experience. Only thing I can think of missing; some reclining chairs?

Nice lounge, though a working area is missing. Comfortable, very good internet, plenty of electrical sockets, very attentive people, trying very much to be of service at all times. Food was excellent, served as in a restaurant with a nice choice of Serbian wines. A very good place to wait for a plane.

Had a long lay over Abu Dhabi to Malta via Belgrade. Service was excellent, lounge spotless and excellent a la carte food offerings. Very helpful staff, did not have adapter for charging but a USB charger which was efficient. Maybe I was lucky as not so many other passengers, but speak as I found.

I was greeted by a hostess at the door. But the staff working in the lounge were more busy with the telephone and talking to each other then serving the guest. I was the only customer at that time. Food great selection but the staff forgot to put the heater on and the chillers. So all the hot food was cold and yogurt was hot. After 40 min I got contact with the staff and the heaters and chillers where put on. Overall mixed feelings sometimes the experience is great and sometimes poor.

Recently opened Air Serbia lounge located next to A5 exit is very modern and with excellent service. You are greeted by hostesses that take care of your carry on if you want to store it and walk you to the sitting area. Service in the lounge is personalized and the menu is restaurant like with a great selection of dishes and drinks. Washroom and showers are well maintained and clean; WiFi works well. I rated lounge comfort with 4 due to the absence of reclining chairs for sleeping.

Aeromexico has a lounge at Mexico City airport but it is closed for renovation. So Business Class passengers are sent to the Heineken lounge which is some distance from their flight gates. The lounge is Spartan, noisy and not a place to rest before a flight. Wi-fi is very difficult to access. To make matters worse, I was refused entry because having landed from Cuba, my onward flight left more than 3 hours later. When I was allowed in there was no food except yoghurt. The staff were very friendly but they have nothing to offer. Avoid if possible.

I think it is the worst lounge I have been. Crowded, uncomfortable, bad food or better said, no food at all. When they bring food out, it is like vultures, people run to it like they have never eaten before. It seems that people there love whatever is free. This lounge accepts just about anyone. You pay a fee and you get in... booze flows, I think that is why people pay to get in.

Appalling. Overcrowded, loud. people and bags and backpacks everywhere. Completely unrelaxing, impossible to work or read. This is what intercontinental business class passengers get? Definitely not worth paying for. This feels more like a bus terminal.

The lounge has been redesigned to meet new distancing guidelines. Noise level is adequate. Free of charge are drinks and only salty or sweet. Everything else is charged and by no means a nominal fee. I ordered a portobello hamburger at almost $10. After 15 minutes I was informed that it was not available.

This was by far the worst airport lounge ever. We arrived around 10:30 PM. First of all this is a very small place with poor seating arrangement and no other amenities to speak of. Second the place was overrun with people. there were no seats available and we had to seat at the bar. Wifi was there but did not work probably because of so many people. Two people were sleeping on bench like area where five to seven people could have set down. Service was noon existent and food was very limited. Place was loud, announcements were sporadic. Priority lounge next door was closed so we had no option but to hang out there for a few hours as flight was running late.

The Aeromexico Lounge at Mexico City Terminal 2 offers comfort away from the bustling masses to Business Class travelers and club members. While quite full of guests during busy times, the lounge is large, and has numerous sections on two levels, all offering seating for small groups, individuals and couples. An assortment of alcohol and non-alcoholic beverages are available, along with basic light snacks.

This is the most ridiculous lounge I've seen in my life. First, they tried to deny access to us, because we purchased cash upgrade. Which doesn't make me eligible for lounge access (had access to SkyTeam lounges in YVR, YYZ). But ok. We got in. Disgusting, filthy, smelly room. With thousands of people. Literally. No place to sit down, as some old ladies slept on the benches. No food, drink selection is very limited. Whatever snacks they had available - couldn't risk to taste them, as they looked very tired. Cleaners in dirty clothes with mops walking around aimlessly and swing the mop in your direction from time to time. In all the years of flying, I have never experienced anything even close to that. Will never pay a single penny to Aeromexico, nor would I ever fly through this horrible airport.

Arrived to the lounge at 5:00 AM so it was almost empty. Plenty of space for seating. Good wifi provided and wide range of drinks. There is not self service alcohol anymore. Just beers and soft drinks. Some light snacks were served later. It is still a good lounge but quality is dropping.

It gets better but is not perfect. The thing I really can complain in the Wi-Fi - this is Stone Age Wi-Fi,2 minutes to receive an email? Toilet clean, Food is fair, some selection of nice yogurts, fruits and nice selection of drinks including famous Mexican Black beers.  People that works there will come to you and offer coffee, and they will serve you. Electric power is available in many chairs and places to charge your devices. A good lounge to be honest.

One of the most unpleasant lounges I've ever visited, bar one other. The refrigerator made a constantly loud, high-pitched noise that nearly drove me out. The food was abysmal with only dried out sandwiches and peanuts available. Drinks were fine. The toilet was small and dirty and inhabited by the only mosquito I experienced on my 10 days in Mexico. The seats were uncomfortable and worn out. The lounge was disgusting. The attendants at the front desk were uncomfortable speaking English and didn't want to deal with us.

The check-in is a bit long and unfriendly. The staff seemed to have to check our entire life history and enter lots of information on their computer before letting us in. However, the lounge was rather large, the toilets clean, and the beverages were great. They even have service to your chair when you order at the bar. The food was limited and not very good quality. The wifi was good. Seating was comfortable, but it was a very well-utilized lounge at a hub and both times I was there it was very crowded.

Never seen a business lounge with so little to eat! You must like chips in a packet. Cold potato salad and some poor quality cheese sandwiches. No hot dish and nothing appetizing! It's incredible! In all the airline lounges of the world, I can dine properly before embarking, then to sleep just after takeoff. But not on this departure ofrom Paris CDG with Aeromexico. I had to wait until past midnight to have my meal on board. Jamais vu un salon business avec si peu de chose a manger! U vous aimez les chips en sachet, c'est ok. Salade froide de pomme de terre De malheureux sandwichs Du fromage. Bref pas de plat chaud et rien d appétissant! C'est incroyable! Dans tous les salons du monde, je peux dîner correctement avant d embarquer, puis dormir juste après le décollage. Mais pas sur ce départ du hall L à Paris CDG Depart a 22:30 pour Mexico. J'ai du attendre minuit passé avent d avoir mon plateau repas à bord.

The international Aeromexico T2 lounge comfort is decent, however, is always so crowded that makes it uncomfortable. The restrooms are really small and always crowded. Beverages are good but what is really awful is the food. Food is really limited and very bad quality, they have ramen soups and terrible mini-sandwiches. Is really a shame that the largest Mexican airline can't have a good lounge.

Terminal Domestic Lounge is easy to locate, clean and decently appointed. It is not a modern or efficient lounge as other airlines provide, but it does its job. Staff is pleasant and eager to help with drinks, coffee, etc. Food options are limited but acceptable - mostly snacks. Toilet facilities are clean but insufficient for a lounge that tends to be crowded. Finding a seat for two travelers wasn't easy. Internet speed was sub-par for a lounge in the main hub of the airline.

Aeromexico Club Premier lounge at Mexico City Airport. The food is poor and unvaried and it's always the same. Churida little sandwiches with lettuce soaked. The internet is not good and often cannot always be used. Some of the staff do not present a nice image when serving you. They appear as if they are fed up or tired, but that is not the fault of the customer.

Aeromexico's lounge at Mexico City airport is very limited. First of all, is always crowded, to the point that the temperature inside is uncomfortable and the air conditioning is not enough to keep the place cool. Drinks are fine, you have a good selection of beers, and a couple of wines, with a decent selection of liquors. One problem is that since the lounge is so crowded, beers are hot most of the time because they don't even have time to get cold. Coffee is very good. The big issue is with the food, which is really bad quality and with all the people inside, the food disappears immediately. There are mini-sandwiches (if you are lucky to find one), cookies, and ramen soups, nothing else. I am a frequent traveller, sky team elite plus member and have travelled in many airlines around the world, and I can say that Aeromexico's lounge in its most important hub, does not have the quality level as other sky team hub (Air France in Paris, KLM in Schipol).

It took a long walk and searching to arrive at the Premier International lounge after mistakenly entering the Domestic one in Terminal 2. There seems to be a shortage of cool air in the public areas of the terminal and the Business Lounge did not provide a relief at that point. Air seems to be in short supply here and was replenished every twenty minutes which seemed to be a long time when the indoor temperature reached 80F. The lounge is spacious with food offering that included: stale sandwiches good mini cheese cakes a good variety of packaged sweet and salty snacks cold drinks and unrefrigerated “iced” tea. Computers for usage was complimentary.

I am writing this review as I sit in the lounge. Door understaffed and young man at desk very obviously nicer to male clients than myself as a solo middle aged woman. Lounge is poorly set up rather like a bus station where toomany travellers require seats for their bags and coats. Food selection is the worst I've seen in a lounge. Drinks selection is better but they sure do not hurry to put out the bubbly. The latest empty has been sitting on a counter for a half hour now. In general lots of empties left around to point some travellers are clearing up instead. Wifi works well at least.

Very nice used it late in the night so not too many people. Nice selection of liquors and spirits. No food (only snacks as pastries some fruit granola peanuts and crackers) as their policy is to serve food only during Mexican meal times (7-9 am 2-4 pm 8-10pm). They have a wine club (paying customers) with excellent sandwiches. Nice selection of local newspapers but they should add some international newspapers and magazines. They have showers toilets video games section for kids internet area free wifi. Staff friendly and professional.

Fairly basic lounge. Nice enough but a little crowded. Good selection of self serve alcohol and soft drinks. No real food beyond peanuts and stuff. Decent wireless and 4-6 internet terminals. Overall pretty nice for Tijuana.

Mexico City's new terminal 2 was barely up and running when I flew out on a Copa Airlines flight that gave me access to the Aeromexico lounge. The lounge is upstairs and is light elegant and airy albeit with no windows onto the tarmac. Comfy seating a separate computer area wifi throughout and attractive palm trees add a festive air. There is a circular bar that was unmanned during my visit plus a smaller self-service bar with an excellent selection of drinks and classy snacks. There is a separate screened-off TV lounge and another wine bar at the back for paying customers only. Since the lounge was brand-new it was obvious an effort was being made to impress. It will be important to monitor progress as time passes to see if the high standard in maintained.
Well appointed lounge, comfortable seating and layout. Enjoyed the coffee we had. Did not eat anything because we had enjoyed lunch prior to arriving in the lounge area.

I had three hours until my flight departed for Anchorage, what better place than the new Alaska Lounge! This is their new 5000 square foot lounge located in the North terminal. It has plenty of room to relax in. I grabbed a chair a coffee, some cheese and crackers and watched the airliners take off for entertainment. The views were great as you can see the entire SEA operation from your chair. The staff that I enter acted with had great attitudes and made my stay enjoyable. Before I knew it my time was up and I had to depart to my gate. My advice, if you need a beautiful, quiet place to relax, grab some refreshments and just chill, you cannot do much better than the Alaska Lounge.
Extremely poor lounge at New York JFK Airport. Very little selection of food (breakfast) , ‘selection of breakfast pastries’ plate empty and no more available. Rude staff, no newspapers.

My spouse and son visited the Boardroom in both Anchorage and in Seattle last week. Both of the Boardrooms were clean, well stocked and employees were first rate. The Anchorage Boardroom appears a bit smaller than the two in Seattle however the service is great. I wish they served a little more variety in the way of food, snacks but the salad and cheeses filled me up. We had a redeye flying south so this is a nice quiet place to chill, read the newspaper and or books and watch the planes arriving and departing. The Seattle Boardroom was just the place for us early arriving folks. It was pretty quiet overall as it was a Sunday morning. The coffee was outstanding as were the rolls etc. I sat next to an individual who had a lifetime benefit at the Boardroom and she used it everytime she flew out. Lovely lady and we spent about an hour talking about Alaska and how things have changed in the past six decades, All in all, both lounges were a great place to relax, chat with fellow travelers and enjoy the service.

I had many hours prior to my trip out of Anchorage so I visited the Alaska Airlines Boardroom in the airport. I had a great time with the wonderful staff and had soup, cheese and various things to nibble on. I enjoy the fact that Alaska really seems to know how to hire the right employees for this line of work, very impressive bunch! My return trip to Alaska, I once again had plenty of time to visit the new North Boardroom. The staff was great, very informative and wonderful attitudes, even at 5 AM when they open. The selection of coffee, juices, breads, etc. was just perfect for me. The quiet that this spot provided was wonderful as right outside the door chaos lives! The noise out in the terminal, with everyone in a hurry, announcements etc. did not get to us inside, thankfully. Again, great service by Alaska employees who understand quality service and care about the customers they serve!

I stopped in at the Alaska Airlines Boardroom in Anchorage before departure and once again had an enjoyable couple of hours. The room was about half full of folks waiting to fly somewhere and all seemed to be in decent spirits. The staff was great as appears to be the case whichever Boardroom I visit. Had a great visit with some people flying back to Washington state. They had been in the Greatland visiting their son and his family. Very enjoyable experience overall. I went also to the new Boardroom in Seattle prior to my flight to Nashville. It is staffed with fine employees as well. The coffee and various snacks hit the spot and I enjoyed my time there. I noticed that a sign had been placed on the bathroom door apologizing for it being the only bathroom there. Apparently I was one of many who complained about that issue. There are plans to have more bathrooms at the next new Boardroom. Again, no problems encountered and I was pleased to have spent my time there, reading the paper and my books. Even though it was quite full with numerous business types, obviously in a hurry, it was a good experience overall.

This is now my second visit to Alaska Airlines new Boardroom in the North terminal at SeaTac. All went well, the morning food was fine as was the coffee, much needed after my redeye from ANC. It was very crowded in there with families, business folks and who knows who else. My only issue is again with their one bathroom. It does not make sense to have only one and that was quite apparent as numerous folks had to wait in line. The staff was busy so I did not bother them in asking why only one? I will contact Alaska and see if they can do something about it or not. I was not the only person wondering about it I can tell you. All in all though, everything else was great!

Access to this Alaska Airlines lounge cost me $45.00, It's a small lounge but it's okay. They have business center with 2 computers, a fax and shredder machine, so you can get all your business done. Staff are friendly. there is no meal buffet, but their are some snacks, soda and coffee machine. There are no showers in this lounge.

My son and I had a few hours until our redeye to ORD so we went to the Boardroom. The service was great overall - good staff! I had a few snacks, a salad and a beer. I read a book and my son used the free wi-fi and recharged his phone. He had never been there so I gave him a quick tour. He was impressed. I told him if he ever ends up doing a lot of traveling he should get a membership. Well worth the money. Another reason is that you can also use the American lounges at various airports and relax there as well.
It is a small lounge which was busy. Basic drinks and snacks. Pancake machinery a visit. Better than sitting outside but nothing special.

I recently joined the Alaska Air Boardroom after receiving a discount as an Alaska Gold member. I was quite impressed overall. The service was outstanding! The women working at the front desk were professional and went beyond their job to assist everyone who came in. Their smiles went along way for the numerous harried travelers. I think that Alaska could use a larger lounge area though - it felt a tad small but I am not complaining, I was glad to relax there. Fine service, great coffee and fun folks to talk to, what more can you want?

I was flying first class from SEA to LAX. Alaska is one of the U.S. carriers (maybe the only one) to grant lounge access to those flying first class domestically and not connecting to an international flight. Lounge was large (didn't realize at first there was a second floor). Selection of drinks and snacks was standard. Wi-Fi access was fine.
