Lounge was crowded on a weekday morning but I had no trouble finding a place to sit and plug in my PC or phone. I don't know if there were showers.

Flying Alaska Airlines from LAX to Vancouver Canada. Lounge in LAX was fine with quiet areas good selection of food to nibble on and nice bar offerings. Even better in Vancouver where hot soup beef stew wild rice and a wide variety of sandwiches and cookies were available. Nice area for self- service wine and other drinks. Very attractive display of food and beverages. Free wifi in both lounges.

Refurbished but with odd furnishings. Better than waiting at the gate. This location was recently refurbished. The lounge is the same size and layout the changes are largely cosmetic (mostly new furnishings). The tables/chairs in the center area are like patio furnishings - very narrow and extremely uncomfortable chairs. The chairs along the outer wall/windows are so low to the ground that it's like sitting in child's furniture - again very uncomfortable. In the morning food covers a wide range (fruit muffins coffee cake and even a machine that makes pancakes!). In the afternoon things like cheese and crackers. A limited range of complementary alcoholic beverages and some really good microbrews. Starbucks coffee. The bathrooms while small are clean and well-stocked. Nice view out the windows of the alleyway between the C and D concourses.

It is an up-to-date low key relaxing yet highly functional business lounge with a large flat screen TV modern and comfortable dark color business tone sofas & tables food and beverage bar a clean restroom with hand lotion and half and full body mirrors 5 clocks of world time pc stations a laser printer a COPYING machine and a killer view for airplane and sunset. Staff on duty are experienced with people professional and skillful finding out what Loungers like me with a point and shoot camera are up to - taking photos of its remedies and breath taking sunset. They made me a single female Asia feel welcomed. Thanks them for making my 1st Board Room experience a positive one.

Located near finger B next to the MASH restaurant, this Aviator Lounge accepts business and first class passengers for a number of airlines as well as a number of lounge cards including Priority Pass and Dragon Pass. The lounge is quite small and given the number of potential passengers this lounge is always extremely busy which makes it somewhat noisy and unpleasant. The staff is friendly but very robotic. The food selection is very limited (bread, cheese, some cold meat and jams) and disappointing to say the least. Generally this lounge is not worth a visit especially if you use a lounge card.

The Aviator lounge was very crowded when we used it, and difficult to find seats together for 3 people! Reception service very abrupt and no section of customer service applied here. Selection of beverages was fine but food was quite limited and poor. Wifi worked well and easy to use. Guess it has been open about 4-5 hours when we arrived, and it was dirty and unpleasant. You can pay to use this lounge, but would advise against that since main terminal areas offer as nice if not better facilities. Certainly not recommended to other travellers.

I went to the Vitosha Lounge at Sofia Airport before my business class flight with Bulgaria Air. It was good, but there wasn't a big choice of food. Only nuts, chips and some chocolate candies. And for drinks you're only able to choose between a coke, water and sprite. There was only one person working in the lounge.

Dreadful, dated, filthy lounge. Poor, uncomfortable sagging seating. Areas under semi-permanent repair. Broken, stained table lamps. Bad food. Try to avoid passing through Shanghai Pudong airport if at all possible.

My expectations for these Beijing Capital Airport and Shanghai Pu Dong China Eastern lounges were modest, but they turned out to be better than I expected. The view from the PEK lounge was over a relatively quiet tarmac, while the PVG lounge had lots of natural light, but no view whatsoever. The PEK lounge had beer and Great Wall red and white wine. The Shanghai lounge offered more beverage choices with some liquor, including Bailey's, but not including rum. The wait staff were more efficient than friendly. The PVG lounge offered a cooking station, but since there was no menu, and the cooks didn't speak English, I have no idea what was available. There were sandwiches.and salads in the cooler. If I had anticipated world-class facilities, I would have been dissapointed, but as it was, this was a satisfactory way to await my flights.

China Eastern Lounge in Shanghai Pudong. The lounge is over capacity and cannot handle all the passengers from China Eastern, Delta, and others. The good is the food, and showers being available. Food is available fresh or what is cooked and already out. Drinks are available from coke/beer and juice/ and wine. Sadly, the coffee machine was out of order going to Shanghai, and on my return to Shanghai. I had to use Starbucks outside the lounge. Also the WiFi is available for free but the Chinese government restricts all the popular apps so it is not of much use. Till the new terminal is completed and China Eastern shifts over to the new terminal and bigger lounge the overcrowding will remain an issue.

This Air France-KLM  lounge was conveniently located near the China Eastern Airlines terminal. However, the lounge is incredibly small. Since Air France and KLM uses this lounge too, it can be pretty packed with no one to sit. The food spread is mediocre and the internet was decent.

The updated International lounge I visited looks very good now. It is pretty spacious with a lot of seating types. It was pretty busy the morning we were there. The first floor where most of the food is was very busy. However, the second level was pretty empty and relaxing with much more spacious and comfortable lounge chairs.  Quick and easy check in by friendly staff. Furniture: updated and new with a lot of electrical plugs around, second level offers a more comfortable seating as well as around 8 to 10 full body massage loungers. Wifi not the best. Food: noodle soup station with a chef that cooks your noodles on demand, there were a few soup toppings available. Breakfast food was also available with scrambled eggs, potatoes, bacon, sausages, variety of breads/croissants/buns/pastries. There was a small salad station. Second floor had a large beverage station with a few snacks. Showers/bathrooms very clean with bathroom attendants stationed inside the bathrooms. It was easy to get into the showers by contacting the staff. The shower was very nice and pretty spacious. I was given a cute little basket with a comb, a toothbrush, a mouthwash, as well as a hair dryer. Overall impression: a very pleasant experience that went well beyond our expectations.

Avoid at all costs. This is a cramped, uncomfortable, dirty, and poorly serviced lounge. It is loud and uncomfortable. The selection of food is poor. If I fly in business on China Eastern, I try the lounge for a few minutes - and always end up at the Starbucks at either end of the T1 concourse. The food is better, as is the atmosphere. That this is a flagship lounge in an airline's home hub is simply ludicrous.

One of the best business class lounges I have been to. Clean and quiet with modern, comfortable furniture, plenty of tables and workstations with power points everywhere. A good selection of snacks and drinks and friendly staff. Highly recommended.

The lounge in the International section of Terminal 1  was outstanding. There were plenty of tables and chairs with power outlets available. There were bathrooms and showers on the first and second floor. The food was excellent. They had Chinese and Western snacks as well as hot noodles and a hot buffet spread. It isn't Singapore Airlines or Etihad Airways style lounge, but it definitely beat the Korean Air lounge in Incheon. I would go to this lounge again.

KLM often departs from a nearby gate. This China Eastern Airlines lounge is big enough. Not enough male toilets avaliable. Different types of chilled and hot beverages and Chinese snacks (nuts etc) and small pastries are available. Wifi is terrible, which is a shame for such an airport. No couches, only seats. Comfort is OK.  If there were better F&B outlets at PVG (which there aren't), I would prefer a good cafe above this lounge.

This China Eastern Airlines lounge is not a Lounge. It is more of a 'holding pen' at best. China Eastern need to visit other airline Lounges to see what a First Class Lounge is really supposed to be. It is hot, uncomfortable, overcrowded. It is dirty with rubbish all over the place. It has no proper tables to eat at. The food looks awful - I had a bottle of water from a fridge that was old, dirty and not working properly. Access to the Lounge wifi was impossible to obtain. There are hardly any power outlets to power up phones or plug in a Laptop. Don't go there you will have a better experience sitting in the airport public area or one of the restaurants.

Dull uninviting tired room. No attendant (we were in at 2am). Egg salad sandwiches left out at room temp made me nervous. How long been there? No coffee. Booze in cooler. Decent washroom. No shower that I could find. A dozen or so people sleeping in chairs and on the floor

I agree. This China Eastern Airlines lounge is the worst I have ever seen. I confirm the disgusting toilet. Waste on the floor, no door handle on single cubicle. Small and poor food choice. No shower. Poor wifi signal. Some in our group paid for entry and fought to get a refund. I was business class so it was in my ticket. Staff only speak chinese.

This is the most disgusting lounge you have ever encountered, urine smell in the toilets, no door handles on the entry to the bathroom, stained carpet and lounges. Front staff don't look up as they on wechat, snap chat and don't care. After paying for first class you get this.  I travel 4 times a year to China and I had to write this as the lounge it is disgrace, the service on China Eastern was first class.

The worst Lounge I have ever been to, it is old fashioned and looks dirty. The lounge staff service is poor, employees speak very little English, seats are so uncomfortable and you are better stay standing up. It is a shame for the SkyTeam Alliance. China Eastern Airlines has to renew these old lounges.

The most basic of all business lounges I have used. Small one room, below main airport Gate lounges. This China Eastern Airlines lounge was dirty and well worn, seats were blue velour and had food and drink stains on them. There were more staff in the toilets than in the dining and sitting area. The reception staff were bored and showed no interest in the lounge. Prior to each flight they would shout out plane number. Loud Chinese passengers were not addressed and were pushy.

The first problem with the China Eastern lounge is its location. Getting to it from most waiting room locations is a long hike, then down an escalator, and then another hike. And when we were there, the up escalators (two of them) were out of commission. Then the seats: they're old and ratty. I tried four before I found one that I could sit in without sliding off. The men's restroom was filthy and had only two commodes and one urinal. The drinks were OK; the food selection was limited and the dishes unappealing. There is no PA. An attendant marches up and down the aisle barking boarding times. Lastly, the air conditioning is substandard.

This China Eastern Airlines business class lounge at Shanghai PuDong Airport is the worst business lounge I've ever been to. Only one bathroom, one urinal, one stall. Business bathroom was always closed, forcing business passengers to share the First Class bathroom. Same thing, stinky, smell of urine, dirty, and crowded. Food was average, and seating very limited. Wifi was slow. Airline delays not notified until asked. Lounge attendants not that friendly - a little testy and short tempered. If I can help it, China Eastern would be my very last possible choice of airlines.
Nice lounge, spacious, clean and cool. Very nice lunch with plenty of choices of cooked food and sandwiches. No alcohol which is a pity because the food deserves a nice glass of red wine.

The best word is "rudimentary".  Certainly not even close to anything offered by China Eastern Airlines peers in Asia, or even airlines from North America.  The lounges were clean, and there was food and some drinks, but poor. They're very basic in the seating department and rather plain.  Gin and warm tonic water were supplied, but no ice.  Wifi is impossible to connect-to unless one has a Chinese mobile telephone number.  There were no shower facilities available.  We went next-door to the First class lounge, it was pretty much the same as the business class lounge. China Eastern offer a comfortable, professional and pleasant inflight experience in business class.  The lounge experience doesn't even come close.

Small crowded very 1974. On the bright side no blaring CNN or other stupid American TV "news" shows because you're in China! No monitor to check flight details. Announcements are made in sort of English but were so muffled and unintelligible to be useless. Very tired looking and in desperate need of a refit. Staff sort of want to help but don't really know how to.

What can I say this is so disgusting one would think that China Eastern could ensure that business travellers have a decent lounge at their flagship airport. Very poor wifi and no music or even CNN. The lounge is dirty even the walls and chairs are falling apart how embarrassing for a nation that prides themselves on being ahead of the rest of the world clearly not in this arena.

This is a domestic first (business) class lounge for China Eastern and Shanghai Airlines. Visited twice in the last 2 weeks and I'd say that this lounge is below average. No outside view of any kind. Boarding notifications shouted by staff. Stir fries and rice offered during meal time but not delicious and attractive at all. Some salad sandwiches dessert and other snacks available. Soft drinks plenty with some beer and wine. Used plates collected from time to time. Washrooms were clean. Biggest complaint is the wifi - uses public wifi which is extremely slow. Overall I only recommend because it has couches (more comfortable than the benches outside) and provides free drinks and edible food but don't come with high expectations.
Very poor lounge. Food is terrible chairs old dirty and uncomfortable. Staff unfriendly. Better to wait at boarding gate.

I had just become an Eastern Miles Golden Member but did not have the card with me yet. I asked the girl at the entrance of the lounge to let my 5-month pregnant wife to enter the lounge with me (something I was entitled to as Golden Member) also considering there were only 20 minutes left before boarding. The staff refused saying they wanted to see the card. I therefore entered the lounge alone: packed as usual (for Chinese it is extremely easy to join the lounge through their credit card membership) some average noodles sandwiches and fruit. I expressly asked the staff to let me know if the gate changed (it happens frequently in China) and they did not do that. Overall the standard terrible China Eastern's service.
Although the food is decent in terms of quantity and quality the furniture is old and highly uncomfortable. Not many electric plug points for recharge etc. No announcements either.

Poor service of staff! Don't think it is their job to inform guests of delays (3 hours). Nobody cleans up after departed guests (or way too slowly). Food served is all packaged crackers and cling wrapped sandwiches. Chairs are old - seats in the public area of the terminal are more comfortable.

There are a few lounges located throughout the terminal with easy access to all gates. Attendants were very accommodating and explained the comforts of the lounge and that they would make a boarding call. Many hot appetizers as well as Asian / Western Dishes available. Well stocked bar as well as soft drinks water and tea. Assortment of Asian and English language newspapers. WIFI worked well and the 4 hours spent in the lounge were very pleasant.
Good lounge big and bright very clean I was there at breakfast and a variety of westernish and Chinese hot and cold dishes were available. Good fast wifi available and comfy chairs.
Lounge has been refurbished to include uncomfortable seating used to be a nice comfy lounge. Snacks and drinks not too bad. Not a place to spend 6 hours (any more).

Small lounge close to gate 46 at terminal 2 with portable wall surrounds to divide from the rest of the waiting area quite noisy because of the walls and also very busy as were all other lounges. Simple snacks and drinks available plus cold Tsingdao beer and red wine. Not bad for a domestic lounge.

Pretty good lounge PVG has lounges located at most international gate ares so not overcrowded. Good selection of hot food and snacks when I was there around 6pm and good bar variety too. Wifi worked well and English papers and magazines available too.

More than adequate lounge separate from business class. Hostess helpful and friendly. Electrical outlets for last minute computer/ pda charging are abundant. Nice selection of hot/ cold food both western and Asian; as well as alcohol sodas and water. I would like to see more Western magazines and newspapers other than the LA Times but that would be the only minor criticism.

In general this lounge was an average one to all the ones I been to. This lounge was also empty. They had a bad section of food but it tasted okay. The lounge felt and looked boring. The lounge had no internet but it had power points. The bathrooms were good but lacked showers. The staff were friendly.

During my visit, the wine service area was completely empty. Despite menu signs listing a variety of wines, not a single bottle was available. Furthermore, the food selection was poor and meager. For a lounge of this class, the variety and quality of catering were unacceptable and did not meet basic expectations. Attached is photographic evidence showing only the empty stands. Staff made no attempt to restock the selection during my entire visit. This is unacceptable for a lounge experience

The aircon didn't work in majority of the lounge areas, except a little room which was selling merchandise. As a result guests had to sit on corners/thick-chairs which had a portable "cooler" which made little difference in the humid heat. The stuffy conditions made many guests wanting to shower. However, the controlled "booking" system meant many having to wait hours before they can use one. I got told it takes "this long because it's 30min per usage". Ridiculous! Nevertheless the showers and nap rooms were very clean and good standard. The cleanliness of other areas though, like for example the toilets were simply not good enough. Staffing was a bizzare issue. Despite being seen everywhere and being very hardworking, no one attended areas where guests needed help, like the tea bar and drinks bar. Guests had to go into the display area to help themselves to cognac etc. In the end, there was a lack of orderliness and the lounge became noisy. And the other area seriously need improving is the English skills. Simple words like "soy sauce / AC" couldn't be understood. The Chinese food offerings were sumptous though: amazing buffet and live wonton-soup making. Wonderful!

This new lounge in the new terminal 2 at Guangzhou airport is very nice. The shower was very clean and everything you needed was already made available in the room. There was quite a few shower and napping rooms available since it wasn't very busy to book them at 1PM in the afternoon. The napping rooms are very clean, temperature controls are easily accessed from the bed and boarding calls will be made with a staff knocking on your door. Food and drink options was also very good.

The Sky Pearl lounge in Guangzhou is adequately large, with many comfortable seating options, a broad choice of hot and cold food options, and a fine view of the tarmac. Nevertheless, there are two areas in which the lounge should improve: the air conditioning is not adequate and the beverage choices are surprisingly meager. There were red and white wines, two kinds of whiskey, and nothing else in the alcohol menu. Perhaps this reflects Chinese tastes and custom. I think that the problem with the temperature in the upstairs section of the lounge is a trade off with the view offered. Large glass widows allow patrons to see out, but they also permit the sun to pour in. There are no loudspeaker boarding announcements, but the staff circulates constantly, and personally informs customers when it is time to head to the gate. In sum, this is a pleasant refuge, but it could be even better.

The lounge for domestic flights are nothing to write about, they are so noisy, always full to the brim and hardly any refreshments, in the morning when the refreshments arrive, there is a mad dash for the same, Totally useless compared to the international lounges, those are perfect and fit in with the international standards

My wife and I have now spent four visits in the Guangzhou Airport lounge over 4 years. Nothing has really changed in that time unlike the in flight service that has improved in leaps and bounds. In flight service is now excellent and it is time to apply themselves to this lounge which is darkly lit, although clean - while food and beverages are very poor in terms of quality and quantity. WiFi is very low quality in terms of consistent coverage, it frequently drops out, and is very slow. China Southern has come a very long way since our first experience 4 years ago but not in the lounge.

The overall impression is that this Guangzhou lounge is much below our expectations. It is out-of date, food selection is very limited, there is only one red wine. Staff is not friendly - they first sent us to another area for elite passenger without food/ drinks instead of business/first area. Two weeks before on our way to Sydney my time slot for shower was given to someone else and I had to wait for another hour.

One of the worst lounges that I have seen. It was overcrowded to the point that it was very difficult to find a seat. The food was rather underwhelming, and the internet connection was very slow. Furthermore, the lounge was very noisy because they announced every flight in English and Chinese.

The lounge is very spacious and comfortable with two floors. The food is plenty with variety and special southern China flavor. The only inconvenience is there is no lift to the second floor, so I had to carry my luggage to the second floor. There is a book shelf with many books and magazines.

The lounge had good wifi connection. The seating was well arranged with an area for sitting to eat a meal as well as comfortable lounge chairs to relax. Flight screens with up to date departure information were visible from most parts of the lounge. There was a good variety of meals, snacks and finger food available. There was a good supply of beer, wine, soft drinks, coffee/tea and other beverages. Staff would announce when flights were boarding and reminding customers to head to their appropriate gate. The lounge was kept in a clean manner both in the lounge as well as the restrooms.

In general this China Southern Airlines lounge is okay. No private wifi, have to share wifi with the public. Food and drinks are reasonable, not exceptional, just a bit better than ok. However, I did not find any fresh fruit. No monitor showing boarding time, very inconvenient. Open area no private air con, sometimes the temp is not right, too hot or too cold

The lounge is on 2 levels with main eating downstairs and more limited offerings upstairs. The food for evening meal was Chinese style but westerners may find something of their liking. There is not much variety of wine and alcohol but juice, soft drink and tea/coffee. Showers are available but you need to book at lounge reception. The lounge is reasonably comfortable and there is a free massage chair. There was one newspaper printed in English.

This excellent lounge is easy to find and well located near the international departures gates. It has a good selection of food, both Chinese and Continental, and a cook ready to prepare your noodle soup to order. Well supplied with a selection of drinks. Being in China, it has a number of high quality Asian teas provided together with cute little tea cups. It is on two levels which both have food and drinks bar. The upper level also has showers and bedrooms with beds so that you can have some sleep during a long wait. Seating is comfortable and there are even massage chairs on upper level. The lounge is on the level of departure gates, no need to struggle up the stairs to it. A short walk will take you to your departure gates.

China Southern business class and first class lounge are combined,  located near Gate 1-5. I was flying business so I was guided to the left where the lounge is located. The right hand side is for general Pearl Club access with minimum facilities. The first thing you notice is it is so hot in there. the lounge is semi-open so the temperature relies on the overall temperature of the airport. It's hot! The lounge has two levels. First level is for dining. There are limited buffet dishes for selection. The food was quite average. Lacking fresh fruit and salad. The only highlight for food is the noodle bar. For me, it is great to have some hot noodle soup during a connection.  Upstairs, there are some comfortable chairs you could lie down, having a nap, drinks. There are showers, there is always a queue and the facilities in the shower room is very average. The bathroom is really small. Overall, this lounge is good compared with lounges in other major Chinese cities. It needs much improvement to match elite airlines lounges.

A disappointing lounge, particularly considering that it was  opened less than two years ago. Compared to other lounges in China, positive points include a large number of seats available, a dedicated wireless network (slow) connection, a very small playground for children and a decent cleanness overall. However the design is cold and impersonal, the quality and quantity of food available is awful (plain rice and steamed vegetables, the choice of drinks is extremely limited (water, Coke/Fanta cans and beers, plus a Nescafe' machine), no newspapers and magazines available and no priority access to boarding.

China Southern Airlines business class lounge at Guangzhou Baiyun Airport was very good. Comfortable seats, the upstairs section had nibbles, and while downstairs had more extensive food. The showers were great. The negative was that the airport was very warm.

The lounge entrance serves for two China Southern Airlines lounges: First/Business class lounge and a frequent flier lounge. The First/Business lounge is very spacious, has comfortable furniture and even bedroom on its first floor. You can get the bedroom key from the attendant who looks after the shower rooms. With a bit of luck a bedroom is available straight away. Massage chair (no booking required) comfortable lounge seats and a food and drinks bar are adjacent to these facilities. A larger food and drinks bar is available on the ground floor. Food is good and a number of dishes are available. Of course, many of them are Chinese dishes. Chocolates, biscuits, sweets and savoury snacks are in jars. Many types of top quality Chinese teas are available for a private 'tea ceremony' in cute crockery. Coffee and standard tea is also there. Good quality wines, champagnes and spirits are in the drinks section with soft drink section in the fridge. Staff keep replenishing the supplies and keep the lounge clean. While the reception staff speak English and also ensure that we don't miss our flights, the domestic duties staff understand more English than they can speak and communicate with smiles. All in all a very comfortable lounge. The frequent flyer lounge uses the same entrance. It has good food and drinks though the lounge is smaller than the business lounge. It also doesn't have the bedrooms. The best thing is that a silver card is sufficient for admission to this lounge. Most papers and magazines are Chinese and a large proportion of food are Chinese dishes. They are rather delicious and should not pose a problem for non-Chinese eaters. The internet may be an option.

I arrived at Guangzhou early in the morning (about 5am). There was hardly anything at the airport. It was hot as we arrived and there was no aircon in the terminal. I was melting just walking from the plane through immigration. Upon arriving at the lounge, I was greeted by a girl who seemed fed up. Maybe she was forced to work at the early hour. Upon looking at my boarding pass, I proceeded upstairs hoping to freshen up with a shower. However, I was told it was not opened until 8am and my flight depart at 8:30am. Anyway, I decided to get some foods and drinks.  This is a disappointment and is a waste of money.

Well below expectation for a First/Business class lounge. Poor food and beverage choice and very limited options for an international traveller. China Southern Airlines Staff at lounge desk do not communicate at all. Poor communication and very, very limited English spoken. Unable to communicate when there are delays or changes. Very poor announcements made. Speaker was broken and sitting behind a cabinet so added to the poor English, unable to hear what was being said. Could not connect to Wifi - staff unhelpful, unwilling to assist. Due to 4 hour delay in flight this was a very painful experience to be stuck here for 4 hours!

Our transit stop of 7 hours turned into 9 due to aircraft delays. The lounge is on 2 levels with main eating downstairs and more limited offerings upstairs. The food for evening meal was mainly Asian style but most westerners would find something of their liking. There is not much of a variety of wine and alcohol but plenty of juice, soft drink and tea/coffee. Showers are available but you need to book at lounge reception. The lounge is reasonably comfortable and there is a free massage chair. There was one newspaper printed in English.

Used twice tired lounge with electric sockets rather tired (upstairs the seat lighting kept not working as plugs fell out). Showers good but have seen wear. Massage chairs good. A lot of cleaners with minimal English and one or two higher staff who have okay english.

In a very basic cold airport this lounge was just okay. As its not very busy there seemed to be enough seating and is fairly comfortable. Staff are tolerant of us but not endearing. The food was fine if you didn't want anything European and there was no alcohol to speak off other than a white red and Kirrin Beer. The classic is that they have a closed smoking room that everyone was using. Each time we left the lounge to stretch our legs we were challenged on our return to show that we were entitled to be there. Just like China Southern their lounge is okay if you can get your head around the fact that its a Chinese airline not a European one!

The lounge is spacious - about 30-40 seats. The sofas are comfortable and the room is clean. A refrigerator is stocked with 8-10 different types of beverages. The food is more a brunch style with several Chinese style breakfast items and a few western style lunch options. I was not hungry that day and I only tried the breakfast porridge and dessert cake. They were both good. The internet is fast with good signal strength.
Quite basic no frills. Breakfast is poor staff are not friendly. Seats are ok if I had to spend a long time in this Lounge I would not be happy.
It's peaceful spacious good airport view. Friendly and courteous staff escort you from entry had a nice snack dinner took a 30 minute nap and attendant woke me for boarding.

My visit was from 1900-2200hrs. At that time it was not crowded and the service level by staff and the food was excellent. Quick tip - On arrival at the lounge book the Clairol 15 minute massage or facial this is free. All in all a very good experience.

I and my husband travelled from LA to Tokyo via Guangzhou on last week. Their lounge is one of the best lounge we have been in. The staff were very helpful. We could spent a good time in classy place.

Beijing-Brisbane via Guangzhou in C class. It looks really amazing very comfortable both upstairs and downstairs. I also had a shower It was the best shower room at airline lounge. Boarding information behind mirror - wow really impressive. But the service at this lounge is just not up the standard. Staff cold and not helpful particular the chef. He was rude and unhelpful I ordered some dumplings on the menu but until my flight start boarding I did not see dumpling anywhere. All in all great facility but unacceptable service.

Fantastic lounge good food reasonable selection of drinks friendly staff and so comfortable. They even a have large screen TV with one area set out like a cinema for those long stays and they staff are always on hand to find you a movie in English or Chinese. Could not complain about anything.

Nothing to write home about. No windows for viewing limited choice of food (packed crackers etc.) and drinks (instant coffee). Recently enlarged to create more space and seats making it a bit more comfortable but in peak hours still busy. This is also due to airport or airline staff using it to invite friends in. Also no wifi available just some PC's for general use (mostly occupied). No showers I have noticed. Staff can be attentive (depending on individual style) but English remains an issue with most of them. There is a first class lounge 50 meters away but it never seems to be open when I am around for catching early morning flights (9 am)? Compared with the domestic lounge at the same airport the international lounge is not up to the standard.

First impressions of the SLOW lounge were of an overly busy place with too few seats and an awful lot of people enjoying the surprisingly generous bouffet. The upstairs area is a little less busy although irritating muzak plays overhead. The toilets are worth a mention as they're 'loos with a view'. The lounge is okay for an hour but I wouldn't want to spend any longer here.

Above average lounge because it was not crowded to the rafters. Food and drink were also better than average in terms of taste and variety. They had Neuhaus chef doing a demo and gave out samples. Business class passengers on get a complimentary box of this chocolate on deplaning. Only downside is that if you are connecting in Brussels to an intra European flight to get Terminal A from B is torture since they only have 2 immigration officers processing a very long line. Not sure I would go through Brussels again. You would never make a tight connection.
Really bad lounge. Food is disgusting and SN staff at desk is the worst helping and unwelcoming. Seats are comfortable but that is all the lounge has for itself.

As the lounge opened at 5am, I was able to get in early to take a shower and a short sleep in the 'Nap Room' for a couple of hours. The Nap Rooms are quite modest and have firm single beds with a small pillow and blanket provided. The shower facilities were good. The lounge is large and spacious, with a variety of furnishings. There is also a colourful children's room and play area. There are two areas of food displays, and the selection was excellent. An attractive self-service bar has a few spirits and a wider selection of wines (including sparkling) and beers. The whole length of one side of the lounge has a clear sight of the apron. Within the lounge is also a shop displaying a selection of Neuhaus Belgian chocolates, which could be tasted before buying. In a joint venture, the airline with Nexus cars meant their product placements are also everywhere.

It isn't a large lounge, but a pleasant place to relax for a couple of hours. The variety of furnishings is interspersed with artificial greenery. There are a few semi-private cubicles to do some work or have a bit of privacy. It got busy for a while late afternoon. However, the staff were quick to clear leftovers. The food selection was modest, a salad bar, charcuterie, pastries and a few hot items. There were plenty of soft drinks, beers on tap, and a few spirits and wines. The lounge is not lavish whatsoever, but it functions well for a short time. There are shower facilities.

The Loft is designed rather beautiful and the people at reception desk are usually friendly, however the catering is really sub par : basic bakery products, jams out of dispensers , the cold cuts and cheeses are of a poor quality and I simply did not risk to eat anything from the "hot" better said lukewarm breakfast Drinks out of dispensers, wines and licor : the cheapest quality. For breakfast there are some salads on display suitable for a lunch. Most people of the service team are not speaking Dutch at all. The restrooms were not very clean, the computers did not work anymore and no newspapers or mags at all - the receptionist did explain those will not on offer again in the future.

Probably one of the dirtiest lounges I have ever seen with food left over everywhere. Showers (as advertised) were not available. Quality of food was extremely bad: canned cassoulet, greasy veal, gyro, all unhealthy. Meals were extremely salty. Deserts were all industrial margarine style. Chocolate stand was closed. Very limited choice of drinks. A sad experience.

The Loft is the lounge for the airlines in the Star Alliance and the principal lounge operated by Brussels Airlines. It was very early in the morning 5 am so there was ample space. There are lounge seats and tables with chairs available. Belgian beer is available, soft drinks are out of dispensers. The choice of the wines and the alcoholic beverages are extremely basic, cheap is maybe appropriated. Aside scrambled eggs there were cold cuts and cheeses, nothing very special - and various breads croissants and chocolate breads. Jams are out of big tins. There were several salads, more appropriate for a light lunch as for breakfast. Reception was friendly, other staff rather neutral. Bathrooms were clean.

First toilet clean but door lock doesn’t function, 2nd and 3rd toilets totally dirty, 4th toilet dirty and splash not functioning. On a board it says last cleaning yesterday, next cleaning at 10! it is now 9:45. Never came across such a place with little care and hygiene.

Marco Polo lounge is shared and used by a lot of airlines. It is a clean spacious place, well maintained. with some quite corners if you want those. Bathrooms were clean. There is quite some decent food, sandwiches with Italian cold cuts, various cheeses, sweets and pastries. There is also fresh pizza. The food is replenished quite often. If you are liking the Italian style coffees, there is a great machine and you get service for it. Unfortunately there were no alcoholic beverages available , only a very cheap Italian sparkling wine, not chilled at all. Also the soda's , mineral water and cola drinks were nearly lukewarm and there was no ice available. So a rather mixed feeling concerning this lounge.

Very nice lounge, spacious, comfortable seating, with a variety of seating arrangements (tarmac view, work, relaxation, eating and drinking), quiet. Small but tasty selection of food (hot and cold, as well as breakfast fare), good beer bar with self-service for Belgian beers, demonstration of production of pralines in the lounge

Quite a nice lounge and usually not overcrowded. It overlooks the runway so daylight. Wi-Fi worked very well. Staff is pretty nice. On the negative side: pretty poor choice of wines on the contrary of what is offered on board long haul flights

Big lounge with wide glass facade and very comfortable looking seat. However, you have first to get one of those things. Unfortunately is the lounge is very often crowded so you have to keep with a small chair. A plus is the different Belgian beers that you can drought yourself at the bar and of course the famous waffle.

Upon approaching the desk, the two ladies were busy looking at something on the same screen. I waited for around 20-30 seconds before they looked up. Not a good start. A very full lounge greeted me. Staff seemed overworked (or the lounge understaffed), consequently they couldn't replenish things as fast as they went, or clean up after passengers. Even serviettes were missing. The tall armchairs look great but aren't that comfortable. The selection of food and drinks are okay. The toilets are adequate but the showers are great -even though it took three attempts to find somebody to open a cubicle. There are better lounges out there but all in all the stay was okay.

Loft Brussels airport a nice surprise. Beer Leffe black draft.  The food is good, soups are great, was 7pm and the place was pretty crowded, full of people I still find a place. Internet was fine and good wines and drinks are on the house. Is a good place I recommend if you are in Brussels. Services on table is also good, toilets are clean under the circumstances.

This lounge at Brussels Airport is in fact the lounge of Brussels Airlines / Star Alliance, but Finnair passengers can use it as well. A really nice lounge, with resting places facing the tarmac, extensive space for eating and working, very nice choice of hot and cold food and drinks, including a beer bar. Ultra-clean toilets and shower facilities Plenty of working power sockets. Modern ambiance, but cozy. Excellent place to stay during stopovers

One of the most sterile clubs I've visited. A fairly limited number of comfortable lounge chairs. A very limited number of very comfortable lounge/sleeping chairs in a secluded room (if you can score one of these, do it). But the main area looks like a classroom  - small desks, each with two opposing chairs in nice neat rows, elbow to elbow, stretching the length of the room. Staff was helpful and friendly.

Had the opportunity of using this lounge on a Lufthansa flight to Munich (Star Alliance). This is the first time I have used this lounge and was very satisfied with the facilities available. An excellent choice of refreshments offered. Good quality seating, excellent location overlooking the apron. Friendly attentive staff I will certainly use this lounge again.

Newly renovated lounge with a nice view of the tarmac. Somehow I’m disappointed with the new lounge as it looks like a big ballroom with all tables / chairs placed in a row, not enough comfortable seating areas compared to the previous one, no privacy. The food presentation looks poor, before salads were prepared in small glasses / verrines, now you have to take them from the buffet, dry and not nice looking leaves and salads. The beverages are ok. Poor compared to Lufthansa or Turkish Airlines lounges.

When this lounge opened its door after ages of revamping and redecorating it was fabulous. It still is except that it gets very very crowed and it is just too small. There is no place to sit or relax whatsoever. In fact I have never seen it so crowded ever. HON and Senator space is unfortunately squatted by any other pax, none or little checking on who can or cannot sit in this reserved place. Food and drinks are of good quality. Some fab especialities and plenty of coffee machines and drinks both acohol and non alcoholic ones. No announcements but quite a few screens in the lounge. I am surpised the problem of overcrowding the lounge was not envisaged by the planners an authorities. It is a real shame.

As the only lounge at Malaga Airport, they take that torch, run with it and do it up right. Large and spacious, you never feel that you are sharing your snacks with strangers. A wide selection of drinks, more than a few food offerings and of course, the ubiquitous Wi-Fi made our stay here well worth the "cost". (which was Biz-Class on Aeroplan) A nice area with computers for "business use" and a separate TV lounge added to the choices of "what to do?" Even if you have to buy access, I do recommend it if hanging about AGP for more than an hour or so. (especially if the airport is exceptionally busy and crowded). Feeling blessed that as our Air France Premium Economy tix next Sept. do not get us access, our Diners Club cards do.
Dirty and overcrowded. Poor selection of food. I would never pay for this lounge. Cleanliness only gets one star as I couldn't give it a 0.

The new Lounge in the Schengen Terminal at Brussels airport is modern and practical. The food and beverages are varied and of very high quality. There is plenty of cooked food, sweet or salty. The internet connection is very good and you can even borrow ipads in case you don't have a laptop.
Newly renovated large light nice view on the tarmac good food and beer on tap plenty of amenities. Definitely above most european / short haul lounges.

The lounge is bright and very spacious shower is clean with towels food is plentiful with great choices and staff are nice and courteous. Now if they could do something about the dilapidated Terminal B lounge.

The new lounge is four times the size of the previous one at over 1200 square metres. Reviews here dating back more than 2 months are therefore obsolete. New lounge very nice in all respects tablet computers are provided for free no password needed for internet access (which used to be limited to one hour previously) Belgian beers on tap mousse au chocolat made of Belgian chocolate - in other words a treat !

The Star Alliance lounge at Brussels airport underwent a refurbishment over the past 6 months. The area has probably tripled and has spacious areas with lounge chairs tables to work comfortable leather couches a quiet business area a sleeping area with "nap boxes" lockers for luggage and an improved food selection. The lounge has a luxury feel to it and reminds me of other high-end lounges.

Very overcrowded small space. Hard to find a seat. No privacy. Very dirty. Wifi with a coupon for 1hour only but it takes 20 mins at least to connect and what you get is hardly enough to Google something. No real food. Heavy thick and fat buttered sandwiches soup and beer. No toilet!

The terminal B lounge is so small and overcrowded. Also it is unbelievable to have wifi only valid for one hour. The condition of wifi usage is much worse then many of the African airports which the Brussels airlines serve. On top of that there are no bathroom nor shower available in the Terminal B lounge.

Worthless lounge. Too small too loud no real food except for some toast and cheese. Luckily sufficient Belgian beers but that could not compensate for the lack of free wifi. You would not believe it still exists in the 21st century.

Quite backwards. Not a single gluten free item not even crisps or peanuts. Very few of the seats have AC outlets. The staff tries their best. WiFi cut off. Too small and too crowded. You wouldn't believe that this is the "capital" of EU.

Just after security for B gates but upstairs from the main concourse. Nice enough lounge although not especially large. Limited seating and very small side tables and the toilets are outside of the lounge in the walkway. Food selection was sandwiches cold meats and cheeses with soup and pastries. Large fridges full of drinks and food quite a pleasant place to spend an hour before the flight home.

An OK lounge designed for short stays and the 5 hours between my inbound and outbound flights did drag even with a couple of walks. Staff are friendly wi-fi good and complimentary plenty of Belgian beers and other temptations. The food is pretty odd though - a massive tureen of soup a plate of dry and dull sandwiches and some plates of cubed salami and cheese.

Very cold welcome by the two SN ground staff the lounge is better than international B gate lounge. The catering is poor for a Star Alliance lounge only some dry cake nuts and vegetables - no sandwiches soups and hot dishes. Nice assortment of Belgian beers and beverages. For washrooms you have to leave the lounge and return to the gates entry section.

What a disappointing lounge. Seems to be designed for short haul where you might spend 30 mins at most in the lounge. Quite cramped. no washrooms or showers (use public facility outside) no free wifi and very old and tatty computer terminal that has a very slow internet connection. Food comprises a few apples biscuits stale bread rolls and rather poor tub of soup! Staff are polite on entrance door but nothing else - they are silent offer no help and apart from talking to belgian customers we noticed they were actually quite rude to many foreigners. A polite description is that this lounge is a dump!

This is one of the poorest lounge experiences I have had. It starts with the fact that you have to drag your luggage up the stairs - no elevator provided. Then you enter a spacious, but quite sterile room without atmosphere. Now, if you expect to get any food then you are wrong. They are worse than any cheap US lounge. Nothing at all provided, not even crackers or cheese or a yoghurt, just nothing! On the huge counter there are some nuts and one selection of crackers, that is it. I wanted to have a coffee, but the machine makes some horrible artifical instant drink which is an offense to anybody. Plus there are not even real cups, just cheap gas station small paper cups. Conclusion: this new terminal was just opened and I was hoping to find some nice lounge. But quality has gone down to zero. This is in fact the poorest lounge I have ever seen. I am sorry I have to say that openly.

This Prime Class third party lounge (and the ZAG terminal ) are brand new. Everything is clean, modern and shiny. The bar is reasonably well stocked, but without rum or sparkling wine. I imagine that they must get many Russian passengers as there are four or five different vodka brands. I visited in early morning, and there were wrapped sandwiches, pastries, and cereals available. The bathroom was clean, but did not offer hot water, and the soap de spender was empty. Perhaps I was overdressed ( coat & tie ), but the lounge seemed too hot and humid for real comfort. In any event, the lounge seems to be a substantial improvement over what other commenters wrote about the lounge in the former terminal.

This is a very poor Croatia Airlines lounge and one of the worst I put a foot into. Food is rather made up by some pickles. Selection of drinks is quite limited. Size of the lounge is also very small.

This lounge is in a quiet corner of the international wing of the terminal and is used by all airlines. It feels bigger than it is in the absence of walls on two sides. There is a buffet of Indian food and a dining space. A tended bar offers a selection of alcoholic drinks including Kingfisher beer in draft. Self service non-alcoholic beverage station. Comfortable couches. Tonight it was quite crowded. A washroom exclusively for the lounge is clean. Local newspapers were available. One desktop computer with internet connection can be used by patrons. All in all, it has the essential elements )you expect of an airport lounge. It is a relaxing space to wait before your flight.

Large lounge considering the size and throughput of the airport - Druk Air only has two A319 Airbus and no-one else flies there. Comfortable sofas and easy chairs. Reasonable selection of drinks (although the fridge was not connected) - only a tin of biscuits for snacks. Washroom facilities other side of security so you have to go through but they let you back when you show your Boarding Card!

Newly opened this week This is a wonderfully typical Centurion Lounge with one great exception. The staff is proactive, efficient, and extremely friendly. The food, as always is plentiful and quite good. I was there for breakfast so I wasn’t able to try out the impressive looking Whiskey Bar. There is also a terrific covered outdoor area with ramp views. All in all, a winner

As a Business Class passenger on an Air France Flight from HND to CDG, I had two options on which lounge to visit before boarding: JAL’s Sakura Lounge or Delta’s Sky Club. I visited the Delta lounge for the first time. Less company and more individual cares than the JAL’s counterpart. At the bar counter many kinds of liquor were served though I missed champagne. While I was taking a meal over a glass of red wine, one of the staff was pushing a cart loaded with fried chicken or something, which seemed to me their specialty, and approaching my table. She offered me one and naturally I took it. I found it delicious.

I returned from a trip to Mexico yesterday with my wife and 8-year-old child. On my way down the previous Saturday, we had a layover in SLC from GEG and took them to the Delta Lounge. I have a Reserve card and was going to use one of my passes for my wife and my daughter I assumed would just come along. After showing my boarding pass the attendant then typed some things to allow my wife in with one of my passes and we enjoyed some time in the lounge before flying out. On the way back yesterday we again stopped in at the lounge between flights. I scanned my boarding pass and the attendant then came over and I said I had another pass for my wife. They said all passes had been used a few days earlier. I said that must be a mistake because I had two and only used one for my wife. They told me both had been used, for my wife and child. The attendant then told me the charge for both of them to enter the lounge would then be $100. I understood the $50 for my wife but I was very taken aback that I was being charged $50 for my 8-year-old daughter who was only going to have a cookie or two! $50 for an adult I completely understand with liquor and food, but a child cannot possibly warrant a $50 charge. I paid the fee because we were already there and my daughter was looking forward to going back and having a cookie, but I felt, and have continued to feel, taken advantage of and this experience has left a very uncomfortable feeling with me. To add more insult once inside they closed down half the lounge's food serving area during dinner time and the lines backed up and the food coming out slowed down. I have always enjoyed the lounge when traveling by myself or with my wife but going forward cannot warrant the cost of bringing a small child so will not be going at all. I don't know if I will continue my business with Delta because of this. It was a very unfortunate ending to a great vacation. I called Medallion customer care to inquire about this and was very bluntly told that this is just the way it is. I think it may be time to give another airline a try.

Another overrun day in a Delta Sky Lounge in Atlanta. I travel through Atlanta at least 2x per week. The lounges in all concourses are over run and generally staffed with employees with abysmal attitudes. Terminal E on Sunday evening 9/10/2023 - very crowded, dirty (cleaned a side table myself from leftover food and drink), People using cell phones and devices without headphones. If Delta think's they are treating their best customers well, they are sadly mistaken. If there were any viable choice in the South East of the US, I would gladly abandon Delta as a "Diamond Medallion" all I get from Delta is constantly late flights, lounges that are overrun, and staffed by employees with bad attitudes.
Impressive food and drink offerings. Very fresh variety including vegan and ethnic. Comfortable seating and great view of tarmac. Gigantic improvement

The finest lounge I've ever visited in America. It is brand-new, with enormous windows, a large capacity, and an open, airy interior. With over 50 culinary options and excellent service, this restaurant takes the cake. Other airport lounges ought to emulate this one.
Beautiful lounge here in New York and very welcoming service. Special shout out to agent Marilyn Henry for her courtesy and sartorial correctness. Highly recommend.

A very relaxing experience in the "Airport Lounge World" operated by Munich Airport. Very clean lounge with lots of open spaces, lots of light, very clean bathrooms and decent snacks. No fancy food and no special amenity.

This lounge is amazing horrible. My visit started well with a great shower. The shower rooms are huge and well equipped. The service there is nice and welcoming. But when I wanted to get something for breakfast I was shocked. First of all it is plastic cutlery and paper plates. This place produces so much rubbish that is incredible. The selection of food was really small. But what was going well was the bar with the alcohol. The layout of the seating looked not welcoming. Chaotic the chairs were standing around all over. Some close to the sockets some far away. The terrace is a great idea, unfortunately it was closed that morning because of rain in the early morning hours. It is not worth visiting this lounge again. If you arrive from South Africa were they offer so many different meals and porcelain and with real cutlery you thing you just arrived in the third world.

The staff and seating are both fine. Staff very friendly and they clear glasses / plates away fast. But there is a lack of toilets and such a small choice of food options. Even the domestic lounge for Virgin Australia has more options than this! It’s such a dismal array of food - everyone is munching on corn chips and olives. The bar is above average (phew!).

This Sky Lounge in Terminal A at Detroit is horrific. Shame on Delta. I flew first from San Diego on my connection to LHR (on Delta One). Dirty, broken chairs, filthy glasses that they expect you to use to get a drink. Every  table was filled with dirty dishes and the such. I left and found a restaurant in the airport. I'd rather pay to not be in the lounge.

I bought a full-price first-class international ticket on Delta Airlines (Seattle to Port au Prince, Haiti) and was denied entry into the Delta lounge because first class to Caribbean countries "doesn't qualify".  Canada qualifies! Mexico qualifies! Arbitrary rules like this are a great way to lose first class international customers.

The Delta Sky Club at LAX Terminal 3 tends to be overcrowded all the time and it does not make it easy to enjoy the experience. There is also no way to get some privacy for a call with the crowd. The Good: - Nice view of the North runways - Power outlets available everywhere - Standing workspace available - Improved food selection in recent months The Bad: - Crowded - Internet was a disaster - Bathroom really small.

I visited two Delta lounges in Detroit, once on outgoing and again on return. The lounges in Detroit can get super crowded during peak travel times and makes it very hard to find a place to sit. Still despite the crowd there was ample food and drink. Plenty option to drink, food options were quite limited and not that great to be honest. The internet worked decently, took a moment to get connected but once connected no issue. The staff in the lounge were helpful and kind. The washrooms were well kept and nice, and I didn't have any need to visit a shower. Probably due to the high passenger volume the lounges in Detroit were starting to look a little worn and kinda dated. The chairs are pretty stuff and not that comfortable. I spend much of my time in the desk chairs in the office area as they were more comfortable. I know Delta can do better, so especially for their hub they should do better.

Delta Sky 4 floor on H and J, just great, clean, bathroom clean. Great food, organic choice, Hummus, lobster soup, French wines. I was not flying Delta but AeroMexico. Wi-Fi works in perfection. Good comfortable chairs, not that much DC Power to charge laptops and Mobiles but a few are around. Fresh apples, bananas, cookies etc. And good view. Employees smile to you welcome you from the reception to the ones that clean the table and also ask you if you want an extra glass of. Making passengers feel at home.

Delta Sky Club Lounge (Terminal 4, Concourse B - near Gate 31). Arrived after a longer international flight for a domestic connection and was looking forward to enjoying a shower and change of clothes, only to be appalled at the condition and quality of this lounge. The lounge was pushing its maximum capacity (so it seemed) and was exceptionally noisy as a result. Food selections were limited and definitely were not top quality nor were they healthy (given the amount of salt apparently used in their preparation from the two items I attempted to sample). Having arrived after enjoying exceptional food and hospitality in First Class on an Asian carrier, I wasn't able to eat any of the prepared foods available (given how greasy they were) and the quality/poor condition of the few selections of vegetables available left a lot to be desired. Bar staff seemed interested in serving the loud/boisterous people who had already consumed previous alcoholic drinks; getting the staff's attention was difficult. Seating was uncomfortable, decor was dated, carpets and floors were worn/dirty and the noise level/announcements precluded my hoped-for snoozing during the long lay-over between flights. Made an appointment to have a shower and was disturbed by the poor condition of the shower facilities, which were dirty (in spite of being "cleaned" between users) and had black mould visible in many areas of the one I was given. Towels were on the small side, were worn and were branded with a non-partnered hotel chain's name. Hair dryers were not available in the room and had to be requested before entering. Shower amenities were of poor quality and were of small quantities. Due to an unannounced gate change, I took the airside shuttle to Terminal 2 and visited the Delta Sky Club Lounge located upstairs on the Mezzanine level. This lounge offered a better selection and quality of food, was significantly quieter and promoted a relaxing atmosphere/environment. Shower facilities were available here but I did not investigate their quality/cleanliness. Overall experience from the T4 lounge was off-putting enough that I will not be using Delta Air Lines for future travel plans unless absolutely necessary (e.g., they are the only carrier serving my intended destination).

My wife and I had a 5 hour layover, the lounge was air conditioned, very comfortable and the lunch food on offer was very tasty. The salads were fresh as was everything else on the snack bar. I had clam chowder which was delicious, fresh fruit and coffee. My wife was very comfortable and the staff were all very friendly and helpful. In Europe I would have had to pay for a lounge as an economy customer so this was a very welcome rest. The whole experience of our holiday in the states was superb, everyone helpful and friendly. Thank you Delta.

Food choice is awful, all snack foods and very limited for such a large lounge. For a gluten intolerant person there was almost no choice, I actually went and bought food from a shop in the terminal in the end. Many of the power outlets don't work, much of the seating is directly in the sun (no blinds on the Windows). Otherwise seating is confortable and the bar is well stocked, but overall disappointing.

I was travelling from Honolulu back to Japan on China Airlines, a Skyteam member, and I am platinum status with Delta. After having gone down to the completely depressing and joke of a lounge China Airlines provided I stopped by the Delta one. It was lovely! It is the old Continental club and full of Hawaiian koa wood. The bathrooms were renovated and clean. Plenty of chairs available at this particular time. The food on offer was much better than the paltry choices available in most domestic Delta lounges. They had curry, soup, chicken salad, fresh fruit, a full bar...plenty on offer. The staff were very friendly and accommodating. The only complaint would be that it is dark inside. Wish I had checked in earlier! It was a fine domestic lounge.

Very friendly personal and welcome you nice. The use of bartenders is probably in some states the result of their Law (useless). Seating, power supplies and cleanness is good. No complain. Not that I go into a Lounge to drink a lot or eat a 5 course meal, but it is cheaper and more primitive than any place I can think about. Someone pays an certain amount in one or the other way to get in, and then get charged (better call it robbed) by arrogant bartenders for almost everything which in any Lounge around the world is free and pay an arm and leg for average, still not good, beer. Thanks I enjoy coffee, where I have to say one of the best Coffee machines I have seen so far "Great". Food selection very cheap, but still acceptable - food is served on Paper plates and plastic forks. Sorry this is more than primitive.

Skyclub at Minneapolis St Paul Airport. Renovated recently with snappy furniture of different styles but all modern. Plenty of open seats. Decent selection of snacks (for a domestic lounge) and drinks. Bartender fetched some fresh limes to cut for my G&T. Excellent wifi speed and they now offer free access to Internet New York Times site while in club.

For the last two years I am in transit in Atlanta twice a month. Since I do not have to pay to enter the Lounge I go there. But I would definitely not pay for this experience. The lounge is always overcrowded and equipped with rather old and outfashioned furniture. The food selection is limited and does not change very much. Worst of all are the toilets. Sorry, but I have seen much better.

Not a very impressive lounge compared to some of the Asian airport lounges. It is a nice place to get work done, and take a shower. There is not much to have when it comes to food, so you can have snacks there, but don't count on being able to get a meal. I would say that if your reservation comes with lounge access, then definitely go. However, I wouldn't really recommend paying for a visit separately.

Used to like their lounges when I had the mileage and paid for the membership; been to the ones in JFK, Orlando, LAX and even the overseas lounges like in Singapore. Nice to sit down quietly and get free drinks, though the foods were pretty awful. Some places had showers. But since they changed the mileage rules, I'm not allowed anymore, plus compared to other lounges like Japan Airlines, they're not as good anymore. I'd rather stay out with the masses because really, it ain't worth it.

I have never been into a Delta lounge before but I've experienced many Star Alliance lounges, all of which were very good. This lounge was the biggest disappointment I have experienced while traveling. After purchasing a premium class upgraded I was excited to experience a "premium" lounge but what greeted me was anything but. The lounge was very crowded with few empty seats. The tables and seats which were empty were covered with dirty glasses and paper plates. The layout of the room was very poor with no aesthetics involved. Rather chairs and tables seemed strewn across the area. When I went to get a drink at the bar, the unfriendly barman, after I asked for a Martini said he didnt know how to make one. Then he asked his colleague who had a recipe to make one, the finished cocktail was undrinkable. Afterwards I asked for a glass of wine. The barman advised me he had run out of wine glasses and so poured the wine in a tumbler. The food selection was also very poor with some soup, salad and basic snacks. When I used the toilet facilities I was appalled at their state. I promptly left the lounge and found myself a comfortable seat next to my gate.

Sanbra Duty Free & Priority Lounge lounge is new and needs some improvements specially in the staff training. They need to be more polite at the front desk and learn to smile. And also they need to know that is not good ask to the visitors for tips when we ask for any drink at the bar.

My partner and myself were travelling Orlando to Atlanta business class. Tried to use the lounge but because we were only travelling a local flight we couldn't be admitted. We are both world travellers and this is the very first time this has happened whether it's been an international or local flight. We always travel Business Class so you could say we were not at all happy with the lack of service!

A 12 Day, 8 City trip from coasts to coast. The Sky Club in the main terminal A in Boston is smaller with somewhat limited seating, a very small bar (Come on the is Boston, Right.) A decent, but somewhat poor value of breakfast offerings. The Indianapolis lounge is a new club and the only lounge in Indy, the furniture is already well worn and looks dirty. The food area is small and messy and the even smaller than Boston’s. The Salt Lake City Lounge is much nicer looking, but very crowded during peak times, Seating can be impossible to find. Food selection was more extensive and well kept. The bar is larger and well-staffed. The San Diego Club has an excellent staff, with lots of personal attention. Standard offerings, but the great staff makes this Club better. Were members with AA Admiral Clubs also, which we still prefer, but we travel a lot with Delta as well and make do.
The Delta Air Lines SkyClub lounge at Frankfurt Airport is a well sized lounge, with enough seats to chose. There was good food and a good self service drink selection.

Delta Air Lines lounge seemed a bit small for the traffic it has to handle at JFK. Food was okay, two soups to choose from, but all drinks had to go thru the bar - also soft drinks, which is annoying. Just water and coffee had a little self service bar.

SkyClub in Seattle was bright and spacious with clean well stocked bathrooms. Seating comfortable with excellent views of the apron. Front desk staff helpful and friendly. Food and beverage options are a lot better than United and American with some tasty soup, salad, bread and your usual snack options. My only gripe is the fact that they had disposable plates and utensils which is not classy at all. Service was decent, lounge staff were a bit timid for some reason. WiFi connection was fast which is always great. Overall, a decent lounge and DL definitely leads among the major US legacies when it comes to lounge food.

The business class lounge at the new Delta terminal at JFK is very disappointing. Poor layout meager offerings in the way of snacks and/or drinks overcrowded and a very poor set up when wanting to order a paid meal. It's very difficult and unclear as to know how to order food/drinks. Instructions at the tables are vague order placement terminals poorly placed and in general a bewildering experience. The seating is comfortable clean with good choices of seating areas. Lighting is comfortable Rest rooms are clean.

Bought a day pass as this is the only lounge at IND. While rather small it never seems over crowded. It has been kept clean and is an oasis of calm. For a domestic lounge Delta has really stepped up it's game on food offerings with a hot soup green and other salads flat breads and the usual raw veggies and packaged cheeses that used to be it. There is no view and no announcements so you need to keep your wit's about you especially if you are travelling on another airline. A variety of seating but no high tech massage chairs. Overall I was impressed.

Large pleasantly appointed lounge on two levels with extensive views of the apron and one runway. A two teir bar system operates in the lounge the majority of drinks are free but items from the "Luxury Bar" ie. non domestic and premium spirits incur a charge. It was therefore possible to sit and drink Jack Daniels all day but if you wanted named Scotch bacardi and so forth you pay. Draft and bottle beers soft drinks and mixers are all free. We were in the lounge from 3 to 5pm and there was plenty of seating available staff were pleasant and efficient. Food was basic; crudities with dips two types of soup pre-packed rubber cheese and a delicious curried cous cous. OK it was basic but everything looked fresh and they kept it well stocked up. Showers were excellent with a good supply of the basic things you need for your grooming on offer before you enter and soap shampoo conditioner and towels ready in the shower area. Overall as good as most European lounges and better than many US ones.

The worst SkyTeam lounge I have ever visited. Ridiculously scarce collection of food and drinks. Another disappointing thing is that the personnel in the Santiago lounge did not care about how bad the service and presentation were. I do not even think that they were trained in the customer service. Shame on Delta!

One word to describe this lounge - horrendous. The lounge is ridiculously small with some people left standing while waiting for seats to become free. The seats themselves are worn and in some cases dirty. Some of the staff were friendly some less so. No hot food and not much cold food either. Delta should be ashamed. While US airline lounges don't compare with those of the European or Asian carriers Delta's Sky Clubs are the worst. My recent experience has shown that Admirals Clubs while not perfect are infinitely superior to Delta's. I like the Delta product in the air but my experience in their clubs has made me seriously consider changing allegiance to American.

I travel frequently and this is one of the worse lounges I have been in. At check in the person in charge was on the phone and I had to wait for 10 minutes. The bar was fine but the bathrooms were appalling. I ended up going to the public bathroom in the terminal. No only the design is bad (3 cubicles about 5 feet tall) but the sinks were dirty the 3 paper towel machines were empty and there was trash on the floor. Who killed customer service and the glamour of travel?
Deplorable. Snacks and sandwiches were days old-the kimchi was rotten they only had Budweiser beer and sweet wines.

Absolute con- just meant to make money off economy class passengers who are led to believe they are paying for luxury. The worst airline lounge I have ever been to. They charge business class passengers for drinks at the 'luxury bar' at Atlanta and it was the worst Bloody Mary I ever had - always thought they was a safe choice. The seats at Chicago were uncomfortable. The lounges were dirty. I will never take a codeshare flight where Delta is a partner. I am worried that they will now destroy the Virgin lounges considering the fact that they own most of Virgin.

This is a contract lounge shared with several airlines including Delta. I was not permitted to invite a guest although I was flying business class and hold a crown Room membership. This is one of the worst international business class lounges - seating is poor - very few tables (I needed to use the floor to place my beverage as there was no table available). Food and drink selection is poor.

Not a large lounge and with a limited selection of free snacks and drinks (there is also a bar) but clean and quiet. Located in Terminal S from which most (but not all) Delta flights depart. Our flight departed from another terminal so we had to take an elevator down to the terminal level then another (or escalator) down to a train to take us to our terminal.

lounge_name: DELTA AIR LINES SKYCLUB FIRST & BUSINESS CLASS LOUNGE REVIEW
review: First time we used the rather new (remodeled) lounge in the international terminal (F). Large comfortable. Plenty of showers. Outdoor patio appended to the main lounge area was nice. Small but decent selection of free snacks beverages. Clean. Can take some time to get from here to domestic gates but not a big problem.

JFK Skyclub lounge is so disappointing after experiencing KLM's in Amsterdam. In Amsterdam you get great food snacks: good breads and cheeses croissants etc. At JFK it's basically just drinks and things that go with drinks as if no one wants to eat anything but carrot sticks and olives. I was upgraded on my next flight from JFK to DTW at dinner time and on that flight in FIRST CLASS there was just a basket of junk food of the kind you'd get at a 7/11. Delta seems to think all people want are drinks. I'm Gold Medallion and was glad for the privilege of the Skyclub lounge in Amsterdam (KLM's) but Delta in JFK (and I imagine elsewhere) is much inferior.

As a very frequent flyer my wife and I think that this is the worst lounge we have ever been in. The staff on front desk surly and totally not interested in their customers who pay their wages they need to be reminded food options non existent. Coffee machine broken not in use . I think Delta need to look around and maybe visit their Atlanta lounge. All in all a very bad advertisement.

This lounge is used by SkyTeam airlines here at Narita and what a poor reflection on SkyTeam as an airline alliance. Why is it that airline lounges operate by US carriers offer such second rate standards with this Delta lounge being cheap overcrowded and very dirty by Japanese standards? The breakfast offering food-wise is quite pitiful some cereals yogurt and low quality pastries - is this what I get when flying First Class with a SkyTeam airline? Washrooms were dirty the showers at best a 2-Star standard. In other words this is a lounge to avoid if you are used to the higher standards normally found in Asia and Japan. My last trip out of Narita was with ANA and the ANA Suite lounges are so so superior to the poor standards that US airlines such as Delta provide.

This is a joke lounge it's really like sports bar. I had to pay for everything nothing was free apart from nuts and carrots. I had prosecco and sushi which was very wrong - really hard rise huge sushi.. Came up $36. I should have just hang out at the gate as it was so far away to get there couldn't be bother to go back again.

I have spent many hours in the SEA Skyclub the last few months. Recently Delta has been testing new food offerings here including soup cold sandwiches and hot and cold appetizers. The soup and sandwiches are a welcome addition and might quiet some of the criticism in these comments. Other criticisms have been the presence of children in some of the delta clubs. Personally I found the children refreshing and much more interesting than the folk that typically populate the clubs. Delta has solved that problem too as they will soon begin to charge $29 per guest including family members unless you purchase a $700 executive membership. The SEA club has a great staff especially the bartenders. The complementary alcohol though is poor quality and the Luxury Bar drinks are not cheap. The seating in this club is generally uncomfortable except for the quiet room. This lounge needs additional electric outlets in the seating areas. There is only one shower but usually not a wait for it. Wifi is always good.

Decent quiet reliable lounge. Was able to have a relaxing wait at SeaTac before my recent flight to CDG. Like most US airline lounges the food was basic and unadventurous but there were just enough satisfying items (among them some good soups that I actually had several helpings of). No showers in the bathroom I think but the washrooms were clean.

Lounge was somewhat of a joke. Interior definitely done on the cheap. Food consisted of crackers and some mystery dip. Room not clean with tables that had not been picked up by employees for some time. Annoying children with parents who think the room is a play ground. My wife and I left after 15 minutes shaking our heads in disgust. We would rather wait at the gate at this airport.
