It was so full that I decided to leave after a while because it was not worth the effort to find some personal space in the lounge. I wanted to go on-line but apart from two free computers wireless was at a charge. I paid quite a hefty charge and I had major problems trying to connect. I could only spend five minutes on-line and I was constantly disconnected. In summary there is significant room for improvement!

I visited one lounge in the main part of T5 only to see a "Boarding Now" sign for my flight which was not departing for nearly 2 hours. It turns out they were trying to get people to the T5B satellite because of enhanced security procedures. I made my way over to T5B and used the lounge there - not crowded and plenty of food good wifi access free computers to use. All in all a pleasant quiet place to spend time before flight. One negative for BA: when I arrived at Heathrow a week previously - the Arrivals lounge at T5 had already closed promptly at 2pm. This seems very early given that the 2nd schedule SFO-LHR flight arrives at 2 pm.

One would have thought that British Airways/Jersey would have taken notice of R Pemberton's review of this lounge - 12 August 2009. Absolutely nothing has changed - for the better that is. At the time of my visit (late afternoon) dirty crockery was strewn across the tables. The elderly male attendant did not even bother to look up when I entered so no check of my credentials and certainly not greeting. It may be that BA Jersey are trying to save on electricity but I could not find any other reason for all the ceiling lights being switched off. There are table lamps but it was difficult to read the dog-eared newspapers on the shelves. Carpets and upholstery are still filthy so no change there. I used the newly built lavatory which appeared not to have been cleaned that day. I live in Jersey and this is my local airport. What sort of impression does this hellhole make on departing passengers?

The recent experience of the BA Terraces lounge at Gatwick was one of total shock - since my last visit in October. 50% of the facility has been closed - what was on two floors providing a very good experience - is now an insult to every BA Club World customer - as it is now located on 1 floor. Passengers cannot find seats (due to overcrowding) - and me and my family of 4 had to half stand and half sit as we ate our snack breakfast. BA's cost cutting has reached a new and deeply insulting low in the way it treats it's premium customers - thankful I am flying with another airline this month to New Zealand.

This is a very cold and dull lounge. The staff are far from welcoming - it's as if you have ruined their day just by being there. As someone else mentioned there is evidence of cost cutting throughout - fine for those in economy but not what one expects after paying so much more for a business class experience. The refreshments on offer were pathetic. I was there for an early morning flight and there were baskets of mini croissants and pan au chocolat cereal toast and coffee/juices etc. 100% self-service. Miserable staff hanging around like vultures ready to clear your table before you have finished swallowing your last mouthful. You can go out to the duty free shops but they don't bother to offer to look after your bags and coats so you need to lug them around with you if you are carrying anything of value which I usually am (laptop etc).

Arrived at Suvarnabhumi Airport a little early in order to check out BA/QF first class lounge. Very disappointed. Nothing special - if anything the Business Class lounge opposite was as good if not better. The First lounge was small very limited food - cheese platter 2 choices two types of rolls and wraps. Only difference between business and First was choice of wines and champagne.
The lounge in Miami needs a total refurbishment its old fashioned with a poor selection of food. A real let down.

Not worth the extra cost in my opinion. The lounge was busy - it was difficult to get a seat. The breakfast was paltry - tiny croissants for instance. There was no sense of luxury - an air of convenience and cost-effectiveness. Staff were not particularly polite.

Though this lounge is very new it really is not big enough to handle the 2 flights which leave quite close together in the evening. The staff however are exemplary - very welcoming professional and friendly with a real sense of enjoying their interaction with the passengers. There is a good selection of food and drinks with very acceptable pre-flight dining. If only the T5 lounges were the same as this one.

Shocked is all I can say. After trying the Concorde Lounge earlier in the year the Terraces was a huge let down. We got to the airport 4 hours before the flight yet told the spa was full. The food was mediocre we had to ask for champagne. It was comfortable enough and the wifi was good.

As a Gold card member I could use this lounge (unlike Heathrow's Concorde lounge which is exclusive for 1st passengers) as I awaited my flight to Antigua. Carpet very worn and dull as was most of the chairs and seating; everything felt like a 60s time warp. Food/breakfast was OK - nothing to speak about. Coffee machine appeared to be the only thing different to the club terraces option. Disappointing.

It's the attentive staff that makes this lounge a real pleasure. Staff members have always gone the extra mile to deal with seating upgrade and flight change and other special requests. Efficiency and smiles are a great combination. Food and drink are average but adequate. Too bad the washrooms are outside the lounge.

This lounge is shared by BA and Qantas and doesn't have many seats. So unless you get there quite early you might find it difficult to find a seat. The seats are old and need a make over. The choice of drinks is limited. Only one red one white and one sparkling wine (not champagne). The choice of food was limited to nuts fruit cold finger sandwiches cheese and crackers and Asian snacks (very tasty). Okay selections of newspapers no TV screens and a limited number of IT stations with one out of order. The lavatories were clean and so were the shower rooms.

There is a daily flight to/from Gatwick from Antigua and it is a disGrace that BA use this shoddy "shared" lounge - landside at Antigua VC Bird Airport. Its like a tomb - windows are shuttered and those not - look into a large waiting area that never seems to be used. An array of snacks are left on the sideboard - a bit of cheese and raw vegetables - drinks are served by a waiter. Dire - if you travel to Antigua and miss it don't worry about it.

The BA lounge in MXP is an old style terrace lounge. The lounge is very clean and the staff friendly and welcoming. The food served is quite good all Italian style focaccia sandwiches small pizzas etc. The choice of drinks is good with lots of typical Italian drinks available. Good selection of newspapers and a few IT stations although only one was working properly. There was also a smoking room available. Dirty plates and glasses were cleared continuously.

This is a shared lounge used by several airlines - pleasantly surprised with plenty of seating available. Lounge looks modern with lots of natural daylight spacious clean. On one side is quite a large bar. No self service for coffee tea etc you go to the bar and have your drink prepared for you - I think this gives a more personal service. On the bar is a menu listing available sandwiches. Around the lounge were monitors displaying flight information and announcements were made frequently about boarding or gate changes which is in contrast to Heathrow T5 where there are no announcements. I prefer announcements as you don't need to keep getting up. Near reception is a smoking room with a television displaying the news. The smoking room was as comfortable as the main lounge and was just as clean with staff clearing cups and plates regularly across the entire lounge. A magazine rack was located near the entrance with daily newspapers and magazines in Russian Ukrainian and English but staff weren't clearing left newspapers often. When my flight was called the gate was literally 30 feet away. This lounge certainly was a relaxing retreat away from the crowds and I wish more were like this.

This is easily the poorest of all the BA 1st class lounges I have frequented. It is a reasonably large space which fills up very rapidly within a few hours of the 2 to 3 late night flights back to London. Very often you will struggle to find a comfortable seat. I no longer eat anything in this lounge as the quality of the catering is not up to scratch. You will hardly ever find a UK newspaper (unless you are 3-4 hours early) and I can't think of a single redeeming feature of this lounge - not even a good view. It is well overdue a complete refurbishment and the general decor is grubby and tatty. Singapore - London is a very busy route for BA and presumably therefore somewhat profitable. If you travel the same route with Singapore Airlines the lounges are far superior as is the general lounge service.

I found the lounge very comfortable. Enough space for everyone although it was a Friday before a bank holiday weekend. The choice of hot food is limited but appropriate. Used plates and glasses are promptly removed by the staff who are polite and assist requests promptly. I didn't use the showers but the Elemis receptionist went out of her way and gave me her unused personal Elemis lip saver although these products were not generally available to passengers. BA should improve the magazines selection.

The new club lounge at T3 is very nice large and spacious with different seating areas. There was a large selection of both hot and cold food. The red and white wines are in different seating areas which is slightly strange and champagne is only available if you ask. The staff were attentive and customer service could not be faulted.

Great improvement on the old lounge. Quite small but well appointed. The First restaurant excellent - although we were the only two customers - with service both efficient and attentive. Bit of a walk to get there from the underpass walkway however although if you're not in a desperate hurry it's no real problem. As usual this comes at the end of a mass of confusion and waiting for security even in the Premium queue.

This is the new improved lounge and is for those entitled to "First Class" privileges but not travelling First Class I was travelling domestically so this was why I used this lounge. Seriously this is the best BA can come up with after how many years. I asked for the restaurant and was shown the buffet. The lounge was nice even allowing for the fact that it was hot in some areas and cool in others. Showers were basic. Staff friendly and helpful. Not worth the effort to try it out.

I recently read a review on this website regarding the Terrace lounge facilities at Jersey airport and was shocked to find it had deteriorated even further from the original submission. Food and dirty plates had been left out for many hours stained carpets and a poorly stocked bar compounded by a member of staff deciding to leave the lounge at 8 pm half an hour before the last flight was due to depart. Passengers had no idea it had incurred a delay and our only source of information came from data streams located on TV’s 100m away from the lounge. Simply terrible British Airways I would recommend that anyone flying Business class from Jersey attempts to spend as much time away from the lounge as you will only be disappointed with the service.

Had a longish layover due to BA delay and resulting re-booking so decided to use one of the cabanas. These are hotel-style rooms with day bed TV and music and a private bath. Had champagne and lunch delivered to the room so very nice. Then I discovered that the room only had one temperature - freezing cold Also the rooms back up to what may be a kitchen with constant banging of doors and other loud noises. Not very much chance of getting a rest here. Finally moved out into the lounge proper which is already showing some signs of wear and struggles to accomodate everyone at busy times. Restaurant food choices are rather uninspired and presentation not of the highest standard. Service can be inconsistent. For an exclusively First Class lounge this could be better.

Club Europe Lounge at Gatwick is very nice. It is on two floors and very spacious. The food selection is simple (only sandwiches pasta salads and similar and cheese with biscuits) plus the usual snacks. The only hot food served is soup. Very good selection of drinks with champagne on request very good selection of newspapers and magazines. IT workstations worked very well and are very modern. The toilet facilities are good with excellent showers and you can ask for Elemis products. The only downside was the lack of atmosphere. The lounge is very quite and with no music played in the background it could have been very boring.
Small but fine for the number of travellers on the day. Good atmosphere. Standard of food and drink good but range limited in comparison to say Galleries. so scores down a little.

Only food available was cheese and crackers. A waitress eventually appeared but did not approach anyone - she had to be asked for drinks. She brought them through and was never seen again. The room is fully enclosed and looks out on the seating area in the departure lounge - before security. The decor is drab a few magazines to read as well as some out of date newspapers. Couldn't wait to get on the plane. Shame as it soured the end of our holiday slightly.

Pretty busy lounge with good wifi and announcement when new UK newspapers arrived. Alcoholic drinks only available through a servery with occasional missing staff and therefore short queues and delays. Pleasant and efficient staff.

What a beautiful new lounge in E20 gate at Beijing capital airport. After 9 months closed and obliged to go to the awful BGS lounge, this lounge is amazing. Confort, good food, nice staff. All the usual seen in CX lounges in Hong Kong.

Their sit-down restaurant concept is genius. Bangkok is my home base now and they have a wide selection of food featuring their signature Pad Thai,unique for their Bangkok Lounge, and their usual dumplings, noodle dishes and more. Bangkok is not Cathay's largest lounge but it beats Thai Airways Royal Silk Lounge and Eva Airways Lounge at Bangkok. The lounge never was not overcrowded and I've flown out of there many times. The bar area, seating area and the work stations with PC monitors are comfortable and nice. The only thing the Bangkok Lounge is missing are showers.

The Cathay Pacific First Class lounge truly exceeds expectations. It’s one of the best lounges I’ve experienced better than even Qatar Airways’ renowned offering. From the complimentary massages to the exceptional five-star dining, every detail is top-notch. The food quality is outstanding, and the island bar offers fantastic service that enhances the entire experience. I felt incredibly welcomed and comfortable throughout my visit, thanks to the amazing staff who make this lounge so special. A huge thank you to them for creating such a memorable experience!

I visited it several times and disappointed. It was impossible to get a massage even if you're in transit for 4 hours. A sort of online booking for the lucky ones and especially their guest. The buffet was also  very limited. It's a total failure in terms of hospitality.

I was flying CX from BKK to HKG in economy, but as a member of Thailand Privilege, I was entitled to access the Miracle lounge, and used the one next to the gates G, to which the lounge provides a direct access. There was a reasonable choice of alcoholic beverages, good sandwiches, an excellent pumpkin soup and different kinds of soft drinks and ice creams. The lounge is quiet, gives a feeling of intimacy and seating is comfortable.

Took a flight with Cathay Pacific that consist of two flight with one flight being First Class and the other being Business class while I transit in Hong Kong Airport. Based on Cathay Pacific website, by right I should be able to use the First Class lounge (as it is stated they will honour the highest tier for the whole journey. I arrived in Hong Kong Airport at around 10pm and my departing flight is at 8am the following day. When I went to the first class lounge, I tried to double confirm on the lounge policy that I am eligible for the use of First Class lounge. The staff at the wing insist that I could only use the first class lounge until midnight and have to go to the business class lounge after. When I informed her that it’s stated otherwise in their website, she demanded that I show her. Despite showing her the website, she insist that the policy is such and I can’t enter the first class lounge after. When I requested to speak to the manager, she questioned me if I still want to use the lounge and brushed off my request. As I wanted to shower after my flight, I told her to arrange for me to speak to the manager. She agreed but clearly did not as I had to verified with the manager (whom I had to inform another staff after I showered) that no one had informed her of my request. The whole experience is just unwelcoming.

Lounge closed for renovations, over peak travel time at Easter? Nothing else open a this late hour at Logan. The BA lounge closes at 2100, CX could have used this one and extended the timing but chose to save money and not bother. Got a vague email about getting 'points' for the hassle. The real hassle is choosing a late flight thinking at least you can wait in the lounge and it will be open until 1230 only to find that nothing is open. Poor show from CX.

It is one of the biggest lounges and has sections like Bar, Tea House, Sleeping pods, Showers, Noodle Bar, Continental. I had a layover of 6 hours. They have plenty of showers so no waiting. If you are a business class traveler and transiting Hong Kong Airport, I highly recommend visiting this lounge.

What a terrible place. After a grumpy "welcome" (we were on a code share flight so had a boarding pass headed Air New Zealand but with a clear Cathay flight identified for our next leg) we entered the fetid atmosphere of a poorly ventilated overcrowded lounge. It was noisy, had very dirty seats, particularly those with a fabric covering which had stains and were thick with dust in crevices between the cushion and the chair. It was impossible to find a quiet space or to distance form other passengers, many of whom were talking loudly and some of whom were constantly coughing. The food offering was very poor; not everyone wants noodles or soup. We left the lounge exhausted, not refreshed. We won't be using it, or Cathay, again.
A large box, many places, there are lounges. Massage is a big turn. The restaurant offers good à la carte food, but the selection is not large. The buffet food is not very good.

This lounge is spacious but still crowded. Food is below average and food choices also very few. It is definitely not suitable if you have special dietary preference. Overall it is below average. Carpet doesn't look clean, maybe it is old. I usually visit Etihad or Emirates so may be my expectation is too. Not quite sure people are saying catering is good. Not recommended.

I spent an hour on the balcony overlooking the concourse at The Deck lounge, the space is peaceful and elegant that you feel you're in a garden café somewhere. Highlights of this lounge include the noodle bar (love the Dandan Mian), the swanky bathroom, and the mind-boggling variety of options from the buffet. I could actually spend 24 hours here, no problem.

I had been to the Wing Business Lounge before but this was a visit to the First which is upstairs. It is a great lounge to while away a few hours. The Wing is a big lounge and has various sections including the coffee nook and the fabled noodle bar. At 5.30 am in the morning the body was not quite ready for noodles and congee but had a light breakfast and shower and out. HK airport must be one of the few where there are so many lounge offerings. The Wing is right up there as amongst the best.

The best place to visit is the restaurant. Really good service, great staff! Food portions are small but you have lots of choice. Toilets are nice and clean, but it can be busy. That is, if you want to sit. The bar is pretty good, yet the experience depends on the bar tender; some are top, others are mediocre (one was clearly busy with his phone, kept going into the kitchen... and looked kind of annoyed seeing 4 people waiting for him for him to return (it wasn't an incident as he kept going back into the room behind the bar... must have been a bad day for him). The one thing I don't understand is that if you ask for a G&T, in the restaurant they will ask you what kind of Gin you like (they do have to better brands), while in the bar they serve you the lower end by default. Some of the couches have reached retirement age, the foot and or neck massage room is better ignored. The waiting time is almost always too long and the staff doesn't look like they like their job. I gave up long time ago but retried this week as it the lounge was pretty empty ... unsuccessfully. Waiting time was over 3 hours, just not enough time.. Interestingly, before telling me the waiting time, they asked for my next flight time details. The question remains ... what would have been the waiting time, if I had said 'in six hours'

The updated lounge might be small, but they were able to fill it with the noodle bar, cold food area, lots of premium drinks and plenty of seating. They have also provided two showers. It is conveniently located near the gates that CX uses.

This is the best Business Lounge I have visited. The layout is easy to navigate and understand what each section offers. The rectangular shape offers a complete view of the tarmac with amazing natural lights. After my shower, I had dinner from the noodle bar and buffet, and drinks were decent as well. Loving the addition of a Tea House. Overall, decor was welcoming and the staff were friendly and keeping the space clean.

The newly built Lounge offering by Cathay Pacific comes with the signature Noodle Bar and comfort on the same level as its other Lounges in Hong Kong. The only downside, this space is smaller than its competitors. The Decor is a favourite of mine, it's warm and welcoming and it's great to see Cathay take advantage of the natural light offered by the main terminal by having seating on the balcony. Food and Beverages were decent, not much at the buffet though the Noodle bar is the hero. I didn't get the chance to use the showers but the washrooms were very small. Overall, it's still a great Lounge and gives passengers a second option along with the Qantas Lounge in the same area of the terminal.

While Cathay are renovating their Lounge at Seoul Incheon, this Lounge is a temporary replacement. It is incredibly under standard for what Cathay normally offers. I find it strange to not have washrooms and shower facilities, as you will need to go out to the main terminal for these basic needs. The food and beverages were limited but the options that were on offer I actually really liked. Although the space was clean and comfortable, it really lacked the typical atmosphere that a Lounge really should be. Lastly, the staff were super polite and nice but I would not recommend you take time out to visit this Lounge.

I usually fly business with another airline and have been underwhelmed by the service throughout all Cathay Lounges. Perhaps it’s because I’m female but I was given no info about the lounge like male passengers after me and I had to ask about the facilities on offer. No announcement on plane to indicate when lounge opens (we landed at 4 am and lounge supposedly opens at 5:30 am. It then inexplicably and thankfully opened at 4:30 am). I used Pier and Wing to and from London and both times people at front desk were surly and unhelpful- really annoying after a long flight. No proper signposting to showers etc and the shower cubicles not air conditioned enough to feel refreshed. Rest of the place okay but nothing that special by comparison to other lounges I’ve been in. It’s all about the service nowadays and Cathay’s is really hit and miss.

A two level lounge with panoramic views of the mountain backdrop to the airport and a ringside seat to the parade of aircraft on the tarmac. Clean bathrooms with comfortable shower facilities - though they are ill-lit and dark in decor. Could do with brighter illumination. Lot of seating and power points to charge your phone and computer. A room had several desktop computers which you can use to surf the Net and check your mail. A variety of magazines and newspapers on racks. I spent two hours during breakfast time and usual breakfast items were available buffet style. There is a noodle bar where you can place orders for cooked items. There is also a coffee and croissant bar. The layout offers several different sections. This morning the place was very crowded. The location was excellent as it was near my departure gate and required less than a minute walk.

One of the best Business Lounge I have come across. Upon entry, you are whisked down a set of escalators with the reception desk in sight with a massive sign of the Lounge's name. I love how the space is split between left and right, each side having its own characteristics. In my opinion, the right is better as it caters a larger food and beverage experience with shower facilities to the left. For relaxation both sides will do the job, with bars offering great drinks. Once again, the staff are friendly and consistently cleaning. Definitely worth a visit whenever a chance arise.

On first impression, this lounge offers a luxurious experience from the get go. From day bed retreats to a la carte dining, you can also find two separate bars, endless shower facilities and a relaxing space to unwind before your departure. The team managing the lounge were very friendly and productive, consistently keeping the space clean. The only downside is the buffet on offer, it just lacked volume and options though the on demand dining was absolutely delicious. Definitely worth a visit whenever in Hong Kong airport.

A very underwhelming experience. I did do some research before my visit but from my experience I find it not up to standard by any means. The space is very small, the small number of the passengers made the room fill up very fast but I managed to find a seat at the office area. The food and beverages were  limited, the only thing that saved it were the Dim Sum dishes. The staff were super polite and professional, a great aspect of Asian carriers. Overall, I don't recommend this Lounge.

At the self checkin machine I received both a boarding pass and a card inviting me to the lounge, being an elite member of One World alliance. The lounge is spacious, overlooking the aerobridges and taxiways. Hot Chinese meals prepared on request - a small menu to choose from. Ample choices of liquor, beer an wine , soft drinks and other snacks. Apple computers to surf the net. Newspapers and magazines. Very clean and tidy. Quiet too. Located adjacent to the gates used by Cathay flights. A good place to wait before boarding your flight though Vancouver airport has lots to do. The lounge only opens a couple of hours before the arrival of a Cathay flight.

CX lounge was stunning. The decoration has a wooden tone, and the lounge was spotless. Drink selection was first class. Food selection was well presented and freshly cooked. I found CX lounge to be functional, clean and quiet and it was perfect to relax or catch up with some work before flight. Bar staff was friendly and personal and happy to make whatever cocktails required.

Visit the Pier during my transit (to/from Taipei) as my planes landed near gate 62/63. The lounge was large and even during busy period it didn't feel crowded. There are many seating and dining area - bar, tea house, food station, cafe, noodle bar, etc. The tea offered was high quality and well presented, and they also serve better champagne then on the flight. The whole lounge is pretty quiet. One of the best features of the lounge is the luxurious showers. On the way out I had to wait to use the shower (around 15 minutes which wasn't a big deal) and on the way back there was no queue at all. The shower cubicles were well designed and stocked with Aesop products. I can easily stay at the Pier for more than 2 hours without feeling bored.

Used this lounge when travelling on Finnair flight. Really nice lounge plenty of seating areas and quiet zones as well as good food options, Both Western and Oriental choices. The lounge has good views over the tarmac so you can watch the aircraft very well. Toilets and Showers were very clean, This lounge can get very busy but did not cause me any problems as we were in the early morning.

I unfortunately dropped from British Airways Gold to Silver status recently. I used to love visiting the Cathay Pacific First lounge at Heathrow so today would be a visit to their Business lounge. I arrived at 11am and was planning to have some noodles and then go onto the Qantas lounge for some Aussie bubbles, I don’t like Prosecco. I was pleasantly surprised to find Laurent Perrier on offer. Also had dan dan noodles, har gau and sui mai - execllent as usual. Really hope Cathay continue to offer this and it will make the fall from Gold to Silver a more pleasant soft landing.

The team were very welcoming and guide passengers to the appropriate Business or First Class Lounge. I notice the exclusivity and luxury upon entering as the lounge was not overcrowded. There were facilities, like The Cabanas (Spa and Day Bed) but I didn't have time as I only had just over an hour during my visit. I did have breakfast in the dining area, which has an a la carte menu and there was 2 separate buffets throughout the lounge. The one thing it did lack was the tarmac views as the lounge was not directly in front but had negative space, It makes more sense when you're there. One of the best Lounges I have visited to date.

I had a 2 hour lay-over in Hong Kong between flights. I visited both The Bridge (gate 35) and The Pier (gates 63/65). The Pier by far is a much better lounge; larger, more comfortable seating areas, wider selection of food and beverages, more quiet areas and computer stations and a better ambiance. Both have great views of the airfield. The food selection was very good, with many Western and Asian dishes, very good pastries and desserts, coffee bar and expansive call bar. WiFi super fast. Highly recommend The Pier if traveling through Hong Kong.

One of the biggest lounges I have visited. Lounge staff was very welcoming and helpful. Boarding announcements made, food and drink options were outstanding. Very clean, not very crowded, amazing facilities with great amenities such as Aesop products in their showers and washrooms. Lounge atmosphere is possibly the best of all lounges I have been to.

The Pier lounge visited in June 2017 has coffee area, food, bar, noodle, tea  and rest areas. It is so large and you can select where to sit, dine or rest. The food is good as well. Highly recommended.

The Heathrow lounge visited in May 2017 is a smaller version of the larger Hong Kong Lounge at The Pier. When we were there, there was plenty of space for each person. It is friendly, good range of drinks and a good range of food. Highly recommended.

I visited the London Cathay First Class lounge on Feb 16 when departing for Singapore through Hong Kong. The lounge is an old-school design with comfortable chairs and a well-designed dining area. There is an excellent pre-flight menu and there is a well-stocked bar area. For a lounge to just sit down and eat and relax, it is hard to top. The views of Terminal 3 operations are good and it is quiet. As a place to work, though, it has limitations - the outlets are limited and there are not work tables (the tables seem to have been removed with the redesign in London some time ago). For work, I find the AA First Class lounge down the hall stronger though it is nowhere near as nice as the Cathay lounge. One of the advantages of T3 in London now is the excellent range of OneWOrld lounges - a new Qantas lounge, the AA lounge, BA and CX. Overall the CX is the most luxurious and it has the best food but space is limited at times.

The Cathay "the cabin" lounge has a great lounge feel to it. Everything signal quality and exclusivity from the furniture to the decor. This is absolutely one of my favorite lounges. Can not wait to get access to the first class Lounge.

The Cathay lounge has a great feel to it. Everything signal quality and exclusivity from the furniture to the decor. That said the food selections in the Manila lounge could have more choices and have a Western non-vegetarian option. Still, the Cathay Manila lounge is absolutely one of my favorite lounges.

I slated the Cathay Pacific lounge at Manchester about 20 hrs ago, but forgot to mention where I was. I am now in the Pier Cathay Pacific lounge at Hong Kong and this is what a business class lounge should be like. Excellent in just about every regard and I am led to believe this is the one most recently refurbished. Well it shows. The complete antithesis of the cramped and poor facilities at MAN - though in fairness, the staff at MAN were very good. Remember your image goes well beyond Hong Kong Cathay Pacific, so maybe take a look at some of those non-hub BC lounges.

Small, overcrowded and the food and drink selection is very poor. Tea, coffee, white rolls, sausages and no bacon. Some lacklustre fruit and porridge. I think there's about 10+ airlines using this lounge and it shows - penny pinching. Toilets etc not even in lounge. Really not impressed Cathay.

The Pier lounge has everything and put in designated areas from Coffee area, Food Area, Bar area, Noodle  area, Tea area and a rest area. Problem with the Hong Kong lounges are there is a big difference between the lounges and I highly recommended the Pier. The Wing is not bad but the Pier is another class in my opinion.

Lounge was great, friendly staff and everything was perfect. But one thing there should be Halal meal available for Muslim traveler, the lounge used by Oman Air customers.  I cannot eat fish due to allergy so ended up eating salad and bun.

Travelling from Rome to Auckland via Hong Kong Business Class. There was a long stopover in Hong Kong but of course had the availability of the a Business lounge. The lounge was a complete contrast to the flight and not in a good way. Staff were perfunctory rather than welcoming, but I guess so what. However, what amazed me was the disgusting state of the furniture. I had thought to find a place for my children to lie down on a couch, but take a look at the photo and ask yourself if you would. I have seen cleaner couches in Car garages waiting for the tyres to be changed. None of the remaining seats allowed for a comfortable snooze and were pretty tired looking as well. I travel a lot with work and have to say this is one of the worst lounges I have come across. Was really surprised, particularly given this was Cathay Pacific's hub.

This is my most favorite lounge. I  think this is the reason why its worthwhile to keep my emerald status on oneworld. The first class lounge is very exclusive, compared to the over-crowded business class lounge. The showers are well equipped with toiletries and spacious. The are such a wide variety of alcoholic drinks and the seats are super comfortable. The restaurant is one of the best, the variety of dishes served and even the peninsula chocolate is amazing. Service   is impeccable for Cathay Pacific. I recommend to always try the special dish at the restaurant.

This London Heathrow Cathay Pacific lounge was a real disappointment. There was no service. The snacks were a few odds and ends in the fridge, with the highlight being British Rail style tasteless white rolls. The help-yourself bar had a notice saying that full bar service was available in the business class lounge, which was odd. The supermarket-style Champagne (Moet) had been left out overnight and was flat. Yes, there was a room out back with unremarkable hot food, but I prefer a seat with a view. The showers and loos were down the corridor, next to the business lounge, which looked better than First. This Cathay lounge is miles behind the American first-class lounge, and worse than even BA, which is an achievement these days.

Travelling on Qantas to Sydney through London Heathrow T3 and the long-awaited Qantas First lounge is still not open. Being a BA Gold, I normally dutifully troop into the BA lounge, but on the advice of recent fellow passenger, I tried the Cathay lounge instead and now regret ever having used the BA one! From the super-friendly greeting, excellent beverage choices and proper restaurant style dinner service, this lounge knocks many other lounges into touch. I used to resent booking flights from T3, but I'm already looking forward to the next one!

This lounge does not do Cathay justice as the lounge is below any lounge standard. Food and beverage and coffee all makes you feel like you being at a cheap 1 star hotel breakfast buffet. Would rather have a smaller selection of quality items such as a nice cup of coffee or a quality glass of wine.

Beautiful design - very appealing but not comfortable - seats are so low almost seat on the floor. Food is served in restaurant and very limited option in the main lounge. Can go to business class lounge attached where you can find the usual noodle bar with the same poor noodles as all Cathay lounges. After 15 min in the most uncomfortable seat ever, I exited the lounge and went to a nearby coffee shop - so much for global Cathay experience

While the nicest lounge in all of Manila (including SQ's new SilverKris next door), the limitations of being in a poorly managed airport is taking its toll. There is an ambiance of calm with partitioned areas for eating, drinking and resting, but the fact that the air conditioner not turned on until 10am is appalling, especially in Manila heat. The ventilation and circulation was provided by strategically placed fans, but that did not do much to help lower ambient temperature. The noodle bar had an excellent selection and the bar had an extensive selection of drinks. Early on, there seemed to be ample seating, but since there was a delay, the place became crowded as passengers for the next flight were also filing in. Washrooms were clean, but ill maintained. No showers. Wifi was present, but not reliable nor fast. The free airport wifi was a lot faster.

The largest and newest lounge in HKG is also the farthest. In fact, it was a 1.5 km walk from the lounge to my gate (19), but the distance was well worth it. With a restaurant, coffee cart, noodle bar, showers, relaxation, lounge and work areas arranged in a very logical way with quiet and busy portions near each other but don't necessarily interact. The downside is that the showers are rather small in size when compared to the Bridge lounge. The food more than makes up for this oversight as the selection is wide, tasty and fresh. An isolated relaxation area allows for snoozes and naps between flights and the Bureau provides an ambiance conducive to productivity. Very nice and worth the extra walk if time permits.

Cathay Pacific's in Hong Kong are incredible and T3 Heathrow is no exception. Designed in very similar style to The Pier lounge in Hong Kong, the LHR lounge is a smaller, more compact version. The signature Noodle Bar is available, producing fresh Dim Sum, noodles, pork buns and dumplings to name a few. Showers are great, very clean and modern. There is a selection of other foods if you dont fancy dim sum. I intially get the airport long before my flight just to make full use of this incredible lounge.

Walked from the Wing lounge to the Pier - it took 30 minutes! Keep an eye on your departure gate and place yourself in a lounge close to it, or you might end up with a very long walk to the gate. Make sure though that you allow time to spend here. This is the most impressive lounge I have visited. The entrance is down escalator and the main entry has the feel of a 5 star hotel. A friendly, efficient check in then to the main area. The first room has a serviced food area, with an exceptional selection of hot and cold food. The next room with the main bar area. The staffed bar has good selection of very good booze, including Champagne. The staff was happy to make cocktails (if they have everything required). Continue down and you will find the noodle bar, where there is a selection of pre prepared noodle or you can have something made fresh. There is a tea room, with staff serving and advising on a large variety of teas. Beautiful space, impeccably clean and tidy. Lovely bathrooms too. We left briefly to smoke (there is a smoking room just a couple of minutes' walk away) then straight back for more. If you want to re-enter the lounge, you should get a re-entry stamp on you boarding pass on the way out. The WiFi was very good, with easy access and good speeds.

In transit from London to Auckland and wanted a shower. BA silver Executive Club so able to go to a lounge. The Wing was closest to the transit security so went there. Warm welcome at the entrance by smiling, efficient staff. Headed straight to the showers. There are more here than any other of the Cathay lounges in terminal 1. Very impressed. Looked newly refurbished, all tiled. Best shower head I have ever been under, with good water pressure and lots of hot water. High quality towels and face cloths. A drawer has useful items, such as toothbrush/toothpaste sets, although no shaving equipment. Not sure if this is available on request. Also a toilet in the room. Mild complaints only: it was a little dark, so will need to take care if trying to do anything in the mirror. Also a bit warm. Next went upstairs to the lounge proper. This is not a huge lounge and not busy late afternoon. Looking perhaps a little tired but plenty of snack foods, drinks etc, with a great selection of soft drinks, reasonable wine and spirits. This lounge has a serviced bar, behind which are huge windows overlooking the apron. It features Cathay's signature round seats that are semi enclosed - very cool. WiFi a bit hit and miss and not very fast. Didn't stay long, as I wanted to try the new Pier lounge.

Cathay Pacific has one of the best Lounges in Hong Kong airport. The lounges are in I think 5 locations catering to different gate locations. Food is among the best, and there is ample shower facilities. Spacious too - a great way to relax with a drink before a flight.

On a recent almost around-the-world trip on Cathay Pacific I took the opportunity to try out various lounges. The one in Vancouver emerged to be my favourite one. It was a haven of tranquility with a cosy and warm interior. The staff was very cheerful, friendly and helpful. I especially liked the high ceilings in the shower suite. The food and drinks selection however was pretty standard but I did not mind because I was looking foward to my first dinner in First Class. It was too bad that I did not have more time to spend in this relaxing environment. It is also a good place for plane-spotters, much better than London or Hong Kong.

Had a 3 hour transit in HKG and headed straight to the Wing Business for breakfast, coffee and a shower. The Wing is a bit crowded and it seemed rather chaotic despite the airy architecture of the place. The long bar was a bit claustrophobic but the coffee area served an excellent cappuccino. I decided to head out to the Bridge as more passengers were streaming in. The Bridge, in stark contrast to the Wing was a lot more quiet, owing perhaps to the fact that it was a lot more isolated and therefore more difficult to get to. No queues in the shower (which was well stocked with excellent water pressure and heat). Food options were wonderful with congee and dimsum in the morning and heavier offerings in the evening (my return flight). I will head straight to the Bridge on my next HKG transit.

Cathay Pacific gave me access to the lounge after a long flight delay, it was quite appreciated and needed. The lounge provided showers, wifi - open bar buffet and comfortable lounge style seating. I utilized the buffet which was sufficient and good quality, the wifi was good. Bathrooms were clean and people were friendly. Overall I liked the lounge.

As a Oneworld emerald member I was invited to spend my connecting time in the first class lounge. It is adjacent to the business class lounge, near gates 1 and 2. You are directed by attendants to go upstairs where the lounge is. You have very good views of the taxi areas, planes at gates or rolling by slowly, with the mountains in the background. Even though it was a rainy morning, it was a memorable sight. The best part of the lounge was that it was very quiet. Computers and printers were available as also a very good collection of international newsmagazines and newspapers. I took a shower in the very clean and tidy bathroom, which was very relaxing though the lighting was rather dim. That and the grey décor created a gloomy ambience. There were food stations and bars and very attentive and discreet attendants. In sum, it was a good place to just relax, enjoy a cappuccino until it was time for my flight.

This is the best lounge I have been in.  Food is great with a wonderful selection. We were there for nearly 11 hours and it was great. The clincher is the showers. I was on a 13.5 hour flight and the shower was a God send.

The Pier is in my opinion the nicest business class lounge I've been to. Located on the far side of the terminal, it is a sprawling complex where one can dine, wine, or relax prior to a flight. Food choices are pretty decent, with a very good Chinese selection with dim sum and a noodle bar. Tsing Tao beer on tap, but there are other bottled and canned selections as well as a wide variety of wines and spirits. Coffee was excellent, but was not able to sample some of the teas on offer. Showers and relaxation areas are also aplenty and since it was not crowded during my visit, there was an ambiance of calm prior to my flight.

This lounge visited at 11am and was a very well laid out lounge with great service from the staff who were always walking around so that you could ask them for a drink etc. Ambience is very relaxing and seating is very comfortable. Toilets kept exceptionally clean and overall a very nice experience -  would use again. Internet was superfast well you'd expect that in Hong Kong but was a joy compared to Cebu where I had come from.

I've been to 3 lounges in Manila's terminal 3 and the CX lounge is the nicest in terms of facilities, comfort and layout trumping SQ's SilverKris in the same terminal. There is a serene feeling once you enter and staff are friendly, but not overly intrusive. The lounge slips as far as catering is concerned, however. The much ballyhooed noodle bar lacked in the freshness of ingredients compared with the HK version, but the coffee on offer was top quality. Wifi was pathetic, with the airport's free wifi performing at 3x the speed of the lounge wifi. It's the nicest lounge in Manila and certainly beats waiting at the gate.

I was really happy that when flying Qantas to SYD from SFO I was allowed as a OW-Emerald to use the Cathay Pacific First Class lounge at SFO airport. I was told uually this is not possible when the lounge is overcrowded but I was lucky that day it was really uncrowded. The lounge was very modern, I got a warm welcome at the reception and the noodle bar was available. I can't say I missed something, I could use the business facilities and print out some documents. Although the main printer wasn't working the lady at the reception was very nice to print them over there and hand them to me. There are big chairs with stereo systems and showers & co. are also available.

The Pier provides all the services one needs during flights. The showers with toilet are clean and perfect aircon. A beautifully designed Restaurant with a great mix of Asian and Western food, next to a self service restaurant with great food and drinks choices. There is a bar with lots of choices as well. Private rooms (cabanas) in which one can rest on a bed and with a great view on the runways. A lot of different rooms with comfortable seats, mostly with power station, etc. a very well equipped business center, etc. All in All the Pier First in one of the finest and most beautiful lounges.

Since the new operators took over this lounge from Peninsular Hotel earlier this year, standards continue to decline. This lounge is no longer worth the long walk out to the pier. Dining was a strong point before, now the service is at best ad hoc. Orders get confused, service is usually out of time with my partner's meal and generally no attention to detail. Today there was one waiter to 4 people in the dining area and still issues cropped up, like how do I eat this meal without any form of cutlery? The only upside of this lounge now is that hardly anyone uses it so you can have plenty of space to relax. It's so sad that Cathay's premium experience has been dumbed down by not understanding understand the subtleties of top tier FF requirements.

Third visit to this Cathay Pacific "The Pier" lounge at Hong Kong Airport in a year and it's great with many options for food and drink readily available. Great shower with good choice of products in each shower room. Early morning it was nice and quite but there seems lefty of room to sit. View was pleasent also. Would recommend this lounge for morning.

The flight, on Cathay business class, arrived 4:30am, so I used the Arrivals lounge facility and at Heathrow T3. Cathay Pacific use the American Airlines Arrivals Lounge. I visited this lounge before but this time I was happy to see that the lounge is renovated, and even at such an early hour service was good and there is adequate supply of food and drink. And with good internet, there is nothing more useful than relaxing at this lounge to spend time till a decent hour to travel to London.

All the Cathay Pacific lounges at Hong Kong airport deserve high praise for facilities, cleanliness and service. The Wing has excellent shower rooms, a food and drinks buffet, and a coffee shop - plus the standard amenities of magazines, wi-fi and working spaces. Staff go out of their way to greet passengers and assure that their needs are met. One highly beneficial feature is the ability to transfer between lounges in the case of a gate change or if your departure gate is not known when you arrive. You can always position yourself at the closest lounge to your boarding location.

Having been recently renovated, the Pier Marco Polo Club a large lounge offering a range of food from snacks to a full meal. There is ample seating and a large bar offering a wide range of beverages. The seating is well spaced and comfortable and there is a good view of the airport activities. The staff are very friendly and professional. All in all a great place to spend an hour or two or even longer if necessary.

I arrived at the airport 8 hours before departure of my flight to Düsseldorf. I went straight to the Pier Lounge and was pleasantly surprised that there are lockers for hand luggage. This enabled me to move around more freely. The lounge consists of different section. There is a coffee/bakery corner at the entrance, a bar-section further on, a noodle bar with asian buffet just next to that, followed by a tea-room and a relaxation zone - there is also a business-corner. The food and drink selection is of wide variety and high quality. The baristas did an excellent job, not only preparing the products but also explaining them. I tasted two different teas which both took between 3 to 5 minutes to prepare and tried to different coffee specialities.  Although the lounge is huge one feels welcome by staff. The downside maybe was the selection of magazines and newspapers which was nothing to write home about.

Small Cathay Pacific lounge at Seoul Incheon Airport but very spacious, looks clean with natural light. Lavatory is provided hand lotion. But the food wasn't a lot variety, and didn't look very appetizing. Far below the expectation, compared with the rest of the lounge in Asia. Wifi worked quite well.

Cathay Pacific does not have its own lounge at London Heathrow T3 and passengers can choose between the No 1 lounge or the American Airlines lounge. This so call No 1 Lounge is probably the worst lounge I have used. It is over-crowded. There are two areas uncongested but Reserved (for no one). Food service is bad quality and quantity for choice. If Cathay Pacific continues to use this lounge I shall fly another airline next time.

You know this is an excellent lounge when there is a champagne waiter ready to serve you 3 types of champagne, Moet NV, Moet Pink and Veuve Clicquot. The hardware is second to none, the selection of furniture, design of the setting would be same as chic cool and comfortable, The food and service is excellent.

Cathay Pacific use the DNATA lounge at Singapore. Average selection of food and of average quality. Many items still wrapped in plastic wrap. Coffee from self service machine tasted sour. Perhaps a problem with the milk or poor cleaning. A proper, industrial coffee machine behind the counter but at 7am there was no sign of any staff member to operate it. Staff at the reception desk were busy chatting to each other and did not even speak to me when I handed over my pass. A spacious and comfortable lounge but could be so much better with decent food, drink and staff.

Worst Cathay Pacific Airways lounge so far. They served cheap white and red wine. The spirits also need to be upgraded. Surprisingly, the food was so basic, instant noodles, sandwiches, and awful dim-sum. In addition, they did not provide good wifi internet connection. (worst!)

My OneWorld Emerald status qualified me to use this Cathay Pacific lounge, which is located near gate 1 to 4 at Hong Kong Airport. A separate section is reserved for first class passengers of CX and Emerald members. It is elegantly designed, with plenty of spaces to stretch out, plus a sit down to order style restaurant. Because of the amount of people it receives with  OneWorld status, it gets too busy to be totally relaxing, Some young kids ended up in here too, and it could get a little noisy. Service is very good overall. The business class section is just next to ours, I took a look, and it honestly didn't look very different, except busier. I'd say this is a First class lounge with a business class kind of feel. Since I didn't have to fly CX first class and still can come here, I wasn't complaining.

As a Qantas Gold Frequent Flyer(Oneworld Sapphire), I was able to use the Cathay Pacific Business Lounge at Hong Kong Airport. Cathay Pacific has some of the best lounges in the world at this airport which I shall discuss in separate reviews. Every time I transit here and i have got enough connection time, I try to use the lounges. I used the Business class lounge at the Bridge for both out/inbound flights. The reception was very nice. I showed my Qantas card and the boarding pass. The dining area is very clean and the air conditioning is comfortable. The buffet has quite a few choices, including both Chinese food and some western style food. Good choices of fresh juices. I really enjoy the food here, though this is not comparable to the First Class lounge where food is ordered and custom-made. Two outstanding things are: the spacial well-equipped shower and the real coffee. You need to get a buzzer to get in the queue for shower, so get the buzzer as soon as you are in the lounge. The shower room was large, equipped with almost everything you need, tooth brush, shaving, etc. A hot shower during connection is always good. After shower, I went to the coffee counter, where a lady would prepare fresh coffee. I guess people in Melbourne are spoiled by the good coffee. I ordered a Latte and got in a few minutes. It was really good, considering this is a lounge. This is a conveniently located lounge, highly recommend!

This Cathay Pacific / Dragonair lounge at Beijing Capital Airport is about adequate, a long room with adequate food and drink service, but not to compare with Cathay lounges in Hong Kong of course. However there are two problems. One is that more often than not the aircraft parking bay is very far from the location of this lounge so that one must allow time for a 10 minute walk. The other is that the internet is rather weak, or doesn't really work, as is the case of the printer, and it seems that they never care to face this problem.

Cathay Pacific has some (I think) four lounges in Hong Kong Airport, each is good and somewhat different. This one the Wing is probably the best and the original, has two floor levels. There is a lot of food of all kinds and drinks. And there are computers with which you can make prints. It is one of the best except it is often crowded, but not a match for Qatar Airways Doha lounge.

The variety of food in this lounge is above average compared to other lounges in Changi Airport but is not as good as those in Hong Kong Airport. Wifi connection here is very poor by Singapore standard. I am here at 5am in the morning when there are not too many other guests and yet, I am getting only <1Mbps connection speed. A typical Singapore home uses 100Mbps! They have international electric sockets which is very convenient. Unfortunately there are not enough of them around the lounge especially the dining area.

Cathay Pacific lounge is open to passengers flying with several other airlines, including Oman Air that I was flying. Spacious and airy, however can be sometimes crowded. Excellent food, western and asian (chinese dishes prepared to order). Quality wines from France and Australia. Seating adequate. Good wifi. PC's also available but no printing facilities. Good choice of newspapers and magazines. Lounge has large windows opening on the aircrafts parking/taxiing areas.

The Wing First Class Lounge (use as oneworld Emerald) is a place I frequent quite often to grab some quick food and to do some urgent work. I notice just about everyone else in here is doing the same so it has a good environment for that type of activity. The showers and cubanas are wonderful and seating comfortable and functional. However, I am not so keen on the small restaurant area where one is often crammed into a small place, with a sense of space invasion by all concerned. Nevertheless, the food and wine is pretty good in this lounge and the service adequate. One aspect is becoming increasingly irritating is the infernal same music/musak track going round and round hour after hour and year after year. If I hear 'Stars fell on Alabama', 'Deep Purple' and 'Misty' (that once I used to like) once more in this Lounge I don't know what I will do. Enough is enough! Nice view of aircraft movements and good newspaper selection.

Beautiful, modern lounge with ample space. I visited around Christmas 2015 on my way back to Sydney and was impressed by the comfort and amenities. Wifi was patchy in some areas, however. The selection of food is excellent, complete with noodle bar and multiple buffet areas. A combination of western and Asian food available; but the noodle bar was definitely the highlight. A fantastic flagship hub and will definitely visit again.

Quite new. Attractive color scheme. Ample seating. 3 Internet computers. Solid wifi. Luggage storage available, but not secure. Downsides:  stiflingly hot. Desk agents informed me that the aircon was "maxed". -Hot Food only upon request, then have to wait for the food. In a major lounge with nice dining facilities (ie. the HKG lounges), this is quite nice. But they also offer the quick, buffet-style offerings, not available here at MNL.

Excellent newly refurbished lounge at BKK. Plenty of seating and decor was subtle with muted tones. Very good noodle bar and excellent service from the drinks bar. If departing with any other oneworld alliance on business ticket or if tier allows it, then recommend that you check out this lounge first.

Cathay Pacific lounge was very well decorated and relaxing with several different types of seating. Drinks were dispensed by a friendly barman and there was a good range of cold snacks available. There is also a noodle bar which was serving some very good food. Lounge had good views of the aircraft stands. Toilets were clean and tidy. A good place to wait for the flight.

Visited the Wing late on Friday evening. There was ample space in the lounge but mainly I wanted to have a shower so used the facilities here. The attendant showed me to the shower room and also where the hairdryer etc. was located. The shower room was reasonably spacious but it was very warm. The shower itself can only be described as fantastic. The shower head is about two feet square and with good water pressure almost washes you away. Having showered, it was difficult to get dry as the shower room was so warm I just kept perspiring. Back in the lounge there was hot food available but because of the short time available before the flight departed I just had a soft drink from the well stocked bar. The staff were very efficient and the lounge was spotlessly clean. I would very much have liked to spend more time here.

Escape Lounge at T2 is undergoing refurbishment and signs directed passengers to alternative lounge, unfortunately signs sent people round in a circle. Eventually found the temporary lounge which was small with limited choice of food on offer and the spirits available were obscure brands that looked as though they had been smuggled into the lounge from a corner shop. Totally underwhelmed by this experience.

This is the worst lounge experience I have ever had, I will never return. Firstly being the choice of the food is very limited, and it tasted so bad. I believed I gave the staff at my arrival lounge invitation, anyway when I was trying to relax at the lounge, the lady asked for my invitation loudly and became quite rude. I asked if I could just finish my beer and I could go to my dad outside the lounge to find the other invite, and she insisted I can't because she need to input to system. I then had to run to my dad outside in front of everyone and try to find the invitation. Later on she said I could stay here and enjoy while she calls and check for me, when she realised that I am travelling on business class. So why couldn't you do that at first? To me that is insulting and disappointing. This also gave me a bad impression on British Airways.

Loved this Cathay Pacific lounge, quite busy but plenty of space and comfortable seating. Lots of great food choices, loved "The Bakery". Free wifi and plenty of spots to charge devices. Had a short 5 minute wait for the showers, they were excellent, large, clean and really quite plush looking and well appointed. Staff were very good and cleared the tables regularly. Really enjoyed our time here.

Not much food on offer in the Hong Kong Cathay Pacific lounge and seems to be cutbacks. Tables took a long time to get cleared. Lounge full of families- kids running around. Beautiful furniture but it seems a bit empty and plain. People arrive very early to use the lounge so often not many seats. The renovated lounge up at gate 40 seems a bit better.

The lounge is very big with many food options and 24 shower rooms available. The lounge itself has 2 levels. Upstairs it has a noodle bar where you can order some traditional Asian food, a coffee area, and a dining area where it is a buffet style. Downstair, it has computers, another dining area where it is a buffet style, and shower rooms (Jurlique products). To enter you must go downstairs first then a lift and staircase will bring you upstairs. If the lounge is busy, you can still visit another 5 One World lounges (Cathay's The Cabin, The Pier and The Bridge, Dragon's G16 and The Qantas HK lounge!)

I checked in very early for my Cathay Pacific flight home (HKG to YVR) and they hadn't designated a gate to the plane yet. So, I decided to walk to the other end of Hong Kong Airport to visit the Bridge and I'm glad I did! The lounge is split into two sections and both were very comfortable. The Bridge also has showers that you can book (wish I had). Food was good, drinks were plentiful and the service was great.

The lounge hopefully will have rebranding renovations soon. Although it is quiet and relaxing, it is quite dated. The furniture looks tired and worn out. The food selection, on the other hand, was not bad. I wish they had some more hot food selection, but the usual dim sum variety did hit the spot. The coffee machine was great and so was the selection of wine and spirits. The counter agent was very friendly.

The Wing (First Class) is on level 6, near gates 1-4 at HKIA. The entrance is very discreet but it over looks the level 5 gates. You go through the bar, IT area, then into the restaurant. The restaurant features a hot food buffet (western and Asian cuisine) as well as a menu. Passengers can have either buffet or a la carte. Marvelous facility and amenities!

The Bridge is Cathay's finest lounge, with a long bar that serves a range of high-end drinks, an excellent array of Chinese and Western food, and comfortable sleeping areas and nice chairs. It's all a bit dark, but that's not unusual to Cathay's Hong Kong lounges (vs Paris and London which are marble/bright). Recommended as Cathay's go-to lounge.

The Cathay Pacific "The Wing" lounge was overcrowded with many people there. Hardly find seat and feel like I was in the tea house in Hong Kong. Food is okay and the lounge is clean and tidy. They really need to address the crowd issue, since it is not quite comfortable with a batch of loud speaking people.

Cathay Pacific Airways The Bridge lounge at Hong Kong International Airport. No fuss upon check in to lounge. Decent size space. Excellent food and drink selections. Good size shower room with amenities. Normally staff will direct guests to main room where the dining room is located. Go to the other side after eating if you fancy taking a shower and just relaxing. It is not too crowded. Has selections of foods and drinks.

Having visited The Pier First Class Lounge twice this month, I am amazed by the changes made to it following the refurbishment. Outstanding food and excellent staff service, combined with areas to relax, work, enjoy a drink, snack or massage. I enjoyed my stay there, and found the distance to my gate from it to be worth the airport train ride or long walk.

Having read some reviews that Cathay Pacific Airways The Pier, First Class lounge at HKG has undergone refurbishment work, I was excited to pay it a visit before my flight, and this did not disappoint. It's a bit of a trek after the security area, but you can get there relatively fast by taking the train and its in the Gate 65 area. The lounge has a very plush feel, a bit like walking into a plush 5-Star Hotel. The lounge has a lovely bar area, Library/Lounge area, Massages Free of Charge, and a full service Restaurant that serves amazing food, that left me wondering if I had not just had dinner at a fine dining establishment. The staff were unbelievably attentive and during a short delay the reception staff were very informative and extremely helpful storing my luggage. Quite possibly one of the best lounges I have visited, and I cannot wait to return there.

We always enjoy the Noodle Bar (dan dan noodles with wontons) and the Long Bar with various drinks and snacks at Cathay Pacific Airways The Wing lounge in Hong Kong Airport. Great selection of reading materials.

Arrive at the airport from a Dragonair flight, with 1 hour left for the connection flight to New york. Boarding gate is 41 so I chose the closest lounge, The Bridge. I enter the lounge at 11pm. I was intend to take a shower before boarding a long haul flight but the staff told me that there are 4 passengers waiting for this service before me and she can't tell the time that I need for waiting. I went to the dining room later but there are limited choice of beverages and food quality is not the best at midnight. I suggest that if you have enough transition times you better go to The Wing which is probably the best lounge in Hong Kong Airport.

I don't like this lounge at all, it is too small, very dated but at least it is clean. My worse complaint is the food choice is awful and very limited, even if you travel in the morning there is no breakfast food. I just wish they would update the lounge and specially give us proper foods. I still strongly recommend Cathay Pacific Airways, but not the Cathay Pacific lounge at Cebu!

Flew BA to Prague and prefer the Cathay Pacific Airways lounge over BA. Food choice was excellent, chose the made to order noodles and they were excellent. A hot buffet was also available and I tried malaysian duck curry and it was great. My companion had carrot cake and cheese and was very happy. Decent choice of drinks and we drank about 4 flutes of the excellent Verve Clicquot champagne. My companion also had a shower and commented how lovely it was. The lounge had great views of the apron and runaway action.

The new lounge has just opened, huge improvement on the old one. Open to all one world pax. The lounge is neutrally decorated with a good Thai menu. Not much else on offer at the moment but I think they're working on it, great bar and lots of staff around . Well done Cathay!

Too busy and small. Lounge used by a variety if other airlines hardly any seats and food drink not so good. I often don't bother. Considering there are so many flights from BKK to HKG I think a bigger lounge needed. Stop messing around with a first class lounge and just make a better one for everyone.

Tiny room. Lots of flights from BKK to HKG so already busy really not much there. Also other airlines use it. They really need a bigger one considering the amount of daily flights. Not much food to choose from.

Atmosphere is acceptable and the noodle bar is a plus. But the noodle bar is hiding behind the washroom area and didn't even know the first time I was there. The food selection is small. The internet speed was as I tested about 3-5 mbps it's ok I guess. Staff courtesy is not so good. Nobody came to greet me at the lounge entrance. Some don't speak good English.

Surprisingly small in size and lack of the luxury atmosphere which you would expect from an international airport which the airline has three A330 flight serving daily. Choice for breakfast items were limited - especially hot plates. I don't see chance for big refurbishment of the lounge due to relative size of MEL airport.

Agreed with comment made by Michael before considering the amount of BKK-HKG flights the lounge could really be improved. Small food and drink selection nice seating areas and it's quiet though. Hard to find. The Emirates lounge here and even the priority pass one next door are superior. Toilets are outside and there's loads of room to have one inside.

The lounge is a small place on the Mez floor between the main airport area and the gates in Section G. It is dingy and without much of a view. The furniture seems shipped over from HK as leftovers from the renovation there. Sat through chairs and chipped and worn tables. So it does not matter that people place their feet with the shoes still on on the tables. Staff are friendly (natural for Thai) but that is the best about it all. Drinks are standard only snacks and cup noodle soup on offer here. If you have the option move over to Louis Tavern lounge for superior service and experience.
Very impressed with the quality and service received at all lounges. Amazing washroom facilities and quite areas for relaxing between flights. Food and drink was also very good!
If you don't like one lounge you can try another and another and another. There is something for everyone and service beverages and calm environment.

This is the newly refurbished Cathay First Class lounge opposite (though upstairs from) Gate 2 at Hong Kong airport. I was disappointed and its very average. I understand the new interior is sleek and modern but when you look beyond that there's not much below the service. No snacks unless you go into the Haven for some crusty buffet food and waited several minutes for a shower attendant to appear and when she did she screeched something at me in Cantonese from the end of a hallway gesturing to a refurbished (though standard) shower you would find in any lounge. Aside from the furnishings I would suggest the Business Lounge next door offers more and certainly the QF First Lounge in Sydney or the BA First Lounge at LHR T5 are far superior. All in all what a disappointing effort from Cathay.

Quite comfortable but generally the size of the lounge is too small and feels a bit crowded and hot. Good wifi connection but not too many food choices available. Staff friendly and very nice. The lounge is located near the gates and flight information is provided which is convenient to passengers.

I heard HK CX first lounge has been renovated but was disappointed. It was still under renovation Entrance staff at ground floor was rude particular the male staff. They treated different passenger differently as well. If you could stay there for a while observing the differences between passengers you will understand where I am coming from. Depends on the time you might be lucky to find a seat. Food at noodle bar is terrible I had some fried dumplings - it was not really cooked some parts still raw. Very limited food option tired staff working at lounge. It cannot compare with QF first lounge in Sydney not even match QF business lounge. Poor service poor quality of food limited space what else left with this lounge?

Floor to ceiling windows with a view of the apron and runaway and choice of food was excellent this included a buffer style English breakfast with some Singapore noodles but we opted to have some made to order soup noodles - superb. There were other snack and dessert items and a good choice of soft drinks. I had a raspberry juice which was just divine. If you are a One World Emerald member I seriously recommend this lounge at LHR T3.

Cathay Wing Lounge across from gate 2. Nice friendly welcome when entering the lounge. Short escalator ride that opens into a very airy setting with multiple seats and hostess around. Ample refreshments snacks and actual meals. Hot tasty and abundant. Lounge is located within easy reach of of Cathay's gates in that area. Plenty of space to work WIFI easy to access. One of the best features is the noodle bar. It is located on the opposite side of the entrance. 5 Choices and great. If you have a chance to try it -you will be very surprised and glad you took the time!

The newest lounge is quite impressive. Fantastic staff (waiting & counter staff) and a great selection of food. The solus chairs were also enjoyable as they allowed me to work and be comfortable at the same time. The waiting staff were employees of The Peninsula Hotel and made for a great experience.

The staff here are friendly; the lounge is comfortable with excellent food. The noodle bar is a must try. The lounge is becoming more congested which can make finding a seat difficult. My main gripe is the truly terrible wireless connection speed. It is now quicker to use my mobile's 3G service than the CX wireless. This has been getting steadily slower over time and now it is just not worth using.

I found this lounge quite good for a short stay. Comfortable seating not crowded and good food/drink options available. The smoothie of the day and fresh panini sandwiches were a treat. One downside were the small restroom facilities which could be a problem during peak hours.
Very ordinary. Feels like it is in the dungeons of the airport. Limited selection of food drinks. More entertainment available within the terminal.

Showers were good with nice extras. Did not find any computers would appear they only provide wifi. Asked for a cabana but told that's only available in the first section of The Wing. Overall quiet pretty spacious and well positioned.

I would agree that this lounge is often overcrowded and looks rather frayed now. Staff were friendly on my visit and quick to offer service. Table service good though food selection has lost its shine compared to a couple of years ago.

Cathay Pacific Lounges at HK International Airport used to be a benchmark but have lost their edge over past 2 years. Overcrowded with wear and tear generally showing throughout. Noodle bars in Business Class lounge or seated dining area okay if you can get a table. Most of the times better to grab a bite to eat outside and use the chairs available at the gates. Cathay needs to take care of premium customers better or accept losing clients.

Just a dreadful experience. The staff was discourteous rude. They ignored my plea for help to correct the wireless problems claiming they could not speak English or help me. It was as if I was troubling their time when I was flying first transpacific and waiting for another lengthy flight onward. The shower was clean if basic. The buffet food sub-par. The lounge looks unclean and tired and not worthy of first class.

Maybe it was the time I visited this lounge but there were so many passengers entering but not enough seats. After walking around for 10 minutes with my wife and daughter I was finally able to secure some seats. Granted the area around the seat had not been cleaned for a while which resulted in heaps of dirty plates and glasses. With seats secured I waited to see if anyone would clean up the plates/glasses. Someone did arrive 15 minutes later to clean it up. The lounge was chaotic around 1-30pm on a Saturday with way too many people and not enough seats. The noodle bar is always good but the sandwiches and other items were not as good. Good supply of drinks/ beverages. As another poster stated the lounge is really showing wear and tear. It is sad because this lounge and The Pier are the barometer for all other Cathay Pacific lounges. Another gripe I had was the elevator that connects the lounge to the departure gates way too small and slow. If I was in a rush I probably would have missed my flight despite it only being 7 minutes away at Gate 21. It may be better to grab a bite to eat outside and enjoy the spacious seats at the gates if the lounge continues to be way it was when I visited.

A little dated and old despite the newness of the Airport. Friendly welcoming staff not bad choice of drinks and food. None of the electric sockets worked where I was seated. Not too crowded. Internet and computers available for public use.

Friendly efficient staff compliment a large open plan lounge the looks out over the airport. There is a great little restaurant style noodle bar with a selection of Chinese food but watch out if you are looking for more western cuisine as it is lacking. So to is the selection of drinks which seems to have shrunk in recent years possibly due to cut backs. There is a large room with multiple PC terminals for good reliable internet surfing. Wi-Fi is free and up to par with speed and reliability. Restrooms and Shower cubicles are small and showing a little wear and tear as the years go by. However they are clean!
