Overall this is a great lounge but slowly starting to show some of its age.

The lounge was small compared to other Cathay lounges I have been at. There was the ever constant noodle bar serving up good food. They had two types of sandwiches (vegetarian and w/ meat) and they had cake + chinese dim sum. Good varieties of drinks including premium liquor and soft drinks. The lounge itself does not compare to the Wing or Pier lounges in HK but for Taipei it provides a nice oasis for travelers to eat and drink prior to their flight. It is a better alternative to the lacklustre duty free that is provided at Taoyuan airport. If there try the beef noodles in soup and not the spicy peanut sauce based noodles. There was free wifi and it was fast as well. Overall a very nice place to spend an hour or two before one's flight.

Haven't been to this lounge since before the renovations but what a difference. Great layout with a combination of lounge seating bar and workstations along the lines of other CX lounges and plenty of filtered light. Good food drink and reading material selections.

As a Diamond Frequent Flyer I enjoy this lounge quite regularly. And regularly experience the comfort excellent service wonderful showers fantastic staff great catering and the WOEFUL internet connection. Which drops out regularly. It seems three wireless services are available but they seem to drop out randomly without rhyme or reason. Even while typing this the connection failed twice. Not good enough Cathay Pacific.

Have to say I was rather disappointed with this flagship lounge for Cathay. It seems to have a rather worn appearance the seats were quite tatty and dirty same for carpet areas and staff service was cold at very best. Nicest staff was the lady cleaning the shower rooms! Did not get to use the cabanas this time but found the shower-rooms rather cramped and dull for a first class facility in Asia. Had a snack in the dining room area and whilst it was quite good again I found the staff to be quite offhand and poor. Had problems with wifi but probably my fault and not that of the lounge service here.

Large lounge. Reasonably comfortable with ample seating some overlooking the aircraft apron. Many Internet stations in good working condition. Well-stocked with snacks and drinks including Dim Sum and wine. Good selection of magazines and newspapers. Two shower rooms and a few toilet cubicles all in sparkling condition. The lounge is not enclosed but sits open-air one level above the general departure area accessible by escalator and lift.

Not much has changed since my last visit to this lounge. Seats were old and dirty. Food selection was mediocre at best. The redeeming quality of this lounge is the attentiveness and willingness of the staff to help the guests.
Cathay Pacific really underestimated the frequency of the shower room. It's always more than an hour waiting while I only have 2 hours transit time.
The lounge is disproportionately small in relation to the number of travelers it accommodates, which is its primary downside. Apart from this matter the lounge is fine.
An upgrade over the last lounge which was bad. However, this new lounge is crowded, hot and still dirty. Food selection is poor quality and no coffee machine is working at breakfast.

The Cloud 9 (business) lounge is hard to find using the signs – it’s opposite Gate A13 – but is large with lots of seats. There were two self-service food areas and although it was relatively full there was no problem in finding either a comfortable armchair or a seat with a table. Wi-Fi access was quick and simple and the selection of food was more than adequate. The lounge had well placed floor panels which, when opened up, revealed a UK-style socket and two USB charging points. There was a sleeping area and a smoking room. The toilets were kept immaculately clean.

Ethiopian Airlines lounge in Addis Ababa is nowhere near the level of other Star Alliance airline lounges. It is shabby, overcrowded, uncomfortable, and the bathrooms have few facilities and no showers. The internet is slow and the staff are so busy that they rarely smile. I have enjoyed my flights on Ethiopian Airlines. But the minute one hits Addis Ababa Airport and the Ethiopian Airlines lounge, everything falls apart. It is to be avoided.

I thought that this lounge was almost as good as the Thai Airways first class lounge, just with more people. The entrance made the lounge seem rather dingy, and the choice of font for the lounge entrance was not exactly that welcoming. The overall design of the lounge is weird. I get that Ethiopian seems to have three colour schemes, red, yellow and green corresponding to their logo, and this lounge was no exception. It had bright red and bright yellow sofas which were enough for the large banked capacity. They also had tables in front of them rather than the usual in between solo couches. The food selection here was something else. I was surprised by the eggs which are cooked in front of you, the unique coffee experience and the large array of food arranged in a restaurant-style buffet. These were incredible. Too bad the food on board is also as good, and I ate a bit too much! I would say that this lounge shone with the offering, but lacks the contemporary design modern lounges have.  This lounge is not perfect, not the best, but definitely the most unique lounge experience I have ever had before. Would gladly visit again.

On transit between my flight from Luanda I had to wait in ADD Ethiopian lounge. Expected the standard you have with regular 4 star airlines I was very disappointed. Food was good and traditional coffee services is excellent but except that services is more than poor. Newspaper limited. Design and comfort horrible.  Nobody can expect such lounge for a 4 stars airlines!
Ethiopian Airlines use the SAA Business Class lounge here. Very pleasant lounge, staff very friendly, good healthy food, nice drinks. And nice views over the tarmac!

Surprisingly nice lounge, extremely large, especially in view of number of flights in Abidjan, but nice decoration and artworks from local artists, good choice of food and beverages (no self-service). Wifi good, without password

Lounge was very crowded when we arrived in the early morning. Still relatively comfortable lounge seats were available. Especially considering the high occupancy, the lounge was pleasant. At the buffet, good food was regularly replenished by very attentive staff. Coffee etc. was excellent (espresso type but also the famous Ethiopian coffee made on request from fresh coffee beans). The bar was open but not interesting to me at this time of the day. The usual selection of newspapers was offered. Internet was rather on the slow side. Washrooms decent and clean.

Watch out which terminal you are leaving from in Addis Ababa. Where T2 is decent and clean, the old Terminal 1 is a disgrace. It is reminiscent of a 1960s third-world market in the worst possible sense. This includes the business class lounge, which on our last visit in June was simply insufferable. One male toilet, flooded with water to about ankle high. Some plastic soft drink bottles and a cheap whiskey on a (plastic) table in the middle of the room, to be “enjoyed” in disposable plastic cups. The lounge was packed with people; finding a place to sit was a challenge. Nobody touched unidentifiable hot food in the corner, which had already developed a skin on top. Apart from the receptionist at the door, no staff was to be seen.

I believe this was the only lounge in Mombasa airport. I was able to use ith with my Ethiopian Airlines Business class ticket. Its not comparable to a European or international lounge but I was happy to get into an airconditioned room, because early afternoon at Mombasa airport is not a very pleasant experience. There is basic stuff like drinks and some sandwiches. I believe I was only able to connect to the internet for 15 min.

There are two Ethiopian Airlines Cloud 9 lounges available for travelers to use. One for Star Alliance Gold and above members was the one that I used. The other is for the business class passengers. I went in to the lounge around 7:00am, it was already crowded. The cleanliness needs to be improved and maybe there were too many users but the quality of food wasn't satisfactory and even though the food stall was empty staff members of ET didn't seem to care to refill them quickly. The floor was dirty and the bathroom was dirty. Overall, I would not recommend to use the lounge if it is possible.

A large, well maintained lounge. There appears to be two lounges  in Addis Ababa- this was Lounge 2 - and though very busy, it was comfortable and clean. A good selection of hot and cold dishes were available as well as alcohol at the bar. Wifi was fast. The toilets were regularly cleaned, and were adequate. Staff were all friendly and helpful.
Packed and only mediocre service and food. Actually there is a better service and atmosphere outside in the ordinary restaurant and sitting in the main airport departure hall.

Welcome is sometimes friendly but not always. Nice view of airport apron. Plenty of drinks served at bar but this can create a queue of waiting customers. Food choice not great. Wifi works well and showers and toilets available. This place is still better then just waiting in airport bar before boarding your plane.

Same feeling and look as rest of this airport. Old scrummy over crowded lounge. Bad seating and poorly working wifi. Dirty toilets have not noticed if they have showers. Food quality average and drinks serve your self to the plastic cups. Tasteless coffee and this for a country growing it own and having a coffee culture. Entering the lounge one of these other things that should be taken care of as verry messy. All be it still better to stay in this lounge and drink lousy coffee for free then having to pay 6 usd cash only for a very poor espresso in airport coffee shop.

Lounge has been remade and upgraded ab 6 months ago. Lounge looks already now as if needs another remake. Food and drinks same as before, nothing special to even very boring, end of very poor quality. Food display also with no concern of hygiene. Reception in lounge professional and fast if no passenger in front of you negotiating the price he has to pay or points he has the submit on one of his credit cards to be able to enter the lounge.

The lounge is easy to find. When you come up from the arrivals to the second floor there is a big sign advertising Cloud Nine. Staff friendly and make announcements for departing flights. Wifi connection worked fine once you get the password. There is a paucity of magazines. This lounge main problem is overcrowding and cleanliness of the bathrooms. There is water all over the bathroom floor and unlike EBB's Karibuni Lounge there did not appear to be an attendant who would clean and/or mop the bathrooms at regular intervals. Didn't try the food so no comment. The lounge has an open ceiling so one can hear all the commotion and noise from the main terminal building. I thought lounges are supposed to be oasis of calm. Despite all its faults the lounge is a better alternative than using facilities in the terminal building.

Old seats from many years ago. Food choice ok all served on disposable plates with plastic knives and forks. Drinks - beer soft drinks and coffee. Lounge has no wifi one tv and is not really clean but better then having no lounge access. Lounge should improve even if it was only by providing free wifi.

Severely overcrowded: not a seat to be had. Apparently a flight to China was leaving about the same time as that to Washington DC as most of the people in the lounge were Chinese. Drinks and food good with a variety of western and Ethiopian dishes. Only three computers always busy.

Shocking in about every aspect. First of all difficult to find as no signs (it's their hub and both the airport and the airline have the same owner: the Ethiopian government!). Then once found terribly disappointing : no welcome from the staff (they pull faces to everybody entering not very comfortable very mediocre food & wine wifi working but weak and slow. Mind you it is in line with the bad experience in the business class cabin after.

Nice small lounge. I do not know if showers are available . Wifi works fine once you received the password magazines are available all be it not a very large or interesting selection . Booz as much as you want. Food choice interesting and surprising freshly prepacked sushi and salads . Warm soup as a toaster to use your self. Many different kind of instant noodles and some of the other regular stuff. Decent place not perfect but will do.

Lounge was overcrowded; food offerings were poor and looked as though they had been there for a while. There is a lack of seating in the lounge at peak times and for some reason ET have decided to make the lounge nearest the gates a frequent flyer lounge and reserve the rear lounge for business passengers. No signage was given only an abrupt 'no you go to the other lounge'.

This is a shared business lounge for most airlines in Dar Es Salaam overall on par with other medium-sized African airports. Large comfortable chairs. Food and drink on par with what you would buy in airport chains. Internet was terrible. Both the Wifi and available computers are so slow many machines will think the internet isn't working. If you can avoid flying through DAR I would : the airport overall is pretty bad.

Large lounge that cannot cope with the volumes of passengers in the mornings. Food offerings included waffles and toasted sandwiches. The food did not look too fresh. Beer soft drinks and spirits on offer. Free wifi. Not enough power points. Toilets were dirty. Not great for a flagship lounge.

Cloud Nine lounge in Addis (Terminal 2) is spacious and excellent food: hot dishes can be dried out which is a big pity. Fresh fruit buffet snacks were so and so. Cake sections impressive. Drinks sufficient. Coffee and tea was excellent. As usual WiFi not working. Very very slow desktops may give you a lifeline to check email but people are at times queuing up to get a seat as there are maximum of 3 computers available. Only 4 power sockets for a lounge to 250 people is very insufficient. Furniture dark heavy and carpets could need a brush up. Toilets are small and insufficient. No shower. The analogue lounge in Terminal is much smaller food and drinks options are much less and no internet. Only one WC. Messy and completely uninteresting better stay outside.
Basic shared lounge for a number of airlines. Dial up but free internet slow but better than nothing. Food basic but fine and drink selection OK. Simple overall but better than nothing.

This Lounge for Cloud Nine Passenger of Ethiopian Airlines is not very big but comfortable. Good array of Ethiopian Food. Poor selection of Drinks. Toilets are very dirty comparable to a Railway Station. Staff service very poor.

The lounge located next to the A gates on the second floor. You should pass the (stinky) smoking area and a few steps after is the entrance. This lounge is dedicated to El Al only and part of the King David lounge you will find in some countries like JFK, Tel Aviv etc. When you enter the lounge the 80' hits you big time! It's like a call from the past. The furniture is the old version of the Tel Aviv old Kind David and have seen better days. The design is like a big mistake, no showers, slow WIFI. The food is totally uneatable, poor, and old as the look of the lounge. "Kibuts" from the 80' offer better meal and better look. Overall – one of the poorest lounge I've seen.

Nice and basic lounge at the second floor of the B terminal. Serve mostly US, Israel and Golf airline The food is very very basic, same as the drinks. They have two showers in case its needed and the shower kit is nice. This lounge has kind of refurbishment during 2017 so this is much better than in the past but again- still very basic

Located at the 2nd floor of the airport. If you fly international out of the EU you still need to go through passport control on the 1st floor. I was here about a year ago and this lounge had a nice refurbishment, its big enough, lots of seats and nice catering. They have variety of food - salads , risotto, pasta, pizza, sandwiches, fruits and drinks - hot and cold. Overall good place to spend before the flight with a nice view on the runway.

Old and basic. Located at the end of A gate. Basic food like a few cakes. Small sandwiches with meat and cheese. Automatic Coffee machine branded Nescafé and very basic tea options. The place is clean and no additional staff team are located in the lounge.

Mediocre like everything else on El Al. The lounge is okay but kind of run down. The food is okay but not great. The staff is polite but not welcoming.  The bottom line is that I would never pay to use the El Al lounge at either JFK or TLV. If the ticket is free then go ahead.

Clean and spacious lounge with a very large food selection. Furthermore shower facilities (not used by me) and even spa facilities (again - not used by me). Computer terminals good view onto the tarmac. Lounge has a large number of El Al staff members on duty which are all eager to help. Much better then the Dan lounge which is used by other airlines in Tel Aviv.

The new Terminal 3 has a large well-appointed King David Lounge in addition to the tired and overcrowded Dan Lounge. (Anybody with a gold credit card can get access to the Dan lounge - regardless of service class.) King David access is restricted to El Al passengers in business class (there is a separate First Class lounge I cannot vouch for) or to members of the King David Club (El Al's upper-tier frequent flyer program also available for an annual fee). I have a King David pass from work and use the lounge whenever I fly out. It is located at the beginning of the "D" concourse to your left - the four concourses are four compass points on the central atrium. There is good food available in the Mediterranean style (kosher dairy and parve) - as well as cakes espresso machines soft drinks. Many seats have power outlets next to them (make sure you have a Euro/Israeli 2-prong plug or adapter) as well as Ethernet ports. There's an upstairs deck if it's too crowded downstairs which also offers workstations with PCs (in case you didn't bring your own laptop) as well as a branch of Carmel Forest Spa (no experience cannot comment). There is also a business center downstairs as well as a service desk. Design is pretty nifty. I haven't seen a huge selection of alcoholic beverages but I'm not much of a drinker so it doesn't bother me. Coffee is as good as can be expected from automated espresso machines.

Dan Lounge is the ONLY lounge at Ben Gurion Airport in Tel Aviv regardless of carrier! The lounge is always packed and with Israeli backpackers and whole extended families that are clearly not traveling in First or Business Class! I think they have some kind of deal with a credit card company or something which allows easy access to the airports ONLY lounge. It only has two toilet cubicles that are unisex and one was out of order so men women and children all had to line up to use the one cubicle! The cold food and beverage table seemed more like a school lunch line with children and youth grabbing things and small children playing with the espresso machine. Last but not least airport staff and airline maintenance and ground crew come through to grab food and drinks laid out for the passengers. I witnessed an aircraft maintenance guy come through a back door and with his clearly dirty fingers and overalls finger several pieces of cake till he found one in the middle he liked stuffed it in his mouth leaving the others aside and walked out the same way he came in! Ben Gurion need to open several lounges to meet the need of its passengers and levels and status. Truly the worst airport lounge I've been in. Really disappointing since the new terminal 3 is so nice!

The check-in staff at Cairo are extremely friendly and efficient but my business class lounge experience borders on embarrassing. I found myself in the Alioth Lounge. Bright lighting with dated furniture. I didn't find anything enticing to eat.

I am waiting for my international flight in one of the Egypt Air lounges in terminal 3. One would expect that at this airline's home base there would be good lounges or at least one. That does not appear to be the case. The food selection is poor. There are a couple of hot dishes, some overcooked vegetables and a meat of some sort. The sandwiches look like the ones I have had on my internal flights, dry and unappealing. There are no showers and the washroom is rather small, although efforts are being made to keep it clean. No newspapers or magazines and a couple of televisions with Egyptian news. The internet connection seems to be quite weak. Of course, this being Egypt no alcoholic beverages are offered, although this is not the greatest failing. All in all a disappointment.

A make-shift lounge that was put together as the regular lounges (for some odd reason have closed). Very little seating, a small fridge with water, cold drinks and stale sandwiches, three empty bain-maries and that's it. I would be extremely upset had I used my own money to get in. Thankfully it has Wi-Fi and a decent coffee machine. Still very far off the mark for a paid airport lounge.

This lounge is the newest in Cairo airport, having only opened this year after closing for renovation. It feels new, and there’s no smell of fresh paint, so it is clear that this lounge is ready to handle passengers. It is split into two sections. There are food corners at the end of each section. Unfortunately the food offered can only be described as lukewarm and the sandwiches weren’t that appealing. There were a selection of cold drinks but no ice, no alcohol as egyptair is a dry airline. The WiFi was nonexistent but I had a data pack so luckily I didn’t need to use it. The one small positive thing I would point out about this lounge is the fact that their bathroom stalls are large enough to keep your carryons inside with you so then you don’t risk somebody going through your stuff. It is a decent improvement from the older lounges, however it is still not of the same quality, even compared to the likes of Lufthansa. I would probably choose to visit again as there isn’t a better option.

Egyptair use the Turkish Airlines Lounge at IAD. Nice selection of food, free and fast WiFi and friendly staff. There are lockers where you can leave your bag for long layovers and TVs showing news/sports Seats are not very comfortable

Unfortunately it’s a very disappointing experience, very poor lounge, lacking the basics. I have traveled many times to different countries and it’s sad to say that my country’s airline lounge is not qualified at all. No food variety, the food itself is poor, washrooms are not clean enough, seats are not comfortable. No entertainment for kids not even a small space and seriously one TV in the whole lounge. It needs a massive renovation to be a lounge

United Airlines lounge is very spacious, clean comfortable lounge. Wifi is good, plenty of sockets to charge devices around. Food selection pretty limited with pathetically small plates to serve yourself (like espresso cup plates). Nice views of the runway and very tidy well equipped showers.

Not much to say about this lounge apart from the fact that it needs a massive renovation. It was disappointing how dirty the toilets were for an airport let alone the business lounge lounge. Food option limited and very dirty and tired overall.

Fantastic lounge. Plenty of seating space. Very clean with sufficient washroom facilities. Buffet food offering was extensive, and includes a full a la carte menu offering. Friendly and attentive service. A relaxing space to enjoy before the flight from Dubai to Cairo. Use my own mobile for internet service, so can't rate the lounge's connection speed.

I visited this lounge during my trip from Cairo to Warsaw via Zurich. Lounge is located in the middle of terminal very close to gate from I was flying from. This lounge is open 24/7. I was there between 0:00-2:00 AM, so choose of food and beverages was quite poor, but if there was missing something stuff supplement on a regular basis. Normal internet connection didn't work for me, but stuff helped me connect to another network which work very fast. Seat was very comfortable, with table and power outlet with easy access. Lounge team was very helpful.

Dirty bathrooms, unpolite people at the entrace, wi-fi that works 10% of the time, food that has not been changed for a long time, extremely cold, a nightmare to spend time in. The only nice thing are the people working inside, that kindly serve you coffee and drinks.

On the main terminal of Cairo airport there are scattered 3 or 4 Egyptair Business class lounges. I suppose that all provide the same service but this is not really truth. I visited all of them and I found the best which is located in concourse F. All others were overcrowded and filthy and the one in concourse F was almost empty. Maybe this can be explained because concourse F is used for the long haul flights, so it was less crowded. Staff kept it clean collecting all empty dishes and all trash left from passengers. On top of this there was a male and I think a female servant, very polite ready to bring you anything, so there was no need to visit the bar for a coffee or some water. Wifi was operating smoothly. There were some sandwiches but I could understand what exactly they were and some stew beef with vegetables and rice, which was tasty but very hard to chew. There was a selection of juices and colas and that is all. Egyptair is a dry airline that means there is not any wine, beer or liquors. Toilets were not is good shape and they were dirty too. I think there was a lady taking care of the toilets, however the specific lady was watching tv and I search the drawers by myself to find toilet paper. Sinks were very dirty and I hesitated twice before washing my hands

On entry near gate F1 there is a sign which clearly states 'Smoking Permitted Lounge'. In essence that doesn't mean there is a smoking area. It means there is no area for the non-smokers. So with 2 hrs to boarding it was going to be touch and go if I would escape alive. If I do for sure my clothes are going to be reeking for the next 3 or 4 days, so a visit to the dry cleaners will be in order. I am tolerant wherever I travel but I am going to be struggling not to cough my guts up with passive smoke inhalation. Very ordinary unhealthy food on offer too. I really should just walk out and find a quiet non polluted area.

Arrived to airport by 6 am, my flight was by 9am. I was directed to Royal lounge by check in staff. Reach to the lounge downstairs, we found it closed and the staff said we open by 7am! This is ridiculous. Back again to information desk, he recommend other lounge far away from the gate. Lounge was too cold, food is not good. Very poor welcome from the staff at reception. I think Egyptair should wake up to the condition of business class lounge and send staff for more training on how to welcome customers.

The lounge was dirty there was a very cool unwelcoming reception from the female at the desk who was extremely unhelpful. The quality of the food and drinks available was pitiful. All in all a really bad experience and Egyptair should wake up very quickly and rectify the problem quickly.

Upgraded to business class because I had a 7 hour stopover in Cairo before travelling to Manchester England. I expected a reasonable comfortable stay. How wrong I was! The seating was extremely uncomfortable and not too clean the food and drinks on offer were at best mediocre. The lounge was air conditioned and thus cold. I never removed my outdoor coat and was still really cold. I feel I wasted money upgrading for something I didn't get. The flights were good but the stay in the lounge abysmal.

Don't expect anything special in Cairo with the exception of staff and their service. For the smokers they have a dedicated lounge. Type of food and drinks are limited and there are very few television screens to watch the news or sports.

Convenient and spacious. Helpful staff. Limited food and drinks but pleasant. Although fairly new starting to look jaded. Chairs grubby walls and toilet areas dirtier than they should be. Isn't going to wear well unless upgraded and deep cleaned.

We used these lounges twice there are four of them with different names but all essentially the same. There is no alcohol (there is none on any Egyptair flights as well). Food/juices are okay nothing phenomenal. Bathrooms were clean though no showers or anything. Check-in on the main concourse for the First/Business class area has lounge-like furniture coffee table and WiFi access.

Smallish lounge but quite comfortable. Excellent free wifi. No alcohol but nice range of soft drinks and juices. Only negative was no showers. I asked at the desk when I entered and they told me there are no showers in the whole airport. That should be remedied.

This lounge is in the newly opened T3 at Cairo Airport. It was dirty and staffed by bored surly individuals. The drink offerings were minimal and food was a choice of dried up croissants or mini pizzas. The irony is that the open eating areas at this airport are now really good. How does Egyptair manage to retain its Star Alliance membership? Take my advice at Cairo avoid the lounge and enjoy some good food in the public eating areas.

Used the new Star Alliance/Egyptair business lounge at Cairo airport terminal 3. Very disappointing. All the newspapers were in Arabic and no magazines. Warm soft drinks stacked on a table and loud children everywhere. There are two rooms one with a nice view of the runways that was jam packed and another which is rather grim that was also pretty full. The floors are tile and echo sounds horribly. Some sandwiches and finger foods and a kettle with hot water. No television or flight monitors in room number two. The staff were indifferent and uninterested in the passengers. Frankly waiting in the main terminal in the food court area offered more options for food/beverages and was just as comfortable as the lounge. Disappointing and not much of an improvement over the old dismal terminal 2 business lounge.

The choice of food for our three hour time here was between mini pizzas and croissants which you could then warm up in a none too clean microwave. Choice of drinks was also very limited - we nabbed the last three cans of diet coke in the lounge. Coffee was instant and made with lukewarm water from a flask by a member of staff. Egyptair is a dry airline and so is its lounge. This lounge in terminal one is situated on a balcony but otherwise open to the rest of the airport so noise and so forth a problem. Seating was reasonably comfortable but old and worn. Staff were chatting to themselves except for the toilet attendants who were intent on making you pay for the privilege of using the loos.

Nothing in appearance has changed since my last visit six months ago, except for a model of the A380 at the entrance. The staff are welcoming and prompt me to order some drinks and food. It was nice to begin the evening at the bar, being served champagne and warm cashews. The lounge features an elegant restaurant-style dining area with table service, offering a menu that showcases an enticing selection of dishes. Hard to resist. Yet as mine was a night departure to Abu Dhabi, I wasn't keen on having a full meal, as I expected dinner during the flight. Deciding to help myself to a light snack, I moved to settle in a quiet corner, where I was served coffee a couple of times. The staff are also attentive, making sure the place is tidy and leftovers are cleared promptly. Although not a large lounge, it never gets crowded, as at most it will accommodate just premium passengers per flight. So there is plenty of seating options and even a few quiet spots. I also like the decor, with ark oak panelling and pretty ornamental objects placed in them. It was another enjoyable time spent here before my short walk to the boarding gate.

On my flights to Asia, I deliberately break my journey in Abu Dhabi to refresh and relax before the next connecting flight. I have visited this huge 3-storey lounge several times, and have always enjoyed my stay. The staff are polite, friendly and accommodating. The plethora of seating areas means that even when busy, you can find cosy spots to relax and have some privacy. And on long layovers, having a private relaxation room for a few hours to get some sleep is a bonus. All floors have a view of the apron, and from the ground floor, you can also watch aircraft taking off. For hungry souls, the food choices are Middle Eastern, Asian and Western. The selection may not be extensive, nevertheless appetising. The main dining room is self-service. And there is also a chef who will prepare a selection of dishes to your liking, while on the third floor, the dining area is a buffet. What always impresses me is also the presentation of food. There are tea & coffee stations on all floors and snacks you can help yourself to. And of course, the fabulous Constellation Bar, serving champagne and cocktails, is a treat.

A first-class venue without a first-class experience. I am rarely impressed by non-airline lounges, as they lack the ambiance of an airlines own lounges. However, many carriers do not have their own lounges at all airports and Plaza Premium Lounges are a popular choice around the world. On my Etihad flight to Abu Dhabi, at the check-in desk, I was informed that I was eligible for the Plaza Premium First near Gate 1, and given directions. At the entrance, I was rewarded with a friendly welcome. At first glance, the view looked attractive with Christmas decorations and Poinsettia flowers. The place was, however, fairly busy and worse - noisy. It isn't a large venue, and although there are sections of different furnishings to choose from, there isn't any place for even the slightest of privacy or quietness. The focal point is the semicircular bar, which was well stocked with drinks and a small selection of cold cuts. And the friendly bar person kindly made an excellent gin-martini, and I managed to find a less crowded spot to settle down. There is a separate dining area with a selection of hot food. However, it was a dull, uninviting place. I guess I was unlucky to be there during a busy period. And I am sure it would have been a more pleasurable and relaxing experience had it not been so noisy. Nevertheless, I did enjoy a couple of drinks and a snack, and a little disappointed before moving on. To refer to it as a 'first class' lounge in my opinion is a gross exaggeration.

A very spacious lounge with three floors. The seat were comfortable. The pasta station offers a great variety of options. There were plenty of drinks. The shower was clean and well maintained but could be in shortage during peak hours.

Flying with Etihad from Singapore to Abu Dhabi, I visited the Ambassador Transit Lounge at Terminal 2. It's a pay lounge, but as a Business Class passenger, I could use it for free. It's a compact lounge, with a few choices of seating, and a small outdoor area designated mainly for smokers, and with a view of the apron. Although not crowded when I arrived, it was quite noisy, and there was no chance of a quiet relaxation time. The moment I entered, the staff were enthusiastic to point me in the direction of food and drink and informed that shower facilities are available. The shower room was very basic, just a towel, shampoo and body wash. However, I glanced at the food and drink available. At first sight, the choice was meagre and some buffet items just did not look appetising. However, there is a small cooking station, and I was treated to a very tasty noodle soup. On the beverages front, the usual soft drinks and coffees are self-service. There was a very small selection of spirits,  The overall ambiance of the lounge at first feels good, but the layout does not afford enough space for a quiet time. It is designed for a short stay and is not my choice for a relaxing time before a flight. The food display was also rather 'cheap' looking. If I had to pay to visit this lounge, expecting a touch of extravagance, I would be very disappointed. But I would give it the thumbs up for the pleasant and attentive staff.

Etihad's Business Lounge at the new Terminal A will impress. Taking up three floors, and covering a vast area, it has an extensive variety of seating, relaxing areas and dining options. Located near the C Gates, it has access to a few gates directly from the lounge. I had an extra long layover before my flight to Osaka, and upon welcoming me to the lounge, I was told I could have a private Relaxation Room available within half an hour. In the meantime, I was able to store my hand luggage and free to wander about. After momentarily exploring the floors via escalators, I was offered a room at the time allocated. It's modest, to say the least, with a single bed, pillow and blanket. As I had landed late at night, it was a welcome treat to get some proper sleep, which I did for about four hours. Waking up very early morning, following a shower and refreshed, I decided to explore each floor. It was eerily quiet, with a few other passengers wandering about like me. I kept bumping into very friendly staff greeting me and advising me of the various areas to relax and have some food and drink. On the ground floor alone, is an extensive dining area with bars, drinks and coffee stations, and at the 'live' kitchen a chef cooked breakfast for me. There are multiple self-service snack bars, tea and coffee stations, spread across all floors. While there was a good selection of International food items and cold buffets, the choice of hot food was disappointing. I have been in much smaller lounges that have more hot food dishes. The Constellation Bar on the third floor, is both stylish and attractive, with a backlit display of alcoholic bottles. The barmen will make a cocktail or mocktail at your request and even adjust measures to suit your liking. And naturally, at busy times this is the most popular area occupied by guests. There's a fair bit of walking to do, as the lounge is huge. The colour schemes and decor are varied, with different styles of furnishings, and make you feel you can enjoy different parts of the lounge. There's a large Family Room, Games Room, Prayer Room, as well as a Smoking Room. Then there's the huge lengthy glass panelling, giving views of the apron as well as sightings of aircraft. It was nice to sit by and watch the sunrise as the very first flights of the day took off. By lunch time however, the main bar and food stations began to get busy. Yet there were plenty of areas to choose to relax and call your own little space. This is one of the best lounges I have visited. And if you have a long layover, it's a perfect place to relax and enjoy.

It's a lounge I have visited before, and it caters to both First and Business Class passengers, thus elevating the dining experience with an a la carte menu and restaurant-style atmosphere. The entrance area is rather modest but has a fairly large model of an A380 aircraft on display. The receptionist welcomed me and offered to help store my cabin baggage. I love the ambiance of this lounge, with soothing colours. As you enter, on the left is the bar with a good selection of premium brand spirits and wines. To your right are all the various seating areas. And it's quiet, it never got crowded. The staff were extremely accommodating and seem to enjoy taking care of you. All the basic facilities are available such as a variety of furnishings, showers, a children's playroom, and prayer room. As my flight was late afternoon, I had decided to have an early lunch. Browsing at the buffet area, all of which looked very appetizing, I decided to help myself instead of ordering from the menu. I tried the Chicken Biriyani as well as Shepherd's Pie - both very tasty. After another glass of bubbly and some coffee, I retreated to sit by a view of the apron although there was nothing much to see. It was only a few minutes walk to my boarding gate.

There are several Coral lounges at Bangkok Airport, and despite my voucher indicating where to go, it took me a while to locate the Coral 'Cosmo' Lounge. A smiling face welcomed me, and I entered a long narrow and quiet place. On the left side of the lounge were rows of seating with tables for dining, and on the right, were comfortable sofas for relaxing. One side of the length of the lounge is open to apron views but was marred by too many screens and metal framings outside. At the far end was a view of the boarding gate areas below. There are shower facilities and I was told even some sleep rooms, which I was not able to see for myself. The bar was small, with a few choices of drinks, but the food department looked very inviting. Sprays of small yellow Oncidium Orchids placed between sections added a decorative touch. The hot food (mainly Asian) was in colourful heavy pans, and the seafood curry and rice I had was delicious. I was there for nearly two hours, and no more than five persons were in the lounge. The barman said that the place rarely got busy, which also suited me fine, as I do not enjoy overcrowded lounges. A bonus was having a complimentary 15-minute neck, shoulder and arm massage, which really made me feel good and pampered. Do remember to generously tip the masseur. For those who wished to exercise, a gym room provided the necessary equipment. The flight information screen wasn't working properly, and as the WiFi connected well, I was able to keep track of my flight boarding notices. I enjoyed a tranquil time here, and the staff were pleasant and engaging.

Flying from London to Bangkok via Abu Dhabi involved a rather long layover, and Etihad's Business Class Lounge was a welcome and restful retreat. Arriving well past midnight, I was pleased to see how empty it was. Following a quick shower (the attendant ensuring it was spotlessly clean), I was able to relax and take in the atmosphere. Storing your hand luggage is a bonus, enabling you to move around easily, without having to haul your cabin baggage with you. Choosing where to settle down, meant many options. There were bright spacious seating areas, quiet dimly lit zones, as well as semi-private booths with your own TV to keep you company. The variety of comfortable seating was impressive. There was also a semi-partitioned work area with several computers and desk space. The restaurant-style dining sections are spacious. The fairly extensive bar features somewhere in the central part of the lounge and has a wide selection of drinks from premium brand spirits, wines, and champagne to soft drinks. Both barmen were engaging in short bursts of conversation while keeping the drinks flowing. The food choice was extensive. From Middle Eastern to Indian, and Western cuisine as well as finger food, there was no shortage of choice. Several coffee stations were spread around, and helping myself to several cappuccinos, and settling in a booth with TV was a good way to pass some time as well. However, large lounges also feel rather impersonal, unlike small cosy ones where the staff make you feel welcome and interact with you. On my second visit, when on route back to London, arriving late evening, the ambiance at the lounge was quite different and disappointing. It was noisy, overcrowded, with luggage strewn all over, and with little space to sit and relax. What spoiled it even more, was the behavior of many passengers. Several had removed their socks and shoes, stretched out on couches occupying three or more seat spaces and exposing their feet close to other passengers. Fortunately, my stay lasted just over an hour and I was glad to leave.

Flying to Abu Dhabi mid-afternoon, I had the opportunity to visit Etihad's First & Business Lounge at Heathrow Terminal 4. I was welcomed by staff who wished me a pleasant stay. As I paused by the bar, even without requesting, I was immediately offered a glass of Joseph Perrier champagne. As they noticed me taking photos, I was quickly approached by a staff member to hold on a bit longer, until they had laid out all the lunchtime food. The display was very appetizing, even though there wasn't a vast selection of hot items. Opposite was a proper dining room with table service. The staff were chatty and made me feel relaxed and comfortable. The lounge isn't particularly large. There are no vast views of aircraft taking off. There are several styles of furnishings, and areas designated for quieter moments, as well as a children's playroom. The decor is soothing, with some of Etihad's logo colours of dark brown, sepia and yellow ochre. Complimenting the design is also dark wood pannelling, decorated with ornaments and airline memorabilia. As I had plenty of time before my flight, I decided to have a tasty light lunch of Moutabbal salad and another salad. The staff kept enticing me to try more Middle Eastern cuisine, but I gently refused, as I knew lunch would also be served on the flight. Later at the bar, I was treated to a Manhattan cocktail, before going to the boarding gate. On leaving, the manager introduced himself and inquired how I rated my experience and wished me a pleasant flight.

Visiting this lounge did not encourage us to use it again. Although we are Silver members, we had to wait in a queue to enter the lounge, because of the many people paying to use the lounge. The lounge was crowded, with very limited seating inside: the atmosphere was like a student mensa, not offering the peace and quiet we were hoping for. Tea and coffee facilities were limited, with no milk available. Overall impression was dirty, noisy and crowded.

While the flight isn’t good like I said earlier. There is some positive and negative aspect of their Lounge in AUH. The lounge itself in Terminal 3 is good enough, sadly it’s still nowhere near as other airline lounges. However, the Terminal 1 lounge is more like a school canteen instead of a lounge. It’s crowded, nowhere to seat and the design is getting too old and terrible. The food and other facilities in Terminal 1 lounge is more awful than Terminal 3. The shower is small and you have to wait 30 minutes each and it’s unacceptable That 1 shower is out of order. (We have no issues at the Terminal 3 lounge and waiting for Shower just 5-10 minutes in T3 unlike T1). The drinks choices were ok in T3, but super limited in T1. My suggestion - Try to fly Etihad only if you fly out of Terminal 3 instead of Terminal 1 or avoid Etihad if there is no choice out of Terminal 3. I hope Etihad take note of their serious issues with their T1 lounge and improved it.

Overall the Miracle Lounge they use at Bangkok Airport was so disappointing. Food & beverage choice very limited. The standard of beverage selection was so cheap. Uncleaned , unattended tables all around which looked filthy. Have to improve it in all aspects.

Early this lounge is good but by 8am it too crowded & very noisy & hard pushed to find a seat as so many passengers flooding in here. The biggest letdown here is the complete lack of toilets as is abysmal that you have this many people in this lounge yet not enough toilets - terrible hence the toilets near to get 35 are a good option. The scrambled eggs are excellent along with the sausages & bacon. Bread was fresh especially toasted so it’s a plus point for the food & a good choice also for morning breakfast. But because of the noise in this lounge & lack of toilets I tend not to stay here now for very long as it’s been spoilt by overcrowding.

So now this is no longer a Etihad Exclusive lounge so obvious the airline is cost cutting & now Virgin Australia now share this lounge. So other airlines will soon follow which means this lounge will soon become overcrowded. The food on offer was very poor no snacks in the form of sandwiches, fresh bread, cakes, biscuits was on offer, no orange juice available & bottled water was scarce. WiFi kept disconnecting so kept in the airports WiFi which was better.

Shocking experience at this lounge. The quality of food has significantly dropped over the years. It is evident that Etihad's cost cutting is continuing, especially with the loss of the nail salon and six sense spa. I tried the food and it was so bad that I left it and went to McDonald's in the food court which tasted 10x better.

On my recent trip from Abu Dhabi to Istanbul I tried entering the lounge using my Velocity Gold card but was quickly informed that I could not enter because Velocity members only had access to the Al Reem lounge (run by Plaza Premium instead of Etihad). However, when I asked if I could pay for the lounge access to the Business class lounge as advertised on Etihad's website, I was advised that I couldn't even do that. It appears that the lounge staff at Etihad's business class lounge are not up to date with the Etihad's policies, which is disappointing and discouraging.

Terminal 3 Business class lounge has become totally inadequate as from 6am onwards is completely overcrowded & no longer a place to relax - no more exclusivity anymore imagine there toilets & showers are totally inadequate for the huge amount of passengers in this lounge. Staff do there best but they are over stretched with the amount of people packed into this lounge. I find myself staying less & less here now as other areas of this crowded airport are better to sit & relax near to a gate not being used. Be nice if you can only use the lounge if you had a business boarding pass only but those days are gone now with the frequent flyer program making it so easy to get into the lounge.. Food is still ok & enjoy the breakfast there. WiFi connection is not stable here still.
Nice airport lounge, large, quiet, good airfield new, a normal food and beverage choice, kids playing room. Nice sitting, near the 1 gate, not crowded. One of the best Russian lounges.

The worst thing about this lounge is the complete lack of toilets and the signage in this place is truly dreadful. It’s not a quiet place to relax and becomes very crowded quickly. It’s no longer a nice experience here due to no more exclusivity for genuine business class passengers sadly. Food is good along with a nice range of drinks from the bar. Let’s hope when the new airport opens the lounge will be better and have decent toilets and a lot more of them along with showers. Internet when I was there was very slow.

A relatively new lounge with good views of planes taking off & landing. Food is of good quality although not great in choices. The freshly baked rolls are delicious & recommended if they are hot. It’s a relaxing place to be with spacious areas giving it a relaxing ambiance before your flight. Staff are polite & professional & will help with any of your queries. Toilets well kept with all the needs you require. WiFi here was good & reliable with fast downloading of websites. Overall a very pleasant stay on my recent flight.

Early Morning this lounge is less busy than night time but gets busy around 8.30am onwards. The breakfast was excellent nicely made scrambled egg & tasty sausages. Seating is varied so a good choice where to sit when it’s not crowded. Staff seemed pleasant as they were not as busy as it can get like at night. The big thing that this lounge lacks completely is toilets is truly dreadful when as many as hundred or more people use this lounge at a time. It’s really wasting time have to queue to use a toilet & not acceptable for a business class lounge. WiFi is poor & kept disconnecting on the time I was there - let’s hope when the new airport opens that the business class lounge there has many more toilets & showers for passengers.

Absolutely mediocre lounge-while the seats were clean, the food/snacks were very limited in variety and looked unappetising. There were no sealed bottles of water on offer, unlike in any other lounge I have seen. No washrooms inside the lounge - the nearest washrooms were filthy and unusable. The wifi does not work. I am shocked that Etihad Airways has tied up with this lounge for its first and business class passengers in Zurich. It is not befitting the image of Etihad Airways.

I’ve been to this Al Reem lounge 4 times now and it is fantastic. I have the option to go to Etihad lounges but I find this to be better with good middle Eastern breakfast. The Homus and Foul Madamas are excellent. I walk from terminal 3 to terminal 1 just to go to this lounge. Well done.

Comparing this lounge to Qatar Airways Business Class Lounge, this Etihad lounge is nothing. May I suggest to put a quiet room or at least 4 rooms with bed, just in case they cannot accommodate all passengers in the hotel if there is any delay in a flight -  waiting for more than 5 hours just for a visa is giving more stress to your passengers. Staff are not that helpful at all.

The last time I was in this airport the business and first class lounge was one in the same and only separated by a seating area. The food was pretty poor and the whole experience was weird but I knew they were remodeling a new lounge area. This visit I was able to use the new space and found it vastly improved and what one would expect from an international first class lounge. The area was set up like a restaurant with prompt service and good food. If you wanted a snack and not a full meal trays of food were put out for the taking. Good coffee and juices. It was quiet and again very comfortable. The airport is going through a build out and once completed it will be hopefully a beautiful airport for gates and services. In the meantime the old terminals have to be suffered with.

This Etihad Airways lounge (used for Virgin Australia flight) has lackadaisical staff in the kitchen. I am told there are 3 chefs and yet there is a very small selection available. Food is at best insipid and you could sense it from the disinterested look on the staff's faces. I asked if they could get some snacks etc organized to which they responded in the negative. The Chef refused to come out of the kitchen. Compared to other airlines where you get a la carte menu served, this is a complete disappointment. They also ran out of the whisky they had on the shelf after serving just the one drink. Something doesn't add up. Sorry guys, thumbs down and I will avoid this lounge if I could.

A new lounge on level 3 and I found it very spacious, lots of natural light and great views of the runway if you liked planes landing and taking off. Food was hot and very tasty, I loved the crispy bread rolls. Staff here very polite, well trained and made you feel welcome. Wifi was quick and reliable with no disconnecting like other places I have been to. Toilets are small and could do with more as when this lounge gets busy you will end up queuing which for a business class lounge should not be the case. I would stay here again.

This lounge is wonderful. Take a pinch of Cathay's lounge, sprinkle it with some Qatar Airways London lounge class and stir in some Qantas Sydney - and you get Etihad first. The best waiters and waitresses, a tad retro, food like at a French top tabl. Even the shaves are great.  Make your transit in Abu Dhabi a stopover in this lounge!

The lounge has everything you need for a break between two flights and I was surprised about the offer and the conditions of the treatments you can get there. As a frequent flyer for Etihad partners I was able to bring an companion with me. The dinner was really 5* and the waiters first class. Very attentive and polite. I could use the cigar lounge after the great meal. The drinks offered are really high end and makes the time pass by so quickly. When returning I did use the shower facilities and together with the massage it made it a gorgeous experience. It was never crowded and it was designed with a lot of style. The only minus is that the menu doesn't change very often, so you have to stick to the 3-4 main dishes they have to offer.

Flying Etihad from Düsseldorf and being a frequent flyer means you end up at the Airberlin Lounge. Like with many of the Airberlin services, you get something bad and they try somehow to mask everything like it was a high quality product. If you live in Germany you recognize immediately the "snacks" which are products from the cheapest retailers, usually heated up in the microwave. The worst quality eggs (from battery chickens) and so on. And there is nothing to eat, only these high quality products. And being small, it is always full. Nobody seems to care about this. The seats, when not taken, are old and dirty. When flying inside the Schengen area you get to use another lounge which is better. It seems if it is not managed by Airberlin it could be good.

Left this Louis Tavern CIP lounge that Etihad Airways use within minutes of entering it and opted for another airline lounge which I able to access using my Credit Card using Lounge Key membership. Food was basic and limited with seating areas looking dull and uniform. The lounge lacked any sort of character and uninviting. I would hope Etihad would use another lounge or even open their own one in Bangkok Suvarnabhumi Airport.

Nice lounge with helpful staff and good quality food, but very overcrowded at peak times. We entered the lounge at 1am and it was full to maximum capacity, however one of the friendly staff members kindly found a table for us and offered to bring us soft drinks. Wifi speed is excellent.

A class above the old Air New Zealand lounge. Showers are good. Food selection limited with a limited menu and narrow buffet selection. Still, a "nice" place to chill while the airport is upgrading around them. The walk to the gate is a surprise as the plane looks close from the window. Overall a big improvement but still nothing compared to the lounge in Abu Dhabi which remains my favourite.

Was flying Jet Airways Business Class so eligible to use the Etihad Premium Lounge at Terminal 1. I entered the lounge just before 5pm on 19th January, and the reception staff seemed insincere. Certainly not a warm welcome. Evidence of cost cutting was apparent. The spa no longer offers complimentary mini treatments. The selection of drinks is not as it used to be. Worse still there was no buffet! I was told that this would be available from 5.30pm only, which was close to my boarding time. Completely unbelievable and unacceptable from a supposed premium, award winning airline in their home hub. Luckily I had access to the much nicer Plaza Premium Al Dhabi lounge where the staff were friendlier and there was a nice hot and cold buffet. So I left. I registered my disbelief on departure, but the staff really weren't interested.

Etihad Airways lounge at T3 Abu Dhabi is large and clean with plenty of seats, which are comfortable. However there are no quiet spots, as everywhere is near a bar or food station and staff are oblivious to endless clattering of plates and glasses!! It's not particularly elegant or interesting and TV's everywhere with nothing you can hear. I think every lounge needs quiet areas for those with long layovers or late flights, and more lounger type chairs to stretch out in. Food nothing special.

Quite a small lounge and it was really busy. We were flying Virgin Australia and there are two Virgin flights departing LAX within an hour of each other. There's only one shower which isn't enough given the size of the lounge. I've also been to their business class and first class lounge in Abu Dhabi and there aren't enough showers there either. Lounge was decorated nicely - they all look the same and it's pretty relaxing. Staff are attentive, they walk round asking if you want a refill/top up. Was well situated for our gate as well.

Good offering. The range of food was good, with Asian, Arabic and Western options. I especially liked the inclusion of Japanese sushi. The showers (lounge in Terminal 3) were incredible. The option of having your hair cut or beard trimmed was also quite a nice touch and was reasonably priced, e.g. AED 90 for a hair cut.

Plaza Premium Lounge is for most of the airlines. Though Jet Airways failed to provide the lounge despite of being Etihad Silver, used my Credit Card to gain access. Since it was early morning the lounge was empty. The lounge was spacious with different seating for short relaxation. live chef was available for egg variety. limited food option, but good enough. decent drinks option. the wifi was a downer as they dont have own wifi, but depend on tata free 30 mins wifi available in the airport. Good lounge for short transit.

I was flying business but they were doing some renovation, so the business/first class lounges were merged for the time I was there. The food was great, and you had access to a spa and business facilities. There were two types of guest attendants, some in a grey uniform who served the food and who were exceptional, and some in a coloured uniform who seemed to be there just to look good and not much else help. The flight was delayed due to fog, and when I asked them for information they were quite rude and seemed to spend most of the time chatting, gossiping amongst themselves.

This was the Premier Lounge in Terminal 3. The lounge is fairly large and could hold a few hundred passengers. I had a long 8 hour layover for my connection to LAX. The lounge was full at 1am when I arrived. I had to walk around looking for an empty seat before I found one. There are no reclining chairs or sofas. So it is not possible to sleep or even stretch anywhere. Food options were adequate though probably a bit limited for vegetarians. The wifi worked well. The most inconvenient aspect of the lounge is the toilet facilities or rather the lack of them. There are only two toilets at both ends of the lounge each toilet with a capacity of two! So there was long line to use them. Amazing to think how anybody could have designed a large lounge so poorly. At one stage I was thinking of leaving the lounge and using the public toilets at the terminal. Fortunately by around 3am there were many flight departures and the lounge emptied quickly. Breakfast buffet was ready by 5.30 and was good. Overall this lounge is only meant for a transit of 1-2 hours. Anything more could easily become a stressful affair during crowded periods.

This is a class setting first lounge for Etihad Airways. Newly opened in an old airport (Abu Dhabi) with wonderful staff, amenities and services. I took a massage for my headache. Food was exquisite. Decor is contemporary Arabic.

The Oryx lounge is the frequent flyer lounge serving other airlines than Qatar Airways. The range of food available was restricted, and it was almost overcrowded. Staff were great, and it was clean, but why let it slip? In such a fine airport other airlines should have better facilities. The best bet is to head for the quiet rooms. The games rooms are mostly empty too.

I left Beijing after a full day of work in the middle of the night without any sleep to Abu Dhabi. When I arrived to Abu Dhabi Airport after another 8 hours without sleep I felt seriously tired and decided to buy in into the Etihad Business Class Lounge because I had to spend 8 hours until my connecting flight was supposed to leave. I paid 145€ entrance fee for 6 hours stay and was really glad to have managed this. After a snack, which was not bad but far from being great, and a drink it did not take long and my eyes shut by itself and I fell asleep. I was surprised when I felt someone shaking my Body in order to wake me up. Even more surprised I was when the Lounge Supervisor told me "you are strongly advised not to sleep in this Lounge" unquote he even told me to sit upright. I was so tired and now I was not allowed to sleep, I could not believe it. For me the consequences are these: I will avoid this lounge and Abu Dhabi Airport whenever I can (just remembering the chaos they had in front of the security check where I waited one hour to get through) which means that Etihad will be not on my list of preferred Airlines any longer. In other Lounges they have even beds and showers where you can spend 8 hours in an Environment which really deserves the name Business Class Lounge (example Bangkok). I should add here that the receptionists were really friendly and helpful.

This London Heathrow lounge should be renamed the Jet Airways lounge as lately the buffet consists mainly of Indian food and on my last visit contained about 50% of the usual selection and was very thinly spread out. Also, before you would be offered a massage as soon as you arrived, but now they seem to avoid you. The icing on the cake was that there was no wi fi available all the time i was there, not even the guest computers on the desks were working

Etihad has two business class lounge one at Terminal 1 and Terminal 3 in Abu Dhabi Airport. This review is for the T3 lounge as both are way different. T3 premium lounge is top quality and beautifully maintained. I happen to have 8 hrs day transit and choose to spend it in lounge. The seat comfort though not great for recline and relax, but have variety of chairs. The bar selection and cocktails made to order was great. The all day food was amazing, but at 3pm, then remove all to prepared for dinner, so during that time no food is available apparently, which could be improved. There is business center with iMac and smoking lounge within. The spa and shave is a paid service, and not free as it appeared or misunderstood. The washroom was felt to be in scarcity given only three cubicles available. Overall had delightful time spending the long transit.

The First / Business class lounge is well situated, clean, and amazing staff. The only limitation is that the menu of the lounge remains the same for all days and months. So if a frequent traveller like me who eats just veg, you would land up having same noodles all the time.

An elegant oasis with impeccable service. Everyone I came into contact with were pleased to assist, I was very well looked after. I sampled the Six Senses Spa and even helped create a new cocktail. The dining was an unforgettable experience, sampling the Emirates Palace tasting menu, with a phenomenal wine cellar to match. Plenty of space to sit and relax and plenty of natural light.

The arrivals lounge is open for premium passengers and is located after customs. The staff greet you warmly and there is an area for seating. Snacks are laid out as a variety of sandwiches and desserts with soft drinks and juices. Shower facilities as well as a shaving facility is present and your clothes can be ironed as well. Overall not bad.

We regularly fly Etihad business class and were very disappointed to find that the "new" lounge at Bangkok airport is little more tha a small holding room. It's small, overcrowded and not at all what a business class customer should have to put up with. There are no toilet or shower facilities in the lounge and seating is limited. We will seriously be considering a different airline when we fly next.

The New First Class lounge is wonderful. The restaurant was 5 star, service exceptional. I took a quick massage, had a shower, a meal and a relax. Faultles. Really wonderful. It is comparable with Qatar Airways wonderful lounge at London Heathrow. Well done.

When I travel Business Class, I expect a decent quality lounge to relax in. As for Etihad Airways, I am seriously shocked to know why the heck I am sitting here. This lounge had basic food (mainly chicken and I do not eat chicken), it looks old and run down, service staff are not friendly (they are not rude either) and generally it is an unhappy visit.

Etihad Airways uses the CIP Louis Tavern lounge in Bangkok. This lounge is way below the standard I expect as a frequent business class customer. The lounge is small and cramped and is very busy and noisy.It is not a quiet area and not a conducive working environment.In the past, Etihad used the Thai Airways lounge which was fine and spacious. We will be giving Emirates our business from now on as on the whole the Etihad business class model is not in the same league as Emirates.

After flying with Etihad for 6 years and experiencing their silver lounge (awful) and experiencing their old business class lounge,  I thought after buying a full business class ticket I would be in for a treat with their new business class lounge. I was wrong. Staff were polite and food/ drinks were abundant and freely available. What I disliked was that the lounge felt like a bus station. It was so ridiculously busy, it took me a while to actually find a seat. People were sleeping across sofas and hoarding seats I actually considered going back to the main terminal. I also reminded myself that on past experiences I could get a free 15 minute massage, which was a fantastic selling point from Etihad that helped build up the their brand. However, the free massage is now only complimentary to platinum customers. I am glad this is my last experience with Etihad. I got the odd free upgrade over the years and I finally bought a business class ticket (which was the aim of the upgrades) but I can happily say I am done with this airline. Economy is shocking. Business is great. But I want to love an airline no matter what class I decide to stay. I no longer love Etihad. It built its brand on awesomeness and a care for its customers. But now it is a cost saving exercise for those at the back of the plane. I don't want to fly with an airline that has that attitude. Goodbye Etihad.

Great lounge.  The lounge has nice decor, but not too spacious. The seating is divided into rooms rather than an open space concept. Basic variety of cold and hot meals and soups. Meals reflect the middle-east and Indian cuisine. The bar is staffed.

A la carte menu, buffet, snacks and non alcoholic and alcoholic beverages available. Washroom with shower. Spacious comfortable and quiet. Staff are professional, courteous and friendly. This is how a Business class lounge should be like.

As a platinum member of Etihad Airways fidelity program I am used to be given an invitation to the Thai Airways First Class lounge which is extremely good. However this time they put me in the Louis Tavern First Class Lounge. This lounge is horribly bad! Very hot, limited and bad food and drinks, uncomfortable and old furniture, no service at all. Etihad should be ashamed. I have sent a complaint to Etihad about this 2 weeks ago and I am still waiting for a decent answer.

I was flying to JFK from Abu Dhabi. The main lounge (before pre-clearance to the US) is fine but nothing to remember, especially for a lounge that is meant to be their flagship lounge. No rest area, very few power outlets. The only highlight seems to be the spa but I did not try it. Food is forgettable. Main issue is the screens do not give proper boarding information. My flight had started boarding which was not displayed. A hostess came looking for me telling me it was the last call more than one hour before departure. She was rude and not apologetic. No one had told me there was preclearance for US immigration either. When I got to the gate, another employee made me feel like the whole flight was waiting for me. When I boarded, the boarding was only half way through! Strange way to treat business class customers. On a positive note, Etihad offers much better lounges at Sydney and JFK.

Etihad Airways business class lounge in Abu Dhabi. Nice layout but when I asked reception about quiet zones/sleep areas she said you cannot sleep here and then guided me to another spot in the airport that has paid sleeping areas. I then visited the Six Senses Spa and scheduled a scalp massage since I'm pregnant and can't get a body treatment. I was then told that scalp, hand and foot massages are also off limits because of the pressure which is absolutely ridiculous. Food and juice options are quite limited especially when compared to Emirates and Qatar Airways lounges.

The lounge is spacious, clean and well maintained, and lots of food and drink. Many TV screens as well as personalized screen (1 seat/TV screen). There are possibilities to access Spa and showers. Lounge is crowded and few places to have some privacy. However none of the PC's in the lounge were functioning.

This Pagasa lounge has to be the worst lounge. Food is only finger sandwiches with three choices. I had to ask the staff to refill the fridge as beer had run out and then again later when the coffee also ran out. Decor is old with stained carpets and old chairs. When I spoke to the staff on duty no one was the least interested in either listening to me or being the least bit interested. Please give us a decent lounge with decent service.

The Etihad Airways lounge I visited was in Terminal One. The lounge is airey and light. The service, food and comfort is excellent. The staff are also on hand to assist with your shower etc. They even have a spa that gives you a free massage for 15 minutes. This is one area that Etihad have it absolutely right.

Etihad Airways Business Class Lounge in Abu Dhabi, and when it comes to dining, there is something for everyone. The food selection beats the buffet menu at many restaurants. Even if you have a tight connection at Abu Dhabi, stop by to grab a bite.

Etihad Airways Business class lounge at Abu Dhabi Airport was very convenient, clean, and spacious plus the food was really nice with a lot of choices. Facilities (chairs, wi-fi, electricity etc.) all are there. Beverages for every taste and demand.

A bright and spacious lounge offering a wide variety of food and beverages. The bathrooms were clean and maintained. Didn't have time to use the spa facilities but a young lady still took the time to explain the treatments on offer. The staff were on hand for anything you needed. All in all and excellent place to while away the time le waiting for your flight.

The lounge staff were outstanding. Cocktails came quick and were perfect, the food was like a top rated restaurant. There were many staff. Well done to every one in that lounge it's perfect even the shower and bathroom. And it has a great view for those who love to watch the planes.

This has to be one of the best business lounges. It has only a couple of flights a day but offers fantastic staff service. I have used the lounge some 6 times in the last couple of years and cannot fault the service.

I have never experienced such a poor lounge, ever. The lounge is absolutely filthy. Surly service, the only food available cheese sandwich and a selection of very sweet pastries. Only drinks available, water or very sweet juice cartons or colas. No glasses, only disposable plastic cups. No alcohol. The staff said alcohol was banned at the airport but you pass through "The Old English Pub" to get into the lounge. It was not permitted to buy a glass of wine at the pub and take into the lounge. Frankly it would be much better if Etihad Airways said they did not provide a lounge service in Cairo as the appalling lounge seriously compromises the Etihad Airways brand.

It is about the best business lounge I have experienced. Great staff, friendly and welcoming. The breakfast is good, you get both a buffet and a la carte waiter service. Linen service as well. A very good place to wait for your flight!

The Wingtips lounge at New York JFK is a dump calling itself as a lounge. Its a shame on Etihad Airways to provide this for First Class passengers. I visited it in the afternoon and all that it had was croissants and cereals left from breakfast. Worse still it had pork products for a Muslim airline. Place was filthy with food bits left on the chairs. The staff were sore and had no mood to welcome the passengers. I was better off strolling outside in the duty free area.

There are 2 Etihad Airways lounges. One before the TSA USA check and one after. I visited both lounges. First one is expansive with a spa and shower, bar and several buffets. Second one is much smaller with a small buffet and coffee. Both were well attended and welcoming.

Wingtips Lounge at New York JFK is small but a pleasant respite while waiting for ones flight. Food choices good, lounge was quiet and not very crowded. The staff were tremendous in keeping travelers informed of their flights, helpful suggestions about the terminal and went out of their way to accommodate travelers requests.

Al Reem Business Class lounge in Abu Dhabi is an awful lounge. Don't waste your money. Not only was it empty but when I fell asleep they woke me up saying sleeping was not allowed! After I paid them several hundred dollars! This lounge is very noisy sub par food and service and I would have booked something else if I knew.
Business class lounge at Abu Dhabi is a very good lounge and service totally let down by stylish but uncomfortable seats and lack of toilets.

Etihad Airways Business Class lounge at Dublin Airport has a very nice atmosphere and comfortable enough after I had to tell someone who roared into his phone to go into the closed off business area. I also told staff this should not be allowed and this is their job to look for and sort these issues. It is not the guest who should have to do this. Excellent A la carte table dining (for breakfast anyway). There is a buffet for fruits yogurts etc.

Business Class lounge at Abu Dhabi has excellent facilities and first class service. High quality food, genuine service and comfortable environment. There appears to be only 1 shower in the ladies room and there is no place to recline while waiting for your flight.

SATS business class lounge at Singapore Changi Airport. Greeted by a polite well groomed man and directed into lounge with subdued lightening light coloured vinyl tub chairs and low partitions (top 3rd frosted glass). These are showing some signs of wear - quite uncomfortable. In one corner 4 cubicles with back-facing massage chairs and a beaded curtain for privacy. First Class area is the just a cordoned off back corner separated by a sign several plants. Food/beverages well below par. Tea preparation is separate from coffee. Array of teabags you find in any chain hotel room - only milk UHT. Coffee from machine worse than instant and tepid. Arrived at 9pm. Food almost depleted yet to be restocked. Tried a tomato/iceberg lettuce/hummus sandwich but it'd been so long it was in it's plastic bag it'd become soggy and the bread curled. Signs indicate hot vegetarian options where carrot soup and mashed potato. Several hot stew looking dishes and several Asian options. Six pcs with good internet speed. Along the entire window length a row of desks with individual reading lamps. Hospitality staff are pleasant. Female toilets: 2 cubicles 2 showers 2 hairdryers. Soap dispensers are the plastic type you buy in a supermarket. Extremely disappointing! I'm popping downstairs to grab a bite to eat.

Etihad Airways Business Class lounge at Abu Dhabi Airport. What a contrast to the terminal 1 lounge last July and the new lounge in Terminal 3 by gate 35. The new lounge is spacious high quality furnishings great bar plentiful supply of food. Only negative is that it appears to be quite focused on Indian hot foods. Staff very attentive didn't use the spa. I guess the previous reviewer is a 1st class customer and would expect a separate lounge other airlines.
