A huge improvement and is matched to the excellent lounge in Dublin. On Etihad you normally get redemption seats which you never get any more with Emirates.

Etihad Airways have closed their existing business class and First class lounges in Abu Dhabi Terminal 3 and opened a new combined lounge (no separate First) near Gate 35 in Terminal 3. First impressions were that this is a high quality lounge spacious and a lot more capacity than the existing lounge. Food and beverages on a par with existing buffet-style business lounges which are very good. Good business area and nice childrens area. Where this lounge really fails is the SiX Senses Spa which is shambolic. I have just queued for 65 minutes for a shower. They had no waitlist so you had to just grab a seat and wait (could not nip out to get food). They had a booking system for spa treatments but the earliest slot was over two hours later so most people could not avail of this. I use their First lounge normally as Gold Elite so the experience going through Abu Dhabi today is significantly worse than before. Lot of unhappy people here. I believe that when they renovate the old lounge area near the shops it will be a dedicated First lounge which will hopefully take the pressure off in this lounge. Poor experience overall.

Terminal 3: Arrived in 'Business' lounge at 0015. Every seat was occupied. Busier than a bus terminal and about as comfortable. Screaming children added to the misery. The lounge is way too small to seat the people paying a big premium for their ticket. Other bleary-eyed travellers were circling the lounge looking for seats constantly. Shag-pile carpet looks dirty couches worn and grubby. Unsatisfactory.

The moment I walked in I could see it was crowded big time and it was hard to find a place to sit. It is 1/20th smaller than emirates lounge in Dubai. Food a good spread and very efficient staff. Quiet room spacious but sleeping on couch is always painful for a tall guy. Washrooms cramped to the core and very small.

We did this lounge in Jan 2014 EY418 to KUL. One of the worst I have been in space wise. I had to give my stool to a furlorn standing lass with a cup of coffee in her hand. My first on Etihad and what a disappointment for the hub airport. The lounge was so overcrowded. Will be travelling J again as Etihad are value for bucks but shall be researching for a alternative airport paid lounge for a convenient place to sit. Staff were doing the best they could given the incompetence and short sightness of Etihad. What a downer on Etihad offerings.

Abu Dhabi Lounge Terminal 3. From the moment you get the lift/stairs to the entrance you feel like a Number. You don't feel special or the dollars you spent on a ticket was worth it. Its too busy Lounge is too small. The spa is brilliant as well as showers. I cannot fault customer service. The biggest problem are size of the lounge way too small. you feel cramped and enclosed. It didn't feel like a Business Class lounge of quality ie: Singapore Emirates Qantas British Airways.

The food and beverage selection was very extensive with several a la carte items offered. The staff was extremely courteous and eager to please. One employee in particular Nerlita went above and beyond to make sure I was well attended and provided superior customer service. I travel a lot for work and I have had the opportunity to visit many lounges- this one tops the list.
Fantastic service and extremely nice people. Love the food and the care of the lounge staff.
This lounge is over crowed. No peace area. Lots of screaming kids. Very limit selection of food and drinks. Atmosphere is a sort of darkish. In general uncomfortable. Not to be recommended.

Just relaxing in the Etihad lounge and the service is excellent as usual. The staff are helpful and friendly and nothing seems too much trouble. The quality of the food is amazing and I'd have no hesitation in recommending this lounge to others.

Etihad use the SATS Premier Lounge in T2 at Changi. We had six hours in this lounge and found it to be better than a lot of airline lounges we have used. Greeted by friendly staff at reception. A huge selection of food was available that was well presented and kept fresh. Choices available from the bar were not so extensive. Staff cleared away dishes promptly. Clean washroom facilities. Excellent WiFi.

One of the worst lounges in an airlines hub city you can imagine. The lounge is very small and was packed with people at 11pm  more people were coming in and simply walking out 3 of us eventually found a lounge chair but there was no real reason to be there. The toilets are very limited food selection was average at best and biggest problem is screens showing flights we could only see one which was only giving details in Arabic (even Tehran airport VIP lounge that Etihad uses has screens in two languages). No sign of any TV or other entertainment was in view in the corner we were located The internet was 3rd world standard slow. As we left we noticed they had opened the door to the first class lounge which had not a soul in it. Maybe there are quieter times but this really lets down Etihad's inflight standards.

Due to our 1325 departure the lounge was not as busy as at other times of the day. However seeing this serves Etihad's T3 I can see how it's facilities can be put under pressure. There was no a la carte food offering just a hot/cold buffet. I asked a member of staff if they could make a little something up for our baby daughter and they obliged. In addition my wife asked if there was any dessert wine available (as there is on the plane) there wasn't but the gentleman behind the bar arranged for a glass to be brought through from the First Class lounge. The fifteen minute complimentary massage at the Six Senses Spa was very good. Unfortunately the children's room was not up to the standard of Heathrow. Finally on using the baby change facility (disabled toilet) after washing our hands we discovered we could not dry them because there was no hand towel in the holder or hand dryer or paper towels.

Plenty of space and facilities. We travelled on the 09:15 departure to Abu Dhabi with our seven month old daughter and made use of the (sound-proofed!) children's room. We had the a la carte breakfast and recommend the eggs benedict and pancakes. Hot and cold drinks regularly offered. There was a buffet with all the usual staples. The fifteen minute complimentary massage at the Six Senses Spa was a nice touch. Overall one of the better lounges we have used.

We used this lounge when travelling on Air Malta flights. London Heathrow lounge is excellent and in the opinion of my wife and myself is on a par if not better than the BA First Class (Concorde) Lounge at Heathrow T5. On entering the lounge we were given a warm welcome. We were there on a weekday morning between 08.45 to 11.00. There was an excellent breakfast (buffet and a la carte) with almost anything you could want. We found the spa in the to be readily available for chosen treatments. Although there is not a self-service bar for alcoholic drinks in the lounge there is a bar where passengers are served with alcoholic drinks. We have used the lounge twice (both times when travelling Air Malta Business Class) and have found the lounge and staff to be first rate.

Very large lounge but with limited refreshments on offer. Spa closed. Lots of staff cleaning tables but no table service. Soft drinks and beer available in fridges. Free wifi. If you want alcohol there is a small bar at the right hand side of the entrance which is easy to miss but they had no vodka left with no offer to replenish it. Wine served in half a glass. Quite disappointing lounge although it was quiet.

Table service for drinks and hot foods. Waitresses very attentive and polite. Only serving one flight so quite quiet lounge. Small buffet area for mezze cheeses etc. I had cream of celeriac soup with mushrooms and truffle oil! fillet of cod with black olive tapenade root veg purée and vegetables! washed down by several well-topped up glasses of champagne. Restaurant quality in taste quality and service. Own toilets not shared as in the other lounges there. A great start to a holiday indeed. Cannot be faulted.

Accessed as part of Gold card member benefits. The drink choices are high quality (excellent sauvignon blanc) - my only minor gripe would be the starter on the dining menu was slightly below the normal standard but an excellent main and dessert. Fast wifi good selection of papers plenty of seating make this my favourite lounge.
An excellent lounge probably the best for choice and quality of food. Abu Dhabi is the worst very overcrowded limited selection of food but staff good.

The buffet food choices were more varied and better quality than last visit - thai green curry and chicken in red wine sauce were both very good. For a pay on entry lounge (I access as Etihad guest gold card holder) the drink brands are always good quality - using Johnny Walker Green label as their standard mixing whiskey (something of a waste but not complaining!). The main problems with this lounge is that it does get very busy at peak times and woefully inadequate bathroom facilities. Good wifi newspaper selection and bbc world news on tv.

Shower and toilet can become a nightmare. Just one shower and one toilet. No cleaning between guests no waiting list - if you want to take a shower you'll have to wait in line in the toilets! A nightmare! Wrote several times to Etihad probably others did never saw an improvement. Make sure there are towels before you start!

Visited this lounge on 6 different occasions in last month. It is by far one of the worst I have used. On a number of occasions I had to sit on the floor due to overcrowding. Etihad have two lounges here and both are as bad as each other. There is no booking system for a shower so it can be impossible to get one. Others mention the food as being great - I disagree food on the plane in business class is far better. The staff are good. In my travels with Etihad I would say that their Dublin lounge is the best I have used so far. You can order proper meals there but you cannot at their home lounges.

Food is great and bar staff are friendly and efficient. The problem is that it is way too small to handle the passenger flow. Can be difficult or near impossible to get a seat. Toilet facilities are very cramped and totally inadequate for the number of passengers they have to handle.
Lounge provided for gold and silver frequent flyers available for other airlines and payment. Small dull normally overcrowded uncomfortable and inadequate toilet facilities.

This is the Air New Zealand lounge shared by Etihad. The staff was vaguely interested the food choice very limited and very very average. There was no shower gel nor shampoo in the showers the shower mixer was broken resulting in nearly boiling water pouring from the shower head. When complained to the head of the staff I heard that how could they no if guests did not report implying there is no cleaning between the guests! All together terrible experience despite very good service on board though. Will not come back again.
Very attentive and friendly staff restaurant food plenty of it great wifi and comfortable seating. Showers and bathrooms spotless.

Used the Etihad Pearl Business Lounge at Abu Dhabi T3 while connecting from a MCT-AUH flight to AUH-MAN in business. Between these two flights the lounge was a huge disappointment particularly with this being Etihad Airways home airport. The lounge was crowded so there were no comfortable seats available the food was okay but lacked choice (four of six hot options were available) - and the toilets were filthy.

Further to my previous post Sep 2011 this lounge has improved. It's still an awkward walk from T3 to T1 but I was pleasantly surprised how improved the lounge was. There is now a newspaper and magazine rack the food selection now has a lot more to offer including cold cuts of meat and various cheeses. A bigger selection of hot ( warm) dishes various teas and coffees and a lot more seating arrangements ( previously the middle and lower tier sections were closed off ) . The washrooms are a little small but a hot shower is available. A well stocked bar with waiter service is a nice touch. On a minus note there didn't seam to be any computers available. Overall a very pleasant experience and would recommend to all. (shame you still have to walk into T1 for a smoke though).

In terminal 1 about 10 minutes walking from terminal 3. Have always found this lounge to be clean and less crowded than the actual Etihad business class lounge in terminal 3. Staff extremely helpful and friendly. Same food and drinks as in the business lounge.

This is the Air New Zealand lounge shared by Etihad. Who on earth decided to use wickerwork rattan armchairs for the "comfort" of travellers who sometimes have to spend hours waiting for a connecting flight - the armrests alone are uncomfortable enough but add in the punishment to the seating area penetrating through the cushion. The only other viable seating is of a benching type so no armrests - but on balance preferable! The food choices were very limited and as such I was not hungry enough to assess the quality.

If you are a silver or gold card holder flying in economy class this lounge is now allocated to you. However this lounge is located in terminal 1 and as most people transit in terminal 3 I don't think it's worth the 20+ minute walk to use what is generally a sub standard facility. I wouldn't pay to use this facility and would rather sit in Starbucks at my own expense.
Whenever I've visited this lounge it's always been overcrowded. Somebody at Etihad has got they're sums wrong. Other than this a good facility.

lounge_name: ETIHAD AIRWAYS BUSINESS CLASS LOUNGE REVIEW
review: Very disappointed by the Lounge and by the lounge staff who were unfriendly and unprofessional. For the food and beverages facilities and the lounge was correct.

Extremely disappointing. Limited choice of food In fact there were on two varieties of tuna rolls on offer along with corn chips and pretzels. Nothing else. My wife and I were traveling to Sydney and had a four hour layover between connecting flights and while the peace and quiet of the lounge was welcomed the lack of food was not.

The lounge was too far from the terminal. The food was not really that hot. The fruits and beverages was ok. The staff told us wifi was going to be fixed soon but I waited for almost 2 hours and still none. Accommodating staff great six sense spa offer but it was so limited - I was only allowed to use 1 treatment instead of at least 2.

This lounge is overcrowded and very noisy. Food good great service but we were there from 2100 to 0240 and it gradually got worse with a number of people standing up and not being able to get a seat at all. I do not agree with the idea of asking people traveling in economy to use another lounge. I will in future organise my connections so I can limit time in this lounge.

As a silver card member I'm entitled to access to the Al Reem lounge at Abu Dhabi. I can't compare it to the Pearl lounge in T3 (I've never accessed it) but as a business class lounge it was good with plenty of breakfast options available stocked and manned bar area plenty of seating (if in a somewhat weird 3 tiered room) and newspapers and magazines available. However Wi-Fi was unavailable whilst I was there (and the staff couldn't fix it) and there was only 3 staff to man the bar clear plates and update the breakfast area and thus they struggled to keep up with demand in a less than half full lounge. The only real problem is the lack of toilet facilities in the lounge for its size.

Small but uncrowded lounge. Quality of service food and drink during my stay was excellent. Free wifi and tv/newspapers available. The criticism would be the lack of a sleeping zone but few lounges of this size would be likely to have that. Definitely much better than either the Al Reem lounge in AUH.

Quite a small but pleasant lounge. Nice reception from the staff and frequent offer to refill drinks and so forth. As it was an early flight we enjoyed a cooked to order breakfast. Very good. You could also help yourself to cold cuts and bakery if you didn't want a cooked meal.

Previously Etihad gold and silver card holders used the Pearl business lounge in terminal three complete with comfy seats and smoking room but now (due to overcrowding) have to use the Al Reem lounge in the old terminal 1. All Etihad flights to Europe and Asia arrive and leave from the new T3 so this becomes awkward. On arrival you have to bypass security and walk (10 mins) to the old terminal and the lounge. This lounge is not a patch on the T3 lounge with a very limited food selection (drinks are fine). There is no comfortable seating area and no papers to pass the time. The next problem is there is no smoking room so you must use the smoking room in the far corner of T1. Then of course to catch your flight head back to T3 and go through security which becomes more of a muddle if another flight arrives as you do - as nobody knows where they are going and can cause another delay.

We were flying First Class Etihad-Europe having previously travelled First Class on Qantas BA Air France and Emirates. The lounge turns out to be the New Zealand Airlines "standard" lounge. This is very much not what we expect when we pay for First Class. It's a nice enough lounge crowded despite a quiet night at the airport (I'd hate to see it on a slightly busy night!) but nothing more. Would not reach Business Class standards for any other airline. As we sit in the lounge we are not planning to fly Etihad again. There's a chance for catch up on the flights and in the other ports but really we've made a decision to fly First Class because we want "First Class" funnily enough! This is not a First Class lounge and as stated above I'd be disappointed if I'd paid Business Class for this. Part of the real pleasure of starting a holiday is sitting back in the lounge with that first glass of champagne. We last travelled Emirates and while they didn't have a dedicated First lounge (shared with Business) the facilities food and champagne are great on board. This is the first time I've ever bothered to write such a review which reflects our disappointment. Etihad has a fair bit of catching up to do at this early stage. There's no way that we'll depart Melbourne with Etihad again. Do what Air France do escort your First Class passengers (in CDG at least) to the lounge make sure they're comfortable and come and get them when it's time to leave. If you're going to ask for 5-10 times the fare make the customer feel a little special!
Etihad business class travellers have to fight for seats in this lounge. This lounge is too small and regularly too full to accommodate all business class passengers. Food quality has declined.

Totally disappointed by this so called premium lounge. Not only was it overcrowded the staff offered no help when you are circling around trying to find a place to sit and eat. The staff at reception was fine. The toilets seemed too small for volume of passengers and I looked for the so called shower facilities in vain. The whole design on top of the huge crowd using it certainly gives you the impression that you are in a canteen and not in a premium lounge. On the return flight the plane from Kuala Lumpur landed in Abu Dhabi around midnight and not only trying to find the lounge from where you got off this time was a nightmare but when I got to the lounge I did not bother to eat (despite being hungry) as I was not prepared to explore every corner just to find a comfortable place to eat. Etihad please wake up and upgrade this lounge I am not being demanding but when you pay to travel business class some comfort in transit is not too much to ask.

Senses Spa would be one of the best things here. Lounge is too small for the morning traffic. Food was good and a variety. Staff is too loud. Waiting for the shower and a line for the toilet - never happened with me before in a Business class lounge. Etihad people need to understand what a lounge means - and not just free food and drinks.

This is not an Etihad lounge as they do not have one at JFK. This lounge is so poor it is unbelievable unhappy person on reception only one person cleaning up the food way below lounge level no champagne warm white wine. We left as soon as possible. Avoid this place it really is very bad.

Rather small feeling crammed and very crowded. It was difficult to find a seat and impossible to use one of the computer terminals. Staff were busy in their attempts to replenish food and beverages. The lounge needs to be much bigger.

Although this is the new lounge in Terminal 3 it can get very crowded. Food and beverage is good but seating is a little close together and there is not much privacy. The Six Senses Spa is great. Overall not a bad lounge but I do not know why Etihad chose to create such a small lounge in contrast to the number of people who use it. Etihad needs to attend to the washrooms as they were not what you would expect from a business class lounge.

The a la carte dining was superb with great attention by the staff. Again the Six Senses Spa is great and just what you need before a long flight. The food and beverage section is well maintained and is of a high quality. Overall this is a fine lounge and rates as one of the best I have been in.

Excellent catering and drinks selection complete with bar service. Abundant large screen iMacs for use as well as Wi-fi. Well-kept though few toilets with a single shower so there can be a queue. There is a Six Senses Spa which gives complimentary 15 minute treatments with free clothes pressing. Inside the Spa are 6 more showers. The rush hour seems to be from 8-9 am. It was virtually empty before and after that.

Lounge was extremely crowded and there was nowhere to sit. The situation with this lounge has not changed for many years, I can only therefore assume that Finnair have no interest in fixing the situation.

A large, spacious, quiet place with comfortable couches and clean bathrooms. A feature that caught my eye was a mechanical shoe polisher - I inserted my boots to give them a bright shine! There was ample food and drinks of all kinds - all self service. A row of windows overlooked the security check in area. International magazines were on racks. A perfect place to while your time before your flight is called. Easy to get to just after security - go up in an elevator; take it down to go to your gate through duty free shops.

Clean and accurate place, but it is pretty crowded over the regular hours, pretty hard to find a place. Food is basic, but fulfilling. Good place to refill yourself, but it might be really hard to find a place and do anything in case you stacked there with long stop.

What a downgrade to previous Premium Lounge by Finnair. The new lounge has been renovated for almost a year without any access to Premium lounge by Finnair. Finnair uses disposable cups/plates etc. in their regular lounge which in these days is a real disaster. The new Platinum Lounge is a total disappointment. Just to get sparkling water/cafe latte you have to queue up in the bar, the bartender (only one) forgets which order people come to order and it is chaotic and not friendly service. Food is poor and logistics poorly planned. Design not Scandinavian high quality as they blame. No views to the planes anymore. Just few seats fave power outlets nearby to charge your phone etc. Terrible work Finnair!

Aurora Lounge at terminal 2 is run by Menzies but the airline I was flying with use it. I have been here many times. There are hot and cold food items, drinks and other basic stuff. It is not luxurious. However, some of the members of staff could be a bit more friendly and service-minded. I was on my way to HEL for an intercontinental flight so I stopped by to use this lounge as I always do when I fly with a Oneworld airline. Got there, stood at the counter waiting to be registered. The staff at the counter was very busy with her phone but I stood there and waited. She got off her phone finally but sounded a bit annoyed. She scanned my boarding pass and then she looked at me and went "are you sure you're supposed to be here?" It said on the boarding pass which lounge I could visit very clearly. It also said business class and sapphire status. What else would I need to be able to enter this very simple lounge? I always try to keep a low profile and don't want to say "oh I'm flying business" or "oh I'm a frequent traveler" because so far all I had to do was showing them my boarding pass but since she seemed annoyed, rather rude and incompetent I replied "Yes, it says on the boarding pass that I'm allowed to be here. Plus I'm flying business and my status is sapphire." Unfortunately this is the only lounge at this terminal.

Krabi is a small airport and the Thai Airways Business Class lounge that Finnair use is before Passport Control, when we arrived it was very busy, Very limited offerings a few small sandwiches and cakes along with a coffee machine, Tea and soft drinks as well as alcohol. WiFi very slow. No toilets you have to leave the lounge and take your chances in the public toilets! we left and went through security and sat in the main departure lounge with everyone else. In all OK but would not recommend.

Luckily we arrived at a quiet time as they have limited seats and was very busy later in the evening, Usual airport lounge nothing outstanding, food was a letdown and very limited might as well use the outside facilities.

Visited Lounge for late night Departure to Hong Kong. Even though still had 4 Long Haul Flights to go there was hardly any decent hot Food left. Food that was left has been there for some time and certainly looked unappetising. Apart from that there was some very uninspiring Salad. Many of the Customers visiting the Lounge were looking rather unimpressed with its offering and Finnair clearly needs to lift its game. The Lounge itself is spacious and comfortable but the Food section certainly is poor.

Arrived in Helsinki from Bangkok at 15:30 on a week day and had a 2 hour layover waiting for my connecting flight to Copenhagen. I was flying business class and used the Finnair business class lounge on the domestic side of the airport (second floor above the terminal area). The lounge was very crowded and no lounge chairs were available. The only seats open were stools at the window counter - nice view of the airport, but not comfortable for a long lay-over. The food and beverage was average, with the exception of some very good chocolates. The bathroom spaces in the lounge are very small and limited, with people knocking on the door for you to hurry-up ! Wifi connection very easy and fast. Recommend only if it is free with your class of travel. I would never pay a fee for this lounge.

The Jet Lounge (a handling lounge) was the worst lounge I ever visited. Being gluten-intolerant I found they had nothing to offer me, except crisps and peanuts. The personnel did try their best but this should be implicit for the lounge keeper. Could also hear others looking for cheese or similar without finding anything. Would very much want to see OneWorld using another better equipped lounge.

During afternoon rush hours the lounge is overcrowded. No empty seats, barely any empty table corner to place a glass, people wandering around looking for place to sit down making the lounge feel very restless. Food salads, soup and a couple of warm dishes from self service buffet, quality varies a lot, sometimes very good, sometimes the total opposite. Outside rush hours nice and relaxing.

Lounge is very big and gives a pleasant feeling once you enter. Several TV's on mute showing news and computers that are always shutoff. Lounge has a neat toilet, for some reason they always leave paper towels on the counter (way too much, always). Disappointing issue is the food-area. 1 out of 7 times i had a chance to taste a good soup, salad looks very un-attractive and should be presented in a better way, there are no sandwiches, pastries, cakes or any other good "snacks"! Once they had only coffee buns, another time they had only crackers. This is unacceptable in Business Class standards to have such food offerings. otherwise no complaints.

One of the worst hub lounges I have ever visited. Packed with 90% of the seats full. Hot food consisted of tomato soup, potatoes and a pretty poor curry. Salad bar had wilting lettuce and only a couple other items. Soup and bread ran out quickly and took time to be replaced. Two draft beers, neither very good. Screwcap sparkling wine (never seen that before). Chocolate donuts were the sweets on offer.

Le lounge était ressent et agréable. Mais il était noir de monde (sur le vol aller comme sur le vol retour). beaucoup de personne cherchaient un endroit ou s'asseoir. Coté siège, vous aviez le choix entre des sièges droits devant une table, ou des sièges basculants face aux pistes. malheureusement c'est sièges se sont avéré très inconfortables, avec notamment une barre dans le dos.
The lounge was nice and feels okay. But it was full of people (on the outbound and return flight) - many people seeking a place to sit. Side seat, you had a choice of seats at a table or rocking chairs facing the outside. Unfortunately the seats have been very uncomfortable.

Service and friendliness have been outstanding in this Finnair Premium Lounge, you feel as a guest. Food choice and beverages at a high standard, excellent wine selection. Love the clean scandinavian design and style, felt comfy and relaxed between the two flights. One of the best airport lounges I´ve been to.

The Finnair lounge at Helsinki Vantaa Airport was exceptional, spacious, clean and helpful staff. Great food (they are not here to provide a 5 star meal) and if that is what you want go pay for it. It's a convenience lounge with great snacks, good food and extensive alcoholic options. Ample seating options.

I am undergoing the somewhat surreal experience of flying Finnair from Brussels to Singapore via Helsinki. Everything has been several points below average. But now I am in the Finnair Business Lounge at Helsinki Airport with several hours to kill. We were told there would be a 2 hour wait before the dinner menu was served. It has now arrived. It consists of a baked potato with optional tuna mayo. Nothing else. I have never, ever had such a poor experience in a Business Lounge. It would be funny, if only it was not so disappointing. I will do everything to avoid the repeat of the whole miserable Finnair experience.

Finnair frequent flyer lounge at Helsinki Vantaa Airport is a beautiful lounge, nice views, great lighting, and overall very relaxing. The food could be better, but no other complaints. Definitely one of the best lounges out there!

Crowded and with poor access. Staircase or one very busy elevator. Very limited food but drink options quite ok. Not really anywhere to relax and check in can be too time consuming. Finnair know how to do it properly with their their Non-Schengen lounge. Why they offer this product is strange considering the airline itself continues to improve.

Spacious, comfortable and relaxing lounge. Reclining chairs with views are pleasant. Food is just ok while the drink options are fine. Very short walk to all non-Schengen gates. So much better than the Schengen lounge it is hard to believe it belongs to the same airline.

While connecting from Amsterdam on a flight to Asia I had plenty of opportunity to wait in this lounge and I can say it was very comfortable. Food and wine selection was more than sufficient as was the seating capacity. But what I personally enjoyed the most were the wonderful recliner seats with a nice view over the apron.

Visited again the lounge on the 28th of November for four hours before a domestic flight. Unfortunately instead of improvements the service had gone worse. No food despite the new space-consuming meal service tables. Not a single copy of the newspapers I normally read there (Herald Tribune Iltasanomat) even though they were sold at general news stands at the boarding area. Waiting lines for the dirty toilets despite the fact that the lounge was half empty. No place to hang one's coat at the toilet (middle one for disabled passengers). A section of the area closed for passengers. Lots of staff but very little service for us frequent flyers. It is a shame that the Finnair 'home base' lounge is like this even though the international lounges are ok.

I Visited this lounge when connecting from Asia to a Schengen destination. Access was via stairs with a significant amount of 2way traffic. The frontdesk area was rather congested as was the food and drink area. It was very crowded so to leisurely pick a food and drink choice with also carry-on luggage to worry about was no option and therefore I settled for some orange juice. That as such was fine for me: I don't visit a lounge for food and drinks anyway (as there is decent food on the business class flight that follows) but I do visit a lounge for some peace and quiet and since there where very few comfortable seats left but an awful lot of traffic instead there wasn't much chance. Also too few facilities in the men's room also here was a small queue forming. I must add however that this was my 1st and only visit to this lounge and the time of day may have been a factor (around 15:30 local time) so it may be better at a different time of day. But in my opinion it is not capable to sufficiently cope with the amount of visitors that I saw during my visit.

The lounge was closed for three months for a renovation without alternative service or compensation for number of Finnair frequent flyers (Silver card holders). After the renovation the standards have unfortunately dropped in a significant way. The two main problems are: Instead of two access routes only one is left (one set of stairs and one elevator frequently reserved for maintenance purposes). As a result long waiting lines to the lower floor delay and frustrate customers. People have to stand on the stairs for up to 15 minutes to check in. The meal & snacks area has become too congested preventing access to the food and drinks for both the customers and the staff. As a result you grab what you can or what happens to be left while trying to avoid stepping on too many toes. The staff struggles to keep the area clean and organized for the same reasons. Add boring selection in regard to hot food and salads (well everything; no changes for years) in particular from the viewpoint of most frequent visitors the supposed priority for the airline. Overall I miss the lounge as it was before the renovation. Whatever goal the renovation served remains a mystery unless the idea was to make it less attractive?

Pleasantly surprised by this lounge. Choice of various styles of seating. Plenty of hot food choices which was good as we had a five hour layover. What was exceptional was seeing a chef testing the temperature of the food in trays. I have not seen this before anywhere and many times endured cold offerings even in so called first tier airlines. Most impressed with Finnair for this.

This was our first visit to this Lounge - what a disappointment! We arrived just after 1300 hours and were looking forward to some nourishment before our return flight to the UK. But the only food on offer was a vegetable soup with cheese some limp brown chopped up lettuce tasteless beetroot - the potatoes tomatoes cucumber and coleslaw were all empty! To make matters worse there appeared to be no one on duty to replenish these dishes. Even the apple cake had dried out! Very disappointing considering it was the height of the lunch hour. The drinks were plentiful and varied. As others have said the lounge had obviously been recently refurbished but all the Loungers on the upper level and the comfortable seats were occupied leaving just "plastic like" moulded chairs and tables? Not the best! To make matters worse an hour later saw an invasion of passengers for the far east and when we went to refill our glasses - as if by magic - suddenly there was Minestrone soup a hot chicken and rice dish hot dogs a selection of fresh salads a selection of breads and fresh fruits. Sorry Finnair but my fare included the entry price to this Lounge I we were entitled to parity of service - which we certainly did not get.

Used the Non Schengen Lounge for our late night departure ex Helsinki. The Lounge was clean and very comfortable with plenty of choices for Drinks both Alcoholic and Soft Drinks. As this was the last flight for the night there were only a few limp lettuce leaves and Soup left so if you planned to Eat before the flight you would be very disappointed!

Beautiful lounge but lacks in the food category. We each paid 48 euros and thought it might be a good alternative to dinner but at 7:10pm there was no dinner in sight and no real food other than salad soup and bread. Lots of drinks available but in general quite disappointing due to no other food/ snacks available. Wouldn't recommend it if you are mainly looking for a meal and drinks.

Helsinki was cold grey and closed it being 12th Night public holiday and so we resorted to a long wait in the Finnair lounge. Catering is quite simple but delicious much better than having endless choices of tepid offerings you don't want. Staff charming couldn't do enough. The lounge large and calm. Lots of Finnish understated design and the raised area with the recliners is the height of deliciousness. When it is crowded the centre can be a little canteen like but crowds are crowds and the staff do a brilliant job.

The most uncomfortable chairs in a lounge I've been in. Not relaxing at all! Whoever designed this lounge is a designer - not a business traveler! Very limited selection of food that did not look attractive at all. A few cheap wines and some beer.

Unimpressive. Low slung Scandinavian furniture - all style no comfort. A five hour transit ended in a sore back. Food supplies are meagre - a few limp salad leaves and a lacklustre pumpkin soup. Plenty of alcohol but not much to soak it up with. The place is littered with dirty crockery and glassware - the attendants only cruise by every now and then to clear it all away. No soap in the women's toilet and the men's urinal (I'm told) smells. Expected better. This is one of the most frugal lounges I have been in.

There was not much food a few salad leaves that was it bearing in mind that the lounge was half full. The toilet was dirty. Considering that this is the flagship lounge of Finnair. You can really see cost cuttings in that lounge. This lounge has not much to offer.

The few dishes that are offered weren't replenished at my visit. In some cases I was met by an empty serving tray of a few odd pieces of crumbles. Drink section was extremely dirty with a lot of spills that weren't cleaned up. The soda machine was leaking. Seating area was better cleaned but I already felt uneasy from the food and drinks section and left soon. There are other lounges in HEL airport maybe better chose another one even if it means you need to pay for your entry.

Very noisy as the lounge was filled over its capacity. It was not the relaxing place you want between flights. Stylish yes. But I found it to be stress-inducing not relaxing. The spa-section mentioned below is closed for good and the lounge offers nothing out of the ordinary. In fact it doesn't even offer the ordinary. The food sections cannot be called a food section. It has some cookies and sodas. There is a bar with a very nice bartender but the drinks offered were of the lower quality. If you like food and decent drinks you need to pay extra.

Lovely calm Nordic feel to lounge. Unfortunate that they did not plan it in a part of the airport with views of the runways. Views of air bridges are not inspiring. That said the facilities are great. Apple computers Marimekko and Iitala crockery - very stylish. A much improved food selection which I would have liked to have enjoyed more of but saved myself for inflight meal HEL-SIN. Comfortable seating and a choice of tables and chairs lounge sets or recliners.

This is the much heralded Finnair long haul lounge in Helsinki. Finnair flights from Europe and Asia arrive and depart within a few hours time frame in the afternoon. meaning the airport and in particular the lounges fill up during those hours. This new VIA lounge has a pleasant and light northern-european design but still feels a bit claustrophobic because of the number of people and the high-density seating. Staff welcoming and free Wifi available. Food and drink situation however not great. Limited choice and low quality (wine from a tap for example). The spa section is free for the highest status members of the Finnair FF program but not for the same level One World frequent flyers.

Not really up to scratch in terms of space or facilities. It feels like an original frequent flyer lounge from when they first appeared twenty years ago. Limited computers and inadequate toilet/shower facilities.

The lounge is located in Terminal B at Dusseldorf airport. Access is allowed i.e. with Priority Pass. Staff are very friendly and efficient. The ambience is quite sober but friendly. There is plenty of seating available. Food selection seems to locally inspired and is not not huge. Everything I tried was delicious. Drinks selection is not large but there are coffee, tea, soft drinks and wine/beer. I think maximum stay is three hours.

Ground floor comprises of a small lounge which fits the requirements of a business class ticket of a budget airline. Food was ok in terms of taste and variety and re stocked regularly. Upstairs is a bar with seating area with snacks. WiFi was poor and kept disconnecting. There were regular announcements when Flydubai flights were boarding.

The LAT Lounge has a modern fit out, however the food selection is quite grim when compared to Gulf lounges which are way more generous. It has a dedicated WIFI but I didn't use it. I saw a selection of alchool beverages, not impressive, but I took a cappuccino which was quite decent. Seating was very comfortable and also the outside view was nice.

Without any doubt one of the worst lounges visited in recent years. The place reeks of cigarette smoke, the wine is almost undrinkable and the food revolting. It was 21.30 and the food on offer was limited and had clearly been "simmering" all day. Avoid this lounge - sadly the only offering for Qatar Airways Business Class

I have been to this lounge many times in hope of an improvement only to find once again it is a disappointment. The food is of little choice and poor quality. The Bintang is virtually at room temperature. The only wine available is the local wine which personally is not my favourite. You have to ask for an alcoholic drink and the selection is beer and wine only. My family and I have flown garuda for many years and enjoy every flight. We are always served quality food and wine inclusive of Champagne. The drink and food selection on on the flight is plentiful. It is hard to believe they are one and the same.

This Denpasar lounge lived up to all the negative reviews. As one of Garuda Indonesia's most important hubs you would  expect something decent. Instead the food was minimal and not tasty. Alcoholic drinks were behind a little enclave that didn't even look like a bar and was barely attended. The range was small and when I asked for a red wine, the young attendant tried to serve it in a sparkling wine glass! And this is meant to be a business class lounge! The lounge was oddly shaped / arranged and hot although I found the whole airport hot with poor air conditioning. Staff were more interested in standing around and chatting to each other than actually doing any work. As this was the beginning of a Garuda business trip, it certainly lowered my expectations for the flight ahead. Certainly not what one expects from a 5-Star airline!

The Business Class Lounge was clean but the seats were terribly uncomfortable. Sitting there for an extended time became painful. Then there was the food. Some rice with a few assorted vegetables with potato wedges and crumbed fish pieces , that was it. No variation of food. The desert was a jelly with fruit and some pastries, the only thing edible was the jelly. The overall food presentation was disgraceful. My sister and I paid $25 each at another lounge last year and had a wonderful feast with lounge comfort seating. I am extremely disappointed with Garuda. They need to pick up their game and for Business Class this was totally unacceptable.

This place really is a joke. I remember years ago when Garuda had a decent business class lounge with a fully stocked, manned bar and edible food. In this lounge the food is luke warm-cold and not very appetising with a cooking station which doesn't seem to cook. If you want a drink there is a fridge with soft drinks in. If you want alcohol there is only wine or beer, both of which you have to ask for if you can get someones attention. For an airline which is otherwise quite good, this is a real let down for the passengers that pay good money for a business class ticket and expect a business class service.

What an absolute disgrace this lounge is! What makes it even worse is that this is Garuda’s own lounge at one of Indonesia’s busiest airports. It could have been a chance for this 5 star airline to showcase its hospitality and local cuisine. What we get us a bland range of salad and totally unappetising food including stone cold spring rolls and the plain cheese sandwiches. Very poor Range of drinks with alcoholic drinks (one red wine and one white wine and a few warm Bintang beers) kept in a manned ‘mini bar’. Absolutely laughable.

Having arrived we were the only passengers in the Garuda lounge at Denpasar Bali Airport which is a first for me .The Mini bar station not manned so had to hunt down staff to serve you from a selection of one white and red wine, very limited and just beer. Mostly avoid the food, rice was Luke warm along with chicken pieces. All the heated dishes were not on or on the lowest setting and spring rolls were stone cold. So very disappointed and crossing my fingers that Bali belly is not caught in the business lounge! They need to seriously educate their kitchen staff to serve hot food and please a smile from the one and only server would have been welcomed. Suggest at least one screen inside lounge for departures so you don’t have to keep nipping out to the main reception to see if boarding is underway. As a seasoned business traveller, this lounge falls way short of the standard.

The lounge at Terminal 3, Jakarta Airport is in a brand new terminal, but the passenger offer has been poorly thought out and the design is average. If Garuda wishes to compete with other 5 star airline lounges, they need to take feedback, particularly from European customers, about what is expected. The quality and range of food on offer was poor. There needs to be a better range of soft drinks, some cheeses, cakes/pastries, fresh fruit such as bananas/apples/grapes on offer as not everyone is happy to eat rice and carbohydrate rich food before a flight. There is no point in having a toaster and sliced bread to use, if there are no knives available/allowed to spread the butter/jam on the bread. The chairs are crowded together, hard and upright, and uncomfortable if waiting 2 hours for a flight. The toilets were clean and there were sufficient staff clearing the tables. Business users with laptops need waist high tables to be able to type comfortably, and the furniture available needs to be better tailored for there needs. Numerous floor plug sockets did not work, so my husband had a problem trying to charge his phone.

To say I am disappointed is an understatement. I cannot believe the lack of service. They had a live cooking station with chicken noodle soup and I must say the operator was the least enthusiastic and friendly person I had met in Bali. I am not sure if she knows what customer service is. No smile, points to the the different noodles and with a grunt asks what ones I wanted and with no finesse slops the noodles and shallots into the bowl. I really felt like laughing it was so unbelievable. The selection of food was poor and the service was the worst. Garuda seriously you should be ashamed.

Terminal 3 Jakarta Airport international business class lounge seating is ok. Food and beverage is a minus. Both domestic and international lounge in terminal 3 are not very good when it comes to the food and beverage selection on offer. Food very basic and beverage is sweet sugary juices, sweet sugary soft drinks and water. Not a decent drink in sight and no alcohol too. Fly out of Jakarta and like to spend decent time in a lounge waiting for your flight. Use a different airline and lounge (not that the others are much better but better they are).

Okay lounge which is slightly better than the premier lounge. Comfy seats although quite busy. Food was good but drink service really poor from a tiny manned bar where you have to find staff to serve you. No cold beers so many angry passengers. We were offered ice but it never arrived so we chose to buy cold beers from the main terminal.

One would expect a 5-star airline to extend this high standard to the Business Class lounge at their main hub. I find Garuda's domestic lounge to be well below a 5-star standard. It is not too much to expect that the toilets are clean & properly stocked. It seems that nobody ever checks to see if there is tissue in the toilets and soap to wash hands. There are staff standing near the toilets but they don’t appear to have any function. I suggest that Garuda lets a company that understands service to run their lounges.

The lounge at the international gates is far from International standards. No air con whatsoever. Sandwiches are not tasty. Food is cold and lounge is hot. Worst lounge I have been to in Asia. Not the kind you expect from a 5 stars airline. They should renovate this lounge.

The Domestic Business Lounge here at Denpasar was okay, just here around 30 minutes. The food was ok, the lounge staff not too attentive. Its quite different from Garuda Business Lounge in Jakarta. I want to take a shower before flying - but the towel is unavailable and I must wait the towel from Garuda International Lounge.

This must be the worst lounge. Hot with no aircon and it is open to all terminal noise. Poor choice of food although at least we had some. On other occasions it has run out. They have an almost non existent beverage selection. Beer and wine was warm. Red wine was chilled.

T3 International Lounge has enough space with some food and beverage selection. Hot towel also provided for refresh our face or hand. WiFi connection was good. Lots of comfortable seat. Location is behind First class lounge, so need to walk more because we have to pass First class lounge first.

Dnata lounge at Singapore that Garuda Indonesia use. Food looked like it had been there for hours without being refreshed. Selection of food is what you would expect from a low-cost/budget carrier, not a 5-star airline where you pay roughly €2200 for a ticket. Showers were dirty: hairs on the walls, stains and dirt in the sink. Overall a very disappointing experience compared to our flight from Amsterdam - the KLM lounge at Schiphol was 100x better than the DNATA lounge at Changi Singapore. Also very poor wifi - we were not even able to do a simple facetime audio call.

A new lounge with nice ambience at Jakarta Terminal 3, but needs a lot of improvement. No enough seat during the peak hours, some of the seats are located far away from the pantry and rather dark. The layout does not seem to consider that many travellers are solo, so no need to have too many 3/4-seater sofas. The way it is arranged today, requires one to trespass others when walking in/out to get food, quite unpleasant. Not all has proper coffee table, so it was quite uncomfortable. Food & drink quality is low, did not match with the ambience. Staff needs more training to be more professional in presentation and attitude. I noticed a few giggling & chatting in public space exposed to passengers. It is brand new but due to low maintenance, things already got dirty, staff do not bother to really clean the place. It is quite disheartening to see the mismatch of the expensive facility with the quality of manpower. If no firm intervention by the management, I am afraid in no time this lounge will turn into a rundown ugly old lounge.

We have experienced the Garuda Bali lounge once again. I am not sure why a prestigous airline like Garuda use this. The beverage access is non existant and when the wine comes its warm. The staff are nice but speak very little English. The food is very average. Surely someone will read these reviews and act on them?

Sad end to a excellent Bali holiday and extremely poor compared to the rest of Garuda's offering. Open to the main concourse and very hot and stuffy. Last thing you want having battled your way to the airport. Wine and beer only available on request, but nothing to indicate you need to order except for other helpful passengers. Food looks like it has been there for hours, coffee tastes like dish water. Definitely the worst business lounge I've experienced.

New Terminal 3 lounge that is remarkably poor in absolutely every aspect. How could they produce this type of facility in 3017. Design and layout is a joke, food a disgrace, signage poor, air con not working. Seating awkward and uncomfortable. Limited toilets that were available for use - cramped and difficult to get around people.

The lounge is located on the left side of Garuda Indonesia's executive lounge. For the first class lounge they dont provide buffet menu, but a la carte. A few snacks and sandwiches are available at the mini table (if you want some buffet you can just walk in to executive lounge and the choices have more variety (mostly Indonesians food). The A La Carte menu only has small choices and i chose the fish option accompanied by Chardonay which tasted surprisingly good. The minus points are that the menu book is in poor quality which looks like has been used for a long time without any changing, and the humidity in the lounge is very high, probably because the lounge is in an opened area which gets very noisy sometimes from the announcements. Overall the lounge facility cannot be compared with The Pier First or Al Safwa but the service from staff a top notch.

Lounge is reasonably comfortable. Air conditioning and general air circulation is very poor. The food...I sat in the lounge for nearly 7 hrs. During that time the bulk of the food sat there as well. All food exposed to the air had dried out, gone cold and hard in relation to bread. Most dishes were flourishing with bar like flies. I would recommend eating downstairs and using the lounge as a semi quiet place to wait for your flight. Staff were polite. Nowhere to plug your usb in unless you have a power convertor. Nothing noted to be child friendly either in this lounge. Children would become very bored. No screen to advise of flight gates or status either.

This Domestic Executive lounge is a comfortable place to wait for the departure flight, friendly staff, clean environment which may be due to a new place, provided a smoking room there. The place was also in line with Garuda Indonesia departure gate so make it easier to ride at the departure gate

My holiday began with visiting the New Sky Team Lounge at Sydney International Airport as I was flying with Garuda to Bali. The lounge is very contemporary with a very clean fit-out, lots of space for easy movement and great views of the Airport. The main thing the Lounge needs to work on is the food options as it was very limited and not the amazing quality that it needs to be. Internet connectivity was efficient and staff was very attentive, overall a great experience.

Flying home with Garuda Business Class, I decided to give their Lounge a visit.  I think the Lounge needs a much prominent space and entry as I walked into the wrong lounge. Two aspects which I think needs to be worked on is the space of the Lounge, it should be bigger and the food options, as it should have more of a western menu and alcohol should be freely available instead of having to ask for it. The staff were very attentive which reflected Garuda's customer service qualities, overall good experience.

I was so disappointed in this lounge. Firstly, it was in an open area above the shopping part of the airport. It was really warm and I ended up hot and with a headache. There was no alcohol in the fridges and by the time I realised you needed to ask for it, I needed to board. The food was appalling. It was luke warm and minimal.  I got to the airport early for my departure from Bali to enjoy the lounge, how wrong I was. It ended up being a long wait. The internet was extremely slow also. The toilets were also not working and instead of teaming up with another lounge on the same floor, we had to go back down staris into the public area. Now public toilets don't bother me and that's not the issue, the issue is they were so far from the lounge. Ridiculous. So sad to be writing a review like this.

The new skyteam lounge has just been opened a few months, it is located near gate 15 in downstairs, occupying what used to be the old Qantas lounge area. It was completely re-designed with comfort and space in mind. There was enough food and drinks, some alcohol beverages. It's fairly peaceful and a nice space to spend an hour or two. All Skyteam airline members share it.

This Garuda Indonesia business class lounge in Jakarta is substandard. Lack of fresh food options and lack of space being the two main reasons. Felt like it was understaffed as there was no one to make sure the passengers they escorted from the Premium Check-in Desk actually did get a seat.

Lounge in Denpasar was above the main shopping area and not enclosed so the noise level was louder than I would have liked, as well as being stuffy and warm. The food was appalling - was minimal, lukewarm, and tasteless. Drinks - there was very minimal selection of alcoholic beverages. One choice of wine and Bintang, normal soft drink selections, juice was horrid. Comfy chairs, charging stations for phones, laptops etc and free wifi. I would have rather paid for food at one of the new eateries downstairs (eg Hard Rock Cafe) than eat at the lounge. One other downside is you cannot hear announcements and the screen for departures was at the front of the lounge. This meant we had to continuously check the time and check the board to see when we needed to leave for our gate.

This is a poor excuse for a business class lounge. There are no toilet facilities, there is no service other than two female staff members at the entry with very little interest in anything. Milk for the coffee machine was warm, the food appeared to have been sitting there for some time with no visible signs of any member of staff attending to it. Other facilities that one would expect from a business class lounge non existent. I was informed the new lounge will be opening within the month. Garuda have let themselves down considerably, there are other lounge areas at the airport available that Garuda could attempt to make use of. If not at minimum provide $25 USD to first and business class passengers to make use of the TG Premium lounge available to all whom visit the airport and are willing to pay.

I  agree with other negative ratings of this lounge. It is a disgrace, staff service non existent, facilities zero. The hot food (chicken and fish) was cold and the when I asked how long it had been out was told 3 hours - the only response from the staff member on the front desk was to heat it up. I suggested that it would be better to replace it. Finally after 2 hours and more complaints it was replaced with fish in soggy batter.

The Garuda staff said that this Emerald Sky Lounge has just been refurbished with new facility and design. It's good to find one shower in this lounge, very much help after arriving from a late night flight. They offered wide range of food choices for breakfast time, including mung bean soup, fried rice, Indonesian fried noodle, breads and pastries. A very fulfilling and relaxing lounge experience while waiting for next flight.

Apart from the chaos that is Sydney International Airport, the new Skyteam lounge that Garuda Indonesia use is a delight. Lots of zones, eating, resting, working and waiting. Nice selection of foods at breakfast time for both western and Asian tastes. Plenty of recharging points, and a nice ambience overlooking the tarmac.

Met at arrival gate by two friendly uniformed staff who helped with hand luggage and navigated us to the sweet quiet and classy ambience of the first class lounge. A Steinway grand provided a background to our restful stay. The lounge is divided into 4 areas. A dining area where we enjoyed a preflight meal chosen from an interesting menu, and in my case designed nicely for a vegetarian. The broth was delightful and the fine beverages were discreetly topped up. Second there is a shower area and an enclosed smoking room and an area with a sign saying reflexology. Shower was spacious perfectly clean and equipped with L'occitane toiletries and a Toto bidet. The third area is for personal tv viewing where I caught my AFL team the Lions, doing what they do best - finishing with the wooden spoon. The final area has semi private sleep lounges assisted by the background piano. Collected at exactly the right time for a wander to the gate just prior to departure.

Whilst this is apparently still a temporary venue, it is an insult to passengers who've paid good money to travel Business Class. What makes this seem even worse is that most Garuda flights to Australia leave Bali very late in the evening. Customers arrive at the lounge after a late checkout from their hotel, feeling tired, looking forward to catching a few hours sleep on the 'flat bed', it is reasonable to assume that they may wish to enjoy a few quiet drinks and a light meal before hopping onto the plane. There are some single armchairs, no tables for putting food/ drinks on, very few power outlets, poor reading materials, no private areas, with the food choices/presentation befitting a canteen. Luckily I had read that it was possible to get a wine/ beer if you know that you must ask for it.  This is all such a pity because the actual flying experience is very good and quite comparable to other airlines charging similar prices for their premium travel.

Absolutely ridiculous that this lounge is still a temporary lounge - the airport has been built, restaurants are open other lounges have been open for more than six months and Garuda  still haven't got their act together. I'm told that Bintang isn't available till 7pm? Maybe Garuda should consider giving a refund to compensate travellers who have paid for business class expecting service - or team up with an open Lounge the other airlines have done. It's not rocket science. And even if Garuda insist on keeping the temporary lounge, at least provide a decent service - it wouldn't kill you.

The lounge have lots of facilities and is overall satisfied. with plenty of seats nice view to the airside friendly staffs. But air-conditional not always working the lounge is a little bit warm. The lounge does not have much food to eat but with enough kind of drink. I went for shower two times (I booked return trip) the first time the shower room it have no shampoo gels or even towels but the second time it was just like an 4 star hotel room which is tidy and with all the things i want.

This is definitely not a business class lounge there are no toilet facilities - you have to use the public ones. Food is ok but wine is below average and you have to chase a staff member to get a wine or beer. We keep being told that this is a temporary lounge but no one can ever tell us when the new lounge will be ready - the new airport has been open some 18 months now - how long can is possibly take. It is disappointing as the facilities onboard in business class are very good with the Lounge in Denpasar being the only let down.

I have seen the business class lounge a few times and whilst the staff are nice and food is okay the rest is overcrowded with poor showers and very limited seating at peak times. Now I use the First Class lounge and what a difference. Restaurant style dining beautiful shower rooms nice TV pods. Staff okay but the aircon is switched down and you need blankets to keep warm!

The lounge cannot qualify as either a Business or certainly not First class lounge and should not be promoted as such. Food is at best basic dipping to appalling. No alcohol served unless asked for then only beer and wine and not promoted. They have been promising a new lounge for 12 months. The old lounge in the old terminal although sub average was better. No shower or restroom given 1 star to both bar and restroom only because I can't submit without adding a score!

Transit of 8 hours after arriving in from Australia to connect onto AMS. Lounge extremely warm one half closed off until close to 8pm. Food terrible alcohol hidden behind a bar never saw any staff member there finally helped myself. No towels in shower asked reception however nothing happened. Major gripe was after asking if I could pay to upgrade to first class was told they could not help me and I would need to go to cashier which is located landside. Therefore I was expected to clear customs to access this. Why couldn't they pick up the phone and ask? Major difference in staff compared to the inflight cabin crew who were outstanding in business class. Not impressed at all.

Domestic departures was through the old domestic arrivals area. Business lounges for both domestic and international flights were fenced off parts of the main concourses with no computers available. No alcohol was on display but I discovered that in the international lounge a waitress would bring you a glass of wine if you asked for one.

No alcoholic beverages are available (or at least not on display). The domestic lounge had very worn furniture with rips in some of the upholstery. The domestic lounge had a shower in the mens toilet which I used but only cold water.

This lounge (Korean Air lounge) is spacious and lots comfortable chairs. Internet speed is good but the choice of foods are limited. Although for some passengers food may not be the things to look for but I like to try local foods and due to time constraints in certain country lounges may be the last place to try and have some local dish.

Lounges set up was nice lots of lights. Because of this lighting which is good but it has disadvantages - generates heat and room temperatures becomes warmer. Staff are very friendly and helpful although they need further training. Supervisors and Lounge manager should be try harder to make this lounge to be among the best.

This is still a temporary lounge which is simply partitioned off from the rest of the terminal. Didn't have and food or drink. Lounges comfortable but only just enough available. As it is really just a part of the main concourse it suffers from the continuous announcements. Not really relaxing but better than the main terminal I guess. Will be interested to see what GA comes up with once the terminal works are complete.

Much better than the old lounge in the old airport but very different what they tell you on the web site. Only beer and vodka available. Food extremely limited. No service. No lounge toilets and have to use public toilets outside. Nice comfortable chairs.

Garuda Business Flyer so went into the separate part for Business Class not much in way of food or beverages sitting where everybody who walks past to departure lounges looks in. Better off paying and going to the Premier Lounge.

Lounge was very small with comfy chairs that were now quite dirty and stained. Food selection poor. Magazines and papers were available at the door and there was a tv. Lounge staff announced departing flights. The 1 female toilet was very dated and had a dodgy lock.

The lounge was large with a variety of comfy chairs. There was a quiet room that had a 3 seater couch and other small chairs and tables. There were 3 computers and lots of powerpoint/recharge points for laptops and tablets. The food selection was good although I felt there was more on the Asian side and as I am a bit finicky I was not so fussed. Lots of drinks and hubby was even given a refrigerated glass for his beer. The facilities were very clean and tidy as was the bathroom shower. There was a shower but there did not appear to be any towels and when I commented on the shower to the bathroom attendent but there was no mention of clean towels forthcoming. The staff were fabulously friendly. Our flight was delayed 3 hours and the staff passed around blankets and as it was late they turned down the piped music and dimmed the lights.

Lounge isn't really Business Class quality and it doesn't give much privacy. At the time I entered the Lounge there were many children running around. Food selection not very good just cheese sandwiches.

This is one of the best Lounge at Jakarta airport nicely designed with comfy furniture with views over the apron. Free wifi and workstations are available. As my flight to Bangkok is in the morning they served breakfast with egg stations with live cooking plenty of toast juices coffee/tea and plenty of reading materials.

In fact its not a lounge for Business Class ticket holders its a lounge for anyone with $12.00 to spend on entrance. The lounge was old worn out and full of people who had paid the $12.00 for the privilege of a good TV free booze and snacks. Can't blame them but there was no place to sit so we stood outside.

As soon you clear customs when departing you will be approached by Garuda employees offering you access to the Garuda Lounge for $100.000 rph Take my advice and jump on it. We all paid the $100.000 rph and headed in. Bintang on tap spirits food tea coffee and free internet access on their computers. Staff ask you what flight you are on and will let you know when its last drinks and time to board. Worth every cent.

Lounge is located in right in the front of entry way from check in rows so it is easy to find. The selection of food is quite vary mainly Indonesian fare but there are some western style selection as well. Beverages selection quite plenty with beer available as well for free of charge. The lounge can be quite crowded in the morning and late afternoon. Bathroom were clean with staff kept going around and cleaning them. Staff were very helpful but they need to improve their English to serve their non Indonesian customers. Overall the lounge is very good compare to European standards.

Visited the lounge 3 times in July. Not a bad facility - not the best but serves its purpose. Gets really crowded in the peak morning departure times but quiet at other periods. Staff quite friendly but not much chat with customers. A fair choice of hot and cold food but needs to be improved to match airlines such as Malaysia Cathay Singapore etc. Small smoking room area nice bar area at one end and 2 internet terminals = wifi not working when I visited the lounge. Washrooms very basic and the 1 shower room was so unpresentable that I preferred not to use it! Not bad for Garuda but they could so much better!

Garuda Indonesia executive lounge is the biggest lounge facility at Soekarno-Hatta Airport. Located in Terminal E-F the lounge occupies an area of 1.419m2 comprising a 757sq m domestic executive lounge with a seating capacity of 148 seats and a 662sq m international executive lounge of 114 seats. The new lounge offers an array of facilities - fully-equipped business center with meeting rooms and IT support a quiet room a refreshment area with shower nursery a luggage area and praying room. As opposed to existing lounges that cater to credit card holders the new lounge is reserved exclusively for the comfort of Garuda Indonesia's Business Class passengers and Garuda Frequent Flyer (GFF) Gold and Platinum card members or Executive Card Plus members.
Dreadful place on every level. 1980s decor, filthy, loud, muzak blaring at a decibel level at which it's hard to work or relax, terrible selection of sad looking sandwiches. Typical Copa.

Mediocre lounges Terminal I & 2 have identical food, essentially appetizers. Dips, raw veggies, tiny sandwiches, cookies, and taco chips. Breakfast includes fruit and oatmeal. Enough to keep you from being hungry, but not a satisfying meal. Decent bar. Coffee drinks tend to be very sweet. Terminal 1 leather chairs look very grimy. Doubt they have ever been cleaned. It is basically, one large room, so can get quite noisy. Very tired, a bit dirty. Lots of food debris on ground, by evening Terminal 2 lounge is new, so much cleaner, brighter. One section has a good view of the concourse, but also consequently noisy. The sectioning of the lounge into several areas, partly with a glass wall, reduces noise in inner areas. Toilet paper gone by 11am and bathroom floors dirty. Seems to be better maintained, with fewer dirty dishes piled up. More appealing bar.

Poor lounge with non existing food or drinks except cheap packaged foods and soft drinks served at the bar, on demand, in a plastic cup. Unrestricted access as the noisy lounge is overtaken by ultimately any credit card holder and their families, including infants and shoppers returning from their shopping spree in Orlando.

Way too many people in the lounge. Business class passengers are piled up wit daily admission fee paying visitors lounge, frequent flyers, Credit card holders. Not like a place to find quietness and working conditions. Food is about non existent.
Beautiful lounge, however food is so poor, two kinds of mini-sandwiches, bits of celery and carrot, and packaged crackers. There is more variety in the bar, that in snacks and real food not be found.

This lounge is a disgrace. In fact, it can barely be called a lounge. It’s seems like it’s easentially a slightly more comfortable space than the sub-standard airport beneath it. Firstly, there is a distinct lack of food - no hot food at all. If you love cheese and crackers with a side of carrot and cucumber sticks then you’ll be fine but if you are looking for sustenance then good luck to you. It is extremely overcrowded and at times impossible to find a seat or get served at the bar. People take the word lounge to a new level and are happy to give a seat to their bag while someone walks around like a lost dog trying to find a place to sit. The Internet is an embarrassment, I have never been to an airport or a lounge with such dire bandwidth. I feel sorry for the staff. They are lovely and are bombarded by hundreds of people trying to enter the lounge. It’s a constant stream that never ends. As a result, the lounge is littered with the remnants of discarded cracker packs and empty bottles. It looks like a rubbish club at the end of the night. My advice would be don’t bother, find a place to park up in the airport and buy yourself a beer.

This was the worst. Food was horrible: cheap crackers and awful snacks. Lounge consistently overcrowded; at peak hours, not even a seat available. Staff tries to be gracious, but overwhelmed by number of guests who flood in, so none of the usual niceties such as informing you personally when your flight is boarding. When I passed through in March, not even a men's room available. Was being remodeled, so had to take elevator back downstairs and walk through terminal. Only saving grace is that long wait in Panama Tocumen terminal would be even worse, so measuring Copa's lounge against that minimal standard I suppose it's worth the trouble. But not by much.

It is crowded, small for the amount of people that visits the lounge. It is very poor in services, it is probably the poorest lounge in food options I have ever visited. The restrooms are also very small for the number of people going into the lounge.

They lounge has been upgraded and is larger since I visited it last, however there was very little to eat or drink in the morning. The choices were banana, apple, and a packed muffin. I think is the lounge with the poorest selection anywhere. Just a little more to satisfy the hunger of the Business Class passengers as the food on board is poor also.

Poor, very poor. Supposedly they have WiFi but it did not work. They dont have computers, you enter the "lounge" and you are disconnected from the world. There is some hot meals, good for that, lounge is not very nice in appearance, it is crowded too many guests for its size even though it is large

For a Hub lounge, everything is minimal in this lounge. Food is almost inexistent. Even if there is a bar refreshment are minimal. Because there is no food I went outside in the food court to buy something and when i came back to the lounge I was told that food is not allowed inside the lounge and i had to eat my sushis outside. This all thing was in line with the business class experience with Copa Airlines which is a huge disappointment when you compare with Air France, Air Canada or any Middle East Airlines.

The lounge was overcrowded and sometimes is difficult to get a seat. Basic snacks selection, drinks, shower and business private room available. WiFi sometimes is very weak and even in the lounge it may not work.

All Star Alliance passengers must be aware that Copa Airlines doesn't offer any lounge service at Quito international Airport to business or any other status passenger. A very basic airport lounge available for a fee. A few priority seats available at the gate. Worth to say that not enough seats available.

Copa Airlines is a fine small airline that works very well if you flight between Central American countries. But, in Los Angeles Copa Airlines use the United Airlines lounge. I travel a lot, an this is the poorest, saddest and most depressing lounge that you can find. What happened with the American service? The bar has an attendant that you have to tip, this is incredible. The food is not that good and there is no choice. Magazines? Yes, The United magazine.

On 26 August 2015 I visited the Copa Club at Juan Santamaria Airport serving San Jose, Costa Rica. The lounge is located in the basement next to the food court. Obviously, there are no views, but the space is comfortable, the WIFI is dependable, the employees are gracious, and the bar is free and adequate.

I revisited the Copa Club at Panama's Tocumen Airport on 26 August 2015. The club is still difficult to find, but the food offering, particularly the bags of Lay's potato chips, are better than I remembered. Also, while there is a good selection of standard free drinks at the bar, there is also complimentary sparkling wine available on request. The lounge is busy and crowded, but the views are excellent. I was more impressed on this visit than I was in July.

Tocumen Airport in Panama is not particularly large, but it sprawls out over a good distance. The Copa Club is centrally located, but it is very difficult to find. The entrance is relatively small and nondescript. There is no signage to help confused passengers, and the directions given by airport employees only made matters worse.
