I am a retired Spanish teacher, so this wasn't a language problem. A few well-placed signs would solve this problem easily. Once the club is found, it becomes obvious that their template for airport lounges comes from the United Club. The food and drink choices are a mirror image of United's with one exception - quality alcoholic beverages are free. I would recommend the airline but not the lounge.

Comfortable and attractive enough but a rather crowded lounge which is difficult to locate. Ground staff are not very helpful and lounge staff not very welcoming. Very little food and limited drinks available. Not a bad place but these and other customer service issues as well as limited facilities and food make this a very basic lounge that will not be remembered well by any visitor. No one would look forward to a second visit.

I had a four hour layover in Nadi as I flew between Australia and California. It was welcome respite and I enjoyed use of the shower to freshen up. The lounge was very nicely appointed, well staffed and had a separate glassed off area of children so that they could run around, play, be loud but not disturb the adults. This was wonderful for both children and adults! Internet connectivity was excellent although the ready availability of plugs and power was less than I'm used to in airline lounges. Nevertheless, I was able to find power and settle into a comfortable cubby which allowed me to sit, lay and lounge. The food choices, although not hugely extensive, were more extensive than is typically the case for domestic American airlines. Everything was tasty although some of the items were a bit heavy on grease and fat for my preference. The beverage service was outstanding with availability of a variety of alcoholic and non-alcoholic choices. The lounge was clean and kept continually clean by an attentive and smiling staff. The only significant drawback of this lounge from my point of view is that on beautiful Fiji, the lounge is under ground and without windows to look out. This was compensated for to some degree by the decor and by large walls that had live plants on them. Nevertheless, it would have been great to be able to look out on the tropical environment and sunshine.

The Qantas lounge is great with wine selection, two hot entrees, two salads, snacks and deserts to choose from. Full bar, 2 televisions, and comfortable seating. They even had a shower! This was the best lounge offered by Fiji Airways and a fantastic way to start my return journey.

Fiji Airways use a shared lounge with Philippine Airlines and others at LAX, overlooking the busy international terminal. The food wasn't fresh - no hot offerings, but the people were nice. It was a great place to wait for a flight. LAX has done a good job with the new terminal.

After an overnight international flight, I really wanted a shower at this Fiji Airways lounge. I had a 4 hour layover and was told they were out of towels and more would arrive by 8am. My flight left at 930am, and the towels had still not arrived. There was limited food - a coffee machine worked on the outbound, but not on the return. Better food selections in the evening on my return.

Disgusting. Hands down one of the dirtiest lounges I've ever had the misfortune of stepping foot in. The seats? Filthy. The chairs and sofas are absolutely revolting, covered in crumbs. The food selection is actually decent, surprisingly. The staff weee roo busy gossiping to even pretend to care about the state of the place. This dump is ancient, falling apart at the seams. And the music? Some god-awful techno that's supposed to be 'relaxing'? Please. Avoid this place at all costs. It's an absolute disgrace.

The Smiles lounge in Terminal 2 Rio de Janeiro (GIG) International Airport opened in 1999 as the VARIG main lounge in Brazil (Smiles is the name of Varig's frequent flyer program now with GOL Airlines). At that time it was the best South America lounge and was used by Star Alliance (Lufthansa United and of course Varig). It was an outstanding lounge with separated areas for first class and business class showers smoke room plenty of reading materials excellent beverages and high quality food. In 2008 Varig went out of business and GOL acquires Varig routes mileage program and VIP lounges. Strangely as GOL uses the Terminal 1 they continued using these lounge in Terminal 2 so it is impossible to board a GOL flight and use its own lounge. The lounge is used by a lot of airlines (Lufthansa United US Airways Diners Club card menbers among others). The good part is that as a big lounge it never get crowded they have good (a bit used) furniture and luxury res trooms. Unfortunately the first class section is now closed the drinks offered are cheap and the food minimal.

Hong Kong Airlines Bauhinia lounge was a very relaxing place. Food was very limited but okay to good. Loved the egg tart and the sweet tofu. Staff was welcoming. The place is very cozy and you can choose to stay in quiet and relaxing areas or bright and busy areas. I also like the location because it is easy to find.

Used this lounge as a Philippine Airlines customer. The lounge is pretty small, but relatively well kept. Food selection a little limited, but the drink selection is respectable. The beer available is Tsing Tao, but not a deal breaker. Good wine selection. Wifi speed is good. No gate announcements, but the staff makes it a point to monitor the flights of the patrons.

Written from the Hong Kong Airlines lounge in HKG prior to my flight to Hanoi. This is a small but quite comfortable lounge with spectacular views onto the tarmac and the active runway. The receptionists are friendly, and the staff bustles about keeping everything clean and neat. There is a good variety of food options, although most cater to Asian tastes, which is to be expected. The bar is self-service and well stocked - including top shelf spirits and an acceptable sparkling wine. One small negative is that there is no hot water in the lavatory for washing up. This was my also my complaint about EVA's Star Lounge at TPE. I miss the old HKG at Kai Tak, but if you are going to be at the new airport, this is a very pleasant place to await your flight.

Accommodating staff in this longue not too big but with all the comforts. Good wifi signal and the availability of internet access points with iMac 27". Buffet with a great choice of Chinese and international dishes, cooked expressed, fresh fruit and good choice of drinks. Very attentive to our every request, relaxing atmosphere.

Located near the gate 23 of Hong Kong Airport, this is a very good lounge, spacious and plenty of seating. Good food and drinks choices available, with some made to order options. Free wifi and quiet separate area for a lie down and shut eye. Particularly impressive is the fact that it overlooks the tarmac, gives you a sense of going on a holiday. This is a great place to spend an hour or two before flying.

A very impressive lounge located near gate 23 with a clear view of the runway. The variety of food and drinks offered is amazing, staff are very friendly and helpful. Plenty of room to lounge about, computers and printers available. There is also an area where you can take a quite nap which is dimly lit and away from the crowd. It is worth mentioning that some dishes are available by ordering, they make fresh for you, a very nice touch indeed.

Quite a nice rather small lounge positioned one level down from the main gate area. Staff were very nice and friendly when I visited and offered help for everything. Good selection of hot and cold food and wide choice of beverages wine etc. Managed to find newspapers ands magazines that I like found a comfortable sleep and relaxed for 2 hours. Lacking of shower facilities but I guess there is no room to offer this in the facility looking at the size. For a small airline I thought this was a great lounge overall - and it was staff service that was so nice.

We used the Hawaiian Club at Honolulu for inter-island flights. While it is nice that Hawaiian does provide a lounge for these very short flights, the club was not very impressive when it comes to snacks and drinks. There was a machine for fountain drinks, a coffee machine and tea. No snacks were offered when we were there. That was a bit disappointing. It is a quiet place and good enough if you want to work. No windows to distract you. The furniture seemed to be new and it was clean. Better than nothing but definitely it a reason to go to the airport earlier.

As an international business class lounge, this Plumeria Lounge is a big failure. Overall vibe is cheap and thrown together. Food and drink offerings are pathetic. Staff is cold and some were not great English speakers. If Hawaiian wants to play with the big boys on an international scale they need to do much better then this embarrassment.

The Hawaiian Airlines lounge at Hilo Airport recently had a refurbishment and it looks better. The wifi is super fast, but the lounge can get crowded due to it being a frequent flyer lounge not business lounge. It has limited snacks and coffee that's it - and 2 TVs. No announcements are made, so you have to keep eye on time for your flight. Also there is no bathroom in the lounge. There is also no staff in the lounge.

Hawaiian Airlines Plumeria lounge at Honolulu Airport is a great improvement over the old frequent flyer lounge. Good wine bar, snacks, sandwiches sweets and a much quieter atmosphere. This lounge is for international business passengers only.

As an Hawaiian platinum member and business/first passenger, Hawaiian Airlines have always had a very poor lounge in Honolulu with coffee soft drink and wifi only. Their new first lounge upstairs at Honolulu has a wine bar, more snacks, sandwiches etc, a good coffee machine and a very quiet location. Good wifi and staff.  All it is missing is beer and spirits and it would be a true first/business lounge.

The lounge has undergone renovation to make it cleaner and a better layout. For frequent flyers it's a good lounge wife coffee soft drinks and packet nibbles for first or business it's not a good
lounge. No cocktails or hot food any sort of meals. Hawaiian would do better enticing more business and first class if they made a lounge for those classes as well as keeping their frequent flyer lounge. At Honolulu airport you are limited to lounge use. I'm a sapphire one world and no lounges available.

Furniture appears to be from the mid 80s. Not comfortable. No private toilets. Has a soda dispenser and a few coffee thermoses. No TV showing flight status. There appears to be a desk for an attendant but no staff were seen for the two hours we were there. There is free WiFi but that's about the only reason to visit this lounge. It's worth noting however that the WiFi login page's certificate was expired.

The lounge itself is clean and well maintained. Seats are comfortable and it provides a respite from the noise of the rest of the terminals. The lounge falls short on catering miserably. People who pay premium prices for first/business class service or for Premier/Pualani Gold/Platinum memberships deserve far more than juice packets pretzels and coffee which they receive in coach class flights. Especially when other airline club lounges offer much more in varieties of foods like pastries fruits hot/cold foods beverages including alcoholic beverages. Hawaiian should work on this.

This has to go down as the worst airline lounge I have been in. The air was thick with the smell of stale cigarette smoke it is a non smoking lounge. There is no food on offer not even a cracker and signs everywhere stating outside food is not allowed in lounge - offer some food if you don't want guests bringing it in. Coffee soda and juice are the items on offer. Very poor for a Business lounge Hawaiian Airlines should be ashamed.
Truly pathetic no food, no alcohol? Coffee and soft drinks? Extremely lame by world standards. One would think they would improve their offering considering what their partners like Qantas offer.

Very basic and rather poor. Only juices tea and coffee. No food. Seats are rather uncomfortable. We only used the Wi-fi and then went elsewhere to have a drink and something to eat. Not good and no private washrooms.

Pleasant enough space but very very basic. One TV. Juice soft drinks tea coffee & inflight bags of pretzels. No alcohol or other food. They're not licensed! There is free wifi - which is pretty quick.

Hainan Airlines and carriers such as Hong Kong Airlines use the recently completed Hainan Club in terminal 2 at PEK. The room is large and comfortable and quite uncrowded (at least for early morning departures ). There is a good view of the tarmac out the large windows, but there was no activity on the ramp while I was at the club. The food offerings were clearly directed at oriental taste, with elaborate choices for salads, but no traditional western breakfast options. Strangely, there was also a broad range of desserts available at 6:00 AM. Beverage options were generous, including a good quality champagne. The lounge was very well staffed with employees eager to serve and lightning quick to remove used glasses and dishes. I will be visiting the club again on Friday, and I will be curious to see if the food options are more plentiful for afternoon flights.

Very nice international lounge, comfortable and not busy with card holders like too many lounges now. However, I arrived, had a quick look around and had a coffee. When I went for food it had gone, they finish very early, only operating for 1 and a half hours. A member of staff was very helpful but it couldn’t bring the food back!

A highly professional business class lounge with a very good standard. Food nicely prepared, selection is very good. The view is great. The personnel very obliging. Seating possibilities suitable, comfortable and sufficient. Signposting in Beijing airport could be improved.

The Business lounge in Brussels Zaventem airport located in the international terminal (Terminal B) is quite decent. The staff is nice and the lounge is orderly and clean. There's not a lot of space, so, I wonder if it can get packed quickly (never happen to me but, who knows...). The food is actually quite good and there's some Belgian beer to get. The seating itself is comfortable and the wifi is good. Each time I was there, it was pretty silent, people are respectful and it's a nice place to relax before a flight or get some work done.

Arrived for at 5am for a 7am flight with the heavy security presence at Urumqi Airport. However the Hainan Airlines Lounge did not open until 6am. Also, there are actually two separate lounges for Hainan Airlines, either side of the Security Checkpoint in Terminal 2. However the lounge opposite Gate 12 features full dining for about 40 people and a small rest area, the Gate 11 lounge has only snacks and a few drink options with regular airline lounge seating. Upon entering the lounge on opening, it turns out that breakfast would not arrive until 6:30am. However despite this, the staff were great and attentive to passenger needs. The breakfast was mostly suited for Chinese tastes with plenty of small sandwiches available for others who prefer more western tastes. Regardless, it was delicious and good before I rushed off to board my flight. There were computer tablets available for use in the lounge, similar to the onboard IFE tablets, but I did not look at them. As for English newspapers or magazines, there was two editions of the New York Times that were two months old, everything else was in Chinese.

New lounge, beautiful, and well equipped. Very nice service, friendly and helpful staff. Nice drink, but I missed the food due to the short stay due to the long queue in the check-in, but look nice. The only comment is the poor air-conditioning, it was very hot, and talked with staff who has not able to solve the problem, the setting temperature was 16C, but the room temperature was still at 29 C.

The new Hainan Airlines lounge at Beijing Terminal 2 is very well set up! Seats are very comfortable, some faces outside providing a great view of the runway. There are plenty of good foods and beverages. Not to mention the ice cream. The staff are very nice. There were old ladies who wanted fruits. Due to their physical condition, they were not able to attend the bar themselves and they were in a hurry to board their plane. The young lady staff is so nice who packed fruits in small boxes for the two passengers to enjoy later.

For domestic lounge very nice and was quiet when I visited very early after opening I the morning. Chef area was doing cooked noodles etc, but I went to smaller and quieter lounge area where just a cold buffet. Shower and toilet looked clean, staff very courteous and nice, but some of them had limited English language skills. All in all, very good for domestic but needs to be bugger I guess.

New spacious lounge with comfortable chairs and sofas. A special area with massage chairs and TVs. Pod chairs. A business area with PCs. Plenty of outlets and flat screen TVs everywhere. Snacks hot (soup dim sum) and cold (salads sandwiches) and a variety of beverages are available with a central self-service counter international magazines and newspapers. Showers and clean restrooms. Toilets are high tech! WiFi works well. Flights are announced. Separate security checkpoint for first and business class and elite members provides entrance to the lounge which has direct access to gates. English proficiency of some staff was limited.
A quite small lounge and in need of upgrading. Staff very pleasant and friendly reasonable choice of hot food at meal times. Quite crowded when I visited and no internet access working properly.

Lounge is tired. And apparently due for upgrade in a year or two… But the staff are super friendly and helpful even when they are really busy. Food is okay (the chef’s savoury mince is great but it is only on the menu at certain times of the year) Reasonable selection of drinks and snacks. But the staff are its biggest asset.

The concourse C lounge in Dubai is woeful. Totally inadequate toilet and shower facilities for the size of the lounge. Having to “book” a shower in an airlines home lounge is ridiculous, and 3 toilets only for hundreds of people is unacceptable. Food offerings ok.

It was like entering a timber mill or woodwork factory. Anything that wasn’t wood, was the same shade in colour. It was that and the overpowering smell of wood that hit me the moment I entered. It looked old and tired and with a low ceiling. The staff are pleasant enough but there were very few passengers, and it was obvious why. It was the complete opposite to the onboard experience. There was no a-lar-cart dining experience here. It was a serve yourself buffet and while it looked white good – nothing was hot – the egg omelettes were cold and so was the bacon to go with them. There’s café style seating or lounge seating – neither was comfortable. I was pretty happy to leave.

A great lounge with all the necessities offered. Tons of space and seating with ample power outlets. Shower is plenty and cleaned before use. Food and beverage options abound with many options available (e.g., healthy food including detox juices, vegan options, and an ice cream stall). The terminal is designed that passengers are allowed to board their planes directly from the lounge. Great experience indeed.
Multiple food stations, enough seating available and a lovely champagne bar to wind down. Showers are a little small, but no complaints. Washrooms kept very clean.

An outstanding Emirates lounge, recently reopened after covid closure. First rate variety of hot and cold food and likewise with drink, both alcoholic and non alcoholic. The staff could not do enough for me; first class service who help at every stage. In short a great way to begin the journey from Bangkok. Emirates at its very best!

This was the best lounge the best and certainly the largest. It seemed the length of 4 football fields and I actually paced it off end to end for a huge 444 paces or close to 400 yards. The food and spirit selections were very good and the service was excellent.
Best lounge I have visited. Food, seating, beverages, magazines etc - all superb. Well done, way better than the Koru lounge there, or whatever it's called now.

I had to stay a few hours in the Emirates lounge at Singapore airport, giving access to both First and business class pax and  gold and higher I believe. The lounge was pleasant to stay, and extremely well kept. Service was very friendly and prompt - outstanding selection of both alcoholic (some premium brands ), champagne and non alcoholic drinks. Food was good and often replenished - maybe with a - for an European passenger - too many Asian dishes. There was a good choice of European cheeses as well. Bathrooms were clean.

It was very early in the morning so breakfast was served. I only ordered some sparkling water and a fresh orange juice and took some small items from the buffet. Champagne was available. The cheeses were very good as were the breads and pastries; service was very friendly. Lots of magazines and some international newspapers. The restrooms were very clean.

Emirates does not have his own lounge at Brussels airport and is using the lounge of Brussels Airlines called The Suite. Despite friendly at the desk this lounge is very poor; more like a canteen in a supermarket. The food is very basic, some rather not so great looking salads, 2 cold cuts and cheese of very cheap quality. As hot dishes : penne with pesto and beef stew with rice - those dishes were lukewarm and the beef stew was more sauce as meat. Concerning the beverages : there were 2 whiskies, vodka, gin and port - all very basic brands. Same for the wine and the sparkling wine. There were several Belgian beers on tap - during my visit glasses for mineral water and soft drinks were not available : only beer glasses and very small wine glasses. So cola zero in a small wine glass ?? Service was so-so , there were several Belgian and international newspapers and magazines in several languages; not a great place!

The Emirates First Class Lounge Terminal 3, Concourse A in Dubai is a very impressive one. It is luxury, big, shiny and of highest quality. Food and dining options are excellent with different restaurant possibilities. I enjoyed outstanding breakfast here. This lounge occupies the complete 1 floor at the terminal and it has an open design and direct access to all boarding gates. It is huge with even own luxury shops. The showers are excellent and the salons are inviting. Due to its size I do miss the privacy and the intimacy that other first class lounges better offer.

The Emirates First lounge around Terminal 3 C gates is a joke. Stinks of cigarettes, rubbish food, showers that would make a prison look luxurious, really a huge disappointment. Go elsewhere and the compromise is a longer walk to the gate. You will thank me. Once here it’s not worth turning about due to the long walk and effective dead end. Worst lounge I’ve been in for a while, claiming to be First though? Wow. Not even close and way off Emirates usual offering. Avoid!

Very lucky to be gold class member to get to use Emirates business class lounges. The last flight I made back to the UK I had several hours stop over. To be able to use such fantastic business class lounges is a life saver. Shower facilities I have used are spotless after doing a 14 hour flight from Sydney (usually in economy) just the chance to have a refreshing shower upon arrival is unbeatable. The food and drink selection in the lounges I have found have always been excellent as well. The only thing that might be quite nice is to have a few extra of the beds to sleep on, in busy periods they can be all in use.
Emirates Business Class lounge at Dubai International Airport is great. Great service, great food and comfort of seats. I strongly recommend it.

Emirates has a number of business class lounges at Dubai airport and all share a very similar design so it really doesn’t matter which one you are in they all have a similar look. While the lounges may look similar. The lounge in concourse B I think is the best but it is huge which means it can get incredibly busy especially around the main food and bar area but if you head to the ends it tends to be a bit quieter. The standard food and beverage offerings at all the lounges are the same and given the varied customer base they have passing through they have something for everyone. Unique to the B lounge is the lovely and usually quieter Moet & Chandon champagne bar which I think had four different champagne offerings and some light snacks that seemed to complement the champagne very well. Also in the B lounge is a branch of Costa Coffee which is a huge chain in the UK and offers a huge varieties of barista made coffees and other drinks and a popular spot to grab something as you are leaving the lounge. Overall the Emirates lounges are pretty good but the one in B area has a few extra touches which make it in my opinion the best choice for eligible passengers even if your flight is leaving from that terminal.

Flying out of Amsterdam Emirates uses the Aspire lounge for its premium customers which given the overall experience I have had with Emirates is a little disappointing given the usual quality of their own lounges. While there is nothing wrong with the lounge it was crowded and had a limited selection of food and drink and used plates didn't seem to get collected during my visit.

Overall excellent quality. Large variety of products and very good quality. Quiet area, fairly good shower. We arrived early so you can see the staff checking if the food display match the company requirements.

Emirates are by now one of the more expensive airlines in Business Class. Their on board provisions and services for this class are excellent. The Dubai lounge is nothing better than a posh train station. It is huge, full of people, and the so called "quiet area" lacks a requisite number of bed and is very noisy. Who on earth has designed this place? It is located right above the main shopping mall and not noise shielded from it. There is only a head high glass wall and an open ceiling. You hear all the pinging of the tills, luggage rattling across tiles, courtesy scooters tooting, some flight announcements and the general hub bub of people talking. It is one of the worst business lounges I have ever visited. When you pay £3000 for a return business ticket UK to Mauritius, you can expect better, especially with a 9 hour stop over in Dubai. A good reason for not flying Emirates on Business Class again.

Now this is one of the best lounges. You  get state-of-the-art emirates service in a very clean and luxury environment. The best is that the lounge is located in front of the track with a view over all landing and departing planes. So if you are passionate into aviation this lounge is hell of a fun.

We flew back from Geneva to Sydney changing planes in Dubai, both flights were with Emirates with a four hour wait (or stop over then changing planes) at Dubai Airport. Entering into the Business Class lounge was very large and impressive. The toilets were very clean..thanks to the toilet staff. The food and drink variety on display was average. After flying with other airlines I was expecting much better. Was totally disappointed and upset with the lack off organisation when my husband and I tried to book in for a shower and freshen up before boarding with Emirates for our second part of our journey to Sydney. It was chaos at the counter for the ladies and mens showers at the time. The male behind the counter was servicing all the men around me when I was first in line to be serviced.  I eventually had to speak up to be noticed. That turned me right off Emirates and the staff. Did not have a shower in the end. Never again! There were two showers areas it was further away from the entrance near the eatery area. Something so small but equal respect is important to me!

The staff on duty was not at all in a welcoming mood and was so rude in communication. Even though the card is charged (for my family members), the attitude remains same. The lounge is overwhelmed with passengers and no place to sit. After a struggle we were able to find a place to sit together. The food and beverages kept were below standard and no choices with very limited option. But at the same time I can see some of the passengers were served with special privileges and with hidden things, not visible for other passengers. The wash room is so small and ended up in queue. It is not cleaned in regular intervals and was so smelly and dirty. Hygiene wise sub standard and we didn't use these toilets. I never expected such an experience in Dubai airport.

The Emirates lounge at Bangkok has almost everything except views of the tarmac/runway. The food choices are rivaled only by the Turkish lounge at Istanbul. The beverage choices are the best - top shelf liquor and Moët Chandon champagne. The lounge is a little difficult to find, but once there, you can enjoy comfortable seating in an uncrouded environment. The desk attendants are personable and eager to please, and the wait staff bustle about keeping the tables clean and the food well stocked. Although there are showers, the sinks in the bathroom do not appear to have hot water.

This is the largest lounge in Dubai in the A Concourse of Terminal 3. There is plenty of space, a fine business work center, and  one can board the A380 directly from the gates alongside the lounge. The downsides are the wait times for the showers and the toilets and the absence of a sleeping area. The wifi connection was either down or terribly slow. On a couple of occasions I had to spend several hours in this lounge for a connecting flight and each time I missed the absence of a quiet sleeping area with flatbed seats. Strangely such sleeping areas are available in the much smaller lounge in Concourse B. The food selection in all the food areas is adequate but nothing great. Vegetarians would have a very limited selection. My wait time for using the shower was over 45 minutes and this was during the leaner period in the early morning hours. There are also minor defects such as the absence of toasters in any of the food areas. One has to approach the staff to even get bread toasted. Since there is so much space in this lounge Emirates could easily designate a quiet area and have more showers as well. And they need to pay attention to the poor wifi service and limited food selection.

The space is inviting and comfortable. Plenty of seating was available, fast internet and restrooms/showers were  clean and spacious. Food and beverage options was somewhat limited, but tasted good overall. The staff were very attentive and pleasant though I think they need to speak more english. Not the best Lounge location I have experienced form Emirates, but an enjoyable experience before a 9 hour flight.

Due to being treated to yet another ludicrous 30/35 minute bus tour of the Dubai Airport complex I had close to no time for my connection. Ran up to the lounge, had a short wait for the bathroom which seemed clean and well maintained then had a quick shower. The shower area was clean and tidy and the attendant was helpful. I had no time to take advantage of food or any of the services in the lounge and had to run to make my next connection flight. In my very short time running in and out after using the shower it looked quite busy but tidy and clean. Hopefully I won’t have to enjoy another bus tour next time I connect through Dubai and can actually enjoy using the lounge next time.

Very nice lounge and easy to find everything. In transit time between Colombo to Melbourne was I used for over 2 hours and after taking foods, drink i continued my flight. This lounge location is up front stairs corner of the near arrival immigration. The Emirates Lounge is located in Terminal 1 of Singapore Changi Airport near Immigration arrival on level 3. The lounge accepts passengers from Emirates First / Business Class and EK Gold and Platinum Skywards members.

My visit to the Emirates Lounge at Melbourne Airport was a great experience. Upon entry, it was very luxe and contemporary an aspect other Airlines need to take into consideration for their own space. Great views of the tarmac were present once we were walking through with plenty of seating available. The dining area was amazing with plenty of food and drinks available and when comparing my experience with other lounges, I find the overall offering from Emirates is on a higher level. Staff were very attentive. Lastly, the showers and toilet amenities where exceptionally clean, including the entire space. This lounge is definitely worth coming to the airport early for.

I know it's supposed to be one of the best lounges, but there much like the rest of the country, there is something superficial and false about the DXB lounges that I just can't warm to. On the plus-side, the service is fantastic and the food and drink options are all brilliant. On the down-side, the lounge is bigger than many airports and to me feels like it's trying too hard to be the best. It's still fabulous.

Usual busy lounge (Business Class lounge gates B) as it was 06.00 rush hour. Vast lounge plenty to eat and drink, toilets and showers busy as usual. Nothing special but okay. Have to search for a seat to relax but I find all the lounges at Dubai are always the same unless you are lucky enough to arrive at a quiet time.

The Mingalar Sky Lounge is huge with plenty of space and lots of food and drinks on offer. Not many passengers in the lounge which made life very easy, toilets and Showers were very clean and totally empty. Great quiet lounge which was a delight.

The Manaia Lounge is definitely not a Lounge worth coming to the airport early for, but seeing it's located at an airport with not that much International routes I can understand. The Lounge just needs a better view to let natural light in to brighten up the space as it looks quite grime from first impressions. Only saw two team members and as for the food, It's very average. Overall, I think it needs an upgrade or preferably I hope either Qantas or Emirates needs to have their own Lounge in the future.

I have always double feelings towards the Dubai Business Lounge. Everything you need is there, but it's incredibly crowded. Quality of the food is good, but never excellent (try Milan-Malpensa Emirates Lounge for that!). The look itself is not as modern as, for example, Doha Qatar. Still good, but somewhat not at the same level of the rest of the Emirates experience.

First time visiting the Emirates Lounge in Sydney, and it's great to see consistency. It was very quiet by the time I entered, and knowing it was breakfast time I was looking forward to trying the food. I love the open space, great selection of food and drinks, and the Lounge was very clean and up to standard. Currently I'm trying to maximise my time within the Lounge, as I'm coming back to Sydney from Christchurch and there isn't an Emirates Lounge available. Looking forward to another visit in the near future.

My favourite lounge. I love the friendly staff, warm decors and furniture, space and quality of food and beverage. It was very quiet when I arrived as the first Emirates flight departed at 3:15 in the afternoon. With the amount of food catered, all freshly made, I made it a mission to try different dishes to have a taste test. For anyone who loves to drink, the lounge provide a very wide selection of beer, wine and spirits, you can even make your own cocktails. I'll be back in Auckland next month and can't wait to make another visit.

The first class lounge is really big with lots of seating. A nice huge restaurant with a la carte and buffet options. A spa, shower facilities, computers, reading materials etc. The benefits of being able to board from the lounge level adds a touch of luxury and convenience. The only down side is the insufficient air conditioning at the restaurant, it could get a little warm especially during the way. That was because of the open sky light design of the airport.

I used this Emirates lounge twice on a return trip to Australia. It's enormous and was busy both times I used it. Consequently, it was quite difficult to find some quiet space. The toilets and showers were so busy that we had to queue, so I didn't bother with a shower even though I really could have done with one. I did find the behaviour of some other lounge users very annoying - people would take four chairs to themselves and put suitcases on seats, meaning one person was using space designed for four people. Not the airline's fault but it made the experience less enjoyable. I think they should configure the lounge better and have more seating designed for one or two people, as the majority of people I saw were alone or in couples. All in all, the only real benefit to using this lounge was the 'free' food and drink (though not really free as I paid so much for the ticket). If possible, I would use the smaller lounges elsewhere in the airport - did this on the outward leg and it was much quieter and more relaxing (also no queue for the toilet!). I also liked the Moët bar at the very back of the lounge as this was quiet and had a buffet too.

Used this Coral Lounge at Phuket when flying with Emirates, As a new lounge everything was nice and fresh although some seats were already stained. There was a good choice of food and a good range of drinks available, although the coffee machine was difficult to work, Toilet facilities were OK. The lounge did get a bit crowded but there was still seating available. An enjoyable experience.

The lounge is poorly designed and is impersonal. There is no feeling of service. Big is not better. It's sad because it's obvious they have tried but the design is all over the place and services all dispersed. A great lounge feels like you are being welcomed into someone's comfortable private club,  this just feels like a waiting area.

Emirates use the Dublin Airport Executive lounge in Dublin airport which is owned and run by the DAA authority . Whilst the lounge is small , has good light and apron views. The service is by a lounge dragon who looked like she had just completed loading bags onto an aircraft. Snarly and felt it an issue to answer a polite question on a canceled flight. The food offerings are a biscuit and as for beverages a broken coffee machine. Some alcoholic spirits . They charge non business passengers 30 euro to use this lounge, stay well away and use the cafes etc as better quality and you will actually get a seat.

An extremely pleasant experience, this Brisbane business lounge is triangular around a central service core. Limited views over the runways but the airport is not very busy so relatively little to watch. Reasonable selection of food and drinks. Comfortable seating including dining tables and chairs. Selection of magazines and newspapers. Shower cubicle adequate with fresh towels and toiletries. Overall a very happy experience with direct boarding to the upper level of the A380.

Seems like the lounge at Dubai is getting busier and busier every time that I've used it over the past few years. On my most recent visit to the lounge in January it was a bit of a challenge to find a vacant seat so I could actually sit down somewhere to eat. There also seems to be a vastly increased number of more selfish travelers using the lounge, taking up positions in the booth areas which can seat four people and arranging the furniture into a private sleeping space. I understand that it's tiring to travel and any chance to stretch out and sleep can be welcome but one person taking two seats for mountains of bags and pushing another two seats together to create a bed is just oddly rude behavior. I understand that there's little that the staff can do about this but it seems like the extra money spent doesn't guarantee the same levels of comfort in the lounge as on the plane these days.

Emirates lounge for business class is not huge but nicely maintained. For choice is not very wide, but they do have a good selections of alcohol and other drinks. Around 8pm it cannot rather noisy and crowded. Being there on new year's eve, it's noisier than before, with many people taking loudly and using Skype to communicate with their loved ones (loudly). Children were let free to run around, creating more havoc. In this case, it's more the customers that let this place down than the lounge itself.

This is a huge lounge with many seats and a few food stations with many options to offer guests. However, look closely, the choice is not as wide as one would expect, but the bar is quite well stocked. Around 7 to 9pm it's rather busy, toilets and showers are amazingly underwhelming and fairly crowded. Quite a long line to queue even at the men's toilet. The shower area is badly designed, hard to bring your luggage in and have a shower and get changed inside a shower cubicle. They expect you to store your luggage etc in their locker-like cabinets and change clothes in the public area, which for some customers would be uncomfortable (think...public swimming pool change rooms). I was expecting an oasis of calm and peace, plus a food galore to feed myself before the flight, I was rather disappointed. Stay here for a short time is ok, not sure about staying any longer one or two hours.

Pretty basic and unimpressive. The food is standard sandwiches which are cut thin so they go dry and stale within 20 minutes. Coffee and the usual drinks are available. No attractive views from this lounge. But worst of all for a business traveller is the WiFi is next to useless.

Finally the refurbishment is finished here which took almost 2 years and (according to Emirates) USD 11 million to renovate this huge lounge. Now the colours dominate with brown and a lot of polished wood - very nice. Still the problem is, that at many times during the day even this enormous lounge is very full, the renovation did not include any expansion. I still prefer their lounge in Concourse A, even if that means to use the train (2 minutes drive) to that place. New is smoking area now at that the farthest end (if you enter from main entrance, the first part when you enter from Concourse C) - really necessary? Food is adjusted to the time of the day, still have a fridge with free Ben&Jerry-ice cream, but in comparison to former years some things are now missing, as eg. raspberries, now only still available in the First Class Lounge.

Excellent choice of food. Dinner service at time of flight. Great choice of food and beverages. Comfortably large considering number of passengers. Staff are very attentive and helpful. Wifi is fast and effective. Simply one of the best I've been in.

As a Gold skywards, i was given an invitation to use this lounge at Prague Airport. The less said the better. Staff were great but thats about all I can say. The space was so cramped and no place for sitting at that moment. The small sized lounge was catering for premium passengers of many flights and Emirates has a high capacity A380 here. It was obvious it could not cope up. Food offerings were dismal and I believe there were other options but you had to pay for it.

Staff were excellent and surroundings and food as well as service were just perfect. My husband And I travelled with assisted passage and the staff here were expecting us and had reserved us a seating space close to the buffet. It really was an exceptional time and one we will never forget. Calm with service over and above any we had experienced in other Emirates lounges, which we rate highly both in Dubai and Birmingham.

I'm liking the Dubai lounges more than I did a few years ago - I didn't like the linear design. They're very large and there are quiet places to be found. Food choices never seem to change much but are reasonable and I prefer eating in the lounge than eating on the flights. No queuing anywhere and the washrooms are kept immaculate. Plenty flight info screens and staff are efficient and polite. Good WiFi.

The second time I've visited this lounge. It feels like you are stepping back in time. On the plus side, the food, drinks and service are pretty good. Everything around the catering area is well presented clean. Unfortunately, the decor and design is drab. Furniture is all caramel and dark wood everywhere. The feel of the whole place seems like 20 years ago. Maybe it is.

For food and beverages and ambience this is the best lounge at Auckland that I have visited. The only downside is that it does get very crowded near the departure of 3 full A380 aircraft. My recommendation (if you are eligible and have time as I did connecting from a domestic regional flight) is to eat at the Emirates Lounge and then retire to the relative peace and quiet of the Qantas Club next door as the Emirates Lounge fills up.

We entered the lounge to find it quite empty, so lots seating areas to choose from. The buffet was set up with hot and cold food. It was dinner time so the food selection was amazing so much to choose from. I enjoyed the cold selection with fruit, cheeses and cold cuts. Lovely Moet and good selection of wines and top shelf. The buffet area had tables and chairs set up for dinning, quite civilized. The toilets were clean and tidy.The Lounge was a great start for our long journey home.

The food, service and the facilities were great.  My gripe with this lounge is that the walls do not go to the ceiling. So all the noise from below just reverberates up into the lounge. So all the people movers beeping, general chit chat from customers etc all echoes up into the lounge. Most lounges I have been in are usually an oasis of calm and reasonable quiet. Not here!! This is not a relaxing place to spend some time.

This is a great business class lounge,  renovated in 2016 and has more space and new facilities. The range of food and beverage was great. There was a full bar and enough food.  Shower facilities are very good, nice towels and a good space. I would have liked a toilet in the shower - offered by a few lounges but not all - Korean, Air France, Malaysia airlines to name a few. This may be a little strange, but I was very impressed by their tea selection.  Seats were comfortable enough, there were about 4-5 different types - I chose a lounge seat in front of the TV area. One comment, while there is little notices everywhere about the WiFi login details, it wasn't that obvious to a couple that were most likely in their 70s. Maybe something more obvious yet still classy? One for the designers. I didn't check the wifi speeds as I was on my phone with a generous data allowance. Bidets in an aussie toilet - thumbs up! Great lounge to get into if you have the opportunity.

Visited this Emirates lounge at Manchester Airport on 21st July at 0700 hours. Lounge was clean and had lots of comfortable seating with good views of aircraft stands. Good selection of food on offer and good selection of drinks available both alcoholic and non-alcoholic. Rest rooms were clean and showers were available. Its a relaxing place to wait for the flight.

Great food, ample space, nice family section to cater kids, excellent shower facilities, direct airbridge from lounge to your flight and a 15 minute complimentary foot massage prior to boarding. Love the service. The vegetarian kebabs were the highlight.

The Club at MCO is the 2nd worst Business or First Class Lounge I have been in.  Quality of the food is very cheap and the staff decide when to tell the passengers to eat and very rude lady was telling me that I have to wait until she is ready with the setting up for lunch, it was past 1200-1230hrs and our flight to Dubai was at 13.20hrs. I told her I have a long flight going back so I needed to eat and although I am on Business Class I was planning to get some sleep on the plane my first few hours. Only concern is that we are ready for our next trip in a couple of months and the thought of having to use the Lounge at MCO is not a good feeling not something I look forward to.

Warmly welcomed to the lounge. Used shower facilities which were clean, well stocked and well laid out. There was a good selection of food suitable for light or full meals depending on needs. A variety of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages that were frequently restocked. Plenty of seating options available, although a 'quiet area' would be useful. A lounge that offers a good hard and soft product and is worth a visit.

I have used this lounge on numerous occasions, it has everything a lounge should. Food is of good quality and service is on par with Emirates standards. Wide variety of drinks available non alcoholic and alcoholic, wifi and ample seating which is comfortable and clean.

This lounge has a nice food area serving hot and cold dishes and away from the restaurant there is a quiet seating area and another seating area with a large TV. The staff were friendly and efficient. I had a 9:20 pm flight and spent a couple of hours in the lounge. There was a superb fillet steak dish which was the most popular item on the buffet but there were chicken and fish and vegetarian dishes, too. It's one of the best airport lounges I have ever been in. I suggest arriving early at the airport to make full use of this lounge.

The beef was nice and soup tasty, but the Emirates Lounge at Paris CDG Airport is not clean enough. Not enough drinks and food options. The sofa is not that comfortable.  I think Emirates did bad in the Paris Chales de Gaulle International Airport because the First Class ,Flequent Flyer and the Business Class lounge is all together

I've used this Emirates lounge many times and although it's a huge sprawling place lacking atmosphere, you get used to it. Emirates have provided assistance directing you where you need to go. Washrooms are always kept clean. Food choices have been pretty much unchanged for years, but are perfectly OK and I prefer the lounge food to what is served on the flights.

We had an early flight from Perth and was pleased to find that the Emirates lounge opened at 4am. We got there about 4.20am and there was plenty of hot, and cold food available. Plenty of seating which was comfortable and spacious. The staff were very friendly and accommodating.

Emirates lounge in Manchester is excellent with spacious and comfortable seating, good food and drink selection and good wi fi access. I had an excellent pre flight dinner enabling me to get quickly to sleep after take off on a night flight. It is however a long walk to the A380 stand at the end of the airport so be prepared for this.

Very pleasant Emirates lounge very close to the gate and natural sunlight and view out to the taxi way and nearby gates. Food was plentiful and well presented with lots of options to choose from. Wifi was excellent and lounge staff very friendly, personable and kept everyone up to date on flight departure time and delays. Lounge was clean and seating arranged so that you are not overlooking anyone else allowing some privacy to do some work.

The Emirates business class lounge at Dubai Airport is absolutely underwhelming - the queues at the bathrooms are interminable. Whats worse, the absolutely lackluster service. I would say everyone I approached was smug. Very dissapointed in an airline I loved and went out of my way to use.

This review is only for the Emirates lounge in Concourse B in Dubai Terminal 3. I had used this lounge a little over a year ago. Things were far better then. There is remodelling going on apparently for many months now. The result is a long wait to use the toilets! Some were complaining that this has been the situation for over six months. Clearly this is unacceptable and Emirates have started their remodelling without any planning. In any case this lounge in concourse B is not comparable to the one in A which is clearly superior in all respects. Avoid and use a different lounge if at all possible.

I had two experiences of Emirates lounges at Dubai Airport. This one is for the main central lounge upstairs in Concourse B. On paper this lounge should be perfect. An array of seating choices from lounging 'beds', comfortable armchairs, tables and chairs etc, large selection of food and drinks, good wifi, toilets and showers - all smartly decorated and finished to a high quality. However the experience of it is far from perfect. The lounge is enormous, which while I understand that Emirates caters for a huge number of Business class passengers, largely transiting, they would be better having a larger number of lounges dotted about, or at least re-designing the lounge so it feels less like a mile long corridor. The food and drink areas are very busy and where as other airlines (and other Emirates lounges) have numerous self service drinks areas dotted about, this lounge didn't seem to. Just a central bar where you queued up.. There were staff walking around and I suppose I could have grabbed one and asked them to get me something, but I work on the principle that unless a member of staff offers me something, then I assume that they have a different job.. besides, I am quite capable of pouring myself a glass of wine. The staff were a bit of a let down generally, as aside from the staff at the entrance checking your ticket, there was not one smile offered from anyone.. They lady serving at the bar inquired to my order by snapping a very sharp "yes!", while not even properly looking up at me.. I refrained from commenting on, but actually left me a bit annoyed. The toilets were far too small for a lounge of this size and there was a queue even for the urinals. All in all, it was obviously considerably nicer than sitting in the main airport departures lounge and did provide the key elements required of a business lounge, but did not feel like a particularly premium experience.

Quite a pleasant experience. While Birmingham airport is far from premium in any way, the lounge was easy to find and offered a calm and comfortable place to relax before the flight. It is not a large lounge, but as there are only three flights through the day, there was more than enough space for everyone. I do wonder how the lounge will cope with the introduction of the A380 later this year. The food selection was fairly small, but still provided sufficient choice and was all of a nice quality, alongside a well stocked self service bar.. There was also a nice choice of armchairs and tables and chairs. The toilets were nice and clean, and large enough to cope with the rush when they announced boarding was beginning. I had no real interaction with any staff while inside, although the two ladies at the entrance were professional enough, without being particularly welcoming.

This is a shared lounge, but a lovely experience. The lounge is beautifully and ornately decorated, which just about remains on the right side of being over the top. The lounge is not particularly large, but there was no shortage of seats when I was there 8:30am-10am. The food offering was very nice, and although I didn't have any, there was also a good alcoholic drinks selection. The staff were one of the lounges best features, with polite, courteous and friendly staff.  There was also spa facilities, although I did not use them. The downside was the toilets, which while clean was tiny and could not cope with the number of passengers. There was always a queue for the 2 cubicles. Also, in spite of being a purpose built luxury lounge, inside a brand new state of the art airport terminal building, you were still required to place toilet paper into a bin rather than down the toilet. I appreciate that Mumbai sewerage might not be up to the same standards of Europe, however this requirement did not exist in the two hotels I stayed in Mumbai. Overall a very nice experience and a nice way to relax before the flight.

Used this Emirates lounge flying business class to Dubai. It is a combined First/Business class lounge. Good selection of food and drinks. Can see out into the runways with plenty of light. Comfortable seating with attentive staff. They were quick to clear away food and plates. Quick walk to the aircraft. Good wifi that was easy to connect.

I have used the Emirates business class lounge on Dubai Airport, and service was excellent. I used the quiet smokers lounge (I think they call it 'the cigar lounge'), where there was no food, only a huge choice of drinks. Because I wasn't able to walk very far (I was brought to the lounge in a wheelchair), a waitress brought me an extensive breakfast from the other part of the lounge. I only asked for cappuccino, yogurt and a fruit salad, but beside that she also brought me fresh juice, apple, banana, cottage cheese, and a small bottle of Actimel. The seat was perfect, soft but not too soft. The wheelchair service provided was also excellent, staff brought me to the lounge, and at exactly the promised time, they came to pick me up to bring me to the gate. There was no cue at the nearby ladies toilets, and the housekeeper kept toilets spotless, and towels, toothbrushes and combs were provided. The lounge was clean (though my arrival time at 5am might be of influence), and Wifi was fast. I certainly recommend this lounge.

First time to try this lounge and disappointed by the experience. Lots of space with very few comfortable chairs to sit in. Food choice would be OK if you have the time to sit and wait for it to be prepared. With a short 45 minute transition this was not possible. Many mentions in previous reviews of the toilet facilities which seem to be busy even during a quiet time. In summary I think they could dispense with the Voss bottled water etc and spend the money on getting the basics right!

Excellent lounge at the airport with helpful friendly staff who were attentive without being overbearing or intrusive. Good food options were available and was a nice touch that tempura was cooked to order and brought over as it was prepared. Very clean and tidy and overall a nice way to start my trip.

Emirates lounge in Dubai is very large, however, despite its size, the queue for the men's bathroom was very long (we were trying to use it during a peak transit time). In addition, there is a lot of wasted space in the lounge with many undesirable uncomfortable seats vacant and not many comfortable seats for a longer layover. There were lots of 'brand name' elements (eg voss water) which should have made me feel special, but what I wanted most was a soft chair and ready access to a bathroom. Skip the bling and provide the basics. Other notes, we were traveling with two small children who were very excited to access the kids play area. As parents we were frustrated because the only way to access the room was to go through the smoking lounge. In addition the only way to get out of the lounge to our gate with out backtracking significantly was to go through the same thick smoke.  Further the smoking lounge was in open air next to the non smoking lounge with no air control or separation. Smoking is a health hazard and should be segregated. Talk about bad space planning. I needed to print out a paper for work while there. I located the business center after much effort and found the only printer there with a sign on it saying out of service and the staff were not able to suggest an alternative.

Pleasantly surprised by the Birmingham Airport lounge. Unlike the Emirates Dubai lounge which is truly terrible, this one had good food, well laid out and had showers and toilets that did not require queuing for long periods. Made the start to the flight very good.

After a several month renovation the new Emirates First Class / Business lounge is spectacularly disappointing. There's no separation between the two classes, so first class passengers (who pay accordingly) must suffer a boisterous cafeteria style dining area, uncomfortable lounge seats, bland food, few places to charge laptops, and children running and screaming up and down the length of the lounge. There's nowhere to hide; it's nearly as hectic as the duty free area.

Arrived on early morning flight so had 2 hours to wait. Lounge was fairly busy but no trouble finding comfortable seats. Excellent selection of food including great smoothies. Good wifi. Only problem was the crowding in the bathrooms which meant waiting.

This lounge is best described as featureless and bland. Chairs arranged around low coffee tables are the name of the game. To the left is a dining area with a hot food buffet and a beverage bar set up against the wall. There is also a single island positioned off the wall featuring cold food and desserts. During the couple of hours that I was there this was not particularly well stocked. The food in the hot buffet seemed to have been there quite some time and really did not look that appetizing In front of the food and beverage area is an open space with dining tables and chairs. At the edge of the lounge overlooking the departure area below was a countertop with chairs, and this is where I settled in. Whilst I was in the lounge new broke of the Paris shootings. There was a single television set in the entire lounge and people clustered around it trying to get updates of what was going on. I would have thought that Emirates could stretch to at least a couple of more sets. The furniture and decorations around the lounge were in good shape and very clean, though there was hardly anything that stood out in the lounge as distinct or particularly appealing on an aesthetic level. There is a business centre which I did not use. The airport has a very good wifi system so I did not have to use the in lounge wifi. The bathrooms were very clean but I could not find any towels. I later found out that fresh towels were in a cupboard under the sink. I have to say that this lounge falls quite some way behind other Emirates lounges that I have used in the past - hence the low score

Visited the business class lounge in concourse B and impressed. The lounge was quiet when I arrived and got busier and busier. The lounge is enormous. There are any number of places to sit, eat and relax. I took a shower and the facilities were great, however, the shower room was unbearably hot and it made it very difficult to get dressed. The food and drink options are great - champagne to cocktails. The food options were good and offered an excellent selection. The disappointing aspect of the lounge in concourse B, is that you cannot board directly from the lounge as you can in Concourse A. I think it is not right to differentiate service for the same class of travel and it is something that needs to be addressed. Emirates make it seem like if you are on an A380, this feature is guaranteed, which of course it is not. Overall, the lounge is excellent and you could easily while away 6 or 7 hours here.
Emirates business class lounge at Dubai Airport. It is crowded and the food selection and quality are not getting better! Wait times at washrooms is ridiculous. Doesn't feel like a business lounge.

Emirates business class lounge at Auckland Airport is excellent. Great food and selection to suit all tastes. Very comfortable and clean amenities. Big tick of approval,  shame they don't follow with First class.

Really nice lounge with excellent food and beverage options from soft drinks to champagne. Well presented hot and cold buffet options meant we ate well before the flight and could therefore get to sleep soon after take off. Comfortable seating, showers if needed and good views of the apron and runway.

Was upgraded to business with Emirates and got offered lounge access at the Oryx Lounge in Doha Airport. It was during Eid holiday, so alcohol was not being served. Food selection is small, but quality is good. Coffee machines are available for use. The facility has showers, but the toilets are small. They have a recreation area with playstation and football. Lounge is good if you have time to kill and just want to have a bit of drink before your flight, but other than that it is quite boring. I'd rather walk around and shop than just sit and wait for another flight where I'll be sitting for at least an hour.

Dubai airport is huge, we were in Terminal 3, and as a OneWorld emerald member, visited the Emirates lounge on the way to and from Europe. The first visit was at breakfast time where the food was limited but good. The lounge ambience was quiet and relaxed and access to the gate is straight from the lounge. The second visit was in the middle of the night (local time). The food was set up for dinner and snacks and was varied. The bar was open and staff to help. The free shoe shine service was open, but I did not see it used (mine were clean). The only problem was that the lounge it was part closed. This meant toilets were quite a distance away and the gate required one to backtrack quite a way. Problems: there were not enough relaxing areas and the toilets (men's) has a queue, maybe because of the closed off areas.
Emirates First Class lounge at Dubai International Airport is extremely big. It offered good and friendly services. Also good food choices, and good if you eat halal. Excellent staff.

First time I have had time to use the Emirates Business Lounge at Dubai. Very nice and comfortable. Selection of refreshments is good and most of all the shower facilities to freshen up and feel human. With these shower facilities, its an idea to book in swiftly as they do get used heavily and often a 20-30 mins wait.

This lounge was under renovation and on our arrival it did not seem to matter as the lounge was empty. Within a short time it filled up very quickly. There are insufficient toilet facilities for ladies. As this lounge can accommodate hundreds of people, there was only one block of ladies toilets (6 toilets in total, if I remember correctly) and only 3 showers! I hope that after the renovations, they will make these facilities more friendly no ladies - not just men. There was plenty of food and drinks on offer.

Awful. Greeting at the reception was rude and surly. She could have at least pretended she liked her job. There were dishes piled up on the tables and too few tables for the number of patrons. Floors were dirty with mess everywhere. Seats (when we could find one) were dirty and uncomfortable. This was no replacement for the closed Emirates lounge.

We were returning to Glasgow from Langkawi via Kuala Lumpur and Dubai, and had 6 hours in KL so we decided to go to the Lounge. I was only allowed for one extra guest to the lounge but they let me take my two kids as well. Some great food, and array of drinks, tea, coffee, beers and soft drinks. There was a great window to see aircraft and there was good wifi. There were many computers. There were no Sofas.

I have used Emirates lounges around the world and this is one of the best. It's just the right size to hold a full A380's worth of First and Business passengers without looking overcrowded. The food was excellent with plenty of hot and cold choices, desserts and lots of good French cheeses. There's the usual self service bar, fridges full of soft drinks and freshly squeezed juices, champagne and wine and a good coffee machine. There's plenty of comfortable seating and a nice observation deck outside where you can stand and watch the A380 arrive and park up right outside. it has a good business centre and nice bathrooms with showers. Overall a very nice and relaxing environment.

This is the best Emirates Lounge I've used mainly because the food is so good but it's also a very nice, relaxing environment to wait before your 8 hour flight back to Dubai. The first time I used it I checked in at 7pm for a midnight flight so spent several hours there. The second time not so long but on both occasions we had an excellent 3 course restaurant standard meal with lots of good, Far Eastern and European choices which were constantly replenished by the busy staff. There's 2 self service bar areas with good aged spirits, mixers, wine and champagne and a good coffee machine. After dinner we relaxed in the comfy chairs and passed the time with a few drinks, magazines and newspapers. There's a good business centre, free wifi and bathrooms with showers. Overall Excellent, well done Emirates.

I have transited Dubai many times on Emirates who use Terminal 3 which is broken down into Concourse A/B/C. I have used all 3 Business lounges and A is by far the best as it's new. C is old and tired and B is under renovation so avoid, if you have a long layover take the short train ride to A. The Business Lounge in A is massive and runs the whole length of the building with several food areas, seating areas, bathrooms with showers, business centres etc. The beauty of this lounge is that it has a proper smoking lounge with good ventilation so as a non smoker traveling with a smoker I don't mind going in. It's a proper bar with chesterfield sofas and TV's on the walls, not just a smoke room. In the food areas there's a hot buffet and lots of cold choices, fruit, yogurts etc. Plenty of drinks options and coffee machines that make a very nice macchiato. A is also the A380 terminal so has the 2 deck air bridges and you board directly from the lounge. A is a 10 but I've given 8/10 due to the other 2 lounges.

I often use this lounge as I have the Emirates Gold card so get a lounge invitation regardless what class I'm flying in. It's typical of most Emirates lounges as they all have the same decor and furniture although this one is quite small when compared to Heathrow. There's always 2 staff in Emirates uniform at check-in who are always warm and friendly and will explain everything if it's your first time. There's comfortable seating with little coffee tables to your left with a big TV and the dining area and self service bar is on the right. And I mean self service, there's no annoying staff who try to pour your drink for you. I've never had a bad meal here, the food is always excellent with plenty of choice. There's a hot buffet and always a soup and a chiller with cold starters, deserts and cheeses. They have 2 self service bar areas with a good choice of spirits, wine and champagne and fridges full of mixers, beers and water, a good coffee machine and lots of tea choices. There's the usual business area with computers and a printer and there's nice bathrooms with showers. The only negative is there's virtually no mobile phone signal.

The Emirates Lounge in Delhi is awesome and massive, there's only 4 Emirates flights to Dubai per day, all at least 5 hours apart so I'm not sure why this lounge is so big, however my son and I enjoyed it on our stopover from Kathmandu to London via Dubai especially after the nightmare of the transit gates in Delhi! The food was excellent with plenty of hot and cold choices. There's a self service bar with a good choice of spirits, mixers, beers, wine and champagne plus a good coffee machine and teas. You get well looked after on Emirates. After dinner we found another self service bar at the far end of the lounge which we had virtually to ourselves. There's more than enough comfortable seating all around. There's a good business centre and bathrooms with showers. The only negative it was too warm, the air con wasn't cool enough. Overall a nice haven from the chaos outside.

It is a common lounge for many airlines oprating from Lagos. Seating is not too comfortable. During peak hours even getting a place to sit is difficult. Food and drink availabilty is Ok. Service quality is poor. Better place to spend time waiting for boarding as other waiting areas at Lagos Airport is horrible.

We got to the lounge at 4.30 am. It was pretty busy. We decided to have a shower after long flight. We were very lucky because the showers were free. In 1 hour the lounge was packed which is not too bad because it's such a big and spacious lounge. HOWEVER there are 3 blocks of male toilets and only 1 block of female toilets which I found unacceptable! They are doing refurbishments so I just hope there will be more female toilets in very near future. There were queues for female toilets and showers. The demand is absolutely not met for female passengers.
This was a very sorry excuse for a business lounge. Far too small and a poor selection of food and beverage. Maybe more time should have been spent on practical chairs and space than on decor!

The lounge is a joke. It is small hence there is little chance of getting a table to yourself. I don't eat meat and I had the choice of rice lukewarm polenta bread crackers cheese salad and fruit. Pitiful. No Baileys.

At 7.30am this huge lounge was impossibly crowded with long queues for the toilets - and even to get a cup of coffee. It was difficult to find a comfortable seat and the food was unappetising. We had 2½ hours turnaround between flights - nowhere near enough in an airport of this size long walks between gates and with long queues for security as well. We wanted a quiet relaxing break breakfast and shower after long flights from New Zealand. No chance - the experience was uncomfortable and stressful. No chance of a shower either - more long queues - facilities totally inadequate for an airport of this size.
Excellent lounge for a smaller airport fantastic range of food and Beverages and attentive and courteous service. Good business centre in the lounge easy to access wifi.

After a long flight from Sydney I had 2 hours in the Emirates lounge concourse B before my connecting flight to Brussels. A nightmare! I spent the entire 2 hours with 10-15 other tired men waiting in queue to take a shower. The lounge is huge and crowded not the kind of place where you can relax and unwind. This is clearly the chink in Emirates armor. They should make separate lounges for business class and for silvers. Next time star alliance. Writing this whilst still waiting for a shower. Must have seen at least 40 persons come and leave shaking their head when they saw the queue. Lots of staff around but what's the point when the only thing they can do is ask to see your boarding pass over and over again.

This lounge is not operated by Emirates but it is the one they give access to. It is terrible. Full with passengers from multiple airlines. The food is not fresh and is cup noodle based cheap and tasteless. There is no power point the drinks are from cans and the staff couldn't care less. Emirates change lounge!
Okay it has not the standard of the Emirates Lounges but I was satisfied. Indian food indian drinks friendly staff. Nice view to the airfield airconditioning. (not standard in India)

Had a 10 hr stop over on the outward trip to Perth sat in the A lounge for half the time service not at all friendly food average noticed there were two shower rooms both had 4 people waiting to use them gave up after a while and went to the hotel out of the lounge and used their showers at least they had 10 rooms although it was $15 was well worth it. Eventually was told on the 8th hour there was a B lounge closer to my departure gate not at all easy to find signs up in the air with arrows pointing every where more relaxer chairs needed and more customer friendly staff needed. On the return trip with a 2hr stop over showers still over crowded. Emirates need to address this shortfall before they lose clients to other airlines

A small and overcrowded lounge there were 2 flights leaving at around the same time so the lounge was packed with not enough seats for all. Food and drinks OK but nothing special. Emirates need to seriously consider increasing the size of this lounge.

A spacious and well maintained lounge good choice of drinks and hot food recommended. Ground staff not so friendly but all other aspects positive . Free Wifi throughout the lounge. Location of the lounge not obvious have to follow the signs which are not so clear.

A relatively new lounge and a VAST improvement on the previous offering at Glasgow. Typical Emirates decor but very light and open. Staff at the reception desk were welcoming and took the time to give a personal tour of the lounge facilities to first time visitors. Seating gave a high level of privacy if required as well as more communal seating arrangements. Food and drink selection excellent and staff were attentive to ensuring the were replaced or topped up regularly. Business area was well sited and conducive to getting urgent work matters tidied up before boarding.

Common lounge for multiple airlines. Space is cramped. Seating arrangement is average. Food & Beverages are available but service is poor. Wifi connectivity OK. The place is better than the open waiting area of Lagos Airport where even the basic airconditiong not available.

A great place to relax. The selection of food and drink is very good as is service from staff. It is very close to the boarding gate that Emirates there is a separate gate for Business class passengers From the Chauffeur drop off to the lounge took approx. 15 minutes

My first experience of the First Class Lounge in Dubai and I was not impressed. It was very impersonal and I was disappointed. The only marked difference from the Business Lounges was that it was Table served for Dining. The offerings were nothing special either. I was absolutely appalled to find a large open Smoking area adjoining the Dining Room with dreadful tobacco smells drifting right through. Very Poor indeed. Frankly I would prefer the Business Lounges at Dubai and would certainly not pay the money to use First again.

Enough space and seating arrangement for the guests. Good place to relax before boarding with good choice of food & beverages. Staff assists with the boarding time. Overall a good place to spend time at Delhi T3.

This lounge hardly qualifies as a lounge at all. It has no shower facilities it's sparsely furnished in a very stark environment that resembles a doctors surgery. No dedicated wireless ( you have to access the Logan airport free wifi and keep logging in when it locks you out). Frankly you would be better off hanging out in the general concourse which is what we ended up doing. The so called lounge is in the Jet Blue terminal which is a budget type US airline and the lounge resembles a budget type lounge. Certainly not what one would expect from an airline like Emirates. At the risk of sounding like a snob when one travels business class you expect certain things in a lounge. For anyone who has visited the Qantas lounge in Karratha airport (regional airport in NW Australia) expect a slightly lower standard and that Emirates Boston Logan Airport. This lounge lets Emirates reputation down big time.

This has to be the biggest let down of the Emirates experience. I was in the older terminal as I was flying on a 777 and the lounge is terrible. Breakfast of cold toast lined up in baskets and who knows how long it has been sitting there. Showers - there are only a few for the couple of hundred passengers and there was no cold water only hot. Toilets the same three men's cubicles so a line was the order of the day. Lastly they have a smoking area that leaks smoke to the general area. Having flown through JFK LAX SYD HKG KUL SIN LHR in the last 4 months on a variety of carriers this lounge gets the worst award. Emirates needs some serious work here on the basics.
Superb lounge. Friendly attentive and helpful staff spotless amenities great selection of meals snacks and drinks wifi access and computer stations. Couldn't ask for anything better
