They do however fail on one point which is that they are incredibly difficult to find the signage at MAD is terrible very confusing. Iberia staff seem to loathe English - the man who admitted me to the lounge looked pained by the act of speaking in English. This theme continued onboard in the business class cabin to LAX and no one but the purser will speak any language but Spanish - on a nonstop serving Los Angeles.

Iberia offers a good quality lounge. Food service during breakfast lunch and restaurant for night flights. The rest of the day light snacks sandwiches and soft drinks/spirits. They offer a desk to try and learn about their wines of the month. The only problem no wifi only cable connection. Toilets showers in good condition. Also a rest area if you need some sleep.

lounge_name: IBERIA "SALA VIP" BUSINESS CLASS LOUNGE REVIEW
review: Before our outbound flight we used the lounge in T4S. This was a pleasant place with several defined areas. Very light and bright with views across the airport. It was a busy time of day with many long- haul flights departing but there was plenty of room. A good selection of hot and cold food as well as drinks. The only thing I noticed lacking were the toilets - too few and not to the same standard as other OneWorld carriers. On our return we used the lounge in T4. This seemed smaller but was still comfortable with a couple of unusual water features and views of the airport especially the impressive terminal roof structure. The food and beverage selection was noticeably more limited than in the T4S lounge. We made use of the shower facilities which were very good apart from the fact that the hot water lasted for 1 minute. When I queried this the attendant informed me that the boiler was unable to cope when all 6 showers were working at the same time. A slight design flaw.

Very large lounge which spans a portion of the length of T4S with great views onto the runway. Great selection of spirits wines and beverages generally. Hot and cold food (including smoked salmon) cereals fresh fruits and various nibbles. Not too busy comfy seats and internet facilities.

The lounge although it has been recently renovated seems to be very small on peak periods. The staff is almost invisible. The available food depends on the time of the day but sometimes everything is empty and nobody cares. The bathrooms are very small and if you decide to go to the WC you should keep dancing all the time since the light detector will turn off the lights if there is no movement.

I used this lounge as travelling on a BA flight. First of all It takes about half hours to arrive to the lounge as T4 Barajas is not a user friendly airport. The lounge is very spacious nice design fantastic view on apron and mountains the selection of food would have been decent if the trays had any food on it the wine bar would have been nice if more wine bottles were available to the public (we had to ask the staff to open a few as there were none left open). The computer area is just ok nothing much the relaxation room is perfecft for passenger who like that. There is a restaurant for intercontinental passenger but this is closed until late at night. Toilets and showers good. The reception staff was welcoming and helpful the rest of staff seemed to be very lazy.
Very quiet comfortable seating but a bit dark. Plenty of reading material OK drinks selection but no real food cookies and nuts. Secluded and not unpleasant though. No free internet access.

VIP Sala lounge again disappoints. The general condition of the lounge is still average with a large seating area and a view (albeit obscured) across the runway. Some of the furniture is worn especially the chairs in the popular locations (near the windows). The TV despite being a large LCD is never really utilised - being tucked away in a corner on channel TVEspana without sound. When I asked to hear the TV (the normal lounge lady wasn't on duty today) the new lounge staff didn't speak English so I had to convert to Spanish. My Spanish is pretty good but I do expect the airport staff - especially lounge staff - to understand English and respond to me in that language if that is the language of my choice. It didn't set us on the right footing. I was told that sound would disturb others so she couldn't change the volume. So what is the point of the TV then? I asked. I got shrugged shoulders. I expressed my displeasure and walked off for a coffee. The coffee was cold. So I went back to the lounge staff. She solved the situation by taking my coffee to the kitchen and (I assume) putting it in the microwave. The cup was too hot to hold! Despite the coffee the bar/alcoholic drinks selection is superb. Even the soft drinks shine bright - Coke without caffeine Coke zero Fanta milkshakes fruit juices etc. all being stocked among the usual collection. By far the best collection of cold drinks in one lounge I've seen. However the food is dire. In fact it could be described as peanuts. Not even an apple or a rotting banana. Nothing except peanuts and a tea-biscuit. Compare this to the Sala lounge at TFN a smaller more regional airport serving mostly national Spanish routes and Tenerife North wins hands down. They even have small sandwiches and a selection of cakes at TFN - but in LPA no!
A lovely lounge very spacious. Good range of food and drinks available. Wonderful views across to the mountains. Staff friendly and helpful.

Clean spacious light airy and very comfortable lounge with fantastic views across the apron and on to the snow peaked sierra. Awful catering : at 10.30am a few "bollos" - sticky buns some under ripe apples and some packet canape bases but nothing on them! Where were all the delicious things that the Spanish usually do so well for breakfast/mid morning snacks; not to mention something more substantial for passengers having transferred to Barajas through several time zones with body clocks after something resembling lunch or dinner? Staff offhand and indifferent.

A pleasant open space with comfortable chairs and amenities (washroom etc) but lacking in substance. Catering non-existent coffee cold stale biscuits no internet. Staff tried to be helpful but English poor. Altogether disappointing.

What a disappointment. Used this lounge prior to my morning flight to Madrid. Staff member at the front desk hardly acknowledge you as you walked in. Food selection was extremely poor nothing more than some stale croissants and some pre packaged mini muffins. Coffee from the machine was horrible. The two computer terminals were both out of order and so were the toilets. Does anything work in this lounge? Lounge was not used much by many of the travellers despite IB having numerous flights leaving around the early morning departure time at LHR perhaps the frequent travellers knew better than to waste their time.

Used the Iberia business lounge at Frankfurt for their code-share Air Nostrum flights out of Frankfurt. Nice welcome and a good selection of magazines and drinks. I cannot quite get used to the largely European practice of having most washrooms separate from the lounge. At Frankfurt this meant a long precarious walk through an area of terminal refurbishment to a fairly crummy toilet. Surely it would be a good idea to equip business lounges with washrooms! Otherwise an odd little lounge but a reasonably pleasant overall experience and a place one could work.

Visited this lounge on a Sunday afternoon - almost deserted. Comfortable seating and spacious airy atmosphere. No catering to speak of and poor drinks selection. Nothing to read either. Ok place for a bit of peace and quiet but otherwise very dull.

An excellent lounge with all imaginable amenities a silent room with sleeping possibility huge space a restaurant for intercontinental passengers who can dine after 9 pm (which could be earlier I know Spanish people eat late but not everybody does) a wine tasting corner shower possibilities (great) separate smoking areas etc. Only wireless internet could be also free of charge.

Yet again after visiting the Iberia Sala VIP lounge at Barcelona airport it seems that nobody works there. After arriving in the lounge tables were overflowing with all sorts of rubbish glasses were not cleared for couple of hours lounge was full of smoke. One of the fridges which was not working 6 months ago when I was last in this lounge was still not working this time.

This is an exclusive lounge which is smart with good views of airside. The bar had limited choice of drinks,choice of food was OK with both hot and cold dishes. Staff friendly and helpful. The departure gates for European flights are right at the end of the pier with a good 20-30 minutes walk, as it is a silent airport no announcements are made, it is your responsibility to start walking to your gate well in time, there is no guarantee that you may be able to avail the golf cart buggies. As the lady at the reception flatly refused that it was her responsibility!

What a disappointment! This lounge is difficult to find, eventually on asking in the 'Shopping Mall' we managed to find it, depressing access and location, communal toilets in corridor which you pass before entering the lounge, the smells were overpowering. Not enough seats available, there was a permanent sign at entrance that they were over crowded and there may be no seating available. By all means sell tickets to fill empty seats but please don't overdo it, legitimate business class users were squeezed out by tickets, sell only what your capacity is, you'll know how many business class pax are travelling on the day as airlines share this info with them, then sell whatever capacity is available. The good impression of T2 was spoiled by this mediocre canteen where the food matched it's description 'Canteen food' !!!

Very Small and cramped place and have to walk a mile to get there. Overcrowded and does not feel like a Lounge. Feed options are also very limited. Comparing against Mumbai Airport this feels like a local restaurant and not worth walking up to this. You can rather just walk around and seating by the gate is far better than in this lounge.

For Jet Airways GVK Lounge is common for business as well Frequent flyers. When you present your boarding pass for entry you will see smirks and grunts if you are a frequent flyer and no sounds if you are entering as Business class passenger. Even as a business class passenger once I arrived 3.5 hrs prior to departure then they will ask in which flight you arrive show us your boarding pass so you will feel end up as if the lounge entry is being provided as a mercy of the counter staff. Food spread is average Salads are of very low quality and those freezers / soft drink coolers are of very low quality / having maintenance issues as they make heavy unbearable noises, out side the lounge is more quieter than the lounge seating is of a pecular type neither they are comfortable nor of any utility. Cutlery perticularly spoons are of a show pieces but not useful for eating.

No lounge access at Colombo? Isn't this an integral part of the business class experience? After check-in and then this, I was left wondering at the airport what the Jet Airways Business Class experience is about.

This is a Jet Airways lounge not worth its name. No air-conditioning or ventilation, no display boards, no wash rooms, warm drinks, stale, cold snacks, mediocre seating, poorly illuminated, mosquitoes doing aerobatics and attacking helpless victim!! The attendant present had no idea about departures, kept on telling us to contact the airline ground staff, who weren't there. What more can I say?

Jet Airways seem to have changed their business class lounge, when last flown in 2014 they were sharing Etihad lounge at Heathrow T4, which was more comfortable and well laid out, this time when we turned up at Etihad lounge we were directed to a lounge further away, this is set on 2 levels and access to it was bit tricky, with no clear markings, had to keep on asking if we had arrived at the right place?? The bar was separate from the dining section, the choice of food was mediocre, WiFi was available, but seating was not that comfortable. This looks like cost cutting exercise!

It is a joke to even call this a Jet Airways lounge at Pune Airport a lounge, as all airlines use it. The door is always open, so there is no a/c. The guy in charge is very rude and couldn't be bothered. Only food is a stale sandwich and coffee which he brings out up on request. There are mosquitoes all over and limited seating. They don't have newspapers either. Outside seating is better and I will never go here again. There is no wash room and one must walk across the terminal to go to one. It is a shame that the airlines don't bother either.

Disgusting. This can't even be called a lounge. Next time I was at the airport (July 2015) I did not even visit it. Also the staff is rude and inefficient. Better not to have this lounge as it is used by all airlines, and it actually is a misrepresentation of the airline, or card company offering access.

Service was good but the lounge becomes very busy as many flight arrive and transit at the same time. Good food and drink choices. Seats are comfortable. Showers are good, but one has to wait as so many people were in queue.
This is an excellently maintained lounge. Good food and great ambience thereby providing great customer experience. Keep up the good work!

The shared airline lounge at the new international terminal in Mumbai was excellent. Elevator down one level after you enter the reception lobby to the business class lounge area. Plenty of comfortable seating in a variety of configurations lounge chairs sofas eating tables with chairs and work stations with outlets. The free WiFi was reliable and fast but the logon process is a little tricky. Separate food bar and lounge areas. The food area had a very comprehensive buffet both Western and Indian food one of the best I have seen second only to Dubai. Lots of snacks and fruit which you could take with you for your flight. The bar had a full wall video screen showing sports and a wide selection of beer wine and cocktails. There were also private work rooms for business calls and shower facilities.

We took a Jet Airways domestic flight from Kolkata Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Airport (CCU) to Delhi (DEL) in business class. At check in we received an invitation to visit the lounge. Lounge was a complete disappointment. Apart of coffee/tea and soft drinks you had to pay for drinks! I’m a Star Alliance Gold member and visited lots of lounges everywhere but paying for drinks when you already pay the premium for flying business class is just unbelievable! I never had this experience before. Food options were very limited as well and for western style food the only option was Danish butter cookies… (Indian style food wasn’t much neither). Overall appearance of the lounge was rather filthy and not worth a visit.

I've been to about a dozen lounges now in India and this is easily one of the best. I've been here twice and on both occasions there was plentiful seating. Chefs can cook you fresh food (dosa as it was breakfast time when I visited) and there is also some western as well as local food, both hot and cold. Good range of alcoholic (pay extra) and non alcoholic drinks. All in all it ticks all the boxes and I would definitely recommend!

Very crowded, with no simple breakfast offerings, (at 8 am), as Curry Rice or Pasta are not really my thing at that time of day. No knives to butter the croissant, but butter knives produced after asking. This was the Business class lounge on the 4/F. Found the one on 5/F to be better organised, and less busy.

I was looking forward to this lounge after reading about it on JAL's website. What a disappointment. The lounge itself was nothing special and not up to first class standard. Food can only be ordered by app that needs to be downloaded. That caused huge problems but a very helpful and patient English speaking staff member assisted. After 20 minutes she couldn't even get the app to work went away to get a printed menu which allegedly doesn't exist. 10 minutes later I got the app to work. The food is disappointing and does not live up to the hype on the website. Plus it's hard to identify what you are actually getting from the tiny thumbnail pics on the app. I had intended to eat my evening meal here before boarding the overnight flight to Sydney so I could sleep on the aircraft but this didn't happen. I hardly ate anything other than a few pieces of sushi, but definitely not enough to get me through the log haul flight back home. Just before boarding I noticed passengers eating plates of fresh chicken salad and udon that I hadn't found on the menu. It was too late to order anything else by then. As boarding at Haneda was by bus and a total shambles (flight nearly 1 hour late departing due to a shortage of buses) it's a huge failing that the lounge doesn't notify their premium passengers so they can have a realistic time for going down to the gate. This was consistent with all my travel on JAL where information was minimal to non existent.

The Club Seattle is a poor lounge. Dirty. Not a biz class lounge by any standards. Next time I will just eat at one of the restaurants in the airport and skip this disgrace. Food was bad, restrooms are like a public toilet, drinks are served by surly staff.

A fairly good size lounge but it lacked the premium feel. The space had four section from dining to relaxation taken care of by the attentive and friendly Staff. The drinks department was very good, but the food really lacked choices. Overall the experience was warming but the Lounge really needs a renovation to keep up with customer satisfaction.

Used this lounge when flying on British Airways. Tokyo Narita Terminal 2 JAL lounge in November 2017. Plenty of seating space, quiet, clean. A more than disappointing buffet - limited choice of foods - pastries dried to the point of being uneatable, slow and spotty wifi. I can say that the lounge experience including the services has slowly been dropping and is no longer a pleasant experience.

After reading previous reviews we were quite disappointed with this lounge. After presenting our Malaysian Airlines business class boarding passes the entry staff managed the barest of nods, no smile or words of welcome. At 8.00am on a Sunday morning the upstairs dining area was full and a sign warned of extended delays. We went up anyway and did find a table for two but after viewing what was left in the self serve food areas wondered why we bothered! Most food trays were empty or well picked over with many people waiting for more that did not appear whilst we had a coffee and minimal food. Back downstairs was comparatively quiet but only a biscuit to eat. The lounge certainly looks good and the toilets the best I have seen in a lounge but it did not deliver in terms of warmth of welcome or food offerings.

I used Japan Airlines Business Lounge as a passenger on Qatar Airways. Great big lounge with two floors to enjoy. Lovely food on offer with good choice of seating and drinks, lovely washrooms and showers and also nice massage chairs. The staff are friendly and very attentive. One of the nicest lounges I have been in lately.

Used this Japan Airlines lounge as a British Airways customer. A fairly limited lounge which is mainly style over substance. On the positive it seems to have enough seating and space. However, the food is an extremely poor selection for a first lounge and not of great quality. The chef being at the station does not coincide with lounge opening times which gives an even more limited food selection. In general the staff are very good but the front desk could do with more training due to one second talking to me and then one of their colleagues and then switching back, then directing wrong way etc. Compared to other Japanese service I've received at things like train stations/hotel receptions it was very substandard.

The Sakura lounge at Shanghai Pudong airport is absolutely dreadful, don't even bother going. A dated, cramped lounge, awful food and dysfunctional wifi. Much better off and much more comfortable hanging out in the terminal area. It is embarrassing the JAL and OneWorld can't do better than this in a major airport like PVG.

The SFO Sakura Lounge appears to provide a very basic experience for JAL customers. Seating is in simple yet comfortable, cushioned chairs aligned in rows. Food options are simple. Temperature in the lounge was OK albeit it a bit stuffy. I left as soon as the lounge started to fill up with passengers for the JL001 flight because the gate area seemed to have better air. Comfort wise I would not revisit this lounge again.

This Japan Airlines Sakura Lounge is in split floor and ground area is with bar some snacks as well smoking lounge. Upstairs area is prepared for dining and offered a very good choice of soft drinks, beverages, wine, mixers and very good quality food.

The Sakura lounge at Narita terminal 2 is very nice. The terminal itself lacks basic shopping and services that are present in terminal 1. However, if you need a place to kick your feet up in a nice environment with a good view of the ramp (to watch the planes), the 2-level lounge is quiet and a lovely place to wait. The second floor had a very complete buffet for breakfast: eggs, potatoes, salad, and other dishes, along with an open bar (mix yourself), coffee and other drinks. Best lounge I've been in for some time.

Both the Japan Airlines Sakura Lounge and the First Class lounges at Tokyo Narita Airport are outstanding, with shower rooms, massages and excellent food and drink. Staff are gracious and accommodating. I look forward to my layovers here.

I flew early in the morning, so there were not many people in the lounge. There weren't many food choices, but the lounge was very clean and efficient. Great way to calm down and kill time. The lounge is conveniently placed and easy to find. I didn't use the showers, but they looked very nice.

The lounge was fairly easy to find once past passport control. Staff very welcoming lounge is tastefully designed and overlooking the tarmac which means ample lighting and feeling of openness. Free wifi available and fast and steady. Plenty of seating. The lounge is split into two levels upper level for dining lower level for tea coffee and snacks. Very clean bathroom and shower facilities plentiful. I was disappointed with the lack of food selections some sandwiches rice beef curry and spicy bean curd dish available. Okay selection of drinks and alcohol. I was disappointed by the lack of sweets and desserts only cookies nuts and bite-size cheese available. It is obvious to see Japan Airlines is trying to cut cost.

Very early departure on BA back to Heathrow. Got there about 0510! Watched sunrise and had some lovely strawberries. Departure delayed 45 mins so as we were travelling First we went next door to First lounge which opened at 0600. Nice peaceful surroundings and a short hop to the departure gate. Very pleasant all round.

One of the best lounges I have been in. I managed to get a 1hr nap in a private cubicle with a bed followed by food and drinks in the restaurant area. This was followed by a massage and nice hot shower.

Lounge accessed as a Qantas Club member for flight from Frankfurt to Singapore. Lounge located Pre-Security screening in Terminal D Space Frankfurt International. The Sakura Lounge is modestly large. Professionally welcomed by front desk staff. Lounge neat tidy well lit. Many seating option for passengers travelling in groups of two four and individual travellers. Showers accessible small but functional. Towels provided. Toilets clean well maintained. A bar/ Soft drinks counter area is well stocked and with plenty of options. A small sign points to the 'Buffet' area. A small counter with two bowls one of cubed fetta cheese and olives. A small buffet hatch contained multiple small sandwiches of meats and cheeses. Modest. Cups glasses plates & attire quickly cleaned by a group of kitchen attendants. Flight information discreetly but well displayed in multiple areas of lounge. Announcements discreet and audible. Plenty of newspapers in Japanese German and English. Light and airy well laid out professional staff. Furnishings looking slightly worn.
Great little lounge extremely polite helpful staff good drink selection. Spa and shower are good and functional.

I waited one hour at the JAL lounge between gates 37 and 38. The lounge was comfortable enough with WiFi internet connections bathrooms and comfortable chairs. What I found very disappointing was the food. Apart from a few croissants a few cookies and a cauldron of clam chowder there was no food. There were two "no Halal" signs that I found rather funny. One was funny because it was set up amongst the few croissants and cookies - nothing was halal because there was almost nothing there I thought. The other was set up amongst all the bottles of spirits at the wet bar. Gee couldn't they find any halal alcohol? At this lounge JAL comes off looking cheap.

This is the worst business class lounge I have ever been in. The drink selection is poor and only a few cookies for food. It is extremely small and the no smoking area wreaked of smoke. It is more comfortable sitting at the gate. At least by the gate you aren't subjected to second hand smoke.

Flew Qantas San Francisco to Sydney. Apparently Qantas uses the JAL lounge rather than the BA for some reason. The Lounge was absolutely packed very small rooms little to eat or drink apart from chips. It was so depressing that I had to leave. Minimal staff not helpful. Very disappointing when a 14hr+ flight is ahead of you!

Two first class lounge at Terminal 2 easy to find dinning area but no restaurant service. Quality of food okay but not outstanding mainly Japanese food. good range of drinks. Staff tried to speak English but really difficult to understand. Wifi service and wired computer available. Spa services only have massage for 10 minutes.

Very small but a haven of peace as they restrict it only To First Class passengers much to the annoyance of OneWorld Emerald members. Food offering poor and no champagne but polite service and free internet.

Qantas use the JAL Business class lounge at SFO as they do not have their own. As there are no JAL flights departing concurrently with the Qantas flight it is exclusively used by Qantas passengers. The lounge is designed with Japanese passengers in mind seats are small and lined in a row not in way that allows groups to sit and face each other. There are a limited range of snacks but plenty to choose from in the fridge. Bathrooms are clean but no shower facilities. Wifi is the standard T-mobile paid service.

Although crowded at peak times this is a wonderful lounge. Very friendly and polite staff always looking to help. Great choice of Japanese and Western food and drinks. Only criticism would be small number of restrooms for such a big facility.

Beautiful lounge with spa like shower rooms available. Complimentary massage was just the topping on the cake. Plentiful buffet and open bar (believe there's a bartender in the afternoon). All staff was absolutely gracious and accomodating. It seemed to be extremely crowded in the morning as we were unable to find two lounge chairs together.

This lounge is for business class premium economy class and their premier class passengers. The first class passengers have a separate one I believe. This lounge was large covering two floors. On the upper floor there is a buffet. Yes an honest to god buffet of food not just packaged snacks. Great offerings of both hot and cold dishes and plenty of seating. As always children annoy me. Why and how do they get into places like this? Their running around and screaming a real turn off.

Good view of apron - convenient for gates for intercontinental flights. Nice breakfast including Japanese choices and eggs/sausage etc changing to lunch at 1100 - plenty of choice fabulous beef curry! Free massages etc. Didn't feel crowded. Remarkable beer machine with automatic tilting to get perfect head.

The lounge is somewhat small and rather crowded with business travelers. However they have a nice supply of traditional Japanese snacks (rice wrapped in seaweed for example) and a good spread of tea sodas beer and cocktails. Definitely nicer than many domestic American lounges though not luxurious.

Small lounge overlooking apron with just enough seating for a 2/3 full business cabin. Beverage and snack range quite small - a choice of red or white wine beer juices soft drinks and tea/coffee. For morning flight sandwiches pastries and some sushi were available. Washrooms very small with few amenities - not even a toothbrush or razor. LAN network available for laptops etc. A reasonable quiet spot away from the hubub of Sydney's international terminal shops. Disappointed that was not advised to stay in lounge but to board plane when departure was delayed 90 minutes due to plane's mechanical problems.

Light and airy with views over the apron - a good lounge. Complimentary massage service. Range of food in service a little narrow but tasty. Self service bar coffees soft drinks etc. Enough computer and printing terminals. Separate smoking room so main lounge remains smoke free. Not as good as Malaysia's KL Business lounge.

Was very pleasantly surprised by the new Sakura Business Lounge in Terminal 2 at Narita Airport. Such an improvement over the previous one. All the necessary amenities were available including a good selection of drinks and snacks reading material and then hot foods and salad offered on an upper level. The lounge is attractively decorated open and spacious with lots of windows. The seating was comfortable and washrooms well maintained. It is one of the better business lounges I have been in over the past few years. Definitely a place you don't mind spending any number of hrs. in before a long flight.

The new Sakura Lounge is a significant improvement on the old one. It is now equipped with truly awesome shower studios and complimentary shiatsu massage facilities. Wi-fi access is also complimentary and there is a large business corner with ample supply of desktop PC's. The mezzanine level also offers excellent hot food catering. Bar facilities offer an average choice of drinks. Seating in the lounge is very comfortable and spacious. Overall this lounge is now up to the standards of its competitors.

Air New Zealand uses JAL international lounge in Osaka. Found the lounge very basic. Very limited choice of drinks and the food was nuts and cookies! Nothing else. Seats arranged in long rows all facing the same way. Not very welcoming or relaxing. Staff essentially not present.

This Business lounge is very small. Located on the 2nd floor after the immigration. In an afternoon is overcrowded and you often have to share your table with fellow passengers. Beverages selection is limited but sufficient for short inter north asia flights : coffee/tea soft drinks juices and a few alcoholic drinks (mostly beer). Food is very limited too : They have only japanese cake that are packed individually plus the nuts and cracker to match up when drinking beer. They are serving wraps from subway. I would love to have some japanese food like sushi or noodles. Lavatories are clean no shower. A separate meeting room is available plus copier machine is also available for use. Free internet access if you have your own laptop. No PC terminal available. Most of the reading materials are in Japanese.

This Business lounge is OK. Located on the 3rd floor after the immigration. In the evening is overcrowded and you often have to share your table with fellow passengers. Most passengers are waiting for their intra-US flights. Beverages selection is limited but sufficient for long haul flight and as a main hub in asia: coffee/tea soft drinks juices and a few alcoholic drinks (mostly beer). Food is very limited too : They have only japanese cake that are packed individually plus the nuts and crakers to match up when drinking beer. I would love to have some japanese food like sushi or noodles. Lavatories are clean no shower. A 15 minutes shoulder and neck massage for free is available from the afternoon till 8pm but you need to register. A separate meeting room is available plus copier machine is also available for use. Free internet access if you have your own laptop there is a separate room for people who wants to use their laptops. No PC terminal available. The lounge has its irish pub style corner where you can mingle with other guest.

I checked in to the IGA Lounge by presenting my credit card(Lounge Key) and boarding pass, then proceeded to enter by scanning my boarding pass at the rotary gate. It felt like entering an airport within an airport. The lounge's size is comparable to that of a small city's airport, and it also has it's own duty free shop. Gazing ahead upon entering we were welcomed by the site of a pool table, a bar, and a masseur at work. Upon walking a few meters and turning right we found an expansive buffet with live cooking stations preparing pidde(Turkish pizza), pasta, and kebabs, along with a buffet offering a fairly wide selection of Turkish food and self service coffee machines. The food was fresh and tasted surprisingly good for an airport lounge. The lounge had considerable seating capacity offering various types of seating - sofas with coffee tables, recliner chairs, and workstations. The seating is comfortable, we did find some seats that were not clean but then managed to find clean ones. Most of the seating was being used, which resulted in an environment that was busy but also fairly quiet. The staff are efficient - some are friendly and others indifferent. None were rude or unpleasant. The shower was clean, spacious, and comfortable. The water was warm with decent pressure, and the quality of the shampoo and shower gel provided was good. They provide a sealed disposable towel, so you don't have to worry about whether it was washed. The WiFi was problematic. The connection kept dropping, and upon speaking with some other guests I found a number of us were encountering this issue. The IGA Lounge exceeded our expectations and made our eight hour layover a breeze without us needing to spend any money at the airport.

Good welcome by the hostess but the lounge is very tiny and food supply quite scarce. Tiny little sandwiches that were very slow to be replaced. If the lounge got any busier we will be sitting on the floor. Thank you for thinking of your clients' waistlines. I felt like I was on a diet.

The Corsair "Grand Class" lounge at Paris Orly airport has very poor foods, and just cheese and bread left. I asked if more food was available, and a very sullen girl said No. I asked again at reception who asked the same girl - same response . Drinks, champagne, wines etc were being refilled the whole time we were there. The carpet was very very dirty and stained etc.

This pay-to-use Rose Lounge is located after the security checks, around Gates 8 and 9. I accessed this lounge using my lounge membership. This lounge is located near the airside and boasts a view of the runway. However, it must be mentioned that the lounge serves food of an inferior quality so my honest opinion was that it was not worth the visit. The lounge offers a cushioned sofa or a cushioned chair option. On point to note, is that the lounge does not provide the boarding announcements. During my visit, my flight had 3 gate changes and I was not kept updated on this due to the absence of the announcement. Moving forward, what Rose Lounge ought to do is to improve on its food quality as well as certain infrastructure to improve the customer experience. I do have to commend the staff for their impeccable service during my visit. Thank you.

Lounge is very far away from duty free and relatively far away from gates as well. However, lounge is very nice and specious; it has some nice food stations with great taste as well as beverages and nice Italian coffee. Toilets are clean and staff are really nice and friendly

ITA airways lounge where Skyteam Elite Plus members have access, situated in the Satellite of T3. Very comfortable relaxing seats. Catering - cheese, ham, vegetables in acceptable choices but not excessive. Drinks included - coffee, water, beer. Nice and clean lounge.

Really enjoyed the KLM Crown Lounge in the non-Schengen terminal. While entering, seeing all the KLM Delfts Blue houses is a nice welcome. The lounge facilities are great, with showers, several bars and probably the biggest lounge I’ve been in since this one has two floors has a lot of space to sit everywhere (also in quiet to work). There was not much food to choose from, but the quality was good. The whole design throughout the lounge is fantastic and the crew was friendly and attentive. It was not always as clean as it should be and some chairs and tables needed some maintenance but overall the experience was very positive.

The lounge is accessed either by escalator or elevator. Glass walls by the escalators display the massive collection of Delft pottery houses which are offered to PX on long-haul flights. The lounge, whenever we have visited has been very crowded, and although huge, seating is hard to find. There are two refreshment areas, one at either end which offer different food items, so it is worth looking at both. Upstairs there is a restaurant-type situation at lunch and dinner times. I cannot comment as we have never used it.

I had free access on this trip as a guest of a frequent flyer, based on his Delta Status. I really like the KLM lounges, the staff are very helpful and pleasant. The options and layout are really nice and although the lounge seemed quite busy, we found space to sit and nap. They have showers,  a really good selection of drinks and I personally like the coffee, however the food is not good. I'd give it a 3 out of 10. I don't understand this as access is usually 50 euro with your boarding pass, and if you need to eat your are not getting value for your money. The food on the plane was better. KLM, you need to step that up. You're serving food that's worse than anything you can buy in a cheap diner.

The KLM Schengen Lounge (25) is nothing to speak of. Very busy at peak times; children running around, babies crying, numerous people talking -loudly- into their mobile phones. Limited seating. Plastic chairs at the tables are very uncomfortable. Only a few more comfortable seats, but they’re always taken by people, sitting in one seat and their feet or luggage in the other. Only one of the two counters was open for food. Not enough plates; took ages before they were restocked. Quality of the food so so: Very bland. Very limited choice. Tables were not cleaned after people had left. 2 out of the 3 coffeemakers on the non-food side were out of order. The restrooms were appalling: 3 ladies restrooms out of order. No more paper towels. Paper all over the floor. Restrooms that were not out of order were dirty! Same for the men’s restrooms: All out of order on one side of the lounge. On the other side, my husband noticed that only 3 men’s restrooms were available. Also very dirty. This lounge is an absolute disgrace for Schiphol and KLM.

This is the KLM Skyteam standard lounge at Schiphol Airport with a modern interior. Lounge is getting very busy at business times but there is usually plenty of room. The food and drink selection is ok although nothing special.

Nothing positive to say. It's crowded, it's loud filled with people talking loudly on mobile phones and babies screaming, there are no quiet zones, the lights are very bright with no dark spaces to try to rest, the food is institutional slop that looks unappetizing and tastes as such, even the showers are lame - they give you one thin towel, no hand towels, no bath mat. It's a third rate lounge from a third rate alliance and unfortunately I'm stuck here for six painful hours.

Went in with high expectations based on several public reviews. I thought they were all wildly off base. This was a very disappointing experience in many ways. I'll start with two positives: the lounge is aesthetically appealing and the staff is very nice. Beyond that it's third rate. First of all, it is way, way too crowded. It's impossible to find a place to sit and if you are fortunate enough to do so then you'll wait in a long queue for poor quality food that's basically poor institutional grade. There were over 30 people waiting in the feed line when I visited. This isn't a quality experience in any way. A lounge is supposed to be a haven and respite away from the madness if the airport. I also checked out the sleep cabins as an alternative and they are pathetic and overpriced. The cabin I was offered had an upper bunk bed that felt like I was in a hostel or pod hotel and was extremely spartan. The Crown 52 lounge is anything but that. I wouldn't buy a business class ticket to access this as a perk nor would I pay to hangout here. It's a huge disappointment and I won't return. KLM should be ashamed of this product.

It is big and well equipped but the food and snacks are rather disappointing I find. Warm food is tasteless and too obviously made in large quantities. Thankfully at a certain point they brought in lasagne that went quickly and was edible. Other skyteam lounges all over the world have so much better food. Drinks are fine, so too are some of the cold options. It can get crowded.

This is one of the best business lounges I have been to. Food is good, drinks especially the Heineken bar is great. Its huge with lots of room, and several themed sections - one for work, for entertainment and relaxing. Wifi was awesome and staff friendly and efficient. I was heavily jet lagged after a nightmare departure from Canada and was able to crash out for 2-3 hours in a relaxation , quiet area. Overall, I had an 8 hour layover which normally would have been a nightmare. But I spent the whole time in the Crown Lounge and the time passed really quickly. Thank you! One piece of constructive feedback. I couldn't find any newspapers or magazine which would have been a bonus.

After three years it was my first visit at the Crown Lounge in Amsterdam.  It starts with the nice staff at the entrance. After I asked for the shower they showed me the way. Unfortunately the system did not work. Therefore I had to go back to ask the staff to help. One minute and I had my key card for the shower. The shower room is a bit small but big enough to have a nice shower. The food area is huge and at lunch time there are plenty of choices. Its true that around noon the lounge is very crowded.  My most amazing spot in the lounge was the outdoor terrace, to sit and get some fresh air. Especially after an 12 hours flight and another 11 hours flight coming up. This lounge is impressive and the staff is great.

Not crowded, enough space. Seats good for sitting to dine and relax. Variety of warm food a bit poor. Coffee was good. Would have appreciated if they had offered gluten free meals, too. As it was offered for a reduced price, the price-value-relation was okay. We would do it again instead of lingering around in those bleak halls with expensive fast food stands and restaurants.

Lounge in Amsterdam provided was the KLM Sky Team “Lounge 52” in non-Schengen area. Very impressive design, views. Space was incredible, extend over several hectares. Must be the biggest lounge in Europe with 1500 seats? The drinks and dining was not up to the lounge appearance. No Asian dishes available, even noodles. Only one beer brand is offered in the entire lounge: Heineken – they must have paid a lot for this monopoly? 1st floor a la carte restaurant (food for purchase) while downstairs all the buffets and bars and other “areas” dominates.

Lounge 52 at Amsterdam Schiphol Airport was clean, safe, spacious and an incredibly welcoming, friendly atmosphere. The travel process to Asia now requires a screening procedure for documentation and health that is done smoothly and efficiently. Staff are really lovely and warm. Option of free shower, snacks and drinks. Excellent value for money and service. 8 hours of layover time passed quickly and I almost did not want to get out. That in addition to two wonderful flights have really pushed KLM to the top my favorite EUR airlines. Well done and please keep up the excellent standards.

A major lounge of KLM in the international concourse of Schiphol Airport. Very big lounge on two levels with actually a good design. The lounge is however overcrowded. You may barely find a place . food is average and is gone in minutes due to the crowd. A beer counter is provided which is very nice.

Very pleasant. Lots of space and a variety of seating options. There is a napping room. Also a shower facility is available. Seems  clean and well kept. Blankets and pillows are available too. The food service is adequate, good service but the food options are a bit limited and not replenished as frequently as I would like. More plugs in the back area would be good.

What a disappointment. I had read about it everywhere but was so disappointed by the actual experience. So so busy, in fact so busy that you have to just wander around watching for someone to leave so you can grab their seat. KLM have made such a mistake closing off the entire upper floor to non-paying passengers. Food and drink ok. A massive walk to the gates too. Next time I'll think twice about going in at a peak time.

KLM uses a pay-to-use lounge at Cartagena. The lounge, like the airport, is small. Food offerings were minimal although there was a fair selection of drinks. Seats were uncomfortable and there was one ladies and one gents cubicle washroom. Better than being in the main airside "lounge", but only just. In fairness, this is a small airport with no air jetties and a few flights only per day. Our KLM was en-route from Bogata to Amsterdam, just a touch down to pick up and drop off passengers and then away. Wi-fi connection was OK but slow.

Overcrowded lounge with poor seating availability. Food of poor quality, beside the salad and veggies. Ridiculous small warm food serving area. Poor wine and beer as well. Other drinks you have to pay for beside regular soft drinks and warm drinks. KLM you have done an extremely poor job with the new lounge.

My first visit to the new lounge, after all the hype I was keen to see what it looked like. The entrance up escalators was impressive and a friendly greeting from a large team as I entered. I was met with a massive seating area - really very cluttered with seating and clearly their housekeeping team had not been fully up to speed with clearing plates, glasses, newspapers etc. - it was a real mess. The various "experience areas" seemed to me to be more of a gimmick, rather than a practical use of the space. A business traveller wants a calm,quiet space.t all these fairground attractions. Furthermore, what possessed them to put a maze of steps up to the next level/bar area...I saw quite a few people struggling with trolley cases etc., trying to navigate this "mountain". Upstairs again the bar was impressive but the staff REALLY let things down....they seemed more interested in talking to each other than serving drinks... when I asked for a bloody mary, a hideous concoction was served. In my opinion this is all style and no substance, what a disappointment after all the months of promotional advertising of this new lounge.

At the time of writing the business lounge in Hato was undergoing refurbishment so C class was given a partitioned off and screened area to sit in with drinks (beer wine soft drinks and coffee) and a voucher for food. The voucher wasn't enough to buy a sandwich so was a bit pointless. That having been said as you seem to spend most of your time on long hall flights eating it wasn't much of an issue for me. I think a few snacks would go down well though. The lounge itself was Ok with views over the airfield and the sea, I’ve been in worse lounges.

I had the pleasure of spending time twice in the Aspire Lounges of Schiphol, I definitely recommend a place in Terminal 3 there is a place to smoke, however I do not support this addiction but it was much easier. Smooth wifi, fresh tasty food. I consider my stays a good rest between flights.
The lounge was huge, set across three levels. Clearly new, but not enough seats or toilets. Would choose another if possible, but due to the size of Schipol we choose not to try and look for another.

I understand that the lounge is being renovated. Didn't seem to be any disruption to services in the lounge that really were of the highest standard. What I want in a lounge is a calm environment away from hustle of the airport at large, nice food and often a shower to freshen up between flights (I frequently need to change 1 or 2 times on my trips). Crown Lounge at Amsterdam knocks it out of the park! Food last night was fabulous, not just bland finger food but tasty soups, chicken wings, pasta. Some lounges might look more spectacular, like Turkish in Istanbul or BA First in London but this place is a very good lounge that does everything travellers need really well. Staff very helpful, lounge kept spotless, shower facilities available. Amsterdam is a great place to fly through.

Very comfortable lounge. I think this is open to lounge pass holders and some credit cards but the size and design of the lounge meant that it did not feel over crowded as some lounges of this kind do. Food available was of a really high standard as was the selection of drinks. There is a rest area so you are able to lie down for an hour or two between flights should you feel the need. I enjoyed my stay at this lounge and will look forward to returning.

Was here with my 4 kids all under 11 years old. Because I have the AMEX platinum FB card I can share my status with the wife and we get all 4 kids in! They loved it. Nice tit bits, pasta pomodori, soup, soft drinks. Informative display on the new lounge end of the year which will boast a sky deck!
Very disappointing lounge. It's a large lounge but nothing exciting about it. The food and drink provided is very basic, and it feels like a huge train station waiting room.

This is a business lounge for non-star alliance passengers traveling through Vienna, the Schengen area. The lounge is located before the security control, and the information on it is safely hidden, so I needed to come back from the security area, and then to re-enter it again. I would never do that, if I have imagined how basic the lounge was, especially in terms of food - it could not offer anything except mediocre coffee and a croissant. You can get much better a breakfast anywhere in the airport at a very reasonable price, and also in a much cozier set-up. Summing up - visiting this lounge is not even worth the efforts for finding it.

Excellent, relaxing chairs, WiFi, showers, restrooms very clean. The food and wine was excellent. Very busy as one can imagine. One thing is very confusing. The location says 52 so you have to walk a long way from and to your gate.

The Erste Premier Lounge (Skyteam + Priority Pass lounge) at Prague Airport. After the security and a 5 minute walk, I accessed the lounge. The reception staff were okay. The lounge was really full and only a few seats were available. I found one at the far end of the lounge. The seat is a leather seat not so comfortable, the electric plug wasn't working at the seat. I guess it's one of the reason why it was still available. The bar offered lots of options from soft drinks to Becherovska, wine and beers. Some of the beers are Czech but the displayed wine was from Italy. Regarding the food, although it was dinner time, only soup was available.

The Al Dhabi lounge felt underwhelming - it was crowded and cramped (too many airlines sharing and some pay-to-use passengers), it struggled to provide adequate sitting space when I was there. The lounge was also noisy and claustrophobic - low ceilings, with no windows at all.

Overall poor. Food is cold, uninspiring and the drinks in the fridge are warm. The lounge is entirely self service and quite poorly decorated with little to no ambience. I would highly recommend a trip to the Cathay Pacific lounges at Hong Kong international airport...by comparison this lounge falls far behind. A very poor effort I am afraid - which I hope will not reflect too badly on KLM. We are already paying a premium to be seated in business class- this is not a good first impression.

This lounge is packed with 'pay to use' drinking people and poor food. Not much space left for business travellers and suitable place to work. In my view not really representing what KLM stands for. The next door BA lounge is of a much beter quality.

I used the KLM Crown Lounge in Amsterdam as a Flying Blue frequent flyer. When I arrived, I found the staff quite rude at the welcome desk, but kind in the lounge itself, which was clean and comfortable. It has many wide seats, with individual lights and power sockets. You can also sit in the smoking area or at one of the many work spaces. Taking a shower is possible too. From the buffet, you can choose between warm dishes, soups, salads and deserts. There is also a coffee and tea corner. The choice is not very large but the quality of the food is good. The bar offers a nice choice between alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks. It was a good experience overall, but, in my opinion, the staff at the entrance should adopt a friendlier attitude.

The word "Functional" is what best describes the KLM crown lounges in Amsterdam Schiphol Airport. The lounge has all the basic things a lounge needs. Many seating possibilities, power access, internet access, drinks, food and clean toilets. However it doesn't have showers or spa treatments like you find in other airline business lounges. The main negative aspect is the low quality and variety of the food available. Almost everytime I visit this lounge, there is overcooked pasta carbonara, not enough fried onion rings and tasteless chicken wings.

Very nice lounge with a lot of different seats, a lot of them are thought for reading and have their own light. Several business positions equipped with a computer. Nice bar. Staff is kind. Evrything is clean and the lounge is also very quiet. The smoking area is nice too. Probably just a little cold.

Had a nice shower before my flight back to Kansai.  However, as the other people have stated, why is that the food selection in this lounge is so mediocre? I only found a dish of warm Penne Pasta, random cheese, and a soup. Besides this, there was no food whatsoever. The food selection in this lounge so bad compared to all the other lounges I have visited. Also, before peak hours the lounge can get very crowded. Maybe its time to install a second one.

Flew on KLM business class from Denpasar to Singapore and was invited to use the premium lounge free. I was a bit disappointed that at first I thought it is a business class lounge but later i realized it was a pay-in lounge, just complimentry for business class passengers. Despite that, the lounge was clean and relaxing, with a delicious buffet dinner. There were boarding calls in the lounge as well.

Leaving on a 3PM flight, we checked in and headed to the bussiness class lounge belonging to Skyteam to have some lunch while we were waiting. The big surprise was that there were just two trays with croissants. Nothing else at all. Completely uninteresting, with no variety of magasines nor journals. Incredibly poor.

The lounge is very spacious and the staff very friendly, but the offering is poor on many counts. Breakfast with a few flakes and some cheese and coissants. There was nothing more substantial. In fact the offering was inferior to that offered in the lounge at Bristol airport, and to almost every lounge I have been in in the last two years. The bar area was tiny. I was really surprised by this as this should be their flagship lounge. Not impressed.

I've been in this KLM lounge at Schiphol Airport three times in the last month, when travelling on business. The ticket system to get help, advice or a shower is okay once you understand it, but no effort is made to explain to 'newbies' . Like a previous reviewer I found the staff curt to the point of rude. On two of my visits I wanted a shower, the first time I waited an hour, the second I timed out after waiting 90 mins, therefore you have to conclude the facilities are inadequate. The food is basic, nothing hot. It's a big space, the wifi is free, but it's not special.

The SkyTeam lounge in LHR T4 is one of the flagship lounges of the SkyTeam alliances and it is one of the better SkyTeam lounges in Europe. The selection of food items was generous, kept fresh and the selection is changed multiple times during the day. I was able to observe the change between lunch and dinner menu due to an extended 6 hours layover in LHR T4.  The selection of beverages is standard, a pretty reputable spirits collection is present as well. The lounge is a two level lounge and the ground floor can be quite crowded, so if you like it a bit more calm and content, go to the first floor. There is no smokers section within the grounds of the lounge, but LHR T4 has a public airside smoking section opposite gate 6.

KLM use the Swissport Aspire Lounge at Birmingham airport. The lounge has a nice view on the Apron,, the quiet zone is somehow misplaced, directly at the entrance of the lounge, so a quiet zone needs to be seen as relative. The choice of food is limited to some warmed up croissants and some soft panini's with bacon and some cereals (I had a late morning departure) which is a bit embarassing, but no surprise for a generic, non Airline specific lounge. The drinks and booze have a significant larger choice, but who really wants to drink heavy stuff at 9AM in the morning?The facility does not offer dedicated toilets and you need to go back to the public toilets outside.

As this is presumably the mother-ship of the KLM lounges, I found it to be very disappointing. It's gloomy and dull and the food offering is very poor. Crackers and floppy slices of cheese, and two pots of some stew-like dish, which didn't look appetising. Nothing looked fresh or appetising. It really wasn't a treat to come to this lounge, and we're stuck here for 4 hours!

Recently refurbished and enlarged. Can be very crowded depending on the time. Drink selection excellent but the food is boring. One of the few places at Schiphol with a dedicated smoking area. Good selection of newspapers. Staff in general are friendly but sometimes can be a bit snobbish. Compared to other Sky Team lounges quite nice.

KLM Crown lounge in Dubai is perfect when all other seats are taken in the airport. Apart from free WiFi, the lounge offers nothing more than the rest of the public area of the airport. It is clean and the staff is professional, but the food offered is nothing good. Drinks are available, but when it is busy you have to be lucky to get you preferred drink. Compeared to the competitors airline lounge this one is a real joke!

The KLM lounge is very large and features a wide array of seats. The seats in the dining area are not as comfortable as the seats in the rest of the lounge, which feature electric outlets to charge your device. The food is nice, hot and cold food throughout the day as well as  alcoholic beverages, coffee and typical dutch appetizers such as 'drop' (liquorish) and 'stroopwafels' (syrup waffels). Staff is friendly, restrooms well maintained and clean. Downside: As air traffic at Schiphol increases (and the Skyteam passengers with it), the lounge, large as it is, is becoming too small for the volumes of passengers. The seats have marks of wear and tear.

Very, very busy. We managed to obtain seats in eating area for breakfast. Food choice OK, just that. Cereals, yogurt, rolls, two choices of ham , one of cheese and some boiled eggs. Alcohol choice much wider but given the time of day we didn't partake. I would have thought that as this is a business lounge the ladies toilets could have at least had some hand cream and a nice selection of toiletries. People wandering in and out at will, if the staff were busy on the front desk no check was made on who was using the lounge. As travelling on a business ticket, lounge included but if I had to pay I would have gone to the main departure area where there was a better choice of food.

Easy to find. Clean and quiet, a nice haven during busy periods. Staff thorough on checking who has access to the lounge, clipped and efficient, not friendly but not rude. The main area has comfortable seats with a range of soft drinks, a limited range of beer and wine. Crisps, nuts, cream cheese and olives set out for self service. There is no hot food, if your plane is delayed, or you need something more substantial you will need to go into the main departure area. There is an additional additional seating area if you walk past the short corridor towards the toilets. This wasn't clearly posted and might be important if you arrive and the first room is full. Wi fi excellent, desks also available. There is only one toilet per gender, normally fine but could be a problem if delayed. For the size of the airport, fine.

The lounge overall was pretty good, a nice selection of drinks and snacks but they didn't have any meals. The lounge seats were really comfortable,  staff were friendly and welcoming. The lounge was clean as well as the toilets, but they did not have any showers. The lounge had free, good WiFi.

Food and drinks were ok but they have a number system to get customer service. This system seems to allow the KLM staff the opportunity to sit around, not helping anyone other than directing them to take a number. Overall the process is inefficient, slow, and not very customer focussed.

A huge disappointment. Limited and poor food and beverage offer (only potato chips, olives and an awful soup), no newspapers or magazines, crowded and dated facility. Internet Access required a complicated check-on process, so we quit. Shame on KLM.

Intolerable noise levels. Constant ringing of some bell for unclear reason, frequent overheads. Frantic atmosphere. No chance of getting a shower. Food is minimal, though not bad what little there is. WiFi a bit sketchy. Bathroom looked like a warzone, used towels everywhere, hadn't been tidied up in quite a while. Inadequate facilities.
Longe was spacious, clean, and comfortable. Tasty food and drink was served enough. Staff often clean our table and the restrooms.

Just brutal. I had a 2 hour layover on my flight from YYC-JNB. I desperately needed a shower so went to this lounge which was miles from my gate. KLM staff were rude and refused to acknowledge my existence. I finally figured out the number system for the shower. Got 65 and they were on something under 30. The lounge was crowded and noisy. I bailed without my shower and didn't even bother with the aggravation on the return trip and made do with wet wipes in the public bathroom. Not what I expected from a Business Class lounge.

This is the worst "Business Class" lounge I have been in by a country mile. In fact calling it a lounge is a joke. It's full to capacity some people going straight back out because there aren't enough seats and only 1 or 2 charging points to fight over the décor is tired and dated. The toilets are absolutely disgusting I walked in then straight out to find some others in the Airport. No wonder they hide this facility down one of the gates and barely signpost it it really is that embarrassing. Most lounges offer easy access Wifi if you fight your way through all the mobile registration palava you're rewarded with a temperamental and incredibly slow service presumably due to the volume of users. Come on KLM you have to do better than this.
Great lounge lots of seating areas good selection to eat and drink. Wi Fi great with no problems staff very good and clean shower toilet areas.

Had high expectations as my family provided solid praise from their visit a few years ago. Was not disappointed. It's not a "huge" place but enough room for all on a Saturday afternoon dealing with a variety of flights. The self-serve drinks were varied and adequate the food skewed a bit to Asian spicy (for China Airlines pax?) and the seating comfortable and varied. A nice view of the apron & planes to boot. The only downside was the staffer on desk duty who was quite perplexed on how to deal with our Diner's Club cards had to ask in the back and in the end (as per my statement) I was charged for 3 guests instead of 3 free card admissions. (now under dispute for a refund). Ironically we were flying KLM and ran into a rather rude KLM staffer who was flogging $35 passes to all & sundry in the check-in area. Said our DC cards would not get us in. (yes they do that lounge desk girl not withstanding). That being said the guest rate for Diner's is only usd$28 or about cad$30. For about the same you can get into the Plaza Premium lounge right across the hall from Crown. However I do recommend it just try to maximize your time there.

We needed to wait for close to four hours as the shopping centre next to the airport turned out to be closed. At Athens international airport KLM uses the Goldair lounge. The lounge offers comfortable chairs and provides good views of the runway but also the car rental centre. Wifi is provided for free but didn't work that well. There are desktop computers available as well as power sockets to charge your devices. What was disappointing was the lack of a shower / changing room (although the toilets were spacious) and the assortment of food was questionable. All in all not a bad experience but nothing like the KLM / Air France operated lounges. We saw that Lufthansa does operate their own lounge at Athens by the way.

The KLM/AF lounge is located adjacent to the international boarding gates in terminal D. It can be accessed from the other terminals as well via the inter-terminal train without having to go through security. The lounge is relative small but I have not seen it overcrowded in the two times I visited. The seating is comfortable with the same types of chairs as the KLM lounges in AMS. In the middle of the lounge is the food and beverage area. The food is better than the AMS lounges with sandwiches salads soup cookies and other snacks as well as soft drinks and liquor. The booze selection is better than you will find in domestic carrier lounges. It is all free and self serve. You make everything the way you like it and no bartender to tip. There are two TVs located t either end of the lounge. The staff will accommodate your channel requests. There are boarding announcements and the gates are 60 seconds or less away. So you can remain in the sanctuary of the lounge until just before stepping on the plane. It would be nice if they added a shower. The restrooms are clean and adequate in number.
Would recommend this lounge came with all the fixings loads of snacks (great variety too) and drinks. Lounge access was only $35 and well worth it great option instead of paying for airport dinner.

Nice surroundings comfortable chairs good connections good food and drinks (but limited choice). Can be crowded at times because so many partner airlines may use it as well. Well kept toilet area and shower facilities. A good start towards a long flight.

If you're flying out of Dammam this is the only lounge in town and it's marginally better than hanging out in the gate area at a coffee shop or the soon to be completed Cinnabon. Service in the lounge is almost non-existent and food selection is hit or miss -- sometimes there was dismal food but no plates to put it on other times there were marginally edible hot dishes (for example: rice a kind of chicken stew some really boring sauteed vegetables). There were not-very-tempting pastries in plastic wrap; maybe they were better than they looked but I didn't give them a try. There's no alcohol because you're in Saudi Arabia; you can get coffee tea soft drinks and faux juice drinks. I couldn't get WiFi and couldn't find anyplace where I could comfortably use a laptop anyway.

We had a long layover at Muscat so decided to crash at Oman Air Business Lounge. Great clean full facilities and food. Have great separate area for sleeping. Biggest problem was noises made by loud staff throwing dishes and they started vacuuming at 2am.

Lounge is open since may 2013 located on the first floor. The lounge is small and has a variety of drinks alcoholic and non alcoholic and breads/croissants. There is wifi (the cloud) and a tv with danish channels. For this small airport the lounge is in my opinion sufficient.

The worst lounge? Like Air France Business Class Lounge in Paris CDG KLM clearly take the view that business class passengers are just a nuisance. The lounge is just row upon row of tired seating. The food is awful and wine undrinkable. Sad to say having just achieved gold status on Flying Blue (by accident!) I will probably have to use it again but I will want to eat elsewhere. And the staff have zero interest in passengers. Finally the washroom was filthy and smelt really bad. The one redeeming feature the WiFi copes will despite the constant overcrowding.
A fairly large lounge plenty of space and wifi. Food choice poor and quality not up to much. Was very disappointing. Being a smoker the only saving grace was the smoking room in the lounge.
Why bother the lounge is so small only sandwiches a few random spirits no toilet/shower in the lounge. Go to the Air France lounge a few meters away.
One of the worst lounges they fill it up until there is no space left food is too basic no shower facilities as part of the entry you have to pay extra. And the service is quite bad.

lounge_name: KLM BUSINESS CLASS CROWN LOUNGE REVIEW
review: Not my first time in this lounge and it has nicely improved for those who remember the previous lounge. Food quality receives an average score. Drinks as much as you want. Cleaning and cooking staff should work faster as many plates of food remained empty too long and many empty plates and glasses remained too long where nobody was sitting. Staff are polite and helpful. Showers and lavatories are clean and comfortable showers can be very busy at peak hours. Seats are comfortable and give you a nice view of airport. If there would be some more tvs and some reading material such as international news papers this lounge would receive a better note.

lounge_name: KLM / AIR FRANCE BUSINESS CLASS LOUNGE REVIEW
review: Tiny lounge for KLM and Air France. In the evening when both flights to Amsterdam and Paris leave within 10mins of each other people were standing around. Very warm poor selection of food. One drinks machine and slow internet. I left soon after and went to main terminal to get more space and air.

The lounge is nice with ample room. The choices of bevarages and food/snacks are OK. Cleanliness is somewhat debatable as the gents toilets were dirty and with an unpleasant smell. But the policy of internet access was really annoying - you get 30 mins free acess - and that's it. When I asked for another acess card I was rather impolitely told that there were only one per customer! Arguably you could use your mobile with tethering but that's also expensive. A better plan for wifi access would be a nice touch.

I have used this lounge for KLM flights to and fro from Kuala Lumpur to Chicago. The lounge is big and spreads out. You can find a comfortable spot. There is a quiet room for those who prefer a nap. The food is not that great so best to have meals outside the lounge.

Best thing to say about KLM lounges in Scriphol is that they are big. Most other services are mediocre. Biggest of all concerns is the attitude with most of the staff servicing customers : they are constantly sipping coffee and tea which they serve themselves from the same place as customers. When it comes to service they are usually short rude and inconsistent (between staff and the two lounges in the airport). I have been coming in the KLM lounges for well over five years and this is a repeated observation.

Visited the KLM Crown Lounge en route between Manchester and Taipei. First visit was 6pm in the evening and the lounge was quiet with plenty of choice of seats excellent choice of food and drink and fast wifi. On the way back we arrived at 7am and the lounge was far busier but the choice of food for breakfast items was still very comprehensive although the Wifi seemed a bit slower. I took advantage of the complimentary shower facilities but had to wait over an hour for my slot as it was so busy but as we had a long lay over it was no issue for me.
Morning visit before my connection to FRA. Very large clean and new looking lounge full breakfast bar hot and cold food and drinks. WIFI was available but didn't have time to use it.

This terminal was under construction while I was there. Its located up stairs and you have to go out of the secure area. Roomy lounge and not crowded with nice view comfortable seating cold/warm food and lots of drinks of all kinds. 30 min before the boarding time a KLM rep came to escort all passengers to the security point and made it to the gate few min just before boarding and all went very well.

I arrived for a mid-morning flight and huge lounge was packed out. The food and drink area was in a circular design to handle the hordes but food was not of particularly good quality and the lounge didn't have a feeling of exclusivity. Much more food on offer out in the terminal itself. Only good point was free wifi and a free drink.

Not impressed with this lounge. At breakfast it was packed to the brim with passengers and the food on offer was very limited. Old computers tired furniture and a hectic atmosphere made me think it would be better to just go outside to one of the many concessions. No elite feeling whatsoever.

KLM Crown Lounge is very large. You might find yourself walking quite a distance to reach depending on which gate you are departing from. The front desk staff are friendly and the wifi log in details are displayed at the desk. The seats are comfortable and have plug outlets. The food is actually pretty good. During lunch/dinner time you can get fried rice with chicken curry. For breakfast they serve a lot of pastries and other stuff. They have a large restroom inside the lounge as well as a business center where you can use the complimentary computers.

This is the lounge KLM inflicts upon it's business class passengers (not operated by KLM). It's small with dated decor. There is only one toilet cubicle for each sex. Food looked very ordinary. No wine. So bad I left and went to the bar opposite - so I could at least still use the free wifi. Please KLM - do a deal with Malaysian Airlines for your passengers to use their lounge. They're your codeshare partner in this part of the world!

KLM/Air France Business Class Lounge in Johannesburg was dirty uncomfortable and shabby. I had the impression that it is the old Virgin Atlantic Lounge KLM/Air France took over the old lounge and that was it. They might think it is not necessary to renovate the place but at the moment it is not the standard of KLM/Air France. During my stay my table was never cleared of glasses or plates. There was nobody to clean the place or to take care of anything.

KLM crown lounge in AMS is far below its sister lounge in CDG. Little food to eat it was lunch time and poor quality of drinks. My seven year old son was charged 45e to be able to get inside the lounge whereas he got in for free at Paris. So I paid 45e so that he could drink a glass of water and have some crackers. KLM staff is rough in the air and on the ground.
Lounge huge with a nice assortment of snacks and drinks and there was a nice beef bourgignon on offer. Plenty of newspapers free WiFi but not the best speed. Staff friendly.

Crown lounge near gates B. Very clean and adequate shower cubicles. Had a few drinks and nibbles from the bar broad choice of newspapers. Very good lounge stylish with plenty of corners and areas to suit mood or privacy.

A large open plan lounge which feels light and airy but very functional. Seats are comfortable with light and power at the vast majority. The selection of food was limited to nibbles/snacks - snack biscuits cheese cubes cheery tomatoes and soup. Not a great deal else - no sandwiches. Wine selection was good Heineken beer on tap and a range of standard quality spirits were on offer. Wifi was free however required you to reconfigure your mailbox if you wished to send emails. An enclosed entertainment area playing news channels made up the centre piece of the lounge washrooms were clean and tidy. The downside of the lounge was that there seemed to be a lack of staff clearing away such a large area resulting in a number of tables having "leftovers" on them for a considerable periods of time.

The lounge is not that bad once you get past the very inconsistent service agents. This time I was refused lounge access as although being a Platinum for life I had a boarding pass for Turkish Airlines!

Used both Schengen and 52 lounge - great improvement over last time I used them - they have been refurbished. Free WiFi was very welcome. Good selection of self service drinks - snacks very limited. A good place to spend an hour or so waiting for your next flight.

Crowded lounge with good drinks selection and meagre snacks. Overall plastic and cheap-feel to it compared to AF or EK lounges in Dubai. Still a welcome haven from the crowded Dubai airport main lounges.

This lounge is shared by several airlines and was a pretty poor show. The lounge was really congested and there were not enough seats for all the passengers. Our flight was delayed so we spent even longer in there than planned. The front desk staff were pleasant but they chatted to one another non stop about another member of staff. As I was seated beside them I could not help but overhear. Not very professional!

A very underwhelming business class lounge. food selection and quality is mediocre it is always busy and the toilets and shower rooms are boiling hot. What use is it to take a shower only to sweat through a shirt before you leave the shower room? At first I thought it was just me because I overheat easily but watching other passengers leave the shower area they were all red faced and sweating. Then there's the obvious issues with cleanliness the showers I've used have all had mould there is no shower curtain so the water splashes out onto your luggage and all over the floor. Add to that no wash cloths one towel and no floor mat and it is an entirely unpleasant experience. I've given them a few opportunities but from here on out I'm just going to go without a shower; remaining dirty is preferable to using these facilities. Then there's the staff on every occasion I've been to this lounge some KLM employees are courteous but most are dismissive rude and not the least bit interested in customer satisfaction. KLM service has been falling steadily over the years and it is apparent that things are near a breaking point as obvious budget cuts and lack of planning/staff training for non-aircraft positions doesn't rank more than a single star. On a plus side there is wi-fi I am using to write this!
