China Airlines VIP Lounge at Terminal 1 was such a hidden gem! Not only it was very large but also extremely elegant and luxurious. Once passing through the check-in counter, we were amazed by a long and beautiful corridor. There were many comfortable seats in the lounge. Shower and toilette were clean and nice. F&B selection was generous, tasty. We really liked the hot station. WiFi was fast too.
The Lounge is a Long stair down. We went for breakfast, it was Basic, low quality and tasteless. Really disappointing for this airline. They close at 10 PM

Very enjoyable lounge for a very long layover! Food selection was great and varied throughout the day. Seats were comfortable with both sofas and tables available with power points easily accessible (regular universal power outlet, no USB). Staff friendly and very attentive at clearing away and helping out if necessary. Internet was easily accessed and very quick and reliable. Bathrooms were clean and showers were very appreciated - there are 2 in this lounge and sometimes you need to book up to 30 minutes before, especially during the peak times (early morning 6-9am and evening 5-9pm). Unfortunately the 2 small 'sleeping rooms' in this lounge had the lounge music way too loud and announcements also played in this room making it impossible to actually sleep! These rooms were also very cold. Almost better off trying to nap in the actual lounge itself than these rooms. They also make far too many announcements in the lounge about delays or gate changes, especially when my small delay of 20 minutes was communicated via text, email and the lounge attendant even came and found my personally to let me know! These announcements affected the relaxed atmosphere. TIP: I also visited the China Airlines lounge on the B side in Terminal 1 and another in Terminal 2 and this A side lounge in T1 definitely seemed the best of the 3!

I used the flagship CI lounge once every few months. On my last visit (end of June) the lounge is crowded as usual. On two occasions after a long haul flight I was told that the queue for the shower rooms (there are only three cubic) was more than an hour. The lounge is very dark without natural light. The shower rooms were also very dark and not well designed - water pressure wasn't great and the amenities provided were very cheap. No body lotion was offered. In the main lounge the reading materials provided were not up to standard so were the food and drink.

This lounge is located in terminal 2, and is fairly nicely designed with a Chinese theme, subtle and elegant. At 5pm it was not crowded and an oasis of calm and peace. Some of the seats overlooking the seats overlooking the tarmac. Food wise, the offering is not big, but consider the small amount of passengers they are serving, it was sufficient. Good selections of drinks and reading material. I have enjoyed my visit here.

Emirates use the China Airlines Lounge at Taoyuan Airport. I was pleasantly surprised by the quiet atmosphere, low lighting and decor of the lounge. However, some passengers and myself were a bit lost finding our way to the washrooms, as the signage seem to blend into decor colours making it difficult to read and spot easily. Fantastic food and the Noodle Bar offered me the Taiwanese Beef Noodle Soup as a pleasant farewell to my visit to Taipei. Very attentive staff, quietly clearing after you've finished your food or drink.

One of the best Lounges I've visited, nice entrance, warm lights in the lounge, nice rest area, shower room is ok. The food and beverage is quite good and variety. I think the lounge looks very luxurious, comfortable seating area and eating area. It's decorated with good taste. The wifi is running quite fast. Very satisfied with this lounge.

This lounge at Honolulu was a complete travesty! It had an awful, musty, moldy smell with powerfully cold air conditioning that hit me upon entry. Once checked in, I found that the size was that of a typical living room. The food on offer was all things purchased at Costco or some discount warehouse with the exception of finger sandwiches. The drinks in the cooler were frozen on the top shelf. The food was meant to be eaten on styrofoam bowls, not even plates. It was utterly depressing. It is the most memorable and disappointing lounges I've ever had the misfortune to enter.

This is not China Airlines lounges, but a handling agent lounge - it was marred by a number of crying babies and paltry selection of food. Sad lack of vegetables, fruit or meats here. Beverage selection was OK.  The staff doesn't seem to actively take care of its customers.

What a disappointment to be sent to this China Airlines lounge at Taipei Terminal 2 (4D)! Worst business class lounge we have encountered. If you want food, computer use or bathroom, then you get to walk down a flight of stairs - no elevator for the handicapped or elderly. The dungeon-like lounge consists of rows of upholstered chairs and small tables, with stains obvious on some of the upholstery. The food offered is marginal and unappealing, even the Asian folks were leaving large amounts of uneaten food on their plates. You'd do better by buying a meal in the terminal. The women's bathroom was dated with chipped and cracked counter and flooring. The electronic toilet with the pop-up lid didn't pop up. Not at all impressed with anything about this lounge or China Airlines. Will use another carrier for future trips if this is an example of the amenities they offer.

Terrible lounge in Terminal 2, TPE. This is one of two China Airlines lounges in T2: the better one is reserved for CI passengers, everyone else from Skyteam airlines gets shunted into the other, a 2 level airless, windowless dungeon-like facility, offering extremely limited, low quality food options. On this spring evening the lounge was plagued with mosquitos and a staff member was wandering around trying to kill them with what looked like a badminton bat. Not much reciprocity from China Airlines as its own frequent flyers get access to the far better lounges of the other Skyteam members (maybe Delta excluded). Using this lounge is a waste of time: much better food in the paid outlets.

The newly designed Dynasty lounge is spacious, lots of food choices and is chic with lots of mood lighting, use of dark coloured wood and stones. It is a comfortable lounge to spend an hour or two, bathroom and showers are plenty and clean. It was a joy to come here and relax. Please note that the lounge in terminal 2 is totally different to this one in T1, this one is more sensational.

A decent lounge with a good selection of food. Attended this lounge in conjunction with a China Airlines flight. The lounge is a shared lounge with a number of alliances (I think apart from One World and Emirates), as well as Priority Pass members. The space seemed to be ample at the time of review - with individual tables for dining and more comfortable armchairs for relaxation. A number of desktop computers were available but these days, a marker of outmodedness. The services unfortunately, was a little tardy. My flight was around dinner time so understandably, many guests were having meals. I have seen plates that were uncollected throughout my 30-40 minute stay in the lounge and hot food was allowed to deplete without being replenished. There were two showers and two toilet cubicles available; and guests would need to inform the staff to get a shower kit. It was inadequate for the number of guests. While not nearly in the same league as the likes of Qantas lounges, it had all the basics.

Small and unimpressive. I used this China Airlines Dynasty Lounge when flying with Asiana Airlines from SFO to Incheon. After using the Asiana Lounge at Incheon, this was a big disappointment. Room filled up, food consisted of sandwiches, sliced fruit chip and noodles. No TV, no flight board read-out, no business center and the list goes on.

Food quality is well and a variety of selection offering at the lounge. I enjoy the noodle bar and also dim sum. Staff are friendly and often look around to see if passenger need to be taken care of. The sleeping room is quiet to take a rest. The seat area like small balcony giving a room of privacy.
Very basic. Overheated. No shower. No fresh fruit or vegetables. No muffins cookies or crackers. Limited selection of indifferent hot food. Both coffee machines were broken.
The lounge is on two levels. While the lower floor is noisier it has a good noodle soup bar. On balance the lounge is acceptable but not as good as most other business class lounges.

Food quality is very superb. I love the noodle bar. The dim sum selection and beverage selections are plentiful. The shower rooms are very nice. There is plenty of room downstairs although as others have stated it can get extremely busy at night when the flights to North America and Australia are leaving.

The food is varied with hot Thai dishes fresh fruit sandwiches cakes and many drink options including fresh young coconut. The flight was delayed and though we were given a coupon for a meal in the terminal there was no need to use it with what was on offering the lounge. The wifi worked but the two computers with Thai keyboards in their business area did not. Friendly and efficient staff. Only complaint is that there is no toilet in the lounge.

Decent food and drink options but nothing spectacular. Comfortable and in a convenient location. The front desk staff does not have a computer connected to the reservations system so the poor attendant could not do anything besides check to see if we were legitimate to enter or not.

Not a fan. It was very crowded as I arrived for a late flight to Taipei. Hard backed chairs no couches or lounge chairs of any type. Very limited plugs to recharge electronics. There was a piece of paper taped to the beverage machine showing some complex code to get access to the wifi even when entered it didn't work luckily got on via the Air France lounge which must be close by. Limited beverage choices. Very bad food. Tiny albeit functional bathroom. If I had known how bad it was I would have stayed in the Delta lounge in the domestic terminal.

China Airlines use the Alitalia lounge which give that Rome is their home base the lounge is poor. Why is it that airlines think that putting a lounge where there are no windows is good. Food and drink selection poor seating unimaginative toilets dirty.

Very basic seating. No view at all. Food very limited although the noodle bar was good. Shower rooms clean but too complicated. Plenty of computer and internet terminals. In the late evening when the North American and Australian flights are due to leave gets very busy with shortage of seats

Heavy crowds with lots of airlines visiting this lounge. To find a seat is really difficult. There are inside and outside (patio) facilities. Poor food selection with basic sandwiches and cheese. Drinks were good. When someone leaves a table, it takes some time to get it cleaned. Nothing special

LAN offered access to two lounges, Sumaq and VIP, in Lima airport for Premier Business and elite passengers. Both lounges were shared with Priority Pass members and were extremely crowded. My friends and I need to queue for 10 minutes, for checking our boarding passes, before allowing into the lounge. Cold sandwiches, fruits and soft-drinks were served inside. Toilets are small and showers only available in Sumaq.

Fast and stable internet connection. Wines were fine. The food was not very varied (mostly sandwiches and some fruits) but there was a nice selection of ice creams and drinks. The staff was very friendly. The press selection was quite limited. Nothing relevant to point out.

Firstly, like all soft LAN products, it's very hit and miss. Second time here and the front desk were ambivalent towards us as opposed to last time where we were warmly welcomed. The food is very basic, really basic.  The wine is passable. The layout is somewhat disjointed, but it does afford different zones. Avoid upstairs facing the runway and views, it's hot, even when the sun isn't beaming in. Maybe someone forgot to pay the power bill which would be very LAN. On the plus side, the seating is excellent and the premium entry is a great idea which means you avoid queues. But no one is likely to tell you, so remember to head upstairs to the right of the terminal, you won't regret it (they don't check your boarding pass so I suspect anyone could use it). I wish it was better, but it's not bad and any lounge is better than no lounge!

The VIP Lounge of TAM/LAN inaugurated in March 2015 is excellent. There are 2 floors with a view of the courtyard from Santiago Airport: good space, plenty of tables and comfortable chairs. Employees were polite and helpful. I took a shower and it was great: much space and an amenity kit available. Wi-fi was good. You can use a sleeping room: a dark and quiet environment. But in terms of food and drink, there are many options but they are not great.

Amazing lounge, a huge step up from the previous ones. Massive in a way you are not used to see in Latin America, but also very well organized, with plenty of space for every kind of traveller. I visited it in a rush hour (late evening departures) and it didn't feel packed. Food provided is nothing to die for, but with a nice selection of sandwiches, sushi and some local specialties. Excellent wines and champagne. Overall, a welcome and much needed improvement due to the size LATAM has achieved and Santiago airport as well.

The new LATAM lounge in SCL Airport. Huge 2 story lounge. Was not crowded in the evening when LAN has lot of flights. Open bar with excellent alcoholic (incl Champaign) and non-alcoholic choices. Food selection good for a Business Class lounge. Sushi was great. There are also tasty Sandwiches. Hot empanadas and pastries apart from chips and nuts. Fresh salads available. Clean showers and clean private restrooms. Good Wifi and there is even a room big screen cartoon for travelers with kids. Another big screen shows sport events. Great Tarmac views. Overall great Biz lounge that beats their competition at SCL, especially the US Carrier lounges. I'd rate 10 instead of 8 if there would be a soup and pasta choice as well for those who don't like Sushi and bread that much and more choices for vegetarians.

LAN Airlines lounge at Santiago de Chile Airport is tucked into a corner of the terminal on the first floor is this pleasant lounge offering a reasonable choice of beverages and snacks. The girls at the reception were welcoming. There were staff circling the lounge to remove empty plates and glasses. The wifi was excellent, the quality of my Facetime call home was superb.

The LAN Sala VIP at Bogota Airport is a crowded and overheated place, it is always hard to find a free seat. EDR airport is tiny for its huge traffic, with only three lounges for the international operations. Limited and poor food and beverages.
LAN Airlines Business Class lounge at Santiago de Chile Airport is a run of the mill lounge, good selection of newspapers basic food and drink. Wifi. Clean toilets.

LAN Airlines Business Class Lounge at Buenos Aires is one of the best lounges I have come across. Spacious comfortable seating well stocked with day's newspapers and well stocked bar and food. Spotless toilets.

The LAN Ecuador Diamond Club Business Class lounge at Guayaquil Airport is a pretty poor Lounge. While the chairs were reasonably comfortable and the Lounge was clean the food quality and choice was very poor. Crisps and nuts were OK but the sandwiches were dried up with a very poor selection. I never discovered what was on the savoury biscuits. There were unlabelled jugs of coloured fluid - presumably drinks - and Coke/Fanta etc available from the bar. Alcoholic drinks were available at a charge. The computer I went to use wouldn't connect to the internet but someone from the front desk sorted it quickly.

The lounge is on 2 levels and generally comfortable, although they don't seem to be able to do climate control very well. The food, however, was pretty terrible - no vegetarian options at all (and we were there through both breakfast and lunch service, unfortunately). Staff don't speak English, are not helpful and there seem to be very few of them. I had to go back to the service desk in the lounge several times to even find someone there. If you inquire at the entry service desk they will just say they can't help you and send you over to the other service desk, which is empty. The internet mostly did not work.

Early morning use of the Aspire Lounge at Newcastle. Good service from staff, a little slow to check in but nothing to bad. Bacon sandwiches very good, but no Irish whiskey of any cider of any type. Come on Aspire, its not much to ask is it!

Divided into several lounges, according to whether you're flying Latam or another codeshare carrier, these lounges are very good. The Latam customer lounge (Premium) is bigger and better but all have plenty of seating, good food choices which are kept refreshed regularly, good drink choices and fast free wi-fi. They have beds (reserve on arrival) and showers. The only negative is that there is no view or windows these days.

It look to me that it was new. Big lounge, with a lot of space, cosy, adequate temperature, quiet. I visited in the morning at breakfast time. There was fresh orange juice, all types of coffee, two types of hot dishes, and a variety of ham and cheese, cereals, dairies. High speed internet, plenty of staff attending guests. The quality of the food was average.

Their lounge is very disappointing. Firstly, it is hidden: there are no signs for it, not even a tiny one at the lifts you have to use to get up to it. The staff are rude and tend to ignore you. The bathrooms are shabby, in need of maintenance and not very clean. The hot water pressure is good, so you can have a good shower, except that the drains are faulty so the water builds up around your feet. The seating is getting rather grubby. The food is appalling. No hot meals, nothing more than preprepared small ham and cheese portions, with or without a small roll. We went out for a hamburger rather than face this. The wine is ok, and there is bottled water. The wifi is extremely patchy- sometimes good, sometimes awful. Certainly not what you’d expect for the Business Class lounge at their main hub.

Big and odd lounge. No food, just some lousy sandwiches. No hot food. No drinks, just still and sparkling water. This is a full OneWorld member and it is a shame that they call this VIP Lounge! I have traveled all over the world with this alliance and nothing compares to this. Miserable and poor. When I asked why the lounge is like that, the answer was even non sensed: "Because this is how it is".

This is a fantastic lounge. Great selection of food and beverages. High comfort with a sleeping area and around 10 fantastic shower facilities. Great crew who are really helpfully. As a economy passenger of LATAM, I have paid my access to this lounge. It is it worth for the money!

Excellent atmosphere, very friendly staff, very attentive willing to cooperate with the necessary information in the case of delayed flights. The service of food and drinks is also very good, the seats and the rooms very well lit with very good signal of internet

This review goes beyond the lounge. When you arrive at Santiago airport all check-in counters are based on level 2 (the usual airport layout), however Latem has created within level 3 an exclusive check-in section for all business, premium economy and high level Oneworld Frequent flyer members. When we checked into the newly established direct flight to Melbourne there was no queue and check-in took no more than 2-3 minutes. Directly next to the premium check-in area is a dedicated passport and security point, meaning you are all done within 5 minutes. The lounge connects to the security point or you take a lift down back to level 2 for some duty free retail therapy. The lounge was massive, spreading over 2 levels. Both levels offer the same hospitality. I did like it upstairs more as it provided a much better view across the airport gates and has an entertainment room ideal for parking some kids in front of a movie. There is a lot of choice for seating from cool park style benches to luxuries leather lounge chairs. Wifi works really well and was easy to connect. The lounge has a modern, sophisticated feel and has a unique, edgy design. Food on offer was also quite nice, without going completely over the top. Overall a good selection of food and beverage for you to select from.

This LATAM lounge is not a First Class lounge but rather at best a mediocre Business Class/frequent flyer lounge for a dozen or so airlines. We checked in at First Class counter Swiss and were escorted through TSA to the lounge.  The escalator area and entry desk aspects look good but are misleading as they lead to an, overcrowded lounge with old and uncomfortable furniture, insufficient lighting and worn/dirty carpets. Considering one gets forced to check in at least two hours before boarding this substandard arrangement is deplorable and accounts for 25% of flight time. Considering that during the subsequent flight one sleeps at least half the time one pays too a high premium for the first class fare. This should be a problem for all the first class passengers of some of the other premium airlines that use the Miami Latam lounge for long haul flights and I wonder why the have not joined to remedy this deplorable situation. Please note however that the food, service and amenities on the subsequent Swiss flight were truly first class as is their lounge in Zürich.

I have used this LATAM lounge four times on two return flights to South America via GRU. This lounge is surprisingly new, large and very well-designed – they’re obviously spent a lot of money on it. It is split into different areas – one for the bar, one for dining, a TV area, a sleeping room and several others with armchairs and power sockets for working. It is bright, airy and quiet. A Wi-Fi code is presented to you on entry to the lounge and it is a strong signal. The large shower rooms equipped with toiletries, shaving equipment and hair dryers are immaculately kept. The food area has a range of hot dishes and snacks, along with cold dishes and range of rolls and sandwiches. The menu also changes at different points throughout the day, and the staff keep it extremely clean. The self-service bar is also very extensive. In my opinion, it is much better than most of the business lounges in Europe and it looks like LATAM is upping its game in premium travel facilities.

Used this lounge as a Qatar Airways customer. We know Phnom Penh very well so we knew not to expect too much. Including ourselves there were only 5 people in the lounge. Friendly staff, very quiet, clean toilets. However there were no spirits, but only 2 bottles of good French wine and no wine glasses. There was a selection of soft drinks and cans of Anchor beer. There were a few sandwiches, warm pastries and small cakes. We were Qatar Business Class travellers so we had complimentary access. We would not pay to go into the lounge. It has potential but we were surprised at the lack of hospitality.

The Pearl Lounge was huge and well maintained. The food options were good but I wish they had lunch options as well - they used to offer lunch options in the morning as well back in the old Airport Lounge. The staff were excellent and the lady who was serving at the middle section pictures was super friendly, attentive and professional. The toilets were clean and well attended but I did not appreciate the dim lighting.

Due to the Pandemic, the lounge was eerily quiet with just a handful of passengers waiting for the first flight out of Bahrain. I was expecting rigorous health checks, and so was equipped with face mask and gloves. But the procedure was smooth and quick via the separate entrance for business class passengers. Once in the lounge, nothing seemed to have changed. There was a modest selection of hot food, but plenty of finger food and soft drinks. The bar area had a small selection of premium brands, wines and coffee. The staff as usual were very quick to clear up leftovers at clean the table areas. I have been to this lounge before, and really like the variety of seating and furnishings it offers - from round table seating for groups, single sating in rather private areas, to family rooms. Anyway, as I had to arrived a good three hours before, it was a rather uneventful and long quiet times, consuming too much food and coffee, before my flight to London.

I had visited this lounge before, and looked forward to the early morning time to spend before my flight. Upon entering, I was welcomed and addressed by name. The staff serving were both friendly and as I had difficulty getting WiFi connected, were helpful. The food department had improved since my last visit, and I was able to have a hot breakfast. There was also a good selection of cold items on display. It was self service for soft drinks, while alcohol and coffee was served at the bar, or brought to where you were seated. Although not large, I particularly like the layout, with seating offering some privacy and the more open seating around the bar and dining areas. Very clean, comfortable, quiet, excellent views of planes landing in the distant, and my 787 aircraft to Bahrain parked right opposite. A pleasant experience.

The lounge is a new addition to Calicut Airport and much needed. The airport has gone through renovation and there are a lot of changes made. The lounge is quite small but nicely decorated. The A/C was too low and after a while it started getting quite warm. They do not have an Alcohol license so don't expect any alcohol. They do not have bathrooms inside the lounge so you will have to go to the one in the Airport itself. Selection of food is limited and tasted just ok. They could do better with more continental items on their menu. The staff are friendly.

The Falcon Gold Lounge was the highlight of the trip and compared to the Business Class flight, I preferred the lounge to the flight experience. It was Ramadan and they did not serve alcohol until after 7pm which was fine. The food was good and had a decent selection. The staff were very friendly and served me refreshments where I was seated. The chairs are comfortable and there are charging ports in each seat. The bathrooms are very clean and well maintained and the atmosphere is quite and relaxing.

I had already checked out info on this lounge and had high expectations. Sadly I was disappointed. It's very spacious and quiet enough, and on two levels, with First Class passengers access to the upper level. However, I was permitted to enter it, but hardly noticed any difference, except for more space and better views of aircraft at air jetties. Yet everything looked so ordinary, gloomy, with no effort to have any mood lighting or really comfortable furniture. The few staff seemed uninterested, and more occupied chatting amongst themselves. The washrooms were so bare, more like public toilets, and did not appear clean. The seating also seemed rather old and a little tatty. Crumbs on the carpets looked like they've been there a long time. I was there at breakfast time, so cannot comment if the food menu changed for lunch. The breakfast food was adequate, with a small bar area and plenty of soft drinks, but nothing really appetising or exotic. I guess as I had two hours to spend here found it rather boring and uninteresting. Its advertising suggests pure luxury, but I think it needs a tiny miracle to compete with the likes of high-end lounges.

Business Class passengers a have a separate entrance for check in, security and passport checks. And once through, you are back onto the normal departure lounge areas, and the Falcon Gold Lounge is a short walk. There is plenty of space, a variety of comfortable furnishings, very clean, quiet areas, and Wi Fi worked well. There is an excellent view of planes taking off and landing, and not too far away. I had arrived early and had a good two hours before my flight to Bangkok. I helped myself to the bar, although a limited stock. What disappointed me a little was the lack of variety of food. Rather a small selection of bland hot food, and the sandwiches selection was dry and unappetising. The staff were very attentive and cleared up tables after meals. they were happy to serve tea and coffee at your table. I did not indulge in too much eating. The lounge has a family room, a nice children's play section, plus a X-Box games room. On my return flight from Bangkok, I was able to freshen up with a shower, and you pick up your towels and toiletries in basket at the reception. All in all, nothing unique about this lounge, but nothing to complain about it either.

A small lounge that serves several other Middle Eastern carriers. It's perfectly located without having to walk miles to get there, with views of take offs in the distance and up close to air jetties - 777 jet noses feel like within touching distance. The staff were extremely hospitable and welcoming. In the centre of the lounge is the bar with the usual wine and spirits (with some premium brands) and teas and coffees as well as Arabic Coffee, all served upon request. As I arrived for a morning flight, the food area was mainly breakfast items. The selection was modest. I was rather disappointed as it catered mainly for western cuisine and I was looking forward to more Middle Eastern specialities. However, for a one hour spend, it was perfectly adequate. The lounge is extremely clean and comfortably furnished and laid out with some privacy in mind. I enjoyed my time here, and short walk to the aircraft.

A welcoming atmosphere, perfect temperature, relaxing background music and smiling staff in reception. Cold, hot drinks, snacks and refreshments. The lounge is not very big, but it is enough for the size of Bahrain Airport.

Highly recommend Gulf Air's Lounge in London Heathrow T4. Have visited the lounge countless times and is better than the one in Bahrain, although its not as big. In mid 2015, they have also changed the catering provider, and have noticed the food quality and variety to be excellent ever since. The lounge is big relative to the 2 daily flights from Heathrow, and have always found space to sit on every occasion. The service is really good, and the tables and seats are cleared shortly after the guests leave making the lounge clean. There is also a prayer room, and showers facility.

This is my home airport, and I travel via Gulf Air as a 1st choice when there is a direct route, so I have visited this lounge many times. The lounge is spacious with various seating areas, including an area for families and a sleeping area. At times the lounge gets really busy and if your traveling with a Family as most of the seating areas are tables for 2. The food is average, when compared to the Gulf Air lounge in heathrow!

I like the layout of this Gulf Air lounge with different areas for kids, business and some big couches to lie down on (though there are only a few of these). The food selection was ok but a little limited, however the service and beverage selection was excellent. The toilets and showers were clean and the shower pack was well stocked with a towel, shampoo, a brush, shaving kit etc. We had a few hours to waste while waiting for a 3am flight and I had hoped to nap a little but the lights were a little too bright and the seats a little too upright for that especially as the big couches were all taken. There is a special sleeping area but you have to pay to access it.

Expensive is the first thing that comes to mind if you are not a member of Gulf Air's Golden Falcon FF program. The lounge charges access in chunks of 3 hours each and when you have a 7.5 and a 10 hour layover as I did that adds up. Sleeper seats at one end of the lounge but the lights have been positioned so as to shine directly into one's eyes and Gulf Air has to discover the concept of eye shades whether on their aircraft or here. The lounge does provide blankets and there is also a shower available to freshen up. While you will be told at check in that flights are not called the reverse is true - some flights are called (very disturbing to sleep when there are no earplugs available!) on a very odd seemingly random basis. The desk staff is obliging while service staff in the lounge tries to be unobtrusive but fails miserably clattering dishes and glassware making a lot of noise when replenishing food and drink etc.

The Gulf Air lounge allows a 'pay per visit' for any traveller. I needed good wi-fi and some good breakfast. I paid £GBP35 each for the two of us. Very friendly staff and club lounge was immaculate with fast wi-fi. However at about 10.00am the remains of what was breakfast was cold and congealed at the self service food bar. I asked in the form of a complaint about the state of the breakfast bar. I was offered a fresh coffee (very good) by one of the girls and told that when the chef returned from his break that he would prepare us some breakfast. This he did. We were offered a plain omelette or some 'fresh' frittata. We opted for the frittata. Two small slices each with no accompaniment. Very disappointing and not worth the money we had paid. Even with the wi-fi and a total of 4 coffees GBP70 was a lot to pay. Will not be going there again.

A nice little lounge located next to gate 7 in Terminal 4. Greeting was friendly and professional. Great views over the southern runway and the stands outside. Food and drink selection was very good but cannot quite compete with the Qatar Airways lounge. Small terminals with movies and series placed at most tables for entertainment. 3 Mac terminals with internet access if you have forgotten your computer and WiFi is available in the lounge as well. Very nice restrooms with showers if required.

Situated overlooking the tarmac the lounge is large and airy with an adjoining self service food area. The central bar has a full selection of drinks including fizz. Full selection of newspapers WiFi and smart toilets and showers. Loads of seats including a section overlooking the aircraft. Because of T4 layout it is still a 5-8 minute walk to your gate even though you can see it from the lounge. Ours was a morning visit and there was a wide selection of hot breakfast food on offer. Well staffed this is a good lounge.

Impressed by spacious and modern lounge in Bahrain airport. The seats were comfortable and able to get a view airside so we could watch the planes coming and going. The food was quite tasty and there was a reasonable selection.

Used this lounge travelling with SriLankan Airlines. Very nice lounge which was refurbished and of good quality. Good selection of food and drinks. Staff were attentive. Showers were locked even though nobody using them not sure if this was because we were not Gulf air passengers. Toilets were clean. Wifi and computers available and seating including some comfortable chairs sofas and quiet rooms.

Clean bright lounge with a nice relaxing ambience with good food and nice selection of drinks. Great to use clean toilets and the staff very pleasant to talk and interact with. Internet was good as was the Wi-Fi. Gets a little crowded at night time though.

Excellent seating variety (it's possible to order a quiet room at an extra cost of 30 BHD). There's a good variety of hot food. It has a good selection of drinks and a espresso machine. Armchair equipped with a portable screen to watch a selection of movies. There's a family room with toys and a separate one for children and teens with XBOX stations. Free WI-FI. Clean toilets and courteous staff.

What a contrast to their own lounge in Bahrain was fantastic on the outbound. They use a Service lounge used by number of airlines dark gloomy depressing. wireless involved sending your personal details and then a text to some number and after 9 tries never worked. Gave up in the end no alcoholic beverages at all. Some hot food but looked like it had been deep fried to its death and was verging on carbon. Staff smiling which is the great thing about Indian people always helpful and courteous. My Advice don't get to the airport to early and save hanging out in this lounge.
Very comfortable with good selection of food and drink. Overlooking runway all down main side of lounge.
Excellent lounge overlooking the departure gate. Very welcoming with good selection of food and drink and a good variety of seating options. Nice bathrooms. Friendly staff and good service.

Plenty of space and comfortable seating on the evening I was there. The choice of quality foods impressed me. Staff attentive and offer to serve at your seat. Internet available to use and plenty of terminals available. Shower and bathroom amenities clean and available.

Comfortable lounge with darkened sleeping area at one end. Selection of food limited but tasty. Not self-service. You choose what you want and it is prepared and brought to you.Staff only too pleased to do whatever they can for you. Reasonable selection of drinks. Internet available in 30 minute blocks (but I went back for several without a problem). Ejected at 2330 hrs as final Airport Security check closes shortly after this.

A wonderful haven of peace and quiet. Helpful staff opened early to accomodate us as flight in was very late. Plenty of space wide selection of food and drink. Very good showers with nice towels provided

This is a haven of peace at T3 and certainly one of the best lounges at Heathrow. Although small it has a calm feeling and has full facilities including full bar with good fizz and tasty snacks. Full internet for those who need to work or perhaps relax under the drapes awaiting your call to board. Gulf will lay on a buggy on request and also you are encouraged not to go to the gate until called from the lounge so you can board last. Look forward to trying the 5* lounge at BAH and the soon to be refurbished Gulf lounge at MCT

GF lounge at BAH is the best I have encountered. From being met at the reception desk by the most courteous staff to being escorted to your gate if requested by the most profesional staff it is a truly enjoyable experience. Computers free wifi a huge choice of food from hot snacks to sandwiches drinks from the finest champagne to sodas. Staff will also pack you a lunch box for a long haul flight if requested - in this lounge you dont have to ask for anything as everything is offered. The lounge has an Arabian theme which is very comfortable. People often wonder what they are paying for with business and first class prices apart from the wonderful service offered on their flights this 5* star treatment in the lounge would put alot of 5* hotels to shame.
Brand new lounge, a great experience. Latest vibe, high quality food and drinks. Finally it seems that KE invests in their customers comfort now they can do the same for their old fleet
Lounge offers a variety of foods and drinks, but rather small and often packed. But it is adapted to the airport and my guess most of the time it is not so crowded. The lounge is very clean

The lounge was not only served KAL passengers, but also some other Syteam members'. It was located near Gate 28 in the main concourse, so if you are departing from the satellite, please board the shuttle train after using the lounge. It was quite a big one with great view, and had a lot of natural light. Food and beverage was good. We liked the Korean ramen, chicken and the beer. Shower needed to be reserved and wait about 30 minutes. In overall, it was a nice place to relax before continuing the journey.

The Royal Lounge operated by Hokkaido Airports was located right above my flight's boarding gate and duty free shopping. It was such a hidden gem, not only because of its super cleanliness but also the beautiful interiors. There were massage chairs, private meeting room. Food was amazingly cooked and prepared. Really loved the hot ramen here. Absolutely one of the best airline lounge in Japan!
The lounge at International terminal was located almost at the end of the terminal was clean but quite small with limited selection of food and beverages. Staff was friendly and nice.
The lounge at International terminal was located almost at the end of the terminal was clean but quite small with limited selection of food and beverages. Staff was friendly and nice.

The new Korean Air lounge at terminal 2 was very different from the previous lounges. I thought it had become smaller and probably it did. However, there were extra features such as sleeping area and independent rooms for families. The main area of the lounge seemed cleaner than before, but the seats were less comfortable. The food was good. However, it had too many people creating seat shortages.

The lounge is good in general, clean with staff walking around to ensure cleanliness. It is packed! I could barely find a seat and wonder if they need to increase the space. Food ran out. While there is a variety of other food available, I would've expected them to replenish quickly. Unfortunately, I did not see that happen.

Flying China Southern from Los Angeles I used the Korean Air lounge, shared by all airlines of the Skyteam alliance. Probably one of the worst lounges I have been to! Dirty, worn and old, no hot meals, wine selection very basic, I think three different bottles of liquor, just ridiculous! Doubt I will ever fly Korean Air if that is the image they show potential customers.

Korean Air lounges both for business and first class are really subpar and very low quality compared to their on board product. It as seems the lounge is just to meet the minimum standard and the lowest point for the experience when flying both business and first class. The food and drink options are very minimal and unappetizing. The hub lounge, which is a paid lounge across from the business class lounge has much better foods and drinks selections with better quality and taste.

I used this Korean Air lounge when travelling with Etihad Airways. I found the lounge to be quite large but with a minimal food offering. I did appreciate the availability of a shower and toilet (both clean) within the lounge itself. The lighting in the lounge was fairly dim but you get accustomed to it after a while. Still, helpful during night flights after 9pm when 90% of the stores are closed.

This lounge is a disgrace for Korean Air's home base at Seoul Incheon. The crowded spaces, terrible food and drink selection. I wish the airline's executives would spend some time in SQ's or Cathay's respective lounges in Changi and HK. There is nothing to recommend a visit, especially as there is free fast wifi in the airport and quiet lounge areas to be found upstairs. After visiting this lounge over the last 7 or so years, nothing has changed.

The Korean Air Lounge at LAX was a welcome haven from the crowds below in the main terminal, however the seats are filthy!! At least 30% of the seating in the lounge is a cream or off white colour which show the dirt that has accumulated from passengers clothing over god knows how long. When we arrived we avoided these chairs and sat on the ones with darker material but suspect that they would not have been any cleaner. The food was average but the bathrooms were clean.

I was pleasantly surprised The lounge, which is near Gate 11 and split into two roughly equal sized lounges either side of receptions and the unisex showers and toilet facility. The services and amenities in both rooms is broadly similar. The lounge in the main building was much better small cubicles or lounge areas a small selection of hit foods and whilst we were there, cleaned regularly. A limited selection of alcoholic drinks although that does seem to be a characteristic of the Korean Air brand on the ground and in the air. It should be noted that the KAL lounge in the satellite is quite spartan with limited range of drinks and almost no hot food although there are good showers.

There are two Skyteam lounges at ICN one on the main concourse and one in the satellite. Be aware that if you get on the shuttle to the satellite you can't get back from there. This report refers to the lounge in the satellite.  The selection of food was limited to a few cold and unappetising options and some "pot noodle" when we arrived early afternoon. The selection was extended late afternoon to include 4 hot options. Drink selection was limited 2 spirits, 2 beers and 3 wines with the usual soft drinks. The showers were clean and no waiting for them. The general cleanliness was ok but the lounge wasn't busy. Wifi was reasonably fast and there was a decent number of places to charge phones tablets etc. Was it the worst lounge I've ever been in? No, but it was a long way from the best. A better drink and food selection could turn this into an acceptable lounge but there's a way to go yet.

We used this Korean Air lounge as travelling economy class on Air New Zealand and we have a Natwest issued Priority pass. This lounge is large and very stark, the seats are in poor condition, the cream coloured ones are stained. The lounge has very basic food and beverages. This would put me off flying with Sky Team airlines if this is an example of their product.

The CIP lounge that Korean Air use at Siem Reap is very poor. Accommodates only few international flights. The staff were friendly and helpful but could not compensate for the shortcomings. Low standard washroom. Patchy connectivity for wifi. Food selection poor, drink selection a bit better. Luckily you do not visit the area for the airport lounge.

Have used this lounge approximately 10 times in the last year. The lounge is very big and viewing the tarmac is easy and pleasurable. The washrooms and shower facilities are good. The wifi connectivity and speed are among the best I have encountered. The food is shocking. The same dishes, frequently un-replenished. A couple of questionable salads, a couple of 'hot' dishes and pot noodles. Every time the same so can confidently say not to expect much. Breakfast time is the worse of all. The coffee is average and soft drinks and beer are self serve, while the water comes in pouches! It can get really crowded, and it could be much much cleaner. The secondary lounge (visited as Vietnam Airlines passenger) is one of the worst I have even been to. You are better off eating in a fast food, and probably more comfortable too. Again, wifi and showers are excellent. Cleanliness is average and food availability is the biggest problem, before we even consider variety and quality.

We expected a decent lounge in Seoul. It is shared with 19 other airlines and it would be the worst airline lounge I have ever been to. It was dirty, tables had coffee markes and stains. Two minuite noodles, water in a plastic pull back container. One bad white and red wine and two whiskies and one brandy, not even basic spirits. The selection of the few bits of food were most unappealing and tastless food. We will not be choosing Korean Air again and looking at the other comments I think they need to smarten up their act, certainly not Business Class Lounge criteria.
One of the worst lounges I have ever been to. Even the ones at Heathrow that you can pay for which the airlines do not provide are much better than this one.

Probably one of the dirtiest lounges I have ever visited: stained carpet greasy windows. The choice of food is very limited and of industrial quality. Choice of alcohol is minimal. On the upside nice view on the runway and fast wifi.

To say we were disappointed and underwhelmed with this lounge is an understatment. Incheon is a huge airport and so the lounge is necessarily huge too although it is cleverly set up is two areas separated by the lift shafts toilets etc. Comfortable chairs everywhere but largely lined up as if in a waiting room. Fantastic views from massive glass onto the tarmac apron. The catering was astonishing in its pausity. One unrermakable red and one unknown (and don't care too) white no bubbles of any sort a couple of self-serve draft beers water came in juice pouch things reminiscent of 1990s economy class meal trays. There was a non-descript pumpkin soup without bread a couple of unappetising salads a couple of pot noodle things (self-serve) a couple of juices and thats about your lot. Empty glasses and plates hung around for a long time including a beer mug on a table that was there when we wrrived and was still there when we left 2 hours later. Toilets were roomy and clean a must-visit to have a play with the electric flush bidet and warm air arrangement. Wifi free without the need of a password and was quick enough for the few emails and bit of browning I did. Will be transiting through Incheon in a couple of weeks on way home but don't think we'll bother going to this lounge at all.

Large lounge with a variety of seating options and a nice view of the tarmac. I visited on two occasions late at night and early in the morning. Food options at that time were limited with only a few eastern and western choices which were hard to assemble into a coherent dinner or breakfast. Wine and spirits were available at both times. Only prepacked cups of water were available - bottles of water would be better. The shower facilities were clean and spacious but there was a 20 minute wait for a shower early in the morning despite the lounge not being full. Overall a satisfactory space though not exceptional.

Used this lounge as Aeroflot passenger. It was dirty and crowded. There was no food accept for few crackers and some cheese. Plenty of soft drinks that were restocked fast. The communication between the plane and the lounge was terrible. We were asked to proceed to boarding and the plane was nowhere near ready! The receptionist was very clueless. We ended up waiting in line in front of the gate for 30 min Overall a pretty depressing experience.

After a six hour flight from Singapore to Incheon in Prestige Class we attempted to use the Prestige Lounge to freshen up before our 8 hour layover. We were denied access stating that it was against policy. I spoke with a very polite supervisor who could not understand why we would want to use their lounge if we were not continuing on with them. When I explained that KE does not fly to San Antonio they could not care less. Thankfully AA has a contract with Asiana where the first class lounge was clean comfortable and well equipped. Next time I want to spend US$5000 between ICN and SIN you can be sure I will remember and inform KE that it is not in "my policy" to waste money on a carrier who only cares about you until you cross the airplane threshold.

I cannot follow to my former writers who recommended this Lounge. No choice of food no bottles of water or coke just glasses. Crowded! Impossible from KE to allocate this Lounge for full paying Business-Guests.

There are two KE business class lounges at ICN. The larger and more plush lounge is located in the passenger terminal immediately past security. Both lounge areas have the same food and drinks but the one on the right is usually less crowded. The food is simple but more substantial than in most US airline lounges wine and liquor selections adequate. The shower facilities are located adjacent to this section of the lounge - clean and everything you need to refresh. The other lounge is on the concourse that serves foreign carriers like Delta and Skyteam flights. This lounge is smaller and is generally more stark and less comfortable. The food and drinks are the same. There are several smaller rooms at the back of the lounge that have TVs and comfortable seating. They are usually empty or have only one or two other passengers. English channels are available for catching up on current events. Neither lounge can issue boarding passes or change seats.

I had a guest pass before by ICN-BKK flight and arrived with around 6 hours to spend in the lounge. Most travelers go to the left from the desk and that side of the lounge is full of people. If you pass the showers on the right there is an area with the same food and beverage offerings but less people. I was there all day the food stayed the same - standard hotel buffet. Nothing super special but filling. The bar was self serve beer wine whisky scotch and Jack Daniels. My only complaint was the smoking room. I know most airports do not have this but in Korea they are extremely necessary. Many Koreans smoke and the tiny closet sized room was continually full to the point of no room to move. The bathrooms were a little dirty upon arrival but were cleaned after I left it.

I was somewhat disappointed in the facilities of the business class lounge at Hong Kong airport. Was waiting to board A380 to Seoul but it was very bland lots of seats and a desk for internet. Food selection not interesting and attendant less than friendly. They really need to upgrade this lounge. Doesn't encourage one to think of Korean Air as a possibility for long haul flights.

lounge_name: KOREAN AIR BUSINESS CLASS LOUNGE REVIEW
review: KAL Business (Prestige) lounge at Incheon Airport is far too small for the numbers of passengers using it. I passed through this lounge twice in a period of four weeks and it was very crowded both times. It is showing it age and is desperately in need of a face lift and a substantial increase in size. The food on offer was poor a couple of hot Korean dishes cheese nuts cakes and biscuits. Drinks were ok but not exciting. The shower rooms were good and kept very clean. The desk staff were not particularly friendly and would not even look at a request for a seat change on my next flight. No boarding calls made but I quite like that is it helps keep the noise level down monitor screens around the lounge enable passengers to see what is happening with their flight.

This has to be the poorest Business Class (Prestige Class) lounge I have ever been in. It is too small and has no ambience at all. The food and drink selection was virtually non existant a few cakes and biscuits plus tea and coffee and a few cold drinks were all that was on offer and this was around noon waiting to board the A380 to Incheon. I didn't use the showers so I cannot comment on the quality or condition. The desk staff were ok and the cleaning staff did a good job of clearing up.

This is really a very disappointing and bad experience. Basically the lounge has nothing to offer and can not be regarded as an intercontinental business class lounge. There is only one lounge worse than the intercontinental KAL lounge in Incheon; it is the intercontinental KAL lounge at JFK for the return flight on the A380. It smells of old tobacco the sofas are old and worn out. The choice of drinks and food is miserable the coffee is disgusting so are the muffins the rest offered is plastic cheese and some plastic sandwiches. Truly a disappointing experience!

Sofas are very comfortable. Complimentary wifi food delicious but would be better if there were more choices. Same applies to beverages too. Newspapers available but only the ones printed in Korea Japan or China. No British American French or German newspapers available. Great view of tarmac from the lounge. Lounge is secluded from the public area so is very quiet. Very clean and nice toilets.

Actually a very poor experience. The lounge itself was fair comfortable seating an ample drinks selection. If one wanted a hot drink one was confronted with a dispenser only labelled in Japanese/Korean staff quite unwilling to help. As there was no catering (only rice crackers and savoury crackers) for this just-after-lunchtime departure. This added to an unsatisfactory experience mostly on the account of the rude and unhelpful staff. I do not consider it a problem to have a limited command of English in a non-english speaking country and working in a mostly non-english speaking place but it is very problematic to combine this with such a rude attitude.

A very pleasant experience and a good start for an overnight trip to Seoul. Lounge is on the way from check-in to gate. Very relaxed and spacious no outside windows. Drinks are made to order. Choice is a bit limited perhaps but the lounge staff are kind and enthusiastic. No meal service only peanuts crisps and the like. Each passenger was personally informed about when it was time to board.

It's ok but not grand. Food selection limited. Beverages are good. Bathrooms are outside of lounge. Internet has always been very difficult when I come here. This time I was told to use Northwest connection which they said is better (and no password setup). They were right.

Large lounge situated upstairs clearly signposted. Comfortable seating. Excellent food and drink - a wide range food changing according to hour. Obliging staff. Shower room I used was fine - large well-stocked. No internet terminals but several hook-up points and I the entire lounge wifi for those equipped with laptops. Magazine and newspaper provision a rather limited. No flights calls but several departure screens available.

Very large business class concept lounge. Many seats in Asian fashion. Very dark minimal lighting overlooking runway. Small central food area with packaged cakes and cookies available various assortments of pot of noodles (the type where you add your own hot water). Small bar area with light beverages available coffee and tea - only three available alcoholic beverages ; Vodka Baileys and Red Wine. Large internet section about 12 computers available. Small smoking room in the corner with door standing room only. Not a very comfortable lounge. Its run by Air China and serves multiple airlines in comparison with the other lounges available in that airport this one is probably the most tatty and messy looking. Carpet and upholstery on seats looked stained not a clean look.

Very clinical looking lounge. However lots of space clean staff friendly. Used by a few airlines in the SkyTeam network. Lots of food available - from sandwiches to sushi to Chocolate Cake. Open bar and coffee machines. Not sure of internet area.

Nice big lounge at Incheon airport solely for the use of Prestige Class Passengers. Took a while to find it though as no clear direction. Comfortable seating a little bit clinical rather than homely feel. Staff Friendly only breakfast cereals and breads on offer at the time I was there  however still had a full bar service. Did not see any computers for internet browsing. Had a small smoking room which was comfortable with Plasma TV and away from the non smoking section.

Nice lounge on the Upper floor. Spacious when I used it. Seating comfortable in groups of 4 chairs but a bit boring in layout - nice views out across runway etc. Staff very polite and obliging and will bring you drink or food to your table. Selection of foods a bit limited and would expect more in a nice F class lounge - drinks etc okay though. Shower rooms and relaxing area but found to be rather basic and short on normal F class lounge amenities. No boarding calls and staff do not check which passenger on what flight so had a real rush to boarding gate in the end.

Very small lounge with no daylight no washrooms etc and full at time of use. Korean need to get something much better and bigger as this was horrid - the main T3 is better and more comfortable and that is Heathrow we are talking about. No proper selection of foods apart from nuts and crackers no internet or wireless and seating is cramped as they try to squash as many people in as possible. Nice staff who are polite and welcoming but otherwise this is a really poor standard of lounge.
The lounge is nice, spacious, and de facto world class. Separate areas, good, varied food options, changing over the day and night. Well assorted bar, sleepers, smoking room, proactive staff.

The food at the lounge was inedible and sparse, of the 7-8 food items they had none was edible. I had to go out and eat at one of the restaurants at the terminal.  The sleeping zones were loud and no pillows or blankets were provided. The service and food at the normal credit card lounges is a million times better than this so called business class lounge

Although I am furious with Kenya Airways right now I will acknowledge that they are trying to improve their lounge service. There is a cook making eggs and omelettes as requested and their cappuccino is excellent. Food rather boring and minimal but a relatively good range of drinks. Wifi is good.

3rd party lounge used by Kenya Airways. Lounge is still good, food is improving, more hot dishes, and more hot savory snacks. Drinks options sparse, but there are good stocks. Lacks windows terribly. No music.

Very disappointing. Tiny for a Business Lounge with too many tables and chairs crammed in. Little choice in the cold buffet with each plate clingfilmed so you first had to unseal the clingfilm, take what you wanted and then reseal the clingfilm. Surely rigid covers which could be lifted off and then replaced would make things much easier? The also limited choice of hot food looked like it had been sat there for hours. Kenya Airways now use this lounge while most others use the vastly better Dzimbahwe Executive Lounge. I shall avoid flying Kenya Airways on a Harare route in future so I don't have to visit this lounge again.

The lounge consisted of a few chairs and tables and a food counter. The only drinks available apart from tea or coffee were cartons of warm orange juice. There was also a half-empty bowl of crisps and two wrapped sandwiches. Although the main waiting area was more manic it at least had two food shops and after a while several passengers in the lounge decided it was better to wait there. If airlines are expecting business passengers to pay a significant premium they should at least offer the basics of what one might expect in a lounge – a selection of food and drink, magazines and a flight display board.

3rd party lounge of world class quality. I paid entrance and got the best and most delicious hot food available. Spacious. Extremely clean. Toilets so clean I feared to use them. Nice large smoking room with views and soft chairs. Huge and varied drink offers especially all sorts of South African wines and beers. Very good internet. Quiet area for sleeping. I will come again.

Excellent Lounge operated by Bidvest Premier Lounge, in my view world class and not expensive to access if pay by cash. Cleanest toilets, smokers section perfect. Good views of tarmac. Sleeping section. No champagnes or a la carte, but perfect RSA-sparkling wines and a huge, beautiful arranged and well stocked buffet beats any a la carte service. Compared to nearby Aspire lounge, it 2 steps up, despite Aspire is also good.

The third party Bidwest Lounge of world class quality. I paid entrance and got the best and most delicious hot food. Spacious. Extremely clean. Toilets so clean I feared to use them. Nice large smoking room with views and soft chairs. Huge and varied drink offers especially all sorts of South African wines and beers. Very good internet. Quiet area for sleeping. I will come again.

I was disappointed with Kenya Airways lounge in Nairobi since this was the home city of the airline. It is very large with five separate rooms; three lounge areas with televisions, a dining room and a quiet communal sleep room. The lobby and first lounge are modern, the rest of the rooms were very drab. The presentation of the food in the dining area is not very appealing and the hot & cold food selection was very basic. They did have very good fresh juices and draft soda drinks. The beer, wine and alcohol selection was minimal. The WiFi was fast and consistent.

In Nairobi I had to spent the night due to missed connection causing a downgrade to economy class. However, fortunately they granted me lounge access due to all the trouble that I have had. The  lounge has food, views, and nice architecture with curving designs and view of tarmac. I love the pulse and dynamics of this lounge with its many sections with different themes. Food is good and drinks are fine and plenty. It has 6 beds in silent area and I slept well till next morning.
Nice atmosphere, very clean but very bad quality of food. The worst croissant i have seen in my life. Almost half of the buffet was empty. Very disappointed and bad image for our destination.

Spacious lounge with good views of the aircraft. Limited food however, mostly snacks. The spring rolls weren't very nice, but the beef samosas were good. Making tea/coffee was hard as you couldn't get your own hot water (they had a very complicated machine) so I had to wait for staff to operate it for me. Something as simple as a kettle or hot water dispenser would've been much more functional. Otherwise, staff were extremely friendly and helpful.

I had not visited the lounge for some time so was glad to stop over, relax and get something to eat before my flight to Kisumu. It was quiet, relaxing and had variety of bites and drinks (hot and cold, alcoholic and non-alcoholic). Kenya Airways hospitality at its best.

Large lounge with plenty of different rooms (eating corner, relax, etc.), relatively comfortable, totally sterile atmosphere. Food-wise and drink-wise, one of the worst lounges, with a miserable selection. Coffee is good, but you have to queue, as the coffee machine is under supervision of a dedicated person.

Stopped here for 4 hrs between international flights. Pleasantly surprised with the relaxed atmosphere of this Kenya Airways lounge. The lounge is on the 2nd floor accessed by elevator from near Gate 17. From the concierge area, you enter the lounge into a private quiet area with nice comfortable lounge chairs, a newspaper stand, a selection of books, and an array of tablets line up on a bench. Then further along is another seating area with tables and comfortable chairs for meeting and chatting, then the dining area. In the dining area, where I spent most of my time, tables are spaced apart for privacy and there is a large screen TV showing news channels with the volume turned down. There are benches stretching along the window in a semi-circle. There was a good selection of food to choose from, including roast chicken, beef stroganoff, mixed vegetables, and a selection of white or red wine, and Tusker beer. Very clean bathrooms. There is a shower area too. As I was not a business class traveller but had a Skyteam elite card I paid $40 for the privilege which I felt was worth the money.

The opening of the new Terminal area includes the new Simba and Pride Lounges (I saw both). The new lounges are world class with great food and beverage options (excellent wines) WIFI varied seating areas including quiet business & TV lounge areas and shower rooms. These lounges are a wonderful refuge before a long flight and service was excellent! This was a huge change from previous years flights from NBO.

While the Sasco-lounge is being one of the most expensive agent-lounges worldwide, it's also one of the worst lounges I ever have been to: usually messy and overcrowded with no left seating abilities, stained tables, trash not being removed quickly. Not even standard beer-brands are offered but just the cheapest Vietnamese beer in the market. The same is true for the wine-selection. In addition, in terms of spirits, all whats available is the cheapest Hanoi-vodka, Ballantines, Gibson's Gin and Captain Morgan Rum. The selection of soft-drinks is poor, as well, not even offering Tonic Water for a Gin&Tonic. While food-selection looks impressive, it lacks taste and texture. The 'signature-dish', the local Vietnamese soup 'Pho' does not reflect at all the rich taste and flavor of the original. There are no newspapers, the staff is not helpful and even the screen where to comment how you liked your stay does not work. At peak times (unfortunately I must use the lounge quite often) waiting lines at the entrance are long because of lack of staff. When commenting about the service (yes, there is a comment form) no feedback is given and nothing is changed. Sasco got a monopol (no other lounges allowed at the airport) and uses it to maximize profit to the disadvantage of its customers. The only positive is that the bathrooms are usually clean - which is true for the whole airport however.

There are few lounges at Warsaw Chopin Airport. Some of them are managed by airport, they are really poor. BTwo of them - Polonez (Schengen area) and Mazurek ( non- Schengen area) - are managed by LOT Polish Airlines and they are much more interesting. Polonez Lounge consists of two parts - bigger one for Star Alliance Frequent Travellers and smaller, more cosy for Gold, HON Circle members and business class customers. Food and drinks are almost the same - usually two or three options of hot meals; sandwiches, salads, decent selection of sweets and alcohol beverages. Both lounges are often crowded, especially in the morning and late afternoon.

Easy access off a long corridor of gates and relatively new. The food counters empty, the shower is a cubicle stuck next to a urinal that won’t fit anyone weighing more than 70Kgs. Shower mat filthy. The counter guy indifferent to your arrival or departure: busy playing a video game.

A small but decent lounge serving a large range of tasty dishes and beverages. Seats are comfortable but tightly packed together. Staff is friendly and helpful. They offer free beauty treatments which are really quite nice. It's a comforting and relaxing place so well recommended.

Although my experience in the air with LOT was very positive, the same cannot be said of their lounge in their home base of Warsaw. The lounge is small without adequate seating. Many of the fabric chairs needed a cleaning. The food selection was really quite limited and there were no international magazines or newspapers available. If LOT aspires to be a better international carrier, they are going to have to improve the lounges in their home city.

The lounge limits access to strictly four hours. I had a ten-hour layover. This policy is not available on the website of the airport -- had I known this, I would not have booked this connection. The lounge is small and crammed, which explains the policy, but it is not a valid excuse if you prepare to get a day's work done while in transit.

I travelled from Paris to Skopje via Varsaw and the way back also. Both time I went to the lLOT Polish Airlines ounge at Warsaw Airport and both time it has been the same. People in charge to welcome you at front desk not saying hello, not smiling. I felt like I disturbed these people. Do they know they are supposed to take care of customers?

The Warsaw lounge Bolero is like an oasis in the desert, which is the Warsaw Chopin airport in the non-Schengen part. The staff is nice and knowledgeable, place sometimes is quite crowded. Delicious and tasty snacks with enough good choice.  It a pity but there is no any changes since years.

The lounge is at the end of the transit corridor, on the left side: easy to spot. I visited it twice in the last week and it was good. It is a medium size lounge. Most of the time it has plenty of space. Food is good, seats comfortable and plenty of USB charging points. conventional power points are bit more scarce. I liked the food and drinks and thought the personnel was nice. It has large windows that let plenty of natural light come through. The only drawback is the speed of internet connection, that sometimes might be demoralizing..

On the Tallin airport you can find information: "Tallinn Airport Business Lounge was named the best in Europe". I cannot agree with this. Of course it's a good lounge with very good catering, wifi service and seating options. It's also very quiet and comfortable with nice staff. But it's still not enough to say, this lounge in the best in Europe. I can provide a list of lounges which are better in Europe. But if we are talking only about contract lounges (not airline lounges) this one is somewhere in the top. Some disadvantages are toilets outside.

The HON Lounge is within the business class lounge and accessible to HON Circle members and Star alliance gold customers (when flying on an eligible airline). The lounge is quite small but has everything that is needed. Fast Wifi. Food offering is quite good (Do&Co), fresh juices, soft drinks and alcoholic drinks.The lounge offers a shower with disposable towels (only one shower which is very small, but better than nothing). Restrooms are within the business class lounge, but more toilets would be better. There also is a spa with free treatments (never used them, though). Rest area Deduction of points:  No windows the HON section of the lounge. Restroom situation - General cleanliness (removal of used dishes).

Elite lounge is a small part located inside Polonez lounge designed for Gold members and Business travelling outside of Europe. Lounge has dining, seating, working and resting areas with very comfortable seats, sofas and beds. Catering in this lounge in on highest level with bread, meat, choice of cheeses, tuna, salmon etc. There are a few hot dishes to choose with soups and second dishes (sometimes with special polish taste). Also bar and fridge is well equipped. Very nice and interesting thing is free massage service for people staying at the lounge, but I never use it, so I have no opinion about it. Also I have no opinion about Wifi because I never used lounge one. Staff in the lounge is very helpful and friendly and lounge is clean. Only one disadvantage there are no showers inside the lounge.

The lounge is very large. Because it is near Halloween, the lounge layout of various types of pumpkin mas , very atmosphere. There are a variety of alcoholic drinks and various types of carbonated drinks, although the hot food is not very rich. The staff inside the lounge is very active, at any time will take away the garbage on the desktop, the lounge allows passengers to wait for boarding time, get a good rest, very good

Elite Plus Lounge in Warsaw is very good for Business Class. Not the LOT lounge but the one they have inside for Horn Circle and Start Alliance Cards. Now the food is amazing, the fresh food, the wine selections. The desert selection I end up taking a cognac with 2 after height, but they even have and made biscuits. Selection of magazines is only in Polish …. Can be better also … But the sofas, the service, they have a chef serving and checking all the food. The lounge is not big, but is spacious and extremely comfortable. Highly recommend a stop there. If you have one of those gold cards.

One of the nicest lounges I visited.  Lounge is divided on many parts, with two kitchens offering extensive selection of hot and cold food, and drinks. Free wifi, ipads for rent. Part of it is Elite Lounge, for Star Alliance Gold has restaurant like menu, little spa, business center. Definitely the best lounge in Warsaw Airport.

Lounge is nicely designed with some sofas and bar seating. In peak time can be so busy it is hard to find a space available. Internet access using WAW airport wifi. Good choice of soft drinks, hot beverages, wine and spirits. Food offers snacks, salads, soup, cheese, fruits and dessert. Friendly staff.
Awful. Why bother. The Lufthansa lounge 50 m is excellent. Why does LOT bother using this tired old lounge from Korean air where the choice of beverages is poor and the food frankly dreadful.

The new LOT/ Star Alliance lounge is an excellent addition. Signage to the lounge can be a little confusing as one can end up in the “old” lounge on the main level. However after locating the lounge upstairs one is greeted in a very modern and open (no ceiling) environment with GOOD natural light. The lounge is not very large but IS comfortable. Free Wi-Fi is available not always available at many airport lounges.

After passport & security control was difficult to find the right lounge - found the Polonez lounge after a while running around the airport. Nice small lounge in warm colours poor food and beverage assortment only some cold cuts and 2-3 kind of cheeses some olives vegetables nuts and chocolates.

In WAW there are 3 lounges all with pretty much the same amenities. In the non-schengen area there is Bolero downstairs. Schengen T2 has Ballada which is pretty small it is much better to make the trek to T1 to use Preludium which is larger and far less busy and has a large screen TV. All lounges have a few internet terminals and wi-fi. Lounges have basic snacks as well as candy sandwiches and hot pasta in a cup bar with spirits wine and beer as well as soft drinks/water. There are plenty of international and Polish newspapers and magazines available. There are no showers.
Lounge is operated by the airport. It's pretty basic. The lounges in Terminal 1 were nicer. Good selection of food and drink. Seating okay. Reading materials provided. Nothing special.

Very nice lounge by Mahan Air. Sofa was very nice and spacious. Not crowded, lighting was good. They provide free wifi connection and was really fast that I could make a smooth WeChat call to my family. Varieties of food choices provided. Soup is really delicious btw. Staff was friendly and would call passenger when its time for boarding.

Marhaba Lounge at Dubai has two separate sections a public section and a private section, Mahan Airlines reserve private section for its passengers. Lounge exclusive section was very quiet and the seats were comfortable. The only problem with this lounge is the low percentage of the toilet that we were waiting for in the queue. Dishes have a fairly good variety. Alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages are served. The coffee machine was ready to be used by the guests. Free internet with acceptable speed it is available to guests

This is the only lounge at Luxembourg, and is used by most airlines for business class passengers and those connecting to First class flights. It is very difficult to find, but actually is just as you come out of security (not signed however, so if you're as dim as me you'll do a tour of the airport before finding it!) The food and drink selection was decent. No hot food, but a good range of cold meats, bread, pastries etc. Limited spirit selection, good range of wines and draught beer is available. Nice views of the apron, and when I visited it was very quiet.

This lounge is very nice with a view on the tarmac reading material good selection of cold dishes desserts and drinks. I have not figured out whether there is free wifi. A good product from Luxair and enjoyable before a flight.

There is really only one lounge in Barbados, located on the second floor in the departures area I had a 5 hour connection so the 30 USD admittance fee was reasonable. Besides, I desperately needed wi-fi and it appeared they were the only place around that had it. Lounge is austere and without any charm. Oddly BA guests have a seperate room but its located side by side with the same amenities. Wi-fi worked great and it was comfortable enough. No, its not the Virgin LHR club room or the Cathay Wing, but what choice do you have? Booze selection sub standard. Johnny Walker Red? You've got to be kidding me! No sparkling and red and white wines mediocre. Food selection marginal. Sandwiches tasted fine and peanuts good. Staff inside were quite nice. But please change the TV screens. I, like so many travellers, are sick and tired of seeing TVs on CNN and their constant Trumpathon. Spare us!
