Since we booked Norwegian Premium we were given access to the Alitalia Lounge. We didn't have high expectations due to the reviews we read and we weren't disappointed. The place was full including crying babies and people talking loudly on their phones. The liquor is an honor bar but they ran out of ice and the person working in the area didn't seem all that interested in refilling it (it was 10:00 p.m. after all). The food was pre-packaged sandwiches and there were sodas and beer available too. People didn't pick up after themselves and left a mess when they departed. Again, no one around to put away the trash. We opted to grab a bite in the terminal. We went back to the lounge to sit for a while until our gate was posted. In a pinch the lounge was fine, but having experienced Alitalia's lounge in Rome a couple of years ago I didn't have high hopes.

Norwegian Airlines uses the No 1 lounge for their Business Class passengers. This is not a really big lounge and they can require reservations. When I arrived at the lounge I was asked if I had a reservation, and I was clueless. When I showed them my boarding pass they said they reserved spots for their Business Class passengers that are on flights so it was no problem. If you did not have a reservation and you were just using your membership or some kind of pass, they were not allowing people in as they were full that day. So, make a reservation if you are not flying Norwegian Business class. As far as lounges go, this was a very nice lounge. It is under construction now so the access is a bit strange. There was a really nice "library" which was a quiet area. Nice comfortable chairs and a long table that had some computers you could use. The main lounge was broken up into different areas which allowed for a lot of seating choices. They do a very nice breakfast spread which they take down at 11:00 and bring out lunch things. They also have a menu you can order from and they will prepare fresh food for you. That was really good! This lounge was better than either of Etihad's lounges in BKK or ABU as far as food choices. They offer the usual beverages, and have a sit down bar with a bartender. I did not notice any shower or sleeping areas. Free wifi. They have a monitor for flights inside the lounge.

Norwegian Premium passengers receive complimentary entrance to the OSL Lounge near the international gates. This lounge also services Emirates, Qatar, Lufthansa and Air France, just to name of few, so you can understand why the experience is so good. The lounge's atmosphere is quiet, calming, sophisticated and comfortable. The food is plentiful, well presented and tasty. There is a broad selection of papers and magazines, even Wallpaper! The wifi works well. Moreover, the lounge was well maintained, not crowded and very relaxing. I spent two hours there in transit and it is now on my "favourite" list of lounges. I wasn't expecting all this from Norwegian - a "low cost carrier". Norwegian is far exceeding my expectations. I am giving Norwegian the experience very high marks because I am not paying for the 5 star price!

Arrived at the Lounge roughly 16.00 on Saturday. Friendly greeting but the lounge was manic and very busy. We had to work out how the system worked as we were not told by the reception staff even though we said we had never visited the Lounge before. Once we figured out the food (hot snacks and cold assortment) and the drinks system, we sat down. The only downside was the air conditioning - it wasn't working. They had very large fans trying to cope with the very hot atmosphere in the Lounge (the lounge faces south with glass windows) but because of the high temperatures, they really couldn't cope. Overall, not a relaxing experience at this time.

Entered lounge at 20.00 hours on a Saturday. Lounge was very restful and welcoming. Not shown what to do but soon worked it out. Good selection of drinks and snacks available. Lounge was very calming and relaxing - just what we needed before a long flight. This is a good lounge and would recommend it.

I had a longish layover in FRA with a late flight out and was planning to eat here so I could sleep on the flight. The food selection is absolutely abysmal for a airline lounge. Meatballs, rice and some disgusting looking white dumplings. That was it for hot food. Really, you need to leave the lounge to eat decently. The lounge itself is large, clean, soulless. The drinks are abundant. But you'll have to drink on an empty stomach.

The LH Lounge at Frankfurt is absolutely one of the most unimpressive facilities.  The only  benefit of the LH Frankfurt business lounge is supposedly the quiet seating area, but the loud  staff interactions that continually came from the kitchen area negated this benefit. In addition, the food offerings are pathetic, along with the warm beer.

The Lufthansa lounge in Washington Dulles is very disappointing, with a poor choice of rather low quality foods. We were on a late flight (10:20 pm) and our goal was to have dinner in the lounge in order to go to sleep immediately after takeoff. The food offering was what you can expect from a school cafeteria. Vegetarian options were particularly pathetic, with essentially no protein available. The coffee machine was out of milk when we tried it and we had to alert the staff for them to refill (the coffee machines are filled with real milk and the replenishing process is rather time consuming). The staff was sparse: only one person in sight when we arrrived (not counting the receptionist). A second attendant showed up a little later. Only positive point, the seats are confortable and modern looking but the lounge is rather small. Star Alliance passengers have the option of using the Turkish lounge instead, which is a much better choice in our opinion foodwise (provided the lounge is not overcrowded).

Since long time one of the worst Lufthansa has on offer for their premium customers “Senator. Besides the uninspiring food (some overcooked mini sausages and cold salads), non-functioning beer tap (in Germany!), warm white wine (cooling system not working) and the friendliness of those working there to say at least unacceptable: attitude of not knowing why being there and for what purpose, arrogant, unfriendly etc. Exception to be made for the nice lady who cleared the tables. I know Lufthansa outsourced all services related matters within the lounge, but this visit was really no good to Lufthansa’s reputation. Unfortunately in Munich it is quite often a hit or miss.

First time transit in the new airport of Berlin and I was positively impressed. Same for Lufthansa’s Senator Lounge there. Granted entrance because of my status. Very nice interior, bright and reasonable offering of food and drinks. Had to spent 2 hours there, had enough space to get my work done and could have lunch before catching my low cost and no frills flight with Lufthansa Group‘s airline Eurowings.

By far, this was the best airport lounge we visited on our four stop trip to Europe (BKK/VIE/ATH/VIE/BKK). The lounge is located a short walk past security control. It is well marked and easy to find. The lounge is divided into two sections - dining area and quiet reading/relaxing area. There are also a few enclosed booths for phone calls, a business area with printer and a few reclining sleep chairs. Restrooms are outside the lounge in the gate departure area. The food and beverage selections were extensive (great wine, champagne, and hard liquor choices) all very high end with a mixture of Western and Greek dishes. Seating was comfortable. Highly recommend !!

Entry permitted because of my Star Alliance status. This contract lounge generically open to business and first class passengers and Priority Pass. If you love paper cups for your coffee, plastic for your drinks, worn out seats, modest (packed) food options, no papers nor magazines, you are absolutely in the right place.

The lounge is very ugly, the food option not many, the drinks are ok, but no Champagne available. It’s not that easy to become senator, after you become a senator you get a bad lounge, not difference than this one from business class.
Good lounge with a decent selection of food and beverage - warm and cold meal, non-alcoholic and alcoholic drinks Other than general LH service, the lounge is good.

This is the recently refurbished/opened new Lufthansa Senator Lounge at BER airport. The facility is located opposite gate B20 and accessible by lift or stairs. The lounge is clean and follows the plain and sober design of the other LH lounges. There is plenty of seating (I used the lounge several times and always found a free seat). There is a small salad buffet and some biscuits and fruit. The drink selection is also not very extensive but there is coffee, tea, wine, beer and soft drinks.

I am quite critical regarding Lufthansa’s tacky approach when offering lounges to their own premium passengers but in Milan Malpensa they have done a wonderful job! The lounge is pleasant, very relaxing with all kind of seating opportunities: work, relax and eat, just a joy. Food offering is outstanding compared to what normally one gets in their lounges. Drinks could be a little more exciting (or better to say less mainstream), but all in all I am impressed and I wonder how on earth Lufthansa isn’t able to offer the same standards in the main hubs.

First time visit in this lounge so didn't know what to expect. The lounge is modern, bright and airy. It has modern communal seating with tables and chairs along with secluded alcoves for a little more privacy, free wifi is available. The lounge also has a viewing terrace overlooking the airport and the Julian Alps. There was a number of Bottled local drinks, including beers, soft drinks and water, long with a wide selection of very good quality wines and a few spirits. There was a Draught beer pump too which was very nice indeed, a selection of local food and sandwiches were in cool cabinets and various snacks, fruit, bread rolls, Cakes, cooked meats and cheeses. There were various savoury snack dotted about amongs the seating.

The Bellini Lounge at Catania Airport is located in the main terminal. One has to go up a flyer of stairs (or lift) at the far end of the (small) terminal to reach the lounge. The lounge us tiny and can officially accommodate 35 people but I‘d say 20-25 people is more realistic. There is a fridge with a few soft drinks and some Prosecco and a bottle of red wine is also available. A small selection of surprisingly tasty snacks is also available. So, the lounge is modest to say the least. The toilet is located outside The lounge and is clean. Most bothersome to me were the masses of fruit flies coming out of the waste bins. Those bins are rather prominent and for some reason, were positioned just under the screens. Don’t make the mistake of paying for a guest as one will get a much better deal at one of the restaurants in the airport.

This is the Schengen Senator lounge in Munich opposite Gate G28. Like the non-Schengen version on the floor above, which I visited a couple of days ago and didn’t like, this lounge is boring and just functional. The food was not very tasty and the selection was very small.

This is a standard Lufthansa Senator’s lounge located opposite Gate H24 at MUC (non-Schengen) The layout is rather modern and functional. It feels a bit sterile but clean and welcoming. There is a selection of German food complimented by salads and sweets. The lounge offers a full bar which is a nice touch. Staff are efficient but not very friendly. The toilets are located outside and seem to serve both, the Business and Senator’s lounges.

A miserable overcrowded experience. Food uninspiring, horrible wines, no seating during this Friday afternoon, tables not cleaned or dirty plates being taken away. Definitely the worse experience ever in a Lufthansa Lounge! Better do oneself the favour to sit elsewhere in the terminal and enjoy in one of the lovely restaurant facilities LHR has on offer: pay a little (or much) and enjoy good food and nice wines! Alternatively, if one has Gold Status and some time, go rather to any other Star Alliance lounge in the Terminal. Consider this lounge as your last option!

Non-Schengen departure, in concourse B. Visited both Lufthansa’s Premium Senator and regular Business Class Lounge. Interestingly Lufthansa pampers Star Alliance Gold Card Members more than their paying business class passengers. At least, that is what Lufthansa still says. While this definitely was true before Covid, now it is not the case. Though furniture and setting are superior in the Senator Lounge, there is basically no real difference between the two lounges: same drinks, same dull and definitely not premium food in both lounges.

On April 17, 2023, we arrived at the Lufthansa Business Lounge in Athens around 3:45pm. The lounge was quite empty but we didn’t think much of it. I went up to get a glass of wine for myself, and some juice and water for my kids. Each time I took a glass, the same lady was on the other side of the kitchen replacing the glasses with clean ones and slamming them down aggressively. I thought it was strange but excused her behaviour as a cultural difference. Afterwards, I poured two small glasses of wine, to determine which varietal I would like to enjoy with my salad. Before I was done, one of the kitchen staff came over and gasped and looked at me. She had a container of ice in her hands so I moved the two glasses out of the way so she could put the ice down. She took the ice bucket and slammed it down on the counter which startled me and my son. She then proceeded to stare at me and then at the empty wine glass. I moved the glass out of the way and asked if there was somewhere else she would like me to put the glass as it was clear that she was angry with me. From there, the lady that was restocking the water glasses yelled that I should leave the glasses on a table by the kitchen. I explained that I wasn’t done and that it would be simple to ask if I could bring the glass to that table rather than coming over and yelling at me and having her colleague slam a bucket of ice on the counter next to me and my young son. I thought I was doing them a favour by bringing the glass back to where they were working and this is what I would do in Canada, and it would be viewed as a gesture of kindness. The kitchen staff continued to slam things down on the counter and dominate the area where people were trying to get drinks and food, making it very awkward for everyone. They had no respect for the travelling passengers and cared more about their unwritten rules of keeping the counter clean and the glasses stocked, than trying to maintain a happy environment with good customer service. When I went back to my table, some passengers sitting next to us explained that they observed the staff being confrontational and rude with other guests. This didn’t surprise me but I said I would go and speak to the ladies at the front desk to determine how I could provide some additional feedback about this incident and I would also go and see if we had access to the lounge next door. Before leaving the Lufthansa lounge I stopped at the front desk and spoke to the two ladies and requested an email address so I could file a complaint. They refused to provide me with this information and told me that as a lounge customer I should know better, and that I should leave empty glass on the table by the kitchen rather than bring it up to the counter. At that stage, it was clear that the kitchen staff spoke to the ladies at reception and rather than work to diffuse the situation they made it worse. I explained to them that rules are different in every country and if we are required to leave glassware on a table by a kitchen, that can’t be viewed from the lounge area, then they should have signage within the lounge that explains that to international passengers. If you are a Star Alliance member, do yourself a favour and do not use the Lufthansa business lounge until they change the attitude of the staff. Go next door to the Aegean Lounge where you will be greeted with a smile and kindness.

Overcrowded and no possibility to sit anywhere except on a high barstool. Very nice Lufthansa representatives at the welcome desk, very helpful checking me in for the return flight (Lufthansa’s App was down, again). Totally different story with the others working in the lounge, obviously not Lufthansa employees but rather working for some service provider. No eye contact, no smile or nice word. I understand it is tough sometimes, but still one can make an effort. Food so-so, drinks okay this time.

The lounge is a very quiet place - excellent reception desk people and service was outstanding. It was breakfast time so I had everything I needed. There is plenty of food, decent quality however cannot match the lounges by the mid Eastern companies. Unfortunately the quality of the Champagnes was sub par in comparison with all the premium whiskies and hard liquors. Extremely clean restrooms as well and a very personal goodbye when leaving the lounge.

Due to Star Alliance Gold Status got granted access to the Sala Leonardo lounge. A fairly ok generic frequent flyer lounge, with a reasonable choice of drinks and food. Bit of too much plastic wrapped food, plastic forks and glasses, which of course is sending a wrong message, besides transmitting cheapness (which definitely doesn’t reflect Milan).

Seems Lufthansa‘s management added a new feature to the many measures, which already miserably downgraded this airline. Not to replace empty bottles. Furthermore, one cannot understand why with all excellent white wines Germany has, Lufthansa insists on disgusting Italian and French sparkling wines. Food, for a premium lounge was average, though acceptable.

We were on a 6am Austrian Airlines flight, so had a short stay in the Senator lounge - access gained by a business class ticket. The lounge opened at 5am sharp - there was quite a queue of people waiting. The Senator lounge is slightly better than the main business class lounge, but there isn't much in it. It was significantly quieter though. Good breakfast selection. Full range of drinks including sparkling wine. Very good coffee machine. Best of all, a magazine selection is back! After 2 and a half years of no mags. Overall, I was pretty impressed.

Because of Gold-Status with Star Alliance, have access to this lounge also when flying in Economy. Senator Lounges are “on level above” regular Business Class lounges with Lufthansa. Food is uninspiring as it has been over the many years (except one adores meatballs or Frankfurters). Wine selection is quite satisfactory, though the champagne once offered in the lounge disappeared and now all kind of more or less poor quality Italian alternatives are being offered (Italy has great sparkling wines, but they are not to be found in any Lufthansa lounge, unfortunately Lufthansa seems also not to have a clue when choosing own German sparkling wines, but that’s another story). This lounge has a nice feature, being the only lounge (except the First Class Terminal) with a bar service. Though staff in the lounge is kind and helpful, this morning/early afternoon at the bar the level of service was dreadful: clearly the lady had a problem coping with people.

Undoubtedly Lufthansa went from good to mediocre and nearly all recent reports confirm this. But this experience was surprising. Having missed a connection through Munich and being it impossible to get me on the last flight to final destination, being LH-Gold I went straight to the lounge to get re-booked. Within minutes this was done, boarding card for the first next day’s flight was given, plus vouchers for an airport hotel (they booked directly, I had not to bother) and transfers by taxi. Within 30 mins I was in the hotel: I was surprised. Visit to the lounge leaving next day was good, with reasonable breakfast and good selection of drinks (appreciated very much the freshly squeezed orange juice). Was nice to see newspapers and magazines back, which one is free to take with.

Terribly underwhelming, from seating to food and beverage. Poor selection of food and drinks, not to speak of the practically no seating for the many visitors. However, better than what happens in the terminal, so even if one doesn’t find seating, it’s recommended to stay inside, as outside it is worse!

I didn't have much time to visit this lounge, but I thought I might as well visit the lounge for a drink and a bit to eat. The selection of food was disappointing compared to other business class lounges I've used. The beverages were fine and the staff were friendly and helpful. Not great, but OK.

The lounge is the only of the two present at the airport that actually works. The lounge has unpleasant smell, unfriendly hostess at the reception, and a very basic selection of food. Very few vegetarian options. Out of baked good, there were only doughnuts and they were not fresh. The tables were not cleaned and in 4 hours there has not been a cleaning person cleaning anything in the lounge.

There are no signs to take you from the airport to the lounge. I crossed and recrossed a busy road and tried to enter a car park before finding a waiting taxi driver and asking the way. Inside the lounge, the few staff are quite busy: Cleaning up, checking invoices or looking at computer screens. Just don't expect anyone to hurry over to serve you. (And a large chunk of the lounge is reserved for smokers.) I loved the private security desk, and the limo to the plane is a great idea in theory, though our stuffy shared minibus was less alluring. I'm just surprised at the lack of attention to detail. Don't expect the kind of service you get from the better Asian and Middle Eastern airlines.

At Terminal 2, there are several lounges and I visited two, on the outbound and return journey. There were no smiling welcomes, and I was  gestured towards the entrance. Layout wise they are similar, both in Lufthansa colours and furniture styles. Plenty of space for those who wished to work, standard tables and chairs for dining, and comfortable sofas to relax in. There are shower facilities, so useful for long haul travellers with connections to be able to freshen up. Although fairly crowded on both visits, the places were spotlessly clean and tidy. There was a continuous movement of staff clearing up tables and food leftovers. The bar areas were well stocked with both alcoholic (including some premium liqueurs) and nonalcoholic drinks. Unfortunately, in both lounges, the selection of hot and cold food was disappointing. The choice was limited to just a couple of items of warm food, like sausages, meatloaves and pasta, and paulry-looking salads. However, there was a selection of sweets in jars, like smarties and jelly beans which I noticed several others could not resist. One other disappointing feature is that there are no views of the apron or runways, other than car parks and buildings. On my return journey, I had a three-hour layover, and was able to use a locker to store my cabin luggage, and wander about at ease. However, with nothing interesting to look at, other than browsing the newspapers, phone, and sampling the unappetizing food, I decided to leave the place and explore the airport shops instead.

A very good lounge, which it's main feature is the wide selection of drinks, both alcoholic and non-alcoholic. However, it isn't the same for food options, as they were slightly limited. For a business class lounge, the amenities were very numerous and the quality of them was amazing. I cannot judge the wi-fi because I used mobile data.

No tv on, no one taking care of passengers. They close a little space with a person inside, and then the person served curry with rice and drinks and potato salad.  If you don´t want to give business class passengers the same conditions before covid, close your lounges. They only accepted you there if you use a white mask, but the staff use a blue mask. So, where is the logic of this?

A small lounge, where the catering part is great but the seating outdated. The seating part is dated and very modest in size. The chairs hardly have power outlets. Staff is friendly and catering is great, but the place seems packed. It's good enough for an hour or so but not more.
Very nice ambience. Food variety is for a Business Class Lounge extraordinary nice; office space is available for doing some work. German beer selection is OK; delicious coffee Quality.

Munich airport has several business lounges from Lufthansa which all offer a high quality product. Seating, service by the staff, cleanliness and choice of food are always great. Even when the lounge is busy, it's generally tidy. Especially compared to Austrian Airlines lounges which are subpar in terms of service and cleanliness. Well recommended to visit during your transit.

Frankfurt Airport Terminal 1 has several lounges. I was encouraged to go to one that was directly connected to just two gates, which I thought was great. This lounge, unlike the regular ones, was vary basic. Understandably the food and drinks was very limited, as it served just two gates. The seating was comfortable, very quiet and relaxing, excellent Internet connection, and views of taxing aircraft. However, some passengers were confused, as when the time to board was up, no one showed up or no announcements were made. There was no staff to board us directly from lounge to plane. We had to go the regular boarding point. On my return flight I used a much larger lounge (which I have visited on a previous trip). Here I was able to take a shower, enjoy a hearty breakfast and relax for my short connection to London. I was not pleased by the furniture layout on my previous visit to this lounge. But this time it was neatly arranged with quiet areas. As my layover was over 4 hours, I was able to get a taste of the hot food menu that changed late morning. As usual, there were plenty of choices for drinks, teas and premium brand spirits. Some European airline lounges just cannot match up to Asian, Middle Eastern Lounges, which are far more charming and enjoyable to relax in.

A large lounge at Heathrow Terminal 2, although rather busy on the Saturday afternoon I visited. The decor is pretty clinical, but there's lots of natural light and a restricted apron view. Decent range of drinks including draught beers, and the food was fantastic. Hot food was a choice of curries, which were fantastic. The desserts were divine, especially the ice cream.

The Lufthansa lounge in Frankfurt terminal B near gate B46 was quite low level standard, not much choice of food, poor and old seating, unluckily the soft drink machine were under maintenance for almost all the time we where in. Lufthansa staff not friendly and this was not an exception. Fortunately we were waiting for boarding with Thai.

As a Star Alliance Gold, I was allowed to use Lufthansa Senator (non-Schengen) for my flight from MUC to SIN with SQ. I have to report that this was the worst experience I ever had with a Lufthansa lounge. First of all, at reception, 4 employees, no smile for pax, just chatting together. It is not a very large room. Lunch food was terrible, sausages or a strange piece of minced meat. Dessert options very limited. I looked for drinks, found some bottles of wine on a counter, but no specific glass. I fetched a glass somewhere ele and helped myself. I was approached by a lady saying in german that I was not allowed to help myself, and that she was the bar tender (not at the bar).  I left the lounge, went to the Lounge next door (LH Business Class lounge), where everything was fine.

This Senator Business class lounge was great, clean toilets, many seating space, good choice of food and beverages, many computer-rooms, sleeping zone and showers. I like that lounge, good to spend some time.

I could access this Senator Lounge through my Star Alliance Gold status. Excellent lounge and it really shows that they value frequent flyers. Private shower  is thoroughly cleaned after every use. Good breakfast selection with eggs, breads, potatoes, pastries etc. Wide variety of coffee and other beverages including a bar area. There was also a private dark area to sleep, which was convenient for a long layover. It had a bed, pillow and blanket.

New Lounge is nice because it is very new - unfortunately little food was offered! Also the personel was almost non-existent except for one nice young lady who was the only person outside of the kitchen. All the others were in the kitchen talking loudly and laughing. Several passengers requested several times from the young lady to refill the food trays that were empty. She went into the kitchen several times, but no refills were done. After 30 min I had to leave because of my flight. Hope it will improve! Such a shame such a nice lounge is so badly managed!

There are two lounges in the gate 60-68 area at Newark, SAS and Lufthansa, I spent time in both, but Lufthansa is definitely better. I find Lufthansa lounges are very similar all over the world. But they are not similar across the Lufthansa group airlines. Austrian has a better lounge but worse food than Lufthansa, and SWISS seems to have the worst lounge of the three, even in their hub airport. This lounge to me, was a shrunken version of the lounge in London Heathrow. Adequate hot and cold food, choice of alcohol and plenty of seats. I noticed that there was a corner for HON circle and First class, this wasn’t roped off but simply had roses on the tables to indicate that they were for first class. Wifi was fast and easy to connect. The problem I really had with this senator lounge was the fact that the offerings weren’t different enough from the business lounge. Normally senator and business lounges are a far cry from each other, but when I hopped over to the business lounge, the offering was more or less the same, with barely noticeable differences. I would only be able to rate this senator lounge a 7, as it feels like a significant step down from other senator lounges across the Lufthansa network.

Dilmun Lounge, Bahrain Airport This lounge is used by nearly all airlines, except Gulf Air (who have their own). Therefore it became quite busy late night when many international flights were scheduled to depart. The lounge faces aircraft in the air jetties and beyond towards the runway, although I could not see much at night. I was expecting this place to be extra special, especially going by their publicity. On entering, it looked inviting, with beautiful subdued colours and lighting. But looking around, the furniture appeared very ordinary, with some of the most uncomfortable seating. I never like sitting in one place in a lounge, especially if it's a long wait, and usually move around trying out other seating options. Apart from a few resting seats and a family room, all other furnishings in this lounge were exactly the same. I found it quite difficult to lean back and relax in these chairs. I was hot and tired when arriving and needed a shower - only a single shower room, which had not been cleaned properly after the previous user! I mentioned it to one of the staff, who was apologetic. On the dining front, there was a good selection of finger food and vegetation options as well, but the few hot food items looked unappetising. The drinks were plenty, including high end alcoholic brands. Overall, I was rather disappointed. I am not sure I can recommend this place, but then there is not much choice either. Hopefully, once the new terminal is opened, there should be more lounges and a better experience.

Business Lounge Frankfurt Terminal 1. I was politely welcomed and informed my flight was all good to go and on time, and how close my departure gate was. I observed was how bland this lounge looked. Although there were several types of furnishing, scattered all over the place, with no particular layout.  However, the food and drinks areas were beautifully arranged and lit, making it enticing. Nice beers with description notes and a good selection of finger food, with a few options for hot food. The seating areas were unimpressive lacking in design. I would recommend this lounge for its food and beverages display, and for a short stay, it was perfectly adequate.

Business Lounge Terminal 2. As I hadn't been to this lounge for nearly two years, I was curious to see if there were any changes or improvements. I was there at breakfast time, and the food was bacon, tomato, scrambled eggs etc. The bacon was hard and dry. One of the coffee machines were broken. But I shouldn't really complain, as there were a few other drinks and food options. For me, the lounge is fine for a short visit. For the longer stays, there are a few resting seats and a conference room with computer facilities.

The Lufthansa Senator Lounge in Stuttgart is one long room with excellent tarmac view. The lounge consists of two section which are divided by a 1.8m high partition wall: one section is the buffet with tables, the other section consists of old-style armchairs with power outlets. Variety of food is subpar. Nothing special. Fairly large selection of booze. All in all not one of the best Lufthansa lounges. Certainly a good alternative to the movie selection on a long haul flight.

There was full English breakfast on offer, and some delicious pastries and croissants. The coffee was just right. There were sufficient seats and a variety of them. The decor was very classic, very contemporary. Luckily this lounge still has the Lufthansa yellow as opposed to their newer navy blue rebranding. If I had to fly intra Europe from Heathrow, I’d be happy to use this lounge again. If I’m flying long haul, I’d probably try the Singapore Airlines or United club as those are probably better. But for a short haul lounge, this lounge gets my thumbs up. I used this lounge simply as I couldn’t be bothered to walk to the satellite at Heathrow T2 until my flight was called for boarding.

Very nice Lounge, that is even bigger then some of the senator lounges in German airport. A very nice view over the airside. A Privilege of lounges outside home bases ist that the few flights are announced in the lounge and the passengers are requested to board on the right time with a direct access to the boarding gate. Very efficient. I like that.

The airport lounge in Kiev that Lufthansa use is surprisingly good. Comfortable, clean, good selection of drinks and snacks, polite staff. Smoking room is right inside the lounge, which is super convenient for smokers. Lounge is large and easily accessible. It's not airline specific, but any business class passenger can get an invitation to use it. I was impressed and very pleasantly surprised.

Delights to Go location: Instead of a lounge, the Delights to Go area is a self-service counter next to Gate G19 where two vending machines distribute snacks. After scanning the boarding pass, one can choose between three different snack boxes. The idea is to offer an option to passengers that do not have time to visit the lounge. Access rules: The usual suspects are allowed: Basically same as to a Business Class Lounge (M&M HON, SEN, FTL, *G, F, C). It was possible to go to the regular lounge before and then grab a snack at the Delights to Go area prior to my flight. As the name indicates, this is not a lounge but a quick option to pick up a snack box. There was an attendant who scanned my boarding pass and let me in. As Star Alliance Gold, I could have brought a companion. Delights to Go offerings: There are two identical snack box vending machines and two coffee machines on the left side and a service counter on the right side. While the coffee machines can be used without scanning a boarding pass, a snack box can only be retrieved from the vending machine by scanning the boarding pass. After scanning, I had a choice between three food bundles: - Balance: Goat cheese wrap, seeds with raisins, fresh apple, still water. - Classic: Tunasalad, Honey spiced almonds, fresh apple, still water. - Local: Meat Loaf Croissant, Brezel with sour cream flavour, fresh apple, still water. These choices vary and on a different occasion the local option was called Oktoberfest and contained a sausage salad, a bag of pretzels, a fresh apple and still water. This time I chose the Balance option. It took some 20 seconds until the box was dispensed. Lufthansa branded paper bags were available to carry the box. The wrap was quite tasty but I didn´t like the small apple too much. I would have preferred a packed fruit salad. It was a nice snack but I would not consider it a replacement for a lunch. In theory, only one snack box is given per boarding pass. Both machines are connected to each other and it was not possible to scan the same boarding pass at each machine. The machine was also smart enough to figure out that the actual printed boarding pass and the boarding pass on my phone are the same and it showed me that my boarding pass had already been used. But I did find a work-around: When I changed my seat in the Lufthansa App an updated boarding pass was shown on my phone. Even though my boarding sequence number remained the same, I could pull another box. It was also interesting to see that the machine apparently does not take booking class or status into consideration: The week before I was flying with my partner (different reservation, no status, economy class) and she also received a snack box. It seems like once you are in the Delights to Go area you can scan any Lufthansa boarding pass. In fact, there was a dad scanning boarding passes and getting snack boxes for his three children and his wife who were waiting outside. It would be interesting to see if boarding passes of other Star Alliance airlines or even of non Star Alliance airlines are accepted by the machine. After my return flight I wanted to try if the machine Also gives out a snack box for arriving passengers, but the agent refused to let me. Verdict: The location of the Delights to go area could be closer to the main security gates. If you have to go to the satellite or the international gates this means a detour. The taste and the quality of the food are quite good.

Surprising very nice lounge of Lufthansa at Washington Dulles. Best Lufthansa Senator Lounge standards, with direct access to the boarding gates. I really love it like this - just stay, enjoy and board when announced.
Very good lounge. High-speed wifi and great service. Lufthansa is a great airline, it has 5 Skytrax stars and the lounge is very good. I will recommend it!

This review is about my recent visit to a Lufthansa Senator Lounge at Munich Airport, concourse G, for an early bird flight to Dortmund with Eurowings. While Eurowings is not part of the Star Alliance, Lufthansa Senators/HON have access to this Lounge when booked in an eligible fare (C or Smart). Furthermore, Eurowings has an agreement with ANA, Air Canada and United and their top tiers can access the Lounge on any fare as long as they have a Gold Status in their programm. Gold members of other Star Alliance carriers cannot access the lounge when flying Eurowings. I only stayed in the lounge for <15 minutes but I find that the food offering has very much improved: a broad variety of cold and hot breakfast dishes was available as well as fresh fruits. As it is vacation time, there was a small buffet for kids and other passengers were enjoying their Weißbier (wheat beer). The bar was staffed and i could have ordered a Gin Tonic - but I had a fresh smoothie which was also good. The lounge was not full and comfortable. Separate working spaces are available as well as regular seating at tables and armchairs. Lounge has its own bathroom. Several newspapers are available for take away and some more upon request. This lounge was quite good and I recommend it. Well, there are no windows facing the tarmac but still a good lounge, especially considering that it is in the domestic/Schengen Terminal.

It was a thursday evening and the Lufthansa lounge was crowded if not overcrowded. It looks like a regular Schengen Lounge in Munich or Frankfurt. Some cold and warm snacks, cold and hot drinks, wines and spirits. It was good enough for me to wait for my flight and have a snack but too crowded to work quietly. Good standard intra-european Lufthansa lounge.

Both lounges of Lufthansa at Dresden Airport (Senator & business) are neighboring each other. Senator lounge is accessible from the business lounge. There you can find a couple of conformable seats a desk area and a little counter for snacks and food. All in all very tiny but lovely and nice for plane spotting.

In the Schengen Area in Terminal A there are only a total of 3 lounges that, at peak times, are more than overcrowded. Schengen departures in Terminal B have no lounge access. Guests in the three lounges (2 business, one Senator/Star Alliance Gold) can stand for an hour and are catered for by a disappointing offer of food. All this leaves regular  customers guessing why the airline gets it so right with their second hub Munich (2 Business lounges and a total of 4 Senator lounges/areas). In their London, Munich and hopefully soon Malpensa lounge, Lufthansa also provides a much more sophisticated food offer compared to its main hub, Frankfurt. So what is it, that is the cause of this difference? Maybe all Lufthansa management responsible for travel experience should be paired up with a passenger and follow their real travel experience for the duration of their Frankfurt airport stay to help realize, how sub-optimal the whole set-up really is.

The lounge that Lufthansa use in Cairo is in poor condition, rugs are torn and the food which is supposed to be hot is cold. There's no beer or wine offered. The signage to the lounges points to the G gates get there are two more lounges in the F gate area of terminal 3. No television is offered.

Very comfortable and nice lounge in Cologne.  It has a circular form and all seats are comfortable. No Wifi connection issue. Food quality is very good but choice is quite limited for the second highest lounge class. The bathrooms are however tiny.

Frankfurt Senator Lounge at the A Gates, I use this lounge a lot, probably the one that I use more. The quality on the drinks and the food is there no doubt. Internet is excellent. I notice that the people there are not so friendly like before. The day after arriving from another flight I notice that they are not cleaning the floor and the tables in a proper way. This is a reference lounge for Lufthansa so I assume they will fix this problems soon.

Lounge in Kiev This is a multiple lounge (for many airlines) I already come to this lounge for a few years (at least twice a year) and I have always positive a note.  WIFI works perfectly! Food is more or less good but almost all fast food, some food is made there but still is not that good to be honest, not even the soup, I suppose that we need to take the country situation in here. Water, some humble selection of wines (one each) same drinks is a humble lounge. People smile and welcome you. Good chairs (red and blue) and not that many electric power available to our devices. Toilets are clean. The lounge is also well located.

Lufthansa Lounge Munich K area Senator. Lounge WI-FI works perfect. They update some thinks on the lunge some are good others not that much. Water comes now from an electronic device, not that good water.  Food for the night not that so enthusiastic. Potato soup with potatoes (German style) are too much for my taste to be honest. Chairs not that clean, they clean the tables and the dishes not doubt on that - and what about the chairs? Reception people is nice. Journal and magazine selection was poor for the end of the day.

This Senator Lounge is a very good stop when you travel through Munich. It's equipped with everything you need: dinning area, bar, electrical sockets, resting area, showers, beds, fast wifi and working area. However it's very small and almost always heavily occupied. Food and drinks also fits my needs but they aren't best quality. Staff is very kind. I recommend this place.

Moscow DME Lounge is a simple Lounge don’t expect too much. Internet works and perfectly. Chairs are colorful and some are comfortable, to be honest I prefer the Swiss lounge is simpler than the Lufthansa one in Moscow but the Chairs are better. The drama is you can’t use your Star Alliance gold member cards in the Swiss Lounge in Moscow DME, don’t ask me why, even the lady that receive you as a Start Alliance banner (what 2 meters long on her back?) but they will kick out; if you don’t fly Swiss you are not welcome - unusual and exotic to say the least.Now let’s getting back to the Lufthansa Lounge, some food is there and drinks but is like you are in a Priority Pass lounge - I suppose that is ok for Moscow. But they can do better, much better - Wi-Fi works perfectly

Frankfurt Lounge Departure Area A Senator Lounge. Star Alliance Gold This is a good lounge always was, and probably always will be.  Even is only for short flights is a great lounge. WI-FI works perfect, always I don’t remember a single time that the Wi-Fi was not working properly. The food is always great today we have Vegetarian dishes and Pumpkin soup (always a great choice in organic and Healthy food. Draft finest German beer, and Newspapers from all over the world, well they have it. Senator Chairs with DC Power for each chair, light, a great view to the airport and a good service. Always excellent coffee. Sometimes we get rush hour but even the rush hour the service is there. People always helpful, and normally they smile. Highly recommended to ones that can go in.

Munich Senator Lounge. This is normally a good lounge. Bathrooms are very clean always. Internet works like a clock, perfectly. Many electric power available almost all Senator Chairs have it. Space is there, you can feel comfortable getting a Magazine and so on, a good wine, etc. The food is normally good. Almost no Junkie food at all, organic juices available, etc. The people on the reception make you feel very comfortable, when is Easter they have chocolate bunny’s to offer you, this kind attention all year around, small thinks that make you fell comfortable. This lounge is also perfectly located.

A nice lounge and not too crowded. There was plenty of room and a nice selection of snacks. Nothing to write home about but plenty of choices. There were no warm meals though. The buffet was clean and tidy. Chairs and sofas were comfortable. There was some good air conditioning which was very welcome as the rest of the airport is very hot in summer. The WiFi was very fast.

Lounge is in two area. One for the business class and one for the Senator member/Star alliance gold members which is better equipped. On the Senator lounge there are red and white wines and prosecco. There is a good selections of liquors. There is also salad, soup, pasta, cheeses and pastries. Quality is good and toilets are clean There is also a relaxation area with a trees wall, very nice. I would recommend this lounge to everybody.

The Senator Lounge in the B concourse at FRA is large, clean, and comfortable. I visited it twice this week, once as a Croatia Airlines passenger and today again flying with Lufthansa. There is an impressive array of hot and cold food, and a wide selection of alcoholic beverages, including sparkling wine. There are huge picture windows overlooking the tarmac and the active runways. The personnel here are friendly and helpful; several of them remembered me from my last visit. This is a very pleasant place to spend time between flights.

I elected to purchase entry to the LH lounge at Washington as I arrived for my flight to Frankfurt quite early. As a PE passenger you're not granted immediate access to the lounge; however, like many things with LH, for a very reasonable fee you can purchase access. In this instance lounge access was a mere $35. On arrival the ground hostesses were very friendly and happy to help/show you the amenities. I didn't feel this necessary as the lounge was quite small. As a fee paying passenger I was happy with what was on offer in the lounge: great drinks selection, great food selection, Wi-Fi, somewhere comfy to sit, charging points etc etc. I feel, however, that if I was a BC Fare paying passenger I would be less impressed. It didn't feel particularly clean or well organised; the appearance was very bland and it was a bit disorganised. Overall a great experience for an upgrader, but room for improvement.

The Senator lounge at Washington Dulles is compact, and on my previous two visits, both around 4:00PM, it was crowded, loud, and messy. Yesterday though, at the same time, despite the fact that there were three Star Alliance flights preparing to depart (Brussels Airlines, South African Airways, and Lufthansa), there were few lounge customers. There were only two attendants tending bar and busing plates, but they were able to provide attentive service. The bar is well stocked, including a good quality German sparkling wine, and the food offerings were limited in variety but delicious and more than adequate for a snack or a complete pre-flight meal. There are large picture windows looking out over the tarmac, but there was very limited traffic to watch. If you are a United Airlines passenger, the trek to the B concourse is somewhat complicated and time-consuming, but the reward is worth the investment. Star Golds also have access to the relatively new Turkish lounge nearby at gate B43. Although the domestic United Clubs are much improved recently, either of these Star Alliance alternatives makes good sense if you have the time and a moderate spirit of adventure.

We went to the Puerta de Alcalá Schengen contract lounge for Lufthansa at Madrid Barajas airport prior to our return flight to Munich on March 12, 2017: a very pleasant experience. The lounge is very spacious, light, airy and modern, very well kept and clean, with very clean toilets and a separate working room with computer terminals and wifi throughout. The best thing is the spacing between seating areas that guarantees privacy, and there are great views over the tarmac and runways, not essential but a nice touch. The food and drinks selection is adequate and of good quality but could include hot dishes, and the two ladies at the reception might learn how to smile. Otherwise, no complaints; thoroughly recommended.

This lounge near A26 is close to the departure gates of most domestic flights. Given the prices for the Business Class tickets on domestic routes, this lounge is hardly worth the money. It was overcrowded and noisy in the morning hours. This issue is helped in a certain way by the great staff (the table cleaners are quick and thoroughly).

The Senator lounge at Berlin Tegel airport was a huge disappointment; although it was spacious it's appearance was outdated and worn. A rather small variety of snacks and drinks were provided on a buffet which was located in the darkest corner of the lounge. The destination board was only in sight of a few fauteuils and the announcements made were accoustically barely understandable.

We spent some time in the Schengen Business Class Lounge Terminal 2 Satellite (Star Alliance) prior to our MUC-BCN flight on and found it to be an enjoyable experience. The lounge is spacious, bright, airy and clean, nicely decorated without ostentation. It provides comfortable seating areas and nice alcoves along the walls for people who want to work and be left in peace. Naturally there´s wi-fi throughout, large screens on the walls airing CNN etc. plus a comprehensive selection of newspapers and journals. The friendly staff keep the place clean and offer a reasonable selection of hot and cold foods and drinks at your discretion, and there´s a nice airside view over the apron. Nothing sensational but still thoroughly recommended.

I heard that Sala Pau Casalls (which Lufthansa used at this airport) promotes itself as "The Best Business Class Lounge in the World". After having visited it, I wonder what standards they judge themselves by. In fact the lounge is rather dark, run-down and downright dirty. It´s in dire need of refurbishing, redecorating or at least vacuuming. The seating areas have dark, sagging leather chairs torn at the edges, adorned with dirty plates and half-empty glasses that nobody bothers to remove. The food and drinks selection is limited to fridges with coke and a selection of lukewarm fruit juices plus Nespresso. The only food I could see anywhere was sweets from an automat. I suppose the wi-fi works as I saw a couple of people working with their laptops. There is no airside view, not essential obviously but a nice touch when you have it. A totally a-typical experience for Barcelona which is a city where things normally run smoothly and things are done well.

The new Business Lounge at the satellite Terminal 2 is a quiet place, where you can wait for the departure of your plane. You will find toilets, showers, newspapers, power to charge your phone/tablet etc., Wi-Fi, drinks (alcoholic and non-alcoholic), cold and warm food, fruits, sweets etc. You can relax or work as you like.

Used the Lufthansa lounge at New York JFK when travelling as an Air China customer. It was your typical airline lounge, perhaps a bit nicer than a few others I've visited. Plenty of seating, drinks, food, areas to plug in, tv room with some big screens. Reading other reviews, it sounds like it's quite a bit better than actual Air China lounges in other areas of the world.

I think that the lounge for Senator's and Star Alliance Gold members in the Schengen area in Frankfurt is pitiful. Unlike Lufthansa's offer in Munich of a total of 4 different lounges for Schengen arrivals and departures, Frankfurt has only one. After the A-Terminal-extension, frequent flyers were hoping a major improvement, but it is clear the lounge was planned too small for all the passengers that would use it. So, this lounge certainly does not deliver relaxation and peace and quiet - it's a fight for space. Also, the food offer is terrible compared to other LH Senator lounges in London or Munich. How can this be at Lufthansa's main hub?

This is my third visit to the Lufthansa Senator lounge at Frankfurt airport. I love this lounge as it has great facilities such as showers, sleeping areas and good food and drinks selection. It has large windows with nice views of the tarmac and it has a lot of natural light. The drinks and dessert selection is nice with some really nice german beers on tap. The food selection is okay (mainly sausage). I wish they had some additional options for hot food.  This lounge makes layovers at Frankfurt airports pleasant and comfortable. The lounge also has free luggage storage areas and their staff are friendly.

This Lufthansa lounge made a bright impression. The typical elegantly designed Lufthansa fauteuils were quite new and cofortable. A fast wifi. Moreover, the provided pastries were delicious and the coffees satisfied me. Genererally the selection of beverages was average; even champagne was avialable. Likewise, the staff was very helpful and friendly.

As a Business Class passenger on Swiss, I was given an invitation to use the Lufthansa lounge in Concourse D. It was around midnight and the lounge was quite full. It had the typical German style decor and the food offerings were much better than LH lounges in Germany. Surprisingly there were no computers or printers if you need to get some work completed but the staff were kind enough to give me the email address where they printed out whatever I sent to that address.

This small lounge has recently been renovated and looks now much more modern than before. Just wider lounge chairs and two relax chairs to lay up your legs. Very nice. Still no daylight, still no bathroom inside the lounge, still very limited food and drink offer.

Senator Lounge Terminal A (Schengen) at Frankfurt. A real disappointment after Lufthansa finally opened their new lounges as part of the Z-Terminal extension. Not enough space from day 1 to cater for all the guests, even in the Senator Lounge. It's a fight for space and quiet. Unfortunately, the food offers pales in comparison to what Lufthansa for instance offers in Heathrow's T2. Why they would do that at their home base in beyond me. But being a Senator at Frankfurt airport - at least for Schengen flights - feels like cattle herded together.

The Lufthansa Senator Lounge in Boston is rather small compared to their counterparts on other airports. Hence it got very cramped before the evening departures started boarding. The lounge appeared very dismal due to the fact that there were no windows except one in the rearward area of the room. The furnishing looked a bit neglected too. By contrast, the washrooms were very clean and modernly done up. When it comes to the catering the only snacks were some packets of crisps, cookies and strange looking sandwiches. The choice of beverages was better but still medicore considering comparable lounges from Lufthansa.

Very comfortable and new lounge. I was really impressed by the quality. There were many types of beverages, from water, juice and sodas, to several types of wine (2 red, 2 white, 1 sparkling), beers and many spirits - coffee and tea were also available in many forms. The buffet was very generous in variety; mostly small snacks and sandwiches, salad, soup and dessert, as well as bread, but the hot snack included very good Brazilian "pao de queijo" and other tasty treats.  Toilets were clean, internet access was fair for the country's quality (above average, indeed), nothing to complain. Another important good point is that the lounge is quite close to the gate. I believe no one would take more than 10 minutes to a relatively far gate (5 minutes for me). And they announce the boarding time, so you can really leave your seat in the lounge straight to the airplane. This definitely makes a positive difference in travel comfort.

All in all, the Munich Business Class lounge complies with what you would expect from such a lounge. As a Lufthansa FTL, the lounge meets all my expectations. I am able to grab a bite from a variety of options and the beverages provided are above average in comparison to similar lounges. Whilst being quite full at times, I have never not found a seat and have not had any real cause for concern.

Senator T2 Lounge at Munich Airport was busy, but not completely full late afternoon during the week. I used one of the lounge chairs which are installed in groups so that you can chat with co-travellers. Had an espresso from the barista at the bar which was good and a green thai curry soup at the buffet together with a pretzel plus very nice basil spread. At least the food was slightly better compared to the business lounges in Munich which I usually visit. Toilets seemed to be worn (but clean) and some parts of the equipment were missing. Still would recommend the lounge compared to other LH lounges I have used.

Had the opportunity to use the Lufthansa Senator/Star Alliance Gold lounge in Stuttgart for a short break before departure to Munich. This was the first time for me here and I must say that I liked the lounge (especially compared to other LH lounges away from their hubs. The lounge is situated centrally close to the gates on the upper floor, overlooking the runway and taxiing airplanes. Like usual for LH lounges of this size there is a Business lounge right next to it. Not too much difference from what I could see. The wireless internet is for free and has decent speed. At the Senator lounge you had the choice of the usual beverages, beer from draft, some wine and spirits. There were some salads, hot wings, and Swabian Maultaschen available from buffet. Not too bad compared to other mediocre lounge food. I had the Maultaschen which tasted good and a fresh pretzel. There was also some yogurt and cake. But I didn’t have enough time to taste it. Next time I will spend more time.

Brand new (in summer 2014) Lufthansa lounge at Heathrow terminal 2. Good quality ham, sausages and bread, complemented by good choice of beers and spirits. Another good thing is the relaxing ambience. Space is huge, and Senator Lounge is separated from the business lounge (which is noisier) with a door and a wall which is nice.

I arrived at the airport 5:20 A.M. on a Sunday and it was pretty empty. I tried to follow the signs for the lounge (VIP) bot got lost somehow and ended up at the gate. From there I walked back and finally found the lounge on the upper floor. My boarding pass was scanned from my phone and my Star Alliance Gold card was checked. A minute late I was in and able to see a nice open space with wide lounge chairs and sofas. Everything was clean and well arranged. Breakfast was ok but not a big surprise: toast, Nespresso coffee (didn't find warm milk), cereals, yogurt, croissants, danish pastries, some fruit. Orange juice of medium quality which is a shame in a city like Barcelona where you get fantastic fresh juice at every corner. I grabbed what I could get in a rush as my flight would depart in 35 minutes. For a short visit I was satisfied. Hope to have more time when I probably flight on Lufthansa again in October.

I use this Platinum Lounge at Budapest Airport very often (3rd party lounge) and they serve exactly the same food! Nothing cooked, only salami and cheese with some corn and olives. They offer something cooked as well but you have to pay for with which is not usual for a big airport. Good selection of soft drinks, coffee, wine and beer. Very hot inside, doesn't matter the time of the year. No toilet, no shower service. For using the toilet you have to walk couple of minute outside of the lounge.

Have been resting at SATS lounges numerous times. Has been mostly a pleasant experience - showers, massage chairs, food and beverage selections. It was no problem having a good rest before boarding my next flight. However, there are a few things which could be improved. As i had a 6am flight and I entered the lounge at around 2am, there wasn't much food at all! The hot food pots were empty and all i had to eat was some bread and jam. I was hoping they could at least put out just a few other types of food as people using the lounges at these timings are the ones that really need some food and rest.

Nice Lufthansa lounge in Mumbai. Only problem is all airlines share the same lounge so it can be a bit cramped and busy. Overall it was clean and spacious with great food and beverage choices and great service even at 1am. Having one lounge for all airlines makes it very hard for airlines to distinguish their product on the ground.

Lounge is very modern, clean, easy to find, efficient, well appointed. It grants a great views of the airport, the runaway and taxiways, and the gates. It has a terrace for visitors to observe airport operations, take offs and landings, a dream for flight aficionados. Furniture is comfortable and stylish, and the various seating areas are well distributed, allowing both privacy and convenience. Restrooms are clean and comfortable. There is an excellent selection of both non-alcoholic and alcoholic drinks, an expresso machine, and one of the best brands of fruit juices. There is also freshly squeezed orange juice during the breakfast time slot. Food is excellent, with a variety of snacks and both cold and warm food (danishes, croissants, jams, yogurt and warm crepes for breakfast; sandwiches, savory pastries, pizza, chips, olives for lunch and dinner). Wines are of good quality and variety. Staff is friendly and helpful. It tends to be a bit crowded at rush times but still acceptable.

Had a connecting flight with SAS to CPH, which does not offer business class. Still allowed to enter Lufthansa lounge on merit of my inbound flight from Delhi onboard LH (Business Class). Had ample space, more than adequate shower facilities and good wifi connectivity. Lounge was clean, well-staffed and well maintained. Unfortunately, food layout was a bit disappointing.

Was on the 3:00am flight to FRA. Food layout lacked both variety and quality. Beverage selection was good. Connecting to the Wi-fi was problematic at first, speeds were slightly below average. Shared a common toilet with SQ's Krisflyer lounge. No Showers. Staff was attentive and active.

Flying out to Houston from FRA. Expected a lot, since it was an intercontinental flight and Lufthansa didn't disappoint. Even though the food layout was slightly below average, the lounge was well maintained, had excellent wifi connectivity, showers were spacious and well maintained, staff was attentive and active. Beverage selection was good. Washrooms were well stocked with amenities and were clean.

At Check-in we received an invitation card to this contract Premier Lounge. It is at the very end of the shopping area but close to the gates. The lounge has a wide seating area and a buffet offering warm and cold snacks in the middle. The selection of food was average. Quality was average as well. The washrooms were well kept and clean. I didn't check the shower rooms. The drink selection was rather limited though. There's a coffee machine and a selection of common soft drinks, but I didn't find any alcoholic beverages apart from beer, which is totally fine for me, but might be bothersome for others.

The Lufthansa Senator Lounge in Frankfurt is very impressive. We arrived in the morning hours and came here to refresh and get a quick breakfast before boarding our next flight. Although the receptionist was unfriendly, the lounge itself is indeed really nice. There is a large seating area available, as well as working desks and a bar like area close to the buffet. The breakfast buffet offers a wide selection of bread rolls, croissants, cold cuts, cheese and cereals and so forth. Also there are boiled eggs, bacon and scrambled eggs available. An extensive choice of tea, coffee, soft drinks and alcoholic beverages is also available. Washrooms were very clean.

Lounge was crowded, poor food selection (soup, pickles, potato salad, pasta with sauces and crackers), beverage selection okay, toilets very crowded when I was there. There's nothing exclusive about it. A shame because otherwise I am a great fan of LH.

I visited the Lufthansa lounge as a Star Alliance Gold member. As my status has just been upgraded, I was not yet in possess of the membership card, but was only having my app and a print out of my membership account. The receptionist was extremely unfriendly and denied my access at first. When I asked her to check up status based on my account number she refused to do so and instead, she was handling other guests while keeping me standing there waiting. She was also not able to see my status from the mobile card in my app. She said she couldn't read it. She only let me pass after I showed her the print out saying, "well I have to believe you then". Having left this upsetting issue behind me I was ready to settle down. The lounge is relatively small there is now view to enjoy, which is very unfortunate. The lounge features an eating area with a buffet, a relaxing area with comfortable armchairs and a working area with working desks. Free wifi is provided, yet a bit slow. As it was rush hour, most of the seats were already taken. We were however able to get some seats near the buffet and served ourselves with some snacks. The food selection was OK. Featuring some chicken wings and a soup along with various cold choices. The cold choices were inspired by the ongoing Oktoberfest. Drinks selection was good and featured all common choices. I especially liked the Lufthansa Lemonade. The Lufthansa branded glasses are also a very nice touch. Staff inside the lounge was attentive and cleared the tables quickly. Overall, the lounge would be quite OK. However it would be nice to have friendlier staff and a better view towards the apron.

This Lufthansa lounge is okay, but little to no difference from their business lounge, other than you can't pour your own beer in first class and have to find a service staff to get a drink. Very roomy with high ceilings, but I liked the low ceilings and coziness in business class lounge better. Not as good as United First class lounge at IAD.
This lounge was good, but not as good as others I've experienced. The food and drinks offering were very average, and the lounge itself was also just above average.

For the small airport of Hanover the Lufthansa Senator Lounge is a very good lounge. Selection of food is good, during afternoon and evening there are hot options available. As well a good drinks and coffee. German and english newspapers are next to the front desk, as well a good variation. Very nice view of the apron and terminal A and B.

A warm welcome from Lufthansa Lounge Staff. Lounge is split into two sections, one larger for business and one smaller for first. It is one of my preferred lounges as it has a direct connect thru a door to the jet bridge of the plane. Food and wine is excellent for a lounge, where the seating area for first can improve. As first class passenger, you can order wine and food from a menu and get it served on your table. For business class there is a food and bar with different kind of warm and cold food available. I got my food served right on the boarding call and the ground staff gave me another 15 min to finish as we were good on time.  Overall great service.
A dignified and relaxing lounge, very attentive Lufthansa staff. Excellent DO&CO cuisine with buffet and a la carte dishes, dreamlike desserts.

This lounge is quite large, and at 10am the seating was adequate and varied with leather chairs, work stations, and eating counters. The food and beverage selections were ample and tasty. The most important aspect however was the Lufthansa staff. There was a major problem with my reservation and ticket that didn't become apparent until after check-in, security, and passport control. When I went on-line to see if the adjacent seat was still open, I discovered that my assigned seat showed as unoccupied. The Lufthansa staff in the lounge spent 30 minutes calling back and forth to various United Airlines agents to resolve the problem. I will be eternally grateful to this staff and to Lufthansa in general. If I we're mean and petty, I would complain that this lounge is located in an interior space and offers no view of tarmac or runway. Nevertheless, if the situation boils down to viewing airplanes or getting to board a plane on which you thought you had a confirmed seat, I will go with the latter. Kudos and a thousand thanks to Lufthansa.

I cannot understand why Lufthansa use this lounge - shared by a lot of companies it is a very unpleasant place. Not very clean with an extremely poor choice of drinks and food. The soft drinks in the fridge were not chilled. Staff unfriendly and slow service.

Visited on 1st June 2015 before UA 918 to LHR. Even though this lounge was overcrowded (at 15:30 )and required a considerable odyssey from the UA gates, it was still worth the trek. They have champagne, free cocktails, and a more-than-adequate supply of good things to eat. There are big windows that overlook the tarmac, and you certainly get a good view of an Austrian Airlines 767. In sum, German efficiency, fine hospitality, and easily the best lounge at IAD If you're Star Gold, take the hike.
Very disappointing. No real food during mid-day. No free wi-fi beyond what the airport provides (one half hour). Not what we would have expected.

Another visit to this lounge and nothing has been done to improve the miserably inadequate levels of catering. Soup or spaetzle potato salad and that's about it apart from a few pieces of bread and some peppers plus sweets and peanuts. So I've made yet another complaint and will keep doing so until something is done to improve matters.

The standard of catering in this lounge continues to deteriorate. Today the only choices were broth or soup - and a couple of trays of stewed vegetables. Plus the usual potato salad bread etc - but no meat of any kind. This lounge was once quite good but is now very mediocre. Also WiFi is often stretched to the limit. The two receptionists seemed totally bored and lacked much in the way of customer service skills. Come on Lufthansa - give this place a much-needed make over!
Fantastic lounge with spacious shower rooms and ample seating. The buffet has a wide variety of food and beverages along with excellent staff.

Lounge was comfortable but a few more quiet areas would have been nicer: i.e. more space. Good choice of snacks refreshments & warm food. No queues & adequate to drink. Was not aware of any massage services.

The lounge is hopelessly overcrowded the wifi doesn't function the food quality & display leave a lot to be desired. The cleanliness of the food preparation counters are unappetizing. Lufthansa & the Star Alliance are doing themselves a dis-service in offering its business class passengers this lounge.

Obviously new. Very comfortable with showers available. 2 beers on tap pour your own. Nice selection of wines. We were there at lunch time and had hot dogs and 2 different soups plus salad bar. Wifi instant connect with no password. Certainly better lounge than a lot.

The most complicated WiFi-access ever. The Lufthansa/Star Alliance lounge at the Delhi International Airport is fine except for the strange WiFi-routines. The lounge is big nice furniture good access to electricity nice staff clean good food and beverage selection clean restrooms but the WiFi! You receive an access code per device. You have to enter these codes and then wait for an SMS with some kind of verification code. When you return to the webpage after receiving the SMS-sent code then you are back to the initial page again and have to start all over again. If you are lucky you are logged in. If you are inactive on the internet for a few minutes you are logged out and have to ask for a new code and start all over again. Why make it so complicated. It is like the domestic Lufthansa lounges in the early 2000s.

The new lounge which was opened at the same time as new Z Concourse is very modern. However I noticed that the food selection and quality is getting lower each month. The sweets are just regular cookies but in the past there were chocolate pastries! The LH staff at the counter inside is far more occupied by phone or chit-chatting with each other than taking care of the passengers. I also noticed they grab drinks and snacks from the main bar and would enjoy them at their work position. No more refreshing towels on display to take. Now you have to ask for them at the counter and you get no more than 2!

Pleasant and spacious lounge with an acceptably tasty selection of warm/cold food snacks and beverages. Entrance staffing is odd. Non-LH entrance check leaves the two LH lounge dragons free to communicate nonstop. Which they do. Not by way of greeting guests more like "nonstop them". Weird choices of hot food: Both dishes were made of pork on both visits highly Muslim-friendly. The longest mobile-phone conversation clearly audible was when a Sky Chefs employee answered her phone to discuss her Sunday lunch. At least it sounded more interesting than what Sky Chefs offered in the lounge. Empty trays used to be refilled at faster speeds so your selection may be drastically reduced during a short visit. Empty dishes are removed from tables at infrequent intervals. Sky Chefs and LH offer a consistent experience: They present themselves as self-serving organisations which will accommodate customers albeit grudgingly and only once done with themselves.

Very decent size with a good range of food and drink available including weissbier on tap which is always welcome and traditional Bavarian specialties; welcoming area and a good amount of seating. Excellent selection of newspapers and a nice place to spend some time before the flight. No announcements; you need to check the screens yourself. Worth visiting again.
The lounge was very busy at peak times however the food was good and the bathrooms were clean.

An excellent lounge - bright comfortable welcoming staff good food and drinks. There was a calm environment friendly and efficient. Food was good in quality and variety and the drinks were plentiful and restocked efficiently. Very good.
Fairly simple in all respects but calm and not too busy. Easy to get things done so functionally good. Service is ok but lacks warmth something I have noticed in the lounge on Level G too.

First time in this lounge used AA Admirals Club and TAM First Class lounges previously while traveling on Lufthansa. This lounge is a downgrade. Very small and claustrophobic with no views and no windows. A small buffet of sub-standard appetizers including small salads and sweets which did not look appetizing. A poor bar selection couldn't find anything I wanted to drink. Had to seat and wait but temperature in the room was really high and I decided to leave and wait close to the gate instead. Hope Lufthansa will find a better options for their First and Business class customers as this does not match their high standards.

Munich First Class lounge is still one of Lufthansa's best. Very well appointed elegant and classy with great service. In the restaurant plenty of good choices both on buffet and a la carte menu. Extensive wines and spirit list. Large magazines and newspapers selection. In the spa I noticed a drop in the level of service they no longer provided bath salts and other toiletries but one generic shower gel to be used as bubble bath shampoo soap and everything else. Even the now famous Lufthansa rubber duck was not available at first and had to be requested. Wifi was not working and receptionist suggested me to use the general Munich Flufghafen wifi which was ok. Later on board their wifi was out too. At the time of boarding had to walk for more than 10 minutes to the gate while in Frankfurt they automatically offer to take you to plane by a limo. They need to maintain the same standard as in their Frankfurt lounges.
A very nice lounge great cocktail bar. Food was also good and a fair choice. Staff friendly. Close to the smoking room. Good size with lots of areas to relax in.

Staff are excellent very attentive and friendly. Kids enjoyed the special kids play area. We spent some time in the shower section. Identical with all FCL of LH but here just only one has jacuzzi. Enzo toiletries and have time to relax and refresh. Breakfast choice was ok but quality of some items (croissant pastries) could be better for this level of lounge. Drink choice was really huge and fine. Food that starts at 10.30 is outstanding. Several dishes on buffet but the real top is the a la carte restaurant. Finally via private car (a Merc mini van as we were 4 ) to the aircraft. In total really 5 star experience.

The lounge was busy and quite small and it is as with Terminal 1 ageing. There was still a very poor choice of food and beverages- only a poor quality English breakfast cereals and various hot and cold drinks were available. The lounge was quite comfortable with clean washrooms and good Wifi that worked well but the tables were quite dirty making for an average experience.

This is nice new lounge with ok food offerings good selection of beverages and newspapers/magazines. The free WIFI is not fast but works ok for e-mails.
