Very poor for a business lounge. The attendant was eager to get rid of us and told us 45 mins before the flight that the flight was boarding even though it didn't show as boarding on the screens. For the second half of our visit the night duty cleaning staff worked around us preparing for the morning rush!

There is no dedicated Priority Pass lounge at Narita airport. Priority Pass shares the Korean Airl business lounge. The customer representative at the front desk is courteous. Food selection is average. There is no cooked food. Just pastries biscuits nuts and a selection of cold and hot beverages. Beer is available. There is no dedicated toilet nor showers. Lounge is quite comfortable with TV and wifi access.

The Miracle Lounge is used by Malindo Air at Bangkok Don Muang Airport. One word. Shocking! Food was lousy. No charging points. Cheap feel and tacky feeling to the place. DMK is a nightmare. Avoid it at all costs.

Spent 8 hours in transit in this lounge. Lounge quite comfortably appointed however it could really use some more comfortable high back chairs. The shower suites were exceptionally nice (Emirates take note). Great tarmac views. Now the food. Small buffet offered and an à la carte menu, which at lunchtime was solely Asian inspired food. Would be good to have a European option available.

The Plaza Premium Lounge at Gate 1 was amazing to us (not operated by Vietnam Airlines, though its Business Class and Elite passengers were invited). It was lunch time and the lounge was not crowded, easy for us to find an empty table actually. Staff was friendly, quick, and helpful. Shower and massage were available but we did not use. The food, especially the beef noodle and the dessert bar were really worth to explore as the dishes were tasty!

Visited this lounge as I was a Skyteam Elite Plus. It was operated by Plaza Premium Lounge, not Vietnam Airlines. The lounge was shiny and bright, beautiful and elegant. Staff was friendly and helpful. Food selection was quite limited. No toilette or shower inside the lounge, which was quite shame!

The Plaza Premium lounge in Terminal 3 is a welcome oasis from the crowds in the concourses and gate areas. Simple decoration, very clean, nice ambience and very comfortable. The staff is very friendly. The food & drink selection consists of the usual sandwiches, snacks, juices, coffee and soft drinks and most importantly a hot buffet with 4 entrée selections including one vegetarian entrée. The chicken kabob skewers were excellent. more than adequate (cereals, sandwiches, juices, coffee and soft drinks). The lounge was busy but not overcrowded. The bathrooms were very clean and maintained frequently at regular intervals. Wi-Fi was very strong and fast.

Used this Plaza Premium lounge at T4 on a Sunday evening, and it is not fit for purpose. More customers than seats, the lounge was filthy, the toilets even worse. As a Business Class customer on China Southern I expected better than this, and it has to be one of the worst lounges I have ever visited. An absolute disgrace, Plaza Premium should be ashamed.

The lounge unfortunately must substitute the closed Star Alliance lounge on a SWISS flight. Obviously when paying everybody can enter this lounge, which is far too small. The place is looking very dated and overused, very poor choice of food, "hot" food lukewarm to cold. Soda drinks out of dispensers not chilled enough and lack of ice. Also guests have to pay for alcoholic beverages. Restrooms not very clean, unfriendly staff. I left this overcrowded place and went to eat something decent with a decent glass of wine outside.

Plaza Premium US Departures lounge. What's not to like about this brightly lit lounge with clean bathrooms and hot breakfast/hot lunch. The hot breakfast offered scrambled eggs, a selection of breads and other dairy products such as yogurt and fresh fruit. The hot lunch offered salads along with 2 other entrees (Asian style chicken and a pork entrée). The lounge was quite busy late mid-morning and just before lunch time. The WiFi was easy to connect too and fast. There is a bar in the middle that divides the two seating areas. Staff was very friendly and welcoming. I would not hesitate to use this lounge again the next time I fly through YVR.

A generic lounge used by numerous airlines and is also pay for use, so probably at peak hours it might get crowded. However this brand new lounge at Soekarno-Hatta Terminal 3 International Departures is definitely a huge improvement compared to the previous far smaller facility. Spacious, lots of seating, nice coffee bar, excellent bar service (though there isn’t a very wide range of alcoholic drinks) and decent food options. There is even a Spa for a quick massage before your flight (did not use it, but prices seemed to me reasonable). Spend some relaxing time and really enjoyed it.

This is my second visit within 5 months but the Lunch menu was same as before. I think they have a fix menu for everyday lunch. Although the food taste is good as authentic Indian food that is the positive thing there. Next month may be I visit this place again. I hope I will not find this Menu again.

New Plaza Premium lounge finally open at Clark Airport. This is a proper lounge. On the time of visit there were three main course meals available, a reasonable selection of wines, no spirits, soft drinks, and a damn good coffee machine. There is also a smoking area. What was outstanding about this lounge was the quality of the staff. Absolute sheer perfect service. Very friendly. Very professional. Very well presented and smart.

Use quite often this lounge as all Star Alliance Airlines do use it for their business class passengers and also Gold Members. It is quite basic but still good. There is bar area, where one can get coffee, beer and wine (haven't seen spirits) and a buffet area. It tends to get a little crowded (and hot) sometime, but behind the buffet area there still is more seating (where it is normally very quiet and cooler).

Plaza Premium lounge used on Westjet Airlines trip. Crowded pathetic and dirty washrooms, not impressive. 15 mins to gate 2a with no real directions. Closed at 8.30 luckily I followed other WestJet travellers who knew that 2a was in that direction. Food options were non existent when I arrived.

The lounge is relatively convenient with tables and decent wifi. However, the food selection is uninspiring and several of the trays remained empty despite having paid for the ‘diner package’. The $35 cost does not include alcohol and you have to request coffee or tea. The toilets, although clean, were not impressive. The most annoying aspect, however, was a near-constant barrage of loud conversations between lounge staff and other airport workers. As well as helping themselves to generous portions of food the staff seemed to wander in and out at random. This lounge is best avoided.

Travelling during COVID-19 you are accustomed to a skeleton airport operation, staring air closed shops while you wait for your next flight. My flight being scheduled past midnight I joyed to see an "OPEN" sign on the Plaza Premium Lounge. After checking with the staff member I learned that this is the only open lounge past midnight with operating hours from 23:00-08:00. Great! or was it? After a USD 64 cover charge I went straight to the buffet. The premium choice I had to make was between 4 cup noodles, a lonely salad in a 300ml plastic cup, and a tomato soup resemblance, in color only. Those were the sad leftovers at 23:38, so 38min after the lounge had opened with about 12-13 guests. Upon asking when the shelfs would be refilled, I was told that kitchen staff had already left. I should better hurry to grab myself a cup noodle, the gourmet choice for tonight.  I could have gotten a cup of coffee and some instant noodles from a vending machine for U$8. Here is what's advertised on the Plaza Premium website. "While we are open to serve you, your health and wellbeing is of paramount importance. Guided by our “We Care of Your Wellbeing” campaign, in-lounge meal service is modified to pre-portioned light refreshments and a range of beverages including coffee, tea and soft drinks." So in short don't bother, and lookout for that vending machine Price is Pre-COVID, service and food isn't.

The lounge interior is pretty nice, the lounge ambience is very relaxing. The staff are very accommodating. The place is jam packed but still quite and relaxing. It's a great place to wait for your flight! It's a new favorite hang out place for me here at the airport. Kudos to The whole team.

Great experience. The best barmen. Great staff. Pretty long list of free drinks and pretty good cold and hot food selection. Tried merhaba lounge above and this one is way better. My favorite place in Dubai airport from now.
Plaza Premium is a very good lounge at Dubai. Much better than the Maharba lounge upstairs. No screaming children and annoyances. Nice and quiet. Very good food and service. Most recommended.

Plaza Premium Lounge at Phnom Penh Airport. I was flying Air China, and so was invited to visit this lounge. This fairly large lounge was very inviting. I was welcomed with a traditional Cambodian greeting and pointed towards the seating areas. As my flight was just past midnight, it was very quiet too. Seating areas were good, with a variety of furnishings and several quiet sections. I particularly liked the semi private cubicles, which was ideal if you wanted to work with your laptop, although you couldn't stretch out or lie down on the seat. There are no views of aircraft or runway here. Food choice was good with a bakery section and an excellent noodle bar. The chef prepared a fish ball soup which was delicious. No self service bar, and the two barmen were friendly and served both alcohol and coffee. No premium alcoholic drinks here and for Cognac, you were served brandy. There was also a massage and beauty service, but you had to pay extra. WiFi was good too, with USB and charging points. Nice mood lighting and clean. Overall it was a very pleasant experience.

Been to other Plaza Premium lounges in KL and always walked away very satisfied. That was not the case this time. Having booked for 6 hours due to a long flight connection, the receptionist greeted me with a grudgy face and somewhat rude tone upon my checkin. The space is confortable with all amenities you need. With the food options, you must tell the cooks to ready one of the options available, which was done with a most fascinating sense unfriendliness. Only good behaviour was the lady in the bar serving draft beers. Upon checkout, another lady with an unexplainable passive-aggressive behaviour towards me. Felt disappointed and not rested, since most of the staff was so unprofessional. Definitely regretted the amount paid for this lounge.

I would like to take this opportunity to express my appreciation for the staff of Plaza Premium Lounge 7 who made my visit at Delhi, Terminal 3 on 21 Nov 2019, a comfortable and relaxing one. The service at reception provided by Mr. Lalit and at Bar by Mr Rawat was very welcoming. The food was delicious and I had the opportunity to compliment the Chef who was on his routine buffet check. The ambiance and hygiene was good; no wonder the Plaza was busy. Hope the Plaza Lounge continues to keep up the good work in making the journey of weary travelers, a relaxing and joyful experience.

This Plaza Premium Lounge in Rome used by Etihad Airways is one of the best lounges in Europe. On demand catering with a small buffet for snacks and breakfast pastries. The selection of drinks and food is amazing for a lounge at an European airport. A good variety of seating with an awesome view of the operating airport. Toilets are clean which for me is an essential evaluation for a lounge. This is definitely my preferred airport lounge in any European airport that I have visited.

The Plaza Premium Lounge is a contract lounge that anyone travelling can pay to enter and is also used by a number of airlines that don’t have their own lounges or use one of their partner airline lounges at the airport. I arrived around 8.30pm on a Saturday night and found the lounge to be crowded but still managed to find a seat which was great but overall I wasn’t overly impressed with the lounge it was nice enough but just lacking something special. On arrival I handed in my pass from the airline and was given a piece of paper back which I just put in my wallet and only later realized it was a coupon for free alcohol as not every guest is entitled to free alcohol which I didn’t end up using so make sure you keep a track of it if you are going to want a drink. They had a reasonable hot and cold food selection but my biggest issue with the lounge was the tiny glasses they use for soft drinks which you probably need more than a couple to get a decent serving. I didn’t use the wifi so can’t comment on it. Spent about two hours here and while it is pleasant enough it just didn’t have a wow factor.

The 3rd party lounge Malaysia Airlines uses in Phnom Penh, Plaza Premium, is nice but food and drink offered has deteriorated compared to 2 years ago when they opened: the so called Bakery is dead and is merely a museum, narrow range of drinks offering, noodle bar with industrialised ingredients only (e.g. fish-balls and meatballs, no unprocessed meat). Only plain Angkor beer and cheap wines. No champagne nor sparkling.

British Airways use the Plaza Premium Lounge at Rome, located on the first floor after past the security checks. The staff at the reception were friendly and cheerful. The main lounge room is spacious and warm at the same time. Different types of sofas and chairs, enjoy the view while drinking a glass of wine. There is a big selection of charcuterie and desserts the only small negative thing about this lounge is that you need to pay for a premium drink like a glass of scotch.

Praise to Malaysia Airlines for granting full access to this lounge for OW elite travelers. Plaza Premium Lounge in PNH is slowly but steadily falling apart in terms of food and drinks. It used to be very good when it opened 2 years ago (see my review 2017 where rated 9/10) but now remains only the nice design, good space and good views in two opposite directions. The rest is going down in the drain day by day: shrinking food options of poor quality, the big “bakery” is now closed. No champagne, only extremely modest wine offering. Only one local draft beer remains. Disastrous and poor management combined with extreme cost savings on commensurables. Shame on them and the management are full of empty promises but only cost savings are done - now only the bone is left.

I used this lounge as a customer of Qatar Airways, and the lounge is used by many airlines and can become very busy and crowded. The catering is school mealish in terms of quality and quantity. There is very limited alcohol provided, one can of Carlsberg in the fridge during my visit. The worst aspect of this lounge is the toilets. One cubicle in the male toilet was available and frequently ran out of toilet paper which angered many passengers. The toilets were filthy. If Qatar Airlines are to increase the flights to Penang, and as a 5 star airline, they should review their use of this lounge.

The lounge was an excellent experience. It was my first time visiting a lounge and had actually gone there to charge my phone. I decided to take advantage of my card which provided free lounge access. This was a good decision. All food and non-alcoholic beverages inside the lounge are complimentary.There is decent range to choose from in food. it was also calm and quiet and the displays were spread all over the place and it was easy to see when a flight was boarding.

Poorly designed Plaza Premium lounge with a terrible food offering. During the morning, they are offering a chicken sausage hot dog and scrambled egg?? There seems to be shortage of seats and I was generally disappointed. Compared to the London Heathrow Lounge, this lounge puts Plaza Premium lounges to shame. The looks to be about £30, which again is pricey for what is actually on offer.

As the Malaysia Airlines Lounge was being re-furbished, we tried the Plaza Premium Lounge. Checking in – Long Queue of 2 lines. One for regulars and others for pay as you enter. Our Priority Pass card was viewed as a “pay as you enter”. The long queue stretched some way into the corridor. It took quite a while for us to enter the Lounge. The Lounge was full. Some had to stand and eat at the same time. It took us a long time to find any seats.  There were quite a few people just sleeping on the chairs. The Food was like Malaysian street food which was good but there was shortage of various drinks. Some of the vending drinks machines were not working. This is probably due to the pressure of people in the lounge.

I reserved the lounge with miles from Avianca. It was a really great stay. I wasn't up to the dress code but I was admitted anyway. I used the shower and it was great, they gave you towels and everything you needed. Many options to eat.

The Plaza Premium lounge I have visited is near gate 40. My visit was around 9pm and a significant part of the lounge was reserved for Virgin Atlantic Upper class passengers. This massively reduced the seating space for other people using the lounge at the same time. This seems to happen from 8pm till around midnight. The lounge was crowded as a result of that. And the seats are not as comfortable as the one near gate 1. Hot food choices range from Chinese soup noodles, rice cakes, dumplings, spaghetti with tomato sauce, fried rice. It was alright. Others include butter and bread, cookies and some snacks. There were apple juice, beer, soy milk, milk, soft drinks. For food and beverages, it was no surprise but also not much disappointment either. Free wifi connects well.

Used this as a Singapore Airlines customer. The Brisbane Plaza Premium Lounge is Brisbane Airports only Pay per use lounge but is also accessible through Priority Pass and affiliates. The lounge is a nice size overlooks the main gate areas and is located on the upper level along with the Singapore Airlines and Air New Zealand lounges. The lounges is neat and tidy and not crowded. Food and beverage selection was good, with a major point of difference being that they offer Barista made coffee as opposed to the other lounges machines. So for Priority Pass members worth pooping into for a good coffee. I do not know what the policy is like for pay per use guest but it must be noted that Priority Pass members must pay for their Alcoholic Beverages.

It is interesting to note that there are 2 Plaza Premium lounges in Taipei Taoyuan Airport and they are just 1 minute of walk away from each other. The one i visited was the bigger one. The lounge was pretty big and empty, not much people, at around 8pm. To my surprise, there was the famous Taiwan-style beef noodles on order and it was quite good. Also, there were fried fish, steamed dumplings, rice bread and some others, pretty good. For drinks, there were also a selection of white wine and red wine, soy milk, milk, a selection of soft drinks, tea bags and juice. Overall, the food and beverage are very nice. The lounge has really nice spacious and comfy seating. And it is very clean and new. Compared to the plaza premium lounge in HKG, this one is much much better.

This lounge is the so-called ordinary lounge as many ordinary credit cards grant free access to this lounge so the food choice, the food itself are all ordinary. And this lounge is often full. This time i arrived at 6 am. Did not have much expectation for such an early visit. There were almost no hot food, just some bread, very bland fried noodles and ordinary rice cake. There were also a salad bar and cookies. The soup noodles with fish balls began serving at 6:30 am and there was a long queue for this as other food are really not attractive at all. There are plenty of drinks choice, almost all soft drinks you can name can be found. As a free lounge it is alright.

It's up on a plaza, not premium, not special. It's more like a retreat from the crowds below. It's toilets are well air conditioned, but it's roof is open to the hot terminal building. It's a help yourself to some nuts, cake and rice kind of lounge. As a first class traveler, or business class traveler you will be happy to escape inside here- but it's no 5 star event. Power for your laptops, not too crowded, a bit noisy from the terminal below.

One of the best independent lounges in Heathrow Terminal 4. Space was ample and seating was spread out, food was tasty and had a reasonable variety. The Karak tea offered at breakfast is great. Very high standards in terms of service and overall appearance of the lounge. I actually prefer using this lounge over other airline provided lounges when flying Business from Terminal 4, as I have access through it via Lounge Key Credit Card membership.

This isn't the nicest of lounges, used when flying with Qatar Airways. At check in we were directed to the Malaysian Airlines Golden Lounge, but when we got there they said Qatar business class had to use the Plaza Premium. This is a facility used by several airlines for Business class, but also by anyone who pays to access. It's a gloomy brown inside. We didn't try the small food buffet, and when we got a drink from the bar we had to show our boarding passes, otherwise the drinks were not free. The showers were closed off. Toilets were just OK. There are views over the apron, which I always appreciate.

I am terribly disappointed by this lounge. The lounge was crowded, noisy and not at all comfortable to relax. The food available was extremely bad, it was like an insult to the passengers. As if having a bad selection was not enough, many of the food trays were empty and was not refilled even after waiting for a while. I would never go back to this lounge.

I used this Plaza Premium Lounge in Phnom Penh (PNH) international airport as a customer with Malaysia Airlines. Was indecisive on choice of draught beers but ended up favouring Carlsberg. My third visit to this lounge and all three times have given me great pleasure for panorama views, service, spaciousness, facilities. Have accessed with Qatar Airways and this time with Malaysia Airlines. Purchased access is also possible though a bit pricy (39 USD/2 hours). A true first class lounge lifted one floor up over the terminal area but open to the terminal providing a good airflow and feeling of lots of space. Loads of good foods, there is even a Bakery! Massage and Spa sections. Fitness, showers, private rooms. View to town on one side and to airbridges on the other. No champagne or sparkling wine. Canned beers have been removed.

Qatar Airways use the Plaza Premium Lounge in Phnom Penh (PNH) international airport. A really good lounge, spacious, view to tamarc on one side and town on the other. 3rd party lounge that most airlines uses. Also, access with PP or pay 39USD/2 hours. Loads of local hot foods, a bakery, massage, fitness, showers. No champagne, 2 wines, international and local draft and canned beers. Good internet, staff very attentive.

The Plaza Premium lounge at London Heathrow Terminal 2 is fantastic. Lovely food, lots of choice, hot and cold. Ample choice of drinks hot or cold. Plenty of comfortable seats, or tables and chairs for eating at. Newspapers to read. Staff helpful. Well stocked bar. Toilet and shower facilities were very good.

A plastic piece in the pastries, black hair in the roti, and a ridiculously complex process to get on the WiFi. Complain to the supervisor who makes a phone call and says the duty manager is on the way and then says he is actually also the duty manager. If this place was in Europe it would fail food hygiene standards and be shut down, while the manager would be locked up for being delusional. This and the poor experience at Hyderabad airport generally does not leave travellers with a good final impression of the city.

The Plaza Premium lounge was busy when I arrived on 5 Mar. It took me sometime to locate an available seat. The food selection was decent and lots of staff on hand to clear up after guests have left. There were limited shower rooms but I was fortunate to get access to one quite quickly for a nice hot shower. Quality towels, shampoo, conditioner, etc, supplied.

Plaza Premium operates four lounges at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (and the company has other concessions at the airport). You can use Priority Pass at all of them. There's one at the satellite terminal at KLIA that is also used as a third-party lounge by several full-service airlines. Frankly I'd be very disappointed if I was travelling in business class with a full service airlines and they dumped me in there as the F&B at none of the Plaza Premium lounges in Kuala Lumpur are up to the levels that you expect from an airline lounge. However, this review is about the three lounges at KLIA2 or the LCCT as Air Asia calls it. If you're travelling on a domestic flight then you have no choice but to use the land-side lounge in the shopping centre that lies in front of the check-in area. There's no lounge in the domestic departures area at all. This isn't a problem as the domestic security check is generally quick but the lounge is a minimum of 20 minutes walk to your domestic gate so you'd really have to leave it about an hour before your departure time. The lounge isn't big but it's new and clean and there's a small selection of breakfast food including scrambled eggs and chicken frankfurters as well as local food and some pastries in the morning. Self service coffee machine and drinks including beer in the fridge. They used to forget to check your boarding pass at this lounge but now they do so you can't just turn up for a free meal and beer if you've got a Priority Pass any more. In the international departures area there are two lounges. The first in pier L is after the second security check so you're in luck if your flight departs from this pier because you can get to your gate in literally a few minutes walk with no additional security check. It also opens earlier than the other one at 4am which makes no sense at all because early morning flights can leave from any pier but this lounge, behind security, only serves pier L. It's a small lounge but has sandwiches, noodles, hotdogs and pots of salad in the fridge. The other lounge is in the shopping area between the remaining piers where most of the flights leave. It's the best Plaza Premium lounge in KLIA but sits before security for the two piers it serves and consequently you need to leave 30-40 minutes before your departure time to get your flight. It also inexplicably opens later than the other lounge at 7am. This makes is useless for the many early morning flights departing from the majority of the gates on the other two piers. I don't know why they don't have this one open at 4am for all KLIA2 flights and keep the lounge at L closed. Anyway, like the other Plaza Premium lounges in KLIA this one is clean and modern. It has a massage centre for additional cost and showers. The lounge has a view of the runway. There's always a few hot dishes and some noodle soup along with pasta and salads in the fridge. Soft drinks and beer are self service in the fridge. The Plaza Premium lounges in KLIA are fine for third-party lounges but the company operates better lounges with better F&B elsewhere at Macau and Phnom Penh for example. I would be very unhappy if my full-service airline put me in them compared to the third-party lounges in, say, Singapore airport like the DNATA or even in Bangkok.

There are two Plaza Premium lounges in Kota Kinabalu Airport. One in the international departure hall and one in the domestic departure hall. Both take Priority Pass. I visited the domestic one twice while changing Air Asia flights to Sandakan one weekend. It's easy enough to find directly on the departures floor and gives a good first impression. Clean and modern with a large food bar in front of you and plenty of seating to the right. Soft drinks are in the fridge directly in front of you. What they don't tell you is that you can ask for beer from the chef behind the counter and he'll happily bring it to you. We missed this first time and only knew about it second time because we saw somebody else asking for it. Food selection was fine and only fine. Given that there were only about five people in the lounge I don't suppose it makes sense for them to have a large selection of food that would have to be disposed of every day. The chef will make noodle soup for you. There was a chicken curry. A rudimentary but fresh salad bar. Peanuts. Cake. If you want a coffee of any sort then you have to ask for it because it's made with a professional machine (rather than a self-service automatic coffee machine). There's a shower available too but we didn't use it. It's nice to find Plaza Premium lounges that take Priority Pass in smaller airports like Kota Kinabalu and I hope that it gets enough business to stay open. It was up to the usual Plaza Premium standard found in, say, KLIA2 but not as feature rich as, say, Macau or Phnom Penh.

I have visited many lounges across the world, and for Europe, I have to say that this Heathrow Plaza Premium lounge at Terminal 4 is one of the best lounges out there. There are various seating areas for dining, relaxing, sofas, private working desks. The food quality and variety was excellent. The reception team, and the service team there were all professional and friendly.

Visited the Premium Plaza lounge in Terminal 3 domestic departures. The lounge was so bad that they should remove both lounge and premium from their name. Lounge was overcrowded with option to have water, tea or coffee. Couple of Indian snacks were available, rest everything was for an additional charge. Even can of coke was chargeable with prices being double that of other restaurants in the airport. There was Wifi, again chargeable even when Delhi airport itself provides free wifi for 30 minutes. I think I wasted my priority pass visit.

Is used Hyderabad Plaza Premium lounge as a Malaysia Airlines passenger, and the lounge seems big - or there were few passengers at the time of day when I visited (around midnight). The food section is ok, but uninspiring with limited choice, dried out sandwiches etc. There are showers to use, but the fittings and the ambience leaves quite a lot to be desired. Overall the lounge is nice, but the details need to be looked after.

Visited Plaza lounge at London Heathrow T2 prior to my long haul flight. As a Priority Pass member I didn't have a high expectation on the lounge but it turned out to be great. The lounge is new and clean. It has a very relaxing and oriental ambience. When I visited it (after 7pm) the lounge was not busy and it was very calm. Plenty of food and drink (including beer, spirits, wines) available and champagne for purchase. Service in the lounge was also great. Very attentive. Plates were collected once the food was finished. Staff walked around regularly. Overall a great lounge - better than the BA flagship lounge in T5.

The Plaza Premium lounge at Vancouver Airport was really busy. Difficult to get seat. Had to queue for drinks and food. An excellent choice of Asian cuisine. Constant cleaning inside the lounge by staff

Nothing much to say except it was good. Not a huge space (I think the company took whatever space the airport had available) but adequate. We were in on our Diner's Club cards but a lot of other pax on our Sunwing flight had bought passes. Hopefully they will expand as the previous lounge exclusivity is becoming the hangout of the great unwashed masses and it's getting crowded. The desk chap certainly was not enforcing the published dress code. However recommended no matter how you get in and it is a good respite before a charter holiday flight.
The Premium Plaza near gate 40 was an oasis. The food was decent. Offered showers computers newspapers comfortable seating clean screen for checking flights. The staff was friendly and polite.

This lounge is starting to become popular so fewer and fewer seats available. Staff very gracious in welcoming you. There is a fairly good selection of food available type depending on the time of day. Nice to have an espresso machine. Staff circulate removing used dishes and glasses. Only complaint is that there is only Toronto daily newspapers Westjet inflight magazine (and they don't use that terminal) and commercial magazines promoting condos for sale in Toronto.

The lounge was nice and being very early in the morning only a few sleepy travellers. We suggest the inclusion of recliners instead of just armchairs. Also the there was some litter on the tables which staff didn't clean at all even though there were only 2 passengers in there when we arrived. Some of the food was tasty but the boiled eggs looked like they'd been boiled for a couple of hours and left out. Not many varieties of food but we still happy at what was on offer. Good selection of chilled drinks. There's also a hot beverage machine. Internet was fast. Washroom was clean. Pretty much sound proofed from the very busy terminal.

The lounge is located past security beside the duty free store and is well signed. Relatively spacious and comfortable seating with views of the runway. Staff were friendly and the lounge was clean and tidy. Washrooms were clean however there are no shower facilities. Food was limited to snacks and drinks. An average selection with nothing very impressive or notable. A quiet place to relax before the flight.

First time using Mabuhay Lounge at Terminal 1, and this is a huge improvement from the previous lounges offered by Philippine Airlines to its passengers. Spacious, wide variety of food, bar and with showers. It has premium feel to it. Excellent view of the aircraft while sipping cocktails.

Philippine Airlines have just moved International flights to Terminal 1 Manila in July 2023. They no longer have their own lounges and use 3rd party lounges on our forward journey - the lounge had limited western food available [plenty of options for Asian palette] and no showers. The return lounge today at least has showers but no hot water or hairdryers, but the only food that looked appetizing were the tubs of ice cream. The seating all needs to be thrown away and start again. No comfortable seats with leg rests to stretch out.  I think the cleanliness needs reviewing also. They are catering to an international clientele, so please cater to non Asian palettes, or at least some less spicy options. We have been in lounge for several hours now, and pleased to see a good rotation of food being replaced after so many hours with fresh items. No quiet zones, so many people talking loudly using earbuds. This particular lounge is quite small compared to others, so hard to stretch out and relax. Reception girls on reception very pleasant. Bar, apart from some wine, nothing else on offer [no beer or spirits]

The Mabuhay Lounge has constantly increased its quality of food and service over the last couple years. Chef Ramos was present in the lounge area assisting people with that huge smile of his. Food was restaurant quality - fine dining. Thanks for the very tasty meals! Service was also outstanding as well as a new large screen tv in the area. Great improvements.

PAGSS lounge got better. This is beside Gate 7. Food was good, and alcoholic drinks is overflowing. It was clean, and a monitor is accessible to see if your flight has changed gates or if it is boarding. But the receptionist will move around to advice the passengers. You can also pay to have access to this lounge, which I will be doing next visit since my frequent flyer with PAL, I might not be entitled for a free pass. Overall, this is a respite for food, and I hope that they will provide a smoking area in this lounge. Since smoking is not allowed anymore in all the three terminals of NAIA. How sad and unfortunate indeed - which gets minus 2 points on my overall rating.

Mabuhay Lounge is really trying to offer a nice selection of food items. The people that work in the Lounge are awesome! The lounge is very clean including the restroom. Its a little congested at times, but other than that I think it's a nice place to relax before a flight. Thank you, Mabuhay Lounge!

PAGGS Lounge (beside Gate no. 7) - PAL Frequent Flyer Mabuhay Miles - Elite Level. My first time on this lounge. I used to go to the paid lounge at this Terminal at the other end. Plenty of food choices, overflowing coffee - Nespresso (I think), alcoholic beverages. The gentleman at the bar was so accommodating, once when the lounge was full he got a bar stool and asked mo sit in front of the bar. I lounged there for three hours. Toilet was clean and smelling fresh. Wifi is available, just ask the password from any of the staff.

We visited the Philippines Airline Mabuhay Lounge in Terminal 2 of NAIA Airport, I was totally underwhelmed by this lounge. The food was tasty, specifically the asian selections. The dim sum was fresh in steamers and there was 2 selection of made to order hot noodle dishes from the noodle bar. There was a decent selection of beers, wines and liquors at the serve yourself bar. The mens bathroom was old and in need of an upgrade, but the bathroom attendant kept it very clean and tidy. The seats in the dining area were alright, but the seats in the kind of relaxation/TV room were uncomfortable. There was no place to kick back and relax in.  During the 4 hours there, I seen staff stocking the food counters and beverage coolers, but not once did I see tables being cleared in the dining room or service items being picked up in the TV room. The floor were filthy. Although it was better then sitting in the general waiting area of the airport (just barely), this lounge was no place to have to spend over 4 hours in. I’m sure this lounge does not reflect PAL’s tag line, “The heart of the Filipino”.

Great selection of food and drinks - I love the choc cookies. The lounge staff in the dining are very courteous and hardworking. In my own opinion the arrangement of dining tables can be improved and not crowded. Need more comfortable chairs. WIFi isn't bad.

I was super happy with the Mabuhay Lounge in Manila at NAIA. There were some great changes in food selection! I was pleased and super satisfied with the type of food and differing items. The Mabuhay lounge staff were also excellent - friendly and accommodating.

Poor food and beverage selection at the Mabuhay Miles Lounge. Not a service expected from a 4 star airline. PAL must upgrade this lounge in order to be at par with the services offered by other airlines.

The Philippine Airlines Mabuhay Lounge in Manila has had improvements over the last couple of years since I had been using it for my flights. And while it is quite spacious, I often find myself without a chair to sit on especially on days when flights are delayed and members across several flights are all crowding in the lounge. Thankfully the buffet table is always well stocked (albeit with limited selections) due to its tireless staff who seem quite efficient at their jobs. One surprising fact I noticed since I last checked is the WIFI speed now available at the lounge which now seems to be of decent speed compared to how it was just last year. Only thing missing for this place to be world class is to have renovated toilets, the current facilities are just tiny and smelly.

As a frequent flyer to Singapore this past year I have been fortunate enough to avail of the lounges facilities on multiple occasions. The food selection was getting to be monotonous with the menu unchanged for a while. So it came as a pleasant surprise when they had new dishes themed for the Chinese New Year Holiday. Congratulations to the Chef and management of the lounge for this exciting change. I hope they do these special dishes for each of the major holiday seasons.

The Mabuhay Lounge was easy to find. I checked in and the receptionists were very efficient and polite. They have a very good selection of food and beverages to choose from. Seats are okay, nothing to brag about. They have WiFi connection. Overall, I would give their Lounge a 4 out of 5.

Club Manila Lounge, NAIA Terminal 1. You can only stay here for 4 hours before your flight. It has a variety of food choices. coffee, Alcohol and Beer is available. Just request one of the staff available there. Toilet is clean and there is a place where you can take a bath. Smoking area is on the next room, and the airconditioning is cold. (Unlike NAIA Terminal 2, where the smoking area is at the far end of the building and outside). Wifi is available and quite fast. Staff are courteous. Add-on: no tipping as the sign on the frontdesk says. (but i wanted to tip for best service) All in all, I miss these pay lounges and where I can sit and relax before I leave and makes travelling less stressful.

Considering that Manila is the main hub of PAL, the Business lounge was disappointing. There is only one shower, for which you have to wait in turn, and the lounge is too small to accommodate the volume of passengers at times. The food on offer is very uninspiring. Bar service is friendly but inefficient, as when I asked for a White Wine, the barman attempted to refill my empty Scotch glass with wine, instead of providing a fresh glass. When using the toilet, I observed a Lounge employee use the toilet, then walk out without washing his hands, and as he was a food and beverage attendant, I found this alarming.

Currently writing this review at the Mabuhay Domestic Lounge while waiting for my domestic flight. The lounge is hidden at the second floor (gates are at the third) with an access lift from a small recess. Signage to the lounge is rather poor and it would be rather difficult to find for a first timer in the domestic terminal of PR. Greeted at the reception by warm and friendly personnel. Pretty sizeable number of patrons this late afternoon/early evening but managed to find a table. Food selection is pretty similar to the international counterpart next door with the excellent arroz caldo (rice porridge/congee with a Spanish-Filipino twist) and pretty fresh selection of fruits. Drinks are more limited but with alcohol options, including Asahi beer (canned, though). Pretty decent wifi speed (5-6Mbps) for Philippine standards and tables are cleared out quite quickly by the attentive staff. Lighting is much brighter than the international lounge and thereby, the place exudes a cheerier atmosphere along with a small window facing the tarmac which allows for plane spotting. There ARE boarding announcements and these are quite clear, if not a tad loud. Overall, a pretty good lounge.

An improvement compared to a couple of years ago. Still small compared to other lounges but could not complain as the food choices were good. Wifi was great. Service was impeccable. If there's one thing I can complain, that is the pretty noisy announcements made when it's time for boarding or when a flight is delayed. Overall, a good lounge.

First time in the Mabuhay Lounge of the North Wing of T2. Aside from the strange location which offers no vistas of the tarmac, the lounge is pretty well kept. Respectable food and drinks selection is available but I can see how seating can be an issue in this small lounge. Access can be obtained by ticket (J class), status (Mabuhay Miles Silver, Gold and Million Milers - with the latter 2 allowed to bring in 2 guests) and co-branded credit cards. Add that to the limited space and you can have a possible marketplace situation. Even the supposed relaxation area of the lounge turned into some sort of rave party. Add to the fact that this area is adjacent to the service area and for a while (until their attention was called), was unacceptably unruly. Still, it's better than waiting in the uncomfortable steel seating outside or browsing through the overpriced "duty free" section. The toilet was terribly small, not that well kept and had this strange odour emanating from it, even at 6AM. I'm on the fence of this one, just to say that it is passable but I've been to better (and to worse).

The domestic Philippine Airlines Mabuhay lounge at Terminal 2 has been renovated in recent years. The lounge offers very basic meal offerings. Several types of sandwiches, rice soup, cookies, bread/buns, and a very small fresh fruit plate. The drink offerings consist of a fridge in the corner containing of canned sodas, a few cans of local and imported beer and canned fruit juices. There is also a large dispenser of bottled water plus coffee and tea available. The lounge gets fairly busy in the morning, it offers free wifi and a small clean bathroom. The lounge is basic and could improve with better food offerings compared to other domestic lounges around the World, but currently it is a simple basic lounge that allows the traveller to relax in relative comfort and enjoy a bite to eat before your flight.

At terminal 2, it's located near gate 8/9, Mabuhay lounge is well appointed and a peaceful place to sit and wait for one's flight. Given that the airport in general has terrible and insufficient air-conditioning, It's really cool here. Food offering is reasonable, with enough hot and cold choices. Great elections of drinks and alcohol too. Free wifi very good. Lots of seating and power outlets. For a 3 star airlines, they tried their best, and I think they've done quite well with it. Staff were courteous and helpful too.

The lounge interior and ambiance look new and refreshing, with dining area in the middle and lounge area on both sides. It has just one shower room with amenities although I had to ask for a toothbrush.  Food on offer ranges from arroz caldo, dumplings, pastries and fruits. The staff are polite and seemed eager to help. A good place to relax.

Philippine Airlines has no business class lounge in BKK and makes use of Thai's Royal Silk Lounge. The lounge has a tired feel to it with the upholstery of the furnishings worn out cracks in the walls and tiles in the toilets and rather dirty carpets. Food was edible enough with a healthy selection of drinks. In the absence of good places to hang out in BKK while waiting for a flight this lounge would do but am sure they can do better. Not the best I've been in but not the worst.

Food very poor - not catering for western customers could only eat scrambled eggs.No croissants or other edible bread Filipino bread tends to be limited to relatively sweet rolls. No bottled mineral water only purified water from a dispenser. They seem to cater for Filipinos. Urinals in toilets were smelly.

For such a lounge it's definitely substandard. What I have not found in previous comments/reviews is the washrooms (there are no showers as noted by others) which are tiny! These which are supposed to handle multiple persons are barely larger than those on the aircraft and have a total of two sit type toilets and inadequate room for those waiting or those wishing to wash hands etc. after use.
Minimal service and a decor that could generously be described as "dated". Food and beverage service was also minimal and it is disappointing especially in a country so strong in the service sector.

For a business class lounge Manila is definitely sub-standard. Some staff are friendly and helpful others less so. Food and beverage are average. Manila however lacks one of the basic necessities namely showers. The lounge is in urgent need of an upgrade.

Apart from the friendly greeting when entering this lounge there is nothing good to report. The food was very basic and not that fresh. Coffee lukewarm. Service staff indifferent. Furniture in need of an upgrade facilities basic. It would not take a huge investment to make improvement to this facility

This is one of the most "bland" looking airline lounge that is in strong need of a major overhaul. Despite this staff were friendly and there was enough food and beverages for travellers. There are no windows and with minimal entertainment despite an occasional DVD played on the big plasma television. Philippine Airlines really need to overhaul and improve their premium services in order to remain competitive.

The lounge was clean and a variety of food and drink. We went there at the morning so they served breakfast for Myanmar and Western Style Breakfast. The lounge is located at the Terminal 3 of Yangon International Airport and at the 3rd Floor.

At check-in at Terminal 1, I was given a card map indicating the location of the lounge, but it was hard to find. I had to ask several people for directions and was then led to a private transfer by a BMW to the satellite terminal (where my flight was). Inquiring for further directions, I finally managed to locate the lounge tucked away at the far end of the mezzanine floor, or somewhere around there (not sure). At the gleaming entrance, I was warmly greeted, which immediately helped me forget the 'journey' that got me here. This is a large open-spaced lounge, with plenty of comfy sofas, high chairs and dining seating areas. On one side is an excellent view of the apron. The lounge has all the facilities one may wish to indulge in - showers, private nap rooms, family room with a children's play area, prayer room and a smoking room. It was not crowded, which added to the quiet ambiance. There was a fair variety of dining options - both Asian and International cuisine. At the noodle station, a chef would prepare a soup bowl to your liking. There was also a good selection of desserts and finger food. The Grilled Salmon and Chicken with Noodles I had was delicious. There was also a lot of staff who made me feel welcome and were constantly busy clearing up and offering to serve coffee to my couch by the apron. One item to note is that alcohol is not served in the main lounge. But just at the entrance was a bar where I was able to have a coffee and cognac before heading for my boarding gate. Overall, it was a very pleasant and restful experience.

Not a great Experience! 1st ever visit - maybe the last! Food was abysmal. Beef was chewy in Hot Dish and Chicken was tough and cold in the Curry with Potato. Young Children running around everywhere getting under your feet. Service Staff were not very friendly. To be honest it felt very much like a low cost carrier lounge. Not a great experience and hope I not go there again.

In itself the lounge is not too bad - spacious, with reasonable tear and wear, and in terms of food offer it is on the verge of reasonable and mediocre. its three sad aspects are that (1) it is severely and unevenly air-conditioned (something not very unusual in tropical climates), (2) its staff absolutely hates their job and everyone, starting from the receptionist is eager to share this attitude, and (3) it is the best kept secret of KLIA and Malaysia Airlines - I am here for the fourth time, I remember where more or less it should be, yet it takes at least 30 min of circling around, as any navigation is absent or confusing, and it is not visible from the passenger hall level. Now, when the airport is under renovation, it became even worse.

Last week, I checked in at the check in counter in Kuala Lumpur international airport for my flight to Melbourne. Being a senior citizen, I requested the personnel at the counter to help me gain entry to the Golden Lounge, using my frequent flyer Enrich reward points. I have plenty of Enrich points which I hardly use. To my surprise, I was told that Malaysia Airlines was a separate entity from the Enrich frequent flyer programme and that they could not help. Why isn't Malaysia Airlines aligned with its Enrich frequent flyer programme in its system. It is so inconvenient, especially for senior citizen to to get into the Golden Lounge without the help of personnel at the Malaysia Airlines check in counters. I am very disappointed.

It's a big lounge. At around noon, it's quite empty, However, it is inadequately staffed. The chef for the noodle station were no where to be seen, I had to signal the cleaner to go looking for her. I also noticed most staff are busy playing with their cell phones, almost totally ignoring their guests. This can only be attributed to poor management of MH. The 4 food offerings were just a beef curry, potato chickpea masala, a tomato based pasta and a veggie fried rice. A sign that the airlines is struggling to survive by going on a strict budget. It might be a while before MH can go back to its glory days.

Their Platinum lounge is tired old, stuck in the 1980s and stale (like the bread rolls). Having been a frequent flyer with MH for a decade I would think that the 2 years of the pandemic would have been a perfect breathing space to revitalise the Platnium (and also the golden) lounge product. One World has some excellent lounges at the emerald level - Cathay’s Home lounges in HK, Qatars lounges in Doha and QANTAS lounges in Sydney. The decor of the lounge while dated is still warm. The failings are on service and food/beverage offerings. In the mornings the bread product should be fresh and the cereal offerings should be more than cornflakes or coco pops. In all honesty the a golden Wing lounge has far superior choices - there you have a coffee machine with a barista - plentiful selection of fresh food All in all I have to say marketing 101 philosophy is your premium customers fly with you say 70x a year or more. They have One World flexibility. Why chose MH when the lounge reflects a sort of apathy towards the upper echelon frequent flyers?
Very disappointed. Cold food and only 2 choices and only 3 drinks available. Also tasteless and boring. Outside food much better and cheaper. Very disappointed.

Front entrance staff were great, very pleasant and polite, but can't really say the same for staff inside the lounge. Often felt like we lounge guests were being nuisances and interrupting their conversations about the guests themselves. Even taking food from the buffet feels awkward. Too many flies in the lounge as well.

Malaysia Airlines has its Golden Lounge in the domestic terminal of KLIA. The lounge receives the same design treatment as the Golden Lounge in the satellite terminal. There are lots of seats with ample of power points available for passengers. There is a children play corner and Muslim prayer rooms in the lounge. I arrived Kuala Lumpur around 8am in the morning and I am so thrilled to find out they serve the signature Malaysian dish - nasi lemak in the lounge. They also have Ipoh Hor Fun which is made-to-order. For a domestic lounge, it has a beautiful view of Malaysia Airlines aircrafts. The choice of food may be limited, mostly Malaysian cuisine (but when you are in Malaysia, why would you go for other cuisine?) Overall, nice ambience, good place to recharge and get ready for my next flight.

At peak periods seating capacity is tight. There is a counter with a reasonable range of made-to-order hot food options, as well as various snack and dessert items from the buffet. The taste of the food items is average, but the portions generous. No shortage of beverage choices, but it's a dry lounge, and the coffee machine was broken when I visited and the filter coffee from the pot was tasteless and weak. Still not as weak as the wifi connection though. Not a lounge to arrive early for.

Nice view of the tarmac from this Regional Golden Lounge, but can get busy during evening peak. The buffet is modest, with dessert options especially limited, even though the food is tasty and there is a noodle bar. I especially like that the lounge has 4-5 different seating areas with distinct styles, so you can dine in one place, grab a drink in another, then watch the tarmac from a third. Lounge has a shower, but didn't look too clean when I visited. The bathroom cubicles come with their own washbasins and counter surfaces so you can actually organise your stuff in there, which is a nice touch.

As a place to chill out before a flight, this place is a great choice. It is spacious, airy, and elegant. I found a reclining chair tucked away in the corner, and spent 1.5 hours there. There is a good selection of snacks, pastries, and beverages, even though the hot food selection is very compromised. I forwent lunch, grabbing only a few slices of cake/some local biscuits, in favour of 4pm airline mush. The staff are courteous, professional, and disposed to going the extra mile to help you feel comfortable. The person who checked me in remembered my flight, and came well ahead of time to remind me to head out. Also, they have a tea tasting station, even if really you should have done your tea-tasting in the city itself!

Overall, the lounge was pretty decent and comfort overall. The lounge is quite empty during my visit in the morning session. The food was well prepared and mostly served with local delights. The food quality was very good. There was a good automated coffee machine to serve a very good coffee too. There also having a private corner for you to rest with a massage chair. However, the lounge isnt enough outdoor sunlight to cheer you up before the flight and without any view facing out the glass window.

The lounge is one of the most spacious lounges I have ever visited. There are lots of wide seats and open area. There is even a genuine bar where one can relax and socialize. Although the food selection is limited and staff could be more attentive and welcoming, I would still give it a 5 star!

It’s really bad. My worst experience with the lounge. The food for the buffet was terrible. All the shower room close only 2 availed for shower. I’ve been waiting for half an hour and finally I leave without shower. When I go out ask the form for complain and the stuff have no pen for me - the only good things was my friend didn’t pay RM250 to go inside with me.

Nice, quiet and spacious lounge with plenty of seats. They offer hot and cold dishes, plenty of drinks to choose from. I was very impressed at first, then I went to use the shower. Everything was nice and clean. I had a shower and changed into new clothes. A cleaner showed up and saw that I was pleased with the facility, which I was - until he started asking me for tip. The exact words he used were "can you give me a tip?" I told him I had no local money. He replied "any money is ok" or something like that. That really put me off as it made me feel that the service was not really genuine, that they seemed nice was because they were expecting me to give them a tip. I have been to many lounges but never been pressured to tip someone. I have no problem tipping people but I want to do it if and when I feel like it and not when someone was blocking my way out. I contacted the airline about this and they said that they had talked to the cleaner. All the cleaner did was trying to help me with the towel according to the manager. They claimed it was a misunderstanding due to some sort of language barrier. I wrote back and asked what part of "can you give me a tip?" was it that meant he wanted to help me with the towel. They haven't got back to me yet. Don't think they will.

One of the best lounges I have used. Very calm and relaxed ambience. A quiet and peaceful lounge with a comfortable smoking room. Staff attentive and helpful. Restaurant options a little limited but quite acceptable. Lots of high quality seating available. Great food and drink selection. Free wifi. Server was down at first but after pointing out the problems I was having logging on manager at the business centre made few calls and had the server re-booted. Empty dishes and tables cleaned frequently. Shower and restroom facilities spotless. Lounge would be perfect if they had a separate "rest area" with lounge chairs and mobile phone restrictions.

All the three newly renovated Malaysia Airlines Golden Lounges in Kuala Lumpur Int'l Airport are fabulous! The two in Satellite Terminal reopened 1 March this year and the one in the Regional Terminal was renovated in October 2017. Spacious, thematic sections, sports bar, nap rooms, showers, smoking rooms etc. Staff very sociable and welcoming. Good food and drinks. Amazing come-back for MH and KLIA.

It is a well-designed lounge but needs updating. A refurbishment could be due as the main Golden Lounge in Kuala Lumpur (KLIA) is being re-furbished or re-modelled. It is the same type of food on display that I have been seen in previous visits. Perhaps they should increase the variety.

Flown from Kuala Lumpur to Medan on business class so had the opportunity to be invited to the lounge. Very good quality lounge although some food could be awful for my taste. Laksa curry which was supposed to be good turned out bland and disappointing. I didn't think I see any shower. Overall service is good and more than average.

Travelling as a couple we both felt comfortable and welcome in this lounge. Two visits in transit from Singapore to Tokyo and return. Firstly at around 8.00am when the lounge was about 60% full and secondly at around 5.00pm when it was well under half full. On both occasions the welcome was sincere and not robotic and all staff we interacted with were pleasant and helpful. The breakfast selection was satisfactory but on our second visit the evening food offerings were excellent in both choice and freshness. My partner does not drink and all I required was a beer so the small bar area met our needs. Great views of the aircraft and as you enter the lounge immediately to the left after the bar is a smaller area with a few amazing lounge chairs - the pick of the seating areas! If it were not for an ordinary toilet area the score would have been 10 (we did not use the showers). In a trip that involved the QF lounge in Sydney, Premium Plaza in Singapore and JL Sakura lounge in Narita (see other reviews) this was our favourite.

Sad to say that this lounge has seen better days. It is still quite comfortable and affords great views over the airport and runway. However the showers are certainly not very good, I wouldn't use them when I was there, shabby and not very clean. The toilets were the same. The food was just about passable but unfortunately no fresh coffee, just coffee vending machines. Plenty of news papers and magazines. The bar is on the left hand side as you enter but it in my opinion was not the type of place one would take their wife/partner. No comfy chairs just a few tables and hard seats. The staff did try to keep the lounge tidy but I suspect that there was not enough of them to keep on top of things. It all looks like MH is cutting back on everything.  They used to be quite good especially when they had their first A380's but now they are trying to off load even them (they too need a refit). Next time it's going to be Singapore Airlines and then back up to KL.

Based on business class ticket with KLM I had access to this Malaysia Airlines business class lounge although I'm emerald one world. The lounge is very spacious and you can eat and drink although the quality is comparing with other lounges, so so. As diabetic I don't use natural sugar but sweetener in my coffee. I ordered a coffee latte and asked for sweetener. They don't have! Only natural sugar. I asked why not? It's because of cost reduction. I went to the desk and I asked again why no sweetener. I received an other answer: out of stock. I know from my visits before that they don't have it at all. So this manager was lying! Of course it's not a world problem if there is no sweetener but the way how they answer and that they don't organise the sweetener, tells enough about their service. It's the only lounge at a sophisticated airport where you cannot get sweetener I guess. I don't feel happy in this lounge anymore. When people lying there is something wrong with the management.

MAS Golden Lounge First Class was anything but first. Arrived late at 1am and decided to use the nap room to wait until the next morning for my flight to SIN. This is the only positive part of the whole experience, that MAS First has a nap room. (it was spartan and needed a facelift but at least there was one) Lounge was empty when I was there. There was a sole attendant that firstly, questioned if I was eligible for a nap room and then begrudgingly provided the keys to one. No offer of a beverage, etc. He then proceeds to sit right next to the buffet with kitchen hand and chat noisily whilst picking at the food from the buffet with his bare hands! Took a shower in a shared washroom. No shower attendant, some shower stalls had no amenities, overall clean condition but also needs a facelift. Nap room was fine, and slept for about 3 hours. This is where the experience goes from below average to downright terrible. Woke up at 6am, no attendants in sight. Hunt one down to return the keys and get my boarding pass. Expressionless and zero hospitality from the attendant. Was curtly told, 'Wait here.' and then subsequently, 'Here you go.' Sat in the first dining room for breakfast for 10 minutes, attendants were noisily chatting in the backroom, two other guests come and sit down as well, ZERO service, not a waitstaff in sight. No offer of drinks, menu. Dining room has 3 tables seated but no service staff. After 10 minutes decide that this is ridiculous and complain to front desk. No response from front desk other than a shrug of the shoulders. Decide to go into the business section of the lounge which had a breakfast and noodle station. Fresh coffee made by friendly barista. Definitely leaps and bounds compared to their first lounge. MAS, if you can't be bothered with a first lounge, just shut it down and focus on doing the business lounge better. Absolute disgrace.

The Golden Lounge in the satellite terminal at KLIA is great, plenty of space good seating areas and lots of different food options, We always go when we have a long connection on our outbound and on inbound flights. Plenty of staff clearing food dishes and replenishing the trays. Both Malaysian and western meal options, I had a great chicken chasseur and potatoes. Staff have been friendly.

Overall average performance at this Domestic Gold lounge, up to the standard. The food was cool, but there was 2 active store with wantan noodles and laksa, the majority local food. A simple interior design with limited facilities for domestics lounge.

The lounge (regional lounge in main terminal) is a little disappointing for a home base lounge, They have lots of spaces for chairs and a mediocre food selection, noodles and a couple of other hot choices ? a few little sandwiches but the lounge just needs a little more. Selection of Hot drinks to be asked for and usual soft drinks on offer. Toilets and showers just about passable but its a shame when they can get it right in the Satellite lounge.

Lounges in Yangon International Airport in Terminal 2 (used by Malaysia Airlines) render two options: both are called Royal Jade Lounge which are 3rd Party lounges. Lounges are old, but well functioning, good chairs, quick internet, and I had many choices for breakfast. Good atmosphere, active staff, though limited language ability. Plenty of beer brands in coolers, otherwise no alcohol. Nice coffee options and loads of cakes and cookies.

Reading recent reviews of this Malaysia Airlines lounge at KLIA left me a little confused, so let me clarify things. The lounge is clean and bright with floor to ceiling windows overlooking the ramp. Food is very limited with a strong Asian bias. Limited beverages and no alcohol. Toilets and showers not at all welcoming. Air conditioning was not great.

Only popped in for 5 mins to quench my thirst on a rushed transit. Better than expected for this shared (SATS) lounge. Limited alcohol is available which is rare for Malaysia Airlines customers. No time to sample small food offer. Showers were available. Lounge does not afford views of airfield.

This was my first time visited the Malaysia Airlines domestic golden lounge. It was renovated a few month ago. The interior was quite comfortable with plenty of seat available. There were side window sofa seat where you can have a very nice view of the KLIA runway. Further inside have seats with proper dining table . The food bar have limited food but they provide a chef on spot to cook some local dishes. The taste was pretty good. Food and drink served over the bar. A fresh brew coffee machine also available. Clean and comfortable area. Fast WIFI provided but may struggle to find some socket plug to charge on your laptop or mobile. The only setback was the front desk customer service staff. Lack of smile and no eyes contact.

Absolute waste of space for a new Airport they just have not bothered with the Airport lounge on the upper floors. Do not waste your time, we arrived and the room was the size of a bedroom! Toilets out of order so you had to leave the lounge go out into the main terminal a wade through the mess - a polite way of saying it. We left and went into the main terminal as it was much nicer. Dirty tables and chairs, staff sitting chatting.

Used both the main terminal (small) and satellite terminal (large) Malaysia Airlines business class lounges at KLIA on 2hour lay-overs between return flights, Bangkok to Sydney. Pluses; good locations with quick access to gates, good WiFi & easy to connect, lots of open seating, comfortable temperature, standard self-service drink selection. Minuses; food very average, salad selection almost non-existent, both lounges look very tired with seats and decor needing modernizing, staff seemed very bored with their jobs, bathrooms on par with a bus terminal, no charging ports for electronic devices in general seating areas. Overall impression not very good for the home base lounges of the national airline!

The Malaysia Airlines Golden Lounge (Satellite) is big, and has good facilities like shower and sleeping area, which is well maintained, but the food choices are bad. There is almost zero options for vegetarians and the food is usually cold. They should change the options more frequently as well rather than keeping the same food for more than 12 hours. Its is a good place if you only want to relax. Its a struggle speaking to the staff as most of them do not understand English.

The lounge is well decorated, comfortable seat, great view overlooking tarmac, wifi connection is good and speed is high. Staff attentive but the catering is very limited. The buffet line consist of a few sandwiches, salad, Nasi Lemak, and some poor selection of cheese. Even soft drinks and fruit juices alternatives are very limited. However, please note that this is the lounge nearest to my departure gate that bear the sign "Golden Lounge Regional".

I didn't fly with Malaysian Airlines, when I presented my boarding pass and my KLM Frequent flyer card, I was welcome in their Lounge. The lounge is really roomy, you got free wi-fi, with a good connection, so I could work on my laptop. Around breakfast time, there is a buffet with a choice of local and international dishes. I had a pleasant time there waiting for my connecting flight. The only complaint, is something what is not the fault of the staff, but the parents with their unruly kids, who couldn't shut up and stayed noisy and run around all the time.

A gorgeous and spacious lounge. Bathroom with shower booth, towels and toiletries inside. Lovely sit-down restaurant with extensive menu and served by courteous staffs. Other lounging area is spacious and well stocked with reading materials, power points and good wifi. They also have rooms for taking a nap too, very well thought-out indeed.

As a sharp contrast to the huge and spacious one in the KLIA Satellite building, this lounge in the main terminal is smaller in scale, and my feeling is mixed. I was welcomed into the lounge, but find staffs inside a bit lazy and relaxed. Food varieties are sufficient but not great. I notice the air conditioning is insufficient makes staying there a little uncomfortable. I feel that Malaysia Airlines should make more effort into upgrading and improving this lounge. The overall experience was just ok, not great, and it should have been. If you have more than 2 hours, or are not pressed for time, don't come here, go to the one in Satellite building instead, it's only a very short aero train ride.

First time at this lounge using my Qantas Gold, Oneworld sapphire. It's a big lounge, very spacious. The food selection is limited. Comfortable enough but felt worn and in need of refurbishment. Now the not so good. The showers were very dated. Cockroach comes for free. Compared to Emirates, Cathay or Qantas these facilities are very poor. The whole place needs a good renovation. Ok for a stop and just as well as KLIA is not the most fun place to be.

Was flying Penang to KL in business when I used the lounge. Food selection was good and had a tasty Nasi Lemek. Lounge had a self serve coffee machine with acceptable coffee. No alcohol available in the lounge but good selection of soft drinks. Seating was comfortable with good wi fi access. Each seat had charging points for devices which was handy. Only downside was lack of information for delay in our flight. Screen was showing ready for boarding but flight boarding was delayed by an hour.

Malaysia Airlines use this commercial third party lounge at Delhi, used by a number of airlines. It is well laid out, modern, clean with a limited but good range of food and drink. Small but good bathroom with shower facilities. Better than expected. Good helpful staff. Wifi available with provided voucher.

Poor all round. Cockroaches in the shower and on the main floor in the lounge, no hot water in the showers and worn out grey (once white) towels. Strangely, passengers were required to surrender their boarding pass in exchange for a towel. The bar had also run out of beer. I visited the lounge twice over a week and there was still no hot water in the showers. I wrote a complaint to the airline who simply agreed that it was not good enough and that they must try harder. Not hard enough for me - won't be flying on this airline again.

Firstly, greeted at the reception by an irate customer service representative. As I was going to deposit my hand carry bag in the locker room - all lockers, except for the top most No. 13 locker had a key. I brought this issue up with the reception staff who explained that the keys were likely stolen and that I should use what's available with a key. Proceeded to the buffet area - noticed a cockroach scurrying across the bar where the bottles of mineral water and cutlery are placed. Again, I brought the attention of the barista manning the counter who made a half hearted attempt to kill the cockroach that very quickly escaped us back into the kitchen area (clean area !). The barista just shrugged her shoulders and continued making coffee. Noted that the toilet floors were wet, toilets doors were worn down. If Malaysia Airlines were serious about their reputation, where the KLIA satellite lounge is the frontline of their premium service - they really need to overhaul - customer service provision, cleanliness and refurbish the entire lounge. Malaysia Airlines need to really up their game because as it is, the Plaza Premium Lounge nearby on the same floor beats this MAS lounge hands down in terms of good, ambience, cleanliness and customer service.

Huge but not cozy, dated and not well designed. Food served was normal and well presented. Flies around, drinking water is served with plastic bottle, come on Malaysia Airline ! It's a lousy lounge, their golden lounge regional and plaza premium lounge are much better than this lounge !

At the time of writing (23rd January 2016) this is a small temporary lounge for business travelers. There was nobody in the lounge when I entered. A small selection of sandwiches and cakes all fresh. Tea and Coffee made to order. Water and soft drinks available. I did not see any alcohol.

A quiet and peaceful lounge with a comfortable smoking room. Staff attentive and helpful. Restaurant options a little limited but quite acceptable. Snacks are also available. Had an 8 hour layover and was offered a snooze room. Showers are available.

This Malaysia Airlines business class lounge is the worst I have ever been in. The toilets were disgusting. Urine all over the floor, dirty doors and smelly. Staff unhelpful. They did not supply and diet drinks which is very strange. They just take your glass away when not finished and dont say anything. The lounge is large with plenty of seating but there was hardly any Western choice food apart from dry sandwiches. Really poor.

I am not sure whether other travellers all rated the same lounge. This lounge is certainly not the newest, but it is okay. They have a good food selection as well as drinks and Wifi is available. The staff is nice and polite.

Considering this is MAS home airport and the main Satellite Golden Lounge for KLIA it is dreadful! Food selection poor, drink selection even more so. No glasses available for cold soft drink so staff gave a mug! Needs to be refurbished as looking very tired and old. In contrast, the smaller Golden Lounge (before monorail to C gates) is fantastic! Recently refurbished, great offerings inc. champagne etc. Friendly staff and much cosier atmosphere

The main lounge in satellite area was overcrowded and very difficult to find seats. It is very, very run down and tired, and during our visit was nothing better than filthy. Choice of food is very limited and clearly quite cheap compared to what they provided a few years ago - this is like a low-cost airline lounge, and clearly the new management don't have a clue what to do in trying to restore their reputation. Don't get me going on drinks (esp wine etc), since they seem to want to keep that well away or hidden from customers! Toilets were also filthy, and not just the mends - my wife said the ladies washrooms had broken taps, lacking towels etc and were also very poor. There is no smile from the staff on the front desk either, and all in all they seemed very dispirited and looking like they want to get a job elsewhere. I cam back to give MAS another chance since they used to be so good, but things have gotten so bad, I would seriously warn all others to avoid this airline for what looks like a long time to come.

Lounge is impressive. Comfy resting area as well as good hospitality from the staff. Food and beverages choices are great. Love to travel with Malaysia Airlines and use KLIA for transit in the future.

A huge lounge with plenty of seating and good views of the tarmac if that's your thing. Food is pretty poor to be honest, toilets a disgrace no other way to describe them. Bar stocks most drinks but measures a little small. If your flight goes from the C gates at KLIA I would wait before you get the train and use the non satellite Malaysia Airlines lounge before you get the train. Its no better for food or drink, but it seems well maintained and clean. I cannot understand why Malaysian Airlines have allowed this Golden Lounge to deteriorate to the extent they have.

Still no hot water in this Malaysia Airlines Golden Lounge, which is not up to expected standards for a Business Class lounge. Arrived about 9pm and was looking forward to a shower before my next flight. It was not to be. Toilets are also less than desirable and were dirty. Food is only average and lacks a good selection.
