Qantas Club at HNL is quite small but run by friendly staff who are available for assistance. The food and beverage areas are small but well stocked. I was there for a morning flight and was happy with the pastries cereal and fruits on offers.

Staff although helpful appeared to think keeping things clean was beneath them. The cleanliness of the place needed to be stepped up a notch for me. Quality of the food was average the fact they shut the coffee bar was completely odd. I was told to use a cheap vending machine? Range of wines and other beverages generally good.

A really small and uninviting lounge compared to the normal QF fare. Incredibly quiet - everyone was whispering! No TV internet. Almost no food (packets of chips only for most of my stay then a few sandwiches) and no staff noticed when the wine ran out. Why not use the BA lounge instead?

A clean and tidy lounge - although by the time all eligible passengers are in the lounge it can be quite cramped and busy. It is operated by two staff who work hard when the lounge is full as it serves both JQ and QF flights including QC members traveling on JetStar economy. I recommend arriving early as access can be denied when the lounge hits peak capacity. There can be a lengthy queue to enter at times as there is only one person manning the reception desk and she must record your details manually as you enter. Food and beverage amenities are adequate. There is no television but there are 3 PC terminals. WiFi coverage is a bit confusing as most pax needing access needed staff assistance to log in. Overall a good lounge and an alternative to the bus shelter that is HNL terminal.

Crowded. One main seating area mainly lounge seats with some cafe tables next to the bar but also separate areas to watch TV. Very limited selection of food although could purchase some cafe style meals. Complimentary vouchers (2/person) for drinks. There is a small children's room with electronic games and computer. Bathrooms located only at one end of lounge which seems a long way from TV areas. Only 2 computers were available on the evening we flew (other 2 out of action) which seems inadequate for such a busy lounge.

Never in many years of travel have I experienced such a bad First Class lounge. Was there mid- morning no food selection to speak of just cereals. Plenty of champagne though. Tiny area with not enough seats for the 4-5 flights that leave around 11am. Received a very late boarding call resulting in us holding up the plane as it was ready to leave. Compared to most Qantas lounges in the world this was disgraceful. Qantas need to re-think how they treat their platinum members especially considering that this lounge also caters for the EVA air flight and JAL.

I was an Air New Zealand Business Class ticket holder and I was surprised the plane did not depart from T1 like most Star Alliance flights but discovered ANZ code share with JAL hence T2. Anyway I arrived from T1 on the inter terminal shuttle and asked at the transfer desk which lounge I could use and I was directed to the Qantas business lounge. I had a shower and used the internet stations. The choice of food was okay - nothing specatular. For a 30 minute use the lounge did the job well.

I have written before extolling the virtues of this lounge and there are none better. Have just finished a delicious breakfast of eggs benedict with smoked trout two of the best lattes I have ever tasted and fresh OJ. The staff here are warm friendly and helpful. It is the best way to start a 14 hour flight to the US.

To be honest the QF domestic Business class lounge is not much different from the QF Club. Aside from fewer people and prettier light fittings almost everything else is the same. The so-called Neil Perry signature food selection amounts to little more than a plate full of fancy party pies. The obligatorily QF Club carrot and celery sticks also adorned the Business class lounge buffet too. I visited the lounge mid-morning and it certainly could have done with a good vacuum clean. Also noted that the tiles in the male toilets had been stripped off revealing the besa-brick construction (very attractive!).

I think this is the case where the hype is better than the reality. Whilst the Qantas First Class lounge in Sydney is very nice with its openness and design the lack of attention to detail lets it down. The first impression upon entering the main lounge - a dirty floor going up the escalator to the top floor. Toilets - not only was the floor filthy beyond belief but two out of the four toilet stalls were either not flushed or had excrement in them. When I informed reception of this they told me that they just had a lot of flights leaving. Is this suppose to be an excuse? If they knew this then someone should have been right on it. Nearly half of the computers did not work. One had a virus warning flashing on the screen! The restaurant had an excellent selection of food which was tasty and made to order. The wine selection was the best I have seen. Also the spa centre was brilliant! I had the best face and neck massage that I can recall. Although my wife was less impressed with her manicure. Overall this is a very good lounge but is let down by a lack of attention to detail.
Friendly and enthusiastic staff good service clean and well maintained and plenty of space. Good food choices - all in all a sense of really being appreciated.

What a surprise compared to the hideous Admirals Club in Terminal 4. Hot meals (chilli con carne chicken stir fry etc with rice and noodles) choice of 3 beers good red and white wines and spirits bar. Plenty of PC's to catch up with emails courteous attentive staff. Great shower rooms although the water outlets need replacement. Plenty of space in a quiet relaxing environment. Can get a little crowded when 2 hours from 4 flights departing. Overall especially in terms of lounges in the US very good.

The ambience is active but quiet. From the telephone call the day before asking us what time we would be arriving so the kurbside porter could help us with our luggage to the boarding of the plane all needs were met. My partner was wished a Happy Birthday from every staff member who met us at check in at the Lounge entrance and after our meal in the Lounge restaurant where my partner was presented with a small birthday platter of fruit. All this occurred by a mere mention of the event during my telephone conversation the day before.

This lounge is immaculately maintained - as was stated previously can become somewhat irritating as they will pounce on a finished glass of drink or cleared plate - can't really complain though. The catering is slightly above basic with some hot foods and soups and the usual au dourves biscuits cheeses and anti pesto. There is no bar but rather a self serve fridge as in Melbourne and Sydney international business lounges and a few post-mixes dotted around the lounge. The wine-bar area and the open round tabled seating area near the main food area are great for socialising while the darker quite areas are adequate but the lounges are not as comfortable as they appear. Plus the big floor to ceiling windows which run around the far side of the lounge are great to watch the goings on of the terminal below. The showers are incredible probably the best I've seen in a non first lounge. On the downside the lounge as with QF/BA First Thai United Lounges a fair walk from the QF/BA gates and up a set of escalators and very hard to find. But it handles to steady flow of numbers very well and never feels full despite the time of day.

The staff were attentive and friendly. As there is no airside pharmacy in Sydney international a staff member actually took my script had it filled at a pharmacy in another part of the airport had it cleared by security and delivered to my table. Now that's service! The menu is the restaurant is short sharp simple and of excellent quality. The facilities are great I like that you can choose to use either Mac or PC in this lounge. They have a very nice day spa hard to get into but when you do very much worth the effort. The bathrooms are not that great but you really are not there to spend too much time in there. It's wonderfully spacious with plenty of places to sit. The only annoying factor was the number of children in the lounge. All in all a great place. This lounge is the only reason that I will continue to use Qantas it's a great benefit for platinum frequent flyers- Qantas inflight service could learn a lot from this lounge.

Sydney business lounge very spacious with nice views. Food quality good hot food offering of soup and meat pies a little disappointing but cold meats cheese were of a high standard and bread was fresh. Lounge feels too modern could do with some nice artwork to enliven the space. Nice light fixtures particularly at the large communal style wine bar. Plenty of room to relax and find privacy if needed. Nice mix of seating arrangements. Nice showers. Overall a pleasant pre flight experience.

The renovated Qantas Club at Perth International is a vast improvement over the old one. It's looks and feels like the other Mark Newson designed Qantas lounges with the seemingly larger space punctuated with different areas serving different purposes. The toilet and shower facilities are also much improved while the food and drink on offer has not changed since the old days. The only major gripe would be the extremely warm temperature of the lounge which was acknowledged by the receptionist as being problematic.

I had a couple of hours on my hands waiting for my flight back up north to the Greatland so I went into the new Boardroom in the North terminal. It was pretty busy with lots of folks there including a number of businessmen/women. The layout appeared to be decent with plenty of chairs both comfortable and modern. The staff at the front desk were professional and welcoming. I enjoyed a cup of soup, very tasty and hot. Plenty of televisions to watch. The only thing I would have added was two more bathrooms, one for men and one for women. They had only one that I could fine under the name Family Restroom. This could become a problem for those needing to "go now". All in all I was pleased though and look forward to another cup of soup in my future!

Before i entered the Sky Lounge, there is a notice written, the Wash room is not Working! I present the invite to the front desk, staff asked me how may of us and are you travelling with a child. after she check everything, she said Go Ahead. The dining area was a mess, there were few tables with left over dishes, no service staff to be seen, i have to move those left over dishes to other table by myself. Got myself a seat There were only two main course, a fried rice and a fried noodle (it was near empty). The selection of bread is very minimal, small packet of butter runs out, and at the buffet area, food and stains almost everywhere, bread crumbs all over the place too. I spend 15 minutes and have not seen any staff adding in more food or clearing up the table. I will never visit this place anymore.

Royal Brunei uses the Cathay Pacific lounge in Melbourne. It’s way down and a bit dark and dingy, no windows, just next to some sort of hall. The bathrooms were nice and clean though. The food selection, while not extensive was adequate although the hot food kept running out. The seating was fine, nothing about the lounge was great but it wasn’t as bad as I feared it might be from previous reviews. There were quite a few in the lounge, however there was plenty of seating. Overall it was ok.

The lounge in Brunei is quite basic. It is not meant for a long stay. The whole airport has been upgraded and slightly expanded. The lounge received some minor changes. It is comfortable and able to handle the number of passengers using it. WiFi worked reasonably well and has improved over the past 12 - 18 months. The food remains fairly limited but is of good quality. I always have a shower on the return to Australia (three hours in the airport) and while the water was hot the pressure was variable.

The Royal Brunei Airlines Sky lounge at Bandar seri Begawan airport is very quiet and very basic. Staff are not very communicative and few and far between. No alcohol served and the only beverages are cartons of long life fruit juice, fizzy drinks and hot beverages - all self serve. The buffet is both limited and unappetising. Lounge chairs are not comfortable for more than a hours stay - my flight was delayed seven hours and it was both a very tiring and tedious stay in the lounge Massage chairs were unserviceable. The toilets are very poor for a premuim business lounge. Two urinals and two toilet cubicles together with two showers (with plastic curtains and broken tiles) are not much better than what one will find in a very basic motel.

A pleasant enough place to take a break for an hour or so and I was flying on a very cheap business class fare so was reasonably happy but if I had been paying full price I think I would have expected more from this lounge. Very small space with limited food choices but what was there was pleasant enough. Instructions on how to use the coffee machine would have been helpful.
A very good business class lounge. The food was excellent and the hot showers that my wife and I had was great and very refreshing. WiFi was great and the staff were more than willing to help.
This lounge takes you back to the 1970's. Although it's clean and tidy it's certainly not up to world standard. Some of the lounge chairs were very uncomfortable.

The Escape Lounge is the only lounge at STN. As such it gets very very busy, and advance booking is almost essential. You can book though Holiday Extras and similar sites to guarantee access, as often turning up with a priority pass will get you sent away due to lack of space. If you are flying BA with status or in Club Europe you are always allowed access. The service is good, and there are limited apron views. Food selection is very limited and not great quality, but the staffed bar has a wide range although many drinks incur an extra charge. Unusually there are no toilets in the lounge, and you have to leave to go upstairs to use the main airport facilities and return to the lounge, which is a tad inconvenient to say the least!

Since we had a long layover at Moscow Domodedovo and the terminal did not have good WiFi, we decided to pay for the Business Class Lounge (£30 each) and stay there. A very relaxing experience with professional staff, excellent catering and lots of comfortable seating areas. At 6pm we were called and we boarded our flight. An excellent experience overall.

Well-appointed with good taste and comfortable seating. During my early morning visit pastries and sweets were available and coffees. A piano and seating area complete with a massage chair which was very nice. Staff spoke limited english and kept a tv set in high volume showing a children program non-stop which no one was interested in and was annoying. Temperature in the lounge was too high almost uncomfortable. No windows. Close to the gates area.

2 different lounges one domestic and one international. Both are small but well appointed with nice decor and comfortable sofas large Windows with apron views. Wifi worked very well service was attentive and professional they came to me to advise a change of gate and staff escorted me to the right direction. Good selection of food appetizers and 2 or 3 options of a hot main dish with some sweets and drinks available including beer on tap. As my flight to Munich was scheduled to leave from a remote stand a private Mercedes shuttle was provided which was appreciated. Nice lounges with nice service.

Lounge entry ok. Grumpy barista serving coffee. Horrible toilets and very long wait to use one! Lounge needs to totally redesign toilets and incorporate high quality urinals to speed up wait times. Toilet problem is not just the lounge but the whole of Copenhagen airport!

Totally overrun. Loud, crowded, children running and screaming around everywhere. Nowhere to sit. Obviously too little capacity. SAS in Norway particularly (but also Sweden) has this ridiculous policy of basically selling gold card membership to everyone. All you need is an Amex Card and a second Eurobonus credit card (total cost for the cards is 350 Euro per year), fly twice and bingo you have a gold card. Massive deflation effect on actual gold membership. When boarding you see a third or more of the passengers get on the plane during business class/gold boarding although there is only 6 rows of business class? So the privilege of early boarding is useless. Less queues when boarding economy :) In fact, all the privileges of a business class ticket is gone due to this policy. Long lines and fewer screening machines at priority security check. You can see the economy security line going much faster. Early boarding is more crowded than economy boarding. Sitting in SAS Lounge is far more crowded, loud and stressful, than sitting in nice lounge chairs located at most gates. So paying for actual business class ticket with SAS hasnt been worth the money for a long time SAS, but now it has become less efficient, more stressful then economy because it is half the plane is a gold member.

Overcrowded, dirty, wine from the tap, no spirits. This Lounge is a shame for any Star Alliance Airline. We are very much disappointed especially because we booked first class from Zurich and are on the way to this flight.

We flied business class on Thai Airways therefore we were able to use SAS lounge at Stockholm Arlanda airport. The lounge is OK but not so big and was quite crowded. Not varieties of food and drink to serve.

We flied SAS to Oslo from Stockholm on economy class but we were able to use Norrsken Lounge because we are Priority Pass nember. The lounge is not so big but not so crowded. However, we found that the food and drinks were quite limited. By the tine we used, there was only one staff to take care the lounge which made her very busy to serve many passengers.
The lounge was so full we could not get in. People sitting everywhere. Unfortunately, lost gold so my J class ticket did not allow me to enter the LH lounge. Bad business class value

Gold Lounge at Oslo Airport. This was a bad experience. Dry pieces of baguettes wrapped in plastic, nothing done with love and care for the passengers. It would have been so easy to put some snacks and delicious small buffet.

The SAS Gold upper lounge has just reopened in September, (the lower level lounge remained shut). A very poor selection of food and drink on offer. No alcoholic drinks are supplied. Is this to stop the spread of Covid-19? Minimum effort by SAS. They should be ashamed of themselves.

This lounge is very difficult for a Lufthansa Senator (Goldstatus) member because they say (even they know it that’s is wrong) senator means silver status and in Stockholm Arlanda you don’t get any access to a lounge with silver status or Business Class Passenger. So I have to confirm with a business center, they give me a written letter that senator status with miles and more is the Gold Status of Star Alliance. Very unfriendly women at the desk, definitely no interest for the guests.

I pass through CDG on a regular basis, and I sometimes go into this lounge with a smile, but I always leave with a heavy heart. This must simply be one of the worst lounges in the airline industry. It is always super crowded, and tonight was no exception. The catering is nothing to write home about, and there are no facilities. I am writing this review from the waiting area outside the lounge, since it is more quiet and considerably more spacious than the lounge itself! SAS, please do something, or close down the lounge.

It’s very difficult to get access to the lounge, big problem if you have only Business Ticket, and gold Status of Miles and more In the Lounge there is ne service, coffee machine defective, only one juice for choice, nearly nothing very fresh to eat. It’s a really bad experience and it’s not worth to go there. Even with the huge access problems You feel very hard that they staff is disinterested to give any service or comfort. The worst lounge in any airport I have ever seen. They are very far away from European health and hygienic standard

I was just once in this SAS Gold Lounge at Oslo Airport as I was transiting. It was very early in the morning after a long haul flight. My connection flight did have a delay. The design is very appealing. Very typical for Lounges in Scandinavia. I changed places to work, to eat or to have a short nap. Everything i needed was available: strong coffee and a nice breakfast buffet.

SAS Business Class Lounge at Terminal B is bigger than LH and provide more choice of food and drinks. Nevertheless the offer is still average. The design of the lounge is attractive though. Many differently designed areas and sitting and working area possibilities. Unfortunately, no showers are provided.
The lounge is too small and overcrowded. The food quality is very poor. I and my family ended up eating at an airport restaurant instead. It was an absolute waste of money.

As it seems the Copenhagen lounge remodelling is almost finished and I am not impressed. They added a Barrista and coffee bar, but the choice and quality of food is still poor and below average: warm curry soup, bread and salad. That`s it! Soft drinks, wine and some strong alcohol. New furniture and design are stylish.

The lounge of SAS is tucked away on second floor in a secluded part of the airport, not exactly easy to find eve for a seasoned traveler like me. The lounge is split into two part, one for business class tickets, one for all the Star alliance Gold members. Typical Scandinavian touch with the use of wood and stylish furniture. Overall it was pleasant enough. However a very limited selections of food on offer. At noon, only a soup and salads that's all. Alcohol selections was not too bad though. On the other hand, the star alliance part of the lounge had a bit more offering and better seating and designs. SAS seems to value Star alliance members more than their own full fare paying business class customers, that's the part which really disappointed me. The toilets, I am not sure if it's a typical Swedish thing, are all individual cubicles without regards whether you are male or female. I find the whole experience rather underwhelming.

As a premium economy traveler you are entitled to use the new lounge only at Arlanda airport, when flying Scandinavian so I said to give it a try. It turns out it is located where the business lounge is, but it uses another gate, for premium travelers and they get a different experience. It was indeed new and it looked great in a nice Scandinavian design. The only thing is that the bottles on the walls were for decorations only and water was coming from the tap. same with the juices or beer or even wine. The food selection was better being focused on a healthy way of living with fresh fruits and vegetables which you could combine from the buffet in a lovely salad. They were accompanied by some crackers cheese and so on, but not much. It had a business desk where one could use a computer and there was a printer too. There were plenty of chairs and tables, but the place was small and they were somehow squeezed inside. Round tables, small tables, armchairs, it had it everything in a Scandinavian design. Not the best place for getting a drink before your flight, but better than waiting at the gate. Also check your time because it is located in the Schengen area, so going to your gate for long haul means going through security and passport control.

What a miserable excuse for a lounge! I have used the SAS domestic lounge in Stockholm many times. It is a small lounge that gets very crowded to the point of standing room only especially at late afternoon. The seating is in groups around tables, plus there a a couple of counters. The furniture is worn and very, very dated. There is no food to speak of in the lounge. There are potato crisps, cookies, and usually a non-descript soup that tastes as if it came directly from a can (which it probably does). Plates and utensils are plastic and paper. Drinks are limited to soda, beer, coffee and water. The worst part about the lounge is how dirty it is. Paper plates and plastic cups are left for hours on the tables before the never visible staff finally collects them. The restrooms probably only get cleaned once a day. Waste bins are overflowing with paper towels. There are no showers. The only positive aspect is that the wi-fi is ok. It is really a pretty misserable place. The only reason to use it is that the domestic terminal itself also can be a pretty misserable experience during peak times, and then it is a question of choosing the lesser of two evils.

The SAS Business Lounge offers you one kind of red wine, one kind of white and one beer. That’s it for the alcoholic drinks. The food is a joke, Hot Dogs - seriously. I’m at a point where I would even pay to get some choice. There’s a CPH apartment lounge in the airport where you get at least a decent choice of drinks - the comfort is a joke too as you can chose between sitting in the departure area style environment or on uncomfortable high chairs or some soft seating that is always taken. The only upside is the friendly staff.

Flying Thai Airways and using SAS lounge. Cask (bag and box) wine and one choice of beer (everyday brand). Crummy cheap in the extreme in the SAS home lounge. We were there at lunch time, and the selection of food was, to say the least, meager. This was a most disappointing experience. The WiFi was also annoying, requiring a long and convoluted logon process.

I was looking forward relaxing in the Gold lounge in Copenhagen operated by SAS. The experience was very disappointing. Limited selection of food and in a desperate cost saving attempt all news papers had been removed and replaced by electronic copies which to access you needed to install an app. Bad experience. I can understand it as a value add a supplement to the physical news papers but as a replacement. Shame on your SAS.

A relaxing lounge with understated Scandinavian design. It has a nice assortment of snacks and beverages. Alcoholic drinks are not served before 7am and only wine and beer until noon. Spirits are available in the afternoon so that may be a little unusual for the international traveler. Staff are courteous and efficient. Overall a nice place to regroup before a flight.

This Aspire handling lounge was very poorly maintained. It was overcrowded, dirty, and the receptionists were not very friendly. The tables were laden with empty glasses and dishes and people had a hard time finding a place to sit. For a Business Class lounge, it really does make the cut.
Hot, cramped, few free seats and those that were were uncomfortable. Lounge open to main terminal so noisy. Lousy food selection as well. first and last time I shall be flying SAS.

Worst lounge ever if we can name it lounge! First the lounge opens late in the morning; then if your flight is early, you won't have a chance to relax and have a drink. The lounge looks like a very old ikea store with very cheap and over used furnitures. The food selection is poor, the croissants are not fresh and taste bad, no coke, few sodas. Not enough seats for all the guests. Poor wifi connection. No toilets.

Silver lounge at Stockholm Arlanda is accessible with SAS-plus ticket, or can be purchased for 200-300 SEK (20-30€). I found it to have a good, fresh and healthy selection of food. Not a lot of choice on food, more choice on non-alcoholic beverages. Very good wi-fi connectivity and plenty of space in the lounge with many different kinds of seats to choose from.

The SAS lounge for Star Alliance Gold members at Copenhagen Kastrup airport has a new and fresh appearance, although the interior looks is a bit too overdesigned. Likewise, there is a large of variety of different sorts of seats wich are randomly mixed. By contrast, the offered selection of drinks is quite good and the breakfast buffet is alright. However, the only big disappointment were the shower facilities which made a terrible outdated and nagged impression. On the positve side I have to mention that the lounge is very spacious, the complimentary wifi is very fast, and the staff was extraordinarily helpful. To sum it up: This lounge is not top-notch but definitely to recommend!

I was resting in this lounge before I took my flight back home. It is a bit small, but quite cosy. The staff was excellent. But one thing: They had only a few food items to chose between. That was ok anyway. There was also plenty of free drinks, both soft drinks, juice, water and alcoholic beverages. It was indeed ok while waiting a few hours for the flight, and it was nearby the gate too. Probably the best experience this time at Chicago Airport (ORD).

SAS Scandinavian Gold lounge at CPH Airport is located outside security. No signage to guide you to it. Poor selection of food, mostly hot dogs. Very busy. Very poor wifi. Not a great place to actually relax. Showers are very dated. Considering how good their business class cabin was, the lounge was a bit of a disappointment.

SAS gives you the opportunity to purchase lounge access during online check-in in for 22€ per person and we wanted to try out the SAS Lounge in Stockholm Arlanda Airport (Schengen area, T5). Entered an airy and relatively large lounge with Scandinavian design for a quick lunch between flights and the fresh cold buffet plus soup with a selection of breads was more than enough for us. This lounge is larger than the one in Helsinki Airport (SAS Lounge) and the cold buffet more extensive, moreover, we didn't need to stand in line for seats to be vacated in the Arlanda lounge, which has been the case twice in Helsinki in April-May 2016. Enjoyable and hassle-free lounge experience in Arlanda!

Wanted to try out the SAS Lounge by paying 28€ per person for entry (I was flying with Lufthansa), felt the fee was reasonable for a try. Busy Thursday evening with three or four SAS flights plus one LH flight departing within an hour from gates 11-15 where the lounge is situated (opposite gate 13). The first thing one notices when entering the lounge: it's not facing the tarmac / runways and the lounge felt cramped and dark. The cold buffet was limited with one variety of cold meat, two salads as well as hot sausages for making a hot dog, if needed. Coffee, refreshments, beer and wines were available as well as a number of Nordic and International newspapers, but missed a view to the planes/tarmac. Not impressed with the lounge: not very good for working nor relaxing at busy times - more like a busy train station with mediocre service.

New SAS lounge at Tromso Airport. Small and sweet lounge. Interior design look simple, blue and white. The dinning area and reading area just side by side .This lounge Only prepare some fruit jus, fruit,coffee, tea and snack (cinnamon bun) only, no much selection.

Purchased access to this SAS lounge when checking in, around 20 USD. For this you get access to standard lounge with free drinks, news, food, wifi. Impression was mixed. There is lots of places to work. Electrical sockets everywhere. Quiet rooms, fine rest rooms, and drinks selection is good. However the food is so-so. There was a salad and a tomato soup when I was there. And the salad bar consisted of 3-4 different things. Not really interestring. Worst though is the absolutely horrible wifi access. 99.9% of lounge guests work here, or use a smartphone in some way. And you have a download speed of around 30 kb/sec? I will get 100 times that speed at any cafe downtown. Simply not acceptable in 2015. I gave up and used my private 4G connection. Next time I will go for the Diners lounge.

Lufthansa lounge at LHR T2. Large windows look out onto runways and taxiways with lots of activity. The lounge is spacious and airy, subdivided by freestanding furniture. So although the room is large, the ambiance is cosy and quiet. Various newspapers and magazines were available. The seating is mainly leather armchairs separated by table units. A dining area is equipped with dining tables and chairs, in front of a well stocked bar and food buffet. As a nice touch there was a big jug of ready made Pimms (with lots of fruit garnish) available as a celebration of Wimbledon. In the morning the food on offer was bacon, scrambled eggs, tomatoes, mushrooms, plenty of breads, cold meats and various garnishes. At about 11am this changed to hot lunch items: rice, chicken casserole, pasta with sauce, soup and various other items. The staff were very unobtrusive and kept the place clean and tidy. WiFi was easy to use. As this is located in the new Queen's Terminal 2 everything is brand new.

The lounge consists of two lounges with the same entrance the Scandinavian Lounge on the 4th floor and the Business Lounge on the 3rd. I believe EuroBonus Silver card holders can access the Business Lounge during Summer time and from mid-december until mid-January and it is thus more crowded than the Scandinavian Lounge. The food selection is ok nothing extraordinary. The beverage selection is quite disappointing (one red wine one white wine one beer). The space is rather nice in classic "Danish" design. The best lounge in CPH.

SAS is one of my favorite airlines but please do something about the Stockholm lounge. The offering of food and drinks compared to Copenhagen and Helsinki are incredibly poor and gives the wrong impression of Swedish service and cuisine to visitors.

Nice lounge nice ikea style decor. View of one of the gates at terminal 5 ample seating. Got in due to star alliance gold status (United). Nice spread of snacks much better than the swissport lounge in terminal 5. Roomy enough seating. Staff pleasant and helpful. Food ok compared to a lounge in the US.

Unacceptable Internet (WiFi) access - Connection is disconnected several times during all my last stays the last 2 years at this Lounge. My colleagues had always the same problem. In no other lounge we had so much problems with internet access. Temperature especially during the summer months is way too high this is very inconvenient. After complaining several times at the front desk nothing happens even no explanation why this problem cannot be fixed. This is really unprofessional.

The lounge itself is nice but hard to find. Visited between 08.20-09.40. Food selection was a bowl of oatmeal som vegetables chips and dip. You cold also choose between apple and orange juice different kind of (coca cola brand) sodas beer or vine. The lounge is self serviced.

Disappointed with this lounge in CPH. The lounge is features a modern design. Food selection is ok and food is quite tasty. Drinks selection very poor no wifi (staff informed me that wifi had not been working for over a month) and lounge very crowded.

I visited this lounge on March 5 between 05:45-06:20. The lounge can often be crowded but not at this early morning occasion. The breakfast offered was very good and tasteful including plenty of selections. The offerings regarding breakfast has however not been changed for a long time. It would be nice with some kind of variation even if the overall concept is very good. The lounge needs some upgrades since especially the (rather cosy) sofas and armchairs starts to get relatively worn and threadbare. The Internet access is easy and fast and I have never experienced any problem top class. The variety of newspapers and magazines are good. The staff are nice and service minded and keep the tables clean and tidy.

I visited SAS Business Lounge available for travellers in SAS Plus at Stockholm Arlanda Airport. The interior of the lounge is ok but nothing special. The assortment of food and drinks are very poor. The lounge was also quite crowded.

The lounge is quiet and clean with a good selection of beverages. However when it comes to getting some food to fill you up (high in protein) there is not many options. The food served is generally healthy but it's lacking protein sources like fish chicken meat and so on. In this regard lounges at VIE FRA are better options.

Scandinavian Airlines lounge at Stockholm Arlanda Airport is ok but at a lower standard than the average Star Alliance lounges at to other airport lounges within the Europe. The lounge is well situated if you have a departure from gate 1-10 otherwise not. The lounge can at some times during the day be very overcrowded. The variation of drinks is good but the food served has not been changed for many years and there is no variation to the menu. The food and snacks offered is often "healthy and sound" but gives the impression that it is composed based on guidelines from the Swedish Government Health Ministry. This is a modern and sound lounge but this makes unfortunately the longe a bit boring and too "Scandinavian perfect".

The SAS lounge at Copenhagen Airport is well situated and has plenty of seats and is seldom overcrowded. The variation of drinks is good and the food served is good and is relatively often altered. The food is to my opinion the best of all SAS lounges but does still not fully match the food served at fellow Star Alliance member Lufthansa at its hubs at FRA MUC and DUS. The atmospere in the SAS lounge is however very nice with a typical Danish touch that to my opinion could be even further developed for the benefit of the experience.

This SAS lounge is very often overcrowded. The variation of both food and drinks is very limited. The lounge is frequently visited by Swedish politicians and civil servants from the Swedish public administration representing the Swedish Government. This may be one of the reasons for the poor and very restricted offering since Swedish government employees is normally not allowed to drink or eat during business trips if not on their own expenses. I guess that SAS as still partially government owned have considered the above fact an adjusted this lounge to be "political correct".
Very limited food no international newspapers (only scrap leftovers) slow Wifi Star Alliance Gold customers are blocked from SAS Fast Lane - stay away from SAS lounge and CPH airport!

I have given SAS a lot of stick over the years. But credit where credit is due. The lounge in Copenhagen is slightly refurbished. Very homy and nordic design. Certain parts like the bathroom and shower facilities are stuck in a less modern state. They have quiet areas. The bar is not stocked with a lot of wines and liquer. The bar offers 2-3 red and white wines soft drinks and water coffee etc. The food is mostly the same. The staff is helpful in regards to boarding passes changing flights and other assistance.

Really enjoy the SAS lounge in Copenhagen airport - especially now when it have been partly refurbished. Cosy and "homey" atmosphere love the fireplace and new seats simple - but good - food (seems to have been updated) service minded staff. Good place to be - like Copenhagen airportt in general.

Mostly I visit the lounge between 0630-0730. During 5 years the breakfast has been the same no surprise or thrill. Lounge is old and worn and would be better with refurbishing. Staff is okay not too fast to clean empties away but okay. You get a nice welcome and when passing the front desk. For later flights the food (especially lunch) could be improved a lot. Getting tired of Cold smoked lax and salad/spinach. But drink selection is perfect.

The lounge has a relatively nice design and atmosphere but it was cramped with people and hard to find any seats. The food is more or less always the same some kind of salmon salad and cream cheese -very limited variation and range. Staff friendly but not as service-minded as SAS cabin crew.

I frequently visit SAS Scandinavian Airlines lounge at Stockholm-Arlanda Airport Terminal 5. The atmosphere in the lounge is relatively relaxing but the lounge is normally far too occupied and there has been no improvement for several years in that aspect. The meal service is very limited and is normally made up of some variant of salmon with cheese creme. The breakfast has never changed during the last 5-10 years but is better than the food served during the rest of the day. Some more ideas would be mostly welcomed. The variety of soft drinks wines and spirits are ok. There are plenty of newspapers and magazines and very easy access to Internet via wi-fi.

Used this lounge while flying back to Canada via Copenhagen and Frankfurt. Attractive spacious good supply of magazines and newspapers. Ample snacks and drink choices. A comfortable spot to while away some time before boarding.
Standard SAS Business Class lounge. Comfortable but nothing special. No other choices at this airport for Star Alliance passengers.

Very clean spacious lounge split between two floors. Good selection of cold food - salad cold meats cheese bread coleslaw etc. Extensive selection of wines beer spirits soft drinks. The washrooms are clean. There is a variety of seating designs - bar-style sofa areas dining tables quiet rooms and television rooms. Very clean airy impressive.

SAS Business Lounge on Terminal 5 is a small but efficient Lounge but the place is in need of remodeling - its very worn out and in need of a facelift. Other than that its a standard kind of lounge with polite staff the snacks are pretty good sadly they don't offer shower cabins!

Thought the lounge was excellent in a functional way - not luxurious. Typical Scandinavian decor and lighting - clean and bright. Plenty of computers (Macs). I was there at breakfast time and they had a good selection of food drink newspapers and magazines. It was a bit full apparently they have another seating area upstairs. Bathrooms just so-so would have expected tip top cleanliness but no. Staff impersonal.

There are two SAS lounges at Oslo Airport; one for business class and one for Star Alliance gold card holders (Scandinavian lounge). Both lounges are nice but the Scandinavian lounge has a more exclusive feel. Food selection is not overwhelming but it's high quality Scandinavian healthy food. Great work stations views of the airport / gates average but professional staff.
I do not know why the SAS staff act like in the old monopoly times food downright disappointing the staff need a training in service and kindness.

I use this lounge regularly and quite enjoy it. It is relatively centrally located or at least easy to reach through fast-track calm and spacious. The staff are relaxed and friendly. Newspaper selection good but sometimes worn out in the evening. The drinks selection is very good with one exception - seems very difficult to get an ordinary glass of water carbonated or non-carbonated. The food is simple but substantial and one can have a healthy snack or small meal. There is a section with good views - this is however let down by the constant blare of a TV with CNN.
Quite nicely designed but very poor selection of food reading materials and drinks. Overall very dull with no real flair.

A bit hard to find but well worth it. Quiet seating areas - booths tables and lounges. Wide variety of food and snacks. Short stroll to SAS gate. Would have liked some written instructions for the wireless internet access.

Nice and comfortable place with a very relaxing atmosphere (lounge was nearly empty). Food variety is limited but this is usually healthy and fresh stuff. Good choice of drinks and newspapers. Washroom facilities are very limited. Free wireless internet or PC stations.

SAS shares lounge with Asiana at SeaTac and the lounge is quite small about the size of an average family's rec room. Bizarrely there are no phones with local service available in the lounge. All phones in the F/J class lounge are pay phones and require a credit card to swipe first to make local calls. I complained to the lounge hostess and it appeared that I was the only passenger to ever have complained about not being able to make a local call without charge from the lounge. United's RCC at SEA has free local phones and I believe that is standard at most RCC facilities. The SAS lounge at SEA is also quite warm.

No information given by the counter ground staff upon check in/ bag drop. The Prime Class lounge used by Saudi Arabian Airlines is located after the immigration and can be easily found. It shares the same roofing as the whole airport (open ceiling - just walls) and therefore uncomfortably cold as the rest of the airport. You can only use the lounge for 3 hours. Whether you want to use it during the first or last part of your arrival to the airport is up to you. The lounge is beautifully decorated, giving me the impression of Arabian tents. However it is a small lounge, sufficient as the number of passengers are not many at the time I was there. Very limited food/ drink options. Toilets are satisfactorily clean. Staff are polite.

The lounge in Jeddah spacious, clean and comfortable; the buffet is ok for those without pretensions, the wi-fi in the lounge was instead a problem to be able to connect. La lounge a Jeddah spaziosa, e pulita, devo dire confortevole; il buffet ok per chi non ha pretese, il wi-fi alla lounge è invece è stato un problema per riuscire a connettersi.

WiFi is non existent, staff service below average and I wouldn’t go near the food. Poor value for money. When you approach the staff about the WiFi, her response was “Mine is working fine” and a shrug. They fall well below the standard you expect versus the price of a ticket.

The Cairo Alfursan lounge welcomes you with the traditional Arabic coffee. Tthe best food with variety of choices between vegetarian to meat, chicken and seafood. The desert are special also. A kids area with video games, prayer rooms, showers, sleep area, meeting rooms, smoking room, cabins for families privacy, computers, charging facilities.

Average lounge with limited seating capacity. Food was okay and had good arabic coffee and dates. Play area play area for children is very small and no toys. I would rather use the other lounge in Terminal 2 which is large and has a better variety of food and drinks.

Very nice place, the furniture is new and elegant and the food quality is perfect. Internet service is free and very stable. Kids area is small but was quite and has some kids entertainments and games. The only thing I didn't like was the food quantity.

Having been to all 3 new Alfursan lounges (Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam), I can say that there has been a massive improvement in Saudia's lounge game. Jeddah's Alfursan is quiet small and not as great as Riyadh or Dammam, mostly due to the lack of space. The food quality is excellent in all 3 lounges, as well as the beverages on offer. Staff make you feel very welcome and are always willing to help.

Jeddah Airport is what I would expect hell to be like - so taking this into account, the lounge provided a welcome refuge. Less glitzy than Heathrow but plenty of seats, a good selection of food (possibly better than heathrow), clean, staff continually clearing away rubbish and dishes and an audible flight announcement.

I was greeted by a friendly staff. There was a very tasty and extensive western and mid-eastern food selection and many hot and cold beverages. Beef tenderloin was dry. Frequent table bussing. There was free WiFi that worked fine. Air conditioning was comfortable as was seating. I would enjoy another four hour layover there.

Simply disappointing. I was really frustrated by the computer facility and the internet connection. After having a look at the food presented I simply grabbed a coffee and cake from the Cinnabon Cafe opposite the lounge. It just looked so dull.

The lounges in Dammam are horrible and it would rank it the worst I have ever seen. I do not understand why Skyteam is not setting minimum standards for business class lounges as the Saudia lounges have no international standard as far as I am concerned.

Very poor. Has the basics but very little. Screens telling you of departure times and gates are in Arabic then 5 seconds in English. Even if it was in English it would be pointless because they put your gate up about 10 mins before it opens then everyone runs and form a massive queue from the front. I waited for 45 mins in a queue because flight was delayed and they never opened gate. When I got to the front they said that it was for a different flight and then I had to go to the back of another queue. Disgrace is too good a word for this airport. I have travelled here on and off maybe 5 times in past 18 months and still the same.

Lounge easy to find (just beyond the duty free shop after security). Quite spacious with a good selection of hot and cold food and drinks. The food was a mixture of continental and Arabic which all tasted nice! A nice touch was the arabic coffee and dates. Three large screen LCD tv's within the lounge and free internet usage. Seating area has a selection of small tables and large leather sofas.

Very small accommodation for 18 passengers which is the maximum per A310. The lounge is small when two or more simultaneous flights. We found it unattended and receptionists not too concerned with the well-being of passengers. The lounge is equipped with a tiny bar and refrigerator was padlocked. No special service as far as access to the aircraft. In a scale 0-10 I give them a 1 on the account that at least the door was opened.

Everything is horrible. The young lady that receives you is genuinely uninterested on receiving you or taking the minimum care about your needs. The refrigeration is weak, so it was hot. No food, just uneatable chinese snacks. A couple of drinks and that´s it. Due to delays on the flight, we remained here a couple of hours, and nobody cleaned the tons of garbage on the tables. And of course nobody speaks a word of English, so if you want a nice cup of coffee, you have to go to the cafeteria and spend 15 dollars. Worst of the worst.

A light and airy lounge and very spacious. A good selection of work stations lounge chairs and dining arrangements. Wine beer and non-alcholic drinks were available but they had completely run out of glasses and were using paper cups. The food was mediocre - just a small selection of sandwiches and some noodles. Overall it was comfortable and pleasant but not outstanding.

SATS Premier Lounge located in Changi Airport Terminal-3 can best be described as a low grade, badly arranged, poorly equipped lounge offering mediocre food of low quality with little or no Indian vegetarian options. The "Check In" PIC was totally unprofessional & though we were 3 adults & a 16 month old Infant, she scanned the Dragon Pass that we had & charged for an infant even though infants under 2 yrs of age are free! (I believe this is incorrect since we have availed lounges all over the world (travelling after Covid) & never had an issue with an infant). The layout was cramped, badly arranged with mostly seats facing each other ,giving no privacy except staring into the opposite person's face. Tables & Seating for families were few & difficult to secure. The food was awful! Apart from a "veg pasta dish", there were no other Veg offerings which is shocking, since Singapore has a large Indian Population & most Indians are Vegetarian. A number of food containers were empty & had no food in them (at 12 Noon).There was hardly any hot Indian Veg dishes available. There was some bread slices but NO butter. Salad was a mishmash of tomatoes, cucumber, onions etc. Even Salt packets were missing. Apart from Yoghurt cups, there was no other Dessert. Some Hard Drinks, Liquor & Soft drinks were available, which we did not avail. The Staff were most unfriendly, communicated little. Even the " massage chairs" were mostly inoperational. Out of the two toilets, one was bad. Overall view is that this lounge is of pedestrian quality and it is shocking how badly this SATS Premier Lounge is operated. This lounge should be avoided by those passengers who are looking for a decent meal, quiet ambience & a relaxing environment.

This used to be my favourite airport lounge at Singapore Changi Airport. But during my last few visits (the latest was on 15 Jun 2019), I begin to sense a drop in standards. Food - Very few choices these days. And apart from the laksa, the rest are mainly vegetarian Indian food. So if you are not into spicy hot food, or not a vegetarian, I would suggest to skip this lounge and try somewhere else.  Similarly, the choices of drinks have reduced tremendously over the last 1 year. In place of can Cokes & Sprites, now you have to serve from a machine, but on one occasion the fizzy gas is lacking (imagine non-fizzy Coke?), and on another occasion, the sugar is lacking. Would really hope SATS Premier Lounge would stop any cost-cutting measures and beef up its food and drinks standards to the past. Also noted the serving staff were tired and lacking. Hope, they spruce up the lively and joyous mood that used to fill up the lounge.

You can either enter the lounge through your memberships (e.g. LoungeKey or Dragonpass in my case). Otherwise, you can also pay for per entry. Food selection at this particular lounge is decent. Beer and wine are served. Newspapers and magazines are also provided for your pleasure. Showers are fairly decent and spacious.

I was travelling with Jetstar Asia from Singapore to Ho Chi Minh City and I decided to pay for a lounge visit using my lounge membership. SATS Premier Lounge is located at Level 3. The lounge has decent features like snacks (cereals and sandwiches), fruits, and other beverages. Lounge was fairly empty when I went there in the morning. One feature that ought to be noted was the existence of massage chairs for our use. Overall, the features are pretty good for its price. It lived up to my expectations.

Used my Diners Club to enter and I was relieved to do so. It is head and shoulders above the neighbouring Krisflyer Gold Lounge that I was entitled to use on this flight. Not just because it has toilets and showers that the other lounge lacks but overall it is not as busy, feels more spacious and better laid out. The buffet area is larger with an island servery and not just lined up along a wall. Food and beverage options were all self-served with a Asian and Western choices which was ample for my needs. The seating area has power sockets and USB ports beside every chair. The toilet and shower area was immaculately clean and large enough cubicles to enter with your carry-on and shopping. The high backed chairs were really comfortable along the edge of the lounge overlooking public area. The staff were happy and smiling, also quite chatty when talking to them which made the stay feel quite relaxed. My plates were whisked away very promptly, before I had even noticed at times. The WiFi was simple and easy to connect to with no passwords required and speeds were adequate for the simple browsing I was doing.

This was my second time in Singapore Changi Airport SATS Premium lounge. I used my Priority Pass membership card to access the lounge since I wasn't flying in business. Lounge is clean and spacious. Food they serve is Indian and Chinese and quite good. You can also get alcohol (beer, 2 types of red and white wine and spirits). Compared to other Changi lounges this was better then most of them and I would recommend using this. They have also showers, magazines and computers. Wifi is better in the lounge than Changi free wifi. All in all very good lounge.

We used Scoot in Style with our booking. That allowed us entry to the SATS Lounge in Changi Terminal 2. It is shown on the barcode of your boarding pass and that is scanned at entry. The lounge is quite big and well worth the cost. Plenty of drinks, alcoholic (whiskey, wine, gin, vodka) and soft. The coffee is delicious.. Everything is self serve, so you can eat as much as you like. Best was the beef stew, nice and tender. Staff were cleaning all the time and topping things up. For a 2 -3 hour stop, you could easily recoup value for the cost.

An okay lounge compared to Air China facility at this airport. Have to go up to top floor in lift and most irritating aspect was the smell of cigarette smoke - despite this lounge being non smoking. A fair selection of Chinese style food is provided and limited choice of drinks. Staff very nice and friendly but cannot speak much English. Internet service was not that good and the choice of newspapers is of course rather limited. A pleasant alternative to the main terminal waiting areas.

We used Scoot in Style with our booking. That allowed us entry to the SATS Lounge in Changi Terminal 2. It is shown on the barcode of your boarding pass and that is scanned at entry. The lounge is quite big and well worth the cost. Plenty of drinks, alcoholic (whiskey, wine, gin, vodka) and soft. The coffee is delicious.. Everything is self serve, so you can eat as much as you like. Best was the beef stew, nice and tender. Staff were cleaning all the time and topping things up. For a 2 -3 hour stop, you could easily recoup value for the cost.

I’m surprised of the bad quality of this Singapore Airlines lounge in Terminal 2. It’s like an old canteen, noisy and uncomfortable. I don’t understand how Singapore Airlines can offer this to their premium customers.

You’ll find this lounge on Level 4 of the Departure Hall in the International Terminal near Gate 81.  It’s looks a bit dated so it’s not about to win any awards and it’s on the small side but this is to be expected. Despite a fairly full flight there were no more than 10 people there when I visited so it was peaceful and quiet. There was a surprising range of hot and cold food available as well as a selection of desserts. I was starving so sampled most of everything and took advantage of the coffee machine to have a cappuccino before my flight. All in all it was a pleasant surprise and well worth a visit.

This lounge offered great tasting food & I had the breakfast which was wonderful. Food was hot & quite a good choice available being morning. Juices were fresh & the mango in the small bottles were extremely good. Seating choice was good but lacking proper recliners which would have been nice. As with most business class lounges these days they become overcrowded very quickly & don’t cater to the true business class passenger anymore so this lounge needs to be expanded to provide more space & comfort due to the increase in passenger traffic. WiFi here was good & stable which gets a plus point. Toilets again need to be expanded as only 2 proper toilets with about 10 urinals. 3 showers only so again needs to be doubled. On the plus side they were kept very clean. Staff were very efficient in cleaning up used plates & dishes which was good to see & very respectful towards the passengers using this lounge. Overall these days I tend to use the lounge to eat have a quick sit down then off into the main areas of the airport due to lounges being overcrowded. There are quieter areas in the main airport than lounges these days. Best thing in this lounge was the food which is worth visiting for before you board your flight.

The only good thing about this lounge is the food. It’s a lounge that is well overcrowded, loud & imagine only 3 showers! We didn’t stay there long as your better off in the actual terminal which is less crowded which is hard to believe! It badly needs expanding in all areas & there no windows so feels like a prison. Best to avoid & use the one at T3 if you can.

What impressed me first was the elegant entrance. A screen of floral art, resembling Japanese paintings, and the SilverKris logo beyond gave it a feel of elegance. Receiving a warm welcome I was ushered inside. It's not a particularly large space, and I was later told it could cater to around 100 passengers. It was seven in the morning, and delightfully quiet.  The excellent mood lighting, design, and soothing colours added to its ambiance. There was a plethora of varied styles of furniture and seating. Some also have semiprivate booths, with a reading light and USB charging point - ideal if you need to do some work. The layout seems carefully designed. The first half of the lounge is typically the seating or relaxing area, in the middle features the bar, and beyond is the dining. What secondly made an impression on me was the well-appointed large bar. It looked attractive, with colourful glass and ceramic ornamentals placed above that added to the design. The selection of alcoholic drinks and cocktails was vast. Despite the early hours, I was treated to a glass of Lanvin & Fils champagne. I was promptly offered a second round and later I came back to be served with a large cappuccino. There was also self-service Asahi and Singha draft beer. The third and final thing that greeted me was of course the food section. There wasn't an extensive selection. As it was breakfast time, the hot food dishes seemed minimal. But the variety of other food items made it all so appetising. It was equally the presentation, lovingly laid out with added floral decoration that made it all look so good. Even the boring old white-bread sandwiches looked upgraded! There was a chef circling and replenishing any items. My favourite was the Chinese Dim Sum. The selection including, Cha Siu Buns, Prawn Siu Mai and Steamed Prawn Dumplings was delicious. Tempted to go for seconds, but resisted knowing that breakfast would be also be served on my flight. There were plenty of hot and cold drinks, and the most refreshing was the fresh young coconut water. Although deserts are not my thing, I did indulge in a chocolate Ice Cream from a Hagen das Fridge. All the usual facilities are available, like WiFi and charging points. The washrooms are basic and there are no shower rooms. No sleeprooms either. I guess these are due to the flights being short-haul, and not necessitating such additional facilities. It's clear that the lounge is not designed for long layovers. Overall, this was one of the finer lounges I have visited and reflects Singapore Airlines reputation. I was there for just under two hours, but would have been happy to stay longer.

I am not sure why they were playing Christmas Carols on 17th January 2025. There were many main-courses but none of them could be described as western, the nearest food item being spicy tuna sandwich or egg sandwich. The TV volume was overwhelming when it should actually have been in silent mode (with subtitles). It is probably the worst airline lounge of all of the airlines that are 4* or 5*. Some customers had PED's on full volume and the place was hardly conducive to a pre-flight relaxing experience. The seating was standard except for a couple of lap-top tables. I expected something better of Singapore airlines so was surprised and disappointed

Terminal 2 is not as fancy as Terminal 3 and that is also reflected in the lounge. Terminal 2 being a bit older The lounge is a good size but often very full so not so comfortable in term of noise. Food choice is ok but far below the lounge in terminal 3 There are not enough staff, for example ice cream bowl and spoon runned out. Not enough staff going through the lounge to pick up dirty dishes.

One of only two lounges at Phuket airport, there's no real choice. This lounge is second rate - the staff are pleasant but food and beverage options are poor and very limited. Food doesn't get updated regularly it seems. Seating comfort is average and seating seems old.

My ticket was with Asiana Airlines but as a Star Alliance Gold member I was able to enter the SilverKris Lounge of Singapore Airlines. The food is superb (they were serving chili crab for lunch and a made-to-order bowl of laksa), the bar is well-stocked and well-staffed, the facilities are top-notch , they offer skincare masks for the face and neck). Definitely the best lounge in Incheon T1.

Visited in June 2023 and the lounge was amazing, there was a various amounts of meals, beverages to choose on. I visited the lounge on dinner time, they had an option of bolognese pasta with cheese, French fries and nuggets, dim sum, prata, etc. Everything is free to grab, all the meals are displayed in one area and you can grab as much as you want. They also had ice cream in the fridge. They also provided wine, champagne, soft drinks, coffee, water, anything you’d like to drink. The lounge was very clean, there was many staff coming to each table, looking if you’re done with your meal so they can clean up the mess and the dishes. The lounge is also very big, bathrooms inside were clean. Showers are also provided, as well as the towel, hairdryer, soap, toothbrush. Be reminded you have to book a reservation for the shower! There was also an area where you could sleep or rest for free. No reservations needed for this one. Wifi was very strong, I could play games, scroll through TikTok, open instagram, text in WhatsApp, etc.
A very busy lounge in the late afternoon. Good food offering, alcohol only available from manned bar and pretty standard. Difficult to get two seats together.

Wonderful lounge to rest before catching the flight to Dubai. This lounge has improved since the last time I flew with SQ. The lounge was nice and kept clean at all times! I was happy enough with the much and better improved lounge at Changi Airport Terminal 3.

First time in new lounge, absolutely packed, seating layout is not well thought through here, many 6 seater semi circle bays were taken up by 2 people either lying down to sleep or full of their bags. Other lounger seats with kids lying asleep. Use of space very inefficient. Aircon not working well and Wi-Fi not working. I have been traveling SQ business class for 30 years and this is by far my worst lounge experience.

Flying with EVA Air, I had the option of Air Canada's Maple Leaf Lounge or Singapore Airline's Silverkris Lounge. I decided on the latter, based on my high expectations of SA. However, I was warned it can get crowded. There was no smiling welcome, but a polite gesture towards the entrance. My first reaction was how small the lounge was, considering it shared it with other airlines as well as two night flights that evening with Singapore Airlines. There was a variety of seating options, tightly spaced restaurant style dining tables, lounge chairs, stools and a few cubicles, but which did not offer any privacy. One side of the lounge had a view of the apron with aircraft in their air jetties. Within half an hour of my visit, the place had got so crowded, that one had to share the seating where others were grouped and chatting. This prompted me to head to the tiny bar which had four bar stools. The drinks selection was limited, but a friendly barman made all the difference, and he was grateful when I showed him how to make a Manhattan cocktail for me. This opened up a chat and along with a few other fellow passengers who gathered standing around, and engaged in small talk, which helped to pass the time pleasantly. One passenger did complain when asking for champagne, was offered only prosecco! When I commented on how busy the place was to the barman, he replied "it can get a lot more crowded than this". There was a nice selection of finger food and salads, elegantly displayed, but small items of hot food - vegetarian noodles, chicken curry, pasta and boiled rice. I loved the little freezer filled with tubs of chocolate ice cream too. The toilets were basic, and although clean, there were no toiletries whatsoever. With all the praiseworthy reviews about Singapore airlines, one expected the lounge to reflect that glamour too. Sadly, while all the basic comforts were adequately provided, nothing outstanding helped to enhance the experience one expected. The lounge layout itself felt too crammed and no quiet areas to relax in. Perhaps too many people in too small a space.

Could use this lounge normally only accessible to Business Class and PPS Members, as the SQ Gold Lounge was still under renovation. Very impressed by the new concept, though seating can be a challenge during peak times. There is a good food and drinks selection and a nice perk is a full serviced bar for cocktails.

My first visit to SIA's new 1st class lounge (which in fact is a lounge for Solitaire PPS members only, because first class-passengers may use the 'Private Room') was disappointing. Located in a dark, not well lit tunnel with no daylight, where you can look from the bathrooms in the very end all the way to the lounge-entrance and believe you are located in an ordinary waiting-room rather than a cosy place to relax. The lounge is half of the size of the former 1st class lounge and was overcrowded. In the center you find a huge dining area, which seems compared to the places to relax, oversized. A small bar (less than half size of the former one) is located on the right and behind it you now find a big open kitchen, taking again space from the lounge itself, rather than hidden in the back as in the former lounge. The restrooms are in the back and while the toilets itself now are equipped with Japanese toilets (water flushing and cleaning), one urinal was covered with fluid and paper-waste was on the ground of the handwashing-area. The showers are an improvement, because they have a private toilet, as well now. The amenities however are poor: no shaving foam anymore, just shaving-cream. New is that they got 4 closed rooms, where you can sleep either on Slumberettes or real beds - but for a maximum of 2 hours only - which is by far too little for a good sleep. Boarding Passes also cannot be printed at the lounge anymore, so you need to walk to a SIA-transfer-center outside to get changes done. Wine is being served out of machines, another human touch gone. The choice of drinks is also lower, e. g. no Grand Marnier any more. As for the food, taste was good while cheaper dishes are offered: chicken satay instead of lamb or eggs any style for breakfast only - with neither hash browns or beans offered. No cheese or sushi-platters, overall the difference to the business-class section of the lounge (which I also visited) is marginal. Magazines and newspapers are not available. In the very end, I decided to move to the business-class section of the lounge with bright sunlight, more empty space and a by far more friendly atmosphere. Yes, the quality of the wines and the champagne is still better in the 1st class section, but other than that and the free Häagen Dazs ice-cream offered there, it's not worth all the money you have to spend becoming a Solitaire PPS member just to enjoy this disappointing place.

A very good lounge with good service a la carte dining ordering via app. Food nothing super-special but sufficient portions and options, and all in all definitely okay and above standard. Showers not exceptional but oK. Friendly staff.

Krisflyer Gold lounge is currently shared with Marhaba lounge. It looks bad, sterile. It is good that the lounge has both Asian and Western food - but the food is very average. If getting the last good meal in Singapore is important,  go to Singapore Street Food and don’t bother with the lounge. The wine selection is also bad. The French Shiraz lacks body, the Australian Cabernet Sauvignon lacks any form of structure. Tip: just get South Australian red wines for a cost effective safe bet. If the benefit of gold is using this loungee, then the only real benefit of Krisflyer gold is the extra baggage.

The Silver Kris Lounge was small but the service was good. At the entrance the staff were very friendly. The food was average compared to the other lounges I went to. The lounge itself was small but was quiet. The atmosphere was nice too and the seats were good.

Singapore Airlines seems to think that their frequent fliers or other Star Alliance gold members deserve less than business class. They seperate the Gold lounge from the business and first class lounges.  The lounge entrance is pretty much the only picture they advertise in their website, and it makes sense because it is the only visually appealing place in the entire lounge. The lounge is dark. The amount of light was equivalent to a dim street. Seats are arranged in rows of four with tables in between them. No dining area or dining tables. I was forced to eat on my lap. The seats themselves almost looked as if they were very dirty. Food was slightly worse than the Silverkris lounge, hot and cold food on offer, but no manned bar, you had to make your own gin and tonic. Rather questionable choice of meat, three chicken dishes, two veg dishes and pasta or rice. There was also stacks of dim sum available on wooden trays. Wifi was the same speed as the airport wifi, not bad. No showers were available. I only wanted a quick shave but this was not possible and the toilets were small. I did not enjoy my time in this lounge.  I would like to say that this was in no way a 5 star experience. I would avoid flying Singapore Airlines in the future because of the way they treat Star Alliance gold members.

Outstanding Ahlan Business Class Lounge that is used by Singapore Airlines. There a hot and cold buffet line, and an a la carte menu to order from. I ordered the Ramen bowl and it was really tasty, and my wife had the Bruschetta and Melanzane Alla Parmigian and she loved both items. Beside the self serve hot and cold beverage bars, there was a full service bar stocked with just about anything you would expect in a Business Class lounge. The seats in the dining area were comfortable and there was also a super comfortable lounging area where you could sit back and relax. The dining room and lounge areas were clean, the staff was constantly picking up the used dishes and service items. The bathroom was elegant and well kept. Service was outstanding, led by the bartender Allan.

On May 7, 2019 we spent 3 hours in the Ahlan Business Class Lounge waiting for our flight to SIN. This place is outstanding! Seats in the dinning area were very comfortable. The food options were great, not only was there a hot and cold buffet line, there was also an ala carte menu to order from. I ordered the Ramen bowl and it was really tasty, and my wife had the Bruschetta and Melanzane Alla Parmigian and she loved both items. Service was outstanding, led by the bartender Allan. Thank you Allen, you made our time at the Ahlan Business Class Lounge extraordinary!!

There is a manned bar, large buffet spread of hot and cold items, ranging from just pre-packaged sandwiches and hot pastry, ice cream, a large handful of hot food and two items made-to-order: Laksa and Char Kuay Teow. I must say, we weren't hungry after leaving. Seats seem to be plentiful, and most of the people are here for the food, so the table seats were the most popular. I did not make use of the work pods, but there were a few available. The thing that I can't understand about most Singapore Airlines lounges seems to be their location. This lounge felt like an underground bunker due to the absence of windows - a little bit of daylight is very much appreciated. Staff were extremely friendly and polite, however they felt slightly robotic.
Comfortable lounge at Heathrow Terminal 2, well staffed and an excellent cooked breakfast on offer before our 10.50am flight to Singapore. A very good start for our holiday to Australia

The lounge is large but it gets very crowded, difficult to find seats. When people cough, it sounds like an infirmary. The lounge has some power points that are almost always taken. The power points require an adaptor if you do not have Singaporean power plugs and you can deposit your boarding pass at guest services in exchange for an adaptor. Food is not bad - quite a lot of vegetarian dishes available too. Service is outstanding- everyone including the old lady who clears dishes were so friendly and now. Still due to the massive crowds and given how wonderful Changi airport is, I think visiting the airport attractions would have been a much better option.

Overall small cosy very good lounge. Menu and service at the table. And good food Good service from the employees. More difficult with the manager of the lounge at the beginning , sort of attitude. Then he relaxed himself. It is a pity because the first impression counts a lot.

A small lounge in Perth airport that is big on quality and service. Comfortable seats, a good variety of food ranging from Western to Australia - both hot and cold. Serving utensils are replaced very regularly, and used plates are cleared very quickly. Wide selection of beverages, wines, liquors and beers. Staff service is the most impressive. Very friendly and efficient.

Terminal 3 has the biggest SQ Lounges which are relatively new. For me the design is not so nice, dark and not very modern and there are not really relax areas. The internet was  bad, almost no connection. The lounge gets very crowded and I had to wait to find available seating, food choice is good. Staff was not very friendly to me. Good is they have shower facilities (you need to queue for this service if the lounge is busy). Their lounge is really disappointing!

The Private Room is definitely one of the best first class lounges. Not crowded, good restaurant, no buffet, but waiters to bring you whatever you want. May be one of the shower room could be with a bath.

Star Alliance lounge at Paris CDG used by Singapore Airlines. The first class part is separated from the general business lounge. Nothing to compare with the home based first class lounge in Singapore. But everything is perfect.

The lounge was small, hence, it was crowded. It was hard to look for a seat. The variety of food was good, but the quality is just okay. There’s no made to order food. Alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages were aplenty. Complimentary WiFi provided had decent speed. Not a great lounge, it just isn’t bad.

As a business class passenger on intra-european flights without Star Gold status, this lounge is a perfect option at T2 in Heathrow, as it offers a quite high value. There is a wider range of food and the ambiance is nice, calm and more luxurious. The 10-15 minutes walk to the A gates was worth it.

I accessed the Singapore SilverKris lounge with my Star Alliance Gold Status. It is a spacious Lounge with a variety of different seating possibilities (Chairs, Sofas, Armchairs, Quietchairs). The variety of food is good and consists of cold snacks, salads and warm dishes as well as desserts and ice cream. The bar has a broad variety of spirits and some cocktails such as the Singapore Sling. I can absolutely recommend the Singapore Airlines SilverKris Lounge at Heathrow.

I visited this lounge twice during transit on MEL-SIN-LHR and return a week later. The lounge was very comfortable and had a good amount and choice of food and drink. It was well cleaned and not too crowded. The one drawback was that on my first visit, 3/6 of the men's showers were not working. This led to long queues and wasn't really good enough for a Business Class lounge. This was fixed by the time I returned a week later. The other matter of concern was that they didn't make a boarding call for my flight to Melbourne on the return trip. I didn't realise the lounge was a long way from the gate. Including the security check, it took 20 mins. If I hadn't been checking the time myself, I could have arrived after they closed the flight.

It’s a large lounge with comfortable seating but I personally find it too dark, too claustrophobic without windows.
