The catering is good, Hot food are really fresh and regularly refilled to avoid staling, lots of beverage including fresh beer dispenser, and selections of good wines/ champagne. Staff are very polite and keep the place spotless. There are working area equipped with public computer, strong and fast WiFi connection, shower facility in the restroom section are well stocked with basic toiletries, not very luxury looking but adequate.

A small but fine lounge. Singapore Airlines manage to reserve the gate of every single flight right opposite to the lounge to maximize convenience. There are lots of comfortable seating with calm, quiet atmosphere. Foods/drinks are of good quality and plentiful. Beer and cocktail are available fresh by a bartender, there are choices of wine for passengers to help themselves. If they can add a shower facility, it would be a perfect lounge.

We visited this lounge twice on a 15 hr layover. We enjoyed the solitude of this lounge and were well served. However, we did not feel this lounge really differentiates itself well from the business lounge or first lounge. Further, the lack of atmosphere meant we didn't think this lounge had any kind of x-factor. We had some mediocre food from the a la carte menu and the soup was tasty. However, the other food we ordered was not very flavoursome and assume it was just microwave. The bar service was equally poor. We ordered what might be considered an obscure cocktail (grasshopper). We were actually surprised when the waiter said he could make it. 5 minutes later he came back and said half the ingredients weren't available. Then he proceeded to twice recommend a rusty nail which is an entirely different drink. First world problems but we just expected a lot more from Singapore Airlines & we've been in better business class lounges.

This is a very small lounge which Singapore airlines shares with Swiss International. SQ flies the A380-800 from JFK to SIN with a huge number of business class passengers. There were limited seats and there was even a queue to the toilet. There were a good selection of food; but I decided instead to explore the airport instead of staying in the lounge. To be fair, the lounge is clean the staff polite. But with the number of people using the lounge I would rather spend time somewhere else, unless you really need to use the WiFi.

This handling lounge at Chennai used by Singapore Airlines must easily rank as the worst lounge I have used anywhere in the world. It should have been demolished long ago. There is seating space for just about 20 people and it gets full easily since it is being used by multiple airlines. The food selection is very limited, the toilets can accommodate only two people at a time and the wifi is slow. There are a couple of other airline lounges at Chennai that are far better than this one. By using this dump as their lounge Singapore Airlines has disgraced itself. I am assigning a rating of 1 only because I cannot go any lower.

This is the first time I visited the lounge since it was revamped. The lounge looks way better than the previous one, and has special seating for relaxation, families, eating and even around the bar (it has a bar). On big big plus point I see is the variety and quality of food. They served local Thai (Pad Thai, Curry, etc.) and even local Singaporean (Mee Sua, Ondeh Ondeh, etc.). Best selection so far for a business lounge. When it was boarding time, the staff did not announce it loudly and instead told the lounge guests personally.

The lounge is clean and quiet. After Singapore's own flights depart the lounge is pretty much empty, besides a few people traveling on EVA Air or Air China. The SilverKris Lounge offers an extensive buffet available at all time. Free Wi-Fi is offered at a decent speed (fast enough for YouTube watching). Staff in the lounge is nice and always ready to help.

The most fantastic lounge I have experienced. Truly exceptional service and very private. When we entered the lounge we are escorted past the business and first lounge to a special area for people who have first or suites seats on the plane. The private room offered personalised menu, where we can choose a specific dish which is prepared fresh from the kitchen. During the wait and after the food is served there are a buffet of appetisers (salads, cheese) and also a wide selection of deserts (log cake - as it was just Christmas, exquisite chocolates, fruits). Wide selection of good wines and other alcoholic beverages. If you happen to fly First/ Suites on SIA, please do drop by this lounge

We visited this lounge 2 hours before our departure to SIN. SIA did not have their own lounge and thus it seems all star alliance airlines departing from HND had to use this lounge. Super overcrowded lounge,  could not get any seats in the lounge area and had to settle for bar stools in the eating area. We registered to use the showers and was told that there are 27 passengers waiting in line for the lounge. When it was time for boarding (1.5 hours wait later), there were still 11 passengers in the queue before our turn. Food and beverage (including alcoholic drinks) were good, the lounge had even a by-order ramen which we could order. The biggest fault of this lounge is the fact that they combined all business class fliers and gold card holders in the same lounge using the same facility thus it is overcrowded (other airports like in Changi or even Helsinki-Vantaa they have clear separation of facility use by level of membership). The staff are very friendly and accommodating. I do not recommend this lounge if you are looking for privacy and comfort.

The lounge, though windowless, is very comfortable. It also has a spacious shower/toilet combo. The food was delicious and varied. You’ve got a couple of hot choices as well as cold ones. This particular lounge offers ice cream, which is a rarity. Let’s hope not many reads this review, otherwise the lounge will become too crowded as those flying Thai, United, Air NZ, and other Star Alliance airlines would flock to this lounge instead of their appointed lounges.

SilverKris Business Class Lounge Terminal 3. A big and comfortable modern lounge. do not disturb and mobile phone free areas are available. HGigh quality beverage with high variety is available. Nice international food is there too. Pretty crowded in the prime time at departure of intercontinental flights.

Substandard and very limited food selection for a business class lounge. No showers and no toilets inside the lounge (first I've seen like that). If only it removed the word 'gold' expectations would be lowered. Not recommended as there are better facilities and lounge areas in the main terminal.

This Anfore lounge has never been a great experience to start your flight, but this last time was no improvement. It was like a cattle pen, with no seats available, with passengers from many airlines using it. It was a relief to get on to the plane. Not an easy problem to solve, but remember that Emirates flies out each day.

I was flying by Singapore airlines from Surabaya to Singapore. I visited Concordia Premier Lounge in Surabaya. This lounge is located behind security control. This airport has only 3 gates for international flights so lounge is not very big but he is spacious and really nice arranged. There is a lot of meals to choose (also hot) but unfortunately they are only Asian style. Choose of beverages was quite poor, however satisfy me. Seats are very comfortable and they are located in the groups so they are giving a feeling of privacy. I got wifi password to be used inside the lounge, but it was not working during my stay. Toilets was clean. Lounge crew was very helpful with any questions.

I was flying by Lufthansa from Singapore to Frankfurt. I had visited KrisFlyer Gold Lounge in Singapore and I'm quite disappointed. I expected more from lounge in hub of five-star rated airline. Toilet was outside, shared with another lounges and terminal. There was no beds or even chaises to straighten my legs. Some of electrical outlets was not working because they was heavily worn. All chairs was in one big spacious room giving no privacy. Wifi was breaking every hour and force you to go to airport page to see an AD. However catering was in good level with choose of Asian and European food. There was also good choose of beverages. Lounge crew was really kind and they clean lounge very often. Wifi was really fast and finally I found working power outlet so I spend few hours feeling comfortable.

I found this lounge to be busy and impersonal. Returning to Perth, in the morning, we stopped into this lounge for about 2 hours. Check in to the lounge was a person glancing at your boarding pass and saying "OK" and nothing else, no greeting, no nothing; it was packed inside as well. Impossible to find a seat to sit down and eat at. Plenty of chairs, but none really conducive to eating a meal were free (there are probably about 60 bench seats in the whole lounge which I estimate seats about 350. Barely saw a smile from any staff and they weren't really present anyway. Lounges in other cities/countries have coffee/drinks prepped and served by someone, whereas here it's a freeforall. Couldn't get the wifi to work - kept cutting out. Perhaps more attention is paid to their First Class customers, but this was a bit of a let down altogether. Would've expected more personalized service/better facilities given this is the flagship location for Singapore Airlines. Food selection was quite good and was stocked fairly regularly.

The new SilverKris lounge in Brisbane was a real treat. Compared to the old dark hidden away lounge. This new lounge located on level 4 overlooking Gate 81 (where most Singapore Airlines flights depart from) airs out a warm, opened and friendly atmosphere. The lounge at no stage felt crowded with enough seating for everybody. The Business class cabin on this flight was nearly at capacity with only 2 spare seats. So 22 people plus Star Alliance and Virgin Australia gold members flying economy in the lounge. The high celling and open design along with the warm and vibrant colours. Make for a very welcoming lounge. Food selection was excellent as was the beverage selection. Both hot and cold dishes to choose from. As well as snacks such as nuts, chips and cheese. The beverage selection was equally good. Two reds on from France and one from Australia, Soft drinks, one cider, and 4 beers of which one was a mid strength. No champagne was on offer but a sparkling white from Australia and 3 white wines. The lounge staff was friendly and attentive. There was only two of them but more wasn't required. Empty glasses, bottles and plates were cleared almost immediately and rubbish or spills around the serving areas were none existent. Internet was fast and easy to connect too. Another great product provided by Singapore Airlines and even better than the old lounge.

Visited this Singapore Airlines Lounge at Heathrow on a Thai Airways ticket after sampling United Lounge. Front desk more welcoming and responsive. Lounge is a bit of a decorative disaster with ill matched chairs and a funny system of informal and formal eating spaces. Same Champagne as in United First lounge. Still no Economist available (they only order 12 per week!), they only had Time. Better breakfast offer than in their Business Class lounge. I ordered scrambled egg with smoked salmon and Laurent-Perrier champagne. I was offered one of the laid out fancy tables. The scrambled egg was identical to the freshly delivered product in the Business buffet section - delicious. The smoked salmon was thick cut, with some inedible gristle and not seemingly a premium product. I did not see the lunch menu. Service was willing but being more busy than United lounge was overstretched. They need at least one more employee on duty. I agree with other reviews that this is nothing special. I regret that when Singapore Airlines First was in Terminal 3 at least you could go to the SAS London Lounge to get good serious publications. If you read my United post, remarkably United had the New Statesman (always available in the old SAS lounge) but little else of interest.
A home away from home is how I would describe it. Very specious, has all the amenities like wifi, shower, and great warm and cold food. I had a few hours to kill and glad that spent in the lounge.

Singapore Airlines use the Turkish Airlines lounge at Istanbul Ataturk Airport. A variety beverages and foods provided, foods taste good, mostly local food, ample seating area with theatre (chair was torn and broken, malfunction) wifi speed reasonable.All areas are clean except theatre -  no cleaning at all. Desktop PC's are available however speed are slow. Washroom and shower room are very clean, but the staff service are the worst of this lounge, lounge front desk is so messy. Before you enter to lounge, you need to scan boarding pass to enter, however, the scanner did not read other airline boarding pass,yo u are required to proceed to front desk to register your boarding pass. I tried a few times and unable to get thru the gate, finally a staff notice and ask me proceed to front desk, no assistance at the access gate as there are at least 5 staffs are sitting there. Shower facilities staff is arrogant and impolite. I am asking for shower in polite tone, she just answer 'wait for 30 minutes'. not even a apology for long wait waiting time.

I have to say that the Kris Flyer Gold Lounge in Singapore is very disappointing. I sometimes wonder what benefit is it being a Gold FF with SIA. When you have just got off a long-haul flight and you just want to relax and refresh and you walk into this disappointing lounge where there No showers, No bathrooms, No rest areas. (Quite Area). When you compare with the oneworld group lounges at Singapore and if you are Gold FF with BA, Qantas, JAL etc you would have access to far superior products all of them have showers! Singapore airlines this lounge is such a disgrace for a so-called top airline.

A reasonable lounge, but quite basic when you stop and remember this is First Class. Used the lounge on a Thai Airways flight, and have to say that the United Airlines lounge nearby will be my choice next time. Arrived as a Singapore Airlines flight was leaving, and a bunch of rowdy passengers off that flight were being quite rude to staff working in the lounge. Foods from buffet are quite basic, they do offer a cooked breakfast and reasonable all day dining menu. Wifi access easy and quite good. Washrooms on the basic side and were just passable for cleanliness. Staff on reception were polite but useless in terms of any information or updates on 1 hr delay. After all the hype that seems to go with Singapore Airlines, this lounge is really very disappointing.

The new Singapore Airlines lounge at Heathrow Terminal 2 is absolutely lovely. It is spacious and light and offers a variety of seating options - eg lounge chairs, working cubicles, tables and chairs for eating etc. There was a good range of tasty hot and cold food, which was being monitored constantly, as well as a cocktail bar. Tables were cleared regularly and the bar-tenders also provided table service. All the staff were extremely helpful and friendly.

Krisflyer Gold Lounge Terminal 3. Why can a 5 star airline such as Singapore Airlines treat their Star Alliance or partner airlines with such a second rate experience compared to how their own passengers are accommodated in the nearby SilverKris Lounge? No toilets is just the beginning. I can excuse having no showers but having to exit the lounge to use the public facilities which are not so easy to find around some corners. I am sure the staff are sick of having to pass on directions to the constant stream of travellers passing through this busy lounge. Speaking of which, this is a busy lounge and can be crowded at times. The buffet servery is small and arranged along the end wall of the lounge, making it crowded to access some dishes. The raised tables near the eatery have a range of power sockets and USB ports here which means these tables can be filled with people using their computers and charging phones because there are few other options elsewhere, making it difficult to eat your meal. No announcements are made for flights so one had to be conscious of their own flight times and gate details as some can be quite distant away.

Newly opened lounge is a huge improvement on the old SilverKris Lounge at Brisbane Airport. It is opened as per the flight schedule from BNE. It is tucked at the end of a long corridor behind the new Plaza Premium and Air NZ lounges, all overlooking the main central airside retail area (above the foodcourt). Upon entry there is a small nook with a tv and lounge seating for about a dozen people. Then you pass the toilets and business suites before the space opens up with the buffet servery on the right and lounge seats beyond. The dinner selection was not huge but tasted good with Asian and Western choices on hand. The staff were quite chatty and I had a good talk with the chef on duty there. After relaxing in one of the high backed chairs overlooking the foodcourt, I asked one of the staff if I could watch the Tour de France tv coverage in the smaller lounge area, as there was only one television in the main lounge with a lady glued to a local drama on it, which they obliged me but they warned me that I might need to move due to an expected VIP arriving soon, but the VIP allowed me to remain in place. The seats in the smaller nook had a low back, so despite looking stylish, they were not really that comfortable. With plenty of notice, we were called to board our flight at a relaxed pace.

I fly Swiss International but they use the Singapore Airline lounge at Hong Kong airport. The lounge was good, adequate food though not to compare with the Cathay lounge, and it is spacious and uncongested. A relaxing time before the late night departure.

Singapore Airlines uses the Premier Lounge at Denpasar Bali which is shared with other airlines and Priority Pass. I would have assumed that for the large number of premium passengers on Singapore Airlines going to Bali (my flight had a full J class in and out, so I'm assuming it might be the norm), it still surprises me why Singapore Airlines would not invest in its own lounge at DPS. Premier is crowded with unreliable wifi. Food is inedible and drink selection limited. The washroom and shower (singular) is dirty and not so well maintained. I encountered a lot of friendly people in Bali and I guess they throw the rejects here. Would pass on this one next time.

SilverKris Business Class Lounge at SIN T2. At 7am, the lounge was crowded with barely a free seat in any of the sections. Queues in the buffet and drinks area reminded me of the overcrowded and poorly maintained lounges in US airports. I find the lighting in the lounge too subdued.  The food on offer was quite tasty and the variety more than adequate. Coffee was OK, but not as premium as expected. For an airport as nice, clean, bright and well maintained as Changi, I find the T2 business class SKL a bit of a disappointment.

The Singapore Airlines SilverKris lounge in MNL, while small and has limited food options compared to its SIN counterpart, has numerous things going for rather than against it. For one, Manila not being a Singapore Airlines hub, the only planes flying out are B772/773 and A330s so there are only a few J class passengers using the lounge, therefore avoiding the crowded feel that is the norm for the Changi T2 SilverKris business lounge. There is a limited view of the tarmac, but still allows for plane spotting. As mentioned, the food options are limited, and the toilets are small but clean. Way better than waiting at the gate.

A spacious Singapore Airlines lounge at Heathrow terminal 2 with various seating options. A good food offering - I was there for breakfast, and what looked like good drinks options. The lounge has a view of the outside and supplies a number of magazines and newspapers. It was clean and tidy. In all, very good.

This EBL SkyLounge is one of the better lounges in Dhaka. The food choice is excellent; but they do not serve alcoholic drinks. The wifi was good, the toilets and shower room was also quite good. The only negative I can say is, the lounge got crowded when there were few flights departing at a time. Strongly recommend if you are travelling through Dhaka, as the general facilities in the airport are quite rundown.

The Krisflyer Gold Lounge is very clean and has a wide array of food and beverages. It also has a quiet and tranquil environment and a lot of seats for passengers to sit and relax. The krisflyer lounge also offers strong wireless network and also have friendly staff to help you. My experience at the lounge was certainly pleasant.

Krisflyer Gold lounge is very basic, no shower, no toilet and very hot. Lounge uncomfortable and small. Food basic and not good! Dont see why gold members should be seperated from the business lounge. The Internet kept dropping out. This is the second time I have experienced this lounge and had the same experience both times.

Had booked my flight in First class with points and was looking forward to my first time in a First class lounge. Was somewhat disappointed but probably expectations too high. Was warmly greeted and upon arrival there were only two others in the lounge. Only 4 passengers in First for the flight and ended up with 12 in the lounge. Would expect others would have have been there due to status. Food was self service and not a great selection. Champagne was Moet. Wifi easy to connect to. Chairs comfortable. Only saw staff when they were there to top up the food or beverages or take away plates.

Singapore Airlines uses the Lufthansa lounge in Dubai Airport. Located near the lounge that Singapore Airlines used previously. Staff were pleasant with good wifi that was easy to connect. Toilets within the lounge but no showers. Beer was glass bottles of Erdinger with cans of Amstel. Wine selection only average. Sparkling wine was a Californian Brut "Cooks" which I did not like with two reds and two whites. The reds were a 2010 Bordeaux Chateau Lagrange Les Tours and a 2014 Rouge from Cotes De Gascogne. The whites were a Pinot Grigio Delle Venezie and a South African Sav Blanc Nederburg. Best of the food was a Indian type chicken dish with rice. Otherwise sandwiches and wraps.

A beautiful lounge with comfortable seating. The selection and quality of beverages and food available, both hot and cold, was exceptionally good. The staff were welcoming and unobtrusive. The restrooms and lounge were tidy and clean. This was a lovely, calm place to relax before the next leg of an extremely long journey.

Regular customer of Singapore Airlines Krisflyer Gold Lounge at Changi Airport. Singapore Airlines  discriminates its gold members seated on the economy class and business class passengers unlike most airlines at its own base, Changi Airport. Facilities are not too comfy, even compared to Silverkris lounges abroad such as the one at Heathrow T2, also compared to other airline lounges such as Asiana at Incheon, Lufthansa at Heathrow T2, etc. The lounges at T2 and T3 Changi Airport only features basic single sofas and side tables with limited work stations. There is no shower and food if arriving late at night/early morning. It is a bad idea to discriminate loyal customers (even though they are in the economy class).

The business class lounge of Singapore Airlines at Heathrow is not too big. I like the layout of the lounge and food was very nice. They served asian breakfast which is nice surprise. The downside is they don't have computer and printing facilities, but customers can use the business facilities of the Air Canada lounge which is next door.

Singapore Airlines Business class lounge at Changi Airport was very impressive. Neat and tidy, and the food and presentation excellent. I loved the shower available free of charge. A very pleasant venue to spend time waiting for a flight.

Le Anfore handling agent lounge. Worst lounge I have been in. Very little food. What there is is stale. Staff are okay but not very happy nor helpful. Dirty toilets. Men's toilet did not even have a seat!

I was flying Turkish Airlines and as a Star Alliance Gold member I had a choice of a number of lounges. I tried the United Airlines lounge first as I heard some positive reviews. However also decided to try the Singapore Airlines lounge. I arrived at around 10.15am. As well as the expected English breakfast buffet, I was glad to see Chicken Sambal on offer. It was really excellent: chicken on the bone (or rather falling off the bone) and I added rice, hard boiled egg and chilli - I really really enjoyed it. I accompanied my brunch with a glass of champagne. The decor was very agreeable, lots of brown leather seating and a good view of the apron. The lounge is not as big at the UA lounge and it does not offer as much natural light. But the decor and food offering makes it a better lounge for me.
The Kris Flyer Gold Lounge in Singapore is miserable. The food hasn't changed for a long time and I am flying SIA regularly. No showers no rest areas.  A shame for a top airline.

Huge lounge with a great selection of food and ample drinks. Superb showers that were cleaned after every use by the attendant and I was even whisked into the first class shower units as there was a queue and 'they didn't want me to have to wait'. Only downside is the lack of nap cabins or a quiet area for a long stop over. Internet was a bit hit/miss very difficult to connect to but worked well when it finally connected.

Very spacious lounge. The individual desk carrels in the back are extremely comfortable and ideal for work. Staff were quite nice. Food was less than mediocre. Biggest drawback is that lounge is a giant den with no windows so mobile reception was iffy at times.

The lounge is one floor down from the departure gates and there are no signs to guide passengers specifically to the the Silverkris Lounge (in contrast to SIA's competitors). Follow the sign that reads: "Other lounges". The premises appear tired and worn with what looks like 1980s decor. This lounge is definitely in need of refurbishment. The bright white neon lights lend it a cafeteria feel. Food and beverage offerings were limited by SIA standards.

Good variety of drinks. Decent selection of food choices. Chairs not exactly the most comfortable. Big negative is no toilets but it appears from other reviews that this is an issue with other lounges in this airport.

A very comfortable if not undersized lounge for the demand placed by the mid-afternoon volume of FFs and Premium passengers on the A380. Food choice was 'good' at best however with the volumes of food offered on board the plane the selection of tasty cold bites and a few hot dishes was more than enough. Staff were exceptional and the hostesses circulated the masses and offered Champagne refills without prompt - a nice touch. The lounge is relatively well appointed but there was no spare seating capacity and I can anticipate this becoming an issue if other Star Alliance FFs flock there given the airlines reputation for high standards in its lounges.

They treat Star Alliance Gold Members as the lower class. Food is not nice no showers not comfortable. I wouldn't recommend this lounge to no one. Airport is nice but Gold Lounge is not comfortable at all.

If you are expecting an experience comparable to the very good services provided by the silver kris lounge in a Singapore you will get a shock. This is a cramped unattractive space with limited facilities that does not compare well with Singapore Airlines overall business class product.

The Port Lounge is a relatively small lounge in Kolkata airport but the food choices weren't bad (Chinese and Indian veg and non-veg including rice fish and other items), you could have a full meal. The alcohol selection is not huge but sufficient. There is a limit on the number of drinks per guest but no one was enforcing such a limit (if it exists). The lounge is clean but it has no view.

We were flying out on Silk air so my normal Star Alliance entrance wasn't applicable. So we used our priority pass card. The lounge was horrible. Stained furniture carpets exposed cables etc. The small amount of food there was looked like it had been there for days. No alcoholic beverages. The whole place looked like a 1950 soviet style lounge. Needless to say we left after 5 minutes. Then they had the nerve to charge my card $34 for each of us even though we should have a free visit! Do not go near Singapore priority pass lounges. I would give them "zero" stars for most choices.

Very average. Every time I am here there seems to be a good gossip session going on among the staff loud and given it is not a self serve bar totally absent when it comes to offering a drink or being at the bar when one is looking for a drink. Much prefer the London lounge a business class lounge close by. Food looks like it has been sitting out forever and again staff don't approach to offer anything from the menu. A shame as Singapore Airlines in flight service is terrific.
Being the HQ large clean lounge. No sleeping rooms like in FC lounge. Bathroom with showers excellent.

Visited the Singapore Airlines T3 lounge at London Heathrow as a passenger with Thai Airways en route to BKK. Star Alliance lounge share. As always lounge was peaceful. Good flow of fresh foods with staff preparing more pastries when they ran short. A much better option than using the London Lounge suggested by Thai as that is a shared First and Business lounge.

New lounge fit-out looks sleek. I travel through Sydney a lot and it was desperate for an upgrade. Staff are friendly. Food really average buffet was cold and tasteless. I would have thought they would have really stepped up a notch with the new look. Unfortunately don't expect to much on the food front.

Lounge is a bit small and in need of revamp. Had internet and plenty of drinks. Food was great and just what we needed. lots of interesting and tasty things on the menu. staff was friendly enough. Seemed fairly busy though.

Visited on 26th December their new revamped lounge. Everything okay and considering they spent some money doing it up they did not really put any effort into the food side. What was on offer was cold meat pie cold grilled sausages curries that were lukewarm (beef rendang that did not even look like the real thing) Chinese congee that had very few condiments and a few other dishes of similar temperature. All served buffet style and obviously as time went by the food becomes less appetizing. Considering they have the Australian consulting chef Matt Moran on SIA's culinary panel why did they not use his talents to come up with something more original like gourmet appetizers rather than the same old tired food formulas. What a disappointment they did not think out of the box in the food department. I wonder why SIA does not win any awards as offering the best airport lounges?

Adelaide Airport - we always make a point of arriving early at any airport and taking time then to relax (approx 2-21/2 hours) but Customs (international gates) at this airport do not open until 90 minutes prior to the international flight so we were unable to access the small Singapore Airlines lounge downstairs. We had assumed that as Virgin are Singapore Airlines "partner" airlines we could use their lounge. Definite not. The customer service lady only granted us access to the Virgin lounge because it was empty we have a Bronze Card and were over 60. Compare that to the excellent Qantas lounge that we had used in the past!

The seating is ok and the decor is simple. This is definitely not the newest lounge and has very little atmosphere. Drink options are unimaginative and not impressive. The only real upside I have to say is that the food is quite good (not many options) - definitely better than the Economy class fare onboard so I always tend to eat my meal in the lounge. WiFi works but is not super fast. The lounge is kept quite tidy by the staff.

The lounge is far too crowded facilities dated and insufficient even for a 747 never mind an A380. Food selection limited to a couple of noodles and a few wilting sandwiches. As for the champagne don't start me on that. Even to wifi was intermittent. The lounge is not disabled friendly with an elevator which has no sides or back to the moving parts.

Different from the better Changi Airport's Krisflyer Elite Gold/Silverkris lounges this one in London is a little bit dirty with some leftovers stains on the carpet more limited choices of drinks no proper meal offered only some tiny tasteless sandwiches and crisps. It's also a lot smaller and much more noisy compared to those in Singapore.

Travelling back to Auckland from Heathrow and after a tedious journey to the airport and then the bun fight getting through check-in and immigration etc we were looking forward to getting in to the Business class lounge to relax and refresh ourselves before the long flight. No chance the lounge was small crowded hot and rundown. The food was minimal consisting of packets of cheese a few biscuits some miserable looking sandwiches and the odd piece if tired fruit fruit. What a let down for a 5 Star airline. Extremely disappointing. Changi was better and so it should be as it is presumably their showplace lounge but not fabulous.

This lounge has no toilet - let alone a shower! It was also very warm. Having got off a long flight from Sydney I was most unhappy. The whole idea of flying business and having access to these lounges is to have an advantage over the rest of the travelers. Not having a toilet and shower is ridiculous! The lounge pleasant enough and service very good but food ordinary.
Lounge was a bit dated however food was great. fantastic variety and very fresh. However did run a little low on portions once it became a bit crowded. Loved the Asian curry.

Used their Changi Airport lounge before heading to Sydney. Facility design is impressive but that's about all this lounge offers. Food are in substandard condition and beverages just as limited as the onboard offering. Too many people about and unsure if it was because I entered during peak times but it felt really cramped. Some tables still had leftover plates and drinks making it look shabby. This lounge does not have bathroom facilities and was told to walk couple hundred metres out of the lounge which I found incomprehensible. Lounge staff pretty much non existent other than at the reception area where they were rude and disgruntled. Very poor lounge to relax in and not worth lugging your bags into.

Silver Kris lounge in T3 - it is a beautiful room ruined by despicable customer service. There were at least five staff in the front desk and not one smiled or made anyone feel welcomed. I watch in astonishment when "elite" passengers were treated like passengers on a bus in a third world country. I don't know if anyone from Singapore airlines will see or read this but the staff on duty on the night of the 1st of May 2013 should really be reviewed especially a short haired Eurasian looking lady. Wished I caught her name but really Singapore airlines needs to lift their game here. When travellers are spending copious amount of money to fly with you make us feel at least welcomed? Silver Kris lounge in T2 - I left T3 because of the overall lack of respect to customers. But what I found in T2 was the direct opposite. This is where everything came good. Staff were so polite and helpful. Goes to show that it does not matter how much you spend on perfecting facilities when you don't have the right people.

Overall a clean and comfortable lounge (both in Terminal 2 and Terminal 3) with a good selection of food. There are no boarding announcements however so make sure to check your ticket for boarding times.

As a gold frequent flyer I was looking forward to relaxing in a lounge on the way back to Australia flying with Singapore Airlines. Given that Singapore Airlines is based at Changi I had high expectations of the lounge quality. However I was directed to the gold lounge that was very disappointing indeed. No service cramped seating flat beer mangy sandwiches and no toilet! I think that Virgin should look for a better code share partner if this is the standard Singapore Airlines have to offer.

The lounge in Adelaide is quite small with no windows but it is only for Singapore Airlines passengers so it didn't really feel all that crowded despite being small. One major advantage is that unlike all of the other lounges it is after immigration and security checks so once you reach the lounge you can just relax. The food and beverage selection is small but sufficient and the toilets (there are 2) are clean.

This lounge was by the far the worst we have ever experienced. It was shabby the staff were rude or just grunted. There were only two toilets one of which was out of order and this was not even clean. The noise level with dishes being clanged and banged at the bar area was unbelievable. SIA need to engage in some serious conversations with Roma airport as the advertising states that "the Le Anfore Business Class Lounge offers a haven of peace from Rome Fiumicino Airport. Treat yourself to the VIP lifestyle!" - well it doesn't!

Very average lounge. Chairs reasonably comfortable but no loungers. No toilets or showers in the lounge. Toilets down very quiet corridor which is worrying late at night. Good food and reasonable selection of drinks. Staff not particularly on the ball.

Very good lounge - lots of food on offer though the selection did not change during my 8 hour stay. The seating was comfy and offering good privacy. The staff were very helpful and even when I walked in and out of the lounge regularly they did not raise a fuss and ask for a boarding pass. The toilets were clean with great showers that were well stocked. The wi-fi was easy to access.

It was really disappointing to access SQ Gold Lounge at Terminal 2 and Terminal 3. No shower facilities available in either lounges. It mainly affects Gold member who transit in Singapore. Gold members are not allowed to access business lounge Singapore gold members do not usually need shower facilities at departure only these poor transit Gold members. It is a big disappointment. After a long flight a shower could make huge difference. Food and drink were limited you don't want to drink a lot anyway because there is no toilet inside the lounge. You have to go outside and bring all your belongings and come back again. So it is another strategy to encourage you drink less and move on quickly. It is really not a lot of point to build up your SQ points you get less and less for benefit.
Lounge is small with very limited food and drink on offer. Not up to the standard of other carrier lounges in Sydney. The restrooms are also very small. I left to eat some overpriced airport food.

SilverKris business class lounge at Changi airport is quite spacious with excellent choice of food offerings. The bar had a good choice of wines and non alcoholic drinks. Good wifi although had a couple of attempts at logging in. Staff service only mediocre as they did not bother to see who was there and kept pestering everybody in the lounge (a total of less than 10 passengers) more than once about missing passengers on some SIA flights. The place was rather claustrophobic without windows and did not have the general airy feeling that was usual at Changi. For a short layover I would just go to the lounge for the food and drinks but exit to enjoy the excellent airport that Changi is.

Sitting here at 1500 hours wondering what happened to SIA's famed food/hospitality. There is one member of staff for the whole lounge serving drinks topping up food (more later) clearing tables etc. The sum total of hot food available is a tureen of lukewarm leek and potato soup. That's it unless you like the one variety of sandwich available or scone and cream or microwave noodles. As for access it's a slog up the stairs or a ride in the service lift. Paint peeling off the radiator in the Gent's loos. Truly low grade compared with their rivals. I had more choice free of charge on the train coming down - bacon sandwiches scrambled egg and smoked salmon for example.

Excellent lounge in Singapore with plenty of room. Good food and wines on offer. Only available for Business passengers on C class tickets not to Star Alliance Gold card holders. Krisflyer Gold card holders in economy must use the lounge next door. Seems a bit off to not allow a larger lounge and have *G use the facilities. I understand that the First Class lounge is currently being renovated and therefore F pax are also using this lounge.

Even as a solitaire member you don't get access to the first class lounge. The business class lounge is really busy on a Thursday evening waiting for the Singapore flight people had to stand. There is rubbish on the tables that does not seem to get cleared for hours. I don't know how much SIA pay for using this but it's too much.

There is still a lack of shower facilities at both T3 and the newer T2 lounges for Krisflyer and Star Alliance Gold Members (SATS lounge at T2 is no longer made available to SIA KFGold Members). As the toilet facilities are located just next to the lounges additional plumbing costs and showers fittings would be at a bare minimum to sat the least - a real disappointment when a shower during transit will be a refreshing welcome between two long haul flights. Singapore Airlines are dropping their standards across the board. A real pity for a once premium carrier.

T3 Business Class Lounge - as usual the staff at the front desk grimaced at all the guests walking in. I was there during breakfast time and the food was dry overcooked. Would have been helpful if they had some fresh fruits - even some apples and bananas on a plate would be helpful. I had a quick bite walked out of the lounge with the customer service staff staring at me. I walk no more than 10 steps out of the lounge turn to go back in as I left my jacket and was stopped at the entrance with a very brusque demanding "Boarding Pass please". Well at least she said please but honestly? If I did not live in Singapore I would never choose to take SQ as my first choice. Customer service is appalling unless you're a well dressed business man.

This lounge is disappointing and perhaps a reflection of how SIA views Star Alliance Gold fliers from other airlines - ie. poorly. The food service area is small with a limited selection of light meals. There are no toilets or showers in this lounge. So it is not a great place for a transit stop. In comparison the SATS lounge in T2 is a better lounge.

I prefer the old brown leather seats in the T2 lounge in Singapore - far more comfortable than the newer seats in the T3 lounge - especially if you have a longish layover. I see they are going to renovate the T2 lounge - I hope that they retain the old leather lounge chairs. I hope if they ever renovate the Sydney lounge that the keep the older brown leather chairs.

I would expect a lot more form Singapore Airlines. Sydney airport lounge is appalling considering the levels of service Singapore claim to offer their passengers. with 4 flights per day from Sydney - and at present two of these are A380 services. The size of the lounge the seating food and beverages all very average. I was very disappointed.

A bit of a journey to find this. Every drink ordered had to be matched to invitation card which was a bit of a farce as they did not keep them in any order. Whilst the decor wasn't special the food and snacks on offer were very tasty. Restrooms nothing special.
The ultimate horror lounge. I was there during peak hour at 11pm. It was so crowded that most had to eat/drink standing. Drink and food choice was reasonable but the size does not match the demand.

Outstanding SIA Business Class Lounge in T3 with many separate sitting areas including one for catching a nap on a sofa. Staff gave me a blanket and pillow and noted my seat number to ensure I didn't miss my flight! Wine and liquor selection somewhat limited. Food selection was excellent with prompt removal of used plates and filling empty food trays. The shower stalls aren't as good as a few competitors but other facilities in the restroom area are very good.

Very quiet and beautifully lit made for a very relaxing wait. the dining and food was great the bathrooms in the first class lounge were stocked full of great toiletries and fluffy towels. overall quite impressive I thought especially after the dreadful 1st class lounge that they use in Terminal 1 at Dubai airport.

A small but well appointed lounge. Plenty of individual body hugging armchairs. A small but very tasty selection of foods including dim sum gourmet sandwiches cold meats yoghurt maggie beer ice cream nespresso coffee machine spirits and soft drinks. Bathrooms clean and well maintained. Staff very friendly and attentive. Free internet and wifi access. Great selection of newspapers and magazines.

Compared to other SQ lounges I have used this was very disappointing. Very small - was awaiting SQ220 departure an A380 with a full Business Class cabin so there were few empty seats. Decided to leave and used the adjacent NZ lounge. Many times bigger better food selection and facilities.

Spacious lounge with clustered seating. Very quiet. Had a good selection of hot and cold dishes and an array of beverages including champagne! Chic look but missed recliner cushy sofas! The washrooms and showers were very clean and attended to! Vast array of newspaper and reading material. Could do with a spa to go with the cool look and good service! The biggest miss was the view of the tarmac!

One of the best lounges I have ever used. Very calm and relaxed ambience. Lots of high quality seating available. Great food and drink selection. Free wifi. Server was down at first but after pointing out the problems I was having logging on manager at the business centre made few calls and had the server re-booted. Empty dishes and tables cleaned frequently. Shower and restroom facilities spotless. Lounge would be perfect if they had a separate "rest area" with lounge chairs and mobile phone restrictions.

There are two minor problems with this lounge: the lack of windows - in common with most of the international lounges at MEL - and the fact that like most of the Silver Kris lounges it is looking a bit dowdy and dated. The amount of space was ok food and drink selection was fairly good and the lounge was very clean.

I agree with the other comments on here about the lack of toilets and showers - completely disgraceful. The lack of lockers for hand luggage is also irritating for a solo traveller as every time you want to get a drink or some food you have to haul all your things with you and potentially loose your seat. Having said that I found the service and atmosphere to be adequate and lounge felt relatively spacious. The food and drinks were fairly plentiful but a bit stodgy.

The lounge is spacious and comfortable and was occupied by another passenger and myself flying on SQ to Singapore. We were informed that free massages were available but unfortunately there was no one available. There was a good selection of Eastern and Western food available for breakfast with a good selection of Sri Lanka tea as well. Toilets were extremely clean with an attendant checking it after each use. Great view of the east side apron and partial view of the runway. Good customer service with SQ ground staff accompanying you to the airbridge.

Definitely dated and was the smallest business/first class lounge I have used. We were there for breakfast just before our flight. Food selection was narrow. The toilets do need upgrading. Another inherent weakness is that they do not offer to look after your handluggage/trolleys whereas in the MAS Golden Lounge you are granted the use of lockers. We were told this was for security concerns; if this was so then MAS would also do the same.

This expansive lounge with its phalanx of greeters the subdued blue-lit translucent columns at entry is as appealing as it is enormous. Huge number of seating options from pleasant views out to the departure gates to snug corners for a snooze. The usual CNN slash ESPN flat screen offerings. A large selection of food; unusual for what you’d expect in a Biz class lounge (SIA has a separate wing for First). About eight hot options some Chinese some Indian as well as dry snacks. Lots of beverage options although probably on purpose the liquor is in a bar area quite far away from the food offerings. There was good scotch Champagne and some OK bar drinks. The array of papers was astounding: All the European dailies plenty of English offerings including a Globe and Mail. The bathroom is large with plenty of showers and has Occitane products. In short our lounge experience far exceeded our flight experience.

This was my first time in the SATS Star Gold Lounge at Singapore. It is big and has a reasonable selection of breakfast food (it was early am). The staff were very efficient and the lounge kept very clean. Not sure if WiFi was available but the lounge did have at least 2 commuter stations with web access. Unbelievably there are no toilets in the lounge. You have to go outside and use a public toilet. There are no showers either in what is a major Star hub this is unforgivable.

Agree totally with Mr Weiss (review 30 October). For a new home base lounge this is totally inadequate. At 8.30am it was impossible to find a private seat. For the one cooking station there was a queue - it really did not matter as there was no table space for one to sit down and eat anyway. I cannot imagine why in a brand new terminal this should happen.

Generally a good lounge with good seating area mind you some lounge type seating would not go astray as we had a four hour layover and it would have been nice to stretch out. WiFi is good but at times very slow. Food okay but have seen better in other business lounges. Plenty of space and lots of seating so finding a good corner not a problem. The showers are especially welcoming and staff are very helpful. They should have a wider range of wine as they only had Reisling on offer. Generally not a bad lounge but I cannot understand why Singapore Airlines do not announce flight departures.

Small and dated lounge but with a nice view of the gates and runways. Food selection so so. However the washrooms were old and not maintained. The public ones were much cleaner. Definitely not up to SIA standards.

Disappointed in the fact that the lounge overlooks the departure gates and has no direct natural lighting. The atmosphere and decor are pleasant. The buffet with a chef preparing breakfast orders is nice but the restaurant seating area is clearly insufficient for the number of passengers. The same facility in the Business Class section appeared just as overtaxed. For smokers there is an outdoor terrace located immediately outside the lounge entrance.

This lounge is apparently a new one opened by SIA. There is a long trek to it - too much of walking actually. The reception staff are warm and just welcome you but do not give much information of the lounge. The worst part is that the lounge does not have any toilets or showers! Something really unacceptable for a newly opened lounge in such a spic and span airport. Hot and cold food items are present and internet access is also free. Overall a good lounge but marred totally buy lack of toilets and its distant location.

Overall a decent lounge. Plenty of seating good access to TV and internet as needed. Selection of food and drink limited though of a good standard. No shower facilities observed. Unfortunately the level of service provided was substandard. Firstly the initial greeting at the reception desk was sullen mechanical and cold on both occasions I entered the lounge. Secondly there was no lounge manager visible to oversee the generally running of the lounge. This was evident by food bowls remaining empty for significant periods of time as well as floor staff (especially the male staff members) who simply loitered around the drinks areas and whose behaviour was unprofessional bearing on juvenile.
I was impressed - staff were wonderful. I travel in and out of Bangkok often and will always use this lounge.

Small and basic lounge. Wouldn't have fitted everyone if business class cabin was full. Decor dated and showing its age. Very limited range of food available (possibly due to early morning departure). Too few bathroom facilities for lounge.
Basic lounge, not comfortable or relaxing. I arrived late in the evening, was tired, but found nowhere quiet to sit and pass the time. Food was good though.

Rude unhelpful staff. The SkyTeam Lounge at Terminal 4, Heathrow Airport is the worst lounge I have ever been into. Not a proper airline lounge. Seem to be just a jack of all. The terminal offers much better service. I will avoid any airline that try’s to pass this off as an airline lounge. It’s a pay to enter lounge.

A very average lounge. Ok food, and you have to push for champagne. Been several times and always find the male employees friendly but the females not so. Only come here as we choose the airline and not the lounge (Garuda).

The Dan lounge used by every airline in this airport beside El Al that have their own lounge. I have criticised this lounge many times before and it seems I am falling on deaf ears. Maybe I am repetitive but let me put it this way. This is the worse and by far the worst lounge I have ever visited. Small dark and many times packed with people buying the advantage entering this lounge. What will a few extra USD do in this airport. Food on buffet has not changed the past 20 years and is still presented in a very poor way. Same soft drinks that's fine and extremely poor wine and this for a country having or producing such good wine they selected Segal and on top of that the lower end from this winery. I rate this lounge even worse then klm lounge in Amsterdam Schiphol airport and that's not a compliment. If I would not be living in Israel and this would not be my home turf I would not even consider this to be a business class or fq lounge.

The staff working on reception at this T4, Heathrow Skyteam lounge are the rudest lounge staff I have come across - this based on many visits to this lounge and they are without exception rude, dismissive and generally will ignore customers if they can. Came through here recently on China Southern flight, usual dismissive wave from reception, proceeded upstairs to find the staff clearing away all the food at 21.00hrs - this some 1.5 hours before my flight and another Aeroflot flight after this. I know the food here is fairly bland and cheap at the best of times, but clearly the staff wanted an early night off and total disregard to customers. Skyteam fail to address any complaints about this awful lounge - I guess that sums up the general standards of them and their group airlines away.

By international standards, this is a pretty miserable Skyteam lounge. It’s just not welcoming and a quick comparaison to the pay to enter Plaza Premium lounge in T4 shows that lounge far ahead of Skyteam. A very poor food offering, hardly any drinks on display and virtually no glasses out for use. Toilet areas not cleaned to normal lounge standards. Overall, not a great advertisement for Skyteam.

Moscow Lounge in my opinion is best Sheremetyevo International Lounge, it is in Terminal D, it is very new and comfortable. It has 2 floors, food line, a choice of beverage many place to sit but it is quite crowded, but it has relax-room where are massage-chair, relax "capsule", PS4 with games and sofas.

Fantastic in every way.  Representatives manned the front desk area with huge smiles and were very gracious and wonderful to talk to. Food was varying and very tasty! Service was incredibly nice and comforting. I really enjoyed my hour stay at that lounge but will probably never return due to the poor showing of my Delta One experience.

I have re-visited the Skyteam lounge at T4 Heathrow airport as a frequent traveller of Qatar Airways. Qatar has its own premium lounge at T4 but that is reserved for business and first class travellers, the silver and higher tier level travellers can visit the Skyteam lounge. (It is a bit unusual because Qatar is a Oneworld member) The lounge was a bit disappointing, offering less food and drink options compared to my last visit two years ago. The interior design of the lounge is still one of my favourites with the living plant walls and when the lounge becomes busy there is a second floor with a very similar layout.

The Skyteam lounge is located opposite Emirates lounge. I used travelling with Saudi Arabian Airlines. The space is modern and relaxed with big windows and view to tarmac. There is a decent food and drink variety as well as alcohol. Also there is a room with a giant TV for more privacy but nothing more that that. Not even toilets, you have to use wc which is outside the lounge.

Has a cold uninviting design, which is similar to other Skyteam Lounges around the world. Lounge was worn out with limited food choices and generally had a bad vibe to it. The upper floor is even worse and reminds me of the 80s’. After a few minutes I decided to use another frequent flyer lounge, which I have access to via credit card.

On our return flight to Jakarta on Garuda Indonesia from Hong Kong we were given access to the SkyTeam lounge. There was a warm welcome from the staff at entrance to the lounge. The lounge is well laid out and all the tables is the sitting area have power supply adapters. The Wi-Fi connectivity was very good as was the selection of food and drinks for both adults and children. The seating, eating and toilets areas were kept clean by a team of eager staff. The overall experience was quite good and myself and my family were quite impressed.

Small, dull lounge with poor quality food. This is the 2nd SkyTeam lounge I have visited within its network and I have to say that the common design they have used is very dull, characterless and uninviting. This particular lounge was very small with limited food choices and poor quality in terms of taste. Seats were very uncomfortable and had no washrooms. If you are flying First or Business with a SkyTeam member airline and have a credit card which allows you to use other lounges, you would be better off doing so, as what I did.

A small, grim lounge that did not do justice to such a beautiful airport. Very little food available, soft drinks and beer in the fridge, no wine available but the coffee was good. Staff tried very hard to make it more pleasant for us but the lack of seating and food was hard to overcome. There was no departures board in the lounge. It was a comedown after the excellent lounge in Beijing. For serious shoppers there was an elegant Alessi homewares shop right next to the lounge. There are no smoking rooms in the airport, smoking is allowed only outside on footpath.

Used this lounge on Air Mauritius flight. Good enough, staff on desk very pleasant found seats easily upstairs and food on offer good enough. Not over the top but all the usual drinks on offer, soft drinks and alcohol along with all sorts of coffee and tea. Food limited but usual hot and cold offerings.

Used this lounge in a Garuda Indonesia flight. Spacious area with comfy seats and the ability to work and use the Wi-Fi. Plenty of food and drink to choose from. The scrambled eggs are the worst. I spent about 2 hours there waiting for my flight. Please keep an eye on the boarding times as it is not announced in the lounge. Overall I was impressed.

As a frequent traveller I have stayed in many lounges, and this one at Terminal 4 London Heathrow has to be my worst experience ever. On first appearance the lounge looks quite nice but it fails to deliver on any of its promises. The range of food on offer was lacking, as were the drinks as both the bar and wine bar were not staffed at all. In fact the only staff we saw at all were the ones downstairs on reception and one that popped out every 20-30 minutes with a plate of food. The oxygen bar (which I was excited to try) was not available - due to a fault we were told and neither was to spa facilities as the staff member was not due to arrive for several hours - by which time I would have been in the air. The whole experience was a waste of money, but unfortunately there is not much you can do about this because their customer service seems non-existent. After finding a contact email to send my complaint I received no reply at all.

Don't expect a warm welcome or smile when you enter this SkyTeam Lounge at Hong Kong Airport, I was hardly acknowledged. My boarding ticket was date stamped and I was allowed entry. A person with a face mask hovered by the toilets immediately cleaning them on each use. Needless to say the toilets and shower were very clean. The food was of a good standard and wine selection was good included Moët. The lounge was large and spacious with plenty of available seats.

Terminal 4 Skyteam lounge, which I have visited on many occasions before, travelling mainly with Aeroflot and China Southern. Staff on reception at 9pm in the evening were rude, did not utter a single word and simply scanned boarding pass. Seems to have been getting more and more like this. Inside the lounge went upstairs - the food counter was half empty, staff were standing in a group chatting among themselves for 25 minutes and taking no notice of anything. Tried a butter chicken and rice dish - whilst visually it was okay, it tasted like it had sat under the lamp for the last 12 hours. Worse than a transport café and that is a totally genuine. Lounge areas quite dirty, especially most tables and many chairs. All in all, standards have become simply awful and unacceptable here, and SkyTeam should be looking for a change of staff, management and catering supplier. The Costa Coffee in the centre airside area offers a cleaner and more pleasant waiting and dining experience. Now this is definitely the worst lounge at Heathrow Airport.

SkyTeam lounge at Sydney airport is the worst I have ever been to, customer service is extremely bad, I ask them to help me to open up a bottle of red wine, one of the staff refused to open it, I asked him why? and he said it's the policy.

The Skyteam lounge at Hong Kong International Airport was well lighted and clean, and had good of seating, but was difficult to find for a first trip. The food was greasy, bready and of poor quality. I left the lounge and went to Cafe Deco.

Worst lounge ever visited. Poor setup and dreary looking furniture, which is in need of replacing. Very depressing and wanted to leave as soon as I walked in. The 2nd floor is more more like a 1980's bus station. Food selection was poor and limited.

The lounge is well decorated, with a living plant wall. Several sofas and armchairs are available with sockets. The lounge has 2 floors floor, upper floor has the same layout but without alcoholic drinks. The lounge has basic but wide range of hot and cold meals. Wide range of soft drinks and a great self-service bar of alcoholic drinks. Beers wines etc. The lavatory is clean, not sure it has showers. Wi-fi was without connection or speed issues.

Visited en route to CDG with Air France. Slow lounge entry with staff taking some time to check our credentials (training a colleague). However, the lounge facilities seemed reasonable. Good selection of drinks and food (chicken curry and rice) of good quality. Toilets and baby changing facilities (important to us) were clean and accessible. My son enjoyed the computer games they provided. Walking around the lounge, the upstairs area had sleeping pods which were reasonable. In short, an acceptable short haul lounge.

Terminal 4 Heathrow, have visited the lounge many times in past years. This August 2015 visit has to be the worst. Lunchtime on Aeroflot, and the lounge was not that busy. Staff at Reception struggle to speak English, so one cannot say if they are rude or just have a real language problem. Went to the upper floor lounge section. The floors were dirty, carpets stained and still the original ones, chairs covered in crumbs etc and tables didn't look like staff had wiped them for a week. Food selection at this time was atrocious, and the quality even worse. Decided to check out the mens room, and that was below public lavatory cleanliness standards.  SkyTeam should be ashamed with these poor standards, and it's about time that airlines who pay to use this lounge wake up and demand some proper value. I left early and found the gate area outside was actually cleaner and more pleasant.

Quite possibly the most depressing lounge I've visited. Flying in Y with Qatar, Sapphire/silver status with BA. Directed to the Skyteam lounge by check-in staff rather than allowed to use Qatar's own lounge. Lounge staff very pleasant, but venue as much ambiance as a morgue. Living wall is nice. Breakfast is woeful. Sparking wine available on request. Being directed to a second-rate third-party lounge devalues the benefits of retaining status with Oneworld.

Nice lounge on two floors. Plenty of seating when we arrived at midday. Food of good quality but limited range. Only two hot choices, but these were of high quality. Good range of alcoholic and non alcoholic beverages on offer. Chairs looked worn and need upgrading. Perhaps white leather may not be such a good idea. Good views over the apron and one runway. Efficient and unobtrusive staff.

A matter-of-fact welcome at the lounge reception. The two-level lounge itself was reasonably empty at around 7.30am. There was a good breakfast buffet - hot breakfast items, sliced fresh fruit, good coffee and fruit juices, pastries and cereals. I cannot report on the drinks section as it was far too early! There are quiet areas and sofas and armchairs alongside the dining areas. The staff kept the food areas full and in good condition. After reading negative views about this lounge, I found it placid, clean and efficient. Wifi is free and requires no password. My only nag is that I wanted to brush my teeth and there were no toothbrush/paste supplies available. The spa staff told me to go to the washrooms and there were none.

I have used lounges all over the world and I have to say the Sky Team Lounge at Heathrow's T4 is one of the poorest I've experienced. I expected the lounge to reflect the premium status Sky Team pace on their Heathrow hub but sadly there is nothing special about the lounge and it pales in comparison to BA's T5 set up and all other major carrier lounges at Heathrow. Example; both floors are set up with a station for making Bloody Mary's, all the ingredients carefully presented together only they don't serve Tomato juice! Crazy. I won't use this facility again.

This is a pretty basic business lounge and would put me off traveling business class from T4 again. The British Airways lounges in T5 are much better. Food - limited choice of pretty basic stuff. I waited 2 hours before any cakes were put out. The staff really do not care. Not interested or even able to pretend they are interested! Insufficient power outlets so spent a good time walking around trying to find somewhere to charge my laptop. Showers are good. Hot water nice cubicles. WiFi works well and sufficiently fast.

Poor lounge. Messy tables and bad experience. Depressing and (like others) made me want to go back in to the main terminal area and work there instead. Food was lukewarm and limited. Very naff and dated decor. Struggled to find somewhere to sit on my own and work. Won't be coming back.

I am writing this review as I sit in the lounge. Door understaffed and young man at desk very obviously nicer to male clients than myself as a solo middle aged woman. Lounge is poorly set up rather like a bus station where too many travellers require seats for their bags and coats. Food selection is the worst I've seen in a lounge. Drinks selection is better but they sure do not hurry to put out the bubbly. The latest empty has been sitting on a counter for a half hour now. In general lots of empties left around to point some travellers are clearing up instead. Wifi works well at least.

Staff on entry to lounge were offhand to the point of being dismissive and rude. Food standards (at 9pm) were very poor and had to find staff in lounge to request that empty plates of sandwiches were replenished - which was eventually done with quite stale and unpalatable sandwiches. The standards in this lounge have continued to fall month after month and it has the air of a canteen that is rather badly managed. Some of the cleaning staff are polite and friendly but as for the rest - they should be ashamed and paying airlines should get the rates reduced. This is certainly not a "premium" lounge any more. The washrooms were not nice either - the floor was disgustingly wet with urine all around the urinals and washbasins were wet messy and poorly maintained. Time to sit in the concourse which is nicer than this poorly managed lounge area. Went to the Qatar Airways lounge here at T4 some weeks ago and this is truly magnificent and makes this SkyTeam lounge look a joke.

Having used this lounge previously I thought that food variety and quality would have improved unfortunately it hasn't. Whilst walking around the very poorly stocked food display I asked if there was going to be any further hot choices provided apart from the chocolate crepes I was informed that there would be. I waited and a staff member brought out a plate of potato and onion tortillas of which all but 2 were placed on plates and disappeared into the back with a couple of staff members. The soup that was on offer when I arrived was spirited away by a chef  I am still awaiting its return. The cheese is nice and crispy around the edges and the salad has seen better days. Considering the cost of flights and the fact that the lounge is meant to make your travel experience an enjoyable one I for one think that there is something lacking. The soup has returned whether it is fresh or reheated I am unsure as I wasn't quite quick enough to look at the previous offering I do not recommend the Skyteam lounge at Heathrow Terminal 4.

Very basic poor choice of food all left uncovered in reasonably warm ambient temperatures. Lounge staff impotent when asked to sort out boarding pass issue for next leg of flight with KLM. No PC's in lounge for passenger use. Will be avoiding SkyTeam on this route in future.

Lounge which is pleasant and kept clean. There are different areas within the lounge but all are basically chairs and coffee tables though there is a dining area and couple of massage chairs. Two tvs in the lounge (which were not working when I used it with my wife). The food is limited to sandwiches and canapes and chips. Good selection of spirits and soft drinks though only one white and red wine and one type of beer. Bathrooms clean and there are two shower facilities in the gents (I assume the same in the ladies area). Staff very friendly and call each flight.

Staff service was abrupt to the point of being downright rude - no point in complaining in the lounge since it seemed to be rather a common trait amongst 3 of the staff we spoke to. Lounge was very crowded and sat on second floor level where floors were dirty tables still covered in plates used cups etc and the lavatories were filthy. How on earth Skyteam can get away with offering this lounge facility in such a poor condition with such terrible staff service is a mystery. We actually left 50 mins before our flight and walked back to Costa coffee shop - where staff were nicer and the snacks also good (plus they keep the tables clean!). Never again to this T4 lounge.

What could be a fantastic lounge is a big disappointment. Good location great views and plenty of space. Decor very dated. A few computers some old news papers and in-flight magazines complete the offer of entertainment. The hostess upon entering seems to always be in personal phone conversation and the bar staff is unfriendly and lazy. No food except for some sad nibbles drinks self service coffee from an instant machine. I arrived at the lounge at 10:30 when it was empty and left around 12:30 when it was fairly full. By that time the place was filled with dirty glasses and trash and the staff had made no effort whatsoever to clean.

The Skyteam lounge in Terminal 4 has a modern design and offers many different areas. The "green wall' with plants is great as well as the wine and champagne area. It offers a wide choice of food cold and hot as well as a great selection of newspapers in many languages. Reception desk staff was very friendly and polite.

Awful horrible plastic cafe sort of place used now by Gulf Air following their move from Terminal 3 to Terminal 4. Was packed everything involved a queue (e.g. 5 minutes to enter; 5+ minutes to get a cup of coffee at the "cute but oh-so-slow" espresso/cappuchino coffee machine). The food bar had no forks (all had been used) for at least 25 minutes despite staff milling about (and chatting with each other plenty). No call service for airlines (hence had to join Gulf Air's uncontrolled mob at boarding time). Basically was glad to leave the place - will try hard to avoid it in future.
Incredible lounge with lots of wines, prosecco, food and drinks. All for free for Sky Express travellers. I was incredibly surprised. Thanks Sky Express.

The Al Safwa First Class Lounge was once a model of calm, a true refuge for the weary traveller. In recent times, however, it has become more crowded and less pleasant. The service remains warm and earnest. Al Safwa no longer feels genuinely exclusive; it increasingly resembles just another premium lounge rather than the sanctuary it once was. One is left to wonder whether entrance standards have been relaxed. Access to this lounge is not inexpensive, and I pay those fees willingly for a particular level of experience. I would not hesitate to pay more if it meant restoring the older Al Safwa climate - quiet, restrained, and unmistakably First Class.

Qatar Airways doesn't have a First Class Lounge in Dubai to the same level as Doha. Instead, First Class passengers flying Qatar are invited to the Ahlan First Class Lounge, which offers a calm luxurious atmosphere, with exceptional restaurant-quality food and drinks. Most importantly, I found the staff to be extremely friendly and attentive.

When it comes to sheer size, design and facilities, the Qatar Business Class Lounge in Doha has no equal. If you were to describe it with one word it would be – ‘breathtaking’. The attention to detail, quality of furniture and fittings are outstanding. This is matched by the food and beverage offering that includes a full al-a-carte dining experience.  Unfortunately, I suffer from terminal cancer and require wheelchair assistance between the lounge and the boarding gates. Despite assurances, this has never gone without a hitch, but this time was the worst. As instructed, I sat in the small waiting area near the lounge entry station. The boarding time printed on my boarding pass came and went without any sign of a wheelchair. I expressed my concern to the staff, only to be told it was too soon, as they were only pre-boarding. My question, “Isn’t pre-boarding for people in wheelchairs?”, received another rebuke. It was only when I demanded to be taken to the aircraft that a wheelchair appeared, still with a member of staff talking insistently in an attempt to justify himself to the point I had to demand he cease talking to me. I was the last passenger to board and very nearly missed the flight.

This lounge is like going to a 5 star hotel with family, quiet and prayers spaces. The quiet places are bedrooms with a shower. One can for a fee soak in a jacuzzi, get massages and mani/pedis. This is a vast lounge with open spaces. Doesn't feel overcrowded even during busy periods. Artifacts from the Museum of Islamic Art are on display. The lounge has its own duty free shop. It has a 250 seat restaurant that serves full service tapas type meals. Staff are welcoming and very professional. For connecting flights, the lounge has its own departure gate which transports passengers in 12 seat buses to their gate. The bathrooms are very clean with constant cleaning by attendants. Since we had a 9 hour layover, we booked one of the bedrooms to rest and shower before our next flight.

This is huge and spacious lounge on two levels. The lower level has plenty of seating with drinks stations dispersed throughout its length. The upper level has a full restaurant with buffet stations and a full service menu serving tapas sized meals. Having experienced the Al Safwa lounge on our outbound flights, this lounge appeared overcrowded especially on the restaurant level and a bit of let down. The staff is very friendly and welcoming. The only drawback to this lounge is that there was only bathroom on the restaurant level. Nonetheless, this is one of the best business class lounges I've been through.

Al Safwa First Lounge, Doha I have visited Al Safwa several times, most recently in August 2025. Physically it is an exceptional space, an oasis of calm. What sets it apart from other great lounges in the same league - such as Lufthansa’s First Terminal or the Swiss First Lounge - is its staff, composed largely of Asians (predominantly Indians), whose warmth gives the place a character unique to the region. By contrast, the European lounges, while elegant and luxurious, can feel somewhat sterile. It was therefore with some dismay that my latest visit fell short of past standards. The lounge felt more crowded than usual, and the wait for a shower exceeded an hour. My sense is that the entry requirements have been relaxed. I would urge Qatar Airways to preserve the exclusivity that once defined Al Safwa.
Outstanding Business Class lounge at Doha Airport offering different dining options, comfortable seating, and shower facilities. Highly recommend the facilities.

This has to be the best business class lounge in the world. It is huge, on two levels, offer many food and drink options, including a la carte. The lounge is very comfortable and There are also showers, luggage storage and plenty of staff members to assist you in any way. i needed assistance to get to a gate far from the lounge, I could not have been more pleased with the service, much appreciated!
Excellent lounge. The best for a long time ago. Perfect service, good food, great comfort, sunny atmosphere at 11 floor. Excellent staff - warm welcome. Congrats !!!

First time visiting this beautiful lounge and definitely not the last. I decided to check out this lounge after previously visiting the same one in the South Pier of the airport. Compared to the South Pier lounge, the Platinum and Gold Lounge North offers a more spacious and open ambiance, providing plenty of room to relax before your next connecting flight. The food selection was excellent, offering both à la carte and buffet options. The staff were attentive and had a great sense of humor, which made the experience even more enjoyable. The only downside? The long queue for the shower rooms. But overall, it was a great experience!

lounge_name: Platinum and Gold Lounge Concourse C
