review: The Qatar Airways lounge for Platinum and Gold members at Concourse C is a perfect blend of luxury and relaxation. The space is beautifully designed—spacious and comfortable, offering an ideal atmosphere to unwind before a flight. Every detail feels thoughtful, from the comfortable seating to the variety of quiet corners. The hospitality is exceptional; the staff are attentive, elegant, and always ready to assist, making you feel truly valued as a member. Whether you're enjoying a meal, catching up on work, or simply relaxing, the lounge experience is peaceful and seamless. It’s a fantastic retreat that elevates the entire travel experience.

Nicely located lounge close to Gate B2 with friendly staff at reception and plenty of space for guests. Good variety is limited but I personally find it one of the best lounges in HIA with excellent WiFi and clean toilets.

Incredible eating options, with excellent bar services. Service generally outstanding, friendly and helpful. I wish I would always have this standard when travelling business class, also with other airlines. It comes close to what a real first class lounge should be, even if travelling in business class. Not airline or lounge to be blamed, unpleasant are some co-travelers dressed like going to the beach or coming from the gym. I am afraid that is a general trend while travelling long haul, but I think it is a little disrespectful towards the well groomed and impeccable staff.

This the best lounge at Dhaka International Airport. Very well decorated lounge that has a very nice prayer room for Muslims and clean toilet. It serves Indian, continental and Thai-Chinese food; food was delicious. The beverages include fresh juice, soft drinks and tea-coffee. The food was prepared by the Westin Hotel, Dhaka. There is a small library to read books, magazines and newspapers.

This lounge is absolutely the best. Customer service is outstanding. As I was walking gingerly with a full cup of macchiato coffee to my seat, a service came right over and offered to take the coffee to my seat! He even made an extra coffee because I spilled some from the cup onto the saucer. The other agents kept track of my connection flight times and reminded me to proceed to the gate. The only suggestion I have is that the rest rooms could have been larger with shower amenities.

A visit to the recently refurbished Al-Safwa lounge at Doha's Hamad airport is always an extraordinary experience. Admission is only for passengers travelling in Qatar Airways First Class or QR Platinum members. Status customers from other Oneworld partners have no access. There is an escalator to the spacious reception where people need to go to be admitted. There seem to be more staff than guests and the atmosphere is friendly and warm. People can go enjoy a drink at the bar or have a meal at the à la carte restaurant. Service at the restaurant needs to be streamlined. I think the staff have not been properly trained as waiters. I hadn't finished my starter yet when soup and main course arrived. The selection of food is great and all I ordered (lentil soup, wagyu beef carpaccio and lamb) was delicious. The champagne was Lanson Brut Black Label. After dinner, I went to the spa and had a great massage. It needs to be mentioned that the spa treatments are not included and have to be paid for. Altogether a fantastic experience difficult to be topped.

Beautifully appointed lounge with plenty of quiet and relaxed seating area. Very nice restaurant area and small but very adequate food range. Very nice toilet and shower facilities . Attentive service. Very clean.

Nice lounge. I arrived around 8am for my 11am Malaysia Airlines flight to KL.  I headed straight to bathrooms who had attendants waiting outside to service regularly. I sat in lounge area which had ample charging facilities and a nice view of some departure gates. I went to dining area which had a sumptuous display of cold items available. The buffet hot food was a little tepid in temperature but tasty enough. Service was efficient without being over bearing. I was advised that non Qatar flights were not announced so you have to check the screen yourself for boarding updates. The lounge was very clean and well presented with drinks and snacks available to help yourself to.  Very pleasant experience.

This is a fabulous lounge. Service is impeccable. Beautiful view of the Garden area of the airport. The staff are friendly and attentive. They try to anticipate what the guest wants. Any reasonable wish will be fulfilled. The selection of food is variable and large. One can order à la carte or use the buffet. There is even a sushi bar. Premium drinks are readily available. There is a quiet area with several tastefully decorated resting rooms which operates on a “first come, first served” base. Drinks cannot be taken into the rooms though. The lounge is exceptionally clean and well kept, but it only opened a few weeks ago. There is a Louis Vuitton cafe which, unfortunately has not opened yet. This is one of my favorite lounges and the best business lounge I have been to lately. Certainly better than First Class lounges of most airlines. Can’t wait to use it on my next flight via Hamad International.

Very nice and big lounge. During my stay there was only a handful other people at the lounge which made it a very nice experience. Also the staff was very lovely and helpful. Food was buffet style but of good quality. The wine on the other hand was surprisingly bad.

While three people scanned my boarding pass to access the lounge and they all noted that there was a problem with the boarding pass, no one could tell me what to do or where to go - or what time I needed to leave the lounge to arrive at the gate in time. Very large and airy lounge with lots of seating and food and drink areas. I couldn't access the menu though was my boarding pass didn't have the required QR code. The shower wait was one hour which seemed like too long. Luckily at the very chaotic gate I received the new and correct boarding pass.
Lounge in Bangkok is small, but good with a la carte dining. A single champagne, Gosset, was offered. Lounge was almost full and quite vibrant. One of the three best lounges in BKK.

El Safwa is too huge with little load. No fish, terraria, no music, no gym.  Worse for me is the design and the granite, glass, and steely. Not a single cozy place. The dorms are OK, very small; lack windows. The high ceilings allow for fresh air. The a la carte dining offered is supposed to be an asset, however my waiting time is >30 Minutes. There is no buffet in the lounge.
Excellent service and well managed lounge with comfortable seating. The overall cleanliness and attention to detail is hard to beat. Quality of the food and wines were terrific.

A lounge with 2 sections. We were guided to the premium section where we were for approx. 2 ½ hours. The lounge is decorated in an attractive way and very comfortable. Unfortunately almost no daylight and a little dark. View on the departure hall. We can imagine that when crowded, people feel slightly unpleasant, perhaps claustrophobic. Great internet. We did not notice if shower facilities were available. The lounge was clean. Food and drinks were pretty well sorted, varied and of good quality and above all tasty. Staff was nice.

Before covid, Qatar Airways used the Qantas Lounge. Apparently they switched to the Marhaba Lounge. Unfortunately and bad choice. The lounge is small, and the sound of the TV filled the room in a very unpleasant way. Although no one was watching, the attendant refused to switch off the sound. We seriously considered to go to another lounge and pay a fee for entrance. The lounge consists of 3 rooms: a bar/buffet with very unattractive furniture, a room to work, however very dark and the main room with the TV noise. Shower facilities were very poor: small space, no vent. Food and drinks limited but OK. Nice view on the tarmac.

The Premiere Lounge is OK but nothing more. WiFi password on a sign at the reception counter. Voucher is not enough to get in so keep your boarding card ready. Alcohol behind the bar so you have to order it. Coffee maker broken so no coffee with milk was available.
This first time I came to the Mariner Lounge since I have been seafarer. It was really best experience, Sohan from f&b was very humble and friendly. Thanks a lot, and all here are free of charge

Qatar Airways use the Menzies Executive Lounge at Stockholm Arlanda Airport, and it is the worst lounge I ever visited! Boring, small and dirty. Extremely limited drinks and food. Stale bread, tasteless cheese, bad red wine on tap, tasteless beer on tap. When you finally got a glass, it was warm. I'll never go back to this lounge. I rather pay for a good tasty sandwich and beer in the terminal. I don't understand how a prestigious airline as Qatar Airways can use this lounge.

This lounge is world famous for its size, design and great services. I had not used it for several years during the hiatus of the pandemic. But on the last trip, transiting through DOH, it was a chance to re-acquaint ourselves. The main priority was to use the showers. But there was a queue of about 10 people waiting to use the only 2 working showers in the larger of the two shower facilities. The other shower facility also had a long queue, with no Qatar staff managing its usage. The lounge itself was extremely busy, with very little seating availability. For their flagship lounge, Qatar Airways seem to have greatly under planned the demand, or over-offered its availability. Luckily there was a very helpful member of staff who helped take us to the Gold Lounge and to use the facilities there, so we managed showers, and to catch our connecting flight. That is impressive, but if Qatar Airways wants to retain its premier title, it needs to rethink its strategy here. And quickly, with the upcoming FIFA tournament.

I used this lounge when it first opened about 4 years ago, and it was excellent. Had read that it was not maintained properly, but on the recent departure from Bangkok, everything was in good working order, with excellent service from staff, and good snacks, The only quibble was the champagne: only Pommery, which was corked. They opened another, but it too was corked. There was quite a wide selection of hot and cold food, and given the dire food service inflight, it would have been wiser to choose to eat here, especially as we complied with the airlines recommended 3 hour pre-flight check in, (which took about 30 minutes, from check in to lounge).

The Al-Mourjan lounge in Hamad International Airport. As with any lounge experience the second time round is often better than the first. I had specifically chosen to have a long layover in Doha as, due to my age, I find that two shorter flights with a layover between is a much more comfortable experience. My first visit to the lounge was a seven hour layover between flights. I didn't know of the quiet area and that I could have a sleep for awhile so I didn't take advantage of that on my first visit. However I did use the shower facilities which were absolutely superb. It will be difficult to find anything bad to say about the staff in the lounge is they were attentive clearing used plates and cups not intruding when it was clear that they were not needed. The lounge is magnificent it's been awarded a place as the number one business class lounge in the world and I can easily understand why. I was there during one of the busy periods when I arrived in Doha, and even so there was plenty more seating available food was available links for available and the number of staff employed were easily enough for the guests in the lounge. We now come along to the food in the restaurant. The breakfast was very nice I had eggs Florentine they were beautifully presented wonderfully served with excellent table service, I had arrived at 7 o'clock in the morning and the lunchtime service didn't take place until 11 o'clock in the morning, had I known then what I know now, I would have taken the opportunity to go and have a nap in the quiet area. However since my flight to London was a little after 12 o'clock I didn't want to miss the chance of lunch in the restaurant so stayed awake. Once again in the restaurant presentation was beautiful service was excellent unfortunately the quality of the food that was served was a huge disappointment, the two options which I considered to be and salmon. The salmon although the presentation on the plate was absolutely beautiful was crunchy on the outside and dry as a bone on the inside. I did try the beef and was told that medium rare was not available as it is prepared by a catering company outside the airport and the restaurant reheat and serves it therefore it has to be well done. Some people may like well done beef, it certainly is not to my taste. To the credit of the restaurant staff I did tell them that the salmon was really rather overcooked, which was an understatement, and they insisted on preparing another piece of salmon for me to try, the chef who cooked it came to the table, I was too embarrassed to tell them that it was virtually no different from the first piece crunchy on the outside, which could be out an okay thing, but still dry as a bone on the inside, so I politely declined to tell them my impression of the second piece. I didn't have time to try anything else on the menu as my flight was being called.

Qatar Airways has closed their own lounge in Bangkok airport during the pandemic, I'm not sure when it's going to reopen. As a result they using the Miracle lounge in Bangkok airport. I would say that the Miracle lounge is only really so-so, the drink selection is quite limited as is the food selection. Whilst of course as in any business Lounge you can eat as much as you like and drink as much as you like the selection really dissuaded you from doing that. The lounge is okay, you do have a multitude of power points so it's not difficult to find a seat with a power point adjacent to it,. Of course you can eat as much as you like I found that a curry and rice was the best option available to my taste, there were few other snacks that I tried but nothing really exciting. During my 4 flights I tried three different lounges one in Bangkok one in Doha, twice. and one in Heathrow Airport the Bangkok Lounge was definitely at the bottom of the list. It's definitely better than waiting in the main terminal or at the gate with no question as to that, I sincerely hope that Qatar Airways is able to reopen their own lounge in the near future.

Since the upgrades to the terminal Qatar Airways now use the 1903 lounge and it is is bright, airy and well laid out with lots of comfortable seating areas and a very good choice of food and drinks available. We were there at 5am and were welcomed by a very friendly member of staff who handed us over to Alexander and Janine who looked after us superbly. I would thoroughly recommend this lounge to any traveller using T2 it makes a wonderful start to your journey.
Very clean lounge with both a buffet for food as the possibility to order freshly prepared food. Impressive selection of beverages. Friendly service and very clean restrooms

Probably the most luxurious lounge I ever saw, and feeling very sorry that it was so early in the morning so i could not try some of the great wines available including 2 second growth Bordeaux. I had a great breakfast with delicious fruits and could not resist one glass of premium Champagne. Extremely friendly service and luxurious and clean restrooms

The Coral Lounge in Phuket operated by AOT must be the worst and most depressing business lounge ever. Super small with furniture from the 1980s. No champagne, ice cold red wine and seating like a school dinner hall. A few armchairs are there but since the lounge is so small you are lucky if you get one. Though you can have a neck and shoulder massage while you drink your cold red wine. This is not where you want to spend 1 or 2 hours waiting!!

I stayed in the Mariners Lounge during my transit stay at Doha airport. The lounge is very clean. Frequent sanitation being carried out by the staff. Food choices are adequate and always replenished. The toilet is large enough to provide the essentials including a shower room. Wifi connection is superb. Most of all, the staff are very accommodating and that’s what made my stay worthwhile considering the long hours spent before my next flight. Thank you for the efficient service.

This lounge has many spots where you can pick up sparkling water and espressos, in addition to full menu dining and buffets which are manned by servers. I had a delightful shower and a nice rest in a quiet zone. We had a close to 8 hour layover, so we made use of the amenities throughout the lounge. Easily the best business class lounge in the world!

Spacious, quiet, peaceful place that allows for good distribution of space between other lounge users. Good range of facilities. Very polite, helpful and friendly staff. Good range of food and beverage.

I had a great experience at the Oryx/Al-Maha lounge. Staff was very friendly and helping. The Lounge ambience and cleanliness were remarkable. I had never observed such a excellent level of cleanliness in rest room with outstanding shower facility decorated with world class toiletries. Just one thing to improve is the range of food, which was very limited but what was available, was good quality in both taste and selection of ingredients. Overall my stay at lounge was sensational and tremendous.

I would like to thank the staff in their arrivals lounge in Doha, for their hospitality and extremely caring. Mr Kunwar was especially kind to me and made sure that every single detail was taken care of.
The Aspire Lounge they use at Gatwick has a poor food selection. The whole place is in need of refurbishment, tables were not cleaned.

This first class lounge is nothing short of exceptional and I can understand why it is the worlds best. The interior decor, finishes and features are above most 5 star hotels I've visited, and although I only had about 90 mins stay, I was able to enjoy a fabulous breakfast that was freshly cooked for me, and served by the friendliest staff. The bathrooms were exceptional, and so many other features I did not use (bedrooms, spa etc). Other staff on the entrance counter and inside the lounge were also exemplary.

This is not the Qatar Airways business class lounge but is for Oneworld Emerald and Sapphire FFs. Cheap seats, not enough capacity during peak hours, limited F&B options, and an overall vibe of indifference and inattention.

I went first time in this Lounge which is at Hamad Doha Airport. I was travelling in economy class but i got upgraded to Silver Member of Qatar Airways Privilege Club and got access to Business Class Lounge. It was very nice and huge with wide variety of Food and sweets and drinks staff was very supportive and respectful. I really enjoyed this Lounge.

This lounge in the early morning is mayhem. It is difficult to find seats at the restaurant. The food is decent however and the staff are friendly. Drinks order are taken a few minutes after you get a seat. The lounge can be improved with more seating.

Visited this lounge during a stopover. Spacious and clean but lacks character. The staff were disappointing and gave an air of superiority over the traveller. I would recommend the excellent restaurants in the airport where the food is superior with a better atmosphere.

This lounge does not advertise it nor does it show up on the Oneworld lounge finder. Yet it is open and there are signs inside the airport that point to the lounge.  The lounge is almost identical to their lounge in Paris. There were comfortable seats and when I ordered something at the bar, the bartender said "I'll serve it at your seat." The food there was just immaculate. There was a hot buffet filled with mostly Thai and Arabic dishes, and actual dining tables with utensils already set up! The staff would always apologise if they ran out of something and would fill your plate up for you on request. They ask you want drink you want and if you want it refilled. My parents had a full meal so they could maximise sleep on the flight. The choice of beverages is astounding, their choice of champagne was Bollinger!  The best bit about this lounge has to be the cakes. Chocolate opera cake with gold flakes, and the best Baklava in Bangkok! The other parts of the lounge were like a super comfortable waiting room, and you felt like royalty while you were in any part of this lounge. I understand why they don't call it a business class lounge. Simply because it would make all other business class lounges look like glorified waiting rooms. One thing that is also very cheeky is the fact that the lounge is located next door to Singapore Airlines, and having been in that lounge, it simply does not compare to Qatar Airways offering. Too bad it's only open for business class passengers, not Oneworld Sapphire/Emerald but at least you can access this lounge using any Oneworld business class ticket.

This First Class Lounge is for OneWorld members travelling in economy class. It's a small L shaped room that has limited seating and disgraceful food options. I wouldn't have booked Qatar on this trip if I knew that this member's lounge was this bad, as the lounge quality is an important driver to airline decision. Wouldn't recommend the lounge to any oneWorld Elites hoping for a first class experience.

Al Mourjan lounge is a great lounge which tends to be crowded especially in the morning busy hours. I would like to focus upon the quality of lounge food which seems to be rather declining. The veg Korma was watery and full of cream, so was the tandoori marinated fish. My question is why can't food be prepared in this lounge to ensure freshness and quality.

Using the Al Mourjan Lounge from 0030hrs 3rd November to 0700hrs. The lounge is impressively huge and spacious with lots of seating spaces of various styles. Few sleeping couches are available at the back area of the lounge. However, due to its brightness and noise from the planes in nearby gates, I'm unable to get any sleep. Better sound-proof walls / glasses and less bright sections are required in my opinion. Quiet period in the lounge is between 0230 till 0500 hours (Qatar time) and i'm lucky to be able to use the toilet and shower room at 0400 hrs. The toilet and shower rooms are clean and consistently monitored by the staff. However at 0600 hr, there is a long queue for the toilet and shower rooms and overheard a passenger saying that he has been waiting for 40 minutes for the shower room. Main dining room on the upper floor is also spacious but at 0600hr it is also crowded. As Qatar Airways is targeting business class passengers as their main client, the impressively vast Al Mourjan seems to be inadequate to accommodate all. Separation of business class passengers into several lounges might be required. Having another lounge near Gate D, E (served by a train ride from main terminal) might be helpful.

This lounge is one of the nicest I have visited, impeccable staff serving great food and drinks, l have used the Emirates lounge at Heathrow , and although very good, l find this lounge more personal. I will make another visit on an upcoming trip, and look forward to my visit, the freshly cooked breakfasts are great, as is the Champagne, cant wait.

The third party lounge Qatar Airways use here is located at the 2B non-schengen terminal of the airport. After the passport control and the duty free corridor turn left and go upstairs. Signs are not really clear so people may struggle finding it. The lounge is quite small compared to other European lounges and may be busy in peak hours. As you enter, the buffet is on the right, seating in front and the other side. I visited the lounge in the afternoon, the meal options were basic, without warm meal. The soda dispenser was out of order so only unchilled soda cans were provided at the time. There are no toilets inside, you must visit the public toilets outside. Since the lounge is located on top floor of the terminal, at the new wing, it has an excellent apron view.

Qatar Airways use the airport Premium Lounge. Quite small lounge but they have good selection of food and beverages. No smoking area. Free Wi-Fi. Staff helpful and friendly. Be sure to check your departure gate and check with the staff how long it will take you to walk there!

Huge lounge! But can get busy especially in the morning. 2 restaurants open 24/7. Bar and tabele service if you catch a waiter. Several coffee stations and soft drinks. Clean restrooms and showers. Small room for smoking. Not the most comfortable chairs if you have a longer transfer.

Really don't understand how Qatar airways can pay to use this handling lounge. Last time they served vegetarian lasagna and a salad. Champagne was out and took the staff about 30 minutes to get hold of a bottle. Generally a bad lounge.
Lounge overlooking the runway and gates. Clean and comfortable with a good selection of food and drinks. Nice helpful staff. Free Wi-Fi password on the tables.

I was booked on one of the first flights from Cardiff to Doha and have flown with QR many times. Qatar Airways have to use the Cardiff Airport Lounge which is hidden away but reasonably signposted. On entry, my heart sank as I am used to the QR business lounge at LHR. It's dismal and an awful start to my holiday experience. Poor drinks selection, poor food choice, down at heel and awful. Seating was poor, tables bland, atmosphere nil. Tables were left uncleared In the lounge, I was asked for my boarding pass, and then instructed to go through another door - my spirits soared! Behind these doors more of the same, 1980's school canteen theme. A dump. QR- please get your stuff together and rectify this shambles.

The Al Maha lounge in Doha is situated on the arrival floor, after security and passport control. Usually accessible for Al Maha customers but not for business and first class travellers. I was lucky to be redirected there due to the refurbishment of the business class arrival lounge. The lounge has excellent toilet and shower facilities, nice dining area and even a business centre. Upon my early morning arrival snacks and warm breakfast options were served with coffee, tea, orange juice and sodas. The place was almost empty so the staff had plenty of time and capacity to take care of us. Altogether it is a great place to refresh after a long flight, but as I mentioned, it is usually reserved for Al Maha customers.

This lounge is  average for an airline that markets itself as top tier. Had to wait 40 mins for a shower and the reception staff are not particularly helpful. The food I had in the restaurant was not high quality.

Nice and cozy Oslo handling lounge above the departure floor in the international part of the airport. It opens at 5:30, alcohol is served"only from 6:30. I visited early in the morning when only cold buffet breakfast was provided. The range was a bit limited, but enough for a light meal. There are comfy chairs and sofas around with sockets at some of them, but it can get crowded during peak hours due to its size. The WiFi connection was quick and stable. Nice lounge without any extravaganza or show stopper feature.

The huge lounge is situated above the departures floor. There is a spacious area on the lower floor with lots of armchairs and some coffee stations. At the back, there is a buffet area, quiet zone and showers. I tried to sleep in the quiet zone, but the shape of those sitting whatevers made it impossible. On the upper floor there is a restaurant, with great selection of cold arabic humus and salads. The warm buffet provides a great selection of meat and vegetarian meals. There is a great soft and alcoholic drink selection.

The Al Maha transit lounge at Hamad Airport in Doha is small, but it works twenty-four hours and is always clean and organized. The bathrooms are clean. The quality of the food is average and there are non-alcoholic drinks available. The only bad thing is we do not have comfortable chairs to relax in long waits and to get some alcoholic drink we have to ask the waiters.

Excellent, spacious and well-appointed lounge. Easy to reach from arrivals, signage to lounge clear, access the lounge from the main transit terminal. Take escalator to lounge, a QA attendant will guide you and verify your ticket and lounge pass. Interior of lounge is two floors, buffet restaurant and bar is on 2nd floor. First floor has many rest/waiting areas and facilities include: showers, sleep areas, quiet area, prayer room, business center with free printing, 1st floor breakfast/sandwich restaurant, fast WiFi service. Lounge is surprisingly quiet despite its size. Tends to have many visitors from 6:30 am onwards.

We have visited both the business and first class lounges at Doha Airport and they are some of the best lounges we have seen in our travels so far. Incredible service, hundreds of employees are there at every step to address all concerns. The business class lounge was massive, had separate nap areas, quiet areas for working, huge eating area upstairs with great selection of food and drinks. The architecture in the lounge is beautiful, there is a massive waterfall fixture in the center of the lounge facility. The customer service during our breakfast was better than a lot of upscale restaurants we have to been to in the US, absolutely killer job by the lounge team

Unfortunately this airport has 2 shared business lounges that are used by around 15 airlines so depending on the time of day you fly the space can feel as crowded as the gate. On this day we were lucky enough to be assigned to a secondary lounge or an overflow lounge that was only being used by our airline and I think 1 more. This lounge had no bathroom so you had to leave and go to the crowded one to use the facilities if you needed. Manila business lounges need a serious make over, both lounges looked, felt, and smelled old. The glass is covered in humidity and the view is horrendous. The service I also have to say is robotic. They all say “Sir and Mam” so excessively that is just not genuine and it makes you even feel uncomfortable at times. The answer is usually “no” followed by a fake smile and the “Sir or Mam” at the end. Manila service in the past was warm and genuine it’s really robotic now and the general attitude seems to be that no one really cares but in a friendly and polite way. The food was mediocre and nothing to brag about however the drink selection was decent. Plenty of soft and alcoholic choices to chose from. I think with a little bit of work, effort, direct supervision and training this can be a great lounge because the destination is amazing. Too bad the experience leaving was dull.

This lounge has plenty of rooms, quiet rooms, family rooms, Internet rooms, and showers. The showers is what I enjoyed the most because after a 10 hour flight and then a 14 hour flight that shower came in very handy. Unfortunately the food is mediocre and I was not able to try the WiFi due to the short time I had before my next flight. This lounge is not only for business class passengers but you can also pay to use.

This is a new lounge that proves CDG airports curves can be wonderful. Modeled similar to the London lounge (missing the Lindt chocolate bowls) but awesome. Showers don’t have toilets but honestly who cares. Staff wonderful, food great - a fantastic new lounge for a great airline. My only query - no chocolate ice cream - but again, I’m not complaining.

This lounge has been appalling on the past 2 visits. Ground staff are barely knowledgeable about One World status levels nor what those levels are meant to offer. Al Mourjan lounge looks grand and oozes promise but it falls short of what I need. Food is western or Asian. Or a sandwich. Thai beef salad? Pasta was dry and insipid. Nothing is a la carte.  Power access to charge phones in the restaurant  they have 1 table with power access and that requires a  2m cable to connect. I write this  on the edge of a seat with a 2m cable stretching around the corner. And watch out if you are One World Sapphire or Emerald. Twice now - and I am ticketed C on QR the ground staff have tried to send me off to their First Class lounge. The staff in the lounge are affable, well-presented and efficient.

Due to short transit times on my flights only had short visit to business lounge on return trip, it's one of the best I've ever been. On previous flights I've had 8 hours in transit no a problem when you have this wonderful lounge with really excellent staff. A fine choice of food either full course or just a snack.

The Qatar Airways Business lounge at Heathrow is first rate. Probably the best I have been to. Relaxed with an option of buffet or restaurant dinning, and the food is pretty respectable. Food you want to eat with great service, table clothes and friendly approachable staff. Generally airlines have their best lounges on their home territory, this is not the case with Qatar's Doha lounge. It is is large and looks impressive but it's rather impersonal. Signage is poor, the food very average - it is perhaps the weak link in what is a very good airline. Scores below are for Doha, London would get top scores!

Having spent more than five layovers in last two years, I can say a few things about this place. Lounge is quiet, easy to get to and provides good service. Bar is well stocked, there is a quiet area where you can lay down. Food quality is good, they do have good showers and rest rooms. There is enough privacy, great place to store luggage. Internet works.

The lounge is superb. I’m not sure if it’s the wonderful staff, the variety of well presented food, the ambience or the free chocolates by the fistful down near the kitchen. It’s lovely. A long shower in a large clean bathroom, towels that don’t smell like they fell out of a one star hotel - this is it. Seriously lovely, small enough to be intimate, a joy to visit.

Excellent experience. The lounge is wonderful, relaxing to the eye and incredibly comfortable. The setup is not to packed, as many other lounges, so a lot of space can be enjoyed. Food is excellent, probably the best I encountered so far. Connectivity is good, crew is supportive as expected.

This is a fantastic lounge. Great opportunity to have a shower and something to drink between flights. This is so different to lounges in europe or the US. Plenty of staff. The showers were clean and looked like spa showers. They have bar and beverage secions and a restaurant. Just awesome.

Big lounge with a variety of seating areas etc. The food on offer is fresh, although depending on the time limited. The quantity of shower facilities is very limited and even outside rush hours one has to wait. Their is something like a booking list but it did not work, the best one just wait at the reception and one might be lucky. The lounge still does not has the air conditioning of the shower suites under control: one showers and is wet again after the shower because it is hot and humid like a steam room.

We had a 4 hour stopover flying from Manchester UK to Sydney Australia and spent some time in the lounge. This lounge is vast with a very open feel, chairs and tables are placed well apart, and there seemed to be a number of workstations available with what looked like tablets set up at each station. There were at least two areas for eating, one for light meals such as sandwiches, the other for cooked meals. We had a very nice sandwich each which was served warm. There were also a number of coffee/tea stations available with staff there to assist.

Nice enough lounge, big (vast) and very elegant. It's starting to date. The chairs in the restaurant are getting a bit haggard. The food is good, but the staff seemed preoccupied with each other. I seated myself in the upstairs lounge, no one approached at the tables restraunt section. I'm not exactly sure what to make of this. Not normal service at all.

Qatar Airways Al Safwa First Lounge at Hamad Airport. Museum of Islamic art architecture inspired with artifices on display. Dimensioned for the gods. A fountain from the sky, unburied, exquisite, unique. Service and food choice exceptional. No barbers shop though - I like it for my grey old beard. This seriously redefines a lounge, it's more like a destination inside some classy space ship. A new type of lounge, unique.

A quiet but very basic third party lounge (Skyserv Lounge) compared to others around the world. On the positives it is very clean and tidy. Negatives are that the food selection is extremely limited almost non existed (only a couple of brioche sandwiches) and there are no power sockets to charge electronic devices. All in all very basic

I visited the Araliya handling agent lounge which Qatar Airways use at Colombo Airport. The lounge is basic, tightly packed worn out seating, slow wifi. Cold unenidble food. Very limited food options, no local food. The lounge is so brightly lit it's as good as a tanning booth, couldn't find any recharging stations only single wall sockets requiring adaptor.  Not a premium lounge by any means.

Qatar Airways lounge at Heathrow Airport is a top notch lounge and one of the best lounges I have ever visited. Staff were friendly and courteous, food was excellent, heaps of seating with fast Wi-Fi. As soon as entered the lounge and sat down a member of staff came up to me and asked me if I would like a drink. Service at its best. Passengers were well informed by staff of the short delay to the flight. Other airlines with lounges at Heathrow should take note of the high level of service and quality of food provided in this lounge.

I wrote last month that I was underwhelmed by this lounge, as I found it to be too big and impersonal, lacking any snug areas to hide away in. But on my latest, slightly longer, transit through DOH, I was able to discover the 'quiet area' which has showers next to it and a restaurant/bar just outside. This was just what I wanted. The quiet area is exceptionally peaceful; you have a private room for your party, to relax on loungers in peace (though their metal arms could be made more comfortable). The shower rooms were clean and well maintained, though it would have been nice to have a shoe horn available

A well designed, clean, organised lounge with ample seating and great staff. Play area for children with MBC 3 (Children's channel) was an added plus. Also within the lounge is a small area to buy perfumes. This lounge offers bedrooms based on an hourly rate. Cannot fault it. Overall nice experience and look forward to visiting it again.

Was supposed to visit the Al Maha Lounge as per Lounge Key (Bank Credit Card Privilege), however was told by staff it is full, and I was directed to the First Class Lounge on the other side. Was disappointed as it was overcrowded, noisy and food below standard for a first class lounge and the queues to get food were long.  Never visiting this lounge again and will insist on the Al Maha Lounge which is bigger and more organised.

I do not rave about this lounge because it's hard to find because signage is atrocious and the lounge is just too big. It may be visually impressive but it lacks warmth, charm or comfortable places to wait for your flight. Restaurant buffet is nowhere near as good as food used to be, even in the old airport.

Very beautiful and functional lounge. Nice and luxurious also. Two level lounge with plenty of couches and coffee bar at the ground. On the upper floor there is a restaurant, a full bar and a coffee place. Flawless service, great food, nice showers and toiltes.

I had a seven hour layover in this lounge and the scale, architecture and styling of this incredible building doesn't disappoint. All soaring space and blonde marble, the lounge is more of a 5 star hotel in both concept and size. While there were large numbers of staff ready to serve weary travellers, the service, while eager and genuine, doesn't always deliver. Arriving at 1am, I was unable to get a bed in the sleep rooms, being told that the next available bed wouldn't be until 7am. I was shown to the 'family area' which featured large sectioned semi private spaces with subdued lighting, comfortable sofas, armchairs and TVs. Before deciding to sleep on the sofa, I asked for a pillow and blanket which never appeared. In the morning, the showers were occupied with 8 people on the waiting list before me. I managed to find a single shower in the family area and after a wait of 20 mins, was able to use that. Again, nice to be able to shower but not if the designers of the lounge had underestimated capacity and the increased traffic for beds at night time and showers first thing in the morning.  Food was good, cappuccino was from a machine and the italian section of the heavily promoted a la carte menu featured 3 different types of pasta.

This handing lounge is the only lounge for business class passengers in the international section of Kolkata Airport, used by all airlines. I had an hour or so before the flight and used the lounge. It is a basic facility with everything you need - food (Indian), snacks, coffee and tea, a selection of alcoholic drinks, free wi-fi, local newspapers, few trade magazines, comfortable couches, a couple of TV screens, and a board listing departing flights. There is one desk top computer which was used the entire time I was there by lounge staff. It is a manned bar but the bartender was not present when I walked up to it. He arrived shortly. The bathroom was clean but the fixtures looked cheap, dated, and crude. The presentation of the food is not appealing and the dining section is dark. At a small cooking station, pasta dishes could be ordered. The lounge serves its purpose but the layout and furniture is such you cannot meaningfully do any real work other than checking emails on your own device.

As an Executive Platinum/Emerald status flyer, Qatar Airways invited me to relax at the American Airlines Admiral Lounge at New York JFK just across the gate from the flight would depart. The lounge is located behind another lounge. There were plenty of drinks, buffet food, snacks, free wi-fi, desk top computers, couches with charging stations, newspapers and magazines. It was crowded but quiet. The two hours I had before my flight started to board was well spent. A staff came by announcing that the Qatar Airways flight was ready to go. I did not use the bathroom or the showers. All in all, a good place to wait.

The Plaza Premium lounges used in Phnom Penh Qatar Airways QR is a 3rd party lounges but of excellent quality. It is new, outstanding, positive surprise with all facilities (incl. fitness room!) and local, hot foods. 4 wines, 2 draft beers, no champagne. Glass panorama windows to 2 sides. Fast internet, lots of support staff. Roomy with good air climate.

As a Qatar Airways business lounge this handling agent lounge at Oslo is pretty average. Food is very basic, cold snacks / sandwiches, nothing out of the ordinary, probably the most basic of any lounge I have been in. WIFI is good. It's a shared lounge with pay to use customers. There is a segregated area behind the reception desk for business class customers. Nothing particularly bad, but nothing to get excited about either. Fair old walk to the departure gate (and you need to pass through passport control, which can get pretty busy) so leave plenty of time.

The international terminal has a lounge that is used by all airlines. It is well-signposted and is reached up a flight of stairs or an elevator after clearing security. With only one flight scheduled in the next five hours, there were only a few patrons. A selection of mostly Indian spirits were available at the bar, served by an attendant. TV screens showed a National Geographic animal program. Cold soft drinks, water, and beer were available. Nearly all of the food were Indian-style and looked unappetizing. One computer available for use, free wifi - decent speed. A collection of newspapers and trade magazines. Very comfortable couches to rest. Good place to relax before a flight. There is a dedicated restroom, including shower facilities, for the patrons and from the balcony one can look down at the departure concourse -- at that hour it was empty save for a couple of armed soldiers patrolling. Overall, it is a basic, serves-the-purpose lounge.

The Al Maha Transit Lounge was full but had sufficient seats available when I was there. There were two types of seats to choose from; armchair seats with low tables and those for dining cafeteria style. There were plenty of staff on hand to ensure that plates and glasses are quickly cleared and the tables cleaned. The food was delicious, fresh and there is a decent variety of choices from soups, salads, hummus, breads, sandwiches, desserts and a coffee machine. There was a chef on hand who replenished the food regularly which is nice. The toilets were packed so for those wishing to have a shower, they might have to wait for sometime.

Qatar Airways use the DNATA Lounge at Singapore Changi Airport which is very nice, it has very nice showers, it features a reading area, a big selection of food choices. The lounge is not big, which is good. The WiFi connection was perfect. It is a little bit far away from the gates.

The Qatar Airways Al Mourjan Business Class Lounge in Doha is the best lounge I have been to. There are two restaurants and couple bars, a cigar lounge, a business conference area and wide choice of soft and alcoholic drinks. The people that work there were extremely friendly and nice.

I recently flew from Singapore to Doha and was disappointed that Qatar Airways used a temporary lounge at Changi Airport shared by other airlines. The airline made no apology whilst checking in that I was going to experience a rubbish lounge in what is one of the worlds finest airports.  Having a good home base is one thing but the other end of the journey is just as important

Qatar Airways used the shared "Escape Lounge". Its quite small, just a room without any views. I went there at breakfast time and you could order bacon or sausage breakfast rolls. Otherwise, the usual fare for self service. Its ok for half an hour - but its not the most exciting lounge I've visited. The staff were very friendly however and they came up to me personally to say that my flight was boarding rather than making a tannoy announcement. I would probably not pay the £25 fee for non business class users as I don't think it would be value for money.

The Qatar Airways lounge was pretty empty on both visits, food was of a very high standard along with excellent showers. Plenty of space to relax. Only issue was very slow internet, as it is free across the airport. Plenty of staff around to assist you. Very easy access from main concourse.

If you're a oneworld frequent flyer (Emerald or Sapphire) you don't use the main Qatar Airways lounges for passengers flying in first or business, but the frequent flyer lounges called First and Business. As a top tier card holder I get to use the First lounge. There's a very simple food offering, cold pasta, salad, slices of cake and wine, tho if you ask they'll get a glass of champagne for you! Otherwise there's not much going on there. The lounge is located under a giant electronic advertising hoarding with flashing coloured lights constantly changing the ambience in the room. With my Qatar Platinum (emerald) card I can use the Cathay First Class lounge in Hong Kong or the BA Emerald lounge at LHR both with excellent food and drink options. In contrast lounges for frequent flyers in Doha are disappointing.

This is probably the best airline lounge I have visited - a big WOW to it as compared with most other lounges, and it is not a first class lounge. But food is served as in First class lounge with table setting and main course served with wine, and I note that they had Amarone or Reserve de la Comtesse. Indeed there are several eateries within the huge lounge. On entry there is a pool that is probably larger than most other lounges. It is great to relax here over a midnight or later flight, as it is tranquil and spacious. No other business class lounge can match it!

The Al Mourjan lounge is located on the third floor of the airport, up quite a large set of escalators. Staff scan your boarding pass at the bottom of the escalator to ensure that you’re eligible to enter. After heading upstairs you’re presented with a stunning water feature. Water shoots up in various patterns, creating quite a calm and pleasing atmosphere. Located above is the larger of two dining and bar areas. A large chandelier (which stretches all the way to the ceiling of the second floor) is the centrepiece of this end of the lounge. Surrounded by seating areas, this staircase will take you up to the main dining area. Suffice to say it’s very impressive. The lower level of the lounge is huge. Outside the raised floor area in the middle are individual and paired seating areas, which are comfortable and very well equipped. Every seat has power and USB ports, along with a fixed tablet where you can access flight information and do some basic web browsing. On a raised area in the middle of the floor are some more seating areas and a small self service bar with tea, coffee, water and a small selection of soft drinks.Here you can clearly see the second floor dining area of the lounge. It’s quite striking from this vantage point and even more so when sitting up there yourself. Standing in the middle like this really gives you an appreciation for how large the space is. The lounge offers both buffet and à la carte dining options. The hot dishes tended to be mainly middle eastern inspired and every dish we had was excellent. These naturally change to suit the time of day. Curtains were always drawn at the far end of the dining area. I assume this is because the view out this window would be less than stellar, or possibly to limit the amount of sunlight coming into the lounge. Qatar Airways have really stepped up their game with the opening of this new lounge. Their previous offering, a Premium Terminal was only available to passengers flying with Qatar and was much smaller. The travel from the plane in a bus and car transfer back out to the plane was also cumbersome. The attention to detail in the lounge is apparent. This new Al Mourjan lounge is accessible to more people, which means it is a lot busier. Definitely a lounge to look forward to visiting on your next trip though Doha’s Hamad International Airport.

Flew business class from Bangalore to Orlando, had the opportunity to visit the well known Al Mourjan lounge at Doha Hamad airport. Very crowded in the morning, managed to a get a table in the buffet area upstairs, breakfast itself was okay, ordered a Spanish omelette which was good. The Sandwich from the Deli counter was ordinary. On my return though, the lounge was pretty thin, the buffet spread was good. The Arabic fusion was awesome, full of flavour and taste, being a foodie and cooking a hobby, managed to taste a few other delicacies like Prawn biryani (wrongly mentioned as Chicken Biryani!) and the dessert spreads were just outstanding. Would like to visit this lounge in future with a bit more time to relax here.

Qatar Airways has a separate lounge for non-QR / oneworld premium members. The lounge is not really impressive and was crowded when I used it and some tables were messy from the previous guests. The choice of food was limited and poor. Kudos to the staff at the restroom and shower facilities who were courteous and always available to help the customers.

Nice spacious 2 levels lounge with good food and great bathroom services. Fresh salad buffet on the ground floor and a la carte/buffet on the first floor. The bathrooms are very clean and spacious. This lounge is even better than Turkish Airlines business class lounge

Its really nice, great ambience decor and mood. Lovely bathrooms and you can tell everything was made with thought. Food not so much. The chicken we ordered slightly hard and tasteless, didn't finish it and had cheese instead. It didnt seem to concern any of the staff there who were sparsely located unless you were beside the bar.  Overall love everything about this place except the dining.

In short this lounge is the best of the best. New vibrant, yet an oasis of calm with the finest wine list and superb service. The food options are various and would meet all palates. Qatar Airways have once again pulled a 5 star review from me. In my view the best carrier on the market.

Qatar Airways Lounge at Heathrow Airport has a big space, bright and nice décor. A la carte menu for main meals. Good selections of fruits, desserts and delis. I've ordered their version of Tum Yum soup which tasted a bit odd. Nice toilets with good amenities. Attentive staff. Very near boarding gates.

One of the most spectacular lounges I have ever visited. Enormous in size, sophisticated design, endless food options, extremely friendly staff, personal service, buffet and/or restaurant style a-la-carte restaurants, gerat selection of drinks and wines, and very good wifi. It does not get any better than this! This is a lounge that makes connecting long haul flights a pleasure.

The Qatar Airways Al Safwa lounge has been opened for two weeks. The lounge is vast and there are many areas where you can find peace and quiet. My husband and I both took showers. My experience in the shower rooms was good. A shower was available immediately and the shower room was roomy and had every amenity I needed. A shower room was not available for my husband immediately so he was escorted to a rest room which had two beds and a bathroom. We then had breakfast and it was the best lounge breakfast I have ever had. Table service that felt like you were in a 5 Star restaurant. This long awaited lounge lives up to all expectations. The service by the staff the relaxing music and the amazing water features. Once again Qatar Airways is leading the other airlines.

Qatar Airways Business Class Lounge at Hamad International Airport is absolutely heaven and paradise on earth.  Every single staff member was welcoming and extremely pleasant and highly professional. Without compare in a league of it's own. Food and drinks out of scale in a good way!

The Qatar Airways lounge at Heathrow Terminal 4 is the best in the business - light and airy, plenty of comfortable seating, excellent cloakrooms and a good choice of food (you can either help yourself to salads etc. or order from the menu). The lounge at Doha's new airport is huge. It has an area at the back with long tables where you can get toasted sandwiches and drinks - not an oasis of calm but useful if you're in transit.

A large surface under a very high ceiling, huge volume, though you find lots of places quiet and giving some kind of privacy; different style of chairs, some are more comfortable than others. Restaurant upstairs either buffet or a la carte menu has a large array of choice and there is also another downstairs were you can order sandwich and snacks of your choice. Showers are comfortable and quite a large number, so I never had to wait. General atmosphere and decor are nice, as all building and decoration materials are sober, mainly wood, stone and metal. Excellent wifi connection and sockets everywhere to charge your phones. I had an 8 hour and a 4 hour lay over in this lounge and I found it almost the perfect place. I say "almost" because when you arrive from transfer level, a bit sleepy after a long flight you may easily miss the sign showing the direction to the lounge (whose escalator is just close by). Also. there is a very large waterpool with a bubble effect and if you sit nearby you may get quickly bored by the ceaseless pop of air bubbles out of the water, so I recommend to sit in another part of the lounge!

The handling agent "Escape" Business Class lounge that Qatar Airways use at Manchester airport is horrible - the worst I have ever been in. Not only is it outdated with uncomfortable furnishings, the food is limited - dry sandwiches. There are no staff to help you. No bottled water. Very limited beverages to choose from. Horrible white wine. And don't get me started on the toilets, they're back down the dingy corridor you have to walk to get to the lounge and are general public (and they were dirty and untidy)! This is meant to be a business class lounge.

This Qatar Airways Al Mourjan lounge by far is the best one I've ever had. When you get in, you're immediately greeted by very informative staff to an oasis. There are two great places to eat, a place for refreshments in the middle, showers, and everything you want in a lounge maybe except for a bed. The food, service, atmosphere, and everything else was great. If I could have this lounge for all my transit stops, I would.

The staff at the lounge Qatar Airways uses at MNL Airport was very attentive and kind, but the lounge itself was just so-so. If you have a guest with you or if you don't have access yourself, the entrance is just $20 which I think is quite reasonable if you just want a quiet place to stay, especially if you arrived a few hours early. Don't expect too much though beyond the minimum requirements of a business class lounge. The restrooms are in a different nearby lounge as well unfortunately. Overall, I was satisfied given my initial disappointment with the airport itself.

Qatar Airways Al Mourjan business class lounge at Hamad International Airport. Fabulous from beginning to end, an oasis of freshness. A good staff attitude and good food.  Excellent refreshments and easy access. I loved it.

Qatar Airways has 3 or 4 lounges at the new Hamad airport. When I was here last year the airport had only been open 3 days. This trip, the airport looked a lot different! Everything was finished and occupied. The lounges are amazing. Being a Business Class passenger you have access to 2 lounges. The lounge is huge, I wish I had more time at the airport to enjoy it! It is two levels. You can find snacks downstairs, and upstairs full-on meals. The food is good, lots of selections, and lots of it if you wish. The customer service is fantastic. This airline does a fantastic job. You will enjoy the lounges at Hamad. They have prayer rooms, luggage storage, toilets, showers, and quiet rooms. Areas for working with your computer, the lounge has it all.

Qatar Airways does not have their own lounge at Madrid Barajas Airport so you use the VIP lounge which is kind of a general lounge for many other airlines. Very nice lounge. When I first got there, I was only 1 of a few people. 1 hour later it was busier. They have two sections so there is plenty of room to spread out. Free wifi, luggage storage, toilets and showers. There is a sleeping room but ironically right opposite the open doorway they have a TV facing the sitting area which had the volume up pretty loud. No one was watching it, too bad they had it on so loud. They have lots of food choices both hot and cold, and bring out fresh food frequently. I filled myself up with snacks and lunch so wasn't hungry for the flight. Plenty of seating. They have TV's scattered throughout if you want to watch TV, newspapers and magazines available to read as well. Clean, the staff was very nice.

Qatar Airways is a really brilliant airline, but their choice of the Bidvest lounge is surprising.  Poorly trained staff, dirty lavatories, dreary dark decorations. Slow and inadequate wifi. The food in short supply, poorly presented and of variable quality.

Great lounge, quiet and lots of friendly helpful staff. Good selection of food in various sections of the lounge. Good shower facilities although I had to wait for about 30 minutes for it to be available.

This is a beautiful lounge - huge with lots of sofas and chairs for rest between your flights. There are very few sleeper chairs around despite its size. The sleepers are found only next to the entrance to the lounge and just above the common area of the airport and near a huge billboard. So despite its intended use, it is not only noisy, you get lots of flashing lights from the nearby huge billboard. Despite having many staff around, nobody comes around to offer you drinks or to top them up. I was at one of the sofa seats downstairs and asked one of the staff if I could get orange juice. His answer  "upstairs sir". Not entirely incorrect but not very helpful. As compared to their lounge at Heathrow airport where the staff are not only attentive but much more helpful than these lot at Hamad airport, this lounge just doesn't cut it for me. However, food wise, they've got it covered well. From the restaurant upstairs to the sandwich bar downstairs, it is vey good. A tip for those having meals at the restaurant upstairs - there is a menu from which you can order food if you do not want to take your food from the buffet table - the staff just don't tell you about it until you ask for the menu. The lamb chop and the beef choices are excellent from this menu. The shower facilities are excellent if you can get past the heat - seems that there is no aircon in the shower rooms. Wifi connection is patchy at best. I've never been able to get a connection to view my home and office cameras in all the times that I've been there. I love Qatar Airways. I just hope that service improves at this lounge as I invariably spend a lot of time at this lounge waiting for my next flight.

The lounge comfort is basic and acceptable but its too small. Internet is okay, staff are very polite. foods limited, fruits, bread and middle eastern sweet. Good things is the juice are fresh from the kitchen.

This is a new lounge at a new airport so very impressive. A good design feature is that it's right in front of you when you come through transfers so no long walks trying to find it! There's a nice check-in area with lots of lovely Qatar staff, then you go through to a nice water feature. There's a buffet restaurant with a la carte menu and bar above up a nice spiral staircase and a 'make your own' sandwich and salad bar in the opposite direction all serving alcoholic and soft drinks. There's self-service coffee machines and tea dotted around. There's a hideous smoke room for smokers, lucky I'm not. You won't need to light up, just walk in and breathe. Overall a good place to rest between flights with showers, free wifi, a nice quiet zone and I think I saw a children's play area. The duty free shops are down a long escalator below.

I experienced Qatar Airways London Heathrow and Doha lounges which were fantastic in every way from the food to rest rooms. This handling lounge in Singapore was a shock, the food on offer was dry and looked like it been sitting there a long time. Certainly could do with spending some money on the interior.

This was a sectioned off area of Servisair Aspire lounge. Very uninspiring and nothing to aspire to. Arrived in the morning for an 11.00am flight. Told where the sectioned off area was. Presented with cold meats, cheese and stodgy bread. The non-sectioned area had a selection of breakfast cereals and a nicer seating area so we set ourselves there instead. Coffee from the machine was good but no fresh milk. A trip to the general area for a glass. Lounge was extremely warm and a fair distance from the departure gates - allow a good 10 minutes at least. Compared to some of the other airport lounges, this third party facility that Qatar Airways have to use is a pretty poor offering.
Great lounge, open and spacious with a decent restaurant on the upper floor. Food was of good quality and staff were pleasant and well trained.

On my outbound flight from LHR to AUH via Doha I was allowed access to the fantastic main Qatar lounge. However, on my return to LHR just 7 days later I was told to use a smaller lounge for oneworld frequent flyers. I was dissapointed with this change in policy, as were other passengers. The smaller frequent flyer lounge has uncomfortable seating and very poor selection of food.  Undermines the point of belonging to a frequent flier programme with lounge access. On my return to the lounge at 3pm I was told they had ran out of champagne and spirits apart from Bacardi. There would be no more until a store was to be opened at 9pm. The point of going for an indirect flight with Qatar was because I had thought I would be looked after in the lounge. It seems this is no longer the case.

As a Qatar gold member I am disappointed at the change in lounge at Doha airport back to the older previously temporary lounge. This lounge is not only too small and noisy but also crowded and uncomfortable with a poor selection of food and drinks. I have no doubt that these sentiments will be echoed by other Privilege gold members and I hope that Qatar Air reconsiders this change in order to maintain its reputation as an airline offering superior customer service.

Al Mourjan lounge at Hamad airport in Doha is really impressive. However missing the old Business and First Class Terminal. It is so huge and far from many gates. I prefer the LHR Qatar Airways lounge. Cozy and more quiet. The restaurant/food were amazing. Very spacious and luxury seating area. However if you are looking for a chaise longue in the quiet area be patient - there was a huge waiting list. Also they forget to install A/C in the shower rooms. So don't have a too long and hot shower because you will be sweating afterwards.

Best lounge I have ever been through Heaven Class. Could not fault the place Great food and Bev staff all helpful and pleasant. There is any amount of food choice and okay WiFi. Anyone who complains about this lounge is simply impossible to please.

Outstanding we felt as if our holiday had begun at Heathrow. The quiet understated luxury was wonderful nothing was too much trouble food was amazing staff were polite and respectful. (Unlike Phuket Business Lounge where it was help yourself to a pot noodle).

Find negative comments about staff strange. We were waited on the whole time we were there. Most of staff were from Nepal and were very friendly. Good selection of food. We take on board about ordering sandwiches. Only real negative comment the lounge was a long way from our gate apparently 1km. No walk ways meant we had to rush to the gate. Perhaps you should consider having a board giving approximate walking times to the various gates.
Long narrow lounge. Bar a long way from food. Easy to miss the bar Noisy. At least we got a seat. Puzzled why we are sometimes sent to different lounges. Food nothing special. Airport a nightmare.

Whilst there is a lot to be admired about this lounge it is clearly designed for business people who have 3 hr+ stopovers at Doha. I'm sure the a la Carte restaurants are excellent but my wife and I had less than 2 hr stopover and after you've made the lengthy walk from the gate had a freshen up etc the only thing we had time for is a cool beer and a selection from a quick and easy 'help yourself 'buffet (sandwich etc). The trouble is that this does not seem to exist because the food and drink section is located at the far end of the lounge and you have to put in orders for tailor made sandwiches. We did not have the time for that so downed a beer and left. Surely it would be possible to put a small selection of buffet sandwiches nachos crisps nuts etc for people who were in our position ? The lounge gets very busy around 11pm to 1 am and it was pretty difficult to find two seats together during that time though when we left it was a lot less crowded.

Wasn't expecting much. No natural light but there was a decent selection of hot and cold food. I just had some fresh fruit cake and water. All very pleasant. I was called to the gate 70 minutes before departure this was too early as I was just hanging about the gate which was too hot and had awful Mosquitos flying about.

An absolute gem of a lounge. Sit at the bar or relax in a comfy seat & enjoy the waited service the choice is yours. There's a choice of informal dining from the Deli or eat in the Brasserie - I chose the fillet steak with peppercorn sauce. When the food & drink takes its toll the 'facilities' are of quality hotel standard. All lounges should use this place as their blueprint; simply outstanding.

On arrival the lounge looks spectacular. But it is too big and loses its exclusive feel. There are some comfortable leather sofas but too many of the seats are uncomfortable. There are two restaurants serving good buffet food which is of good quality but the Heathrow Qatar lounge has a superior offering with cook to order dishes. As Qatar Airways treats this airport as a hub with potentially long transit periods then a few more facilities should ideally be provided such as a spa and lounger type seating allowing you to have a more comfortable sleep. After paying good money for a business class flight I don't feel I should have to pay good money for a transit hotel. As M Clarke mentioned in the review below  there are loads of staff who hang about doing not a lot I don't want to be fussed over but it would be nice to be offered a drink or something. Overall a good lounge but underwhelming maybe I was spoilt at the Qatar Heathrow lounge but I think this lounge could do better given all the hype on their website.

A fantastic lounge the best I have visited and in my opinion better than the Al Mourjan lounge at Doha which I visited on my arrival. The restaurant was amazing with made to order dishes and superb dessert station - I don't have a sweet tooth but just couldn't resist. Very spacious and luxury seating area with staff taking your drinks orders. A minor and amusing point was the waiter (who claimed he was the barman) had never heard of port I explained it was similar to sherry but he was still unsure what I was on about (he sounded eastern European) in the end I settled for another glass of Bollinger champagne.

First things first - to go to the loo when you arrive (not an uncommon destination I think) you have to go up a long ramp and then down another long ramp diagonally opposite then double back on yourself and walk another 30/40 feet; this is bonkers. Every time I arrive here I try a different seat - there is not a single comfortable seat in the place; there are a couple of nice leather sofas that look really nice but I've never been able to get near them because they're always 'full'. There are weird modern seats (very 60s - they look great) that are too low and you have to virtually lie in them or odd seats (that are at least higher) with big 'conservatory type' surrounds but they really aren't that comfortable. Then there are the seats beside the very fancy looking computer monitors that are at a completely unrealistic angle for use but although these seats look vaguely comfortable it's like sitting in a corridor. There isn't a scrap of carpet anywhere that I can see. There's what looks like a nice restaurant about a quarter of a mile away (seems like with the up and down ramps) and several tea and coffee stations and then at the opposite end to the restaurant is a deli. The old Ppremium terminal at Doha was lovely - nice people would pass by and ask if you'd like a sandwich and bring it to you with a glass of something. This place is absolutely crawling with really lovely helpful staff but they don't seem to actually do anything. Worst of all there is NO SPA free or otherwise unless you check into a hotel no hairdresser either. For a lounge purporting to be world class this is way off I think. I would happily pay for a massage and a shampoo any day of the week but there's nothing. I spoke to a member of staff this evening and was bemoaning the fact that you have to zigzag all over the place to get anywhere and that I loved the old lounge and she said she couldn't count the number of people who had said that. I love Qatar Airways but this lounge is a bit of a fail for me - a great shame because I spend about 4 hours here every couple of months.

Qatar Airways is a spectacular company dealing with distinction its premium passengers. The lounge for business class is the best I have met in the world. Must impeccable service Krug and all the delicacies of the company's staff of care. Are to be congratulated.

Qatar Airways is a spectacular company however this Sao Paulo Airport executive class lounge used by the company is awful. All companies of the OneWorld use this lounge in the new T 3 in GRU. The catering is horrible the drinks have few options and low quality.

At present probably the best lounge in the world matches and exceeds other first class lounges. Modern extremely spacious food and drink selection simply amazing. Modern architecture all perfectly organized.

Had a long layover here. Lounge is super impressive as far as the aesthetics go and the range of different seating options is good. The food was of a good standard: I ate upstairs and went for the mezze option rather than the a la carte. The staff were really friendly and helpful. I wanted somewhere to sleep and was lucky enough to get one of the quiet area cells. Not very comfortable but I was able to get a few hours sleep and a shower before the next leg of my flight. Overall a really good experience: felt much less busy and cluttered that the equivalent in Dubai.

I was disappointed and alienated by the huge lounge sections which lack any cosy atmosphere and personality. Facilities are there but not always easy to find or access. A desert of steel glass and marble. It is far too big.

The business class lounge is horrible for more than 1-2 hours. A 7 hour layover is an ordeal given the absence of facilities for lying down to sleep. If you find the quiet area tucked away just off the main dining area there are no loungers or blankets or pillows - but I was offered pyjamas! The room reverberates - too much stone metal and wood. The facilities are spotless and staff very polite and helpful.

This has to be one of the most dramatic interior spaces at any airport anywhere. The size of at least several football fields with several levels it is both restful and convenient. While we sampled just a bit of the food the mezze and the rest looked wonderful. We were there mid- morning and the space seemed almost empty. Staff were terrific helpful and informative.

I was in transit for almost 9 hours so delighted that the lounge is now fully operational. As much as I loved the old premium terminal there were times when it would be so crowded it was impossible to get a seat but that was often due to passengers taking up a table and three chairs for the coats bags or newspapers no such problem now as there is a range of different types of chair and sofas spread around the bottom floor in different areas. The design is exceptional with a very nice water feature. At the time I' usually there the lounge tends to be quite busy when I arrive but after a few hours its almost empty. As this was the first time I' had any time to spend there I had a good walk around and bumped into two members of the staff of the old premium lounge who remembered me from previous times. There are two restaurants one on each floor a number of deli type counters and a few places where you could help yourself to tee coffee or soft drinks at any time. I tried a number of different chairs before managing to find an vacant sofa where I could stretch out for a few hours. Later I tried one of the work stations so I could use the USB charging unit each of the stations has a small bag of snacks and a bottle of water. I'd just finished changing the phone and reading the printed copies of the UK newspapers when staff told me that breakfast was being served in the upstairs restaurant. All the staff were helpful and friendly.
The lounge is a great place to stay to pass the time between flights. The lounge offers wonderful food plentiful drinks and the wonderful showers.

This lounge is very spacious and comfortable there are many areas and dining options. The staff are very helpful. But there is a problem with the lack of toilet facilities first time I've seen a queue for the gents. In general very good but I still prefer the old premium terminal.

The lounge didn't feel exclusive and too overcrowded. Lounge open to noise of the rest of the terminal and very difficult to find. Had breakfast and food offering was extremely bland. I expected so much and was very disappointed. Compared to the Premium Lounge at LHR this is a joke.

Poor air conditioning lack of food choices terrible internet (spent 45 minutes trying to download 17 emails and never actually managed it). Even the on-table tablets couldn't connect to the internet. Very poor in comparison to the old premium lounge.

Qatar Airways new business class lounge is up and running and is quite exceptional. A simpler more elegant version of Emirates lounge in Dubai. I was there when it was not very crowded so it will be interesting to see what it's like when it is full - that was the worst part of the old premium lounge. The lounge has 2 dining facilities several snack areas and bars lots of seating a business area and as with its old premium lounge a lot of staff being helpful. Big and airy it is open to the new terminal but the noise did not seem to be a problem. There are numerous zones for seating broken up by architectural screen walls interior plantscaping and changes to the floor level. Most seats have a touchpad for announcements and surfing and a small set up of bottled water and simple snacks. Aesthetically the design is flawless.

Expected more from the temporary lounge it is not close to the standards of the lounge at the old airport. Only 5-6 tables for eating the rest are small narrow tables with two electric outlets placed between two armchairs not enough room for two to place plates.

The temporary lounge is a real shame compared to the previous one : overcrowded poor choice of food and drinks. Terrible when you have many hours of transit in the middle of the night. No wifi dedicated to the lounge but Airport free wifi very slow.
Business class lounge was full with no where to seat. Very limited food.. Refused entry to the Oryx even though there own website states I should have been allow in.

The business class lounges at the new airport in Doha are sill under construction and won't be open for another 3 months a fact you will only find out at checking as we did. There is a temporary first and business class lounge but access is highly restricted due to their limited space and normal oneworld status privileges don't apply. The temporary first class lounge is cramped hot offers a coffee machine with a few snacks. If you are going to be in transit for any length of time recommend you avoid the temporary lounges and head to the transit hotel instead or stay in the main concourse where it's cooler and less congested. I am very surprised that they didn't put the building of their new premium lounges as a priority prior to the new airport opening.

Cost for the Oryx lounge is 40USD. Given the state of Doha airport whilst the new one is being constructed I think it well worth the money. Showers alone after a long haul are worthwhile and the buffet whilst simple is plentiful and the coffee good. Spacious clean and plenty of seating.

The Premium is huge but there are often too many passengers using it. Staff are very courteous and tried very hard and found tables for us in minutes. Lots of choices in buffet food and drinks.
