A great lounge which has strict entry control. Its been opened a while starting to look a little shabby. Good choice of food and drinks pleasant service. Shower facility a bit poor and cramped.

Would have written about their lounge in Colombo but never could find it! However I can write about their lounge in KUL (KLIA). Rather than have a lounge of their own or sharing with one of the major airlines that have lounges there they send their business class to the horrible little lounge that anyone can buy a pass to. Crowded dirty a smoking area that can at best hold 5 people standing (and almost always packed) poor food. It was so bad that I went to the public area and paid for food and drink.

Very comfortable and spacious overlooking the runways. Excellent choice of hot and cold food hot and cold drinks alcoholic and non alcoholic. Free massage showers and internet access. Good selection of international and local newspapers. All in all as nice a business class lounge as I have used.

3 hours of transit in Colombo with access to Serendib Lounge in CMB airport. The lounge access is not really clear no indication just a small label on white doors. Its spacious with modern stuff for a biz lounge : hot meal shower 6 internet access and massage service to de stress from your flight. You have 6 rooms to sleep. The only negative point is that shower were used by a staff member when I tried to get inside. For passengers holding a Skywards Gold card or Silver and travelling on Economy UL has built a small corner separated from the noisy airport with small garden barriers and awful furniture. The buffet of this economy lounge consists in sandwichies and cakes with free drinks. You have also 2 internet access.

TAM do not use Oneworld lounge at Frankfurt Airport since it operates on Lufthansa Terminal. In the past Senator and Business Class Lounges from Lufthansa were offered but it looks like the TAM Airlines need to cut down costs, so they have changed to Air Canada Lounge.

Apart from its new location no effort has been made from previous locations regarding catering. The snacks quite often are stale with cheap cold cuts and poor quality cheeses. A mediocre service quite in tune with the TAM overall performance.

The lounge is a dark affair without any natural light and deficient artificial lighting. Very poor layout in a meandering way. Food is very basic and drinks acceptable. WiFi was adequate with an access code. The lounge is used by several airlines and tends to get crowded. One of the poorer lounge experiences.

In what is supposed to be the biggest airport in Latin America LATAM is providing a crowded place with poor seating availability miserable food offerings where dough seems to be the basic ingredient. Do not dare looking for plugs either. Better show up with a fully charged laptop.
A very crowded place. Very warm. People sitting on the floor as no seats available. Left the lounge early to find somewhere to sit! Boarded plane early so we could sit down.

Departing on Lufthansa First Class to Europe I visited the TAM lounges. The newly opened Business Class Lounge on Terminal 2. A big one with many sofas and family room computer stations self-service bar etc. It looked new and had views of the apron but I found it kind of tacky. Its buffet had a coffee machine plus petit-fours and cakes wines and other drinks. I asked the receptionist about the First Class lounge she said it was a 5 minutes walk to Terminal 1. So I moved and found it closed! I went to the opposite door the TAM Business Lounge and was invited to wait there as their First one would open soon. This is an older and smaller lounge it was very crowded and was even hard to find a place to sit. Noisy and dark but it was well-decorated. The buffet was ok with some wraps and wines/beers choices. Soon the receptionist came to me and said I could move to their First Class lounge. Small but decorated in good taste piano in the entrance leather sofas but no apron or outside views. The room looked exclusive and private. The menu had great choices as Lobsters Carpaccio salads etc. A great wines and spirits list.

A disappointing lounge in one of the worst international airport terminals (Terminal 2 at GIG). Rubbery plastic-wrapped food small selection of drinks awfully slow complimentary wi-fi provided via a scratch card and limited to 2 hours. Furniture and decor are standard airport lounge fare. Bathroom had broken fixtures. The place is basically unstaffed.
Very clean and elegant but limited services. Wifi through a 3rd party company which gives you limited time (1 hour card). Nice selection of beverages but food in a "canapé" style.

Lounge small and very busy people were sitting on the floor as there were no seats. Internet access good. Food dreadful. Limited quantity and what was available was awful. No cups or glasses available. Wine good but appears soft drinks were only limited to local brands perhaps due to the high volume of passengers in the lounge at any one time. Receptionist very pleasant but catering staff very sullen. I left very promptly after writing this review. Colleagues who have also passed through this lounge have had a similar experience.

I quite enjoyed the lounge - only negative is that it can get overcrowded. But since my flight was a later one pax from other flights left early. I had a nice shower and enjoyed the toiletries. The food is in reasonable - tasty snacks and cakes. Drinks are good and wine is served if asked. Quite enjoyed the live music played by the pianist which always set a soothing mood. Internet is good and wi-fi password is given as you enter the lounge by receptionist.

Small but nice place as long as it not crowded. Choice of newspapers/magazines as well as snacks is limited. Surprisingly there was beer and hard liquor but no wine available. Internet computers are available for free. Nice and welcoming staff. Shower was great with lots of towels and toiletries.

This is a lounge that could improve. A choice of drinks comfortable seats but little food and an internet connection that comes and goes. But the staff are nice and announcements are made timely. The location of the lounge itself (near the gates) is convenient but the gates location are not (you have to walk across the entire terminal and to use stairs so if you have any duty-free shopping to do you should plan to do it before going to the lounge).

Like everything in Guarulhos airport TAM's lounge is too small. Signalling is poor: the lounge is located on the second floor (turn left just after passport control before entering the duty free shop). But generally you will find a place to seat in one of the three rooms. The selection of snacks is not wide but fresh and they can fix you a caipirinha if you ask for it. It has a shower (what a blessing!) and if you use it they will give you a nice selection of L'Occitane toiletries. The Wi-Fi works well. Sometimes a musician plays the piano. Announcements are made timely. Staff are helpful and proficient in English sometimes in Spanish.

It offers fairly basic comfort levels but would expect more from the home airport for Transaero Airlines. No shower was possible during my stopover and disappointed by that. Internet was okay lounge not too crowded when I visited (midday) but food choice was quite limited. Did noty find the staff friendly - they seemed to be poor on English language skills and just stared at me politely for most questions.

My recent visit to the SWISS First Lounge at Gates E was a sublime prelude to my journey. I was welcomed into an atmosphere of calm elegance. The lounge offers a well-curated array of spaces. The seating options are abundant and comfortable, with plush armchairs that got panoramic views of the tarmac and distant Alps. A particular highlight was the dayroom. Outfitted with a remarkably soft bed and minimalist design, it provided the ideal sanctuary for rest.  The culinary offerings deserve special mention. From refined à la carte dishes to a buffet selection showcasing Swiss and international flavours, the menu is generous and sophisticated. The presentation was elegant, taste impeccable, and the service discreet yet attentive. Connectivity was seamless, with strong WiFi. That said, the initial login process required scanning one’s boarding pass and then entering a code online which was a minor inconvenience that could perhaps be streamlined. In sum, the SWISS First Lounge at Gates E is a serene enclave of refined comfort and thoughtful design.

Big lounge in the main terminal. Quite busy in early afternoon but still adequate seating. Hot food limited to cous-cous with veg and rice, which was disappointing but fairly good salad bar. Plenty and varied drink offering including draughty beer.

The lounge is very small and there were a lot of guests during our stay. There was a very good breakfast and the service was very courteous. There were no toilet facilities in the lounge. These were located outside and were shared with the other business lounges.

This lounge was incredible. The food was delicious (and had ordered options with cooking in front of you), including a nice slow-cooked chicken dish and many delicious puddings. There were unlimited drinks, tasty buffet food and a nice, comfortable seating area.  It was also clean. The wifi also worked well and was free. I have Lufthansa Frequent Traveller status and therefore had free access, but the price of purchase was CHF 49.00 which I would was was expensive for what it was, even if it was lovely especially because Zurich airport is quite nice.
The size of the lounge is too small, it is too crowded and seating possibilities are too often not given. Food is ok but missing air condition. ZRH AP needs to improve this lounge.

Nice design and a lot of space. 2 bedrooms with view to the runway, several shower rooms etc. and a lot of option to avoid other passengers. The lounge is located on the to floor of Terminal E with outdoor view, and has a huge terrace with view to the alps and the runway. Dining options and wine on offer are like in a gourmet restaurant. This time I just asked for a cheese plate and was not disappointed: beautifully arranged with a nice variety of Swiss hard and french soft cheese. The staff is friendly and knowledgable about food and wine. A truly First Class experience.

Return visit to this appalling "Business" lounge. Dirty, filthy carpets, chairs with armrests actually blackened with dirt, dirty seats. How on earth have you allowed your business lounge to be in such a disgraceful way. Dreadful choice of food. We left without eating a single thing. I am sure there is a serious hygiene issue here. Shame on you Swiss.

Redesigned and seems a bit smaller, but nice inside. Always a bit crowded but always 3 hot meals selection, plus cold dishes and good drink selections. Unless you want the quiet section (old longest bar area), nicer seats downstairs. Apart from the food offerings, go to the Alpine Lounge, but this lounge is a good if busy, product

Very poor lounge and more so as its a Swiss business lounge. A dreadful selection of foods and and equally poor selection of beverages. It is quite a soulless lounge with no atmosphere at all.  What did not add to the ambiance was the toddler who insisted, to the joy of her parents, to scream continually while we were there. This is not acceptable to the others in the lounge. Politely asking the father if he could perhaps take the child outside or ask her to stop was met with a very aggressive stance by him. I did not engage this man who looked a bit worse for wear.

Very nice lounge, much quieter than the normal Business Class Lounge. Great views of runway and a chef to cook you hot dishes. Good selection of drinks and very friendly staff. Only for Lufthansa Group Business Class & Senator etc., so more exclusive feel.

It is a beautiful lounge. There is ample food for breakfast however drinks are rather basic. The service was friendly on reception as in the lounge. Soft drinks are from dispensers. Still no newspapers or mags. Computers were not working decently . Very clean restrooms.

This is a lounge were you simply pay. It is a very dated place with old furniture. There were many drinks to chose from. However you still were not allowed to take the food yourself and I had the impression the people who were serving were instructed to give as less as possible. I had to insist to receive 2 slices of cheese. Service was far from friendly, not on the reception desks nor in the lounge. Cleanliness of the restrooms could be better.

First time in this lounge and very nice with friendly staff. Very good selection drinks and happened to straddle breakfast and lunch. They cook the food in front of you and a buffet selection too. Great views of the runways

Although Vienna currently is under the highest alarm level with COVID-19 and has a mandatory mask requirement, I confronted by the entire lounge staff - two cleaners, one food server and the door attendant - wearing masks under their chin and not over their nose and mouth as required by law. Their refusal to protect the lounge customers made it necessary to leave within five minutes, it is not worth risking my life to accommodate them. Avoid this lounge literally like the plague.

We flew SWISS but as Star Gold members, we could use the Lufthansa Senator Lounge at Berlin Tegel Airport. It is outside of the departures area (the airport basically has no departures area) so its easy to get in and out of. The lounge is decently sized, with plenty of comfortable seating available whether you're eating or just want to rest. There's plenty of drink options and not much food options available, however, the meatballs that they had were simply delicious and are a must try. The lounge provides decent wifi and power outlets to charge your devices.

I was a bit skeptical before visiting this lounge. Purposely, I had booked a 4 hour layover since I wanted to use the lounge, courtesy of my Star Gold status. I was extremely happy throughout my stay in the lounge! The first thing that makes me aware I'm in for a treat, a smiling and soft-toned receptionist. It's such a little detail but it really set the tone for such an amazing lounge visit. I entered the lounge at half past nine when breakfast was still being served, and was able to ask for a fresh-cooked omelette, done right in front of my eyes! The food area didn't feel huge because everything was laid out in a way that it didn't look super crowded. Later in the day there were a couple of dishes being served. Unfortunately you're sort of stuck on one dish, whereas normally I like to take a little bit of everything. A small minus there but just personal preference, I guess. You were spoilt for choice for drinks and snacks, both sweet and savoury. I loved the small chocolates, and I took home a handful of various sweets, since they were placed very temptingly. There was also a whisky bar which has 208 different whiskies, and the barman appropriately recommended various whiskies for me to try. The outdoor terrace was open, and I was able to enjoy watching planes take off and some aircraft and vehicle movements which is very nice. There are also some binoculars available to make spotting a bit more convenient. The overall design of the lounge as an open space with lots of wood and windows makes it feel super welcome and Swiss ... a design which Swissair seem to be give you the impression of. There were napping chairs available, the washrooms were kept clean, although I would prefer if there were more washrooms, as they are a bit far from some corners of the lounge. In any case, this lounge is a complete and total winner for me. I can see myself re-routing itineraries around Europe to fly past Zürich just to use this amazing lounge. I can easily say that this is the best hub lounge I have visited, and that it is the best Star Alliance lounge ever.

The business lounge was very crowded - however there was still enough space available. A lot of Swiss and international newspapers were available. There was cold food and a chef was preparing egg dishes made to order. Ample choice of drinks - alcoholic or non alcoholic also several open wines despite it was still early in the morning. Also there were a lot of sweet items, cakes cookies candies and of course chocolates. Very good wifi connection. Maintenance was good, bathrooms were clean however the direction to restrooms is not very clearly given.

The Swiss business lounge at Zurich A gates is a large lounge which seems crowded. The lounge is a let down: food quality is subpar, offering only soups, 1 type of plain warm meal and salads. The choice of drinks is large. The place is messy due to the large amount of travelers. Not really recommended.

I’d heard so much about this lounge on the Swiss website and couldn’t believe that Swiss touts this as their best. This lounge is filthy. The floors are splashed with dried drinks and the ventilation grates are full of debris. The furniture needs a good clean and someone needs to pick up the dirty dishes etc. No meatless options at the food buffet, like being in the dark ages. No to this lounge.

I love this lounge. It's big, many places to seat, very good buffet with cooking in front of you. Good free internet access for all passengers of the airport, and the best of the lounge is a terrace on the roof of the airport, in front of the runway.

The lounge is extremely small, nothing besides the seats, a small buffet with a couple types of drinks. A few places to seat. I dislike this lounge, and it's better to walk thru the Duty Free or if you have Priority Pass or Star Alliance or OneWorld card, it will be better to visit Lufthansa / Austrian Lounge, S7 lounge or the airport Lounge.

I do really like this Senator Lounge at the E Gates. It is by far one of the best senator lounges of Lufthansa group. An open cuisine for breakfast and very good choice on beverage and food. Don't miss this one if your are in Zurich and if you have access.

Very nice modern lounge, very airy. Several areas, dining area, relax area, seating area and also a whisky bar. All in a very modern design, very stylish. The food choice is good and the quality as well. Staff is friendly. This lounge is very clean and tidy. I can highly recommend this lounge, for me one the best lounges at the moment!

New lounge, nice modern design. Different areas, dining sector, seating sector and resting sector. The big issue here is that the lounge is often very crowded and you can't find an empty seat which is not nice. Food choice is a bit limited, the quality is also not convincing. Service staff is mixed, some are OK, but some are rude. Also here some room for improvement! Overall not great experience - I very much prefer their lounge in Terminal E.

The Senator Lounge is a bit old and dated. There is no daylight in the lounge. The staff are often not so friendly, in particular the staff at the welcome desk. There is a good food choice and the food quality is quite ok. There is also a choice of alcoholic beverages but the quality does not impress. Overall not an impressive lounge though ok for a short stay. Hopefully they will one day renovate this lounge.

Modern large lounge, very nice design, large lounge area, dining area and some private meeting rooms. They also have a nice terrace where you have great views on the tarmac. And then there are some nice shower facilities as well as two day rooms which are very luxurious like a hotel room. Staff is very friendly and attentive. Food is very good. Wine choice is nothing special. For me definitely one of the best first class lounges.

Nice modern lounge, nice design with high ceilings. The lounge is very large with many seating areas. They have a large food selection and also a bar where they mix drinks including caipirinha. There are also some showers. The lounge is used by all airlines of star alliance so it can get crowded. The first class section is very small and has no additional Features. Conclusion: good business lounge, average first lounge.

Compared to the SkyTeam Lounge in TXL or the defunct Airberlin one, this lounge is a class ahead. I am talking here how spacious it is, the amount of newspapers and magazines they have and the food and beverage selection. I visited it in the morning and the breakfast buffet, although limited had a lot of quality products, fresh bread and so on. When it comes to beverages, all lounges are OK, this one was even better. A very nice place to wait for your flight, too bad is before security and makes you leave earlier than you should.

Can SWISS please ask staff to say at least bonjour on the first contact. It s been 17 years we live in Geneva and we are also Swiss, they never changed their attitude to people. I've never seen a smiling face.

The Swiss first class lounge at Zurich Airport is very good. There’s an a la carte restaurant, showers, light buffet and Lindt chocolates. After a long flight, the ideal place to relax. Highly recommended. They do not announce your next flight, so be aware.

This is a very good lounge. They have food which we can order from an in-house chef and the lounge staff in general were very friendly; they offer service and food. The food were delicious and variety is amazing. What I am disappointed about is that I have not heard back on the feedback I gave their front desk staff. The lady in the front desk was rude. She looked unhappy to be there in the first place and seem to unleash her frustration at the lounge guests. I gave her my boarding pass and pointed me to the business lounge. I showed her that I had a gold Star Alliance member and she said ‘whatever I don’t care go to whichever’. I came back to her for the shower key and she didn’t even bother to show where the showers are nor to even open the door to the shower areas. She the let down on the whole service and exclusivity of the lounge. I hope steps are taken to improve the overall impression of the lounge. Two stars for service due to the lady’s attitude.

I was flying from Cairo to Warsaw through Zurich. I missed my connection flight and I was rebooked to next flight, so I had spend 5 hours in Zurich. Lounge in Schengen area was closed due to maintenance, so I was able to go to the lounge close to gates D in non-schengen area. Senator lounge isn't very spacious, but it's located in very quiet part of airport and not much people are there. Seats are very soft and comfortable, power outlets are located very close to sofas and really easy to use. Wi-Fi connection was very fast and works without any interruptions. Due to very early morning choice of food was not very big. Hot meals appear after 10 am and they was very tasty. Choice of beverages suits my needs. Lounge was clean and staff was very nice. Toilets are outside, located in public area.

I have been traveling on a weekly basis and I have been using the lounge in terminal A over the last three years. The lounge has very limited space. Accordingly to the time you want to use the lounge you have 10 minutes waiting time to get into the lounge and after that you have no seating possibilities. The food is realatively poor. You have pre made sandwiches. No warm food. No healthy, gluten or dairy free. On top of this the lounge has been closed to be refurbished and if you want to use the lounge you have to a different terminal and go through passport control twice. Of course the lounge in terminal D is smaller to accommodate all the people and you get the same circle over and over.  Running between terminals and not having a seat where to seat or a newspaper to read or wait 10 minutes to get into the lounge make the all experience uncomfortable and unnecessary.

The Lounge has a lot of space, and different areas, including a huge open terrace: all of them with view to the runways, other Terminals, etc. (Including Swiss Alps!). In addition the lounge is beautifully designed with best Swiss Materials. The reception gives one already a very warm welcome, one feels from the beginning like checking-in a exclusive Five Star Hotel. Due to my limited time I took just a small entre and some wine in the restaurant, again all in best 5 Star Gourmet Quality. Unfortunately - due to limited time - I could not use one of the double rooms for longer lay-overs, but I was shown one of the rooms. The double room could be in a five Star Hotel, the only difference is that they offer view to the runways. Lastly the lounge does not look very busy, no wonder, only Swiss First travellers have access. Without doubt my best Experience ever in a First Class Lounge.

Dubai being one of the biggest airports in the world, I assumed Swiss or Lufthansa would have a First Class lounge.  While they have a business class and senator class lounge (terminal 1, concourse D) the latter was totally full and no seating available. The fact that I was flying First was not acknowledged at the desk and the staff was clearly not interested. This must be the worst LH/LX lounge I have been to. So after 2 minutes I left that "lounge" and went to the nearby Marhaba Lounge (I have a Priority Pass card) which was great: quiet, decent food.

I enjoyed my stay at the new Star Gold Lounge in Zurich. After 13h stranded on their Boeing 777 it was a good relief to relax and sip a coffee. The ambiance is calm, it has 2 floors hence more rooms. Wonderful drink selection and for the food bar it was the basics items, nothing compared to the Lufthansa Senator lounge in Frankfort. Overall nice experience.

I used the Swiss arrivals lounge. It is located after you exit form the gates on your left hand. You ring a bell and the door is then opened. The lounge is a level above and reached by an elevator or stairs. Staff took my boarding pass as apparently entry is strictly controlled only to Swiss or Lufthansa passengers and not star alliance. The staff asked me if I wanted to have a shower and told me to wait while they prepared one for me. In that time I went around the lounge. There was a good assortment of the usual breakfast items - both cold and hot with strong coffee options as well. I used the shower room which interestingly had different names of cities. I was told to go to the Tokyo room for example. The shower room was of good size with strong shower. However there was not a single item of toiletries like combs, shaver, tooth brushes etc which was disappointing. Probably I could have asked for it but this isn't how it should be. I left the lounge totally refreshed and ready to hit the road.

Star Alliance Gold member. Departing from Zurich to Milan. The Swiss lounge was clean and relatively new. There were quite a lot of people on both floors, and we had to wait to find a seat. The seats were comfortable. There was free wifi which worked well for me. They staff didn't interact, but came to clean up the tables which was good. The food and bar collection was kind of disappointing though. Not sure if there were showers (only there for a short time.) Would recommend.

Swiss use an awful Alitalia lounge here at Rome FCO Airport with the seats caving in, old an some lounge seats were torn. The food snacks were just as bad with the only thing edible was the fruit sticks. Shocking for a business class lounge. A bad image for Alitalia, I have travelled all over the world an this is one of the worst lounges I have seen.

The Senator/Star Alliance Gold lounge in Zurich is very spacious and is expanded over two floors. Although the lounge gets quite crowded at certain times a day it is still a pleasant place to relax and unwind. It is also very suitable for working due to power outlets at each armchair and a fast wifi connection. Furthermore, there are three special working stations avialable with desktop computers, printers and fax machines. The lounge offers a buffet with various delicious snacks and disasappointing few hot meals. When it comes to beverages, the selection is hillarious: From champagne to orange juice. Especially the good coffee machines are worth to be mentioned! The lounge interior is very well designed and makes an elegant and ageless impression. A special highlight is the smokers bar and the provided cocktails there. In general this lounge is a comfortable spot to escape the masses between flights.

This lounge, as well as all Berlin Tegel lounges, are not airside, but it was a good lounge to relax before taking off. I flew Swiss but they usd the Lufthansa lounge here. There was ample breakfast items and drinks and snacks in the morning, and overall I am satisfied given that his is a lounge in an older airport.

I had a long transfer between flights in Zurich and had the time and pleasure trying the Swiss Business class lounges at both the A gate and E Gate. The A lounge was good, multileveled, faultless, but it was the E Gate lounge that wins my vote as one of the best anywhere! It is very spacious for the capacity of passengers at E Gate, very comfortable, with wide range of food and drink, an almost flat-down lounging area, a smoker room, and even an outside terrace to relax before flight. It is really one of the best as far as Business Class lounge is concerned.

Unfortunately, the SWISS Senator Lounge in Zurich Airport does not offer any lockers. We wanted to leave our carry on luggage there, while we were strolling around the airpot. However, the lounge itself was quite OK. There are two floors. The downstairs are features some snacks and a coffee machine, plus some seating area with some bar-tables. The upper floor features hot and cold drinks plus some snack. Due to the fact, that we visited the lounge in the afternoon, there was neither lunch, nor dinner but only some cake, simple sandwiches and soup which was served. The lounge itself is rather small and the atmosphere was pretty much like a waiting hall. Nothing compared to other Senator or Star Alliance Gold lounges. Food quality was OK, but nothing special either.

The Swiss Lounge at Terminal 4, New York JFK is, in a word, mediocre. Those customers used to US domestic lounges may be impressed, but international travelers will be disappointed. The space is convenient and attractive, and the picture windows overlooking the tarmac and runways are excellent. Although the lounge was crowded at noon, there were still comfortable chairs available. The principal shortcoming of the Swiss Lounge is in the area of food and beverages. The food offerings are limited to fruit and pastries - no hot choices, at least up until I left at 1:40. The beverage options were even more meager; there were no spirits at all. There was beer and wine hidden away in the cooler. On a positive note, there were bottles of champagne if you knew where to find them. This lounge is an acceptable refuge from the crowded terminal, but as international Star Alliance lounges go, this one is inferior.

Senator Lounge in ZRH Dock A. Sadly you can only say one word for this lounge and that is bad. The area is to small, in rush-hours its impossible to get a free seat even on sundays- thats not acceptable. Food limited - very small offer, no hot items during the day (Except a small soup). Quality not very fresh. Unfriendly staff, not very clean. Avoid to much time in this lounge! Not acceptable for an airline like Swiss.

I nominate the new Senator Lounge in Zurich Terminal E as the best business class lounge. I know all the very fine lounges in Asia and until now SWISS has not measured up at its home airport. The new lounge that just opened a month ago is spacious, light and airy with lovely views of the runways, comfortable seating on leather chairs, excellent wifi and even a deck where when can step outside when the weather invites. SWISS has also stepped up the food game. Eggs cooked to order in the morning hours wins me over. Bravo!

Overall this Swiss lounge at Geneva Airport is bright, clean and roomy. The front desk staff has always been pleasant but are separate from the catering staff and therefore can have no impact on problems to do with the catering side. The catering staff are continually checking the supplies and clearing away which is great. There is a good selection to drink but the food available is very poor. I myself are coeliac and practically everthing available is bread, pizza or sausage rolls. I travel alot and visit many lounges were the food choice is far superior - even when only offering salad. Sounds from the comments I have read this is a very common complaint that hopefully can easily be addressed.

Star Alliance designated lounge. Lounge is light and looks on towards the parked aircraft. Seems rather outdated decor. Food offering was basic as well as refreshments. Wide selection of newspapers, even for country of destination though it was a day old. Wifi was good. Not sure if there are shower facilities.

The Swiss Lounge D at Zurich Airport has a selection of food that is beyond poor for an international airport lounge. Drinks are fine. Lounge is too warm. When I complained to the lounge reception, I was told: "this is what there is, there are better facilities in the first class lounge, but you cannot use it". Not worth the money - far from the gates and duty free.

Star Alliance airlines use the Aspire Lounge at Manchester Airport, and we were travelling with Swiss Intl Air Lines. I have to say this lounge is not great and this our second visit mirrored our first visit a year ago. It was dirty, with used glassware and crockery everywhere and the lounge was not busy. There was a poor selection of food and beverages and the staff were not great. As we tried to check in the lady on reception was being pestered by a member of the kitchen staff to talk to his friend - as part of his phone conversation with that friend - while he stood behind the desk using the receptionists desk phone. It was not good practice. We actually left after 15 minutes and went to one of the public bars downstairs, it was a better experience.

I visit this Senator Lounge at Zurich nearly twice a month. Very busy and in the rush hours (especially between 4 and 6 pm). It is impossible to find a seat when you are enter the lounge. So you must wait. Lounge is not the cleanest but its ok. Food is bad, only hot food in the afternoon and evening, unacceptable for such an international airport like ZRH. As well the offer is nearly the same as on the reopening from the lounge. Quality is ok but nothing special. No typical Swiss food, only pasta and rice. Cant understand why LX offers such bad lounges. Staff rude and only speak english (no german!) sometimes. Showers are ok but as well nothing special. Selection of drinks is ok. Wifi fast but only works for 60 Minutes then you must get a new code by the staff. Selection of newspapers good but downgraded every month - why Swiss? All in all a bad lounge, not recommended.

The La Vallette Club seems to be the only airline lounge at Malta airport and it covers all types of traffic. From paid memberships, through business class pax for various airlines and also I believe for Star Alliance Gold and I guess One World Gold pax too. Though there was some confusion over guest access for a member which is plus one for *G everywhere, at least that I'm aware of. They were happy to let the card holder in but had to consult the rule book for a companion. This took a while but all was OK in the end. Perhaps it was because Swiss was new to this airport, but then they have had other Star Alliance carriers for a time now. The lounge itself is a decent size but it's on the basis side when it comes to food and beverages. The white wine was especially poor. But lots of nice leather lounges to sit on, free and fast Wi-Fi, active TV news monitors, windows albeit to the landside of the terminal and a business centre with desktop computers and a printer. The lounge has dedicated bathrooms and a shower. The lounge guys were very pleasant and it was an easy place to wait it for a few hours during our flight delay.

First impression: Two very unfriendly ladies at the reception. They refused to let me in as I had no invitation. I told them they I had checked in online but still: No. They sent me a transfer counter where they would issue me an invitation. But they said: No you can access lounge without invitation. So back to the lounge and finally without excuse they let me in. The lounge itself is dark no windows artificial lights dirty. The food supply is - how shall I call it - rather limited und looks disgusting. I only took a coke as it was in a sealed bottle. WLAN was okay. Very loud music was played. Restrooms outside the lounge. I left the that place rather quickly and spent the waiting time in the terminal. It must be one of the worst lounges I ever visited. Don't bother going there - shame on Swiss to offer such a hole to its passengers.

Apparently Swiss shares the Lufthansa lounge at Boston MA Logan International Airport. At least this was the case on May 21st 2015. I arrived at 5pm to wait four hours for a connecting flight to Europe. There appeared to be a decent assortment of alcoholic beverages a starchy soup hours d'oeuves of "finger foods some cut up cheeses. I was glad I was not too hungry! Furniture consisted of small tables and chairs and nonreclining plastic-covered "armchairs." It was the least comfortable Business Class lounge I've ever visited. There's nowhere in this small two-room place to put your head back and relax.
Long queues to enter lack of seating, food selection terrible, angry personnel - unfortunately it's been like this for several years and reflects Swiss Airlines approach to customer service.
Always much too crowded impossible to find seats. Selection of foods poor; low quality and hardly any choice. Selection of drinks okay but minimalist. Staff unfriendly. View is nice.
Visited this lounge on Jan 4th at midday - the only food available were several dried up croissants as apparently being Christmas they had a problem with supplies! Unacceptable.

Food offer not good - how about a simple healthy build-your-own salad. It wouldn't cost more than the food offered. Or offer food brought from one of the restaurants downstairs. In order to get decent food I now need to stop working and get to the airport restaurants outside the lounge area and then check in again. Apart from that this is a good calm and clean lounge.

Very unfriendly staff they hardly greet you and do not want to help you even if you have a medical problem. When asked they told me to go to the Swiss counter they would not help as it is not their job - being a Gold Star Alliance member for many years I must say this is unacceptable. I would expect some more support. The food is bad no choice and the few things they have are without any taste. The lounge is always too crowded so it is hard to find a seat and there is a lot of used glasses and dishes around the staff is not fast enough to clean and maintain the lounge in a good way.

I used the lounge as an Avianca customer. I entered the lounge at 7 AM. The food was passable but flimsy. There was a coffee machine which worked with various types of coffee old and freezing pieces of fruit cereals. There were old croissants and peanut butter. No butter. The internet was free but I was on line checking my banking when twice my e mail was interrupted and the Swiss logo appeared. One of the woman at the desk said that there have been problems and I asked her why an out of order sign was not put on the machine. No answer except that people have had trouble recently with the machines. The lounge is long but not so bad nothing to do no tv no reading material and no staff. On the way out the same woman said that I was the first to complain about the machine which contradicted her previous statement. It was an unpleasant experience and I left. I will not return to that lounge when I return to the States from Buenos Aires. It is unprofessional; perhaps that is for the morning travelers and the Swiss evening travelers are treated differently but it was just a waiting room with broken internet a large area with lounge chairs and no staff and a chilly room at that no warmth at all. I am by no means a business traveler but have used the lounge before and it was the same. It is called the Swiss lounge but doesn't cut the mustard. No staff? Just two people sitting at the front desk? Maybe it was the hour but again I quote the European gentleman who was appalled. JFK is not a luxury airport although they have made improvements for passengers. They do not allow baggage to be wrapped in the building where the lounge is they do in other terminals. It is risky but no one will tell me why it is permisable in other terminals (the lounge is in terminal 4) and no airline can wrap a bag in plastic. Since this is supposed to be about the lounge I have seen one or two glorious lounges and this pales in comparison.

We were flying on Lufthansa from Geneva to Frankfurt with an onward connection on Lufthansa in international business class to Dallas/Ft. Worth and were able to use the Swiss business class lounge. We arrived at the door to the lounge at 5:20am only to find it was closed. However the hours of operation were posted and the lounge opened at 5:30am. Once inside we found a clean and spacious facility that was virtually empty of passengers as it was a Saturday. Given the hour we passed on the rather well stocked bar featuring a number of different alcoholic beverages (beer wine and hard liquor but no champagne) and opted for coffee orange juice and croissant instead. The food offerings were a bit limited; however we knew we were on a breakfast flight in business class to Frankfurt so no problem. There was also a good selection of newspapers and magazines. However there was no washroom located inside the lounge. All in all this was a very nice lounge.

Very disappointing lounge experience: old and outdated lounge old design with dark colours (very seventies style) not very comfortable seats. Food choice and quality far below average. Also wine selection and quality offered very bad. Service not very attentive. Very surprising as usually Singapore and other major Asian cities offers good quality but this lounge in Changi Terminal 2 is clearly a disappointment!

Absolutely underwhelming. 2 hot foods which are mediocre and a few salads during meal times plus 2 sandwiches which are the best of the offerings which says it all. Drinks selection is acceptable but nothing more. Very crowded you won't get seats in the rush hours. Toilets are too small too showers are ok but not really nice (Arrival Lounge is very good in comparison). Internet needs a code which you can get by text service or at the reception.

For Swiss minimalism read scowling staff one choice of pasta soup straight out of a packet and that's it. Swiss lounges are probably the most basic I have visited with virtually no selection of food or drinks and staff who seen incapable of smiling.

Very basic lounge no bubbles ready packed sandwiches limited alcoholic beverages. Old and tired decor. Needs a total revamp and not a pleasant experience. Staff could not be bothered. WiFi access intermittent.

I've been to this lounge twice in 2 months. Although large spacious and well lit it falls short of everything else. After flying in from Newark I requested to have a shower and was told abruptly that I have to wait. When I mentioned to the lady at the desk that the staff did not refill the shower & body lotion she gave no response. The food offered in this lounge can hardly be described as edible. The main course for lunch today is macaroni and potatoes! Pale yellow and totally unappetizing. Very little else is on offer. And they don't do " smiles" either. A little later when I enquire with the same lady if they had a day room she almost rolled her eyes! Swiss has failed badly in their effort to provide a Business Class lounge that could warrant any star rating.

This lounge was refurbished about 4 years ago when it became Senator lounge. The staff is far from being helpful and you do not feel welcome at all. The selection of food and drink has been the same from the re-opening. I will never understand that no food available from 10am - 1230 pm and from 1500-1730 h. Only hard dry sweets peanuts and that's it. The selection of newspapers downgraded each month. Waiters are very noisy joking ans shouting in the kitchen. Hot meal also the same for ages; rice with curry rigatoni with spinach pasta with corn. I always think of how they advertise themselves: "Swiss hospitality". Where are all those chocolates cheese and other delicious food from Switzerland?

Swiss should be ashamed of their flagship lounge. First of all the location is a bit weird specially for those traveling international. The lounge is accessed after security but before immigration so you need to leave well in advance if your gate is in the E area. Staff are not welcoming and the bar staff are surly and rude and find it cumbersome to make a drink for you. Food is limited with 1 rice and some cold unappetizing sandwiches. Sadly enough of none of the cheese or chocolates which this beautiful country is famous for are seen in the lounge.

Small lounge with limited food and drinks and by far the unfriendliest attendants from any lounges I've experienced. This lounge has only got one shower be prepared for really long wait for a shower. Luckily I do have few hours between the flights. When I asked about wi fi the answer was 'it is all written here'. Why work in service industry if you can't be bothered to provide service!

Swiss provides lounge service for all Star Alliance carriers at JFK T4. Its probably the skimpiest lounge I have ever encountered anywhere. Catering in the morning is limited to some berries and some stale bagels. The cappuccino button on the coffee machine is disabled (saving milk?). There are no newspapers. The only thing there is are armchairs at least 10 years old and uncomfortable. I mostly use the lounge before the Avianca flight to Bogota in the morning and I thought that Avianca is the poor cousin in the Star Alliance and its passengers get correspondingly offhanded treatment. Not so. A couple of months ago I took Swiss First to Zurich and used the F section of the lounge. Indistinguishable except for a simmering pot of unidentifiable meat and half a bottle of champagne. Isn't Swiss service supposed to be something special?

In transit and we first stopped in at Swiss Lounge D. Nice comfortable facility but only one shower available. As we had a long layover the agent recommended we head over to the Arrivals Lounge just past customs. Clean classy and functional. The showers were a great size with clothes pressing relaxation zone and good breakfast variety. You feel more than refreshed leaving here. The one annoying thing is that the internet is limited to 60 minutes free.

Out of 8 lounge visits in a two week trip this was one of the smartest ones we experienced. there are two showers that were more than spacious and well kept for use. The food choices were a hot buffet with 5 items (Thai Chicken curry stroganoff stir fry etc) and a full fridge of sandwiches sushi and fruit and yogurt as well as soup and self serve liquor coffee and drinks. Each zone allowed you to be private and work and the TVs were at a low volume so as not to disturb. The internet was a little slow and depending on where you sat would lose connectivity. Definitely worth seeking out and less crowded than the Bidvest and SAA Baobab Lounges that we also stopped in at.

I am an occasional visitor of the Geneva SWISS Senator lounge and my Friday evening visit (25th January 2013) was my worst experience here. The lounge was very crowded and food trays were empty - the only food available was pretzels peanuts and candy. I waited for the lounge staff to replenish the food trays but they only brought out cake. Not this lounge's finest hour.

This Star Alliance Lounge in LAX could be the worst First Class International Lounge in the US. First - it is ugly no life and for the next year no natural light due to airport construction. The seats are large but arranged in a train format - 2 by 2 and then 8 rows back. If you want to see the TV - almost impossible beyond row 3. Today - the seats were filthy - dry food on the first three seats that I sat on. The food is meagre and uninteresting. Some sushi - but overly cold and poor quality. Sandwiches are clearly made only once a day in the morning. Desserts not bad. The worst part is the staff - unpleasant and unresponsive at best. When I asked for the TV channels to be changed the front desk staff said that it would take 20 minutes - because that they needed a supervisor to do it. When I then asked one of the food clearing staff she changed the channels immediately. The staff at the desk tals so loudly that twice I had to ask them to quiet down so I could conduct a phone call on my mobile.

High expectations on Senator Lounge on my first visit as Gold pax. Unfortunately in Zurich the Senator (Gold) Lounge has less space available then Business Class lounge at least at some hours. Walking around till someone leaves. Worse than 2nd class waiting rooms at train stations. In the meantime I learned to change to Business Class lounge (just more seats and more possibilities to find a quiet corner). Food about the same (extra sandwiches) and drinks also not too spectacular. Staff (waiters) the same as in Business lounge not very interested in the customer very loud speaking among each other and handling plates/glasses. A disappointment if you're hoping for a higher level of service.

I had high expectations on this lounge and I can say my experience was not the best. I arrived around 7pm during a busy evening at Zurich Airport. Beautiful reception area and an elegant restaurant sided by a long bar which was almost full of passengers having dinner. Another room with large leather sofas sided by a buffet and bar. Windows with great views of aircraft. I opted for the buffet. Great choices of appetizers cheeses and breads all of high quality. Also great range of wines and spirits. Soon the lounge became crowded - used plates and glasses quickly filled the cocktail tables and buffet space. When I went to choose one of the hot entrees all of them had finished with no replacements. It is a well appointed lounge but service should be improved.

The new Swiss arrivals lounge at Zurich is really excellent - particularly after a long-haul flight from Hong Kong. Located near the exit from Arrivals hall 2 (near customs) it has well-staffed showers (20!) that are very spacious and well-supplied and they also offer a 10 minute ironing service. The lounge area itself was large and at 6am-8am - the time I was there - the breakfast selection was excellent and regularly replenished. An ideal place to refresh while you wait for businesses or shops in Zurich to open!

One of the several options open to Swiss passengers this one is located towards the north end of the main terminal on the upper level. Its clean and comfortable and peaceful. Good selection of drinks and during the morning a variety of breakfast food is available. Alas on the day I came back the only hot food provided was curry soup or Indian style rice (neither an option for me on my diet). Papers and magazines appear to be limited to german language editions although the FT was available in the afternoon.

The new lounge in the recently opened Terminal B/D (non-Schengen) for flights to London etc. looks modern nice and has nice views of the tarmac but that is where the praise ends. Staff is typically LX being cold and not overly friendly. Food selection is a disgrace. One hot dish soup and bread with some fruits. Not really what one would expect from such a good airline. Drinks selection is ok and you get 2 hours of free WiFi with a voucher. Toilets are outside and the lounge is hidden in the far end of the corner. Staff in the kitchen is quite loud at times which means it is not that relaxing. There is also only one screen to check the status of your flight and it is not conveniently located. Swiss can do better than this.

This is probably the best SWISS lounge (also doubles as Star Alliance Lounge). Amazing views of the runways from this circular lounge with surprisingly tasty hot food good selection of drinks and above all a very calm and relaxing atmosphere - even to the extent of having laid back chairs/beds to watch the planes take off and land. Free high speed WIFI. Worth choosing Basel to fly from if convenient compared to Geneva or Zurich just for the excellent lounge. SWISS do some things well (not all by a long stretch) - and this is definitely one of them!

A brand new but typically Swiss lounge: cold staff no atmosphere very poor selection of food (rice apples and bread rolls) and a limited selection of drinks. Internet access is not free and costs a staggering 25 francs (20+ euros)! Very poor when compared to every other major airline.

Staffed by moody unsmiling staff who fail to recognize that customer service is part of their job. The food choice is particularly poor - the usual cheese pasta (a staple in all Swiss lounges) and dried out sandwiches. Overcrowded and chaotic - on a par with Lufthansa.

I regularly use this lounge when transferring at Zurich. There is a good choice of seating. There are plenty of newspapers also foreign ones. Although a non-smoker the smokers' bar ie. the upstairs area with the serviced bar is my favourite spot. Best view nice light conditions very friendly bar staff and good choice of drinks. The choice of beverages in the self-service areas is very good. I love the Rivella a Swiss lemonade which is milk-acid based and very rejuvenating. The problems of this lounge are the lack of good food especially hot food items if any at all are very poor standard. Another problem are the loud service staff which sometimes make it hard to relax and refresh in this lounge.

Very disappointing. The lady at reception was unsmiling and made you feel like you were keeping her from more important work. The lounge itself is adequate but it was entirely unacceptable that no hot food was available an hour before closing only old stale sandwiches. It's strange that the toilets are outside. The view was nice but the Swiss business lounge in terminal A is far better overall.

Flew with TG and they use the Panorama lounge or Swiss lounge in Zurich. As we first wanted to use the Swiss lounge they told us that we can only use one lounge and if we used the Swiss lounge we could no longer use the Panorama lounge. I found this policy to be confusing and insulting if you have a business class ticket. So we decided to go to the Panorama lounge as it was closer to the gate but took around 25 minutes to get there first. Once in the lounge the food selection was ok and the drink selection was fine too. The views are magnificent and the lounge was not crowded even though TG SQ BA LX AC etc. all use this lounge. In comparison to other lounges worldwide it is average/below par. Internet is not free.

An awful experience. Staff not friendly. There were a miserable small plastic dishes on top of the bar with three pieces of sandwiches. The food selection doesn't exist. The drink selection is poor. Very old structure. Not recommended.
Staff were friendly and efficient there were three computers with internet. Seating comfortable and spacious food selection good in comparison to other lounges. The drinks selection was very good.

Tacky uncomfortable Lounge. Toy-town furniture. No privacy even from the corridors outside as some walls are only glass. Food judging by my numerous visits over the past few years is usually a bowl of tasteless puff pastry discs which often runs out before 5pm. Drinks reasonable. In short the lounge is almost completely neglected and permanently dirty. No information nor flights called as staff are too busy communicating with their friends. Toilets outside lounge. Wi-Fi sometimes sporadic and temperamental but always very slow. The airport should provide better both in quality of lounge and staff. Not under SWISS direct control of course but I feel they should insist on a better product than this.

Reasonable Lounge but not up to the standard of the Senator Lounge in ZRH. Pleasant and helpful desk staff. Service staff do not seem to want to replenish the stocks in a timely manner. Drinks but especially food run out quite often. Cleanliness does not seem to be top of the list either. White wine & Prosecco never kept cold. A dozen ice cubes will not do much for two or three bottles and cannot be expected to last for 2 hours! PC's now work since being replaced. Wi-Fi is available if a slightly complicated phone-back system is followed and the provider actually phones back. Lounge ambience is not too bad although not really relaxing as the lounge is usually quite full. Access is via an escalator up but only stairs back down to departure gates. Toilets are outside and quite a way from the lounge too far considering the Senator Lounge is supposed to be a "prestige" product.

Ugly lounge with poor seating comfort poor internet services no good snacks or dishes. Even worse the personnel is very noisy (shouting laughing making lots of noise with empty glasses and bottles). Completely impossible to relax in that environment. Will definitely avoid ZRH for transfer in the future.

Aesthetically pleasing bright lounge. Quiet good availability of computers amazing coffee machine good drinks selection. Main complaints is lack of food beyond peanuts and fruit and absence of bathrooms (you need to go outside).

Food choice limited to one hot dish. Only one internet computer worked although there seemed about 5 or 6 available. Lounge clean staff unfriendly wash rooms needed cleaning as no clean towels for showers. Overall not up to First Class expectations.

Very clean and well decorated. Welcome personnel is nice but limited to one. Internet stations work well and fast. Coffee machine is up to the state of the art. Alcohol drink choice is small. Snacks cheeses breakfast breads and croissants are plenty and healthy choices too. Fresh fruits also available. Only no hot choice is offer.

Pathetic. Choice of a only a handful of drinks. Internet was not free credit card system in place. No food. Staff spent most of their time on loud bphone calls. Seats/tables not particularly clean. Toilets reasonable. SWISS should provide better.

Staff excellent. Clean toilet / shower facilities. Nice view from upper floor. Free Internet. Reasonable food selection and good drink selection. One minute from security checks to gates. Much quieter than Zurich. Bar seating café-style seating leather armchair and relaxer seating upstairs.

A very poor lounge on all fronts; a tiny lounge with no windows and hideously cold air conditioning. Although not full (that really would have been disastrous) it felt cramped and unwelcoming. A meagre selection of food available some nice Kenyan finger food and the usual beverage selection. Counters near the food were unclean and food looked unappetizing (although to my surprise it was good). Internet was slow and only 1 terminal available. It was a welcome break from the very old terminal building which was very overcrowded but far below par for a Star Alliance/SWISS lounge and very disappointing.

Swiss use the Millenium lounge - quite a pleasant experience. Staff was friendly and efficient there were two or three computers with internet but no wifi. Seating quite comfortable and generous. The food selection was very good in comparison to other lounges : fresh healthy things like crudites goat cheese savoury and sweet pastry sandwiches. The drinks selection was equally impressive. Despite most areas were naturally lit the disadvantage was perhaps the lack of any view towards the outside.

The lounge is nice but what is strange is that the offerings between the adjacent business class lounge and the supposedly higher Senator lounge is not that different. The bar selection is identical. Senator offered a few more snacks and a pasta with spinach dish. Business had a curry dish. Both were very good. The Senator lounge has two levels and there is no elevator to the second floor. So you need to ask one of the attendants to open the door if you want to use the elevator which is in the Business lounge. The seating is modern and good.

Very nice lounge great views across the runways and good selection of drinks (including different champagnes) and hot food with a restaurant section. Pleasant showers to freshen up and a leather seated limo service to take you to the E Terminal for the long haul flights. Staff the usual Swiss efficient but seemed friendly and were very helpful.

In the old days of Swiss Air there were no lounge facilities at Rome Fiumincino. Today the use a lounge on pier E opposite gate 31 which is run by Alitalia staff. To enter you need to use the lift and go down a floor. This means the lounge has no windows. On entering there were 3 receptionists. None of them were interested in serving me they were too busy on their mobiles. I stood like an idiot for 3 minutes for one of them to say hello. The lounge is not a nice haven. It has old large photo's on the back wall of Rome. It has a bar area toilets and that is just about it. There were no newspapers or magazines. The bar was stocked with basic drinks and beer on tap. The food was terrible curled up sandwiches where you had to search out the filling. The bar attendant was always in the back talking to someone else. I stood for 10 minutes waiting for him to come back to the bar. You could hear him but not see him. The WiFi cost 10 euros per hour which I did not use. There was simply no saving graces to this lounge. This has to be the worst lounge I have EVER used but given the fact that it is run by Alitalia is it any surprise it is so bad. Swiss needs to think about using this lounge it really is bad.

It is actually the old First Class lounge remodelled and in atmosphere it beats the old lounge. Quite comfortable leather chairs good lighting and new stone walls in beige make nice surroundings. Food and drink selection as in the previous business class lounge. Already quite a lot of people (on Friday evening and Tuesday morning) but all in all a nice place to spend some time.

Newly opened lounge. Plenty of sitting area good choice of food drinks and snacks. Separate area for dining serving mostly pre-flight dining for night flights. Very much the spirit of the LH First/HON lounge concept. Very nice showers. The whole experience is 'Zen'. You really feel relaxed when you leave the lounge.

Zurich Swiss First lounge is a separate area within the Swiss Business lounge with a separate reception and service desk. The reception will identify eligibility for car transfer to US bound longhaul gate at the midfield terminal and arrange it with the visiting passenger-a very nice service indeed. Comfortable leather seating. Extensive self service bar extensive soft drinks. Hot drinks machine. Moderate assortment of hot food buffet including soup. Good selection of cold snacks. Swiss style hard cookies. One compact shower for First with access to the several similar Business Class section showers. Access to the Long Bar it is part of the Business Class section and connected to First by stair and a door or exit First section to Business and take the elevator- it faces the tarmac and is a nice feature. One or two computers for use not sure of WiFi. Quiet and relaxing atmosphere Swiss staff efficiency.

I booked this La Valette Club Lounge as I was unsure what facilities were available at Malta airport. The email contact I had when booking was very efficient & courteous. The lounge is very comfortable overlooking the runway. The snacks & drinks available were plentiful & a high quality, staff were attentive but not in your face. This airport lounge was one of the best that I have been in.

This lounge provides some comfort and tranquility away from Istanbul's busy and crowded departure lounge. Wifi and computers aviailable. Soft drinks, beverages and snacks available. The fruit flies around some of the available snacks did limit my choice of food. The soft drinks dispenser was not working although a nearby fridge did provide soft drinks and alcohol. This lounge is just average, nothing really special, but as stated earlier a welcome break away from the crowded departure lounge.

Nice lounge, comfortable sofas and chairs overlooking the airfield, lots of windows providing natural light. Relaxing quiet area, bar area serves hot and cold food, beverages and soft drinks, also showers available. A nice lounge, staff pleasant although spoken English is limited. All in all quite a comfortable stay whilst waiting for my flight.

There are two lounges next to each other, used by all airlines. Located above Immigration, the main view is of the gates and runway. Access is by invite (Business Class and/or top tier FFP member). Operated by the same company, the food and beverages are limited in choice and are the same in both lounges. Staff serve you alcoholic drinks/juices and various types of coffee/tea. and  the hot items from the food station. Soft drinks and cold food are self service. There is a smoking room. At the peak time of the day 08.30-11.30, the lounge can get very full and in this case you may be invited to use the lounge next door. Some staff have limited English and on this visit were relatively friendly. The toilets were clean. There is free internet/wi-fi as well as 2 computer stations for guests to use. There is also a limited choice of reading material in Ukrainian, Russian, French, Dutch and English. There is room for improvement and hopefully the lounge management will make this a priority.
Nicely designed, decent wine, food selection not great (but good Pao de quiejo) Not too crowded, there is varied types of seating.

They renovated their catering offer which is now much better than before. The lounge can get very crowded, even forming queues outside it but this time it was rather bellow average occupancy. Staff is now different too and much more courteous. Well done.

Horrible experience and way below average of what you expect of an airlines main or flagship lounge! The space is too small for the amount of people using it, food and beverage options are terrible, hot food on my visit was something looking like chicken breast but tasting like fish! Rice was full of sauce rests as people would just use any spoon to dig in. Not even at my school canteen I got such terrible food! Finally, space is so limited that passenger bags block passage. Toilets were also in a deplorable state. I would not recommend this lounge to any non-business class travellers paying their visit. Tap advertised this lounge recently as refurbished and better than before. My last visit to this lounge in 2019 was definitely better than today!

Greeted by a warm and enthusiastic employee, in a terrible gloomy day, I was very surprised by the quality of TAP's lounge, an airline which I nurture some hard feelings. Food quality was great, service by barmen was polite and professional and it was clean, cozy even though not too big with good views to the tarmac. I would love to visit it again.
The lounge does not exist at JFK. You are paying for business or having Senator card but TAP has you deep. They did not pay other longest for their business / senator passengers.

The Lisbon lounge is a disaster from the point of view of cleanliness, the sofas have years of stains to make a fine show of it. The food I found quite good, a lot of variety. good quality wines too, at least the reds, the same ones that are then offered in flight by TAP. Newspapers available for all tastes, good Wifi.  La lounge di Lisbona è un disastro dal punto di vista della pulizia, i divani hanno anni di macchie a far bella mostra di se.... detto questo, il cibo l'ho trovato abbastanza buono, molta varietà. di buona qualità anche i vini, per altro, almeno i rossi, gli stessi che vengono poi offerti in volo dalla TAP. Giornali a disposizione per tutti i gusti, buono il Wifi.

Spacious and quiet with views over the runways. Reasonable range of alcoholic, beer and soft drinks and kept clean. Food is very limited to bread rolls, pastel da nata and crisps - nothing hot. Disappointing for the cost of €25.

Some of the previous reviews in this section pertain to a different lounge, called ANA Lounge, which serves some Star Alliance airlines. The TAP lounge is next door to the ANA lounge. I've been to the TAP Lounge several times as a Star Alliance Gold member. Food is very good by European airline standards, including cooked food. Snacks, pastries, and salads are available, as well as several coffee machines, soft drinks, beer and 8 different wines. A wide range of multi-lingual newspapers and magazines is available to take away. Front desk staff have always been very helpful and really nice. But I have experienced a few problems with the staff in charge of replenishing food and drinks. Just today there was no spring water available in the water area. I asked a staff member if they were going to restock it.The reply (in Portuguese, in which I'm fluent in) was "Why don't you go to the bar on the other side of the room?" The staff attitude is probably the only negative note about this lounge.

I used the LOT lounge in Warsaw when flying with TAP Portugal, and it has some great seating, is conveniently located and easily accessible and there is plenty of food. However, there are some areas of improvement I would suggest: - more newspapers/magazines in foreign languages (only one newspaper in English!) - more room, given the number of people that use the lounge wider areas, given the luggage and people going around - as there is a security gate right next to the lounge, quietness is not ensure for half of the lounge

Food options at the lounge are very scarce, the food is mostly represented by dry sandwiches with tiny pieces of meat or veggies. There were no hot food options, no liquid food or even yogurt. Overall the lounge is not very clean, particularly the restroom.

I have only been to 3 airport lounges, but this ANA lounge one was my favorite. Extensive drink and food selections (including hard liquor), clean bathrooms, big showers, lots of comfortable seating, wifi, charging stations for your tech. View of the runways. Stylish decor. Highly recommended. Part of the Priority Pass lounge roster.

We arrived there and the person who was attended us, was very rude and there was no smile on her face. It seems she was doing a favor to us. Catering in the lounge was limited water, coffee; bread and butter. Terrible lounge. At the end, we went to the near coffee shop, and we had a great juice and sandwich.

Lisbon TAP Lounge is dirty, no one cleans the carpet, I don’t know if they don’t see it, or if they see it and don’t have moneys to buy detergent - what is there problem to be honest.  The carpet is full of wine, food, whatever that falls there and later they can clean it, or give up on trying. The service is like the wind - some days east other days north.  Consistent in one thing, those Pasteis de nata (the typical Portuguese cookie) they serve hot, are never there at 5.00 in the morning,  maybe we can have them at 5.45 something like that, the staff  will serve a coffee for themself etc but the service for passengers will be ready around 6am, sometimes 6.15, when many flights are boarding. IF opens at 5.00am is it that difficult to have the lounge ready to receive the passengers in a proper way? For the toilet I recommend go to the ANA lounge if you can, is clean and with proper facilities (next door).

Lounge Casablanca Terminal 1 (not the one from Airmorroc) Multiple Lounge Airlines, Is better than a few years ago, new chairs etc etc . No Wi-Fi (Airport WI-FI was down on that area?). Poor food, really some drinks and water, I ask for a glass of wine and they serve me. But no real food I end up going out and have a sandwich at the PAUL Café. By the way I use the internet also in that area. So not the best experience to be honest, No Wi-Fi, no proper or decent food. I didn’t use the bathroom, I just get out of there faster I can and next. If you can get the Royal Air Maroc Lounge is better (if you can go in). Trust me

There is a New TAP lounge in Lisbon. The WC for man when you open the door that gives direct view access to urinary functions in that bathroom, people (Ladies) pass on the corridor and 2 feet way and if the door is open, you can imagine. And the toilet was very dirty. The sofas are very colorful and to some extend comfortable, but 10 people sit together and they have only 3 power outlets.  The food is little better than the previous TAP Lounge, still basic junk food, some wines and beers and liquors and some fruit, but no natural juices, no nuts, etc. They have some cakes, but no signs regarding what type of cakes. Light is good and TAP offers Magazines and Journals in the Lounge and a good selection to be honest. But for a brand new lounge is poor.

Good selection of cold food. Warm stuff: rice with duck and Tortellini filled with pumpkin and tomato soup, sweet cakes and fruit. A selection of beverages and a comfortable and clean atmosphere. Plenty of power outlets and USB ports too. The staff is attentive, it is clean. The lounge I like better is the Turkish Airlines lounge at Atatürk Airport.

Visited this shared lounge for the first time. Perhaps it was an off weekend but on arrival tables was covered in empty dishes and glasses with food and trash strewn on the floor. I will not even mention the condition of the bathrooms. Also no soft drink selection and limited food. As a last impression of Barcelona this is not the one he would want a visitor to have.

I never write reviews but this time I could not help myself with a hopeless idea that someone who manages the lounge and its people can take an action to improve the quality. I flew TAP Portugal first time from Boston to Barcelona with a layover in Lisbon. I upgraded to a business class ticket and my experience in my first Boston-Lisbon flight was great.  Unfortunately the lounge in Lisbon was a complete turn off for me and I don't think TAP Portugal and Lisbon airport will be my choice next time. After skimming through the comments before mine, it is clear - the food is mediocre, the seats are dirty, overcrowded, people fighting for coffee cups. But the reason I am leaving the review is because of the customer service - People. A woman who was working in the lounge was openly rude to me, I approached her very politely, asking where I can find milk for the cereal, then it just went downhill. After the look she gave me that was worth a thousand words, she told me "There!" pointing in a direction of the counter with cereals where I just came from, then, she told me rolling her eyes: "it is right here, can't you see?" in the most rude manner. It was stream of hot milk barely coming out of a Nespresso machine. I asked her: "Is this a milk for the cereal? Hot? You don't have cold?" after what I was afraid she is going to scream at me, which she thankfully didn't but the nespresso machine spilled milk all around it so she was clearly mad cleaning the mess. I said "Ok thank you" and left the bowl because I am not sure how it is in Portugal but usually people don't eat their cereal with hot milk. As I was walking away she said in a bit higher tone "You are welcome". It is not a customer service of an airport that wants to offer the best (or at least good) quality and experience, she was not "not polite" to me, she was openly rude. And that attitude translates into dirty chairs, not stocked cups, dirty washrooms (disgusting), unhappy reviews and customers choosing another connecting airport. Hire new people, retrain the ones you have but the gap is there and if you want people to come back you have to do something about it. One of the questions is if I would recommend the airline I flew with - yes if you don't have any layover in Lisbon.

This TAP Portugal lounge is just a shame! The chairs were dirty and so was the floor. Unable to find any electricity plug, I left the lounge again to find one in the public area. What an utter disgrace! Being Lufthansa Senator and thus used to the service in Frankfurt, I think the Lisbon people responsible should visit Frankfurt or in fact almost any other decent airport to see what to improve!

The ANA lounge for business class passengers is just shameful! The food is disgusting sandwiches, the service is horrible: they aren´t polite in any way. The cleaning ladies are always among the passengers, talking loud with themselves and cleaning. There is not enough space for all the pax flying, for example, at 07:00, on a week day. I suggest TAP to visit a business class lounge of better airlines to see what business class lounge is, and how staff treat passengers.

This is the poorest excuse for a Business Lounge. The lounge was dingy and dark and overcrowded. There were no seats available and the refreshments were cheap and mediocre at best. The fact that TAP had delayed my first flight which caused me to miss the connection did not help the situation. I was tired and could no place to sit. Don't stop in Lisbon if you can help it. If I could give them less than a score of 1 I would. This is embarrassing for Portugal.

This TAP Portugal home base lounge is one the worst lounges I ever been. Lack of space for passengers to seat; the food is disgusting - this lounge is for passengers in business and first class, and it's a shame. Service is so bad. I know that there are passengers who prefer to pay a meal outside the lounge, instead of going there.

Poor, shabby, crowded. Hard to understand this lounge being used by TAP in their home airport at Lisbon. It is a paid lounge and TAP is but one of many airlines using it. Maybe they have their own lounge under renovation? In any event it removes a substantial reason to upgrade to business class wit TAP.

The lounge was good some years ago. Fantastic food and drinks. This is now closed. The lounge is mostly dark and very uncomfortable seats. The food standard has rally gone down. What has happened? How about going back to the old standard. We really miss the old lounge.

ANA airport lounge used for TAP Portugal flights at Lisbon airport was a bit crowded, but large enough. Desk staff courteous, large choice of magazines/newspapers. Different seating provided: table seats, armchairs, larger armchairs with footrest, dark cabins with sort of 'beds' for longer rest. Restrooms found clean, drinks offered so-so with an average tawny port wine (no 10 years port, no ruby port) and a cold white port in the fridge. Food limited: croissants, small sandwiches plus some sweet mini pastel de nata which were very good. Reasonable choice of coffee (nespresso capsules) and tea. Nice view of the planes and take off track.

Despite the fact that I was flying Business Class on TAP Portugal, and my boarding pass mentioned I was a Star Alliance Gold, an unsmiling staff at the entrance of the lounge in Geneva demanded to see my Star Alliance Gold. It took time but I found it, during which time he chatted with his colleague.  Lounge was average.

This lounge is too small. It is always full and difficult to find seating. They have a good selection of magazines if you speak Portuguese. Having just spent an hour in the lounge the coffee spilt on the steps was not cleaned.
