There were no hors d'oeuvres Pepsi and Pepsi light taps were only pouring water there were no small bottles of water and practically every single table was dirty with dirty dishes - yet there were four people in the lounge kitchen. Apparently all too busy having a morning conversation rather than doing their job and making the lounge presentable.

This lounge for Star Alliance airlines dates from prehistory as well as its furniture and decoration. I don't understand what is Lufthansa and other serious Star Alliance companies doing here. The food is poor the drinks are okay. The showers are old but working fine and clean. Overall quite a depressing lounge.

The TAP lounge is very difficult to find as there are no signs to navigate passengers to the Lounge. I arrived from non-Schengen flight and was transported by bus to the gate and as my flight was to non- Schengen country I passed the security check and entered the terminal where I tried to find the Business Lounge. After some minutes of walking and finding nothing I asked the staff at one of the gates to guide me to the Business Lounge. I had to go back to the Schengen terminal pass the passport control and security check. In the Schengen terminal no signs navigating to the Business Lounge. When I finally managed to find it it was about the time to go back to non-Schengen terminal again through the passport control. The only advantage was that I spent 40 minutes walking which was healthy exercise between 2 flights. I had a little chance to use the Business Lounge but the first impression was a strange light and very small space but a good selection of refreshment but no time to enjoy.

Very nice airport and efficient public transportation. Staff is helpful and friendly. However the lounge is terrible. It is difficult to find but has nice views over the boarding areas. Food is just peanuts and a tiny dry "montaditos" which are gone in a second. When asked for more the staff did not bother. Coffee is another joke a coffee machine which pours "black water" has nothing to do with nice portuguese coffee.

I like this quirky lounge. The staff is young and polite and willing to help. They sometimes take care of my carry-on which I can leave for some hours while in town. I can understand some people do not like the atmosphere. Pasteis de Nata and other salt pasteos are to die for. All the food is pretty much the same bit is replenished regularly. Wifi and PC work fine. My concern is that it is very cold. You need a blanket in the summer as they keep it below 18 degrees.

Being a Gold lounge for the Star Alliance standards it is very poor. Low light level give you the feeling of being in a night club. Food choice and quality very limited and poor. Staff service as for TAP airline very rude and not polite. Total lack of professionalism.
TAP uses the ANA lounge at Porto Airport. Lounge with good selection of snacks and drinks. There is no bathroom. Workstations and no wi-fi including chargers for smartphones.

The lounge has a reasonable quantity and quality of drinks sandwiches and various snacks. Comfortable chairs with wi-fi and desktop workstations. TAP employees especially rude in dealing with passengers. The lounge has only three toilets insufficient for the large number of passengers in the lounge.

Nice ambience spacious comfortable lounge reasonable selection of drinks and sandwiches though nothing hot. Delicious Portuguese baked custard pastries! Couple of free internet terminals and range of newspapers in different languages. Desk attendant helpful. One of the better lounges and the food selection puts other Star Alliance European airlines to shame!

The Club looks spacious but served very very simple Continental breakfast at a small corner. If you don't eat bagels or instant oatmeal there will be nothing for you to eat. No snacks for the breakfast. I was looking for helps. A waitress sat by the bar without uniform looked at me as if she was one of the customers. I didn't know that she was a working staff until she started to take trashes away from tables. Apparently she was not professionally trained. The receptionist did offer great helps proactively to arrange disability assistance.

Had a short one hour layover in Charlotte and decided to try out the Admirals Club. Luckily as a BA Silver member I have free access to US domestic lounges regardless of my itinerary. Lounge was a reasonable size with plenty of chairs. The selection of beverages and food however was pretty pathetic. Just yoghurt bagels and coffee - nothing else. I certainly wouldn't bother paying for the privilege to use it but it served its purpose for my short layover since I had time to grab a coffee and a couple of bagels.

If you ever consider to pay for club membership this should keep you from doing it. Old and worn out seats some as shabby as their airliners' seats. Unfriendly staff that tries to avoid work at all cost: my flight was delayed and I asked them to let me know when boarding would begin. Answer: We can't do that you have to go to the gate to find out. Food: in the mornings bagels muffins yogurt like a typical middle class hotel buffet. Decent bar with a lackluster bartender (see above about avoiding work). Pretty small place so it can get crowded. WiFi is the free wifi available all over the airport. And remember even if you fly first class as I do you have to be a club member or pay $ 29/50 for a day pass unless you fly intercontinental. This money is much better spent in one of the airport restaurants.

The US Airways lounge at Phoenix Airport unfortunately is no different from much of the companies other lounges. Old and worn out. The food selection is unhealthy and poor. The interior is worn old and cramped. Worst of all the staff seem to be as worn out and unattending as the decor and the food. They walk around looking very busy no smiles more like robots. Maybe the staff is told by the company to show no positive emotions so clients don't ask any questions. The only comment I got was how busy the previous day had been. It's pretentious and so not up to date.

The leather seats were very uncomfortable. Red wine was tasted by most and either left or they went back and paid for an upgrade. Food not so great. Bartender could not open the wine bottle. I had to do it for her. While that is not a big deal for me I did rank the staff low only because she had not been trained at all.

This club is comfortable and flexible as you have the choice of sitting in the quiet area or the louder tv area. I like the two story window looking at the planes/weather etc. House wines and beer are no charge. Food options are limited. The soup is good but NEVER changes. The staff are courteous and as mentioned do a good job cleaning the whole complex. The Internet works well. It provides clean rest rooms and a place to get some work done.

Although this lounge wasn't crowded for my early morning departure as Club members with USAir United and Air Canada international Business Class and international Star Gold economy passengers can access this lounge it does get crowds at times. This lounge is very comfortable as you have the choice of sitting in darker areas or in the light of the panoramic two story window looking at the Tarmac. There is also a large and separate quiet room for relaxing. Drink options are great as there are self serve options as well as a separate bar room. That being said food options aren't the best as there are just apples and chips most of the day. I do give this category 3 stars however as I have heard that in the evenings when the long haul departures are they offer more food that could be a full meal. The staff are very kind and courteous and do a good job cleaning the whole complex. The Internet works very well also. Overall I definitely would not purchase a $50 day pass to experience this lounge or even buy it for $29 when I booked my flight but if I fit into the criteria I described above it is better than waiting at the gate.

Large lounge. Often crowded in the main area but the quiet room was nearly empty. Very limited selection of snacks but we did get vouchers for a free premium drink at the bar (generic drinks were free). Unlike some United Clubs and Delta Sky Clubs no showers at US Airways clubs. Would have been nice after an overnight flight. Decent Wi-Fi.

Small club with no windows but it was clean and relaxing. Decent but small selection of snacks. We were flying first class to connect to an international business class flight out of Charlotte and while the US Airways agent at the check-in desk said we probably wouldn't be allowed in the club there was no problem (because of the same-day connection to international business class).

There is no longer a dedicated lounge for Envoy Class - it is just the regular Club with one free drink ticket for which I got an undrinkable bloody mary. Only chips and salsa and some cookies as the food offering. Anything more substantial has to be paid for. Hardly Business Class standard especially when compared with the excellent BA lounge in this airport.
Terrible. No room to sit. People allowed to use up sofa space with bags and no challenge from staff. Wifi too slow to be usable.

The club is very pleasant and what makes it worthwhile is a large quiet room with a sign stating no cell phones or loud conversations. It was actually quiet. A man was talking loudly on his phone and a staff member very professionally but very firmly asked him to go to the main lounge area as he was disturbing people in the quiet room. This room is a welcome relief from cell phones loud conversations etc. that can be jarring especially after a long international flight.

Travelling First Class Boston to Philadelphia on entering lounge advised that US Airways did not have a first class lounge in Boston and that this lounge was a pay lounge was advised that the lounge did not serve alcohol. The lounge had tea coffee and water if you required a soft drink you had to find someone to get it for you snack selection very limited and poor. In short do not pay to use this lounge.

Friendly staff at reception desk. Pleasant relaxing atmosphere though unable to see out of windows because of louvres. Very poor selection of magazines - not even their own inflight magazine. Simple snacks but plenty of snacks and beverages.

Pleasantly furnished though selection of free snacks is small. On an evening arrival we were given two vouchers for free "premium" drinks from the bar. When I went back for a second drink ready to pay for a bottled beer I found that draft beer was free (okay it was just Bud and Bud Light). Our US Airways flight's departure time was moved back from 1015pm to 11pm but before it was 10 pm there were announcements that the club was closing right at 10. One staff member went around shutting off the TVs when that time approached. We waited the rest of the time by the departure gate. WiFi access decent. Wish they had PCs to use.

A rather sad facility. Run down seating staff variably friendly or totally disinterested and more concerned with their personal affairs. Drinks and snacks a minimal offering. Frankly I often just sit in the terminal instead. Wouldn't waste my money for this.

We arrived on international Envoy (Business) Class so had access to the lounge. It was roomy and nearly-empty quiet room was nice. Small selection of snacks coffee juice etc. No showers. Wi-Fi available but if you don't have a computer with you the only PCs available must be rented with a credit card. I didn't buy drinks at the bar.

Small but comfortable a small selection of domestic beers and wines free (others for sale). Sandwiches from a restaurant downstairs were okay albeit a bit expensive. Selection of free snacks fairly good.

Envoy lounge at PHL above departure gates is excellent. Good selection of food (salads meats cheeses) adequate selection of drink. Staffed bar on 1 side self serve on the other. Only downside was the bartender he definitely needed coaching on how to work with people. Not a people person at all.

The membership is not particularly cheap and it offers less all the time. Selection of free coffees has been cut back and on this occasion the $12 salad was inedible (old) so was exchanged for a barely edible sandwich. Their food for purchase used to be good but no longer the case. Alcoholic drinks overpriced considering you already paid for the membership and staff friendly and helpful only when they feel like it. Restrooms often dirty.

Large lounge and convenient. Chips and snack mix left out that is pretty much it. Bar area has drinks for sale good selection of flavored coffees available for free. Lounge is impressive when entering then you notice that almost all seating is tattered and in need of repair. Staff is nice- though other lounge on Concourse B is more intimate with great staff. Noticed that lounge also has wrapped cheese crackers and other items. Someone continuously circled cleaning the space as well.

This was the worst and most low-budget lounge that I've ever been to as a business class passenger! Upon arrival at the front desk you are asked if you would like to use the cocktail-bar. The lounge is huge. Plenty of seats and these are quite comfortable (the only good point about this lounge). you get free coffee tea tab water with loads of ice from a pitcher and free apples as well as some this unidentifiable mixture of small crackers pretzels etc. Yuk! Soft drinks or juices: Forget it! That's what you need your cocktail-bar voucher for. You have the choice of 1 (yes: one) free alcoholic drink soft drink or juice. If you want more grab your wallet and pay big time: A beer will cost you 8 bucks! A very limited choice of magazines (no newspapers!). If you have time in Charlotte International don't go to the US Airways Club and rather have a seat in one of the rocking chairs or have a snack in the excellent food court. It is better and cheaper!

US Airways actually has 3 lounges at PHX as this is a hub. There are 2 on the second floor (Low-A gates and Low-B gates) and one on the concourse level (High-A gates). The High-A lounge is the newest but also the nicest - with a modern hi-end decor. Unfortunately at times it gets very crowded and you may have trouble finding a seat. All 3 lounges offer the same amenities - coffee tea soft drinks free of charge alcoholic beverages are for purchase only. There is a time appropriate range of snacks - pastries and fruit in the morning; cheese crackers chips and cookies at and after lunch hour. The "fresh baked" cookies are usually quite good. In the Low-A and Low-B lounges there are separate TV lounges. All 3 also have business centers and conference rooms available. All also have good views of the tarmac/gate areas. There is free wireless internet available via a monthly changing password. Staff here is generally senior and quite helpful. They can be great help in securing first class upgrades at the last minute - and will always offer to call gate agents to check on individual flight status.

They only serve pretzels and some sort of vegetarian nut mix. Otherwise you can have a coffee or hot chocolate from the vending machine. Drinks costs five dollars and no free internet not even any desk top computer stations.

Outstanding lounge in Bangkok. Professional service as I booked the fast track departure which included assistance through immigration and access to this lounge. Nice selection of hot and bike foods as well as drinks. Free alcohol. Very clean space to relax with Wi-Fi. Staff were amazing and attentive. Assisted on round trip arrival also. I was out of the airport in 15 minutes.

The Platinum lounge at OR Tambo Johannesburg is great. The staff are very attentive and smiling. The lounge is generally quiet and not very crowded. The food on the buffet is fine, a decent array of choices. There is also food that you can order off the menu which is usually much nicer. A seperate room for watching news/sports or even kids channels is located off the central area and provides a nice getaway that doesnt seem to disturb the rest of the guests. A computer room is available with small meeting rooms for the business travellers.

This is one of my favorite Star Alliance lounges. The food is very good with excellent variety, coffee made to order, the showers are great (and I've never had to wait, unlike many other SA lounges). Staff are helpful and friendly. It can get crowded at some points in the day, and the wifi has always been spotty, but other than that it's a very comfortable lounge!

Very pleasantly surprised by this SAA Premium lounge (is used this as a passenger of Ethiopian Airlines), good food selection (loved the lunch buffet), nice wines and other beverages, very friendly bar staff. Seats a bit worn but nice views and like I said, very pleasant stay!

When I arrived OR Tambo Intl Airport, I headed to Baobab lounge to take a shower and take some snack for breakfast. It wasn't so crowded. Wifi worked well. Cleanliness of the lunge was overall good, shower facility was well maintained, the beverage choices were very good. The taste of food was also good. I truly enjoyed the hospitality of staff and well-maintained facility. I recommend you to make full use of it.

South African Airways use the Qantas lounge at Perth. Quite busy late evening, with numerous international departures. Comfortable seating and good wifi. Reasonable drink selection but poor selection of food which was not being replenished. Adequate but nothing special.

South African Airways international arrivals lounge at Johannesburg. After luggage and passing through customs at the JNB airport is the arrivals lounge. It's cosy space and only a handful of users. Various private rooms offering shower facilities. The bathrooms are well appointed. On offer is more snacks than hot food. Refreshments are abundant. It's a perfect place to freshen up, grab a snack and move on to your next place.

We were flying Lufthansa when we used this SAA Baobab Business Class lounge. battled to find seating and when we did went in search of something to drink and a snack. The bar staff were really not interested and it took a long time to get served, (no sparkling water at all) and when we asked for a packet of crisps because they were not on display like they are at every other airline lounge we have been into - the staff dispensed one packet per person and no negotiating for extras! Everything besides the coffee machine appears to be under lock and key. What caliber of people are they allowing into this lounge if they have to dish everything out like children in a playschool? We have traveled to a lot of places and been into a lot of business class lounges and I have never encountered one as bad as this.

Lounge is large and comfortable with a nice view of airport. Wifi is working well. Food choice is good and ranges from salads to hot soup chicken as warm pasta and more. Drinks are served at the bar by the glass for booze and wine. Soft drinks and beers are served in cans. Not much reading material but a decent lounge to relax before a long flight.
No hot water in showers. Waiter who was laying out food dropped cutlery on floor and then without cleaning it put it on table for guests to use.
Pleasant welcome. Had the lounge all to myself - early Sunday morning. Good selection of snacks and drinks. Spacious - comfortable and varied seating with views of the airport runway.

Large lounge overlooking the tarmac. Lots of different zones to sit in but it got really crowded with Start Alliance and SAA flights using this facility. The mini wraps and sandwiches are acceptable but you have to ask for bottled water and chips and the attendant had a bit of an attitude. The internet was very good and the shower facilities good.

Refreshing clean well staffed and friendly. Didn't mind spending time here waiting for my flight. Staff were very friendly and polite and made us feel very welcome on arrival and departure. What you would expect from a business class lounge.
The layout itself is not very appealing and the food selection is quite basic. I don't take pre flight drinks but the choice I noticed was very limited and the access poor.

A large comfortable lounge with good amenities (including smoking room TV room children's room and showers). A nice selection of packaged sandwiches and wraps and a bar with a good range of alcoholic beverages as well as a proper espresso machine. Staff were friendly and pleasant.

Checked in at 10am en route to JNB and Hong Kong. On arrival at the lounge counter staff were chatting among themselves - not really interested; no verbal communication from them - even after our "hi" - just a pointed arm in the correct direction after we accidentally turned toward the first class lounge. The lounge itself is light and spacious. Enough choices of food and some fresh fruit. Surprisingly no decaf coffee - not an uncommon demand these days. Upon leaving we again had no acknowledgement - the ladies did not even glance at us as they chatted. A simple smile with a "hello and welcome" and an "enjoy your flight" as we left would have sufficed. It left us wondering if the rest of our flight was going to be like this - thankfully it wasn't. Johannesburg Business lounge (on our return) could give them a few tips.

Great new lounge SAA has in place now from the World Cup. Large and comfortable. Free wifi smoking room good views on tarmac food good expresso machine run by staff instead of just self serve. Overall great new installation in the airlines home airport.

Very large lounge with plenty of sofa style dining recliner seating. Seperate kids area smoking zone TV zone work stations etc. The bar is manned and decent selection of drinks. Food selection is average for J class lounge. No hot food just sandwiches fruit and salads. Excellent showers and bathroom facilities. The staff felt too much at home and were loud and obtrusive. Excellent view over the aprons. Free WiFi. Overall great lounge.

SAA have an arrivals lounge just after you clear customs before exiting into the arrivals lounge. It is well marked to the left and upstairs. It is not large but has 4 excellent showers good selection of food (breakfast was cereal toast pastries sandwiches fruit tea/coffee etc.) No alcoholic beverages. Smoking room. Comfortable seating. Again the staff are too loud and obtrusive but provide good service. Free WiFi.
I thought the lounge was excellent. I thought the staff were great and facilities good also. Its no Singapore Airlines but its fine for price paid for ticket.

As we were flying first on Emirates we had access to the South African Airways lounge. First class passengers were directed to the right and business class pax to the left. The lounge is not really big but it has all one needs except wifi. There are 2 computers but the connection is really slow. There is a nice coffee corner with snacks and some alcohol aswell as a smokers lounge. The nicest feature however were the showers: really big clean and with lots of amenities.

Pathetic is the only word I can use to describe this lounge. I asked at the first class lounge why we were not allowed in there (facilities fabulous for first class). After complaining about the lack of warning for business class passengers about the lounge they would still not budge saying that we are unable to use the facilities besides the toilets which were located in the first class lounge (none in the business class lounge and quite far away!). Very disappointing. Like other reviewers it is unacceptable that SAA expect business class passengers to pay the full price but do not provide the full facilities.
Very poor. At approximately 10am it was impossible to find a seat. Selection of food and drink minimal. No wireless and only two computers. No toilets. No telephones.

Business Check in counters independent of the main hall, as well as customs and security checks. Small Duty Free Shop for business passengers. Restaurant style lounge on the 1st floor, full bar service (including Uzbek sparkling wine) and large choice of snacks, warm meal on request. Very good experience.

Shocking lounge. It is extremely hard to find in HCMC airport and staff don't help very much. Poor service-you walk in and have to help yourself. basically staff are not even interested in you or care about your flight, which is always delayed. food is shocking!

Small lounge at KHH was primarily used to serve not only China Airlines', but also Skyteam's frequent flyers. Entrance was easy to navigate as it was right after the immigration. Staff was super friendly. Hot dishes were available, with acceptable quality.

I had no idea why Vietnam Airlines used this lounge as it was a pay-to-use one, meaning everyone could enter. Staff at check-in desk was inefficient slow. The lounge was super busy, crowded, and hard to find a seat. Food was limited in both quality and quantity with cold and tasteless dishes.

The lounge was located right after passing the immigration and KIX duty free area, on the 3rd floor. It looked quite new, modern, bright with many comfortable seats. Toilette was large and clean. WiFi was fast. Food and beverages were the downside, instead of being the star of the lounge. Empty trays were everywhere, and food quality was so-so, not as excellent as expected.

I liked how the lounge had been renovated to be brighter, modern and offered a warm welcome to the guests. Food and beverage selection was really good, with some hot dishes were available. WiFi was free and fast. Staff was nice, helpful and dedicated, even the lounge was so crowded since flight was delayed. One thing to be improved in the future: no toilet in the lounge.

The Miracle Lounge at Concourse F was one of the worst lounge ever! It was located on the 3rd floor without clear direction. The lounge was relatively small, with limited number of seat. Food and beverage was at average quality and quantity. No toilet in the lounge. And staff did not mind to help us find a seat. Bad experience, and have no idea why Vietnam Airlines keeps using this awful lounge!

Lotus Lounge was operated by Vietnam Airlines and dedicated to its VIP, Business Class, and Elite passengers, located on an upper floor of the international departure, close to the security screening. In overall, it was a nice and big lounge. We luckily got a table with a view to the tarmac and runway. WiFi was free and a bit slow though. Food selection and quality were good, particular the Vietnamese noodles at the hot station. However, cleanliness was something an issue here. Someone threw trash in the toilette and it was cleaned. Worse, we took a pair of "new" chopstick at the food bar, and found the leftover on them!

Took a chance to visit Vietnam Airlines Lotus Lounge 2 which was right next to Gate 18 before flying. It was relatively small with beautiful view to the tarmac and the gates where we could see planes taking off, landing, taxiing, parking. Seat was comfortable, and to us, quite elegant. WiFi was fast. Food selection, however, was quite limited with average quality. Staff was quite friendly though.

The lounge was not large but very new, elegant, clean and beautiful. It was located right next to the security (after security screening). Staff was friendly. Food was nice, with hot dish was available.

I went into the Lotus lounge. I was shocked to be honest for business class it was horrible. No arrangements of alcohol wine and poor canned beer that was it. No choice of wine either, just super sweet and it tasted old. The only food that seemed to be good was the fruit options. I tried to have a salad and found a big black hair in it. No salad dressings to be had just a piece of lime. I tried to have the chicken and way over cooked rice.  It is not worth the visit at all unless you drink like a child and love pop and juice and have no appreciation for a well made drink or even the lack of ability of making one because there is nothing to make one with. I asked for vodka and you would think I had three heads! I went downstairs and got a really cold tiger draft beer and some Pho it was delicious and I would rather pay and get something delicious and worth it rather than eat a drink what they serve for business class at the Lotus lounge domestic. Dreadful and not worth the effort of calling it a business class lounge! Very disappointing and dissatisfied. The should be ashamed. The bathrooms didn’t even have soap! I think they have something or someone that isn’t very well versed on what business class is or should be.

Paid to use this lounge when travelling with VietJet Air. Food options are ok. Comfort is ok. Only 2 beer varieties and not cold, no wine or spirits. By world standards not very VIP. Not really worth paying to come here.

Da Nang International (T2) is dominated by SE-Asian tourists and a lot number of small airlines. The Airport is renovated and a pleasure. The Lotus Lounge that Skyteam airlines use, is extremely nice and well maintained; it is a huge, unexpected gem find in a small airport. The Lounge has very good food offerings; cold delicatesses, and at least 7 hot meals in buffet. Drink options are a bit below average and only cheaper, local products (2 cheap wines and 4 beer brands, all alike) are offered. Background music appreciated. The décor is of high standard; even smoking and business rooms exist. The lounge appears underutilised, I found only 5-10 other visitors during the 3 hours I spent there.

This is a great place to have a rest before the flight. I really love the food here. There are plenty of choices for drinks, snacks, fruit and hot food. One of my favourite is chicken "Pho". I have also tried the massage machines there, it is comfortable. The working area is a little bit small, but convenient and private enough.

Lounge quiet on arrival so plenty of seating overlooking the airport. Wine served by the glass and was okay. The food was so disappointing. A beef stew and pork with lime, both meats were chewy. Rice and little sausages were provided. There was a variety of Vietnamese cold choices which did not appeal. Slices of dried bread into what we put cheese that we unwrapped from plastic wrapping. No soup, No cappuccinos. Dirty crocks took a long time to be cleaned away.

Nobody sitting at the desk when we arrived! A staff member appeared after a couple of minutes to check our invitations. We appeared to be the only people there for about 15 mins but the staff manning the beverages just looked at us and continued to sit down. I asked about a shower and was directed to the female toilets where the “bathroom” was locked although I could hear giggling inside. 30 mins later the door was open but both cubicles occupied and a staff member was using the sink to wash her face. I complained to reception and was told that it was passengers using it. Since I and my friend were the only female occupants of the lounge at the time, I found this hard to believe. The receptionist then came to find me to tell me the showers were vacant, but nobody had cleaned them and the floor was still soaking wet and no towels or amenities were there. Apart from comfortable seating this is an appalling business lounge and the staff need training in customer service.

We stopped by here while waiting for our flight to Hanoi. It was very pleasant, friendly staff, comfortable seating, a wide selection of food and beverages. The food is pretty good. Great time. Thanks to the staff for doing such a good job! I think i will visit this lounge again next time

There was not any map of the location of the lounge on the invitation card and no one told me where it is when I check in, so that is difficult to find it which is at the corner of 3rd floor, even though lounge is very closed from security check. This lounge was not crowded at peak time, so that it was easy to get a view seat I could be watching plane on the tarmac when I was having a meal. Food and beverages is enough abundant that hot food can be provided such as popular food, Vietnmanse Beef noodles. What's more,this lounge contains any standard facilities of business lounge like speed wifi, business centre, toilet and shower room.

Currently Vietnam Airlines business class passengers use this lounge run by SASCO instead of the older and cramped Lotus lounge. This lounge is much roomier. It has showers in the toilets, WIFI, food and alcoholic beverages, massage chair and a view onto the tarmic. The food selection was reasonable although I abstained as I had no appetite. The alcoholic drink selection was self service but the selection was limited. Ice wasn't kept topped up during the time we were there. This lounge is okay, but not in the same league as the world's best business class lounges.

Passing through Hanoi en route to Paris CDG from Bangkok. As this is a night flight I chose to go via HAN as there are showers at this lounge whereas there are none at SGN.  It is however the only good thing about this lounge. The rest is rather average. I'm sure VN went out to buy furniture for this lounge based on their colour scheme or fashion or price, they certainly didn't sit in any of them. The seats are the most uncomfortable seats of any lounge I have experienced with the only exception being the very tired and old SATS Premier Lounge at Chiangi airport. Even the day beds were uncomfortable, perhaps the massage chairs would have been OK but they were in a little room next to the smoking room (I think they have moved them out of there now). Standard food service, noodles, fried rice, pho, some very dry and tasteless spring rolls, better to satisfy yourself with fresh fruit there. Standard beverages and some strange local concoctions. WiFi works, not the fastest but OK for emails and some surfing. Power points everywhere so charging is no problem, but be careful if you use US equipment as their voltage (like most of Asia) is 220v. As previously mentioned I wanted to go via HAN for the shower, there are 3 units in the bathroom, all well equipped, soap, shampoo, shower cap, towels, slippers etc, but no toilet, that is separate. Early in the evening it is quiet but as there are several long haul flights leaving late in the evening it gets busy. Same disinterested staff here as on their flights. No flight departure announcements as is often the case in many lounges.

Nice sized Vietnam Airlines lounge on the first floor with views over the main departure lounge and the apron. Good selection of snacks and beer/wine. The lounge was quiet when we were there and plenty of seats. Wifi fast enough for emails. Clear flight status TV screens - but be warned - The flight status never goes to 'boarding' or 'final call' and no announcements are made. We were able to look out directly onto our gate and saw that they were boarding otherwise we might have been late.

Domestic Lounge is old, but quite efficient and provide good views, hot food, snacks, and drinks though no spirits nor wines. Onboard, the A321, the business class seats were providing full comfort. Cold snacks, beers, and sparkling sodas provided. Priority luggage, boarding, shuttle, and check-in lanes provided professionally for business class passengers. Miles for my Flying Blue were inserted the following day.

Visited the new Vietnam Airlines lounge in the new terminal at Hanoi airport. The new terminal is really great, with a modern and airy feel and as of yet, not too many people. The new VN lounge is also a comfortable space with a variety of seating and decent food and beverages. There was a manned bar with a good collection of spirits, however, the barman was far from knowledgeable about his trade. There was also a number of self-serve fridges of soft drinks and local beers. Food contained a number of hot options including fried rice, fried noodles, pasta and various dim sum and Vietnamese spring rolls. Food quality okay but not spectacular. There was also a make your own Pho station which was quite good.  I took a shower and there was about 4 or 5 shower units which were quite good and clean. My only complaint was that towards the end of the night, VN has a number of long haul departures which means the lounge gets very full, so if you get a good seat, hold onto it. Overall, the new lounge is excellent.

In the old Da Nang airport, the Vietnam Airlines business class "lounge" was an area in the main waiting room set off by a series of planters. The business (and first) class lounge in the new airport is outstanding. Its seats are plenty and comfortable. Its selection of Vietnamese and western food and drink was good. Two monitors showed arrivals and departures. The smoking "section" for the airport was in the open, just outside the door to the business class lounge.

We pay for a business class experience with Vietnam Airlines, however we received the worst reception out of all the airlines we fly.  As we walked into the business lounge, the staff there was sleeping. When entering the lounge, there were children running and screaming, using the chairs as their personal play area. While The adults were yelling across the room about their daily life. People throw trash on the floor. This is not a good experience from an airline that promises the world.

This lounge provided a good quality of food as well as beverage. The internet connection is fine. Although there are no shower, there is a the washroom. The staff is friendly. I think Vietnam Airlines should upgrade their lounge with showers in order to improve the guest's experience.

The lounge is pretty good. It's clean the food is OK There is a well stocked bar WIFI shower not over crowded - everything you want really. I've been in there 3 or 4 times and it's been fine - no complaints.

Actually it was so bad today it was more pleasant sitting outside in the general terminal. Apart from the horrible interior design the place was filthy tables not wiped food scattered over the floor stained carpet - it was just too disgusting to sit in. Vietnam Airlines is getting slack and this is an unacceptable example of it here.

This lounge is in the new part of the airport (not the main Business Class lounge in the older part of the terminal). We were the only people in there apart from staff and it would have to be the worst lounge we have ever experienced. The food looked as if it had been there for hours and was all dried up and only luke warm. The staff were only interested in helping themselves to food and drink and as soon as they got back into their office they microwaved all the food they took because it wasn't warm enough. They weren't the least bit interested in us and we couldn't believe the poor attitude they had.

Some food available - noodles curry some snacks in wrappers. Extensive soft drinks 4 types of wine (2 almost completely undrinkable) and many choices of beers. Good wifi comfortable chairs and not overcrowded. No showers available. Overall this is a pretty basic lounge and none of the food or beverages on offer really interested me but it was a pleasant enough place to spend a six hour layover - showers would have been nice.

Slightly shabby and old style chairs no showers for those coming off overnight flights. Food not enticing who eats partly cooked carrots? A curious mix of Asian and western foods meant that for the most part little appealed . The mouse baits visible in front of the plate glass window are not a good look. Staff tried to please but often misunderstood the question. Internet worked well unlike the Hanoi business lounge a month earlier . Charging iPad and iPhones possible at one location. Seemed to be a lot of staff doing nothing behind the bar counter.
Business class lounge was clean reasonable selection of cold and hot. Average selection of spirits and wine. Good wifi no showers but clean toilets and massage chairs with good view of tarmac.

The lounges are well equipped with soft drinks beer snacks hot dishes (but mainly very boring industrial food no tasty real food). Nice seating. I once spotted rats in the domestic lounge in Hanoi and heard from others that they are pretty frequent. Lounge in Hue have water all over the floors when rains are hefty. Internet free and works with fairly high speed. Nice smokers’ rooms. No showers except in the international lounges and of very poor quality.
Nice and quiet lounge with a good view to the apron. Excellent choice of food and beverages. Free Wifi is also available.

Accessed this lounge based on Skyteam Elite Plus frequent flyer membership. Few type of sandwiches available, some yoghurts and soft drinks. Limited variety of alcoholic drinks. Couches not very comfortable, one can seat at table as well. iPhones cannot be charged at the charging station, but only with your charger connected to a power socket.

When entering the lounge the lady at check in counter was sleeping. Average to small size lounge. Seating available but not comfortable. Drinks no problem, plenty available from espresso to soft drinks and local wine. Food nearly none existing some crackers, salt or seasoned chips you can buy in any cheap supermarket . I believe I have seen some sandwiches it they looked really poor. Disappointing lounge, one of the poorest I have visited .

Nice, cozy but if you have a guest travelling with you its 44 euro, not worth it. We ended up not using lounge together as for 44 euro you can have more from local shops than from the lounge. Orices like in JFK but not warm meal option. Bad.

Tarom Lounge in Bucharest is operated by the airport authority and branded for Tarom. Considering it is a small airline it wasn’t too surprising that the lounge wouldn’t be that good. But actually it was less than expected: as it is on a mezzanine in the terminal it was quite loud and warm. There was enough seating but not many power outlets. There were several charging stations for cell phones. Toilets are outside the lounge. The food selection was four kinds of different potato chips, wafers and yoghurt. They had a good selection of soft drinks and alcoholic drinks. Verdict: The lounge is better than nothing and we bought our own food at the food court and brought it into the lounge. Drink selection was good. I wouldn’t go to the airport earlier for that lounge and wouldn’t choose to connect via OTP for that lounge if I had different options in the same price range. Last year I visited the lounge that is used by Lufthansa and to be honest, it was not better.

Tarom Business Lounge (With Lufthansa Invitation) at Bucharest. This lounge is coming better, still a long way to go. Offering Internet of 110K per second that for downloading an email will be 4 to 5 minutes if you have images or videos.  Decent Internet is a must in our days, I know that is Romania but we don’t need to take this to the extreme of offering Internet like we are in deep desert. Food is still junky fast food, but now that have a bigger selection of Yogurts and I saw salads, that is a nice twist, they serve (premade) vegetable salads. Drinks are still cheap alcohol drinks far from a decent Baileys or a decent cognac, but the wine (the Red) is a good one. Like I said,a long road to go until we have here a proper lounge, but they are improving. Toilets are outside in the same floor, but clean!

Low selection of food. Just some chips and nuts. There is also some Romanian yoghurt, but no hot food. No obvious place to charge iPad or iPhone. Chairs are hard, and there is no air conditioning, which makes for a very hot lounge in the summer. The selection of drinks is fine.

Huge lounge, average food and drinks, but extremely friendly staff. Though filled with people and being noisy and definitely not nicely set, quite enough seating options. Not the best I have seen, but ok for a short stay.

The lounge was luckily not very crowded. While the buffet and drinks were very limited, the staff ended up being very friendly and made me some vegetarian wraps as there were no savoury vegetarian snacks on the buffet. The coffee bar was efficient.

Unfortunately the lounge was very crowded, yet the upper floor remained closed. Food options were ok, as there were several vegetarian dishes/snacks available. Biggest draw back was the shower. It was dirty, no shower curtain, shower gel was empty, mirror broken. For a lounge this was a disgrace. Also lines for the customer service in the lounge were very long.

Waste of time opening. This morning I entered the lounge, grabbed a coffee and went to get something to eat. No hot food, I do not understand why, as Qantas have continued to serve hot food. The menu at Virgin, cold pre packaged banana bread or muffins, Cereal, not wrapped but poured into bowls, sitting in the open and yoghurt. Okay I though, I went outside and purchased a croissant, on returning to the lounge I was informed I was not allowed to eat it, I could sit it on the bench, but don’t attempt to consume in the lounge. Why on earth not? They aren’t offering anything, they have reduced the service to nothing (but blame it on Covid) which isn’t true. All I can see is them saving themselves lots of cash! Next trip, I will go Qantas, this whole experience has left a very bad taste in my mouth and has spoilt was was meant to be a great few days away.

Absolutely disgraceful. My wife and I (Gold member) who flies regularly for business entered the business lounge in Brisbane today at 10:30 am 21/12/20 with our 1-year-old daughter. After sitting in there for 30mins my daughter needed to have something to eat. She couldn't eat any of the food that the lounge provided for medical reasons which was muffins, sandwiches, and sweet chilli chips we always carry her own foods with us. My wife started to feed her a baby yogurt and a female staff member approached me saying you cannot consume any food in this lounge that is not provided by the lounge. I said to her my daughter is 1 and cannot eat anything that you have on offer she told me if I wanted to continue to feed her the yogurt I will have to leave the lounge area and give it to her out in the common area in the airport and enter again once she has finished. So she stood over us watching me pack all our belongings back up and my daughter crying because we stopped feeding her and escorted us out of the front door. We have never been so embarrassed and mortified. My Wife won't fly with Virgin ever again and my business will be going to another provider.

Great clean lounge to use. Comfortable and plenty of friendly staff to assist you. Variety of food for different needs such as vegan and vegetarian. Staff were extremely considerate as my cousin cannot eat over a certain amount of protein, they suggested safe options for us.

The Strata Lounge is great Lounge to relax before a flight. The interior is spacious with plenty of seating but lacked the appropriate number of rest rooms. The food and beverages were much better than what some major airlines offer. The food options were freshly made including plenty of options of drinks from alcohol, coffee and soft drinks. Not plenty of team around, I think it was just very early but it would have been a nice touch to see staff around. Overall, it's worth a visit if you fly out of Auckland.

A warm welcome from reception made my first visit very pleasant. The space is not large but it is used very wisely to make sure overcrowding is minimal (in my opinion). The tarmac views was a highlight, offering amazing natural lights bringing the interior to life. The buffet was not up to standard, I honestly think there could have been more options and fresher products though the A La Carte dishes tasted fantastic. Lastly, the team during the service were very attentive. They were very reactive to passenger needs and keeping the dinning tables cleaned. Definitely worth a visit any chance I get.

This lounge is large and has sufficient seating, but the fluorescent lighting is harsh, and the decor is utilitarian rather than comforting. Food and drinks are limited, but staff are friendly and helpful.

A similar surrounding compared to Virgin's lounges in Sydney and Melbourne. It's a lot more open with its high ceiling and welcoming atmosphere. Great layout for those on business to have privacy and for those relaxing before a trip away. The Lounge staff  are friendly, keeping the space tidy. The catering was above average, but I think more hot options need to be on offer. One attribute is the premium exit. Overall, a pleasant experience.

As I had a complimentary pass from my credit card, I thought to give the Virgin Lounge a visit for the first time at Sydney. Being an early departure on Sunday, the space was rather quiet but exclusive at the same time. The layout and decor gives this Lounge an edge over the Qantas Club, from privacy to open space. All staff in the lounge were friendly and professional with food and beverages on offer being above average. I wouldn't hesitate to visit again.

I love the lounge, staff at the reception are friendly and helpful, tables are cleared quickly by polite and friendly staff and the bathroom spotless. However, at 7.45am on the 21st December the 2 baristas in the lounge are the most sour faced, customer service devoid - no eye contact or festive cheer. You need to realize that on a breakfast shift you are the first point of contact, you are the face of Virgin and your customers are possibly requiring a serious caffeine fix - baristas you are letting the team down!

I've been a regular user of this Sydney Domestic Lounge for the last few years and always find it to be consistently really good. The food and beverage choice is very good, cleanliness is excellent, service always excellent across the board and entry / exit seamless, helpful and friendly. The seating is my only negative, as I find the "bucket" chairs uncomfortable and awkward. Better to sit at a bench where chargers can be plugged in and more upright seating enjoyed.

As a business class passenger to Samoa I got free access to the Strata Lounge, which is on the first floor (in the "old" Air New Zealand Lounge space). The shower Suites are still available, but the rest of the lounge is newly furnished with more space. The food selection is very nice with cold and hot dishes. Overall a very nice and different experience compared to the overcrowded new Air New Zealand Lounge. The staff is very helpful and very friendly, what a contrast to the old lounge.

Friday afternoon is when you can see the domestic lounge go into full speed ahead. A large volume of travellers, food being eaten, drinks being made and the change over from afternoon tea to pre- dinner drinks. The lounge staff were excellent keeping everything running very smoothly, clean and refreshed. Good place to catch up on last minute emails and a calming drink before taking off.

Clean and spacious Virgin Australia lounge at Perth. Great quality coffee and cookies, although not a wide variety of breakfast options. No hot food options except pancakes from machine although this is probably acceptable at 11am. Very clean toilets. Nothing to write home about but overall comfortable.

I was greeted at the Virgin Australia Melbourne lounge by a friendly staff who checked me in and provided me the bathroom amenities as requested. The upgrades to the lounge since my previous visit were very apparent and a welcome improvement. Not only was it more spacious than before, the premium exit for passengers leaving to board their flight worked great. Coffee and breakfast (served until 11am) were both on point. I highly recommend.

My first visit to any Virgin Lounge and was impressed. My flight was a morning flight so had a good breakfast in the lounge. Was in the lounge from about 8.30am to 9.30am and it was very busy but as it a large lounge plenty of room for everyone. Barista made coffee which is always a bonus. Meal selection was good. Could see a good selection of drinks but as it was breakfast time not available. Seats and tables were comfortable and wifi easy to connect.

First use of the lounge and I wondered what the fuss was really about. I was greeted unceremoniously and was questioned over the validity of my one time purchase voucher to the lounge. I didn't feel good about standing around for 10 minutes whilst they scrutinized over my membership, boarding pass and voucher while another couple came to the counter with their kids. The father had a membership and asked how much it would cost to bring his wife and kids through. He was told his wife would be free and any children under the age of 12. So he pulled out cash and was going to pay for his 13 year old daughter($65) and the representative said, its ok, just go on through!!! I did not know why they allowed him, first I thought it was how I was dressed. Neat casual, jeans blouse & laced up shoes. The couple and children had flip flops on and shorts/summer dresses and when I finally was allowed in, I looked around and I was a minority! The food was bland, - some salad bits and bobs, make your own toast/toasted sandwiches, you can have alcohol or coffee from the barista (neither of which are great options for long flights) chips and spicy Indian noodle and nut snacks, some gnarly soup and air dried bread. Did not see any dessert or pastries options (probably refrigerated). I found the bathroom area clean and stylish although I didn't use the shower it looked like it was serviced well. There was an attendant there hovering and folding toilet paper for the next person. As for the rest of the lounge, there was wifi service, tv and non cushion seats were not comfortable. There were no quiet comfortable area to do some thinking/resting or even getting some work done. I would not recommend a membership. I thought you could get better service, better food and a quieter spot in other areas of the airport and for less bucks!

The Virgin Australia Lounge in Sydney is really annoying, particularly during weeknights. It is always too full. It is hard to find a seat (even harder now that for some ridiculous reason they let their pilots use the lounge - even though they cover up their uniforms by wearing a cardigan or jumper, it's pretty obvious who they are). They have a second level of the lounge, which is frustratingly never open. I travel though Sydney at least three times a week for work, and spend a lot of my time in that lounge standing up. If they can't provide a lounge that I can easily get a seat in, then I am heading back to the competition.

This lounge remains one of the best lounges I have visited. I last visited 4 years ago and the lounge has become very crowded. WiFi has become easier to connect to. No more getting a WiFi code. Instead one logs into Turkish Airlines WiFi, enters flight number and seat number, and voila you're connected to fast internet. As with my last visit in September 2022, the lounge has an open airy feel. Its food offerings are varied/excellent with various cooking stations throughout the lounge to satisfy one's palette. One definitely gets a taste of Turkish cuisine. The salad bar is extensive with a wide variety. We were not able to get the free massages to the neck and shoulders this time around, but, one can't go wrong with offering this type of service.

International business class passengers with Turkish Airlines have the choice of 2 separate lounges. The Turkish Airlines Business Class Lounge opposite Gate E1 is the primary location. The second option is the Turkish Airlines Miles & Smiles Lounge opposite Gate C1. Both occupy and area of 5,600 m2 and can accommodate 765 guests. To enter, you simply scan your boarding pass at one the turnstiles. Then you can stow your carry-on baggage in an all-glass locker and join the fray. There are street-style cooking stations where chefs serve hot pide breads stuffed with meats and cheeses and fresh pasta dishes or head for colossal salad bar where you’ll find a remarkable selection made from fresh produce. There’s the typical barista station, self-serve selection of local and French reds and whites as well as prosecco in golden bottles. Plus, there soft drinks, a water or beer available from open fridges. If that’s not convincing enough there are roving masseurs giving free 10-minute massages to weary travellers. If you haven’t got the time or patience to circle around in search for a seat, I recommend you head for the Miles & Smiles Lounge were there are usually much smaller numbers.

Big lounge but very crowded. We were lucky as a few minutes after we arrived the lounge was completely full. Food was good with various stations around with different cooked food options. We visited in the evening on our outbound leg and in the morning on the inbound. Big let-downs were the fact that there are no sodas available in the lounge. No Coke or Pepsi products at all and, when I went to ask about a shower, the wait time was three hours! Seating very hit and miss due to the crowding. Nice touch are the lockers you can use for bag storage.

The lounge at Istanbul's old airport was phenomenal, so the expectations at the new airport were high not even close - no place to practice golf swings, no toy race tracks for the kids, no huge display of desserts from Do and Co Vienna, no chandeliers in the rest rooms, and only 6 stalls in the ladies' room, causing the inevitable queues food counters with onsite chefs were still good but what a disappointment overall! (also a bit hard to find even with wayfinder in the Turkish Airlines app - it's upstairs but how to get up there? eventually we found the entrance for disabled passengers and the man there was kind enough to let us in)

This is an overcrowded mess. I pass through that lounge 4 times a month and now I really feel like commenting. Before you go upstairs you have some rude staff who easily greet you with "where are you going". No excuse me Can I help you ! This happened many times to me. After you have passed these staff you go upstairs to the lounge where you enter with your boarding pass. So really why do you have people downstairs ? Once inside, doesn't matter the hours, I was in a refectory atmosphere and not a lounge. It is overcrowded with not enough seating. It is loud and no quiet area at your service. Although, THY thought of all amenities to make the stopovers as comfortable as possible, many of those are not used and just occupy space. I am an Elite plus card holder and qualify for that many times within one year There is no extra area dedicated to them. The food stations although impressive are busy with preparing food instead of serving. The cooks are overwhelmed by the amount of passengers annd are doing their best to keep up. The food buffet for cold dishes is always well stocked and no problem to serve yourself. In the last visit I left. There was no space. At 5:50 am. It is for me ungraspable how a lounge at such a big airport has to be in the middle overlooking shopping areas and not have a view to the tarmac. This could have been easily one of the best lounges in the world. Instead people rate it as excellent merely on the food options available if available. This is not a lounge where you feel or experience some sort of privilege.

The lounge that I went to on my recent flight with Air Serbia was very good. There were 2 lounges available for Air Serbia flights: the Turkish Airlines lounge and the ProPass lounge. The views and the drink options were both magnificent, but the food, well not so much. There weren’t many choices and the choices provided didn’t look fresh. The staff were nice, but the lounge was a bit noisy. The mini chocolate muffins were amazing, a must try! The toilets were very clean and had a pleasant odour. It also was a bit crowded and there was limited seating, but the seats were amazingly comfortable! The WiFi was great too! (Also I don’t know if there were showers!) In conclusion, this lounge is great and I would recommend it!

While the Turkish Airlines business class lounge highlights private rooms as a premium feature, the actual experience is anything but premium. The showers follow a reasonable queue system, but the private rooms are an elusive and undignified ordeal. Despite being advertised as part of the business class offering, they seem more like a marketing ploy. There’s no queue system in place for these rooms. Instead, passengers are expected to pop in and out, begging for availability. The staff, with stiff body language, offer vague and inconsistent time estimates—anywhere from 25 minutes to over an hour. To make matters worse, there’s no time limit for how long guests can occupy the rooms, leaving others in a constant state of uncertainty and frustration. This process leaves passengers feeling more like beggars than valued patrons. Turkish Airlines should either implement a proper queue system or charge a fee to ensure a fair and transparent process. The current setup is nothing short of undignified and far from the business class experience one would expect. I finally got my room after 3 hours of waiting in uncertainty, and it should not be like this.

This is a very busy lounge with Priority Pass members being put on a waiting list for approximately 45 minutes. Seating was scarce on the first floor. The food quality is excellent. The lounge had a nice selection of Mediterranean cuisine e.g. kefta kabob with tomatoes and aubergine, grilled creamy chicken, assortment of cheese and crackers, hummus and Turkish Tea. WiFi worked flawlessly. There were lines for the bathroom given the number of passengers in the lounge. Nonetheless, the bathrooms were clean.

I travel business class internationally due to poor health conditions and advanced age. I have heart disease and cannot walk very far, and my wife has nerve damage and also cannot walk long distances. We both require wheelchairs. We arrived to IST on February 7th, at 2:43 pm, from Toronto. We had a 7-hour long layover in Istanbul, before our flight TK708 departed for Karachi, Pakistan, at 9:55 pm. Because of the long connection, we tried to reserve a nap room and specifically chose IST for this purpose. My wife was unable to sleep on the 9 hour flight from Canada and was exhausted. A young lady at the concierge desk provided unprofessional and rude responses to us when we asked her for a nap room. She first said there were none and to come back every 30 minutes to check. My wife walked back and forth (with great difficulty) from distant seating areas over the course of 2 hours, every 30 minutes, because I cannot walk very far. The young lady at the concierge desk did not have the courtesy to take our phone number or to put our names as next in line. After 2 hours, we tried again (the 4th time), and a younger man quickly walked ahead of us to the desk. The concierge desk then gave the next available nap room to this young man, who only showed up the first time to the desk, instead of my wife and I, after we were waiting for 2 hours and had been to the desk 4 times. We pleaded with the young lady at the concierge desk, asking why she gave the room to the other man. The concierge simply said "he came to the desk faster than you". For 7 hours we were unable to rest and sat in regular seats in the lounge, waiting for our connecting flight. This has been the worst business class experience I have ever faced in my life.

I miss the old TK lounge at Ataturk airport. This lounge is always packed. And the food variety and quality goes downhill every time I’m here. And now, with Turkish (or Turkiye) boycotting US products, there are not only no Coke products, but no soda of any kind. Sorry. I’m headed into the terminal. Worthless to sit in the crowded lounge and you can’t even get a Coke. Turkish has really dropped its game in their lounges.

We definitely received very good service. They provided every service in the best possible way. The food is very delicious, the seating areas are comfortable and wide, and there are many activation systems to pass the time. So you will lose track of time while waiting for the transfer.

Exclusive Turkish airlines lounge, huge space, different rooms to relax, big variety of food and drinks, local sweets. There is also a piano, sometimes they play it. Easy to spend a few hours here. Free Wi-Fi

I had on other trips been in their excellent business class lounge and flying this time in economy but being in possession of a Star Alliance Gold Status I had been granted entrance in this CIP Lounge.  I read it is inferior to the Business Lounge but besides just a couple of food stations less, I must see I truly am impressed: excellent food and drink selection, lovely atmosphere, simply a great place to be and spend some time.

I heard that this lounge was opened to give passengers who paid for a business class ticket a slightly more exclusive experience by leaving out status customers and thus making the lounge less crowded. This has not worked. The TK lounge at Ataturk airport used to be really fantastic and special and it was one of the reasons I booked with TK all the time. This time seems to have passed. I am just sitting in the TK Business lounge at Istanbul new airport, feeling like waiting in an overcrowded train station. This feels more like a free fast food restaurant or an all-you-can-eat holiday venue, than an exclusive space to relax and wait for the next flight. Virtually all seats are occupied, mainly by bags and coats to reserve a seat for people who seem to be wandering around. People are shoveling piles of food onto their plates and leave the tables completely covered with leftovers and rubbish. Even the supposedly quiet areas are overcrowded. Having been in the fantastic Qatar Airways Business lounge at Doha airport, this is the complete opposite… crammed, crowded and ordinary.

Using this lounge on a SWISS flight. The place is simply horrible. There are plenty of alcoholic drinks especially whisky, served by a bartender - the food is terrible and extremely poor. There was a very salty soup, a lot of vegetables and bread with tuna salad. Some small kind of a saucer with limited food like pieces of cheese with one grape, pineapple, melon and berry. Another 3 cubes of chocolate cake. The soft drinks in the fridge were lukewarm, in a basket some melting ice. I left the lounge and went to an eatery to have a decent sandwich. Maybe this lounge is Ok if you want to drink alcohol but not for a decent snack at all. The restrooms were not very clean.
After all the hype I was expecting something above average. What a let down, seating in the food area was very poor, no bar, and incredibly complicated internet access.

Transited twice through this outstanding and impressive lounge. As with my last visit in May 2022, the lounge has an open airy feel. Its food offerings are varied/excellent with various cooking stations throughout the lounger to satisfy one's palette. One definitely gets a taste of Turkish cuisine. The salad bar is extensive with a wide variety as is the tea bar with its variety of teas. On both visits we were able to get free massages to the neck and shoulders. Can't go wrong with this type of service. WiFi connection was excellent. Bathrooms are very clean and maintained by attendants.

I was looking forward to visiting this lounge because I had heard so much about it. Well, maybe the food is ok but not for Vegans. Even the lentil soup and white rice had butter, nothing for Vegans but a bowl of green salad. Next time I can arrive at the airport a bit later and have food outside - complete disappointment.

Turkish Airlines' flagship business class lounge is outstanding and impressive. The lounge is on an open-level overlooking the main part of the terminal. There is plenty of seating and space. The seating is very comfortable. The lounge is immaculate and its food offerings are superb featuring freshly cooked food at various cooking stations throughout the lounge ranging from grilled foods, pasta and baked cheese, spinach and meat pies, cheeses/olives, salads and desserts. One definitely gets a taste of Turkish cuisine here including Simit (sesame seed bagel) and coffee/tea. The latter can be served in glass cups you get in Turkish restaurants. There are quieter darker seating areas akin to seating in a library like area. There is a room with 12 TV screens to catch up to the news. The lounge also features virtual golf and a holographic flight experience. The bathrooms are very clean and maintained by attendants. Our flight was at 2 pm so all the cooking stations were manned and food aplenty. Depending on the food station there were some queues. The staff kept the tables clean removing used dishes/utensils promptly. WiFi worked just fine; however, you had to scan boarding pass to get WiFi password.

What a great lounge! From the freshly cooked dishes ranging from typical Turkish kebabs through Moussaka, Chinese spicy chicken stir fry and pasta stations you could see all those being prepared. In addition various meze options and a few sweets including an array of the ubiquitous baklava variants. Drinks stations (DIY) were dotted around. One nice feature was the lockers in which you can leave your bags, using a combination of your choosing. There is a golf simulator and other adult toys including a Scalextric track! Comfortable seating in a variety of types and a quiet atmosphere.

The only hot food was toast. Other than that, it was pre-packaged rubbish.  The coffee was weak, stale and tepid. There was no draught beer, only tiny cans. It is probably the worst airport lounge of any big city in the world and a national embarrassment. The WIFI involves fiddly codes that you must obtain from machines.

My inbound flight was 09h30 min, and my outbound was 06h30 and in between a layover of 14h. I was denied a sleeping room while it was given to passengers between 04 and 09h layover. So, I spent the whole 14h in the lounge, couldn’t get near nor shower.

Food was average. Turkish wine is on a small cart tucked away in the corner in a massive lounge. You will need to argue to get into showers or the private suites. They do whatever they can to not give you what you are allowed. I dont understand it. We had a SFO to IST flight with a 4 hour 50 minute layover. Concierge said it was 3 hours and 45 minutes. You will have to argue. Very unfortunate. This lounge is dirty. Check out the seating the corners and the small tables. Sticky, hair and gross.

Turkish Airlines did not provide any lounge for this trip, for my full-fare-paid business class. Both a Swiss lounge and a lounge serving several Star Alliance Carriers are present but closed. Both British Airways and a Skyteam lounge are open, but Turkish did not make any arrangement for business class customers to use them, though Ethiopian Airlines did. I think having a lounge should be a basic element of an international business class itinerary, and no mention is made of its absence. I think it is lame that they do not provide a substitute if the lounge they usually use is under construction. The check-in agent confirmed there is no lounge access.

Despite the website saying I would have access to business lounge, they were all closed. Crammed everyone into regular lounge. Food was prepackaged garbage at domestic and lines for hot food in Intl were 15 to 20 deep. No bar service, just small bottles of soda/water/juice. Absolute garbage. No social distancing but used COVID safety as their explanation for Business being closed. And no lounge was open at Izmir or Kayseri. Shameful.

How to transform one of the best business lounge in one of the worse. Covid is an excuse for mediocrity. Turkish Airlines is the champion of it. It is easy. No more anything. And what is left: sandwich are really badly done no flavor, no nothing. How sad Forget traveling in business with them. Not worthy at all

The business lounge has become worse than it was at the old Istanbul airport. The choice of food there are no replacements for everything old. Stupid rules for using sleep rooms and they do not go to the rescue, even when the the room is free.

The lounge is quite big and has a diverse variety of foods. It has an area for desserts and for salads and few live counters. Excellent food selection, comfortable seating. Only problem is that it is difficult to find a good seat and the lounge tends to get crowded. Even after splitting Business class and Star Alliance Gold customers, the lounge is still crowded and noisy. Moreover, the free wifi is pretty weak. Otherwise, the ambience and staff are excellent.

It is open 24 hours, which is puzzling as the Turkish airlines flights depart in the late evening. In the morning when I visited, I was greeted by the receptionist who took my boarding pass and placed it in the photocopier. She said that her computer is broken so she can’t scan my boarding pass and will have to log my entry on paper. She handed it back to me and gave me a WiFi password. The lounge is slightly dark, but has natural daylight coming in, with a view over a garden in the airport. It has plenty of seating, ranging from couches, armchairs, dining tables and work tables. The breakfast spread was a bit puzzling, some fried rice, sausages and cooked ham, a basic selection of pastries and a rather large selection of cheese and nuts. I was wondering where the eggs were, when I discovered that they were made to order. I had a pretty good breakfast in the lounge and I enjoyed my eggs.  There was a bar although it was not manned, and there was Turkish tea, coffee and lounge drinks you’d expect. I like that they had Turkish tea glasses and the tea was excellent. I think this lounge is a good option, considering how new and unknown it still is.
The best business class lounge I have experienced, out of this world. Food was brilliant drinks free flowing and recommend the lounge. Just don't fly Turkish airlines to get the experience.

This lounge is a massive disappointment! It is a circus inside, nothing relaxing about it. The areas look beat up and old and in need of a refresh. I honestly felt the lounge was on the "cheap " side. Ive had better experiences even in Priority Pass lounges! I qualified for a "Suite" to rest in. I asked to shower an the attendant showed me to my room and said it was all busy for now and she would come by to get me as soon as one would free up.. She never showed up! The whole place is a Circus and the staff generally rude. It is loud, crowded and the suite for resting was a bit on the cheap side as well but did the trick for a 3 hour nap.

The lounge was a bit difficult to find as it was in the centre of the airport and both flights I took park at different sides of the airport. The lounge was huge (two-storey lounge) with modern decoration and facilities like a cinema, golf room and loads of seats and fridges for drinks. But the lounge had a lack of food even and only local food, fortunately that day there was a Japanese food selection. Although the lounge was huge, there were huge numbers of people and seats and facilities run out quickly. The toilets were clean but too small compared to number of people in the lounge. There was a locker to store a luggage. The WiFi can be access by scanning my boarding pass on the kiosk and received the WiFi code. The WiFi itself was fast but disconnected very easily when devices were turned off. Overall, the lounge was acceptable and could be improved.

After 6 years using this lounge regularly I am in a fair position to evaluate it. The food has not been changed during this entire time. Soup, wheat (bulgur) salad, cheese and little cookie type of things all the time. Heavily overcrowded. Hopefully at the new airport this will be altered.

Overrated, before travelling I spent time trawling the net & you tube looking at and getting excited about what was to lay ahead of me when I had my 3 hours lay over between flights. I was over whelmed at what I was seeing, a spacious lounge with so many amenities, choices of the different foods on offer along with areas to sit and rest in peace. Making my way to the lounge was a trek in itself, it seemed miles away from the gate we had landed at and for an airport so large there are not many travelators, and the walk went on and on! The airport at time was very busy, it’s close to midnight but i wasn't worried as soon i would be in the sanctuary of peace and quiet, a plate of tasty food and a long drink. How wrong i was, this place was manic, what could be described as a busy street in Istanbul during the sales! It was busier inside than it was out, I was first met by a group of unruly kids on the pool table, shouting, screaming with no regard for other travellers, as i ventured further inside the worst it got, it was cramped, no available seating and ques for the various food outlets winding all over the place, as for a seat -  no chance. A far cry from what I had seen on you tube and the glamorous descriptions given by Turkish Airlines, i have been in better lounges this by far was one of the worst, I started to suspect the videos where made at a time the airport was closed. I duly left!

Plenty of seating areas available to relax for a long transit. Excellent and delicious variety of Continental and Turkish food. Good choice of beverages. Lounge is not very noisy and toilets are super clean. Ambiance is beautiful. Great to have a movie area. However, there is still no information about the massages. They say they offer it and then when I asked, they said I needed some appointment. I did not get clarity on it. It's 100 times better to sit here than the overcrowded, noisy and dirty waiting area at the terminal.

Very nice lounge, good quality. Surprised by the catering offer which was excellent. If all lounges were of this quality, I will take a subscription. Congratulations to Turkish Airlines for this lounge, and to the staff who were very friendly. FR: Tres beau lounge, de bonne qualite. Surprise par l'offre de restauration qui etait excellente. Si tous les lounges etaient de cette qualite la, je prendrai un abonnement. Felicitations a Turkish Airlines pour ce lounge, et au staff qui etait tres sympa.

This is an amazing lounge and one of the best that I have been in. It is large and spacious and I arrived at about 12.30 am. The kitchen staff were gradually closing down in preparation for the morning rush so the available food was quite limited and there was nothing available that was freshly cooked (this is not the norm). There was plenty to drink. I wanted to take a shower (my previous one had been in Jerusalem early on the previous morning. All the showers were taken and there was a problem with the buzzer so I was disappointed that I missed out. Previous experience says that the showers are good and the bathrooms and toilets are very clean. WiFI connection was good and fast. It was a reasonable walk to the departure gate from the lounge. Overall not as good as previous visits but still a very good lounge.

This is a regional lounge for Turkish Airlines. They had a chef preparing breakfast/lunch food when I arrived and found it quite tasty and suitable for non Turks and Turks alike. I liked the ambience of the lounge - it was spacious and there were quiet areas if you wanted to work, there was television and areas for computers, including recharging. WifI was good and no problems with connection or speed. The toilets were clean. There was no shower. This was the only negative. The variety of drinks ws good and easily accessible. It was a relatively short walk to the departure gate.
