The seats are comfortable, but the tables are super low, and makes it hard to work while I wait for the flight. The lounge is noisy. The staff has good English and are helpful (in their Benagli way) There is an espresso machine but the coffee is not the best quality. the price for the lounge access is less than 1000 taka.

My husband wanted to surprise me with business class tickets to Cancun for our 30th anniversary & my 50th birthday. We we arrived at the airport for our 6 hour layover we tried to get into the lounge at 2:00am so we could rest and freshen up, but they wouldn’t allow WestJet business class in since they were closing at 3am and reopening at 6:00am. We paid a lot extra for business class but got no value from it. West Jest has screwed us almost every time we have flown with them. 0 value for our dollar. Beyond frustrating, especially when we are exhausted and were told when buying these tickets the lounge is included.

Dreadful, dated, filthy lounge. Poor, uncomfortable sagging seating. Areas under semi-permanent repair. Broken, stained table lamps. Bad food. Try to avoid passing through Shanghai Pudong airport if at all possible.

My expectations for these Beijing Capital Airport and Shanghai Pu Dong China Eastern lounges were modest, but they turned out to be better than I expected. The view from the PEK lounge was over a relatively quiet tarmac, while the PVG lounge had lots of natural light, but no view whatsoever. The PEK lounge had beer and Great Wall red and white wine. The Shanghai lounge offered more beverage choices with some liquor, including Bailey's, but not including rum. The wait staff were more efficient than friendly. The PVG lounge offered a cooking station, but since there was no menu, and the cooks didn't speak English, I have no idea what was available. There were sandwiches.and salads in the cooler. If I had anticipated world-class facilities, I would have been dissapointed, but as it was, this was a satisfactory way to await my flights.

China Eastern Lounge in Shanghai Pudong. The lounge is over capacity and cannot handle all the passengers from China Eastern, Delta, and others. The good is the food, and showers being available. Food is available fresh or what is cooked and already out. Drinks are available from coke/beer and juice/ and wine. Sadly, the coffee machine was out of order going to Shanghai, and on my return to Shanghai. I had to use Starbucks outside the lounge. Also the WiFi is available for free but the Chinese government restricts all the popular apps so it is not of much use. Till the new terminal is completed and China Eastern shifts over to the new terminal and bigger lounge the overcrowding will remain an issue.

This Air France-KLM  lounge was conveniently located near the China Eastern Airlines terminal. However, the lounge is incredibly small. Since Air France and KLM uses this lounge too, it can be pretty packed with no one to sit. The food spread is mediocre and the internet was decent.

The updated International lounge I visited looks very good now. It is pretty spacious with a lot of seating types. It was pretty busy the morning we were there. The first floor where most of the food is was very busy. However, the second level was pretty empty and relaxing with much more spacious and comfortable lounge chairs.  Quick and easy check in by friendly staff. Furniture: updated and new with a lot of electrical plugs around, second level offers a more comfortable seating as well as around 8 to 10 full body massage loungers. Wifi not the best. Food: noodle soup station with a chef that cooks your noodles on demand, there were a few soup toppings available. Breakfast food was also available with scrambled eggs, potatoes, bacon, sausages, variety of breads/croissants/buns/pastries. There was a small salad station. Second floor had a large beverage station with a few snacks. Showers/bathrooms very clean with bathroom attendants stationed inside the bathrooms. It was easy to get into the showers by contacting the staff. The shower was very nice and pretty spacious. I was given a cute little basket with a comb, a toothbrush, a mouthwash, as well as a hair dryer. Overall impression: a very pleasant experience that went well beyond our expectations.

Avoid at all costs. This is a cramped, uncomfortable, dirty, and poorly serviced lounge. It is loud and uncomfortable. The selection of food is poor. If I fly in business on China Eastern, I try the lounge for a few minutes - and always end up at the Starbucks at either end of the T1 concourse. The food is better, as is the atmosphere. That this is a flagship lounge in an airline's home hub is simply ludicrous.

One of the best business class lounges I have been to. Clean and quiet with modern, comfortable furniture, plenty of tables and workstations with power points everywhere. A good selection of snacks and drinks and friendly staff. Highly recommended.

The lounge in the International section of Terminal 1  was outstanding. There were plenty of tables and chairs with power outlets available. There were bathrooms and showers on the first and second floor. The food was excellent. They had Chinese and Western snacks as well as hot noodles and a hot buffet spread. It isn't Singapore Airlines or Etihad Airways style lounge, but it definitely beat the Korean Air lounge in Incheon. I would go to this lounge again.

KLM often departs from a nearby gate. This China Eastern Airlines lounge is big enough. Not enough male toilets avaliable. Different types of chilled and hot beverages and Chinese snacks (nuts etc) and small pastries are available. Wifi is terrible, which is a shame for such an airport. No couches, only seats. Comfort is OK.  If there were better F&B outlets at PVG (which there aren't), I would prefer a good cafe above this lounge.

This China Eastern Airlines lounge is not a Lounge. It is more of a 'holding pen' at best. China Eastern need to visit other airline Lounges to see what a First Class Lounge is really supposed to be. It is hot, uncomfortable, overcrowded. It is dirty with rubbish all over the place. It has no proper tables to eat at. The food looks awful - I had a bottle of water from a fridge that was old, dirty and not working properly. Access to the Lounge wifi was impossible to obtain. There are hardly any power outlets to power up phones or plug in a Laptop. Don't go there you will have a better experience sitting in the airport public area or one of the restaurants.

Dull uninviting tired room. No attendant (we were in at 2am). Egg salad sandwiches left out at room temp made me nervous. How long been there? No coffee. Booze in cooler. Decent washroom. No shower that I could find. A dozen or so people sleeping in chairs and on the floor

I agree. This China Eastern Airlines lounge is the worst I have ever seen. I confirm the disgusting toilet. Waste on the floor, no door handle on single cubicle. Small and poor food choice. No shower. Poor wifi signal. Some in our group paid for entry and fought to get a refund. I was business class so it was in my ticket. Staff only speak chinese.

This is the most disgusting lounge you have ever encountered, urine smell in the toilets, no door handles on the entry to the bathroom, stained carpet and lounges. Front staff don't look up as they on wechat, snap chat and don't care. After paying for first class you get this.  I travel 4 times a year to China and I had to write this as the lounge it is disgrace, the service on China Eastern was first class.

The worst Lounge I have ever been to, it is old fashioned and looks dirty. The lounge staff service is poor, employees speak very little English, seats are so uncomfortable and you are better stay standing up. It is a shame for the SkyTeam Alliance. China Eastern Airlines has to renew these old lounges.

The most basic of all business lounges I have used. Small one room, below main airport Gate lounges. This China Eastern Airlines lounge was dirty and well worn, seats were blue velour and had food and drink stains on them. There were more staff in the toilets than in the dining and sitting area. The reception staff were bored and showed no interest in the lounge. Prior to each flight they would shout out plane number. Loud Chinese passengers were not addressed and were pushy.

The first problem with the China Eastern lounge is its location. Getting to it from most waiting room locations is a long hike, then down an escalator, and then another hike. And when we were there, the up escalators (two of them) were out of commission. Then the seats: they're old and ratty. I tried four before I found one that I could sit in without sliding off. The men's restroom was filthy and had only two commodes and one urinal. The drinks were OK; the food selection was limited and the dishes unappealing. There is no PA. An attendant marches up and down the aisle barking boarding times. Lastly, the air conditioning is substandard.

This China Eastern Airlines business class lounge at Shanghai PuDong Airport is the worst business lounge I've ever been to. Only one bathroom, one urinal, one stall. Business bathroom was always closed, forcing business passengers to share the First Class bathroom. Same thing, stinky, smell of urine, dirty, and crowded. Food was average, and seating very limited. Wifi was slow. Airline delays not notified until asked. Lounge attendants not that friendly - a little testy and short tempered. If I can help it, China Eastern would be my very last possible choice of airlines.
Nice lounge, spacious, clean and cool. Very nice lunch with plenty of choices of cooked food and sandwiches. No alcohol which is a pity because the food deserves a nice glass of red wine.

The best word is "rudimentary".  Certainly not even close to anything offered by China Eastern Airlines peers in Asia, or even airlines from North America.  The lounges were clean, and there was food and some drinks, but poor. They're very basic in the seating department and rather plain.  Gin and warm tonic water were supplied, but no ice.  Wifi is impossible to connect-to unless one has a Chinese mobile telephone number.  There were no shower facilities available.  We went next-door to the First class lounge, it was pretty much the same as the business class lounge. China Eastern offer a comfortable, professional and pleasant inflight experience in business class.  The lounge experience doesn't even come close.

Small crowded very 1974. On the bright side no blaring CNN or other stupid American TV "news" shows because you're in China! No monitor to check flight details. Announcements are made in sort of English but were so muffled and unintelligible to be useless. Very tired looking and in desperate need of a refit. Staff sort of want to help but don't really know how to.

What can I say this is so disgusting one would think that China Eastern could ensure that business travellers have a decent lounge at their flagship airport. Very poor wifi and no music or even CNN. The lounge is dirty even the walls and chairs are falling apart how embarrassing for a nation that prides themselves on being ahead of the rest of the world clearly not in this arena.

This is a domestic first (business) class lounge for China Eastern and Shanghai Airlines. Visited twice in the last 2 weeks and I'd say that this lounge is below average. No outside view of any kind. Boarding notifications shouted by staff. Stir fries and rice offered during meal time but not delicious and attractive at all. Some salad sandwiches dessert and other snacks available. Soft drinks plenty with some beer and wine. Used plates collected from time to time. Washrooms were clean. Biggest complaint is the wifi - uses public wifi which is extremely slow. Overall I only recommend because it has couches (more comfortable than the benches outside) and provides free drinks and edible food but don't come with high expectations.
Very poor lounge. Food is terrible chairs old dirty and uncomfortable. Staff unfriendly. Better to wait at boarding gate.

I had just become an Eastern Miles Golden Member but did not have the card with me yet. I asked the girl at the entrance of the lounge to let my 5-month pregnant wife to enter the lounge with me (something I was entitled to as Golden Member) also considering there were only 20 minutes left before boarding. The staff refused saying they wanted to see the card. I therefore entered the lounge alone: packed as usual (for Chinese it is extremely easy to join the lounge through their credit card membership) some average noodles sandwiches and fruit. I expressly asked the staff to let me know if the gate changed (it happens frequently in China) and they did not do that. Overall the standard terrible China Eastern's service.
Although the food is decent in terms of quantity and quality the furniture is old and highly uncomfortable. Not many electric plug points for recharge etc. No announcements either.

Poor service of staff! Don't think it is their job to inform guests of delays (3 hours). Nobody cleans up after departed guests (or way too slowly). Food served is all packaged crackers and cling wrapped sandwiches. Chairs are old - seats in the public area of the terminal are more comfortable.

There are a few lounges located throughout the terminal with easy access to all gates. Attendants were very accommodating and explained the comforts of the lounge and that they would make a boarding call. Many hot appetizers as well as Asian / Western Dishes available. Well stocked bar as well as soft drinks water and tea. Assortment of Asian and English language newspapers. WIFI worked well and the 4 hours spent in the lounge were very pleasant.
Good lounge big and bright very clean I was there at breakfast and a variety of westernish and Chinese hot and cold dishes were available. Good fast wifi available and comfy chairs.
Lounge has been refurbished to include uncomfortable seating used to be a nice comfy lounge. Snacks and drinks not too bad. Not a place to spend 6 hours (any more).

Small lounge close to gate 46 at terminal 2 with portable wall surrounds to divide from the rest of the waiting area quite noisy because of the walls and also very busy as were all other lounges. Simple snacks and drinks available plus cold Tsingdao beer and red wine. Not bad for a domestic lounge.

Pretty good lounge PVG has lounges located at most international gate ares so not overcrowded. Good selection of hot food and snacks when I was there around 6pm and good bar variety too. Wifi worked well and English papers and magazines available too.

More than adequate lounge separate from business class. Hostess helpful and friendly. Electrical outlets for last minute computer/ pda charging are abundant. Nice selection of hot/ cold food both western and Asian; as well as alcohol sodas and water. I would like to see more Western magazines and newspapers other than the LA Times but that would be the only minor criticism.

In general this lounge was an average one to all the ones I been to. This lounge was also empty. They had a bad section of food but it tasted okay. The lounge felt and looked boring. The lounge had no internet but it had power points. The bathrooms were good but lacked showers. The staff were friendly.

I’ve used this Primus Lounge a couple of times now. It’s very small and can get crowded. Only water and hot drinks and only a couple of choices of hot food. No snacks are available. Not one to write home about
A relatively quiet lounge meant I had a choice of seating. Food was plentiful with several hot options. Has its own wifi. Overall one of the better lounges I have visited in India

Busy, as a lot of Indian lounges can be, however there was sufficient seating inside. A good choice of food, with 3 or 4 hot dishes to choose from. Not much in the snack depart, just some sandwiches. Non alcoholic Drinks are free, but alcoholic ones you have to pay for. No Wi-Fi though

Very small lounge but good selection of sandwiches and snacks. Hot soup provided. Small bar with good selection of drinks. Edward provided friendly and efficient service. Surprised there was only one male toilet facility. The lounge only opens 3 hours before departure.

Excellent small lounge opposite gate A32. Two levels with views of aircraft taking off and landing. Friendly and efficient staff. A good choice of beverages - alcoholic and soft. A small food menu with a range of microwaved dishes. We had Chicken Tikka Masala which was OK and an excellent Apple Crisp.

This was quite possibly the worst Business Class Lounge we have ever visited! There was a poor choice of food, which was continually running out and not being replenished. Likewise the availability of clean plates was continually running out and when pointed out to the staff, they brought out just 1 plate! The tables were rarely cleared or wiped down properly, resulting in almost every one overflowing with dirty cutlery/glasses and plates that were simply left for over 2 hours in most cases. The staff were very few and those who were there, extremely rude. The restrooms were of inadequate number and quality. We could not find any USB sockets to plug our phones into either. I simply can not imagine why Virgin Atlantic choose to associate themselves with this company and lounge as it does not reflect well on them at all. I would avoid this lounge at all costs!

This is a pretty small lounge area with no external windows as it is situated on a lower level than most others. The range of food and drinks offered was pretty impressive and the wi-fi was fast and smooth. The staff were very helpful and obliging. There were only two toilets, a male and a female assisted toilet and one mixed-sex cubicle. It seemed enough for the clients there that evening though. There is only one real drawback, no showers and no Bistro. Showers I would have thought would be a standard feature of an airport lounge which is dedicated to long-haul travel and after driving several hours and putting up with the hot and crowded security and TSA process pretty necessary. While I can appreciate Virgin having the need for a small lounge, they do not have many flights each day, I cannot excuse the lack of a shower facility.

My Partner was lucky enough to win online upgrade to Upper Class so we made use of the Upper Class Lounge at T3. It was on Christmas Day and was superb. The food and service was excellent and I wish I could experience this again. The lounge is spacious with different zones and so much to keep you occupied. It is absurd there were more staff than customers for the majority of our stay but I guess it was Christmas Day and probably not always like that. The staff working were lovely and really made us welcome. The food and drink was first class and the Spa treatments great. There are plenty of magazines to read, a Pool Table and great washrooms.

DL Skylounge was overcrowded, people sitting on the floor, I am sure max capacity was exceeded. Food on the floor, dirty, no seats, cabin baggage all over the place, ordered a drink and was charged $9.98! When I complained to the reception supervisor, she rudely advised me that Virgin Atlantic Upper class passengers were no different to any other passenger and certainly no better, then followed me to the lift door repeating over and over the same. Certainly no comparison to VS upper class lounge at LHR.

Always like to be welcomed at Virgin Atlantic. The reception is warm, the service staff are attentive. The music is great and the vibe is amazing. It’s usually not big but the drinks are good and so are the food.

The lounge is OK - just that. The range of drinks and food is all one needs sandwiches - wine spirits etc. There are some comfortable seats and tables to eat at. The downside is that there is no air conditioning and anyone can pay a small charge and use the lounge which results in it becoming absolutely packed. One family arrived with ten children which caused mayhem. I am a parent and I am not against children on flights. There would not have been a problem if the children were using the play area, watching TV etc. but climbing all over the furniture and tables, screaming, snatching food at will resulted in many fleeing the lounge for the quiet of the departure area downstairs as the parents made little attempt to modify their behaviour. For a leisure trip it can be annoying but if one is on a business trip one is left with nowhere to work. The airport needs to balance their policy of allowing entry to anyone who pays with providing a quiet work area for business travellers.

Flew Virgin Upper Class back to Heathrow from Miami and they use Club America at this airport. Looks like it is used by other Airlines. Nowhere near the standards of Virgin's Clubhouse or some other  Lounges it was at least, when we visited, quiet and uncrowded and we found two comfy chairs in a quiet corner to use for a couple of hours easily enough. Seemed clean (with at least two attendants going round and also serving), average choice of wines (no sauvignon blanc), beers and spirits. No hot food options with mostly snack type foods (potato chips, dips, cookies) it also had some sourdough sandwiches filled with mild cheese and unidentified meats. The cheese sandwiches were not too bad. WiFi was slower than most glaciers but at least we had it. Not the best lounge but far better than waiting in one of the fast food/sports bar/coffee shops in the main concourse.

First time in the LHR Virgin Clubhouse for a few years, nice welcome and despite being very busy with evening flight passengers the atmosphere was very nice it didn't feel crowded.. Found a quiet spot to relax for an hour, lounge staff soon on hand to offer drinks & dinner which I accepted.. I ordered a signature burger. Not expecting anything special it was actually very good and well presented. Spent a further 40 minutes checking emails & social media before the flight was called. Very nice lounge one of the best at LHR.

As Virgin Atlantic moved to Gatwick Airport North terminal two days after I wrote this the lounge layout description, it would be superfluous. All of the staff are transferring with the move. All the people from the waitresses serving food and drink to the receptionists were great with cheerful smiles and good service. If this is carried on to the North terminal it will be great.

This lounge at Barbados Grantley Adams Airport is used by multiple airlines and some passengers who can buy entry to the lounge. Views over most of the apron and runway is obscured except for one window so not much to look at other than the interesting green and orange colour scheme. Small selection of sandwiches and nuts/nibbles etc. A reasonable selection of spirits, wines beer and soft drinks. As in most of Barbados people are pleasant and helpful.

This lounge is an experience, staff welcome you and explain the layout and features. Food is plentiful and you order from a menu. There is a Deli section as well. In addition there is a library, spa, sauna, jacuzzi and other aspects unique to this place. I enjoyed my complimentary facial. This is a lounge where you can easily pass a couple of hours without being bored.

I flew Los Angeles to London Heathrow in July 2016 and visited the Virgin Atlantic Clubhouse lounge briefly. The seats were incredibly uncomfortable; the “background music” was loud and intrusive — I moved seats three times to try to get away from the overhead speakers (without success); the menu was very limited and definitely not outstanding. I stayed about 30 minutes, couldn’t take the noise any longer, then headed across the hall to the Air Canada lounge where it was peaceful, the food choices far more varied, and the seats very comfortable and relaxing. “Trendy” Virgin may be, but a seasoned traveler, who is not looking for a flashy faux nightclub atmosphere, will prefer another quieter airline lounge. I may travel Virgin Upper Class again but won't be going back to their LAX lounge.

As a lifetime member of the United Club, I had intended to visit our lounge at HKG; it's temporarily closed. Because I am flying on EVA Air to TPE, as a Star Alliance Gold, they gave me a pass to the Virgin Clubhouse. Normally Star Golds would have three options at HKG: a Singapore Silver Kris, a Thai, and the United Club. Access to the Virgin Clubhouse is the bonus. The views are absolutely spectacular. The food and beverages are outstanding. There is even a printed menu outlining the various options - not quite the equal of the Turkish business lounge in IST, but still more than adequate. At noontime, the lounge is essentially empty. There are bar stool seats, counter seats, and comfortable cushioned chairs aplenty. The receptionist and all the service personnel are polite, efficient, and attentive. I had hoped to compare and contrast the United Club here at HKG with the impressive new club at LHR. The fact that the club here is closed ended up rewarding me with an unexpected outstanding alternative experience.

New lounge for Virgin Atlantic after years of sharing the Air New Zealand facilities. Opening hours from around two in the afternoon to probably nine at night when the second flight has departed. Opened in the spring of 2015. Very bright, plenty of space as I assume it only covers the two flights a day to LHR. Food rather limited, you can sit down and order a cooked snack similar to the Heathrow lounge, but food is more limited. However it is an improvement on the dry bread and salad offered in previously used Air New Zealand lounge. Nice bar quite well stocked, this is waitress service and not the old help yourself drinks. Good wifi and views of the runway. Staff polite and helpful. Our main complaint would be the seating, flashy, bright but dreadfully uncomfortable. Some of the couches have seats that are three feet deep - unless you have four of five cushions behind you, there is no way on earth you can lean back. Again most of the chairs have very little back, or make you sit at a weird angle. They have obviously paid some way out designer a load of money to select the seating, but as a relaxation before boarding its a one out of ten.

The No.1 Traveller Lounge at Gatwick was offered as part of booking and isn't the Virgin Clubhouse. I'm amazed anyone would pay for access to this lounge. It's cramped. The food is decidedly average and over breakfast : early morning they struggled to maintain quantity never mind quality. Bar is serviced and limited selection only. Toilets were a disgrace and need refurbishment. When we arrived had to clean tables to find a space. Subsequently an overworked but pleasant young staff member got on top of the cleaning of tables - just! Perhaps some of those standing around at the bar / entrance might have helped? Paper selection was ok and same goes for magazines although both were limited in number.

Virgin Atlantic Clubhouse at Boston Logan, and the food selection is wide meaning you can have some posh nosh, or a simple burger. Varying types of alcohol mean you aren't restricted in choice and service is plentiful, you aren't sat long before you're offered a drink. Toilets are private, exactly what you want before a flight to allow you to freshen up, change clothes even. Staff are friendly and willing to make a joke or two. Whilst this lounge is very small, it's such good service, you really won't mind in the slightest.

The Virgin Atlantic Clubhouse in LHR is a big open space, great seating, table service, a full bar, a deli area, outdoor patio with views of the airfield, spa/salon, showers, pool tables, business center, video games. You can drop your bags off with a porter, great food and service, large TVs.
This is the best lounge that I have been in. Eat what you want. Service is fantastic. Free spa services. I would fly Virgin again so we can experience this lounge once more.

A bit disappointed. My lasting memory will be the red covered pool table rather than the food or ambience? Shame it's a nice spot but let down by the limited choice of menu. The staff were friendly but working with limited resources in terms of food. Time to innovate?
For a brand new lounge the internet was a disaster everyone was getting frustrated. I came to the lounge 3 hours before my flight to work what a waste of my time.

What a disgrace our first and definitely our last. Not quiet shortage of food shortage of drink empty soap dispensers in toilet generally not clean and dreadful WiFi. I guess I shouldn't be surprised the whole airport experience from moment of landing to leaving was horrid. When people pay thousands to travel first class we expect far better. We certainly expect better of Virgin Atlantic with whom we were traveling.

This lounge needs redesigning with a wrecking ball. A place of peaceful relaxation - certainly not. Liquor - yes get drunk to avoid the disappointment. Service - what would that be? Food dodgy looking soup plus a few skinny sandwiches and biscuits. Wine - that'll be red or white then. Milk for tea. Oh ok- they found some - peculiar these Brits and they like it to be hot. Sitting in it right now resisting urge to send out for a pizza.
Worst lounge ever no food no beer no staff. Complete disappointment. Felt like back to the past.

We had four hours in this lounge while waiting for our Qatar airways flight. The service was exemplary and made us feel right at home. The showers were clean and great before the flight home. Well done to the ladies who served us.

Excellent lounge with very attentive staff. Lots of seating options and a good size dining area. Showers excellent. We found seats by the window with good views of the apron and runway. Food was great we had several items off the tapas menu to share. The deep fried squid and the cheese on toast were exceptionally good.

Just arrived home from LAX. Totally shocked at the way we have been treated as upper class passengers! We were made to walk from terminal 2 to terminal 3 so we could use a lounge. The Virgin Loft Lounge only caters for Shorthaul passengers - lacking any decent food (a cookie and a grape at best with cheese cut to the size for a mousetrap!) No showers small toilet and wash facilities. We have always used Air NZ lounge previously which was excellent. Virgin must rectify this situation quickly otherwise Upper Class passengers will seek alternatives. The shuttle bus ride back to term 2 was such an experience - we have now seen areas of the airport no one would want to see - trash bins cleaning vehicles etc (all part of the luxury upper class experience no doubt!)

Was offered the lounge as an alternative to the Air New Zealand lounge as an Upper Class Virgin Atlantic passenger. The lounge is poor in comparison to other lounges that I have experienced Bar is okay if a little limited but food is very poor - bread cheese soup and cookies No showers or changing facilities. No comparison with the Air New Zealand lounge at LAX or Virgin Lounge at Heathrow. Very disappointing!

Although we were transiting to Manchester we had over three hours at LHR and so decided to use the Arrivals Lounge. It was an excellent choice. The friendly staff on reception offered us showers immediately and after these we sat in the lounge and enjoyed an excellent tasty well cooked breakfast served by more friendly staff. The lounge was comfortable and clean with excellent shower rooms. The WiFi was slow at first but then speeded up to an acceptable level. It was a pleasure to be in this lounge after the grim lounge we had experienced on departure from Miami. The lounge was not crowded while we were there although given its size it could be if a lot of flights arrived together.

As grim a lounge as I can recall for many years. A couple of apparently arguing staff on duty. The lounge was totally enclosed with no view of the outside and the seating was in my view not up to the standard you expect in a business class lounge. The food was nothing special pretzels cookies and when a few sandwiches appeared they were soon grabbed by the nearest passengers although they were edible. WiFi seemed to be an acceptable speed for what I needed. Toilets were adequate and clean (just about) although they had a strange smell. With only one flight a day I accept that Virgin's choice is limited but they really need to have words with Club America as this lounge does Virgin's reputation no good.

Worst lounge I have ever been in. Empty of staff empty of any food except pretzels and wifi so slow that when I tested the speed it came back with basically the equivalent of 56k dialup modem. Fine for the 1990s but just appalling. I know it's not Virgin's own lounge and with 1 flight a day they are not going to do anything about it but Club America ought to be ashamed.

I was lucky enough to get access to this haven of peace and good vibe. The lounge is upbeat but relaxing music cool staff and gourmet food and champagne. All you need do is find a nice seat (plenty on offer) and a decent magazine and wave your hand and one of the cheerful young waiters/waitresses take your order. I enjoyed Lanson champagne with excellent choices of food.

Virgin Little Red lounges at Heathrow Terminal 1 and Edinburgh Airports are basically space in the Servisair Lounge. When the route LHR-Edinburgh started I could get into both lounges using my Singapore Airlines Gold Card as per normal Virgin lounges. At Terminal 1 in Heathrow it is a good 10-15 minute walk about as far apart as you can get in the terminal from lounge to gate. Three time I have been refused access here - you have to go back down the stairs go to the internal desk hope it is manned or the person is free get a pass from them and go back. it is more hassle than it is worth. In Edinburgh twice they said "no" then looked at a card document and realised it was "yes" but this apparently changes in September and the SQ card is no longer welcome there. Basically it's Virgin Gold or nothing - it would have been nice to communicate it. Whilst the in air product competes with BA on the routes on the ground they are poles apart. Sad to get driven back to using BA because of this.

No staff on duty. Only pretzels or Cookies to eat. When you walk in its business ticket passengers to the right and others including priority pass to the left in a separate lounge. Never have I felt so second class having a Priority pass card.
Very close to the gates 5 minutes or so to boarding. Service a bit slow did not manage to eat as it took 10+ minutes to get the food served. Showers were very useful.
Nice place to hang out prior to flight. Enough sofas to lie down and take a nap. Meals okay lots of space to relax. Showers useful with steam function. Did not try the massage or beauty treatments.
Nice to be able to wash up and have a shower on arrival in London Heathrow. Breakfast was tasty and efficient. Not crowded but space on the smaller side.

This is a shared lounge with Cathay Pacific and several others. It is also the type of lounge that appears to be accessed by anyone paying a nominal fee or having a paid-for lounge pass. As such it was absolutely crowded out - we got two of the last seats available on a Thursday afternoon. There was nothing to eat apart from soup (unnamed) and crisps and only quarter bottles of indifferent wine (the white ran out about an hour after we arrived) with a few general spirits such as G&T. This is not a proper business lounge of the type you would expect from Virgin and we were very very disappointed. There were no UK papers hardly any magazines and the room was small and cramped. We watched people come in walk around looking for a seat and then leave again. I asked the woman on the reception desk what happened when the lounge was full and she told me that she "sent them away". When I asked where to she replied "out of here". Chicago is not a small airport in the middle of nowhere it is an important international hub and as such business passengers should be provided with facilities to match the price paid.

This was the worst lounge experience I have ever had. My wife and I arrived for a 12.30pm flight to Cancun at about 9am. The lounge was practically empty There were a few holiday makers. There were no help yourself drinks - you had to ask for an alcoholic beverage. The spectacular view of the runway was a row of industrial air vents on a roof. The cooked breakfast would not have fed a sparrow. I went to get my free spa treatment to be told that they could fit me in at 3pm. This was 10 am - a bit problematic considering that I would be half way across the Atlantic at the time. So my wife and I had no free spa treatment. There was one lady getting her nails done but the problem was that there were no staff around - probably did not want to pay them overtime on Easter Saturday. To cap it all I went to the loo and there was a disgusting smell of smoke as somebody had been in there smoking. Considering we were offered the exclusive privilege of being in there for the princely sum of £50 each I just did not rate it at all. Very disappointing indeed - stay clear unless it's free!

We arrived at the airport very early had small snack from Gravlax counter/salad bar. Excellent choices and very tasty. Very pleasant service from waiters. Good changing facilities for baby. Main meal of curry with very decent Merlot. All very relaxed and nice to get out of way before night flight. My wife got hair treatment. Staff food and drink quality and the extras of beauty salon/ barbers all made the start of trip very easy.

Shoe polish free spa treatments or free haircut in the salon. Then off for a shower if you so wish then find a seat and the waiter will attend your beverage requirements. The food choices are amazing they have a full Deli counter or you can choose from the extensive food menu. After this you can play pool or retire in the library while the kids can play in the softplay. And the best bit is you can check in as many hours before as you like we have a connecting flight from the North so we always take a flight early in the morning so we can spend longer in the Virgin lounge.
Not as grand as LHR but present staff food and drinks are fine the only issue is sharing with other airlines can become very crowded. It is clean and comfortable.
The perfect way to relax before your flight. Quality food and service delivered with a smile.

Paid £125 to book into the clubhouse - but ended up spending an hour on an over crowded bench eating junk food in the terminal as the clubhouse would not let us in (they had lost our booking). Basically it would have been cheaper and less stressful to rip up a £10 note and throw it around every five minutes before the flight. Staff unhelpful and Virgin not interested in refunding or helping despite nearly two months of trying.

I'm currently sitting in the lounge. Only 3 other passengers in here so I'm wondering if there is another Virgin lounge here as this one is abysmal. No food whatsoever. No atmosphere. Probably the worst lounge I've been in. The staff begrudgingly trundled off to get me some milk for my lukewarm tea. Just dreadful.

They provide a Meet and greet service upon arrival  we were expedited through immigration and customs and taken out to our taxi. Upon departure we were meet at our taxi checked in and assisted through Immigration security and to the lounge -there is a small fee. At the lounge there is a snack table and fully stocked bar there is also a smokers gallery. Air Conditioning cable TV wireless internet access and reading materials. Very welcoming and friendly efficient staff.

Pretty basic normal Club America standard. This facility is used as a shared lounge by Virgin and British Airways. Quite comfortable and well laid out small business centre with a couple of terminals free wi-fi available. Soup and a few sandwiches available they seem to run out of these at regular intervals but rather than just getting more made appear to fill them once an hour. The problem is that if there is a sudden influx the sandwiches soon disappear but you may have to wait 45 minutes for them to bring in any more. Drinks not too bad spirits and beer ok a couple each of reds and whites more in fridges if you scratch around. Soft drinks are from large two litre bottles can be a bit flat - coffee and tea available with a dish of cookies. All on self service. If you are a bit hungry then you may do well to eat before security and then use the lounge for a relax and drink. The eating on air side is dreadful - Burger King Pizza and Panini is all that's available.

I paid the $35.00 fee for the Virgin Clubhouse at SFO which is immaculate. The agent at the Clubhouse upon my telling her it was my first visit showed me the amenities and features. She made me feel welcome.
An oasis of calm in HKIA. Attentive staff make sure that your drink is always full and that you have food - which is good - when you want it.

I was eager to try the newly renovated Clubhouse. About the second nicest lounge I have used and the most stylish. Seating comfortable cooked breakfast good plenty of room and the business centre provides laptops as well as wifi. There is a Cowshed spa - and here is my only criticism. The old lounge had perfectly good complementary spa treatments and offered free shaves and haircuts. Cowshed charges for most of its services and offers only massages facials and related therapies: great if you just want pampering but useless to a busy male flier like me who just wants to look his best at the other end of his flight. Also there is no "revivals" lounge at Gatwick - and Virgin do not have their own lounge in Orlando.

Kenya Duty Free First Class Lounge. Virgin really need to do something about this lounge. It is a shared lounge but dreadful - words cannot adequately describe it. A dingy windowless room with worn out old leather sofas. Terrible selection of drinks and nibbles. A handful of several day old newspapers. Dial up internet pc was so slow I gave up.

Cowshed is great laze around in a jacuzzi shower have your suit pressed and shoes cleaned. Sit at the bar eat a meal at the restaurant. Deli counter for lighter bites. Great drinks great staff and viewing areas. Pool table and cinema sized screen with lazyboy chairs. A sanctuary at Heathrow airport loved it!

Only one daily flight from JNB to LHR for Virgin so lounge is not huge. It is however very classy and has most things needed. There is a full menu or drinks and food several options which are all freshly prepared and very nice. Several shower rooms to freshen up. Business suite with three computers free internet etc. Comfortable private seating areas and a sit up bar. Table and chairs if you would rather eat at a table. Nice looking lounge and works well. Long way to gate for flight 10 mins I'd guess

Absolutely fantastic facility. We were delayed 8 hours at Gatwick on our way to Vegas. Staff in the V Room could not have been better - food and drink provided throughout the day and no queue for the toilets. Staff even kept the lounge open late to provide us with a haven away from all the fraught tempers downstairs. If you are able to access this lounge it is worth the cost - especially if you are delayed. We travelled with an 8 year old who didn't complain once and was kept entertained with facilities on offer.

There is no food at all and you are forbidden to bring food that you may have purchased elsewhere into the lounge. The staff were not very helpful when I asked if there were any newspapers to read - I was advised that if I couldn't find one they must have all been taken. Its a shame that Virgin and British Airways have to use this facility - its only the second time I have used this lounge and wouldn't bother again we cleared our own table which did seem to prompt the staff to clean other tables that had been left.
Fantastic. Got breakfast included drinks also. Could have had a glass of champagne but as not a drinker so missed out! Funky washrooms - unisex so be aware. Staff polite friendly.

First time user of LHR Clubhouse and very impressed. Shown the various areas by a staff member and looked around ourselves before deciding on a seat viewing the runway. Firstly deposited bag and given a ticket to collect it prior to boarding. There were many different types of seating areas: cafe style; by Tv; in library; lounge style; child area; IT area - lots of choice. Chose a wicker hanging chair and sofa behind bar and ordered chicken curry and burger and champagne and espresso martini. The food came first with drinks shortly after. Had another drink and then went for our pre-booked shave and manicure in the cowshed. Found a seat in the same area following our treatments and had another couple of drinks and a dessert.

This is a new lounge dedicated solely to Virgin Atlantic. Not too impressed on the first visit very little food on offer a few crackers two types of rather solid or stale bread cheese and a type of ham. This was before one of VA's sleeper flights we were warned at check in that a hot meal would not be served to us as we were located at the front on the upper class cabin how you are supposed to exist on this baffles me. The drinks are pretty poor as well only two white wines on offer tasted both - in my opinion undrinkable went for the 'champagne' a californian sparkling wine. did manage one glass but resisted going back for another. The staff pointed out that there was only one diet coke left they would not have any more until Monday (this was Thursday afternoon). In all the lounge was very crowded by the time the flight was called. If part of upper class fares are to cover the lounge then this is not good value. A general lack of toilets needed to queue to use.

Smallish lounge although with only 1 Virgin flight a day this no surprise. Felt a little crowded on this full flight in Upper Class. Nice design - deli feel with plentiful drinks selection and reading materials. Staff ranged from pleasant to fairly disinterested. Food selection a little limited - expected more hot choices but clam chowder was delicious. Flight delayed which not announced until fairly late.

This lounge makes a night flight work. Check-in early complete all outstanding work issues here rather than the office. Wander over to the bar and have a champagne while contemplating the menu at the restaurant. Enjoy a freshly cooked rather than reheated food and wine tasting as it should at a table as opposed to your seat. If you want a haircut or massage these too are available.

Very impressed with Virgin's Clubhouse at Heathrow. The lounge was quiet spacious and well laid out. Food was excellent. I took advantage of the Cowshed and booked a wet shave - great way to start a morning flight. Staff were very attentive. Overall experience was good - a very relaxing start to my trip.

Early morning and an early start meant the lounge was very quiet. It was a pleasure to use. Food was excellent high quality and staff generally very attentive. Very pleasant and relaxing start to the journey. Highly recommended.

I found the staff very helpful at all times. The food and drink selection was very good with the option of having dinner before the flight. Bathroom & shower facilities were excellent and kept very clean. Its locality to the departure gate was excellent with only a 2 minute walk to endure. Overall very good.

This is the worst business lounge I have been to. The food selection was appalling with cold stale offerings. These consisted of literally a few paltry plates. I ate nothing. The drinks section worse. One type of beer, one kind each of red and white wine, gin and whiskey. No sense of a business class lounge at all and this is Xiamen Airlines home base .. so they should have it as a model for the quality of their airline.

Domestic lounge was tastefully furnished, comfortable and spacious lounge. I can't say anything about the food, but it looked like noodles. Being my first visit to China I didn't have my WeChat account set up, which is the easiest way to access wifi in the airports. The staff at the front desk went the extra mile to enable me to connect my phone to the wifi. I would recommend this, especially considering that this is a domestic lounge. International lounge is a disappointment compared to the domestic lounge. There was clearly only one international flight going out and it looked like they had only grudgingly opened it up for passengers. Soft drinks, a few half full bottles of wine and no beer. Pot noodles were available if yu like that sort of food; otherwise just a few miserable biscuits. What a contrast! The score below and my averages, but I'd say the domestic lounge is twice as good as the international one.

This lounge was very disappointing for the simple reason that there were no bathrooms within the lounge. One has to use the bathrooms in the terminal. Why pay for membership to use a lounge when one of the basic amenities (bathrooms) are not available. Notwithstanding the above, the facilities were clean and the lounge had the usual hot and cold food choices plus beverages (soft drinks, water etc.) available with Turkish breakfast items available (olives, cucumbers, tomatoes and various cheeses). If I had known that this lounge had no internal bathrooms, I wouldn't have wasted $$ to enter the lounge.

This is one of the best non airline lounges. The lounge is very spacious. The lobby is very welcoming. The long hallways stretch the length of the lounge reflect the Islamic and Omani architecture. There is plenty of seating. There is a main food station plus 2 others at either end. Given our early morning departure, the buffets had breakfast items (both western and Arabic), cut and whole fresh fruit, salad bar, pastries and assorted breads. The main food station has a live cooking area where one can order eggs/omelets any style. I did not use WiFi so I can comment on connectivity. Restrooms were very clean and seating was very comfortable.

This is a small lounge. The food quality is good. The portions are tapas sized which can be ordered from the menu by scanning QR code on the tables. The lounge had a variety of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages available. Service staff was very polite and friendly. WiFi was very easy to connect too and very fast with plenty of outlets to charge phones. The only drawback to this lounge is that the bathrooms were out of order on this visit meaning guests had to use the facilities in the terminal.

This lounge is small and very crowded for an early morning flight. There was a dearth of sitting options. From what I observed, the food/beverage service was very limited. Worst of all, there is only one bathroom in the Lounge. I chose to leave the Club and use the facilities in the airport and waited for my flight at the gate. We were able to use this lounge because of our business class tickets. It seems this is the only lounge available in Terminal 3 so there is no choice but to use it.

The Club at CLT is a welcome addition to this airport for those who are not AA's Admiral Club members. I was pleasantly surprised with this small Priority Pass lounge. The staff is very friendly. Unlike most clubs with a buffet selection, this Club offers an automated albeit limited menu. Scan the QR code and order. Unfortunately, due to the lateness of the day, the Club ran out of the entrée I ordered. Nonetheless, this lounge was well worth the long walk from Concourse B. Bathrooms were clean and the WiFi had a strong signal.

This Swissport lounge is pathetic. The only nice thing about this lounge was the gentleman receptionist and the hot chocolate. The seating is basically nothing more than a barebones seating area. Snacks, soft drinks and a few alcohol offering are the extent of its food/beverage service. We were able to use this lounge because of our business class tickets. However, I certainly wouldn't pay to use this facility. It would be throwing money away. WiFi worked but I felt it was spotty.

When i arrived at the Toronto Pearson Plaza Premium lounge on Jan 9th in the afternoon it was completely full, it was unbelievably uncomfortable. I stayed for about 5 min and had to leave. I emailed priority pass and asked for a refund because i did not use the lounge and was very dissatisfied. After several emails and phone calls they refused to give me a refund.

Would never use priority pass again I will never use priority pass again - I was given 2 passes with my credit card. I used the passes at Sydney international - where there is no priority pass lounge but suggested bars - the wait staff said I could use both passes and was with guest, so I did. I was told I could use $72 Australian. Today I received a $48 Australian dollar - $36 US - charge to my credit card as I have since been advised that I was not eligible to use both passes. So my $36 meal is now a $48 charge to my credit card. Unfair !! If priority pass are going to elect cafes and bars for priority pass guests as opposed To providing a lounge - such as at Sydney international- they should equip the staff to be able to give the correct information to pp members. Definitely has proven not benefit for me and won’t use them again

The lounge is conveniently located for non-~Schengen departures, just before passport control. We have used it many times over the last 20 years. For most of the time, it was a friendly, comfortable place to sit, let down badly by the choice of food and, to a lesser extent, drinks. The catering has had a revamp and is now immeasurably better. Don't expect a full meal but there is a large range of sandwiches, savoury and sweet pastries, as well as a couple of hot options. I'm not sure that I would pay the €20 odd entrance charge on a pay to use but, with the Priority Pass card, it is a real haven.

This is a very nice lounge with comfortable chairs, tasty food and a good WiFi connection. The food selection is somewhat limited with fruits,donuts, soup and bread available for breakfast. Coffee machines, sodas, self serve alcohol are available. The lounge is very clean with hard tiled floors throughout. The staff is very courteous especially the receptionist who was very friendly. The lounge was not crowded at 7 a.m., therefore there were no issues using the Priority Pass crowd.

Pleasantly surprised with this small Priority Pass lounge. Stylish decoration, very clean, great ambiance and seating options (recliners). The staff is very friendly. The food & drink selection is more than adequate (cereals, sandwiches, juices, coffee and soft drinks). We were taking an early flight and the lounge was not that busy. There are 4 MAC computers for those inclined to get some work done. Bathrooms are very clean. Wi-Fi is strong.

Do not waste your money or time on this useless scam of a card.  I have had the Priority Pass Select for over 2 years now. I am a global business traveler. I received the Priority Pass Select as part of my benefits package with my Chase Sapphire Card. To date, the Priority Pass Select card has been the most useless card for lounge access. Every single time I have tried to use it anywhere in the world, I have been turned away due to the pass being applicable to any of the lounges only at very specific time slots. As a business traveler, I cannot and will not make travel plans around specific windows that Priority Pass has negotiated with specific airports.

This is a really dreadful "lounge". and nonsense to call it a lounge. First, when we arrived airside to this Lounge there was a sheet of paper on the door to tell us to go way back to Information, landside, to get a code to scan for entry! Can you believe this? So we made the 15-minute journey landside to get the code, back through security and to the lounge. It is appalling. No food, no alcohol and a few, I mean just a few, seats. So, why is it called a lounge? It is just a quieter seating area. There was nobody on duty. We went back outside preferring to pay for some nourishment in the cafe. It really should be closed down.
Comfortable and clean lounge with few visitors on a Saturday afternoon. The Pros: plenty of food and drinks, comfortable seating, quiet. The Cons: no dedicated work space, single bathroom.

The only reason we upgraded to Platinum with Interval International was for the Priority Lounge access, so-called, benefit. What a mistake! We used it for the 1st time in Los Cabos on June 25, 2018. There was barely room to stand and no room to sit. Carry-on luggage was everywhere. Full of screaming, running kids. We decided to use the restroom and leave as the airport was much more comfortable. The restrooms were upstairs. Walking upstairs, we realized why the lounge was so full downstairs. It was, like, 100 degrees on the 2nd level. We used the restroom and left. Now, they want to charge me $27 PP? Good luck. I spoke with a very nasty, so called, manager to no avail. Am I surprised? Not at all! Don't waste your money on this service!

A Priority Pass lounge worse than Faro Portugal. The lounge here in Istanbul is overcrowded, dirty, the food is dry and disgusting and I'm not even going in the toilets. What seats there are, are uncomfortable. Getting fed up being ripped off in priority pass lounges. In the unlikely event I renew my pass I will definitely check reviews to avoid dumps like this!

The worst we have ever been to. An utter disgrace to call this cheap, nasty, canteen style room a lounge. No food, no refreshments, no seats but plastic chairs. Can you believe? NO food - the only alcohol were bottles of wine in a pay machine!! Truly awful and so we left, preferring a cafe in the airside.

I really like this lounge. It is my local lounge but still, I review it as I see it! Always a friendly welcome and we have not had any issues with seating. Nice clean bright lounge. The choice is what you would expect and a lot better than many other lounges. Lots of papers and magazines with Sky news on the TV's. There are monitors for departure live times and info.Breakfast is particularly good with fresh fruit salad, fresh fruit, yoghurt, pastries, croissants, cereals, breads, meat, cheese, etc, etc.

I was flying in economy, but I was able to access this lounge as a Priority Pass member. The lounge was very small and busy, but comfortable. Free food included breads, muffins, soup and some small ham and cheese wraps. There were also some small fruit dishes. I only got a bottle of water from the manned bar, but alcoholic drinks were also available. Wi-fi was slow and disappointing. The lounge has an outside balcony with a small swimming pool, which was a nice touch. The vast majority of people using the lounge were (loud) Americans, so not really somewhere you would go for peace and quiet.

The staff at the DNATA T1 lounge is friendly and welcoming, some of the staff  take their time for a chat. The furniture is a bit worn and needs an update. There is a good selection of food and drinks. It is fairly quiet to be a lounge of this size. I like this lounge and that's why I always comes back.

My Wife and I were traveling on a weekend getaway leaving Friday evening after a long week of work. We had a little time at the Airport and decided to visit the Priority Pass Lounge I am a World Class Elite Master Card Holder with a Priority Pass Card which allows us access to the Lounge even flying West Jet Plus. As we entered the Lounge we were greeted by a gentleman at the front desk and he swiped my card granting both of us access. We sat down at a table full of empty drink glasses ( the Staff was behind cleaning tables) and had a lovely snack or almost a meal. An attendant came and cleaned our table off, my wife then proceeded to go and ask for a drink of spirits. The attendant told her this would be her last drink because she already had Three. She did not this was her first drink and she explained to the server that the dirty glasses were from previous patrons. She did get a drink. Then I went to get my first drink of spirits and the server tells me I am cut off loud,ly enough to be heard through out the lounge. Very Embarrassing! I asked to see a Supervisor and the server tells me she is the Supervisor? The bar staff and attendants are very unprofessional We pay extra for this service and to be treated like that is unacceptable.

The Miracle First Class Lounge is near Gates D5 and D6 which are the closest gates from the immigration area. The lounge is spacious and clean and never seem to be swamped with people which is always a welcome relief after leaving all the queues behind in the public area. The space is bright, quiet and calming with a good spread of hot and cold food at the buffet and additional food items at the counters freshly prepared by the service staff. There are also toilets and showers available within the lounge.

This SATS Premier Lounge is in Changi Terminal 2. This lounge can be crowded at times but on the Sunday morning that I was there, the lounge was less than half full. The food selection is wide and varied. There are fresh salads, cheeses, cooked items, dim sums and a big basket of washed fruits. A popular item is the self service laksa noodles which is a signature dish of the SATS Premier Lounges through Changi Airport. There are showers and toilets available within the lounge.

Nice, large lounge with good seating and modern art deco look. The lounge also has a small duty free corner which sells perfumes and small accessories. The downside is that food variety and quality is poor and they don't operate as a buffet system unlike other lounges. Instead the passengers have to ask the waiters behind the counter what they would like to be served on the plate which is then prepared on tray for the passenger to take to the table to eat. Also the quality of beverage products and sweets has declined during the past year, for example Evian mineral bottled water was supplied initially and now cheap local bottled water is given instead.

Unpleasant! Children running around facility. Loud and crowded. Food bar limited to dip and crackers. Dip was a cream based needing refrigeration but just sitting out, but more importantly dirty. Picked through by the hoards of travelers. Bathrooms unclean. Told by staff I needed coupons.

I first went to the SATS Premier Lounge where I was informed that the lounge was unable to accept any priority pass holders until 11pm that evening and was directed to the Ambassador Transit Lounge about 5 mins walk away. The Ambassador Transit Lounge had over 25 seats and no more than 5 guests present when I was there. A selection of alcoholic and non alcoholic beverages were available. The lounge is well maintained with service staff clearing used utensils and crockery away. There were at least 6 shower stalls available which come with towel, shampoo and shower foam.  There was also an attendant present in the facility.

Out of the three lounges at Sofia Airport, the Vitosha lounge has the best food. Beverages are the same across all lounges. Vitosha is the smallest lounge with very few tables. For working the downstairs lounge is the best one. The lounge has partial view of the apron.

On 14 March we paid to enter the lounge, it was overcrowded and cramped. Seating was very uncomfortable. Food average. I made use of the shower which was the only upside. Returning on 5 April we again tried the lounge, before paying looked to check whether it was busy - it was more crowded than before. I am beginning to think priority Pass are not keeping up with demand for space. I have now decided to cancel my membership.

This Lounge is always crowded and it is not a very relaxing place. There are few comfortable lounge seats (there is much more but both times I have been there these extra areas were closed off). There is ample charging facilities and the food is not bad.

After visiting this domestic lounge at Shenzhen Airport I was very disappointed that I had used one of my 10 passes with Priority Pass. This lounge was very basic. It was just an addition onto the main walking path and so the lighting was not subdued and not very relaxing. The food consisted of instant noodles and some other plain items. I would have been better off spending the same amount as my pass would have cost and sat in a nice restaurant and had a nicely prepared meal. This Lounge is not worth visiting.

This Priority Pass lounge (Wingtips) at New York JFK is small, crowded. Food very mediocre. I would not recommend this lounge unless you don't have other options. The food is like you would expect at a cheap hotel breakfast. The chairs are not that comfortable. Better than no lounge, but not worth walking a long distance.

A very nice surprise. an American lounge with complimentary alcohol! Decent food and other drinks available too. They also made a point of coming in to announce the flight calls, which again is unusual. Definitely impressed and I will use again on my next visit

The lounge is quite small and gets crowded after 4pm with most tables occupied but there were ample individual sofa seats. There are not many socket points and most were situated some distance away from the tables/seats. Available on the buffet was salad with a decent selection of ingredients and a daily soup. Breakfast cereals and milk available. There was also a selection of breads and jams. Various options of beers, wines and liqueurs available and of course coffee and teas. Constant staff presence, in this busy lounge, who were busy topping up the food and drinks. Tables were cleared quickly after guests leave. The lounge is bright with floor to ceiling view of the air field from every seat. No showers but restrooms are available within the lounge.

American Express Platinum Members: Beware of this particular lounge (not sure if this happens in other Priority Pass Lounges). Upon entering the club, they will ask you to sign for your visit. If you are not careful (since this is not seen on the specific screen you sign on), they will add a "Guest" or two to you visit thus adding an automatic charge to your credit card (in this case for Amex Platinum is $27). I did call the the Priority Pass company who manages several lounges across Latin America, Europe and the US to complain about this fraudulent charge and they will happily tell you that there is absolutely nothing they can do to revert these charges since they have signed proof that you have authorized them. This is a disgrace given the fact that one of the main reasons I sign up for the Amex Plat card was to have access to these lounges. I do have to say that the Amex customer service is top notch and they promptly accommodated my request to give me due credit and investigate. Since you will not know of these charges until the time they are authorized and posted, a few days may elapse and you may forget. Again, just ask for proof of what you are signing for upon entrance to the Priority Pass Lounges. Save some headaches and your hard-earned cash! Disgusted customer.

Louis Tavern has several lounges in the departure area of Bangkok airport, all accessible to Priority Pass card holders and premium customers of different airlines. Although it is described as a First Class lounge, I see no differences with the nearby CIP business lounge. Food and beverage selection is satisfactory, WiFi works well but seating is limited, newspapers and magazine selection rather poor (mostly airlines in-flight magazines and local newspapers). No toilet facilities (you need use public toilets in the concourse).

I visited the SATS Premier Lounge in Changi's Terminal 2 on 5 February 2017 at around 9pm. The lounge was around 60%-70% full. Even though it was quite late in the evening, there was a good selection of food and beverage available. The self-service laksa station is highly recommended and great for its delicious laksa noodles. The fruits basket had a good selection of fruits (a display informed that the fruits were pre-washed). Compared to the United Club lounges I have visited in the US and Tokyo in December, there was a wider selection of food and drinks variety in the SATS Premier Lounge. There are around 6 shower stalls available in the gents. Service crew is on hand replenishing food items and clearing after guests. The lounge is conveniently situated near the entrance to the transit area and one level up which offers guests a quick escape from the crowd without having to go too far.

Frequently at Manchester Airport, Priority Pass holders are refused entry to lounges. On this occasion T2 has a brand new Escape lounge, however, Priority Pass members are re-directed to a smaller older Escape lounge. It is very small, laid out like a factory canteen rather than a lounge. Food limited and a bit grim. Fatty chewy bacon sandwich or small cubes of processed cheese. Staff not very friendly either. It's a grim place to visit, neither relaxing, comforting or offering anything better than being in the terminal. Would not waste my time or money in going back.

The Sala VIP Pau Casals (Priority Pass) lounge was spacious and clean, the staff very friendly and efficient. There are not flight announcements so you need to watch the clock. The food was okay with a small but variety of snacks, sandwiches and other nibbles. The drinks are both alcoholic and non with a reasonable selection. The wifi is the free airport one so you do need to log in again as the system drops you off.

This Priority Pass lounge at Berlin Tegel was a shabby lounge. Hard to find this lounge. Very small lounge (capacity approx. 20 people) and extermely cramped. Limited food and drinks. WiFi did not work. The receptionist was rude and unhelpful. Not recommend and not worth for the paid price.

Used the lounge while I had a technical stop over in Bangkok. The lounge was spacious, easy to find. Good selection of beverage, food and fruit. It has been consistent over the years. What is lacking in the lounge was the cozy and homely atmosphere. However I would still recommend this lounge. It's close to CIP lounge in Gate F but the one in Gate F tends to be very busy and it was much smaller.

Priority Pass Lounge at Istanbul Ataturk Airport. Shower facilities make this lounge a good stopover. Food selection is mediocre but wi-fi is strong. Lounge seating is showing its age. The staff is helpful and friendly.

I had a 6-hour layover at Paris CDG. Being a Priority Pass holder, I decided to use the ICare Lounge at T1. My departing Air France flight was from T2E so I had to make a trip to T1. ICare Lounge at CDG T1 is an embarrassment to a major air hub and airport like CDG. It is small, tired and dated. Passengers departing from T2 have to make a convoluted journey to T1 in order to access this lounge. Firstly, they have to take the shuttle train, CDGVAL to T1 having to pass through long passageways along the way. At T1, passengers have to go to the Alyzia counter to obtain a lounge invitation. Then one has to clear immigration before taking the elevator up to the lounge. The whole journey from T2 to ICare Lounge took 45 minutes including immigration clearance. If you are departing from T2 and have the Prioroty Pass to use the ICare Lounge, you'll be better off staying in T2 where there is adequate seating, shops and restaurants to keep you occupied.

Priority pass lounge used by several airlines in Calgary. Lounge is comfortable enough with a selection of refreshments. Please be aware there is no hot food -  except soup - and for this reason I give this lounge a huge fail.
Used my priority pass to access this lounge. Very comfortable seating. Snack offering abysmal. Drinks ok. Free wifi but only for 30 mins.

This is an excellent lounge. It puts to shame many USA airline lounges in the USA with its food offerings and amenities. The lounge is not crowded and is brightly lit. The seating is very comfortable and spread out. There is is a good selection of Ugandan newspapers and magazines. The hot food snacks are delicious especially the samosas. Wifi connection is provided as a free service by Airtel. The bathrooms are cleaned frequently by an attendant. There is a flight monitor in the lounge and gate agents come into the lounge to make announcements for flight departures. I would highly recommend this lounge.

We are Priority Pass holders and were refused entry into the lounge. This is the second time Manchester has refused us entry once in Liverpool and once in Dubai. We don't travel as much as we used too but to be refused entry as much as we have and those booking online and walking straight in makes you realise it isn't worth the money you pay so consequently were opting out. Just on another note some of the lounges we have been in are so poor in what selection and quality is of the food and beverage results you having to go out and buy the stuff anyway. In a nutshell I wouldn't bother unless your getting it as a freebie.

This is a rather small lounge but a welcome respite from the departure hall at ZNZ. The lounge is air conditioned. WiFi Internet connection worked well. The staff is friendly. The lounge offers hot snacks (samosas pies) which the staff gladly heats up in a microwave. There are 2 flat screens showing Al-Jazeera English but no flight monitor. Good selection of local magazines. The only drawback to this lounge are the bathrooms. They are located outside the air conditioned lounge on the 2nd floor. The bathrooms are clean.

We have been members in good standing for 2 years with the Priority Pass Program. When we entered the Priority Pass Lounge at Calgary we were expecting a hello how are you Welcome to Priority Pass Lounge. Instead the young woman challenged us and made us feel like we were “sneaking in. There was no Hello No Greeting instead the staff barked at us and said “Do you have A West Jet or KLM boarding pass?” We were insulted and feel that other customers may also be treated in this manner.

I visited this lounge at 10:45am and got to see the breakfast and lunch choices and was very disappointed. Any food court in Singapore would provide better quality and choice for $5. The breakfast hot dishes were hard boiled eggs hash browns and chicken hot dog sausages. At 11:00am the eggs and hash browns were replaced with rice and a cabbage and bean mix the hot dog sausages remained. There was some fruit salad from a can the orange juice was cordial. Alcoholic drinks were not free. Basically you would be better off saving the entry fee and using the money for a decent meal in one of the many eateries in the terminal. Changi is a fantastic airport and the facilities outside the lounge are better than those inside. The TVs are bigger and the chairs more comfortable in the public areas WIFI is free. I have a Priority Pass with unlimited lounge visits and I wouldn't bother going in again even though it wouldn't cost me anything. PP holders can access the Green Market lounge in the same terminal which does a nice Japanese lunch.

Visited the Ambassador Lounge at Changi Airport T3. To say the least it was a huge disappointment. Cramped seats some of the seats/resting places were located in nooks & corners unlike the Priority Pass Lounge at Terminal 2. But that was in 2012. It was big spacious and it did not have that cooped up feeling. Food was also lousy as compared to the T2 lounge. Beer & wines need to be purchased as compared to the T2 lounge. All in all it is Spartan in amenities and adjust your expectations downwards.

We used our Priority Pass card here as we were flying SAA and they had no lounge. This is by far one of the most tragic of facilities we visited - it may have been excellent about 20 years ago but it seems like a place that time has forgotten. Old dirty couches and insufficient seating. Snacks in bowls (chips popcorn and nuts) and some sandwiches on a tray. The place got so full that people had to leave or move furniture just to get to the single restrooms. It probably did not help that both SAA and British Airways had their flights within 20 minutes of each other! No Wifi and while employees were all smiles they didn't add much except to check us in and guard the door.

Refused entry as per book guests given priority over Priority Pass (Platinum Amex) members very poor attitude from staff  have had this before but they obviously oversell this lounge at the expense of scheme members. No 1 lounge round the corner far better (also Priority Pass).

Really terrible. I paid $58 for my son and I to enter lounge. No food no bathroom no showers no tv working no drinks other than poor coffee water and juice. Uncomfortable seats. Worse than sitting at the lounge near the gate. This lounge was the biggest rip off of my life. Priority pass you should be ashamed.

Hard to find near butterfly garden. Includes hotel and showers. Nice staff on door. Was politely informed that all alcohol is to be bought about USD8 per can of beer! Cheaper at cafe outside! Food wasn't up to much either a few hot plates and a bowl of apples. No cans just a cheap soda machine. Ice has to asked for. Not even a pack of peanuts. Really not worth the entrance I paid for my friend to enter.

Quiet and relatively comfortable. Free wifi is just the Schiphol-wide wifi that kicks you off after 30 minutes and is limited to 1 hour per day - the sign-in won't work if you have services running on your computer that communicate on non-standard ports eg. mail clients or spotify. The food is very basic - cheese puffs cocktail biscuits cup-a-soup and cake. The bar selection is much wider; they do two different beers on draught and several different wines. They also have a soda fountain and a decent water selection as well as a self-service hot drinks machine. Whether it makes sense to access the lounge with Priority Pass depends on how busy the airport is. If it is very busy it is nice to have somewhere quiet to sit and charge a laptop. If it is quiet then you're probably better to spend your $30 entrance fee at the bistro and make use of the relaxation area in wing F.

One of the worst lounges I have ever been in. The staff were totally disinterested the food was stale and minimal and the lounge area very small with tacky furniture. Avoid this lounge its a lousy excuse for a lounge. I hope Priority Pass takes notice and stops ripping off customers in this way. Its totally not worth it.

This was my first experience with my Priority Pass and I have to say I was very disappointed. Although this is a very small Airport the lounge was no more than a few couches and a magazine or two no Internet Access was available and the snacks were crackers or cookies in a package along with soda and water. This was all you received for $27 per person! I let Priority Pass know as soon as I arrived home and their response was sorry. In reading some other reviews it seems there are no standard levels of service with the lounges although they all charge the same price for access. I am sure there are some very nice lounges to offset the ones like I experienced perhaps a rating system would help prevent someone from experiencing what I did.

We arrived at the 24hr Lounge at 1.30am and even though the front desk was attended the lights in the lounge were all off. There was a small cheese selection and stale pakora snacks that had obviously been sitting out for a while. An attendant changed the food over to a breakfast selection which my wife tried. Beans Mushrooms tomatoes etc all freezing cold - very strange. The alcoholic drink selection was ok although when I got a coffee from the machine it tasted very odd - bad milk maybe?.
