The bathrooms were clean one shower room which I didn't use and there were 4 computer terminals and strong wifi signal. This lounge is used by Singapore Airlines First class and Qatar Business class. I would be very unhappy if I had paid so much and this was the offering.

It looked a little worn but the wifi worked well there was a good selection of drinks and staff provided nice selection of appetizers. Between the ability to escape the airport crowds and the access to free wifi I was content with The Oasis.
My first experience of a lounge with Priority Pass. Disappointing. The atmosphere was just slightly above waiting at departure gate. Looked tired minimal refreshments. The wifi was fine though.

As many of those non-airline branded Priority Pass lounges pretty poor. Stained carpets really small and no free Wifi or even computers for use. Very limited selection of snacks asked for soft drinks but was told there are none. Strange as you could get almost any type of alcohol you could think of. No bathrooms so you Need to use the (dodgy) Public ones.

As many of the lounges you that you can use with the Priority pass card this is far below what you get in one of the real airline lounges. Actually this must be one of the worst lounges I've ever been: There's no staff so you need to obtain an access code fir the door. Instructions to the desk are actually incorrect on the PP website the ground service desk has moved to Terminal 3. Lounge itself is extremely underwhelming hardly any food apart from some chips and the likes booze they have selected the cheapest of the cheapest brands around. Interior has the charm of a dentist's waiting room and there is no free Wifi available. As there is no staff you get dozens of self- printed signs on the walls telling you to clean up and not to do this or that very German. Avoid were possible!

Dreary dark lounge with a very limited range of snacks. Facilities not what one expects from an airport lounge. Lounge quiet empty (no wonder). I was sorry I wasted time finding the place. The plus is that it is quieter than in the airport; at least it was possible to sit quietly prior to boarding. No toilets or washroom inside the lounge. Lots of staff but little for them to do since there were few passengers in the lounge. Most staff looked bored and who can blame them.

Three Lounges named Louis Tavern CIP in share with Priority Pass. Provide a maximum 2 hours stay for Diners Club members (who only just recently got access to these lounges). None of the lounges have toilets or shower. Two of the 3 are very small and cramped. Clean. Food snacks OK but very industrial. Staff friendly. Chairs are too soft and very low - once seated hard to raise. Difficult to orientate yourself in the airport (even after 6 visits hard to find where to go for check in counter as they each are separated for certain airlines).

The only lounge available at BEY airport. As well as being the lounge for MEA it is used by the likes of Emirates and Qatar etc. The lounge is split into different areas with a nice smoking area and a children's area equipped with playstations etc. Fully stocked bar but the food was a let down - only a small selection of sandwiches and pastries available. Toilets were clean and usable. A business centre and wifi in the lounge.

The lounge was very busy on this evening with many flights leaving. The facilities are pretty good with about 8 terminals for the internet. The bathroom is clean with shower facilities available. The let down here is the food and drink area there are only ever two types of sandwiches available. Both were stale on this visit there was also lentil soup available which I didn't try. There are no other hot food options - alcohol is available but you must ask the attendant for it presumably to stop people taking advantage.

We chose this lounge because the Air China Lounge was supposed to close at midnight and our flight was not until 2. The agent was trying to tell us that Air China was the service provider for our flight so their lounge was open for us but language barrier prevented us from realising this until after. Lounge itself looked quite nice and comfy. The toilets were clean and there was a very well equipped shower facility which my wife tried to use but there was no hot water! A business centre available with internet terminals. The big let down was the food and drink selection. Only alcohol available was wine beer vodka or tequila - packaged sandwiches which were two days past there best before date some Koka noodles and a stale piece of bread. Very poor for a business lounge. The attendant was eager to get rid of us and told us 45 mins before the flight that the flight was boarding even though it didn't show as boarding on the screens. For the second half of our visit the night duty cleaning staff worked around us preparing for the morning rush!

There is no dedicated Priority Pass lounge at Narita airport. Priority Pass shares the Korean Airl business lounge. The customer representative at the front desk is courteous. Food selection is average. There is no cooked food. Just pastries biscuits nuts and a selection of cold and hot beverages. Beer is available. There is no dedicated toilet nor showers. Lounge is quite comfortable with TV and wifi access.

This lounge remains one of the best lounges I have visited. I last visited 4 years ago and the lounge has become very crowded. WiFi has become easier to connect to. No more getting a WiFi code. Instead one logs into Turkish Airlines WiFi, enters flight number and seat number, and voila you're connected to fast internet. As with my last visit in September 2022, the lounge has an open airy feel. Its food offerings are varied/excellent with various cooking stations throughout the lounge to satisfy one's palette. One definitely gets a taste of Turkish cuisine. The salad bar is extensive with a wide variety. We were not able to get the free massages to the neck and shoulders this time around, but, one can't go wrong with offering this type of service.

International business class passengers with Turkish Airlines have the choice of 2 separate lounges. The Turkish Airlines Business Class Lounge opposite Gate E1 is the primary location. The second option is the Turkish Airlines Miles & Smiles Lounge opposite Gate C1. Both occupy and area of 5,600 m2 and can accommodate 765 guests. To enter, you simply scan your boarding pass at one the turnstiles. Then you can stow your carry-on baggage in an all-glass locker and join the fray. There are street-style cooking stations where chefs serve hot pide breads stuffed with meats and cheeses and fresh pasta dishes or head for colossal salad bar where you’ll find a remarkable selection made from fresh produce. There’s the typical barista station, self-serve selection of local and French reds and whites as well as prosecco in golden bottles. Plus, there soft drinks, a water or beer available from open fridges. If that’s not convincing enough there are roving masseurs giving free 10-minute massages to weary travellers. If you haven’t got the time or patience to circle around in search for a seat, I recommend you head for the Miles & Smiles Lounge were there are usually much smaller numbers.

Big lounge but very crowded. We were lucky as a few minutes after we arrived the lounge was completely full. Food was good with various stations around with different cooked food options. We visited in the evening on our outbound leg and in the morning on the inbound. Big let-downs were the fact that there are no sodas available in the lounge. No Coke or Pepsi products at all and, when I went to ask about a shower, the wait time was three hours! Seating very hit and miss due to the crowding. Nice touch are the lockers you can use for bag storage.

The lounge at Istanbul's old airport was phenomenal, so the expectations at the new airport were high not even close - no place to practice golf swings, no toy race tracks for the kids, no huge display of desserts from Do and Co Vienna, no chandeliers in the rest rooms, and only 6 stalls in the ladies' room, causing the inevitable queues food counters with onsite chefs were still good but what a disappointment overall! (also a bit hard to find even with wayfinder in the Turkish Airlines app - it's upstairs but how to get up there? eventually we found the entrance for disabled passengers and the man there was kind enough to let us in)

This is an overcrowded mess. I pass through that lounge 4 times a month and now I really feel like commenting. Before you go upstairs you have some rude staff who easily greet you with "where are you going". No excuse me Can I help you ! This happened many times to me. After you have passed these staff you go upstairs to the lounge where you enter with your boarding pass. So really why do you have people downstairs ? Once inside, doesn't matter the hours, I was in a refectory atmosphere and not a lounge. It is overcrowded with not enough seating. It is loud and no quiet area at your service. Although, THY thought of all amenities to make the stopovers as comfortable as possible, many of those are not used and just occupy space. I am an Elite plus card holder and qualify for that many times within one year There is no extra area dedicated to them. The food stations although impressive are busy with preparing food instead of serving. The cooks are overwhelmed by the amount of passengers annd are doing their best to keep up. The food buffet for cold dishes is always well stocked and no problem to serve yourself. In the last visit I left. There was no space. At 5:50 am. It is for me ungraspable how a lounge at such a big airport has to be in the middle overlooking shopping areas and not have a view to the tarmac. This could have been easily one of the best lounges in the world. Instead people rate it as excellent merely on the food options available if available. This is not a lounge where you feel or experience some sort of privilege.

The lounge that I went to on my recent flight with Air Serbia was very good. There were 2 lounges available for Air Serbia flights: the Turkish Airlines lounge and the ProPass lounge. The views and the drink options were both magnificent, but the food, well not so much. There weren’t many choices and the choices provided didn’t look fresh. The staff were nice, but the lounge was a bit noisy. The mini chocolate muffins were amazing, a must try! The toilets were very clean and had a pleasant odour. It also was a bit crowded and there was limited seating, but the seats were amazingly comfortable! The WiFi was great too! (Also I don’t know if there were showers!) In conclusion, this lounge is great and I would recommend it!

While the Turkish Airlines business class lounge highlights private rooms as a premium feature, the actual experience is anything but premium. The showers follow a reasonable queue system, but the private rooms are an elusive and undignified ordeal. Despite being advertised as part of the business class offering, they seem more like a marketing ploy. There’s no queue system in place for these rooms. Instead, passengers are expected to pop in and out, begging for availability. The staff, with stiff body language, offer vague and inconsistent time estimates—anywhere from 25 minutes to over an hour. To make matters worse, there’s no time limit for how long guests can occupy the rooms, leaving others in a constant state of uncertainty and frustration. This process leaves passengers feeling more like beggars than valued patrons. Turkish Airlines should either implement a proper queue system or charge a fee to ensure a fair and transparent process. The current setup is nothing short of undignified and far from the business class experience one would expect. I finally got my room after 3 hours of waiting in uncertainty, and it should not be like this.

This is a very busy lounge with Priority Pass members being put on a waiting list for approximately 45 minutes. Seating was scarce on the first floor. The food quality is excellent. The lounge had a nice selection of Mediterranean cuisine e.g. kefta kabob with tomatoes and aubergine, grilled creamy chicken, assortment of cheese and crackers, hummus and Turkish Tea. WiFi worked flawlessly. There were lines for the bathroom given the number of passengers in the lounge. Nonetheless, the bathrooms were clean.

I travel business class internationally due to poor health conditions and advanced age. I have heart disease and cannot walk very far, and my wife has nerve damage and also cannot walk long distances. We both require wheelchairs. We arrived to IST on February 7th, at 2:43 pm, from Toronto. We had a 7-hour long layover in Istanbul, before our flight TK708 departed for Karachi, Pakistan, at 9:55 pm. Because of the long connection, we tried to reserve a nap room and specifically chose IST for this purpose. My wife was unable to sleep on the 9 hour flight from Canada and was exhausted. A young lady at the concierge desk provided unprofessional and rude responses to us when we asked her for a nap room. She first said there were none and to come back every 30 minutes to check. My wife walked back and forth (with great difficulty) from distant seating areas over the course of 2 hours, every 30 minutes, because I cannot walk very far. The young lady at the concierge desk did not have the courtesy to take our phone number or to put our names as next in line. After 2 hours, we tried again (the 4th time), and a younger man quickly walked ahead of us to the desk. The concierge desk then gave the next available nap room to this young man, who only showed up the first time to the desk, instead of my wife and I, after we were waiting for 2 hours and had been to the desk 4 times. We pleaded with the young lady at the concierge desk, asking why she gave the room to the other man. The concierge simply said "he came to the desk faster than you". For 7 hours we were unable to rest and sat in regular seats in the lounge, waiting for our connecting flight. This has been the worst business class experience I have ever faced in my life.

I miss the old TK lounge at Ataturk airport. This lounge is always packed. And the food variety and quality goes downhill every time I’m here. And now, with Turkish (or Turkiye) boycotting US products, there are not only no Coke products, but no soda of any kind. Sorry. I’m headed into the terminal. Worthless to sit in the crowded lounge and you can’t even get a Coke. Turkish has really dropped its game in their lounges.

We definitely received very good service. They provided every service in the best possible way. The food is very delicious, the seating areas are comfortable and wide, and there are many activation systems to pass the time. So you will lose track of time while waiting for the transfer.

Exclusive Turkish airlines lounge, huge space, different rooms to relax, big variety of food and drinks, local sweets. There is also a piano, sometimes they play it. Easy to spend a few hours here. Free Wi-Fi

I had on other trips been in their excellent business class lounge and flying this time in economy but being in possession of a Star Alliance Gold Status I had been granted entrance in this CIP Lounge.  I read it is inferior to the Business Lounge but besides just a couple of food stations less, I must see I truly am impressed: excellent food and drink selection, lovely atmosphere, simply a great place to be and spend some time.

I heard that this lounge was opened to give passengers who paid for a business class ticket a slightly more exclusive experience by leaving out status customers and thus making the lounge less crowded. This has not worked. The TK lounge at Ataturk airport used to be really fantastic and special and it was one of the reasons I booked with TK all the time. This time seems to have passed. I am just sitting in the TK Business lounge at Istanbul new airport, feeling like waiting in an overcrowded train station. This feels more like a free fast food restaurant or an all-you-can-eat holiday venue, than an exclusive space to relax and wait for the next flight. Virtually all seats are occupied, mainly by bags and coats to reserve a seat for people who seem to be wandering around. People are shoveling piles of food onto their plates and leave the tables completely covered with leftovers and rubbish. Even the supposedly quiet areas are overcrowded. Having been in the fantastic Qatar Airways Business lounge at Doha airport, this is the complete opposite… crammed, crowded and ordinary.

Using this lounge on a SWISS flight. The place is simply horrible. There are plenty of alcoholic drinks especially whisky, served by a bartender - the food is terrible and extremely poor. There was a very salty soup, a lot of vegetables and bread with tuna salad. Some small kind of a saucer with limited food like pieces of cheese with one grape, pineapple, melon and berry. Another 3 cubes of chocolate cake. The soft drinks in the fridge were lukewarm, in a basket some melting ice. I left the lounge and went to an eatery to have a decent sandwich. Maybe this lounge is Ok if you want to drink alcohol but not for a decent snack at all. The restrooms were not very clean.
After all the hype I was expecting something above average. What a let down, seating in the food area was very poor, no bar, and incredibly complicated internet access.

Transited twice through this outstanding and impressive lounge. As with my last visit in May 2022, the lounge has an open airy feel. Its food offerings are varied/excellent with various cooking stations throughout the lounger to satisfy one's palette. One definitely gets a taste of Turkish cuisine. The salad bar is extensive with a wide variety as is the tea bar with its variety of teas. On both visits we were able to get free massages to the neck and shoulders. Can't go wrong with this type of service. WiFi connection was excellent. Bathrooms are very clean and maintained by attendants.

I was looking forward to visiting this lounge because I had heard so much about it. Well, maybe the food is ok but not for Vegans. Even the lentil soup and white rice had butter, nothing for Vegans but a bowl of green salad. Next time I can arrive at the airport a bit later and have food outside - complete disappointment.

Turkish Airlines' flagship business class lounge is outstanding and impressive. The lounge is on an open-level overlooking the main part of the terminal. There is plenty of seating and space. The seating is very comfortable. The lounge is immaculate and its food offerings are superb featuring freshly cooked food at various cooking stations throughout the lounge ranging from grilled foods, pasta and baked cheese, spinach and meat pies, cheeses/olives, salads and desserts. One definitely gets a taste of Turkish cuisine here including Simit (sesame seed bagel) and coffee/tea. The latter can be served in glass cups you get in Turkish restaurants. There are quieter darker seating areas akin to seating in a library like area. There is a room with 12 TV screens to catch up to the news. The lounge also features virtual golf and a holographic flight experience. The bathrooms are very clean and maintained by attendants. Our flight was at 2 pm so all the cooking stations were manned and food aplenty. Depending on the food station there were some queues. The staff kept the tables clean removing used dishes/utensils promptly. WiFi worked just fine; however, you had to scan boarding pass to get WiFi password.

What a great lounge! From the freshly cooked dishes ranging from typical Turkish kebabs through Moussaka, Chinese spicy chicken stir fry and pasta stations you could see all those being prepared. In addition various meze options and a few sweets including an array of the ubiquitous baklava variants. Drinks stations (DIY) were dotted around. One nice feature was the lockers in which you can leave your bags, using a combination of your choosing. There is a golf simulator and other adult toys including a Scalextric track! Comfortable seating in a variety of types and a quiet atmosphere.

The only hot food was toast. Other than that, it was pre-packaged rubbish.  The coffee was weak, stale and tepid. There was no draught beer, only tiny cans. It is probably the worst airport lounge of any big city in the world and a national embarrassment. The WIFI involves fiddly codes that you must obtain from machines.

My inbound flight was 09h30 min, and my outbound was 06h30 and in between a layover of 14h. I was denied a sleeping room while it was given to passengers between 04 and 09h layover. So, I spent the whole 14h in the lounge, couldn’t get near nor shower.

Food was average. Turkish wine is on a small cart tucked away in the corner in a massive lounge. You will need to argue to get into showers or the private suites. They do whatever they can to not give you what you are allowed. I dont understand it. We had a SFO to IST flight with a 4 hour 50 minute layover. Concierge said it was 3 hours and 45 minutes. You will have to argue. Very unfortunate. This lounge is dirty. Check out the seating the corners and the small tables. Sticky, hair and gross.

Turkish Airlines did not provide any lounge for this trip, for my full-fare-paid business class. Both a Swiss lounge and a lounge serving several Star Alliance Carriers are present but closed. Both British Airways and a Skyteam lounge are open, but Turkish did not make any arrangement for business class customers to use them, though Ethiopian Airlines did. I think having a lounge should be a basic element of an international business class itinerary, and no mention is made of its absence. I think it is lame that they do not provide a substitute if the lounge they usually use is under construction. The check-in agent confirmed there is no lounge access.

Despite the website saying I would have access to business lounge, they were all closed. Crammed everyone into regular lounge. Food was prepackaged garbage at domestic and lines for hot food in Intl were 15 to 20 deep. No bar service, just small bottles of soda/water/juice. Absolute garbage. No social distancing but used COVID safety as their explanation for Business being closed. And no lounge was open at Izmir or Kayseri. Shameful.

How to transform one of the best business lounge in one of the worse. Covid is an excuse for mediocrity. Turkish Airlines is the champion of it. It is easy. No more anything. And what is left: sandwich are really badly done no flavor, no nothing. How sad Forget traveling in business with them. Not worthy at all

The business lounge has become worse than it was at the old Istanbul airport. The choice of food there are no replacements for everything old. Stupid rules for using sleep rooms and they do not go to the rescue, even when the the room is free.

The lounge is quite big and has a diverse variety of foods. It has an area for desserts and for salads and few live counters. Excellent food selection, comfortable seating. Only problem is that it is difficult to find a good seat and the lounge tends to get crowded. Even after splitting Business class and Star Alliance Gold customers, the lounge is still crowded and noisy. Moreover, the free wifi is pretty weak. Otherwise, the ambience and staff are excellent.

It is open 24 hours, which is puzzling as the Turkish airlines flights depart in the late evening. In the morning when I visited, I was greeted by the receptionist who took my boarding pass and placed it in the photocopier. She said that her computer is broken so she can’t scan my boarding pass and will have to log my entry on paper. She handed it back to me and gave me a WiFi password. The lounge is slightly dark, but has natural daylight coming in, with a view over a garden in the airport. It has plenty of seating, ranging from couches, armchairs, dining tables and work tables. The breakfast spread was a bit puzzling, some fried rice, sausages and cooked ham, a basic selection of pastries and a rather large selection of cheese and nuts. I was wondering where the eggs were, when I discovered that they were made to order. I had a pretty good breakfast in the lounge and I enjoyed my eggs.  There was a bar although it was not manned, and there was Turkish tea, coffee and lounge drinks you’d expect. I like that they had Turkish tea glasses and the tea was excellent. I think this lounge is a good option, considering how new and unknown it still is.
The best business class lounge I have experienced, out of this world. Food was brilliant drinks free flowing and recommend the lounge. Just don't fly Turkish airlines to get the experience.

This lounge is a massive disappointment! It is a circus inside, nothing relaxing about it. The areas look beat up and old and in need of a refresh. I honestly felt the lounge was on the "cheap " side. Ive had better experiences even in Priority Pass lounges! I qualified for a "Suite" to rest in. I asked to shower an the attendant showed me to my room and said it was all busy for now and she would come by to get me as soon as one would free up.. She never showed up! The whole place is a Circus and the staff generally rude. It is loud, crowded and the suite for resting was a bit on the cheap side as well but did the trick for a 3 hour nap.

The lounge was a bit difficult to find as it was in the centre of the airport and both flights I took park at different sides of the airport. The lounge was huge (two-storey lounge) with modern decoration and facilities like a cinema, golf room and loads of seats and fridges for drinks. But the lounge had a lack of food even and only local food, fortunately that day there was a Japanese food selection. Although the lounge was huge, there were huge numbers of people and seats and facilities run out quickly. The toilets were clean but too small compared to number of people in the lounge. There was a locker to store a luggage. The WiFi can be access by scanning my boarding pass on the kiosk and received the WiFi code. The WiFi itself was fast but disconnected very easily when devices were turned off. Overall, the lounge was acceptable and could be improved.

After 6 years using this lounge regularly I am in a fair position to evaluate it. The food has not been changed during this entire time. Soup, wheat (bulgur) salad, cheese and little cookie type of things all the time. Heavily overcrowded. Hopefully at the new airport this will be altered.

Overrated, before travelling I spent time trawling the net & you tube looking at and getting excited about what was to lay ahead of me when I had my 3 hours lay over between flights. I was over whelmed at what I was seeing, a spacious lounge with so many amenities, choices of the different foods on offer along with areas to sit and rest in peace. Making my way to the lounge was a trek in itself, it seemed miles away from the gate we had landed at and for an airport so large there are not many travelators, and the walk went on and on! The airport at time was very busy, it’s close to midnight but i wasn't worried as soon i would be in the sanctuary of peace and quiet, a plate of tasty food and a long drink. How wrong i was, this place was manic, what could be described as a busy street in Istanbul during the sales! It was busier inside than it was out, I was first met by a group of unruly kids on the pool table, shouting, screaming with no regard for other travellers, as i ventured further inside the worst it got, it was cramped, no available seating and ques for the various food outlets winding all over the place, as for a seat -  no chance. A far cry from what I had seen on you tube and the glamorous descriptions given by Turkish Airlines, i have been in better lounges this by far was one of the worst, I started to suspect the videos where made at a time the airport was closed. I duly left!

Plenty of seating areas available to relax for a long transit. Excellent and delicious variety of Continental and Turkish food. Good choice of beverages. Lounge is not very noisy and toilets are super clean. Ambiance is beautiful. Great to have a movie area. However, there is still no information about the massages. They say they offer it and then when I asked, they said I needed some appointment. I did not get clarity on it. It's 100 times better to sit here than the overcrowded, noisy and dirty waiting area at the terminal.

Very nice lounge, good quality. Surprised by the catering offer which was excellent. If all lounges were of this quality, I will take a subscription. Congratulations to Turkish Airlines for this lounge, and to the staff who were very friendly. FR: Tres beau lounge, de bonne qualite. Surprise par l'offre de restauration qui etait excellente. Si tous les lounges etaient de cette qualite la, je prendrai un abonnement. Felicitations a Turkish Airlines pour ce lounge, et au staff qui etait tres sympa.

This is an amazing lounge and one of the best that I have been in. It is large and spacious and I arrived at about 12.30 am. The kitchen staff were gradually closing down in preparation for the morning rush so the available food was quite limited and there was nothing available that was freshly cooked (this is not the norm). There was plenty to drink. I wanted to take a shower (my previous one had been in Jerusalem early on the previous morning. All the showers were taken and there was a problem with the buzzer so I was disappointed that I missed out. Previous experience says that the showers are good and the bathrooms and toilets are very clean. WiFI connection was good and fast. It was a reasonable walk to the departure gate from the lounge. Overall not as good as previous visits but still a very good lounge.

This is a regional lounge for Turkish Airlines. They had a chef preparing breakfast/lunch food when I arrived and found it quite tasty and suitable for non Turks and Turks alike. I liked the ambience of the lounge - it was spacious and there were quiet areas if you wanted to work, there was television and areas for computers, including recharging. WifI was good and no problems with connection or speed. The toilets were clean. There was no shower. This was the only negative. The variety of drinks ws good and easily accessible. It was a relatively short walk to the departure gate.

Very good lounge. Food was incredible, and reception staff friendly. Choice of alcohol (wine, beer) is also nice. I took the opportunity to discover Turkish beer. Congrats to Turkish Airlines for their lounge. I recommend it for sure
This lounge is one of the best in terms of service level, offerings, comfort, staff etc. I have been to turkish airlines lounge in İstanbul but this is better than that one.

It was the first time I came in a business class lounge, and I used this lounge when flying with United Airlines. I must admit that I was impressed by the quality of the lounge of Turkish Airlines in Washington. All the chairs were of very good quality, and the food was amazing. Better than any airport restaurant. Congratulations to the chef. I advise everyone to try this lounge, it's an amazing experience.

Checking in for my flight to Istanbul with Turkish Airlines, I was fast tracked to the Lufthansa lounge. My early morning flight meant the place was near empty. It wasn't large, but was curious to find another 'Senator' lounge within it. I was told it was for the 'elite' passengers, and having made a peek I could not see what was so special. Back to my area, the furnishings were formal complimenting the Lufthansa colours, comfortable but not luxurious. I imagine once the place got busy there would be no secluded spaces for relaxation. However the overall appearance looked rather business like. The eating areas were more like a canteen with  white tables and chairs. The breakfast was good, with a selection of hot western cuisine, cold cuts, plenty of fruit, cereals and pastries etc, including a small bar. The staff were efficient in clearing up tables quickly, leaving the appearance clean and tidy. Overall a satisfactory experience, but nothing to shout about. And as I spent only an hour there, I enjoyed the quiet time.

Travelling from Istanbul to Hanoi and back to London, I was able to experience this lounge at different times of the day. So much has praise has been give to it, I was looking forward to it. My first visit was at midnight. To my surprise, found it crowded and busy. Covering two floors, the area is quite large. The interior architecture and design is beautiful and very inviting, unlike some other lounges that appear too formal. There was plenty to explore and occupy a long wait, like games, pools table, library, computer stations, and of course a huge selection of food and drink. Several areas served hot food with chefs preparing in view. There were innovative themes, like a tempura bar, where the chef would prepare a dish to your liking. The furnishing were varied, to suite everyone's tastes, from dining areas, to reading, typical bar like areas and cosy furnishing for simply relaxing. I wanted to try the sleeping area but was turned away due to my departure time being too close. The staff were very attentive and kept clearing up spaces and used tables. The food was excellent, from European to Asian. Plenty of varieties of soft drinks, wines and spirits (although not a huge selection of premium brands). I also found several mini stalls of sweets and pastries, and although I wanted to try some, I was already quite full and wanted to leave some space for supper on my flight. On my return flight, I landed at 5 am, and the lounge was near empty, so spacious and quiet. I did not have to queue for a shower, and feeling refreshed, was able to settle down to a hot breakfast. Later I was exploring quiet dimly lit spots, to bright dining areas, and sipping plenty of Turkish Coffee in-between. And hour later, that rush had begun, and by the time my boarding came up, I could hardly see many empty seats! This lounge is great, and has plenty for the long wait traveller to enjoy.

The NIA Lounge at Hanoi Airport is one of the nicest lounges I have visited. Not because it's luxurious or large, but because of the layout, greenery/plants, comfortable furnishing, and very friendly staff. The lounge is used by many airlines, and I was surprised to find how quiet it was. I was told the busiest time will be in an hours time, around 10pm, but the time came and went, and there were only a few more people. The shower facilities were basic, with sachets of shampoo and shower gel provided. On the food department, I found an excellent selection of Asian and Western cuisine, some delicious sushi, salads, and plenty of fruit. One little complaint I had was that the dining cutlery was plastic, considering how neatly the area looked and presented. On the drinks front, beer and soft drinks were self service, but you had to ask for wines and spirits to be served. There were no premium brands and the wines were pretty ordinary. But it all made up for the lovely atmosphere of the place and the staff, and even though I had a two hour wait, it was very enjoyable.

Beautiful, large, clean, very good lounge to be in. Unlimited food and drink. When there is a wait between flights very much like to be there. I was there several times there and it was fun, there are also showers, a place to rest, a place to see movies, fruits, vegetables, drinks and more. It is highly recommended.

Amazingly huge lounge on two levels. In the morning  a cook can prepare you omelette, scramble eggs, fresh croissants are available. Espresso, capucino and all the classical breakfast you can find in a hotel - everything is made on demand and served fresh. There is a movie theater, a kids playground, a piano lounge area and hundred of comfortable seats The only hiccup, just average friendly staff at the entrance

Great lounge in general. Nice and large but still always busy. Showers are great but they either have a rain-shower setup (not recommended when you don't want to wet & blow-dry your hair) or it's hand-held as the shower head otherwise has a about belly high wall fixture only, making it a tad uncomfortable. The range of salads is amazing but there could be a little more vegetarian food on offer in the warm and specials section (i.e. food of the week was Thai - with chicken once week and Chinese with beef another week - also the local pasta dish is only available with meat - please offer a veg option). Unfortunately some of the male staff tend to talk loudly / large it up, while all the female staff is able to 'hold back' without any problems. The biggest drawbacks of the lounge is unavailability of transport to the gate other than by wheelchair for lesser abled passengers - it's easy enough to get some buggies in action, I would have thought. The second biggest drawback is that there is no sparkling wine or Champagne on offer at all, for those who don't drink white, red, beer or other (top shelf) alcohol. Please include a Cava of sorts in future.

This Turkish Airlines Lounge at Istanbul Airport was an amazing place with fantastic interior and all kinds of food and beverages. The lounge is huge over 2 floors. In every floor you see things related to Turkish culture.  I'd like to visit it again soon!

The Turkish Airlines domestic lounge was extremely crowded and consequently somewhat dirty. Nevertheless the lounge offered a nice respite from the crowded terminal with comfortable chairs, snacks, and soft drinks. A nice feature is that passengers were taken by bus directly from the lounge to their connecting Turkish Airlines domestic flights.

The Turkish Airlines lounge in Istanbul remains the best lounge I have visited. Everything works well and the range of food and drink is outstanding. I spent nearly three hours in the lounge, sampled the food and drinks. Chefs were cooking nearly all the time that I was there. It is a very large and busy lounge but I managed to find space for myself, I got access to the Business Centre and was able to print privately a couple of documents that were needed for Bangkok; WiFi worked well. I enjoyed a shower shortly before my flight (enabling me to freshen up after a full day - leaving my flat in Tel Aviv at 06.15 am and having a day in Istanbul). The bathroom area was very clean.

The lounge on first impressions looks great and impressive but when you get in it isn't up to my standard for a business class lounge. There is plenty of seating,it's huge, it's got plenty of drink bit I didn't find plenty of food. The selection was limited and quality is poor. They had a promo on chilli chicken that I found horrendous. The toilets, it's great someone is there cleaning them but does he need to clean every cubicle before someone else goes in? The masseuses walk around apparently and offer this service but I haven't seen this service. Shower room I was told there is a 2-3 hour wait. Surely priority should be arranged based on ticket bought versus frequent flyer in economy and departure time. The concierge team there were rude and unhelpful to me. Wifi good speed and easy to use. Good luck finding your way there once you get past your gate from arrival if transiting. To round up, I'm glad I'm not paying exclusively to go into this lounge. It's priced in my ticket. I understand that. However it really isn't up to standard and needs working on.

Stunning lounge, better than most first class lounges. Stayed overnight in the lounge reclining seats in a cinema inside the lounge so was able to rest. If you are flying business or are Elite Plus with Turkish you can use one of the beds inside the lounge. Loads of food options, loads of stuff to do in a really cool environment. Really well thought out lounge, well done Turkish Airlines!

The Sala Cibeles at MAD terminal 1 has won its place as my new favorite lounge. Turkish Airlines uses this lounge, and it's a perfect choice. The food offerings may be less remarkable than TK's home lounge at Istanbul, but the views here are spectacular. There are huge picture windows in three directions overlooking the tarmac and the active runway. There is also an outdoor patio for those who smoke and/or enjoy the aroma of Jet A. There is a fine alcohol selection, including a good Spanish cava. Although there were no hot food options, there was a great variety of tapas, sandwiches, and salads. For plane spotters and airline enthusiasts, this lounge is exemplary. If I had known about the Sala Cibeles ahead of time, I would have come to Barajas much earlier before my flight.

On my most recent trip I spent 9 hours in this lounge on the out-bound trip and 2 hours on the return trip so I would consider myself fairly familiar with it. I enjoyed the fact that there is a free device-charging locker facility available so you can lock up your phone while it is charging. The food and beverages weren't amazing but quite decent. The bottles of sparkling water were not screw-tops and so not possible to enjoy once the bottle opener went missing. There are plenty of seats throughout the lounge with space for everyone. There are screens on two sides of the lounge that allow you to easily check the gate and status of your flight.

I purchased lounge access, the lounge itself was pleasant and the food selection was decent. At around 8pm we noticed there hadn't been a bar tender for about 10 minutes. I informed staff who then told me that the bar tender was on a break and would be back in 10 minutes! I said that was ridiculous as we had a flight to catch and she simply ignored me. I then went behind the bar and poured myself and about 3 other patient lounge patrons a drink. The bar tender returned about 20 minutes later. This didn't leave me with a very good impression of a lounge that has a lot of potential. The customer service is rude.

This review is being written from the Turkish Airlines lounge at Washington Dulles Airport. At noon, when I entered, the lounge was essentially empty. Slowly, the room is greeting new passengers - mostly Star Alliance Golds traveling on South African Airways. The staff are both efficient and friendly. The bar is open and well stocked. The sparkling wine is some Hungarian brand I have never heard of, but it is acceptable. The food choices were relatively limited at 12:00, but by 1:30 there appeared a good variety of soups, salads, meats, and deserts. Although there are impressive picture windows overlooking the tarmac, so far airplane movements have been quite limited. There should be a Lufthansa 747-800 arriving shortly, so views will become more interesting soon. This is a most pleasant place to await your flight if you are a Star Gold.

Two experiences and very different at this Turkish Airlines lounge at Istanbul. On the outward flight from London we arrived at midnight. The lounge was packed and as busy as outside. There was no space to relax or find a quiet corner. I had wanted a shower before my next flight but told there was a two hour wait for showers, exactly the time I would be in the lounge. So no shower. The lounge is huge and with so many passengers quite confusing. No indication of how to find details of WiFi. Fortunately another passenger saw me looking and gave me the code. On the evidence of this experience I would not recommend the lounge. Return to LON, arrived at 06:00 for a morning flight. The lounge was quiet and calm with few passengers. It was possible to move around and sample the many types of food available. This experience was very good, a complete change from the earlier experience. It is difficult to give ratings for this lounge since one is very poor whilst the other is very good!

Had the opportunity to utilise this lounge twice this trip. Was told by many and by the airline what a beautiful lounge it is, and it turns out to be very beautiful indeed. Unfortunately, the kind words would end here. It is a very large lounge, but lacking much to do. Food and beverage options are not impressive, same stuff repeating throughout the lounge. WiFi service is dismal. Very slow and often disappeared. Ability to charge your mobile devices or laptop from your seat is almost nonexistent. Worst of all, and probably partially the fault the place is so big and difficult to maintain, the lounge is quite dirty. There were a lot of debris (mainly food related) on the floor and around seats. And the staff always seem busy, making them non-responsive to customer needs, sometime to the point of being rude.

I first saw this lounge at Washington IAD on my way to Seattle. I had visited the Lufthansa Senator Lounge and passed by the new Turkish lounge on my way back to the C gates. I saw the Saudia logo as well and thought that this might bode ill for alcoholic beverages. My flight back from SEA to TPA left barely over an hour for connecting in IAD, but we arrived almost an hour early. I hustled over to the B concourse, and I am pleased to report that this lounge should easily qualify as one of the 10 best business lounges world-wide. The lounge is new, bright, clean, and roomy. The view onto the apron is open and gives good views of taxying aircraft. The food options are not the equal of its big sister lounge at IST, but the choices were adequate and delicious. Despite the shared Saudia logo, the Turkish lounge has a well stocked bar including sparkling wine - a beverage not offered at Ataturk. The attendants at the door were welcoming and cheerful, and the cleaning staff bustled about quickly clearing used plates and replacing food items to the buffet. Most clients were seated in the area around the buffet table, but there was more than ample room in a separate area with big, comfortable chairs, and a collection of barstools in the separate bar room. There is one shower room available and a small prayer room.

I entered this lounge with my Priority Pass, on an evening lay-over. It is at far end of the Terminal and the downside is that there is a lot of aircraft noise. It is large and comfortable and was fairly empty while I was there. The high spot was real coffee from an expresso machine made to order. The food was very standard fare, rice and pasta & a few salads, certainly no turkish specialities. The wine was poor but other drinks were fine. There were integral toilets, showers & even a small prayer room. Overall a pleasant enough lounge.

This Turkish Airlines lounge at Istanbul Airport is a great and grand lounge at the same time, full of amenities such as pool billiard table, library, room with comfortable chairs in the dark with silent music to take a nap, very good breakfasts and nice lunch / dinner food, fantastic selection of local food such as olives, honey and sweets. It may not be too cosy as it is 2 big floors, but you will find your space. Impressive place to be!

The lounge is pretty small, but it was nearly empty of passengers. It is not nicely decorated and the chairs are not that comfortable. There was no staff present, only occasionally coming to replenish the food. I had to wait until my empty plates will be taken away from my table for quite some time. There is alcohol beverages available for self-service (inclusing champagne). There seems to be a bar with a cocktail menu, but there was no bartender to service visitors at the time I visited, so no cocktails were served. Although food selection was very minimal, what I really liked about the place was that hot food was available and very tasty - hot soup, curry chicken, grilled vegetables, etc.

This lounge definately looks much better on pictures than what you experience in real life. It was extremely full, hot and the choices of beverages (no sparkling wine) very limited. The food selection was good. What bothered me is that the entire place is filthy and is showing signs of heavy use.  I'd rather have a wider choice of beverages and not so much food - and most importantly, sit on a clean chair.

We used Kris Fyer Gold to Enter Istanbul TK business lounge, looks really awesome inside, one of the best lounge I ever visited, with locker, cinema with popcorn cart outside. snooker table, library, children play ground, very special piano, with 3 stories with wide space. good dining- local cruisine / dessert/ fruit and nut/ wide selection of wine and drink.

This is a shared third party lounge facility at Manchester Airport also used by pay-to-use customers who seem to be on a mission to get drunk. Extremely limited snack selection. No hot meals available. Alcohol is a bar service though often no-one serving. Nice views over runways. Toilets are outside.

This is a huge lounge on two floors.  Lots to do here including a snooker table, library, Scalextric, virtual Golf range, cinema, grand piano etc. Plenty food and drink stations serving hot and cold and freshly prepared foods. There are supposed to be wandering masseuses but I did not spot any. Can get very busy at times. I didn't find a problem with the toilets. Free lockers for your luggage and phone charging facilities. I couldn't find out where to find champagne.

Turkish Airlines flagship business lounge looks great in the pictures though the reality is not quite up to it for one simple reason - it's very busy. Istanbul is one of those frantic crowded airports and this carries over a bit, so you can have difficulty finding a seat, and the tranquil quiet ambience of many lounges may be a bit lacking. The other features are good - plenty of catering, and those quirky things (model car racing, player-piano) from the ads are there to be enjoyed if you're into that. Oh - and mirror walls in the bathroom cubicles, so you can contemplate an infinite sequence of yourself "on the throne"? Really?

I have used this Turkish Airlines lounge at Istanbul multiple times and always had positive experience, this time i took my wife and  kid along with me. I am a Star alliance gold member, so i can bring 1 guest with me without issue. I was worried about my 14 months child, if they will ask money for him, but they didn't. Inside lounge there is nice play area for babies and changing room. I am a vegetarian and in almost all airport I face problem to find vegetarian food (which is not plain salad), but this lounge was fine. Enough vegeterian food with taste. plenty of drinks option and Dry fruits. Fully satisfied with this lounge. Only not so positive thing would be its distance from boarding gates ( which i had to use) without traveletors.

The best business lounge I have been in. The place is so huge if your looking to get away from the hustle and bustle you can always find a quiet spot. For some strange reason that normally happens as people like to congest near the main entrance, strange really. This place has everything the traveler needs for a short or very long stay. I sometimes have to stay here for 8 hours for connections and it is relaxing.

The Turkish Airlines Lounge at Ataturk is one of the best I have been to. The interior is stunning. There is an abundance of lighting and seating options but it does get crowded. The staff is attentive and readily clears your table. The food is the best part - from delectable cold and hot Mezze to on-demand dishes made by the chef. The quality and ingredients are excellent. I am definitely looking forward to flying to Ataturk again for the lounge!

Really poor 3rd party "Aspire" lounge used by Turkish Airlines for business class passengers at Manchester. Food offering is quite poor - dry bread roll sandwiches with minimal filling. Had to get 4 of these to make one decent sandwich. Not much else on offer - drinks are bar service, but the bar is poorly manned so you wait and wait and wait for service. This is probably deliberate. Quite a few families with very badly behaved children, running uncontrolled around the lounge and making lots of noise. Parents didn't notice or seem to care. Tables dirty, not cleared. View of the airport is good. Only positive. Only giving this lounge a 1/10 because I can't give it a 0.

Amazing lounge, great food, lot of variety. Food is restaurant style, open almost 24/7, sometimes too crowded. Its the best lounge where I've been. Cleaning of course not as good and the showers are a bit old.

This is one of the two finest lounges I have ever visited. Outstanding food in variety, quantity, etc. Dozens of food stations and superb Turkish food. A salad station with a dozen choices; olive station with 12 different olives; dessert station with a dozen desserts; turkish dessert station; fresh fruit; etc. Wonderful variety of hot and cold drinks. A massage area, pool table, golf practice range, children's play area, movie theater and more. Very comfortable and abundant seating. Huge space on two levels.

Very nice experience visiting this lounge! Lots of space and no issues getting a nice seat. Several different places to get both snacks and food. Many places to get several different kind of soft drinks, tea, coffe, beer and other liquid. Lounge being attended by service personnel all the time. Just a great experience!

This is worth a transit in Istanbul, putting up with the deteriorating care of Turkish Airlines for its passengers, the deteriorating quality of IST airport (see separate review) and concerns about security in Turkey. When in the care of TK, they offer best hospitality in line with Turkish tradition. Scrounging and penny pinching of European airlines can be forgotten, once you experience the published luxury of this lounge.

The lounge is new and basic compared to international lounges of Turkish Airlines, but domestically is acceptable. The separate bus to the plane is a nice touch. Access from the airport interconnecting is an absolute joke, you have to walk 5 minutes outside the airport main building to get there. This is only a problem for connecting/car rental passengers as if you are being dropped off there, you can just drive up to the lounge directly. Once you are there, however, it is a nice and quiet environment.

Huge lounge with plenty of seating, excellent food and drinks and well working WiFi. Location is a bit awkward and not easy to find, with long walk to gates. Limited flight departure displays (shows less that airport displays). Service is fine.  Could have a few more bathrooms.

While this is a nice lounge with good food, the customer service is terrible. I was transiting through Istanbul with my cat, and asked for a day room. Because my layover was more than 7 hours the front desk supervisor insisted that I would have to leave the airport for an outside hotel and could not have a day room even for a few hours. I pointed out that I could not leave the airport with my cat due to quarantine requirements but that made no difference. She said that staff are only there to enforce rules and don't have the ability to help. Some empowerment of staff might help the attitude and customer service in this facility. I found a comfy chair and got some sleep anyway.

This Turkish Airlines lounge is one of the more amazing lounges I've been. Stopovers aren't long enough to enjoy the lounge - food is abundant and delicious. Staff at the entrance could be nicer though, and also the staff should also improve their foreign language skills.

Turkish Airlines business class lounge at Istanbul Ataturk Airport is amazing and very spacious, with loads of seats. Plenty of food and beverages. Shower facilities are clean. Wifi is strong. Has some lockers for those who want to do some last minute shopping. All very comfortable, and look forward to my next visit.

I am surprised to now see more and more DO&CO service staff in this Turkish Airlines lounge wearing the poison green latex gloves! Working myself in the hospitality business and as frequent traveller, I never saw such lounge service staff wearing latex gloves. This reduces the quality of service and appearance of this wonderful lounge and is not at all DO&CO standard.

Always a nice momentum at the Turkish Airlines lounge in Istanbul. The quality of food is a must, but the staff service could be better. Concierge service just very basic - ask once for a Japanese newspaper and you will understand. Look yourself is their answer, just walk around the 2 floors. Another time I was able to get a room to rest and refresh between two flights coming from Osaka. However, once the staff walk around on the wooden floor with high heels you are not able to sleep - just impossible to sleep.

Had a six hour layover on the outbound flight, and Turkish Airlines lounge is a great place to spend that time. Plenty of seating of different types and lots of different cooking stations throughout both floors of the lounge. Self service bars at numerous locations all with top quality drinks available and soft drinks available from large chiller cabinets. Quality of food and variety was very good and there was lots to do to pass the time. The toilets were spotless, although the use of mirrors opposite the entrance and sliding wall of the entrance could be confusing. On the return journey only has two hours and although the lounge was very busy we found seats easily.

I am writing his from the Turkish Airlines lounge in Istanbul. This lounge is much hyped by commentators, so I arrived three hours before my LH flight to FRA. As others have observed, the lounge is huge and crowded. At noon, there are seats of all types available. On the negative side, the floor and the carpetings are tired and dingy. The front desk staff were efficient, but not particularly welcoming. The food choices and quality are unsurpassed in any lounge I have ever visited. It's like patronizing a five star restaurant where everything is free. There is a huge salad bar, two hot soups, an endless choice of hot dishes from the kitchen, and desserts - particularly pastries, to satisfy any craving. There are at least two well-stocked bars. The impressive thing here is that they not only offer top shelf spirits, they offer a choice amongst top shelf alcohol. For instance, in rum, they have Bacardi, Havana Club, and Captain Morgan. There is a very large selection of red and white wines, but lamentably, no sparkling wine. This lounge is eminently worth a visit. Come early and come hungry; you won't be disappointed.
This Turkish Airlines lounge at Istanbul Airport is something that you need to experience. Good food, service and all the things you can do during a longer layover.

Excellent lounge with dedicated entry from check in. Great foods and drinks, spacious, on the spot neck massage fab. Fresh delicacies and plenty of space. Although always crowded. PC and printer available. Library and cinema, TV areas, snooker, video games. You can leave luggage in transparent locker which are easy to identify and very handy. All divided in two floors with direct exits to gates or shopping areas.  Showers and restroom impeccable. Snooker room and library plus plenty of siting room.  I personally find it crowded no matter what time of day you visit it.

This is what you call business class, in fact you could call it First Class. Mountains of food, good wifi, friendly and professional staff, plenty of seating. But it is the food that makes this place. Prepared by DoCo I believe.

Friendly reception, clean, big windows, calm atmosphere. No clock or time visible, Not easy to find (mainly due to work in progress at the terminal).  Broken glasses offered. Lighting was on, while there was more than enough light from outside because of the sunny day. No shaded windows. The inside temperature was high, in combination with the lighting. High occupation, during busy times so even less comfort and food available. Grey interior, not welcoming, feels more static. Food is scarce. Very little improvement overall, compared to prior to the renovation. This is an outstation shared lounge, affecting all customer airlines of the ground handler.
Best business lounge I have experienced. Plenty of drinks and food and lots to keep you entertained. Spotlessly clean.

Massive with different areas ranging from a romantic setting in the middle next to a large Turkish Airlines globe to an elegant piano bar a garden setting in second floor and tea bar etc. There is even a golf course simulator downstairs. Food is delicious and staff extremely attentive and friendly. My negative feedback is that they do not have nearly enough English Spanish German newspapers. I can understand why they will not have ES or DE newspapers but surely they can muster better than only the Wall Street Journal in English?
This is one of the nicest Star Alliance lounges. Large with excellent selections of fresh hot and cold food. Beverages are excellent and a huge range to choose from.

Excellent lounge although the toilets always seem to be busy. It must be the fantastic food and very good selection of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages available. I have read it gets very crowded but when I used the lounge - for 7 hours on the 7th of February - it was less crowded than for instance Thai Lounges in Bangkok Singapore Lounges in Singapore or Air NZ lounges in New Zealand. I won't stoop so low and comment on how much superior this lounge is to typical North American business class lounge: everyone who travels knows that.

Lounge in IST apparently won prizes which is beyond me - feels like a major cafeteria/canteen - it is huge and not to me liking. Absolutely crowded despite being so big and completely lacks all levels of personalized service feeling. Upon entering the lounge boarding pass beeped by a TK rep with zero eye contact. Food on offer very confusing and one has to go to several different places in the lounge to for instance get a breakfast plate. Eggs one place juice a second place and then coffee a third place etc. Highly time consuming and feels like a marathon for both customers and staff.

This is for the domestic CIP lounge in Izmir. This is a lovely clean lounge with great bathrooms and friendly staff. The design is homey yet modern. There is adequate amount of snacks but not extensive hot food selection. No alcohol only coffee tea and soft drinks. They drive you directly to your flight (so you do not need to go back to the gate) which is fantastic!

A massive airport to negotiate. Staff very unhelpful and rude. Once the lounge is found the staff at the desk and barriers are rude. The lounge is large and needs to be as its extremely busy. The food choices are excellent. We had a 6 hour wait so saw breakfast and lunch. Spotlessly clean.

This is one of the best business lounges I have been to. Lounge is huge with all kinds of food and drink stations throughout each with many choices. Tea & Coffee stations Alcoholic Drink Stations Cold food and hot food stations and they are very good to excellent. Lounge personnel are helpful and friendly. Shower facilities are nice and very clean. I would say that they can definitely do better on their Wifi service as it is problematic which is annoying.

With the exception of staff language skills this lounge is simply exceptional. Food and beverage choices are unbelievably wide. There is plenty of activities to pass time and the food quality is terrific. Bathrooms are spotless and very nicely appointed. Showers sleeper suites and complimentary massage service are fantastic Quite possibly the best business lounge out there.
Busy lounge but large enough to accommodate everybody. It has traditional cooking stands amusement for kids nice style calm and spacious.

It is amazing. Food centres in different spots cooking areas a great array and choice. Comfortable seating plenty of seating and very clean washroom facilities. It was a pleasure to be waiting in this business lounge definitely.

Unbelievably good. Pool table & library many bars glass enclosures with locks for luggage many chefs and self-service top-shelf liquor game room for the kids showers etc. The food was fantastic of course Turkish coffee and Turkish Delight and probably an acre in size. I've been in hundreds of business class lounges and I thought nothing could top Singapore Air in Changi until I flew through Istanbul.

A very pleasant experience. I enjoy using Turkish Airlines - good fares and helpful staff but the airport can be cramped and crowded. As was the lounge until expanded recently. A joy to visit - you hope for a longer stay between flights! Good food variety of seating areas and airy. I can't wait to use again. Probably only downside is the number of toilets and washrooms which are often very busy.

The best business lounge I have had the pleasure of spending time in. Food excellent. Roaming masseurs were welcome. Showers spotless. Bag storage area neat. Beautiful design. Toilets immaculate. My only gripe was my stop over was eight hours and a suite could only be booked if staying 4-7 hours. I was offered the use of a hotel room in Istanbul but declined. Lounge was only really busy from 06.30-08.30 during my stay.

First time in the new lounge area and wow - what a difference! Divided on two floors so much space and not overcrowded any more. The food options are truly second to none with freshly prepared food counters in many parts of the lounge. Got to use a lounge bedroom (very comfortable) and enjoyed shower in 5-Star hotel standard bathroom. Big boy's Scalextric track also fun! At last it looks like Turkish Airlines have really turned a corner in progress and this is the best lounge I have visited. Pity that the rest of Istanbul airport is so poor.

Following the expansion of the THY lounge at Istanbul Ataturk it is no longer overcrowded. It has an impressive selection of freshly made foods and pastries but also services such as cinema and massage. The atmosphere is nice and quiet (no boarding calls) and the lounge is light with plenty of windows and lighting to make it comfortable.

I visited twice in the last week and both times it was "full". The design is quite interesting but in trying to accommodate so many people it is not a relaxing place to be. The staff were working hard but it is not easy with so many people.
I used this lounge twice flying from BRU to BKK and back. A catastrophic visit in both cases totally overcrowded almost no seat to find very noisy and really unacceptable!
This is one of the best lounges regarding food and beverages choice activities (eg. a theater where you can watch movies or concerts billiard piano). Lounge team work in rush hours to avoid problems.

Very neat design very large with lots of seating areas many food stations. A real treat on a long layover traveling from Houston via Istanbul onto Dushanbe. This has to be one of the top airline lounges.

In theory the lounge is quite nice but at peak periods you should not even bother going to the lounge. It is normally full to overflowing staff will not offer any assistance to find seats etc. The washrooms and shower facilities are quite poor and badly maintained. Good snack and other foods if you can find anywhewre to sit. Staff service is good for the catering type staff but Turkish Airlines staff are rude and well below standard.

The literature states that this place has a capacity for 331 people. There must be at least twice that many here. No seats no food no power sockets. This cannot be called 'business' as it is impossible to do any. All I wanted in my three hour stop over was to charge my laptop send some emails and have something to eat. Impossible. Never using Turkish again to fly on business travel. In summary - overcrowded noisy access to basic facilities that the business traveller needs non-existent and a surly overworked team of staff.

Huge sprawling open-plan lounge rammed full of people with a very random and disorganised lay-out. Also not one real quiet area with groups of people sitting around shouting people listening to iPads laptops on speaker - just very chaotic and not a nice place to wait for a flight.

After a quite long walk over the airport you find a big lounge. There are lockers where you can store your bags a small cinema kids-area several coffee and tea-bars a grill where you can get sandwiches bbqued chicken and beef soups cheese salads pasta and desserts. Food quantity is impressive all offers taste good some very good. Internet stations are available and free wifi. The shower rooms are clean and nicely designed.

I travel frequently from IST but typically don't use Turkish Airlines for business so this was my first time in the new lounge. I didn't use the showers nor many of the other amenities but the one's I tried to take advantage of didn't instil confidence. I wasn't impressed with the lounge: I thought they might be having an "off" day so I asked to speak to someone in charge. It took nearly a half an hour to find someone. the excuse for not having an available manager in the lounge was that it wasn't a busy time of the day despite it being 3:30 in the afternoon on a Friday and packed. It was far too busy and loud. If indeed the mornings are busier I would hate to see it. After sorting through the piles of newspapers that seemed to be tossed haphazardly on the tables - they don't use magazine racks - I found that there were no English newspapers in the lounge. According to the lounge manager they "have them but they typically run out in the morning". Knowing that the idea of having some more for the afternoon passengers hadn't occurred to her. Food quality seemed good but accessing catering was very chaotic. For example there are two chefs working in tandem; rather than create a staggered system where some food is constantly coming out of the oven the two of them prepare food together load the ovens together then stand around until they take everything out then start the process again. Of course by the time each batch is ready there is a hoard of people are lined up and instantly they run out until another batch is made. Lockers were an excellent touch and the library was nice though I think that it's more for show than actual use in that it is as exposed and equally noisy as everywhere else in the lounge. A lot of people seemed to be highly irritated with the service on the day I was there and although each one of us seemed to be complaining about smallish problems I got the overall sense that things were simply not up to standard.

I was looking forward to visiting this lounge but my experience was bad. We arrived at 6am from a long Hong Kong flight and had about 90 minutes to rest before the next leg. The lounge was crowded and there were no seats! We wanted coffee and just to relax but there was no place to sit we wandered around for almost 20 minutes before finally grabbing an open seat. All the lockers were also full so nowhere to stash our carryon bags we had to lug them around the lounge too. And to make matters worse the showers were all full for an entire hour. We felt like we were at the Grand Bazaar pushing and shoving our way just to find a seat and a cup of coffee. In a word it was stressful not relaxing at all.

From dedicated baggage screening luggage lock boxes baristas preparing a la carte coffee drinks Apple Computer Stations luxurious bathrooms well furnished and decorated lounges to cordial and helpful staff wife and I were thoroughly impressed with Business Class Lounge. Turkish Airways single Airport Club to serve every category of premium ticket holding passenger or frequent flyer may not be for those seeking exclusivity or tiered service areas yet it worked well for us. Accounting for quality and quantity of food when flying long-haul business class we found food selection and portions appropriate for a lay-over stay in lounge. We were also not expecting nor did we avail ourselves of a private sleeper rooms in Business Class Lounge. I disagree with reviewer stating that Turkish custom of allowing Police officers to eat/drink for free must be stop. I did not observe police coming in and drinking tea/coffee. People in their role as citizens or public or private policy role of any given country that treat those who provide service whether public service / infrastructure or service industry as second class citizens have much to learn from Turkish way if not Turkish Airways! I found it a pleasant surprise when observing Turkish hotel employees eating from breakfast buffet.

Lounge is expansive and nicely furnished with a lot of options for how to spend your time. It can get quite crowded though and while there are lots of drinks on offer the food is limited and more snack based. The reception staff had a smile which ticks that box and the rest seemed very pleasant though they were just picking up cups. Overall nice place to spend time though worth exploring it to find a quiet corner when busy.
Wonderful lounge excellent food and nice drinks. Beside the chefs the TGS ground staff had poor English and provided a very cold and impersonal service.

They offer full selection of hot and cold food wines spirits every sort of soft drink and dessert bar. Showers and suites are available. Wifi is available. Movie room especially handy for children. Prayer rooms available and massage therapist roams giving free chair massages that were amazing.

Excellent catering delicious cakes lots of space for reading relaxing. Wonderful showers and toilets very good internet PC. Like the arabic touch in some areas very clean and state-or-the-art design. Staff must improve in all areas especially at the entrance and waiters.

Pleasantly surprised when I visited after an absence of 10 months. Much bigger and nicer than the old lounge. Lots of food and drinks choices. Washrooms are nicer. I am not sure I like the "minaret" style. Too Arabic for my liking. Must point out the interesting acoustic trait the minarets have caused. If you start hearing random people speaking and there is no one around you don't worry you haven't lost the plot or turned schizophrenic. The minarets carry and bounce voices around much like the whispering gallery at St Paul's cathedral. I could hear some talking a good 40 meters away around a 90 degree bend. The Turkish custom of allowing Police officers to eat/drink for free must also stop. They kept on coming in and drinking tea/coffee. Didn't interact that much with the staff so can't really comment.

The lounge is nicely redecorated and looks stylish. The coffee bar is amazing but other than that there is nothing more nice to say. Staff at the reception were rude unfriendly and unable to help with flight changes. There is also no fresh orange juice - though they specially announce it - the same thing onboard. It is not even juice just lemonade with part juice concentrate content. Dayrooms are unavailable as they give them out late at night for 6 hours and with 4am arrival all rooms were blocked. As well there are not enough showers - a waiting time of 60 minutes is not acceptable. Not thought through for an airline with mainly transfer pax. No high-quality amenities - bulk stuff in a push-bottle! Everything is meant good but not done well. Staff has a lot room for improvement!

A great looking Lounge but third class service standards. I have not seen a lounge with such poorly trained staff. The lady handling Concierge desk was the most unpleasant one. No smile no care or consideration for the customers. Staff continuously talking to each other and could not care one way or the other for the passengers.

The live pide bar was very good and popular amongst passengers. The WC area is interesting with canvas partitions at the entrance. Feels a bit like going to the loo at a village fete! All in all pretty good.

This newly renovated lounge provides a relaxing experience and is very spacious. The toilets/showers are stylish and modern. The negative comment I would make is relating to the staff who I found rather unfriendly.

The lounge has just reopened after a 3 month renovation. The design is very modern with a circular theme. There are numerous drink stations and food bars with most delicious Turkish food provided by Do&Co. Plenty of space food drinks barista service multiple TV entertainment Pool table and a library. The shower suites and toilet facilities are very stylish with marble tiling wood paneling and mirrored walls. High quality Etro toiletries provided in the showers along with towels slippers and bathrobe. There are only 8 iMacs for guests which use an odd keyboard with many standard keys replaced with non-standard keys. No @ symbol on the keyboard which made them almost impossible to use. The only downside is the that the staff are still coming to terms with the new facilities and on the whole they all need to learn to smile and relax a bit instead of grunting.

Showers are shabby and dirty a disgrace to this airline. Towels were thin and when we complained they were able to give us regular towels. Housekeeping of the lounge is reasonable and the tables were cleaned more often than they do at the other airline lounges. Thoroughly disappointed re the lounge amenities.

Tired and shabby. Shower very poor not really clean small thin towels shower head kept dropping forward. Food choice poor and only soup as a hot option - which for breakfast i found unusual! A poor location for Turkish Airlines home Lounge at Aturturk. Have no desire to return.
Lovely modern lounge plenty of new computers. Only beer and soft drinks lack of hot food - only soup small dry bread rolls with cheese.

Lounge in the airlines home airport - large open lounge with good coffee/food for morning departure. Not as fancy as some airline home airport lounges but still very good. Wifi was good. Selection of flat screens at one end but remote on one we sat at did not work.

I used the Turkish Lounge at IST as a J pax with another Star Alliance carrier. The lay out was airy and the decor was mainly Ottoman-style. There were shower facilities (again Ottoman- style with marble sinks etc). Food choices were adequate for mid afternoon with the usual selection of hot & cold snacks. There were a few different areas (large comfy sofas quiet area computers etc).

Good choice of facilities. Business services prayer room refreshments etc. Range of seating available - in seperate lounges for meals on sofas in open plan area etc.. and plenty of space for discreet discussions if required. Decoration quite impressive. Intrusive noise though from 4 tvs on different channels plus some noise from other areas of airport. Nice choice of drinks and snacks available and constant cleaning from staff kept the whole area very neat and presentable. As a non- drinker can not comment on size of a glass offered as on other reviews but range of drinks was quite broad if wanted. Soft drinks include teas coffees orange juice waters etc. Staff I found to be excellent not at all rude or dismissive and very welcoming. Also there was no pervasive cigarette smoke evident - very welcome to a non-smoker in Turkey. Location of Lounge is at one end of the airport and can be quite a few minutes to walk to gates but shops and other services close to Lounge so no need to walk unnecessarily far. A good and comfortable service.

Small CIP Lounge with nice choice of drinks and snacks. Limited office space for business if required comfortable sofas / seating and quiet space without excess noise from airport operation. Nice lounge conveniently close to gates and good efficient staff to assist if needed.

The lounge is very specious and has an interesting decoration. I have been at all peak times there and there was always enough space to sit and relax. There are showers available (some review say it has not) - to use it you should contact the front desk staff for amenities and staff was mostly friendly. The choice of alcoholic drinks could be increased though and size of glasses as well. A slient room for taking a nap is missing though.

The "new" lounge is located at the exact opposite end of the airport. It is quite a hike there but most flights to Asia and the US depart from there so I guess it is ok. It is quite unique : huge sofas and armchairs impressive chandeliers (like in a palace) and soft carpets. At peak times seating is very limited and I saw people leave the lounge because of not enough seating. There is an open bar with a wide selection of drinks (alcoholic and non alcoholic) - albeit glasses are very small - and some snacks (puff pastry and sandwiches). There are no showers which is quite a disappointment after a long flight. Bathrooms could be cleaner. There is a business center with free internet access and there are of course muslim prayer rooms. Staff is rude (as you would expect from Turkish Airlines) but all in all the lounge is a vast improvement over the old one.
